items.statement: Expects sustainable volume growth of 7-8% per annum driven by structural demand drivers
items.quote: We expect a sustainable volume growth of 7% to 8% per annum. The structural drivers are firmly in place, India's urbanization story, the government's infrastructure commitment.

items.statement: Committed to add 37 million tons capacity to reach over 242.5 million tons by FY28
items.quote: We have committed to add a further 37 million tons, which will take us over 242.5 million tons in a phased manner by fiscal '28.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton (excl. acquired assets) at INR 1,296 in Q4 FY26 vs INR 1,225 in Q4 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA per ton, excluding acquired assets, is at INR1,296 per ton for the quarter. For the context, this metric was INR1,225 in Q4 '25.

items.statement: Blended cement share and premium portfolio contribution both moved higher as conscious strategy
items.quote: Our blended cement share, premium portfolio contribution both moved higher, which is a conscious and a deliberate strategy going forward.

items.statement: West Asia conflict creates near-term cost headwinds on fuel, bags, freight and import-dependent supply chains; not a structural demand reversal
items.quote: West Asia situation is near-term cost moderator, not a structural demand reversal.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected to exceed 10% annually driven by market share gains in CPaaS industry growing at 8-10%
items.quote: And, it's going to be definitely more than 10% a year.

items.statement: Annual capex trajectory of ₹100-150 crores expected to continue
items.quote: Yes, yes. Yes, absolutely, yes.

items.statement: SMS pricing pressure continues; reset expected but timing uncertain; WhatsApp blended realisation impacted by shift from promotional to utility messages
items.quote: It is on the cards. When it will happen, I can't say.

items.statement: Cement demand expected to grow at 7-8% CAGR in medium term
items.quote: I expect the cement demand to grow at a CAGR of 7% to 8% in the medium term.

items.statement: Core cement ROCE improved 200 bps to 12.1% in FY26
items.quote: In financial year '26, we have been able to improve our ROCE from core cement assets by more than 200 basis points, going up from 9.9% to 12.1%.

items.statement: Targeting better-than-industry volume growth in FY27
items.quote: We are aiming to deliver better than industry.

items.statement: Premium product share 24% in Q4, launching Weather 365, aggressive premiumization in FY27
items.quote: Trade percentage for the quarter was 67%, and our premium product share was 24%. We'll continue to drive the agenda of premiumization aggressively in FY27 as well.

items.statement: ED land attachment case proceeds reduced 90% to INR 93 crore, land released against bank guarantee
items.quote: The alleged proceeds of crime have been substantially reduced from INR793 crores to INR93 crores, which is nearly a 90% reduction. The ED has also ordered for the release of the entire land parcel by substituting the same with a bank guarantee of equivalent amount of INR93 crores.

items.statement: Internal cost reduction target INR 50-100/ton annually, adjusted cost down INR 100/ton YoY in FY26
items.quote: Internally, we will always keep looking to deliver INR50 to INR100 cost take-out on an annual basis going forward.

items.statement: Net debt INR 1,428 crore, net debt/EBITDA 0.46x, well below 2.0x threshold
items.quote: Our net debt stands at INR1,428 crore, translating to a net debt-to-EBITDA of 0.46x, which is well below the threshold level of 2.0x as per our capital allocation framework.

items.statement: Renewable energy capacity to reach 576 MW soon, share jumped to 47% in Q4
items.quote: We will also be commissioning 128 megawatts of RE capacity soon, which will take us to 576-megawatt renewable energy capacity. This will further increase our share of renewable power consumption and reinforce our commitment to sustainability.

items.statement: Guided FY27 AUM growth of 20-24% aided by new businesses scaling up
items.quote: In terms of AUM, we're confident of a 20% to 24% AUM growth, aided by new businesses that we've launched in the last few years as they begin to scale.

items.statement: Guided FY27 credit cost (loan loss to avg AR) of 145-160 bps, down from 165 bps in Q4
items.quote: We expect this to continue to trend down. The reasons I talked about earlier, which is winding down of 2-wheeler portfolio and in the MSME business being out of the woods by June'26.

items.statement: Guided FY27 ROA of 4.4-4.6% and ROE of 19-20%
items.quote: ROA came in as of fourth quarter at 4.6%. We continue to guide for 4.4% to 4.6%. Return on equity came in at 20% in the current quarter, we continue to guide for 19% to 20%.

items.statement: Guided FY27 opex to NTI improvement of 25-40 bps from current levels
items.quote: On opex to NTI, we expect to see continued improvement of 25 to 40 basis points from current levels.

items.statement: Expect MSME business to return to double-digit growth between Q2 and Q3 FY27
items.quote: We expect that it should come back to double-digit growth or the company growth momentum between Q2 and Q3 of FY'27.

items.statement: Expect captive 2W/3W portfolio to wind down to under INR 1,500 crores by September 2026
items.quote: This book will principally just wind down to less than INR 1,500-odd crores by September '26, it will lead to further improvement in GNPA and should result in lower credit cost for FY27.

items.statement: Not disclosing specific AI capex but investing heavily in talent (203 to 363 by June'27), compute, and use cases
items.quote: We are not pulling back any stops in investing whatever it takes in being front of the seat and center.

items.statement: Expect marginal NIM moderation in FY27 contingent on interest rate trajectory
items.quote: NIM, we expect marginal moderation. It's a little bit contingent on how interest rates play out, caused by geopolitical tensions.

items.statement: Consumer momentum strong; likely to cross 5 million loans in a month for first time
items.quote: It's very likely we'll cross 5 million-plus loans in the month. Our last peak was 4.6-odd million loans, and that was in festival period.

items.statement: Gold loans, tractors, CVs expected to grow faster than overall AUM; portfolio mix to remain stable
items.quote: There are a few businesses which are in nature, like gold loan financing, tractors, CV and so on and so forth. They may grow faster than rest of the business because of very, very low base.

items.statement: FY27 guidance contingent on easing geopolitical tensions and macro stability
items.quote: Of course, I must just flag that the FY27 assessment is based on expectations of easing geopolitical tensions and macro stability.

items.statement: Deploying 600+ autonomous AI agents across operations, DMS, HR, technology and risk in FY27
items.quote: In FY27, we expect to deploy 600-plus autonomous agents and across operations, DMS, HR, technology and risk.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 21-24% range for the year, with short-term volatility expected due to raw material cost increases
items.quote: You would remember, we always have given the guidance of 21% to 24% will be our operating EBITDA margin range.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin at 21.3%, within guided range; Q1 historically softest quarter due to cost profile
items.quote: if you now look at the Q4 of last year, we had a very high EBITDA margin of 26%. But if you look at my Q1 of previous years, you will see Q1 is always the softest quarter because of our cost profile.

items.statement: One round of calibrated pricing action taken end of March 2025; further pricing and cost optimization to protect structural margins
items.quote: We've already taken one round of pricing. Our cost optimization is on 24/7. So, we will try to mitigate any such impact.

items.statement: Volume growth of 7-8% YoY in Q1 FY26; rural portfolio high double-digit growth; premium brands double-digit volume and value growth; industrial business double-digit growth
items.quote: 7% to 8% volume growth is what we have delivered for the quarter.

items.statement: Signed MoU with HPCL to explore Re-Refined Base Oil ecosystem in India
items.quote: We have also signed an MoU with Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited to explore Re-Refined Base Oil ecosystem in India.

items.statement: Operating expense run rate expected to decline from Q1 FY26 level (INR 338 cr) as one-time employee costs normalize
items.quote: there are some one-time in this quarter. So, they will go away. So the future quarters should be lower than this.

items.statement: Targeting 1.5x IPM growth, translating to 12-15% revenue growth for FY27
items.quote: We continue to maintain that guidance, sir.

items.statement: Reaffirmed 1.5x IPM growth target for FY27, implying 12-15% revenue growth
items.quote: We are certainly targeting a 1.5x of the pharma industry growth. Currently the pharma industry is trending anywhere between 6%-7% to 8%-9%. So this is the window in which it is operating. And if I calculate 1.5x of that, it translates to anywhere between 12% to 15% right now.

items.statement: MAT growth of 12.2% per Pharmarack, outperforming IPM by 3.6%; Q4 growth 14.2% vs IPM 10.5%
items.quote: On a MAT basis, which is annual sales, the company has delivered 12.2% growth as per Pharmarack, outperforming the market by 3.6%. And this momentum accelerated further in the last quarter, which is Quarter 4, where the growth reached 14.2% against the industry growth of 10.5%.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin ~21%, PAT margin ~16%; Q4 EBITDA margin ~16%, PAT margin ~14%
items.quote: For the full year, FY26 revenue grew by approx. 7% to INR287 crores and operating EBITDA stood at close to INR61 crores with the margin of approx. 21%. At the profitability level, our profits from operations grew by 19% year-on-year to close to INR45 crores, reflecting a margin of approx. 16%.

items.statement: Price growth 6.5-7% vs industry ~5%; 92% portfolio outside NLEM allowing up to 9.9% price hikes
items.quote: Our price growth is little shade higher, which is at around 6.5% to 7% on the price side.

items.statement: No demand impact from Middle East situation; IPM grew 7-8% in Q4, company outperformed at 14.2%
items.quote: Clearly from a demand perspective, there is no impact of whatever is happening on the Middle East. Okay. So the demand remains secular as far as the industry is concerned.

items.statement: Top 10 brands 58-60% of sales, 9 of top 10 ranked top 5 in category; growth led by Gynaecology and Dermatology
items.quote: Our top 10 brands currently constitute approximately 58% to 60% of our total sales, depending on the quarter, providing both the scale and stability for the business. Importantly, nine out of these top 10 brands are ranked within the top five in their respective categories.

items.statement: Asset-light model, no significant capex needed for organic growth; cash >INR190 cr, can raise INR200 cr debt for acquisitions
items.quote: We do not require any capital beyond what we are spending in terms of growing our business. So any use of real cash that we have is only for inorganic strategy and not otherwise.

items.statement: INR40 cr buyback at INR250/share (16 lakh shares, no promoter participation); 200% dividend incl. 75% special; total cash return >INR66 cr
items.quote: Between buyback and dividend, the company shall be returning over INR66 crores to the shareholders.

items.statement: Execution risk primarily macro (new product market acceptance); internally confident on operational excellence
items.quote: One execution risk may be that we may go over-aspirational on certain products, but yet we want to give them a full try with our heart and soul so that we are able to achieve them. But we are not sure how those molecules will eventually emerge as a macro market.

items.statement: New product launches: 6 products + 3 SKUs in FY26; targeting 9-10 in FY27 (half legacy rejuvenation, half new in Gynae/Ortho/Derma)
items.quote: We had total of six new product launches and three SKUs, I mean the brand extensions. We intend to have similar number approximately 9 to 10 in this current year as well.

items.statement: MR count unchanged; Q4 growth driven purely by productivity improvement of existing field force
items.quote: Number of MRs continue to be same, there is no new addition of MR in the last quarter, which is under reference now. And productivity, the growth that you are looking at is pure play, productivity improvement by the existing MRs.

items.statement: Working capital cycle ~11 days, best-in-class; no change expected from productivity initiatives
items.quote: Working capital remains well-managed with net working capital cycle at close to 11 days, reflecting our continued focus on financial discipline and prudent capital allocation.

items.statement: Gross margin stable at ~64.2% FY26; minor 20-30 bps variation due to product mix/timing, no structural cost increase
items.quote: Our full year gross margins are largely in line, there has been minor change, but it is more or less 64.2%. Yes, about 20-30 bps, which is just a product mix issue, nothing more than that.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target of at least 25% YoY and order inflow target of INR 25,000 crores
items.value: 25% revenue growth; INR 25,000 cr order inflow
items.quote: Revenue should be at least 25% more than this year. And order book this year, we have secured around INR19,000 crores, you can see more than that, maybe INR25,000 crores is our target.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR 350-400 crores, up from INR 260 crores in FY26
items.quote: '27, it will be more. It will be around INR350 crores to INR400 crores.

items.statement: Current work-in-hand at INR 29,000 crores including INR 1,600 crores L1 and INR 3,200 crores secured in April
items.quote: Yes, we have included INR1,600 crores and another job is secured in April, INR3,200 crores. So put together it is INR29,000 crores.

items.statement: Pipeline of INR 70,000 crores including group (35-40%) and external opportunities in roads, highways, tunnels
items.quote: We can see that there are at least INR70,000 crores of job in pipeline, some in tender stage, some tender yet to be out and some we have submitted the tenders

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin of 15.1% boosted by INR 100 cr claim realization and provision reversals; sustainable margin 10-10.5%
items.quote: But this will not be a regular phenomenon. It will be around 10% to 10.5% going forward.

items.statement: Vadhvan port project delayed due to local issues; breakwater tender delayed with no visibility; payments from some state governments need caution
items.quote: Vadhvan project, as you know, we have been there for last more than a year because of local issues, which is beyond our control, things are getting delayed

items.statement: Data center division secured INR 3,000 crores from group; focusing on group opportunities; no tower manufacturing in T&D
items.quote: So far, it is around INR3,000 crores we have secured from our group.

items.statement: No fundraising planned; current funds sufficient
items.quote: No, I think we are okay with the fund what we have. So there is no plan as yet.

items.statement: Dividend delayed but to be declared within few weeks
items.quote: dividend was supposed to be declared, but there is some delay in our process. It is there. It will be declared very soon. Within a few weeks, it will be declared.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guided at 14-14.5% for FY27
items.quote: Margins between 14% to 14.5%.

items.statement: Capex of ~Rs 1,000 crore planned for FY27 including carry-forward, adding ~1.10 lakh MT capacity
items.quote: The Company proposes to commit capital expenditure of approximately Rs. 1,000 crore during the year, including carry -forward commitments from the previous year.

items.statement: Windows & Doors plant at Kanpur Dehat started production March 1, 2026; expects Rs 200-250 cr annual revenue at full capacity
items.quote: Once we achieve full capacity utilization, then it should be about INR200 crores to INR250 crores annual revenue.

items.statement: Agriculture demand picking up strongly in Q1 FY27 after PVC price correction; plumbing demand steady
items.quote: Now demand has started full force. There is no issue. Big demand now coming from agriculture segment.

items.statement: PVC prices fell ~Rs 34/kg (30%) in April 2026; current price ~Rs 81/kg; expects prices to rise due to weak rupee
items.quote: Current pricing around INR81 a kilo. And we anticipate that as rupee is going down and pricing will go up now.

items.statement: Gas piping: supplying pipe and electrofusion fittings to 3-4 gas companies; more orders under negotiation
items.quote: We got order from 3, 4 gas companies and more orders are under negotiation.

items.statement: Zero debt, strong balance sheet; no fund raise mentioned
items.quote: With its strong balance sheet, zero debt, expanding manufacturing base, technology leadership and diversified business model, the Company is confident of delivering improved performance in the coming year.

items.statement: Export target: grow plastic piping exports from $5M to $50M shortly; focus on piping systems (pipes + fittings) globally
items.quote: Our export business plastic pipe section is only $5 million. We are working first how to reach $50 million very shortly.

items.statement: FY27 disbursement target INR13,000 crore; AUM growth ~14% (net addition INR6,000 crore)
items.quote: For the current year, we are targeting that if this is a present position, then we may have a rundown of about INR7,000 crores for the entire year. So based on that, with a INR13,000 crores disbursement target that we have kept for the year, we should be having a net addition of about INR6,000 crores to the book in FY

items.statement: FY27 spread guidance 2.75%, NIM guidance 3.75% (conservative); current spread 2.8% after quarterly reset conversion
items.quote: However, again on a conservative basis, we therefore continue the guidance of 2.75% spread and 3.75% on the NIM for the FY '27.

items.statement: FY27 credit cost guidance 15 bps (conservative); FY26 actual ~10 bps
items.quote: And while it has been about 10 basis points for the current year as a whole. However, on a conservative basis, we would still like to continue with the guidance of 15 basis points, although we don't see any stress and it could well be below that by the end of FY '27.

items.statement: FY27 ROA target 2.4%, ROE target 18%+ despite IT cost increase
items.quote: So overall, next year, we hope to be able to maintain our ROA of 2.4%. And therefore, ROE might slightly be impacted because of the cost, but still it will -- we hope to have an ROE of 18% plus.

items.statement: IT project total outlay INR300 crore (INR100 crore capex, INR200 crore opex over 5 years); FY27 incremental IT cost INR40 crore (depreciation + opex)
items.quote: In INR40 crores is for the entire year because currently, the entire IT project was -- has a total outlay of INR300 crores, of which INR100 crores was capex, INR200 crores was opex spread over 5 years. So the depreciation will kick in mainly from this financial year, that is FY '27.

items.statement: FY26 disbursement INR10,531 crore (vs INR10,500 crore guidance); Q4 INR3,245 crore all-time high
items.quote: So first of all, in terms of disbursement performance as against the guidance of INR10,500 crores of disbursement that we had given for the entire year, the company has ended with a disbursement marginally in excess of that figure of INR10,531 crores, and this has been supported by consistent quarterly performance wher

items.statement: Portfolio yield 9.8% after quarterly reset conversion (85%+ of book) and 15 bps rate cut passed on; spread 2.8% maintained
items.quote: So now as -- on the entire portfolio, after giving the impact of this quarterly reset half -- 50 basis points to all our converted customers, as well as after considering the 15 basis points that we reduced in January, also, the entire book yield will come down to 9.8% and that also excluding the -- any reversal in NPA

items.statement: LAP share up ~2pp in FY26; self-employed non-professional (SENP) up, salaried down to 83-84%; incremental yield ~9.8%+
items.quote: Our incremental yield is also 9.80%-plus because that's the breakup post our change in our mix from housing to a little bit of non-housing LAP increases and all those things and also increased slightly from our self-employed segment, which has happened from our salary, which has come down from about 89% has come down t

items.statement: GNPA 0.85% (down from 0.87%); PCR up to 56% from 49%; BT-out INR400 crore in Q4 (flat vs Q3); 85%+ portfolio on quarterly reset reduces BT risk
items.quote: Overall, in Q4, we have seen a reduction in our overall NPA numbers also. So that also has brought down our GNPA number 2 below the last year number of 0.87%. So we ended with 0.85% in terms of our NPA numbers.

items.statement: Management budgeted 18% AUM growth for FY27 but will relook after Q1 given fuel price and monsoon uncertainties
items.quote: We have projected and budgeted 18%, and we'll grow at 18%.

items.statement: FY27 NIM budgeted conservatively at 8.5% despite expected cost of funds benefit from rating upgrade and equity infusion
items.quote: Interest margin, we have budgeted 8.5 only.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio guided at 26-27% long-term range
items.quote: we should be in the long-term range, it should be around between 26% to 27%.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance unchanged for now; will revisit after Q1 based on fuel price and monsoon impact
items.quote: The credit cost as of now, we don't see a big challenge there. But we will be revisiting the number after the first quarter result

items.statement: Industry CV sales growth expected to be muted in FY27; flat sales would be an achievement
items.quote: this year, we expect the overall growth to be muted. I don't see a big growth in this financial year.

items.statement: Tractor demand expected to decline in FY27 due to weaker monsoon forecast
items.quote: we expect the demand to come down a little.

items.statement: Passenger vehicle financing targeting >20% growth in FY27
items.quote: You will be able to see more than 20% growth in passenger vehicle.

items.statement: New vehicle financing proportion in disbursements at 15-20%, expected to rise 5-10 percentage points over next two quarters
items.quote: it's around must be around 15% now on yields 15% to 20% now. But it may not go to 30%, 35% of the proportion.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 NIM at 8.61% vs 8.25% YoY and 8.58% QoQ
items.quote: Our net interest margin in Q4 FY '26 was at 8.61% as against 8.25% in Q4 FY '25 and 8.58% in Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds was 7.2% in Q4; overall cost of liabilities fell to 8.59% from 8.69% QoQ
items.quote: The incremental cost of fund is not relevant because we've not borrowed much, but still it was 7.2%.

items.statement: Potential asset quality stress may emerge post November-December if monsoon is weak and fuel prices rise
items.quote: Post November, December only, we will see some stress.

items.statement: Expects 100-200 bps EBITDA margin improvement over coming periods, driven by internal efficiencies and gross margin gains.
items.quote: So I think on a similar trajectory, you can see that happen, for another 100, 200 basis points going forward over the coming periods.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR30-35 crore, primarily for welding consumables capacity expansion and maintenance.
items.quote: Our capex is generally in the region of approximately INR30 crores-INR35 crores for the coming year.

items.statement: No long order book; 80-85% of sales via distribution with quick cycles. Current inquiry levels in line with last 3-4 months.
items.quote: We don't have long order book periods. We normally have very rotating quick cycle period. I can tell you that so far it is in line with pretty much what we have seen over the last three-four months.

items.statement: Domestic demand tracking steel consumption/IIP; export demand healthy with order book and approvals improving, though Middle East dispatch delays occurred in March.
items.quote: So far this year, what we have seen is the order book, inquiry base, and approvals where we are set up, exports should do better -- should do well, should do better for the markets we operate in.

items.statement: Focus on high-end consumables (nuclear, wind, nickel), automation (robotics, cobots, laser), and Miller partnership for submerged arc welding equipment.
items.quote: We have added products that have nuclear approvals for consumables, and we are adding more and more consumables for the wind manufacturing industry, for high-end nickels, for all the special critical welding applications.

items.statement: Doubling volumes in 5-7 years would require INR100-150 crore capex for plant, machinery, and capability (ex-land).
items.quote: I will say anywhere in the region of INR100 crores to INR150 crores.

items.statement: Domestic market share estimated at 17-18% (+/- a few percent) in organized welding market.
items.quote: I think we believe ourselves to have anywhere in the region of approximately 17%-18% plus or minus a few percent in terms of market share.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected at high single-digit to low double-digit with EBIT margin in 14.75%-15.75% band and ~80% OCF to net income conversion
items.quote: Despite ongoing macro uncertainty, we expect to deliver high single-digit to low double-digit growth, supported by disciplined execution and increasing demand for AI-led transformation in FY27. From a margin perspective, we remain committed to operating within our target band of 14.75% to 15.75%.

items.statement: Pipeline expanded 38% YoY to all-time high with 69% AI-led; net new TCV $2.12Bn for FY26 (68% YoY growth) and $407Mn in Q4
items.quote: Across FY26, our AI-first strategy drove significant pipeline expansion; 38% YoY, with 69% of the pipeline now AI-led. Consistent conversion of this pipeline has resulted in a record net new TCV of $2.12 Bn, representing 68% growth over the prior year.

items.statement: Q4 EBIT margin 15.4% (+20bps QoQ); FY26 EBIT margin stable at 15.3% within target band
items.quote: Q4FY26 EBIT margin expanded by 20 basis points sequentially to 15.4%, while full-year EBIT margin remained stable at 15.3%.

items.statement: Strong AI-led demand driving 64% of Q4 wins; BFS Direct grew 17.4% YoY, Insurance 46.5% YoY; TMT softness expected to reverse
items.quote: Notably, 64% of our wins were AI-led, further reinforcing the central role AI is playing in driving client demand and deal conversion.

items.statement: Direct revenue 98.6% of total; Enterprise Applications 76.5% of revenue growing 14.8% YoY; ITO declining 21.6% YoY due to ATM scale-down
items.quote: Our Direct business continues to be the primary driver of growth. Direct revenues for the quarter were $456 Mn, crossing an annualized run rate of $1.8 Bn and contributing 98.6% of total revenue.

items.statement: Continued investment in Neo platform and AI stack including Theory & Practice acquisition; leadership hires in Insurance and CPG/Retail
items.quote: We will continue to strengthen our competitive differentiation through sustained investments in our Neo platform, with the integration of Theory and Practice accelerating the build-out of our AI stack.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 62 per share for FY26
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that the Board has recommended a dividend of INR 62 per share for FY26.

items.statement: Consolidated core EBITDA margins of Q4 FY26 (12%) seen as sustainable going forward
items.quote: Absolutely. Absolutely right. Absolutely right.

items.statement: MDF capex INR425 cr total; ~INR300 cr in FY27, ~INR125 cr in FY28
items.quote: I think INR425 crores was only on the MDF segment, out of which I think almost close to INR300 crores would be in the current FY and INR125 crores would be in the next FY.

items.statement: Plywood capex: Odisha plant ~INR130 cr, technology upgrades ~INR45-50 cr across plants
items.quote: In the Plywood segment on Odisha ply, the total cost will be around INR130 crores for Odisha plywood. And all the other plywood improvements would be around INR45 crores, INR50 crores, all plants put together.

items.statement: MDF Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 17% sustainable; plywood 10.4% sustainable if volume targets met
items.quote: On MDF, we are not worried about the margins. I think 17% is something we can sustain because whatever cost has increased, we've already passed on.

items.statement: Implemented price increases: MDF 15% (5%+10%), Plywood 4-5% in April 2026 to pass through chemical cost surge >50%
items.quote: To mitigate the cost pressure and protect margins, we implemented calibrated price increases of 5% and 10% effective from April. In the Plywood segment, the impact was relatively lower and the price revisions were in the range of 4% to 5% during the same period.

items.statement: Strong start to Q1 FY27; unorganized players disrupted by raw material cost surge and payment terms, benefiting organized players
items.quote: We have seen a strong start to Q1 FY'27, and we remain confident on sustaining this trajectory, supported by an improvement in margins.

items.statement: MDF value-added (pre-lam + HDHMR) >50% of revenue; plywood shifting to OEM/readymade furniture demand
items.quote: So, then that would be higher than 50%, but it's not -- we cannot give you the exact number for that. But that will be higher than 50%.

items.statement: Income tax search conducted Feb 26-Mar 2 2026; no demand/notice received; matter at preliminary stage
items.quote: A search and seizure operation was conducted by income tax department at certain business premises of the company from 26th February 2026 to 2nd March '26. As on date, no order, no notice of demand or penalty order has been received by the company for the said proceeding.

items.statement: Dubai entity (GMEL) impaired INR15.16 cr as exceptional item; all potential liabilities fully provided for
items.quote: We have disclosed a total of INR15.16 crores as an exceptional item representing impairments to our investment, financial guarantees, and advances to GMEL. This onetime adjustment is a proactive measure to safeguard our financial integrity.

items.statement: Net debt INR461 cr, debt/equity 0.52; may peak at 0.7-0.72 in FY27 then return to 0.5-0.6 range
items.quote: maybe for 1 year, we might peak out to maybe 0.7 or 0.72 debt/equity. And then again, we come back in the range of 0.5 to 0.6 the following year itself.

items.statement: PVC/WPC plant commercial production started April 2026; peak revenue potential INR75-80 cr
items.quote: Around INR75 crores to INR80 crores is the peak revenue we can achieve in the given capex.

items.statement: Furniture fittings JV to break even mid-FY28 after Phase 2 capex; current PAT loss INR50.8 cr (12M FY26)
items.quote: I think the year after this, somewhere in the middle of the year, we should reach a situation where the business starts breaking even.

items.statement: Effective tax rate guided at ~22% for FY27
items.quote: So, the effective tax rate is around 22% because we have in the Greenply, on the standalone, the tax rate is 22% and in our subsidiary companies, the tax rate is around 17%. So effective it will come to around 22%.

items.statement: Advances growth target 2-3% above industry credit growth for FY27
items.quote: So, in terms of vision for '26-'27, with respect to advances, we should be 2% to 3% over and above the credit growth of the industry.

items.statement: ROA target 1.65-1.67% for FY27, up ~10bps from FY26
items.quote: I think we should exit this year with at least 10 bps more in ROA, so we should be there between 1.65% to 1.67%.

items.statement: NIM expected stable in FY27 within narrow band of 5-10bps
items.quote: We expect the stable net interest margin for the current financial year '27 with almost in the same narrow band of maybe 5 to 10 basis points this way or that way.

items.statement: Opened 70 branches in April FY27, targeting 75 branches for the year
items.quote: In the first month, we have opened 70 branches. We expect an elevated operating expenses for the current year in the range of 15% to 18% over the last year.

items.statement: NIM improved to 3.74% in FY26 from 3.60% in FY25 (+14bps)
items.quote: For the year ended 31st March 2026, the net interest margin is 3.74%, which is 14 basis points more than the 3.60% whatever we reported in the financial year 2025.

items.statement: MSME demand driven by capacity utilization nearing 85%, CC limit usage rising
items.quote: You are able to see things reaching there and we could see many of these units are reaching their near capacity level, they are going for expansion, the utilization of the CC limit and all these things are happening.

items.statement: Gold loan per-gram lending capped at ~INR10,300 despite market price >INR15,000, providing cushion against 10-15% price drop
items.quote: So, when it went to that INR15,000, INR16,000 and all, we had continued to give at the range of around INR10,000 per gram, or not, we had never crossed INR10,300 or something like that.

items.statement: Gross NPA below 2% at 1.91% in Q4FY26 after 11 years; SMA 2% at 0.72% down from 1.59% in Q1FY26
items.quote: Our gross NPA % had reduced to 1.91% from 2.17% in the Q3 financial year '26. The gross NPA has come below 2% mark after 11 years.

items.statement: ECL circular allows adjustment through opening reserves with no P&L impact; Tier 1 >20% provides comfort
items.quote: Looks like the ECL circular has come. Looks like it has now asked the banks to adjust in the opening balance itself in the reserve so that no impact on the P&L.

items.statement: Third-party distribution limited to 1-2% of overall book; focus on branch-led business with 1,000 branches
items.quote: Our business through third-party on an overall bank book we envisage to be only between 1% to 2%. Hence our focus on secured products will continue for the year.

items.statement: Fee income to contribute 55-60% of other income in FY27, similar to FY26
items.quote: With respect to fee income to other income, we will be in the range of 55% to 60% as like last year, contribution of fee income to other income.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin target maintained at 30% plus/minus 1-2% for full year
items.quote: we've always maintained that we will endeavor to do 30%. Given what we know today of the business circumstances, plus/minus 1% to 2%, which we've always said, yes.

items.statement: Additional HFC capacity of 15,000 MTPA R32 on track for Q3 FY27 commissioning
items.quote: Our additional HFC capacity expansion equivalent to 15,000 metric tons per annum of R32 remains on track for commissioning in quarter 3 FY27.

items.statement: Dahej MPP debottlenecking capex targeted for Q3 FY27 commissioning
items.quote: Our Dahej MPP debottlenecking capex is progressing well and is targeted for commissioning in quarter 3 FY27.

items.statement: Chemours project on track for completion by end June or early July 2026
items.quote: The Chemours project is on track and expected to be completed by end June, early July.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals has robust pipeline and order visibility for FY27 with ~80% capacity utilization visibility
items.quote: as we look into FY27, we have visibility almost up to about 80% of our capacity utilization

items.statement: FY26 operating EBITDA margin expanded 992 bps to 32.6% driven by favorable mix and operating leverage
items.quote: Operating EBITDA more than doubled to INR1,082 crores with margins at 32.6%, an expansion of 992 basis points, reflecting a favorable mix and operating leverage.

items.statement: Able to pass on raw material inflation to customers with some lag; no material risk seen currently
items.quote: we've also been able to pass on a lot of these back to the customers. There could be some lag effect. But other than that, we are pretty confident of passing on the price increases to the finished product

items.statement: No demand destruction seen; agrochemicals seeing volume recovery with pricing lagging; CDMO demand robust
items.quote: we are not seeing any destruction of demand in our numbers as we speak now as well, right?

items.statement: CDMO portfolio balanced with ~50-55 molecules, half in late-stage/commercial, half in early stage
items.quote: we are working close to about 50, 55 molecules, half of them being in late-stage commercial and half of them being in early stages

items.statement: Monitoring Middle East volatility for raw material availability and logistics; no disruption seen so far
items.quote: We are closely monitoring and navigating the developments with agility, particularly given implications on energy prices, logistics and supply chain disruptions.

items.statement: Net working capital days expected at 75-80 days vs previous guidance of 90 days
items.quote: Going forward, the net working capital is expected to be in the range of 75 to 80 days versus our previous indicative guidance of 90 days of sales.

items.statement: Employee cost growth guided at 7.5-9% for FY27 after optimization completed
items.quote: I would model it in the range of between 7.5%, 8.5%, 9%, not more than that. We're very careful on maintaining it in that threshold.

items.statement: AHF plant commissioned in February 2026; commercial supplies commenced in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our AHF plant was successfully commissioned and commercial supplies have commenced during the last quarter.

items.statement: cGMP4 block commissioned for Fermion; Phase 2 (cGMP5-7) possible if volumes warrant
items.quote: cGMP4 was commissioned last quarter again, and you would see that or December, if I'm not mistaken. And you will see the revenue sort of kicking in this year

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA per ton guidance raised to INR 8,000-11,000 from previous INR 7,000-10,000
items.quote: So this year, our guidance is now up from last year, which is INR8,000 to INR11,000 a ton EBITDA.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA per ton of INR 9,000-12,000 in two years (FY29)
items.quote: And from 2 years from now, I think we are confident now that this range can be increased further to 9,000 to 12,000.

items.statement: Total committed capex ~INR 2,600 cr (INR 2,000 cr greenfield steel plant, INR 475 cr forging plant, plus internal/replacement)
items.quote: So the total capex that we have planned for the new steel plant is about INR2,000 crores. For the forging project, it is about INR475 crores which has been announced.

items.statement: Plans ~INR 1,200 cr equity infusion (INR 385 cr already in) and ~INR 1,200 cr debt; target debt/equity <0.75
items.quote: So roughly, we see about INR1,200 crores of equity infusion, out of which INR385 crores has already come in. About INR800 crores or so roughly equity and about INR1,200 crores of debt which will be raised.

items.statement: FY27 volume target 250,000-255,000 tons rolled products (vs 225,000 tons in FY26)
items.quote: And this year, we would like to cross 250, maybe 255 we target. But let's say, for your calculation, keep 250 in mind.

items.statement: Strategic shift to 30% non-automotive steel (railways, oil & gas, bearings, windmill, aerospace, defence) over 10 years; ingot casting to start small in FY27
items.quote: We have taken a strategic view that over the next 10 years, we will be about 30% non-automotive steel, 70% will be automotive steel.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton improvement driven by volume, cost cutting, process improvement; product mix change minimal in near term
items.quote: As I answered in the earlier question, the product mix, I don't see much of a change just now. So it is volume, cost cutting, process improvement.

items.statement: Seeking price increases from Q1 FY27 due to higher scrap prices; spreads protected by cost-pass-through in auto contracts
items.quote: And therefore, we are asking for a price increase from Q1, and we are likely to get those price increases in Q1. Those discussions are ongoing.

items.statement: Export strategy shifting to indirect exports via component manufacturers; targeting OEs and global forging majors for India sourcing
items.quote: Exports for us will be more and more indirect exports rather than direct exports.

items.statement: Dividend recommended at INR 3.50/share (up from INR 3.00 considered); Aichi raised stake to 24.9%
items.quote: Overall, seeing the confidence in the future, our Board decided to recommend a dividend of INR3.50 a share.

items.statement: Expects double-digit volume growth in India for next 5-10 years
items.quote: We are very bullish on the Indian market, and we believe the growth should continue in double-digits for the next 5-10 years at least.

items.statement: International business expected to grow at double-digit rates comfortably
items.quote: But if we do not have external issues, our growth should not be less than double digits comfortably outside or in the country.

items.statement: India CAPEX expected to be less than Rs. 500-600 crore in CY2026
items.quote: Our CAPEX will be less than Rs. 500 crore - Rs. 600 crore this year for India. It will be very low this year.

items.statement: Twizza FY revenue ~Rs. 800 crore; Crickley Dairy ~Rs. 160 crore
items.quote: Well, revenue was Rs. 800 crore for Twizza and about Rs. 160 crore for Crickley. So, about consolidated maybe close to a Rs. 1,000 crore between the two.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin improved 112 bps YoY to 23.3% consolidated
items.quote: In India, EBITDA margins improved by 112 bps, supported by operational efficiencies from strong volume growth and improved gross margins.

items.statement: India realization per case declined 1.5% YoY due to pack upsizing and selective price points
items.quote: In India, realization per case declined by a marginal 1.5%, primarily due to volume growth initiatives such as upsizing of packs and selective price point launches in targeted markets to onboard new consumers.

items.statement: Raw material inflation impact minimal for next quarter due to 6-month inventory cover internationally and partial cover in India
items.quote: We are completely covered for this quarter, and we are partly covered for the next quarter also.

items.statement: Strong demand outlook supported by favorable weather and market expansion
items.quote: What we are hearing, summer looks to be very good. A month has already passed, and the trends are looking very positive.

items.statement: Low/no-sugar products now ~63% of consolidated sales volume; dairy growing 60-70%
items.quote: In line with our focus on healthier offerings, the mix of low-sugar and no-sugar products increased to the level of ~63% of consolidated sales volume during the quarter.

items.statement: Transportation cost increase from higher oil prices is a near-term risk but absorbable
items.quote: The only thing which can affect us slightly, which you cannot stock, is the transportation cost. There will be some impact, but we will be more than able to absorb it.

items.statement: Interim dividend of Rs. 0.50 per share (25% face value) approved, cash outflow ~Rs. 1,691 million
items.quote: In accordance with our dividend policy, the Board of Directors has approved an interim dividend of 25% of face value, Rs. 0.50 per share, resulting in a total cash outflow of approximately Rs. 1,691 million.

items.statement: New plant payback period typically 3-4 years targeting 30% RoCE
items.quote: Normally we work on a 3-4 year payback. 30% RoCE.

items.statement: Aluminium can shortage and cost increase managed; cans <2% of volumes, secured supply
items.quote: Well, first aluminium cans sales is less than 2% for us. It is very small. Secondly, we have tied up a reasonable quantity to more than cover up our 2% volumes and even a little higher, so, we will be able to get cans.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected at minimum 15% YoY, similar to FY26, with upside if global conditions improve
items.quote: minimum we should be able to deliver this kind of a growth that we have done in this year and if the situation globally improves, it will only add on to our growth plans

items.statement: FY27 capex rephased to Rs 50-75 crore vs earlier Rs 192 crore plan, focused on pharma facility and aroma chemicals
items.quote: The CAPEX plan for this year would be I think anything between Rs. 50 crore to Rs. 75 crore, that is the plan. We would not like to spend anything more than that

items.statement: Core B2B business delivered 14% EBITDA margin in FY26 vs consolidated 11.9%, B2C drag of Rs 250-260 cr revenue
items.quote: Excluding the institutional and the B2C businesses, our core B2B operations delivered an EBITDA margin of 14% for the year

items.statement: Strategic shift to high-margin segments: pharma (PEGs, esters, coatings), agro, oil & gas, aroma, personal care, food; exiting low-margin consumer businesses
items.quote: The focus on food, personal care, pharma, cosmetics and also, animal health and nutrition. These are all high-margin areas which we want to focus on

items.statement: Middle East conflict creates raw material, supply chain and logistics uncertainty; El Nino may affect agro season; Saudi expansion on track despite geopolitics
items.quote: The ongoing conflict in the Middle East has created uncertainty across raw material markets, supply chains and logistics and this may have an impact over the coming quarters

items.statement: Strong project pipeline from last 12 months BD efforts; export growth driven by Latin America, Europe, SE Asia, Africa; North America entry for personal care and agro
items.quote: We see a good pipeline of projects, which our sales teams and business development teams have worked on in the last 12 months, and we should be able to see results from those initiatives

items.statement: Institutional/B2C business targeting breakeven or profitability in FY27 alongside divestment of loss-making low-margin products
items.quote: In FY27, we should look at breakeven or even profitability, along with the divestment of some lower-margin businesses or those that contributed to EBITDA losses

items.statement: No formal guidance given for FY27; management says focus on CASA, liabilities, ATS and SFB build-out
items.quote: I'm not going to -- we're not putting currently any guidance. But however, I can just provide a direction in what we were looking at.

items.statement: Cost of funds on core CASA book remains below 2%; ~300 bps advantage vs typical SFB; NIM target 8-10% for SFB
items.quote: Our cost of funds remained structurally low below 2% on the core CASA book, entering our SFB phase with approximately ₹2,800 crores of low-cost liabilities, it gives us a cost of funds advantage of approximately 300 basis points relative to our typical Small Finance Bank.

items.statement: Deliberate de-risking of digital payments: exited program-manager flows, paused UPI P2M onboarding, active clients down from 347 to 229; special review of product/process underway
items.quote: We have intentionally trimmed down on this segment as we recalibrate our approach, reflecting in our active client base declining from 347 in December'25 to 229 in March'26.

items.statement: No capital raise required for SFB launch per current business plan; CAR at 83% vs 15% regulatory minimum; fund-raise only if/when needed
items.quote: As things stand now, from a business projections perspective, we are technically not requiring to have capital. So our SFB launch is not dependent on any capital based on the business plan which we have drawn across.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at approximately INR200 crores, similar to FY26 spend of INR190 crores
items.quote: It will be largely in line with what we have incurred in the current year, approximately INR200 crores.

items.statement: FY27 capex of ~INR200 crores for greenfield expansion, automation, digitization and replacement capex
items.quote: So it is a combination of what you have said. Something will be obviously towards our greenfield because the customers have already announced their expansion plan. We need to cater that. Second is something will be towards automation and digitization also. The third will be a replacement capex also in terms of the exis

items.quote: See, the cost will be recovered fully with the lag, and there will be a denominator effect, which will be there, right? Because there is no percentage increases, whatever increase will be built in the sales, same amount will be built in the cost. So due to denominator effect, some marginal dip will see in the EBITDA al

items.statement: Existing plants running at ~80% capacity utilization; expansion backed by firm customer orders
items.quote: Regarding the capacities, our existing plants, they are running around 80% of capacity utilization at this moment. And the greenfields are in the different stages. items.statement: Customer model launch delays in Pune and Navagam caused front-loaded manpower costs; diversification across customers/products mitigates concentration risk
items.quote: And just to add also that in these plants, the customer has also postponed their project launch also model launch also. So it has gone delayed. But for us, as we said in the past also that we have to front load with manpower to make the skill and all that.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free since inception; ROCE ~40% in FY26; focus on ROCE over plant-level margins
items.quote: I'm also pleased to highlight that MSWIL continue to maintain a debt-free status since inception, supporting our preparedness for the future with a diversified powertrain portfolio, disciplined capital allocation and a steadfast focus on operational excellence.

items.statement: Manpower growth to normalize for ramped plants; new greenfield/brownfield expansions will require fresh hiring
items.quote: Look, at least for the plants that have already started and ramped up, they are now in a good way, and they should deliver better returns because they've been fully utilized and everybody has been trained over there. For some of the newer capex and new expansions, of course, they will, again, the same process would hav

items.statement: Management does not provide revenue or margin guidance for FY27
items.quote: Mihir, unfortunately, we do not give any guidance. But as I said, if you look at the last four quarters, the growth momentum is there.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin 24% and PAT margin 14%; FY26 achieved 26% EBITDA and 16% PAT margins
items.quote: I keep repeating, I just want to be cautious here, that we always maintain that we are happy with 24% EBITDA margin and 14% PAT margins.

items.statement: Acquired land for new campus in Indore; rent recovery expected in 9 years; 30-40% for own use, rest to lease
items.quote: We realized that the amount of rent we are paying today here in this campus, you know, the cost can be recovered in nine years if you put your own campus.

items.statement: No hedging policy currently; stopped hedging in January 2026 after inconsistent results
items.quote: Currently, as we speak, there is no hedging policy, we have stopped doing it starting January this year.

items.statement: 94% repeat business; 7% of FY26 revenue from new clients; 24 new clients added in FY26
items.quote: We have about 7% business coming from the new clients. And I think you have to understand in the services industry, a new client has a very long tenure.

items.statement: Receivables up Rs 22 crore due to Fortune 500 clients' 90-day payment cycles; provisions maintained
items.quote: They come up with their 90-day kind of a payment cycle, which is where the receivables have been increasing for us. But we don't anticipate any risk there.

items.statement: Promoters plan to dilute up to 3% by October 2026; sold ~0.5% in last quarter
items.quote: There is a public statement that we made in October where we said we will dilute up to 3% or we will pledge up to 3%.

items.statement: Dividend of Rs 1/share approved (50 paise regular + 50 paise special); 11% of FY26 PAT
items.quote: This year, the board has approved a regular dividend of 1 rupee per share, which is four times what we used to pay last year.

items.statement: Uniware expected to sustain double-digit growth in FY27; Shipway to grow double digits at a faster pace due to lower penetration and larger addressable market
items.quote: We expect Uniware to sustain double-digit growth, while Shipway should also grow double digits year-on-year at a faster pace, given its lower penetration and a larger addressable market

items.statement: Full-year FY27 operational profitability expected to be higher than FY26 despite near-term investments lowering adjusted EBITDA and PAT in next two quarters
items.quote: However, we remain confident of delivering higher full year operational profitability in FY '27 compared to FY '26

items.statement: Investments started in Q4 FY26 across sales & marketing, AI product development, mid-senior leadership, and AI tools; will continue for next two quarters impacting near-term EBITDA and PAT
items.period: Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27, Q2 FY27
items.quote: We have stepped up investments starting Q4 FY '26 focused on sales and marketing expansion, AI-led product development, strengthening mid- to senior leadership, embedding advanced AI tools across product and GTM and these investments will happen across both Uniware and Shipway

items.statement: Onboarded 450+ enterprise clients in FY26, strongest year ever; Q4 alone added 149 clients including Onida, Kenstar, Lacoste, Vedantu, Allen
items.quote: We onboarded 450-plus enterprise clients, our strongest year ever. These include several well-known names such as Onida, Kenstar, Action Tesa, Nayasa, Ajanta Shoes, Lehar Footwear, Himalaya Wellness, Rupa, Lacoste, SuperYou, Trunativ, Vedantu and Allen

items.statement: 40-45% of Uniware enterprise customers using quick commerce and B2B modules; 5-6% adopted UniReco within 3 quarters; 1-2% adopted UniCapture within a quarter
items.quote: 40% to 45% of our Uniware enterprise customers are now using quick commerce and B2B modules. 5% to 6% have adopted UniReco within 3 quarters of launch and 1% to 2% have taken up UniCapture within a quarter of its launch

items.statement: Price escalation clauses added to new customer contracts since last year; plan to incorporate into existing contracts going forward; benefit to show in subsequent years
items.quote: Having seen the success of price escalation being applied on the new customers, we now plan to incorporate this in our existing contracts as well. The impact or benefit of that will be demonstrated in the subsequent years

items.statement: Evaluating merger of Unicommerce eSolutions Limited and Shipway Technology Private Limited to improve operational efficiency, simplify structure, reduce compliance overheads
items.quote: We are currently evaluating the initiation of our merger process between Unicommerce eSolutions Limited and Shipway Technology Private Limited. The objective of this proposed merger is to improve operational efficiency, simplify our corporate structure and reduce compliance requirements and overheads

items.statement: No dilution planned for acquisitions; intend to leverage cash (INR81.3 cr) for M&A; ESOPs issued to existing and new mid-senior talent aligning incentives with growth
items.quote: Our intent is to not look at dilution when they're acquiring, but leverage most of our cash to be able to do this. In terms of issuing ESOPs to talent, we have issued ESOPs to both existing talent as well as new incoming talent

items.statement: NRR remains above 100% in FY26 excluding top-10 bucket churn; new client contribution to revenue steady at 7-8%
items.quote: NRR for the year was above -- so we have maintained that our NRR continues to be above 100%. We have -- in FY '26 as well, our NRR is above 100%, excluding the churn of this we saw in the top 10 bucket

items.statement: Shipway not EBITDA positive due to deliberate investments in sales, marketing, AI development to capture larger market; standalone Uniware adjusted EBITDA margin expanded from 25% to 37.5% in FY26
items.quote: So in this quarter, we are not EBITDA positive in Shipway because those are the investments we are doing in to drive growth. At the same time, in the stand-alone business, we have seen our adjusted EBITDA improved from 25% to 37.5% for the full year

items.statement: Cross-sell rate between Uniware and Shipway at 10%+ (up from <5% at acquisition); large addressable market for Shipway beyond Uniware base including Instagram sellers, B2C brands, drop-shippers
items.quote: We are already at a 10% plus cross-sell rate. But I also want to call out that beyond Uniware, there is a large market for Shipway, which consists of Instagram sellers, B2C brands, drop-shippers, who may not require Uniware platform

items.statement: FY27 ROA expected at upper end of 2-2.2% medium-term range, with ~10 bps compression from 2.3% FY26 ROA due to NIM pressure partially offset by opex and credit cost benefits
items.quote: We should be in the medium term range with a bias towards hitting the upper end of the medium term range in the ROA, which is our computation.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 NIM fell 12 bps sequentially to 3.8% due to 14 bps portfolio yield compression from lower acquisition pricing and higher-rate book attrition, partially offset by 4 bps COF benefit
items.quote: Net interest margin for the quarter dropped by 12 bps sequentially from 4% in Q3 FY26 to 3.8% in Q4 FY 26, largely due to moderation in net interest income as I explained above.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 yields expected broadly sideways with slight compression; COF to see marginal 2-5 bps benefit from borrowing resets and NHB refinance
items.quote: Yields in quarter 1 -- there would be slight compression. We'll see there also while cost of funds side also we'll see some marginal benefit of 3 to 5 basis points.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 spread compression expected as lower-rate new book replaces higher-rate attriting book, partially offset by opex efficiency and lower credit costs
items.quote: Through the year, we will see some contraction in the margin, which will get partially offset by opex efficiency and a partially offset by lower loan losses.

items.statement: Home loan industry growth at ~9.5%; company targets 21-23% AUM growth, driving faster non-home loan growth to maintain PBC compliance via assignment
items.quote: At a 9.5% IHL growth and if our ambition is to grow much faster than that, which we have put out at 21% to 23%, naturally the opportunity in the non-IHL will be better or higher.

items.statement: Sambhav (affordable/near-prime) AUM reached ~INR9,000 cr with ~70-30 affordable/near-prime mix; monthly disbursements INR410-425 cr, targeting INR600 cr+ monthly within 12 months
items.quote: So close to INR9,000 crores is the Sambhav AUM now roughly. The mix you asked for the mix of near prime and affordable. I have to do the mix. So I have to do the mix. I'll come back to you, Viral. Ravi will inform you later on.

items.statement: Geographical network expanded to 226 branches and 182 locations as of March 2026
items.quote: Geographical network of the company now spans across 226 branches and 182 locations.

items.statement: FY26 NIM moderation contained to 7 bps vs initial 15-20 bps guidance due to higher fee and assignment income
items.quote: Company managed NIM moderation to 7 bps as against our initial assessment of 15 to 20 bps on account of higher fee income and assignment income than planned.

items.statement: FY26 AUM grew 23% to INR140,000+ cr (upper end of guidance); PAT up 20% normalized; Opex/NTI improved to 19.7% vs 20-21% guidance; GNPA 27 bps vs 35-40 bps guidance
items.quote: All metrics were in line or better against the initial assessment as the company performed well across AUM growth, opex, asset quality and return metrics.

items.statement: Expect cost-to-income ratio between 40% and 50% going forward

items.statement: Yield expected to remain in 32-40 bps range, focus on PAT over yield
items.quote: We are comfortable with yields being in the range of 32 to 40. That's the range we look at, but we focus more on PAT.

items.statement: Investing in technology and digital platforms for regulatory compliance and investor experience
items.quote: There are some, which are related to technology investments that we've made to support the regulatory environment.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue yield improved to 39 bps from 35.5 bps due to expensive assets exiting and cheaper assets entering
items.quote: We believe that it is likely because of expensive assets going out of the system and replaced by cheaper assets.

items.statement: BER/TER structural change impact being evaluated; at worst neutral, at best may gain a couple of basis points
items.quote: At worst, we will be neutral on this, at best we probably may gain a couple of basis points.

items.quote: We are planning to do is actually set up sales teams dedicated to SIPs. So, we are doing that across five locations and we'll expand it further if needed. items.statement: Digital channel contributes 28% of AUM; launched digital campaign to reactivate paused SIPs

items.quote: ELSS as a scheme has SIPs in it, but because of the changes in taxes, that will see some challenges going forward across the industry.

items.quote: When you look from a B30 perspective, it is largely, Q4 mark-to-market impact, which has happened. Also, I'm sure you'll appreciate that when you look at the overall assets for us, it is predominantly dominated by equity.
