items.quote: The employee has increased, the branches has increased, and we have given a normal incremental rate. So that assumption is not correct, sir. This is the clarification.

items.statement: Q4 other expenses up 34-35% due to one-off NFO marketing, regulatory and labour code costs; expected to normalize
items.quote: There is a one-time expenses included, because we have a NFO in the last quarter, in fact in the March. So, some of the expenses, advertisement and marketing expenses related to that NFO and we are having a regulatory and other risk-related costs, which are one-time in nature.

items.statement: Expect high double-digit growth in seeds business in FY27 driven by combination of volume and price growth
items.quote: So I expect a combination of price and volume growth and expecting to deliver high double-digit growth again this year.

items.statement: Crop protection revenue growth likely double-digit in FY27 due to 15-20% input cost increase leading to 5-10% price increases; margins stable-to-soft
items.quote: So revenue growth probably will be maybe double digit. I don't know what it could be because our input cost has gone up by 15% to 20%. It is going to lead to price increase for sure. It will be 5%, 8%, 10%.

items.statement: Raw material costs increased 15-25% due to war-induced supply disruptions; company has announced price increases to pass on costs
items.quote: So we have seen 15% to 25% is generally the range.

items.statement: Below-normal monsoon forecast (92% LPA) and El Niño risk may cause 5-10% demand cuts for herbicides/insecticides; farmers may down-trade to lower-cost products
items.quote: Erratic patterns risk 5-10% demand cuts for herbicides/insecticides.

items.statement: Kharif demand uncertain; farmers will plant crops even in poor monsoon but may reduce premium seed and high-cost crop protection purchases
items.quote: Farmers will plant something. They might make different choices. They might also down-trade on the kind of seed they buy.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 standalone B2C gross margin softened due to liquidation of Clasto and Benzilla inventory; consolidated margin supported by CSM, SPH, exports and seeds
items.quote: On crop protection, stand-alone basis it was marginally down because, you know B2C business because of Benzilla and Clasto.

items.statement: Seeds margin outlook uncertain due to drying/processing cost volatility and recovery risks; full costing known by end of quarter
items.quote: I cannot predict that. But obviously, effort is when your business grows, cost would not grow in the same proportion, that should have positive impact on the margin.

items.statement: Focus on five strategic seed crops: cotton, maize, millet, mustard, rice; cotton grew 35%, maize 20%, millet 8% in FY26
items.quote: In the Seeds segment, our primary focus will be on five strategic crops: Cotton, Maize, Millet, Mustard, and Rice.

items.statement: B2C crop protection growth driven by herbicides (+15% YoY) and fungicides (+5%); insecticides down 3% YoY; SPH grew 27% in Q4
items.quote: On a yearly basis, our herbicide business is up by 15%, fungicide by 5% and insecticide is down by 3%.

items.statement: Middle East conflict escalation remains key risk for supply chains, crude prices, and basmati demand; below-normal monsoon and fertilizer availability add uncertainty
items.quote: The near-term outlook remains contingent on the evolution of the Middle East conflict.

items.statement: Building inventory for Kharif season by procuring raw materials early due to war risk; not building excess inventory beyond Kharif needs
items.quote: We did take some risk to build some inventory.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 results expected to be impacted by ongoing MENA conflict and export shipment suspension; recovery timing uncertain
items.quote: Factors contributing to Q4 muted performance persist and we expect its impact on Q1 results of the current year also.

items.statement: Abu Dhabi subsidiary holds order book of ~$180 million (~171,000 metric tons) giving ~9 months visibility as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: And as of March 31, 2026, the subsidiary holds an order book of approximately $180 million, which is close to 171,000 metric tons, giving a visibility of approximately 9 months of operations.

items.statement: All export shipments to MENA region suspended since March 1, 2026 due to force majeure from military conflict; no shipments from India or Abu Dhabi facilities until safety allows
items.quote: Consequently, all shipments from India and Abu Dhabi facilities in Middle East are suspended until further notice and further -- until safety conditions allow for safe passage.

items.statement: API monogram suspended for carbon seamless pipes after API audit nonconformances; auditors to revisit Nashik plant in May 2026 for verification; approval timeline speculative
items.quote: Auditors appointed by API authorities are scheduled to revisit our factory in Nashik in May 2026 for verification. Following this, the final approval to use the API monogram on seamless pipe is expected in due course. Given this, providing a specific time line for approval at this stage would be very speculative.

items.statement: Domestic water pipe demand remains at macro level; Jal Jeevan Mission fund releases to states underway but execution may take 1-2 months to reach reasonable pace
items.quote: We still feel that it might still take a month or 2 before the execution starts in a reasonable pace.

items.statement: Ductile iron pipe segment faces overcapacity; other segments (longitudinal, helical, seamless) well-placed with no overcapacity
items.quote: So, what we feel that in ductile iron pipes, there may be some oversupply in terms of capacities. But apart from this, other segments are well placed like longitudinal, helical as well as seamless.

items.statement: Stainless steel pipe margins (both seamless and welded) face challenges; improvement expected from H2 FY27 as company targets value-added upper-end segments
items.quote: So impact of that will come, I think in this year, the second half. So -- but otherwise, I must say that complete business of stainless steel will face the margin challenge.

items.statement: Seamless pipe segment margins expected to improve due to robust demand from ONGC deepwater exploration projects (~$20 billion)
items.quote: So, there will be improvement -- yes, there will be improvement in margins in seamless segment because we envisage that demand should remain robust and that will actually result into the little bit better margins.

items.statement: Balance sheet can handle increased debt for MENA expansions; long-term debt low (standalone INR525 cr, consol INR650 cr); lenders have appetite for project financing
items.quote: Yes, balance sheet can handle increase in the debt. Secondly, as you mentioned that in Saudi, we are not -- it's not 100% subsidy. We are -- we would be 51%. So, a proportionate -- at the best proportionate, let's say, impact would come.

items.statement: MENA conflict creating new pipeline infrastructure opportunities for oil, gas, water; India also fast-tracking gas pipeline rollout and ONGC announced $20B deepwater exploration
items.quote: We expect the countries in MENA region to invest significantly in the replacement and new pipeline infrastructure for oil, gas and water. Similarly, India will also need to invest significantly to work on energy security.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation from INR88.88 to INR94.84/USD in Q4 FY26 caused INR48 crore foreign exchange cost on dollar-denominated exposures
items.quote: Company also reported a INR48 crores foreign exchange cost during this quarter following the revaluation of U.S. dollar-denominated exposures. This was driven by the rupee's sharp decline over the quarter. It fell from INR88.88 per dollar to INR94.84 per dollar.

items.statement: CASA ratio target of 36% remains achievable; currently at 32.94%
items.quote: Why not? Piran, as you know, we are close to 33% now, right, 32.9%. We are almost 300 basis points up since we started this journey, right? If we can do that in 12, 15, 18 months, we have done that. There's no reason for us not to believe 36% is getable at some point, yes.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio guidance maintained at 53-56% range
items.quote: We had always guided that we will remain in this range bound in this 53%, 55%, 56% kind of range bound, we will remain depending on the quarter. It has some seasonality impact as well. Right now, we have, again, no reason to change our guidance on that.

items.statement: LCR comfort zone maintained at 115-120%; consciously reduced from 135-140% to protect NIM
items.quote: We are comfortable operating at 115% to 120%. In fact, we have consciously brought it down from earlier levels of 135%, 140% that we used to maintain earlier. That is also a NIM destroyer, right? Higher LCR than required is also a NIM destroyer.

items.statement: Plan to open ~100 branches in FY27 after adding 39 in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Now we have more comfort, and that's why you see in the last quarter alone, we have added over 30 branches, 39 branches in the last quarter. We think we will continue to be focused. As of now, we plan to launch about 100 branches in the next year.

items.statement: NIM expanded to 3.20% (+2 bps QoQ); further deposit repricing potential in Q1 and early Q2 FY27; multiple levers for continued NIM expansion
items.quote: There is still scope for deposit repricing. As we have earlier also guided that our deposit pricing goes into next -- I mean, the first quarter of this year as well as maybe early part of the next -- second quarter as well. There is some -- still some deposit repricing potential that is possible from here where we stan

items.statement: Full-year NIM declined only ~2 bps despite rate cuts; among best in sector
items.quote: If you really look at our NIMs of last year versus this year, full-year, if you just take the last full year NIM versus this full-year NIM, you will notice that we have just lost about 2 basis points in our NIM over the entire year basis. That's probably one of the lowest in the sector, right?

items.statement: CASA crossed INR 1 lakh crore to INR 1,03,390 crore (+8.26% QoQ, +21% YoY); NRE deposits crossed INR 1 lakh crore to INR 1,02,620 crore (+13.2% YoY)
items.quote: CASA balances crossed the INR 1 lakh crore mark to close at INR1,03,390 crores, growing 8.26% sequentially and nearly 21% Y-o-Y. Our NRE deposit, which is our moat, reached a significant milestone crossing the INR 1 lakh crore mark to close at INR1,02,620 crores.

items.statement: Low-yield book reduced from 52.2% to 49.8% YoY; mid-yield segment up ~2.5%; high-yield segments (cards, MFI, PL) growing
items.quote: If you look at our journey in the last, say, 1 year, March '25 to March '26, our low-yield book has dropped from 52.2% to 49.8% kind of numbers, right? It's about 2%, 2.5% movement. Our mid-yielding segment has moved by, again, similar number, about 2.5%, right?

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio grew 26% YoY and 9% QoQ; LTV below 54%; LAP grew 8% QoQ with acceleration expected
items.quote: Our gold loan portfolio delivered a robust performance once again, growing 26% Y-o-Y and 9% Q-o-Q. This momentum in gold loan growth has been maintained despite the fact that we were downsizing the book of a specific subsegment to ensure full alignment with the latest regulatory framework.

items.statement: Commercial banking grew ~6% QoQ and 26% YoY; CV/CE up 8.5% QoQ; agri and microfinance up 5% and 7.28% QoQ respectively
items.quote: Commercial banking grew nearly 6% Q-o-Q and 26% Y-o-Y, maintaining its position as a primary growth engine. Agriculture and microfinance both saw healthy traction, growing 5% and 7.28% Q-o-Q, respectively. Our CV/CE business saw a sharp uptick of 8.5% sequentially.

items.statement: Floating provision of INR 456 crore created for ECL transition buffer; not linked to asset quality deterioration
items.quote: Having said that, the fact that it's a onetime gain, we wanted to be conservative and create a buffer. This, we believe we can -- as per the draft guidance, we can use it during the ECL transition, which is around the corner.

items.statement: Cost of deposits declined 5 bps QoQ to 5.43%; cost of funds down 4 bps to 5.46%
items.quote: The steady improvement in our funding mix is materially enhancing our durability with the cost of deposits declining 5 basis points Q-o-Q to 5.43%. On advances, our gross advances closed at INR2,68,369 crores, up 3.65% sequentially and nearly 13% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Combined company revenue expected at $12.4 billion with 27% from innovative medicines, 51% from established brands, 15% generics, 6% biosimilars
items.quote: I think the combined company's revenues will be $12.4 billion. What's more important the innovative part of the business will from 20% moves to 27%.

items.statement: EPS accretive from day one of transaction close
items.quote: So we believe this will be EPS accretive from the beginning.

items.statement: Cost synergies estimated at $350 million over 2-4 years
items.quote: There are also significant potential synergies that could come out, which we have highlighted could be in the range of about $350 million which could be materialized in the next two to four years.

items.statement: Combined free cash flow generation of $2-2.5 billion annually
items.quote: both the entities together generating free cash flows of close to $2 billion, $2.5 billion on an annual basis

items.statement: Transaction financed with $2-2.5 billion cash surplus and balance via committed bank financing
items.quote: The financing is going to be partly out of our own cash surplus which could be in the range of $2 billion to $2.5 billion and the balance would be funded through the committed financing from our banks.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA of 2.3x post-acquisition; focus on accelerated debt repayment
items.quote: Sun from a net cash positive position post this acquisition will get into a net debt by EBITDA of 2.3x. However, with the strong focus that we have in terms of continuing to get cash generation, we are confident that we would be able to focus and accelerate the debt repayments.

items.statement: China market opportunity: Organon has $800M+ sales with 8 large brands growing single-digit; Sun to leverage platform for innovative products and in-licensing
items.quote: the current sales of Organon in China is more than $800 million and they have eight large brands which are also growing in a single-digit. It helps us to take this platform to the next level and potential to grow further.

items.statement: Biosimilar portfolio growing 13% CAGR (from $400M to ~$700M); $320B LOE opportunity by 2035 translating to $70B biosimilar market
items.quote: From 2021 the portfolio was $400 million is now grown to close to $700 million. But the future opportunity is even larger. So as you can see there are more than $320 billion patented drugs are losing LOE by 2035 which translate into an opportunity of $70 billion potential biosimilar market going forward.

items.statement: No major divestments required; negligible overlap between Sun and Organon portfolios
items.quote: there is a negligible overlap between Sun and Organon. It's a very negligible and the few product which we may have to divest, but other than that there is no major divestment required for the for the business going forward.

items.statement: Deal expected to close in 6-9 months subject to Organon shareholder approval and regulatory clearances
items.quote: we expect this deal to close in about six to nine month time.

items.statement: Organon gross debt $8.5B with ~$900M cash; net debt interest charge ~5.5%; Sun expects higher credit rating for refinancing
items.quote: currently the debt profile of Organon, they have a gross debt of about $8.5 billion and cash of close to $900 million. The net debt is having an interest charge of about 5.5%.

items.statement: Established brands business (51% of combined revenue) targeted for single-digit growth via line extensions and brand equity leverage
items.quote: I'm hopeful that the established product business which is stagnant today and not growing will also turn around and will start showing some single digit growth, yes.

items.statement: Organon has ~10,000 employees including 4,000 field force across geographies
items.quote: there are about 10,000 employees out of which 4,000 is in the field force. And these are spread across geographies including commercial field force which is marketing their innovative, biosimilars as well as established products across geographies.

items.statement: Management expects to hold EBITDA margins around 11.5% in FY27 despite strong headwinds from zinc and forex volatility.
items.quote: my sense is that we should be able to hold around the same region. But yes, these are turbulent times. It is -- some parts of it are in the unknown. But going into the new year, we are looking towards maintaining similar kinds as last year.

items.statement: Jammu alkaline battery facility commissioned with ~INR200 crore investment; peak capacity 360 million units annually; commercial production starting in weeks.
items.quote: With an investment of approximately INR200 crores, the facility has a peak capacity of up to 360 million alkaline batteries annually with a phased ramp-up planned over the coming years.

items.statement: Alkaline battery share targeted to reach 20-25% of India battery market in 3 years from ~15% currently; Eveready aims to exit at 20% alkaline market share.
items.quote: My sense is anywhere between 20% to 25% towards alkaline and 75% of zinc will be how the category will reposition itself.

items.statement: Jammu plant expected to improve alkaline margins vs imports; operational breakeven in Year 1, full payback in 5-6 years.
items.quote: the very movement allows some amount of margin decompression to happen. And as the plant starts improving in its overall production and absorbs those overheads, the margins will continue to improve over the next few years.

items.statement: Further price hikes in zinc and alkaline batteries possible in Q2 FY27 if cost ambiguity persists; already taken calibrated increases in FY26.
items.quote: If this ambiguity continues over this quarter as well, we may then need to look at the pricing again somewhere in quarter 2.

items.statement: Urban demand recovery seen in last 1-2 quarters; may face challenges if geopolitical situation extends beyond Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Currently, the trends for the last couple of months has been some amount of urban revival. If the situation carries on more than quarter 1, then we could see challenges.

items.statement: Noida Plot B1 sold for INR116 crore; Plot B2 expected to fetch ~INR136 crore; proceeds to be used for debt reduction.
items.quote: Total INR251 crores. So this is around INR116 crores, another is around INR136 crores.

items.statement: A&P spend to remain at ~10% of sales in FY27; tax regime transitioning to 22% (Section 115BAA) in FY27 subject to business loss utilization.
items.quote: We've been holding on to about 10% A&P and that will go through even in the new financial year.

items.statement: Zinc prices expected to remain elevated; rupee at INR94-95/$ and crude above $100 pose cost risks; calibrated pricing and hedging to continue.
items.quote: We expect this trend to continue into the next quarters as well.

items.statement: Flashlight BIS mandate implemented Jan 2026; expects market share gains from unorganized players in H2 FY27 as compliance costs rise.
items.quote: Our outlook on some of the rechargeable flashlights for the future taking away from the unbranded sector looks to be quite positive.

items.statement: Targets 20% EBITDA margin at reported level by end of FY27 (Q4 FY27)
items.quote: Despite these headwinds, our structural margin profile continues to expand in line with our guidance of 20% at reported level by end of the current fiscal.

items.statement: Expects Enterprise and Data Center segment to scale to 30% of revenues in FY27
items.quote: Looking ahead, with accelerating AI data center investments and pipeline visibility, we expect the Enterprise and Data Center segment to scale up to 30% of revenues in the current fiscal.

items.statement: FY26 order inflows more than doubled to INR 7,687 crores (up 109% YoY)
items.quote: In FY26, order inflows more than doubled to INR 7,687 crores, up 109% year-on-year as compared to INR 3,672 crores in FY25.

items.statement: Open order book at INR 7,309 crores (up 67% YoY), with INR 1,468 crores for Q1 FY27 execution
items.quote: Our open order book stood at INR 7,309 crores in FY26, up 67% from INR 4,378 crores in FY25, reflecting healthy order inflows and strong market confidence. Of this, INR 1,468 crores are slated for execution in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 15.1%; full-year FY26 margin improved to 13.2%
items.quote: Q4 FY26 revenue stood at INR 1,441 crores, reflecting strong 37% year-on-year growth momentum. EBITDA margins expanded to 15.1%, supported by scale benefits and better product mix.

items.statement: Does not sell in spot market; focuses on long-term contracts with select global customers
items.quote: We do not play in the spot market and we do not sell in the spot market. We are very, very focused on long-term contracts with our select customers globally, particularly in Europe and U.S. and in India.

items.statement: Launched Neuralis AI-DC portfolio, Hollow Core Fiber (35-47% lower latency), and 654E fiber; secured first commercial order for 654E
items.quote: The launch of India's first Hollow Core Fiber (HCF) cable marks a defining milestone in STL's innovation journey and reinforces our leadership in AI-ready digital infrastructure.

items.statement: Prysmian litigation appeal filed Sep 2025; two further appeal stages available; tariff refund process initiated in US but timeline unclear
items.quote: We had filed our appeal in September 2025. So that's where it is, that's progressing. As I said, we continue to believe we have a very strong case. And we do hope for a favorable outcome in that matter.

items.statement: QIP approval is an enabling resolution; no immediate funding requirement identified
items.quote: So this has always been an enabling resolution which we take year-on-year basis. So this year also, this needs to be considered as an enabling.

items.statement: Net debt INR 1,128 crores; debt/equity 0.5x; net debt/EBITDA 1.3x (target <1.2x)
items.quote: Net debt stands at INR 1,128 crores with debt to equity of 0.5x and net debt to EBITDA at 1.3x, comfortably below our earlier target of 2x with a revised ambition of moving below 1.2x.

items.statement: FY27 focus on sustained US FDA readiness at Gagillapur, scaling GLS commercial contributions, accelerating complex product shift, disciplined capital allocation, and preparing for potential US product launches including 9 applications await
items.quote: The focus in the year ahead remains unambiguous: achieving sustained U.S. FDA readiness in Gagillapur; scaling commercial contributions from GLS; accelerating the shift towards complex and differentiated products; and maintaining disciplined capital allocation.

items.statement: Raw material and freight costs rising due to West Asia situation; confident of price increases to compensate but timing uncertain; current inventories provide buffer for 1-2 quarters
items.quote: There's a small -- I mean, there is a little bit of uncertainty, but we are sure we should be getting price increases to compensate for the raw material increases.

items.statement: Finished dosages 74% of revenue; complex generics meaningful share of filings; 6 US ANDAs, 3 EU dossiers, 1 Canadian dossier, 15 other regional filings, 6 US DMFs in FY26
items.quote: Complex generics accounted for a meaningful share of total filings, reinforcing the long-term direction of the development pipeline and the company's focus on sustainable value creation.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR4,021M from INR7,061M in FY25; net debt/EBITDA improved to 0.34x from 0.75x; supported by INR6,656M equity infusion in FY26
items.quote: Net debt reduced to INR4,021 million from INR7,061 million in FY '25. Net debt to EBITDA improved to 0.34x from 0.75x. The reduction in net debt was supported by an additional equity infusion of INR6,656 million during FY '26

items.statement: FY27 net debt expected flattish or slight increase due to capex timing and working capital buildup from cost escalation
items.quote: There can be a flattish net debt or a slight increase, depending upon the timing of the capex and increase in the growth. In the current uncertain period, because of the cost escalation, the working capital investment is also going to be higher side.

items.statement: Working capital to sales ratio target maintained at 33% range for FY27 despite cost escalation uncertainties
items.quote: We would want to maintain our working capital to sales ratio of 33% range.

items.statement: Remediation spend FY26 ~INR50+ crores; FY27 remediation expenses substantially lower, already down in H2 FY26
items.quote: FY '27 onwards, it should be substantially lower, which has already come down Q3, Q4. The expenses were very high in H1. Cumulatively, only the remediation expenses we have incurred close to INR50-plus crores in the current year.

items.statement: GPI Virginia facility: IQVIA rank improved to 27th among US generic companies (from 74th in FY21), 4th in controlled substances; reached targeted operating potential
items.quote: I am happy to share that as per IQVIA, GPI as a company had moved to 27th position of all U.S. generic companies in terms of sales value in FY '26 as compared to 74th position in FY '21. It also stands at 4th position in the controlled substance space.

items.statement: FY27 AUM growth guidance of over 20% supported by urban finance, gold loans and rural franchise
items.quote: As we enter FY27, the first year of our 5-year strategic plan Lakshya 2031, we expect the momentum gain in FY26 to sustain, with AUM growth of over 20% supported by robust consumer demand in urban finance, gold loans and our rural franchise

items.statement: FY27 NIMs+Fees guided to remain stable in 10% to 10.5% range
items.quote: We expect our NIMs +Fees to remain stable in our guided range of 10% to 10.5%

items.statement: Target RoA of at least 2.8% by Q4FY27, achieving Lakshya 2026 goal with four-quarter lag
items.quote: by the last quarter of FY27, we are targeting to achieve a RoA of at least 2.8%

items.statement: Lakshya 2031 targets: Book growth CAGR 20%+, Credit Costs 2% or less, RoA 3.0-3.2%, RoE 16-18%
items.value: Book CAGR 20%+, Credit Cost <=2%, RoA 3.0-3.2%, RoE 16-18%
items.quote: We will attempt a Book growth CAGR of 20%+ over the Lakshya period. We will endeavor to drive Credit Costs down to a level of 2% or less. We will target to reach a Return on Assets in the range of 3.0% to 3.2%. We will strive to deliver a Return on Equity in the range of 16% to 18%

items.statement: FY27 branch expansion: 150-200 micro-loan branches, 150-200 micro-LAP branches, 400-500 gold loan branches
items.quote: we continue to plan setting up about 150 to 200 micro-loan branches, further 150 to 200 micro-LAP branches, and about 400 to 500 gold loan branches

items.statement: Gold loan branch deployment rate of 1 to 1.2 branches per day in FY27
items.quote: the rate of deployment of gold loan branches will be at the rate of almost 1 to 1.2 a day

items.statement: Q4FY26 NIMs+Fees at 10.47%, up 6 bps sequentially driven by yield optimization, fee improvement, liability management
items.quote: NIMs+Fees to 10.47%, a sequential increase of 6 basis points, largely driven by a sharp focus on yield optimization across businesses, fee improvement, and efficient liability management

items.statement: Lakshya 2031 opex-to-book ratio targeted at 3.75% to 4% range factoring tech and branch investments
items.quote: In terms of the Lakshya 31, the opex to book range, I think we are looking at a range of 3.75% to 4% range, primarily keeping in mind the investments that will be required

items.statement: Credit cost target of 2-2.2% by Q4 FY27 and sub-2% over Lakshya period
items.quote: Overall, at a balance sheet level, we still, we still sign up to that 2% to 2.2% corridor by Q4 FY27 and over the Lakshya period, sub 2% is what we are signing up on.

items.statement: Opex plus credit cost corridor revised to 5.75-6% for Lakshya period from current 6-6.5%
items.quote: Now we have moved that to a corridor of 6% to 6.5%. And during the Lakshya period, we expect that to be in the corridor of 5.75% to 6%.

items.statement: Plan to deploy 400+ gold loan branches and micro-LAP branches at rate of 1-1.2 branches per day in FY27
items.quote: So, the rate of deployment of gold loan branches will be at the rate of almost 1 to 1.2 a day.

items.statement: Disbursement yields higher than portfolio yields due to mix shift toward higher-yielding products like gold loans, micro-LAP, personal loans
items.quote: To your question on whether the disbursement yields are higher, it is yes, it is higher because of the change in mix which is happening.

items.statement: Two-wheeler monthly originations grown from ₹650 Cr to ~₹1,000 Cr with prime contribution up from 65% to ~90%
items.quote: prime throughput on our two-wheeler business while we have two-wheeler business monthly originations have grown from ₹650 Cr to almost ₹1,000 Cr, my prime contribution has gone up from about 65% to almost 90%.

items.statement: Stage 1 provision coverage permanently raised to 80 bps from 52 bps; Stage 3 PCR at 68% with overlays, targeting 60-65% long-term
items.quote: 96% of the portfolio which is in Stage 1, there we have actually enhanced the overall PCR from 0.52% to 0.80%.

items.statement: Cyclops underwriting showing early results: 2W 30+ DPD at 2.8% vs industry 7.1% at 10 months; similar trends in tractor, SME, personal loans
items.quote: our 30+ DPD portfolio at 10 months from the observation period is 2.8% where the industry average is 7.1%.

items.statement: Co-lending done selectively in personal loans; open to opportunities in home loans, SME, warehouse receipt finance at favorable terms
items.quote: Co-lending we do on the personal loan side, but on a very selective basis with only a couple of partners. Co-lending always remains on the plan for us.

items.statement: Expect to maintain or improve EBITDA margin in FY27
items.quote: We are very confident on maintaining or improving this EBITDA margin in FY '27. We are comfortable in maintaining that. Yes.

items.statement: Capex guidance increased to INR3,000 crores over next 2 years (FY27-FY28)
items.quote: Although we said INR1,000 crores earlier, now depending on the prospects what we need capacity and what projects in front of us, we are increasing our capex spend there. And we expect to spend around INR3,000 crores in the next 2 years.

items.statement: KRKA JV formulation facility Phase 1 completion by mid-2027
items.quote: Lastly, we are also spending on formulation facility under our KRKA joint venture in Hyderabad, and we expect Phase 1 will be completed by mid-2027.

items.statement: Affordable Medicines order book in place for FY27, expecting strong growth
items.quote: So for the next year also we have our order book pretty much in place. So we will continue to reflect a strong growth in the next year as well.

items.statement: Gross margin maintained at 60.4% for FY26, 61.4% in Q4; confident of maintaining gross margin despite solvent price pressure
items.quote: See, we are very comfortable to say we'll maintain gross margin for sure despite our challenges on the solvent price and all. We are confident.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 670 bps to 26.8% in FY26; Q4 at 28.9%
items.quote: EBITDA for the year stands at INR1,826 crores with a 26.8% margin, which is well in line with our broader outlook. For the quarter 4, EBITDA reported INR523 crores with a margin of 28.9% due to strong operating leverage.

items.statement: CDMO demand momentum strong; expect good growth in FY27 with possible quarterly lumpiness
items.quote: If you compare year-to-year, we expect a good growth in CDMO segment. There could be lumpiness quarter-on-quarter. But we don't expect any challenges for us to record the growth in FY '27.

items.statement: CDMO share grew from 13% to >30% in 6 years; ARV share fell from 67% to 41% while sustaining absolute sales
items.quote: Today, our share of CDMO business has increased from 13% 6 years back to over 30% right now. The contribution from ARV revenues come down from 67% to 41% in the current financial year, while sustaining absolute sales and global leadership in HIV therapy.

items.statement: ARV revenue to remain ~INR2,800 crores by FY30; CDMO to reach 50% of sales by FY30
items.quote: By FY30, we expect CDMO revenues in general will be 50% of our overall sales. And the ARV percentage will come down significantly. While the ARV sales remain constant, but percentage contribution will come down significantly.

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions may impact raw material availability and logistics, creating near-term OTIF pressure
items.quote: However, increasing geopolitical disruptions may impact raw material availability and logistics, potentially creating a near-term pressure on OTIF performance across the industry.

items.statement: Target ROA of 1.6%-1.8% by Q4FY27 (give or take 10 bps)
items.quote: we will be working towards seeing how we can gradually keep on improving the ROA towards the guided level of between 1.6% to 1.7% ROA by the exit of FY27, give or take 10 basis points.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 1.6%-1.7% by Q4FY27
items.quote: our guidance, we have mentioned was between 1.6% to 1.7% by the exit of FY27, which is by Q4FY27. And we will still endeavour to work towards that.

items.statement: Loan growth guidance of 14%-15% for FY27
items.quote: We are particularly aiming a growth of around 14% - 15% in the credit.

items.statement: NIM expected to improve 10-20 bps over next 2-3 quarters from 6.2%
items.quote: we do expect at least another 10 to 20 basis points of improvement over the next 2 to 3 quarters.

items.statement: PSL cost expected to reduce ~50% in FY27 and neutralize in FY28
items.quote: we are expecting that the PSL cost would come down by almost 50% to what we have incurred in FY26. That is our aim this year. Going forward, next year, it will be almost neutralized or coming to zero.

items.statement: NIM improved to 6.2% in Q4FY26 from 5.9% in Q3FY26
items.quote: NIMs improving to 6.2% up from 5.9% in Q3. The margin uplift was primarily driven by nearly a 23 basis points QoQ reduction in deposit costs, along with a 14 basis points improvement in advances yields.

items.statement: ECL transition impact estimated at INR 1,250 cr (INR 250 cr/yr for 5 yrs) based on Dec-25 portfolio
items.quote: based on the earlier draft circular in December 2025 portfolio, the transition that we expect is to be roughly around INR 1,250 crores, which as we are allowed to transition it or spread it over 5 years would translate to about INR 250 crores per year impact.

items.statement: No adverse collection impact seen in April from elections or Middle East conflict
items.quote: till now, there is no adverse effect on collection on account of, I would say, either election or middle east war. The collection efficiency, what Rajeev has stated is continuing.

items.statement: Dividend of INR 1.50 per share recommended for FY26
items.quote: the Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of INR 1.50 per share, subject to the approval of the shareholders at the forthcoming Annual General Meeting.

items.statement: Expects FY27 revenue growth similar to FY26 (18%) and EBITDA around INR 1,500 crores
items.quote: we are expecting the same revenue growth, which we are currently having in '25-'26 in the next financial year. And EBITDA growth will in line of growth in volume. So we are expecting around -- we can say INR 1,500 crores of EBITDA.

items.statement: Total PNG connections reached 1.1 million with 137,000 added in FY26; CNG stations at 705 (140 CODO)
items.quote: For the entire financial year '25-'26, we added about 137,000 new customers, taking our total household tally to 1.1 million.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA grew 5% to INR 1,225 crores; Q4 EBITDA up 13% to INR 310 crores
items.quote: EBITDA for the fiscal year 2025-'26 rose by 5% to INR1,225 crores.

items.statement: Calibrated price pass-through; prioritized consumer affordability over full cost pass-through during gas price spikes
items.quote: Price has been calibrated. We have not been able to pass through in the interest of a consumer while we maintained our reasonable profitability.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in West Asia disrupted gas markets; government priority allocation and pool pricing at $12.42/MMBtu in March 2026 mitigated supply risk
items.quote: For the month of March, the gas pool price was $12.42 per MMBtu.

items.statement: Gas sourcing for CNG: 85% from APM/HPHT/WG/contracts, ~15% spot market (Brent-linked and asset-linked)
items.quote: For CNG (T) so 85% of our volumes are met from the APM allocation plus HPHT and WG volumes and the different contracts for care. So balance around 16%, we are buying from the market on a spot basis.

items.statement: KFC underlying SSSG momentum of ~6% (ex-Navratri) seen in Q4 FY26 continuing into April FY27
items.quote: For the quarter, we delivered 4%, ex Navratri, 6%. So that kind of momentum we are seeing in April as well from an SSSG point of view.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 expected to be similar to FY26 (~INR 320 cr)
items.quote: When I look at the coming year, we see a similar number of capex, similar number in terms of the capex spend for FY '27 as well.

items.statement: Sri Lanka store expansion to accelerate to high single-digit to low double-digit annually for next 2-3 years
items.quote: we should be able to accelerate store expansion as well as in Sri Lanka, which would be anywhere between, let's say, a high single digit or low early double digits as well. So that's possible for the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: KFC restaurant EBITDA margin improved 110 bps YoY to 16.8% in Q4 FY26 on positive SSSG and operating leverage
items.quote: This, along with the operating leverage, which we generated out of positive SSSG, meant that we improved our restaurant EBITDA by 110 basis points, which came in at 16.8%.

items.statement: Consolidated restaurant EBITDA margin up 100 bps YoY to 13% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our consolidated restaurant EBITDA grew 21% year-on-year and margin was 13%, up 100 basis points.

items.statement: Vendor support offsetting gross margin impact of INR 99 meal; potential 50-70 bps gross margin headwind if support withdrawn
items.quote: As a result, we've been able to hold on to the gross margin. That's the reason. Having said that, if I look into the future and if the vendor partner support goes away, we expect the gross margin impact of anywhere or a gross margin investment of anywhere between 50 to 70 basis points.

items.statement: LPG price up 25-40% could hit EBITDA by 30-50 bps; Pizza Hut store closures <3% in April vs <5% in March; KFC zero closures
items.quote: the bigger challenge right now is the LPG price where the impact could be anywhere between 25% to 40% increase in terms of the cost, which could impact the EBITDA by 30 to 50 basis point.

items.statement: Merger with Devyani International expected to complete by end of FY27 (12-15 month process from Jan 2026)
items.quote: I would say it looks like by the end of this financial year, we should be in a position to consume the merger. That's the likely scenario by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: KFC marketing spend increased 75-100 bps of sales to support consumer recruitment strategy
items.quote: anywhere between 75 basis points to a 100-bps additional marketing spend we have put behind the brand.

items.statement: Sri Lanka Pizza Hut delivered 11% SSSG (15% LKR revenue growth) in Q4 FY26, 6th consecutive quarter of double-digit SSSG
items.quote: We delivered our sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit SSSG, along with healthy transaction growth.

name: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Ltd

items.statement: Targeting sustainable high-teen growth and mid-teen to high-teen ROE for FY27
items.quote: we are more focused on what is our Company's strategy and objectives, which is to have a sustainable high-teen growth, and a sustainable, hopefully mid-teen to high-teen ROEs.

items.statement: Retail loss ratio improved 3% YoY to 64.8% in Q4 FY26; full-year retail loss ratio improved 1% to 68.2%
items.quote: The retail loss ratio improved 3% YoY to 64.8% in this particular quarter for FY26.

items.statement: Combined ratio improved 2.3% YoY to 98.8% in FY26; expense ratio improved 30 bps to 30.1%
items.quote: improvement in combined ratio by 2.3% from 101.1% in FY25 to 98.8% in FY26. The improvement in combined ratio was further driven by improvement in both loss ratio and expense ratio.

items.statement: Annual price increases across all products; repricing ~80% of book from Q4 FY26 to Q1 FY27
items.quote: our strategy has been that we will take an annual price increase in all our products. We will continue to follow that strategy.

items.statement: New-to-insurance customers 94% of fresh additions in H2 FY26 vs 92% in H1; industry retail health grew 30.2% YoY in H2 FY26
items.quote: our new-to-insurance customers accounted for 94% of fresh additions in H2 FY26, as compared to an already healthy 92% in H1 FY26.

items.statement: Proprietary channels (agency + digital D2C) contribute over 90% of retail business; SME segment now 78% of Group Health vs 58% in FY25
items.quote: Our proprietary distribution channels, which are the agency channel and the digital D2C, now contribute over 90% of the retail business

items.statement: Digital investments: 95% fresh premiums collected digitally; app has 14M+ downloads, 1.5M+ MAU; platform modernization and AI deployment ongoing
items.quote: Acquisition and onboarding are now predominantly digitalized with 95% of all fresh premiums collected digitally.

items.statement: Marked-to-market equity loss of Rs 558 crore in Q4 FY26 (Rs 127 crore full year); adopting normalized 8% investment yield for reporting
items.quote: The geopolitical tension-induced correction in the equity markets led to a Rs. 558 crore marked-to-market loss during the quarter.

items.statement: Expect NEP growth to catch up as long-term policy sales unwind; volume retention ~86-87%, best in industry
items.quote: I think that's why the NEP growth will have a lag effect, but it will catch up in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Agent force target: 1 million agents in next 2 years (currently 8 lakh+); agent productivity up 37% on fresh, 18% overall
items.quote: We are confident of getting to 1 million in the next two years. We maintain this, that we will be adding 1 lakh agents every year for the next many years.

items.statement: Normalized PAT (8% investment yield) grew 45% YoY to Rs 1,222 crore; ROE expanded from 10.1% to 13.1% in FY26
items.quote: Under this normalized framework, our profit after tax increased 45% YoY in FY26 to Rs. 1,222 crore and ROE expanded from 10.1% in FY25 to 13.1% in FY26.

items.statement: IRDAI EoM regulations awaited; company operates within current guidelines; Bima Sugam platform supported as shareholder
items.quote: we await IRDAI's guidance on EoM. There has been some data that the regulator has asked which all of us have supplied.

items.statement: Fresh retail growth 38% YoY in Q4 FY26 (37% full year); policy count up 11% YoY in Q4, 8% full year
items.quote: Fresh retail growth on N basis for the quarter was 38% YoY. Fresh growth was driven by both value and volume as the number of Retail Health policies expanded by 11% YoY.

items.statement: Food volume growth target for FY27 is mid-teens (double-digit), with priority on top line over margins
items.quote: we would certainly want in FY '27 food volumes to grow in double digit, at least in mid-teens kind of number, which we are looking at

items.statement: Food business to remain EBITDA neutral till FY27, targeting INR 1,500-2,000 per ton EBITDA from FY28
items.quote: food will remain an EBITDA neutral till FY '27. And after that, we will try and build INR1,500 per ton to INR2,000 a ton kind of EBITDA in the food from FY '28

items.statement: Steady-state consolidated EBITDA per ton range guided at INR 3,500-3,600
items.quote: steady-state range, you can build around INR 3,600 a ton or INR3,500 for a safer side, you take it, I think we should be able to deliver within that range

items.statement: New Oleo chemical installation at Krishnapatnam expected by early Q4 FY27 to add volume
items.quote: our new installation coming up at Krishnapatnam by end of early Q1 of -- Q4 of '27 should be able to add more volume to this segment

items.statement: Edible oil complex prices rose ~10% in March, passed on to consumers; packing material cost up 10-15% but only 2-3% of overall cost, impact ~25-50 bps, price corrections expected by end-April
items.quote: the edible oil complex went up in the month of March, close to 10%. And I think that 10% of increased prices and every player has passed it on to the consumer somewhere in mid of March or end of March

items.statement: Alternate channel margin ~50-60 bps higher than general trade; overall margin ~1.5-2%, so 25-30 bps change significant
items.quote: the general trade versus this is hardly a 50, 60 bps lower than -- higher than the general trade. Because in our overall scheme of the things, the margin itself is 1.5%, 2%

items.statement: Quarterly AUM growth guidance maintained at 5-7% for FY27
items.quote: Our overall guidance remains unchanged at 5% to 7% on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: AUM could potentially double over next 3-3.5 years at current growth pace
items.quote: At the current pace of growth, the segment presents an opportunity to potentially double the book over the next 3 to 3.5 years.

items.statement: Branch network to stabilize at 275 branches in FY27 after adding 46 in FY26
items.quote: We expect to stabilize at 275 branches during the year, allowing us to consolidate and evaluate the performance of these investments before scaling further.

items.statement: Gold loan share may gradually move closer to 25% of AUM from current 21%
items.quote: Given the firm outlook on gold prices and addition in branches, this share of gold may gradually move closer to 25%.

items.statement: Portfolio mix between MSME and gold expected to remain stable at 75-25%
items.quote: Overall, the portfolio mix between MSME and gold is expected to remain stable between 75% and 25%.

items.statement: Spreads expected to hold at current 9% level with over 90% variable rate book
items.quote: We are expected to hold the spreads at the current level. More than 90% of the book is variable.

items.statement: Opex expected to decline by 20-25 bps through FY27 as new branches mature
items.quote: Our opex is expected to decline by 20 to 25 basis points through the year.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to remain range-bound at 1.38% with marginal 5 bps benefit possible
items.quote: We will continue to be cautiously optimistic and while we have a credit cost at 1.38%, we are expected to remain range-bound all through the year with some marginal benefits of 5 basis points here or there.

items.statement: Disbursement run-rate of INR 300 crores/month achievable when environment improves
items.quote: Can we move back to a number of roughly on an average of INR 300 crores a month? The answer is yes.

items.statement: Capital sufficient for 2 years growth to INR 18,000-19,000 cr AUM at 33% CRAR
items.quote: We are at 33% CRAR. If you just extrapolate on INR 11,000 crores, we can easily move 2 full years to around INR 18,000 crores to INR 19,000 crores.

items.statement: Co-origination disbursements at 16% of total, 18-19% of AUM; expected to remain at similar levels
items.quote: Co-origination disbursements account for 16% of total disbursements and 18% to 19% of AUM for last quarter, and we are expected to remain at similar levels all through FY27.

items.statement: No management overlay on provisions; only model refresh adjusting stage-wise provisioning
items.quote: We don't have any additional overlay. It's just the refresh of the model happens in March, and that refresh is reflecting on stage wise provisioning.

items.statement: Overall AUM growth guidance of 20-25% for FY27
items.quote: Yes, Meghna, so we've been giving an overall guidance last year also. And we said we will be a 20%, 25% AUM growth company, and we'll continue with that.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM growth of 20-22% even with flat gold prices
items.quote: But overall level, even if you have a flattish kind of a price play next year, we still should see a 20%, 22% growth on the AUM on the gold side for a flattish price.

items.statement: ROA improvement of 20-30 bps in FY27 over FY26 average
items.quote: So the trajectory will be in that direction. So if you're seeing a 20, 30 bps improvement on ROA, then at a PBT level, if I say 40 bps, that should come from credit cost or opex.

items.statement: Opened 148 new gold branches in FY26, will continue expansion in FY27
items.quote: As promised, we have opened 34 new gold branches this quarter, bringing our total to 148 new branches this year, and we will continue to expand our branches in FY27, too.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM reached INR10,352 crores, up 76% YoY with 12% tonnage growth
items.quote: Gold reached INR10,352 crores, an AUM growth of 76%, substantiated by a tonnage growth of 12%.

items.statement: Co-lending book at INR2,127 crores (21% of gold AUM) earning ~4% spread
items.quote: So our overall book under CLM is 21%, which is around INR2,100 crores. And that gives an AUM level spread of around 4%.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing hardening post-February; hedge rates on foreign currency borrowing up materially
items.quote: On the interest rate outlook, we saw cost of borrowing hardening post February as well as hedge rates on our foreign currency borrowing going up materially.

items.statement: Gold loan disbursements INR10,744 crores in Q4, up 37% QoQ and 135% YoY
items.quote: Gold disbursals for the quarter reached INR10,744 crores compared to INR7,853 crores in Q3 FY '26 and INR4,580 crores in Q4 of the previous year, indicating a growth of 37% and 135%, respectively.

items.statement: Doorstep gold loan AUM up 108% YoY to INR1,730 crores (17% of gold AUM)
items.quote: Our doorstep gold loan business continues to perform with an AUM increasing by 108% Y-o-Y to INR1,730 crores.

items.statement: Credit cost limited to 0.8% for FY26 and 0.7% for Q4; GNPA down to 1.9%
items.quote: We have limited our credit cost for the year at 0.8% and for Q4 at 0.7%.

items.statement: Raised INR450 crores subordinated debt in Q4; CRAR improved to 22.4% from 20.5% in Q3
items.quote: In Q4, we have raised a subordinated debt of INR450 crores, which has supplemented our capital adequacy by 3%. Consequently, in spite of the healthy asset growth, our CRAR at 22.4% as of March is up from 20.5% in Q3.

items.statement: ST LAP disbursements INR289 crores in Q4, up 39% QoQ; collections team doubled, internal issues resolved
items.quote: The ST LAP business has disbursed INR904 crores during this financial year and INR289 crores in Q4, reflecting a 39% increase quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance 0.15%-0.25% for FY27, below 0.3% by FY29
items.quote: We always intend to maintain in the range of 0.15% to 0.25%, and we are quite confident to maintain in this particular range just with a negative bias for the next year.

items.statement: Opex to average assets target 2.9%-3% for FY27 with lower bias
items.quote: As a percentage of the average asset opex over the medium term to take it below 2.85%, in the year 1, that is our current fiscal FY '27, we intend to keep it between 2.9% to 2.95% or 2.9% to 3%.

items.statement: NIM improved to 4.06% in Q4 FY26; expect further expansion from deposit repricing (53% of term deposits repricing in Q1-Q2) and CD ratio improvement
items.quote: NIM showing early signs of improvement and improved to 4.06% in Q4 FY '26 versus 4.01% in Q3 FY '26 and the same is attributed to reducing cost of deposit on repricing at maturity.

items.statement: Cost of deposits declined to 5.75% in Q4 FY26 from 5.86% in Q3 FY26; 53% of term deposits due for repricing in next 2 quarters
items.quote: Cost of deposit has started showing declining trend and stood at 5.75% in Q4 FY '26 against 5.86% in Q3 FY '26, that is a quarter back, backed by initial start of the deposit repricing.

items.statement: Healthy disbursements of ₹919 crores in Q4 FY26 (20% YoY) and ₹3,508 crores for FY26 (23% YoY); sustained demand across MSME, mortgage, agriculture
items.quote: Fresh disbursement stood at ₹919 crores during the quarter and ₹3,508 crores during the year, registering a robust growth of 20% and 23% year-on-year basis, respectively.

items.statement: MSME/business segment grew 9% QoQ and 46% YoY; LAP grew 5% QoQ and 19% YoY; agriculture growth moderate, limited to Punjab/Haryana
items.quote: The growth driver for the quarter is MSME/business segment, which grew by 9% on quarter-on-quarter and 46% on year-on-year basis followed by LAP, which grew by 5% on quarter-on-quarter and 19% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: ECL transition expected to be P&L neutral to positive; NBFC-MFI exposure small (₹5.49 crores net NPA) and fully provided; no fresh lending to NBFC-MFI
items.quote: Initial understanding, it will not be P&L negative. So we will be either P&L neutral or P&L positive with this ECL.

items.statement: Gross advances ₹8,687 crores (20.9% YoY); total deposits ₹10,018 crores (20% YoY); CASA stable at 34.7%
items.quote: As of March 31, 2026, our gross advances stood at ₹8,687 crores, reflecting sustained momentum in credit growth. On a year-on-year basis, advances grew by 20.9%.

items.statement: Yield on advances dropped to 10.8% from 11.1% due to 25bps rate cut and agri NPA interest reversals (7-8bps temporary impact)
items.quote: There was a 25 basis points rate cut coming in this particular quarter, which has slightly impacted the yield on advances. That is the point number one, but which may be affected the yield on advances by 10 to 12 basis points.

items.statement: Fee income target 0.85%-0.95% of assets for FY27 with upward bias; Banca income ₹9.5 crores, plan to add one new product in FY27
items.quote: We intend to make it between 0.85% to 0.95% also current year. The current year goal which we have taken for the other income number we have derived is 0.85% to 0.95% range, so with the upward biasness.

items.statement: PPOP for mature branches (5+ years) at 2.75%-3.25% vs bank-level 2.1%; Haryana CASA share identical to Punjab
items.quote: If I talk about the PPOP levels at the above 5-year branches, which is above 5 years, the same number remain presently is in the range of 2.75% to 3.25%.

items.statement: Volume and EBITDA growth target of 20% for FY27 once demand normalizes
items.quote: But once conditions stabilize , we still expect us to return on our targeted 20% growth trajectory, supported by our strategic initiatives and already available capacity.

items.statement: Cash flow generation target of INR 600 crores by 2027
items.quote: we were able to generate a cash flow of INR 333 crores exceeding our initial target of INR 250 crores and we remain on track for achieving our total target of INR 600 crores by 2027

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR 150-200 crores, funded from cash flows
items.quote: FY27, or in fact, even in the year later, I think our CAPEX strategy is now focused on our cash flows. So, what we are expecting is majority of or maybe 60-70% of our cash flows, we will put back into CAPEX. So, maybe INR 150 crores – INR 200 crores, something like that

items.statement: Capacity expansion of 1.2 lakh tons at Dadri by end of FY27, taking total capacity to 8 lakh tons
items.quote: From 6.8 lakh, it should be at least 8 lakhs. And with Sanand coming in, it might be 8.5 or 8.6, something like that.

items.statement: Order book of 30-40 days causing EBITDA hit from gas price spike
items.quote: we have a 30- to-40-day order book. So, although we have started getting that increase from our customers, but the 30- to-40-day order that we have has to go with that kind of cost level

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 7%, impacted by gas price spike of INR 4,000-5,000/ton in March
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR 80 crore, with a margin of 7%

items.statement: EBITDA per ton expected to normalize after 30-40 day order book rolls over
items.quote: After that it will return to normal. So out of 90 days I think at least 50 days of standard EBITDA we should get.

items.statement: Gas prices up 50% blended in Q1, up to 300% in some units
items.quote: Blended I would say would be at least about 50%.

items.statement: Steel price increases of 10-15% passed through to customers on fresh orders
items.quote: even today the orders I am booking are with an increase pricing considering all these increases that has taken place

items.statement: Demand sluggish across all segments except automotive; Q1 volumes at 80-85% of normal
items.quote: we are now expecting about 80 -85% kind of our volumes to be there. But other than volume, there is also an issue in demand as of now. Other than what I would say the automotive segment, all other segments that we see, we still see a lack of demand

items.statement: Product mix stable at 55% low carbon, 25% high carbon, 20% stainless; Speciality <3-4%
items.quote: I think 55 %-ish of low carbon, 25 high carbon and 20 percent stainless steel in general. This is the broad start process that we have and there has not been a major change here

items.statement: IHT Wire Phase II adding 6,000 tons capacity; March utilization at 25%, rising 10-15% monthly
items.quote: Phase- II of the expansion is also progressing as planned, adding 6,000 tons of capacity on the existing 9,000 tons

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (Iran-Israel) caused gas supply disruption, production cut to 35% in March
items.quote: Our production took a cut to 35%, which also had a short-term impact on our production schedule.

items.statement: Project portfolio average ADR to exceed INR10,000 by FY29 and surpass INR14,000 by FY31, nearly double current INR7,500 level.
items.value: INR10,000 by FY29; INR14,000 by FY31
items.quote: Our operating portfolio ARR stands at approx. INR 7,500, and as we commission more luxury properties through FY '29 and beyond, we project this to exceed INR10,000 for an average ADR by FY '29 and surpass INR14,000 by FY31, nearly double of what it is today.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR3,600 crores, with INR400 crores already invested by FY26; 60% debt-funded, 40% from internal accruals.
items.value: INR3,600 crores total; INR400 crores invested
items.quote: Our planned capex of approximately INR3,600 crores, of which INR400 crores has already been invested by FY '26, will be funded through a balanced mix of debt and internal accruals. Around 60% will be financed through borrowings with the remainder supported by internal cash generation.

items.statement: Courtyard by Marriott Chennai (45 keys) targeting Q3 FY27 opening; Kochi hotel rebranding from Four Points to Courtyard by Marriott in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: In FY '27, we will further strengthen the base with the launch of the Courtyard by Marriott in Chennai, World Trade Center, a 45-key hotel that complements our existing presence in high-demand business district of OMR in Chennai.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 37.5-38% excluding one-off GST 2.0 impact (1.4% in Q4) and property tax hit; utilities at 5.4% of revenue for FY26.
items.quote: If we weren't hit by these one-off cases and GST, then we would have also hit about 37.5% to 38%.

items.statement: Domestic demand robust at 73% of business (up from pre-war levels); international at 27%, expected to normalize to 30%; cancellations of INR7-8 crores in Q4 and April-June due to war.
items.quote: If you look at our mix now, I would say domestic business contributes about 73% of our overall business and international only the balance 27% or so, which was not the case before the war started.

items.statement: War-related cancellations of INR7-8 crores in Q4 FY26 and similar in April-June; gas supply disruptions managed via induction cooking and alternative fuels with no restaurant closures.
items.quote: We saw cancellations worth of about INR 7 crores to INR 8 crores for the quarter, which was about 5% of the business for the quarter.

items.statement: Internal accruals expected to contribute over INR1,000 crores in coming years driven by ARR growth and operating leverage from new assets.
items.quote: We expect internal accruals to contribute over INR1,000 crores in the coming years, driven by steady ARR growth and operating leverage as new assets ramp up.

items.statement: Gift City hotel adding 2-3 new F&B outlets leveraging liquor license advantage; no new supply expected for 3-4 years.
items.quote: We are going to invest a little bit of capex to add two more restaurants into this venue.

items.statement: Portfolio occupancy at 78% in Q4 FY26 (5 of 9 hotels in mid-80s); target to move average to mid-low 80s without compromising occupancy for ADR growth.
items.quote: In fact, if you look at quarter four, almost 5 of our 9 hotels had occupancies in the mid-80s. So we do believe that there is gap to move this average portfolio occupancy from 78% to somewhere in the mid to low 80s.

items.statement: Kochi rebranding expected to deliver mid-teens ADR increase; Bangalore hotels averaging INR9,000-9,500 ADR vs portfolio INR7,500.
items.quote: We believe that you should be able to get something in the mid-teens, a double-digit growth.

items.statement: Acquisition strategy open but selective; building from land remains core USP due to cost and time efficiency vs buying assets at higher per-key cost.
items.quote: Our strategy has always been to acquire the land, whether we buy it outright or we lease it, and then develop because there are very few people in the construction space of hotels.

items.statement: MICE event cancellations may return later in year but timing uncertain; F&B revenue declined 3% QoQ in Q4 due to large event cancellations.
items.quote: Yes, hopefully it should come back at a later part in the year. That yes, once things stabilize, hopefully it should come back, but honestly very hard to predict what will come back and what will get cancelled.

items.statement: Module line of 6 GW integrated expansion to be commissioned by end of calendar year 2026; cell line by end of FY27
items.quote: we expect to see the module line getting commissioned by the end of this calendar year and the cell line getting commissioned at the end of this financial year

items.statement: 6 GW integrated cell and module facility capex estimated at INR 4,500-4,800 crores; IREDA sanctioned term loan of INR 3,306 crores at 7.95% interest
items.quote: roughly give or take around INR4,800 Crores of capex spending on the 6 GW integrated line, INR4,500 crores to INR4,800 crores

items.statement: Ingot and wafer facility planned at 9 GW in phases: 5 GW Phase 1 in FY29, 4 GW Phase 2 a year later; capex estimated at INR 600-700 crores per GW
items.quote: we intend to set up an ingot and wafer facility of about 9 gigawatt integrating us fully in phases. And we plan to set up our first facility in FY29

items.statement: Order book grew to 9.4 GW in FY26 from 4.9 GW in FY25; Q4 FY26 order inflow was 1.27 GW; average order size for top 10 customers increased to 221 MW
items.quote: Our order book increased from 4.9 gigawatt in FY25 to 9.4 gigawatt in FY26. For Q4 FY26, order inflow stood at 1.27 gigawatt

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 34% from 31% in FY25; PAT margin improved to 21% from 16%; management says EBITDA spread remains resilient going into FY27
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded to 34% compared to 31% in the previous year

items.statement: DCR module pricing at INR 21-22 per watt; non-DCR module pricing at INR 14-15 per watt; management says pricing is resilient with no significant upward movement seen
items.quote: For DCR module, it is about INR21 to INR22 on a watt, and module is around like INR14 to INR15 per watt

items.statement: Demand outlook strong across segments; C&I fastest growing; ALMM List 2 implementation from June 2026 benefits integrated manufacturers; IPP demand expected to come under ALMM by FY28 or late FY27
items.quote: the demand outlook for a manufacturer like us has been strong. You can see that our Q4 inflow has been strong as well to the extent that we required

items.statement: FY26 capex of ~INR 650 crores spent mainly on two 2.5 GW module lines (Unit 5 in May, Unit 6 in Dec) and INR 311 crores for Devanahalli land acquisition
items.quote: largely this is capturing the capex of these two module production lines. And rest, land if you see almost INR 311 crores was the land acquisition for the expansion project

items.statement: ALMM List 2 deadline may face petitions for delay (as happened with ALMM 1), but management says a 1-2 month shift won't impact their DCR/non-DCR mix or capacity plans
items.quote: even like a small one-two month plus-minus will not really make a difference in what we intend to do because we've been cognizant of our capacities

items.statement: IPO completed in November 2025 raising INR 2,900 crores (INR 2,144 crores fresh issue); INR 1,621 crores used to prepay term loans; net debt to equity at -0.06x as of March 2026
items.quote: We completed our IPO and public listing in November 2025, raising INR2,900 crores, including INR2,144 crores of fresh issue proceeds

items.statement: FY27 focus: ramp up utilization across existing capacity, execute order book with discipline, progress 6 GW integrated expansion, strengthen TOPCon platform, maintain balance sheet discipline
items.quote: Our immediate focus remains clear: we will continue ramping up utilization across our existing capacity, we will execute our order book with discipline, we will progress the 6 GW integrated expansion as planned

items.statement: Management does not issue formal guidance
items.quote: No, Varun. We do not issue a guidance as such.

items.statement: Capex for CY2026 expected in range of INR 400-500 crores
items.quote: So, it will be in the range of what we had earlier, INR 400 crores to INR 500 crores investment this year.

items.statement: Export order book for CY2026 showing minimum 10% growth
items.quote: The order book for the year is solid, . Currently, it's showing 10% growth, minimum 10% that we are likely to register.

items.statement: Q1 CY26 EBITDA margin at 19.3%
items.quote: Our EBITDA, we brought in about INR 483 crores at 19.3% EBITDA, and the year-on-year growth has been 18.6%.

items.statement: Input cost increases from fuel price hikes; pass-through takes 6-18 months for full recovery
items.quote: We talk about the price excellence, that means we try to pass on the input price increases. It takes somewhere between six months to 18 months to have the full recovery.

items.statement: Automotive sector demand trend expected to remain robust going forward
items.quote: Clearly, we see that the automotive sector demand trend should continue the way it is, and we believe that it will remain robust going forward as well.

items.statement: Localization levels reached 80% overall, industrial bearings around 60%
items.quote: Almost 80% localization is our total revenue we are talking and not just industrial. Within industrial space, we might be around 60% or so.

items.statement: Supply chain headwinds from Middle East crisis impacting fuel costs and logistics
items.quote: We have been able to weather the headwinds and continue to deliver and create value for all our stakeholders.

items.statement: Industrial aftermarket saw demand slowdown due to liquidity crunch in distributor community
items.quote: We have seen a bit of demand slowdown in the aftermarket side of the industrial business, surely. And there appears to be a liquidity crunch in the market as a result of which the cash flows to our distributor community has been impacted in this quarter.

items.statement: Q1 CY26 capex spend moderated to INR 80 crores (3.1% of sales)
items.quote: Talking about capex. As I said, we had marginally reduced the investments, but nevertheless, close to INR 80 crores still continue d to be the investment within the quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 19.1% for Q1 CY26
items.quote: Overall, the consolidated resul t, INR 2,585.6 crores revenue, 19.1% on the EBITDA, registering a 15.6% EBIT margin at a consolidated level.

items.statement: Fuel costs (LPG, propane) increased due to Middle East supply chain disruption
items.quote: So, LPG, propane and some of the fuel items, which India relies heavily on imports has been impacted and the prices definitely have gone up there.

items.statement: Export growth outlook for CY2026 upgraded to 10-12% from earlier 5-10%
items.quote: And very likely, if we go run rate of the full year, we will be close to 10% to 12%.

items.statement: E-axle localization Phase 2 underway with supplier development for local sourcing
items.quote: We are already into the Phase 2 of our localization activity. One of the important steps that we are also working on is the local supplier development to start to source locally and cut down our imports as we move forward.

items.statement: Competition intensifying in industrial bearings leading to portfolio recalibration
items.quote: Well, that is one of the reasons as well that we see our competition is also intensifying their activity within India. And hence, it is important that we recalibrate our portfolios as well.

items.statement: Expect 20% volume growth and 5% price-driven growth in FY27; volume growth 15-20% minimum annually
items.quote: Out of the 25%, we are expecting 20% volume growth and 5% increase in prices. Between 15% to 20% should be our volume growth minimum every year.

items.statement: Value-added product mix rose from 52% in Q1 to 62% in Q4 FY26; target 66% by end of FY27
items.quote: We've already reached around 62% at the end of quarter four, and we are planning to get this up to 66% by the end of next year.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg reached 62 in Q4 FY26; management targets sustaining 5% EBITDA margin (60-65 per kg at current copper prices)
items.quote: EBITDA per tonne, 5%, comes to about 62 rupees. I'm looking at 5%, and current market prices of copper, it comes to about 60 to 65 rupees.

items.statement: Pass-through mechanism for copper price increases to finished products; additional EBITDA per kg not fully passed on; need more value-added products to improve margins
items.quote: We have a pass-through mechanism of the copper prices to the finished products. However. Passing on the additional EBITDA per tonne is a little bit of a stretch.

items.statement: Lead recycling dropped for next 1-1.5 years; focus remains on copper value-added products and plastic/aluminum byproduct recycling
items.quote: Lead recycling, for the time being, we have dropped it. At least for the next one, one and a half years, we are not looking at lead.

items.statement: Targeting commercial start of TOPCon upgrade by February 2027 with 2-month ramp-up to full capacity
items.quote: We have already started on this project and it seems that by February 2027, which is less than one year from today, we will be able to upgrade the line and start commercial production.

items.statement: TOPCon upgrade capex estimated at INR 250-270 crores for 150 MW capacity addition
items.quote: We are expecting as of now that it will cost around INR 250 to INR 270 crores for this upgrade.

items.statement: Confirmed order book of INR 1,161 crores as of Q4 FY26 with 40% cells and 60% modules, book-to-bill 1.02x
items.quote: On the order book front, we closed Q4FY26 with a confirmed order book of INR 1,161 crores with cells contributing around 40% and modules contributing 60%.

items.statement: Current cell realization at 13-13.5 cents/watt, module at 22-22.5 cents/watt; TOPCon DCR pricing around 14 cents/watt
items.quote: In line with what we have shared on the previous call, the cell realization is around 13 to 13.5 cents per watt and the module realization is around 22 to 22.5 cents per watt peak.

items.statement: Strong demand from PM-KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar schemes; no demand issues currently; ALMM List 2 mandate from June 2026 supportive
items.quote: As of now our focus is on DCR market. So we are largely concentrating on PM-KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar. And we are not facing any demand-related issues as of now.

items.statement: Module sales increasing (highest ever in Q4), causing EBITDA margin compression; future expansions to be integrated cell+module
items.quote: Module margins are structurally lower than cell margins and definitely as in Q4 we've reported our highest ever module sales, the overall EBITDA has been impacted because of that.

items.statement: Technology transition risk managed via phased expansion; TOPCon to Back Contact shift expected to take 2+ years; keeping equipment flexibility
items.quote: We are keeping ourselves safe, so that even if that comes within say the next 2 years' timeline, we will be able to adopt that as well.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh 4 GW integrated facility targeting June 2027 for first 2 GW phase; land and execution planning underway
items.quote: I think June 2027 is what we are targeting.

items.statement: Currently funding expansions through internal accruals; will raise debt later to minimize debt component
items.quote: At some point of time, definitely we would have to raise some amount of debt, but the idea is to use our current surplus to get down the debt component as much as possible.

items.statement: Expecting full run-rate utilization across all lines in coming quarter; cell utilization currently above 90%
items.quote: As we move into the coming quarter, we expect to approach full run-rate utilization across all our lines.

items.statement: Ingot/wafer backward integration targeting June 2028 ALMM List 3 deadline; MOU signed with Linton for technology and training
items.quote: The target is that by the deadline of June 2028 ALMM-III, we will be completely ready.

items.statement: Depreciation policy updated: TOPCon equipment at 8 years, Mono PERC at 3 years (down from 12 years)
items.quote: We've already reduced the useful life for the new equipment which is the TOPCon to 8 years and for the Mono PERC we are maintaining it at 3 years.

items.statement: FY27 production guidance 11-11.5 million tonnes and sales 10.5-11 million tonnes
items.quote: With that context, our production plan for FY 27 is 11 million to 11.5 million tonnes and sales between 10.5 million to 11 million tonnes.

items.statement: FY27 capex allocation INR 7,500-10,000 crores for sustenance and expansion
items.quote: Our guidance has been fairly clear that we will be allocating INR 7,500 crores to INR 10,000 crores to our capital expansion programs or sustenance capex as we call it.

items.statement: Remaining capex under current program INR 11,545 crores
items.quote: During FY26, we have invested a further INR 9,574 crores out of the total planned capex program of INR 47,043 crores. Along with the INR 25,924 crores already invested up to FY25, the remaining capex under the program is INR 11,545 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA per tonne INR 10,093 vs INR 10,482 FY26 full year
items.quote: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was INR 2,647 crores and an adjusted EBITDA per tonne of INR 10,093.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 coking coal prices expected to increase $20-25 per tonne sequentially
items.quote: For Q1FY27, we expect coking coal prices to increase by $20 to $25 per tonne sequentially.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 blended ASP increased INR 4,743 per tonne sequentially
items.quote: The blended ASP has increased by INR 4,743 per tonne on a sequential basis.

items.statement: India steel demand projected to grow 7.4% in 2026 and 9.2% in 2027
items.quote: the country continues to assert itself as the world's fastest-growing major steel market with domestic demand projected to expand by 7.4% in 2026 and accelerate further to 9.2% in 2027.

items.statement: Australian mine shaft closed, impairment INR 1,433 crores standalone and INR 834 crores consolidated; no further write-offs expected

This quarter, we have closed the shaft, and the reserves are no longer accessible, although we still have the license. Accordingly, we have recognized an impairment of INR 1,433 crores which equates to USD 159 million in the stand alone business and INR 834 crores, which equates to USD 93 million in the consolidated

items.statement: Leverage metrics expected to normalize by Q2 FY27 with net debt/EBITDA 1.66x and debt/equity 0.43x as of March 2026
items.quote: As of 31st March 2026, consolidated net debt was INR 16,019 crores with a net debt to EBITDA of 1.66x and debt to equity of 0.43x. With the ramp-up of new capacities and corresponding improvement in operating cash flows, we expect leverage metrics to normalize by Q2FY27.

items.statement: Rail rakes program: 72 of 79 rakes delivered, remaining in 2-3 months
items.quote: So, we are at about, I think our rail rakes program was about 79 rakes. We had about 72 rakes and the remaining rakes are also very soon getting delivered. So, I think in the next 2-3 months, we should be all in.

items.statement: Iron ore prices expected to move +/- INR 100-150 per tonne monthly; difficult to predict beyond that
items.quote: It is plus/minus INR100, INR150 here and there. So that is how it moves. But anything beyond that is very difficult to articulate on.

items.statement: No delays in capex execution seen; infrastructure program rolling out supports 9-9.5% market growth
items.quote: I think it is fairly healthy. I think I indicated towards a 9%, 9.5% market increase that we are expecting. And with the kind of infrastructure program that we are rolling out, we do not see any issues on that side.

items.statement: FY27 deposit growth guidance 9-11%, advances growth 11-13%, CASA ~40%, CDR ~80%
items.quote: Coming to the guidance, we are giving deposit guidance between 9% to 11%. Advances growth of between 11% to 13%. CASA, approximately, we will maintain around 40%. CDR around 80%
