So, that's why I'm giving guidance between 3.10% to 3.25%. ROA also, I'm giving some guidance between 1.20% to 1.30%. Credit cost, we'll maintain less than 1%. Slippage ratio, we'll maintain less than 1%.

items.statement: FY26 NIM 3.24% down 17bps YoY; Q4 NIM 3.23%; expects pressure from elevated cost of deposits
items.quote: NIM, if you see for the quarter, it is 3.23%, but if you see annually, it has come down from 3.41% to 3.24%, so 17 bps decline. We have given guidance of between 3.15% to 3.30%, so we have maintained that.

items.statement: Cost of deposits expected to remain elevated as advance growth outpaces deposit growth, pressuring NIM
items.quote: I don't see further rate cuts, but cost of deposit, I expect that it will remain elevated because advance growth is outpacing deposit growth. So, I see some pressure on the NIM.

items.statement: Credit growth outlook tied to GDP growth; expects to grow 1-2% below industry while protecting NIM and asset quality
items.quote: Growth, I believe country, government, and RBI, as you must be seeing in the newspaper also, they will take all measures to sustain the GDP growth. So, if GDP growth is intact, I believe credit growth will also be intact. If there is some headwind on the GDP growth, of course, then impact will come on us.

items.statement: Jewel loan growth may moderate in FY27 after strong FY26 driven by gold price increases
items.quote: But one thing why I am giving guidance of 11% to 13% in advance, let me tell you, around 16% to 17% of my book is jewel loan. And last year, jewel loan, because of the increase in price, we have seen good number. So, maybe similar kind of growth, we may not see in jewel loan this year.

items.statement: Sanctioned pipeline of Rs 51,000 crore; sanctioned but unavailed term loans Rs 34,000-35,000 crore
items.quote: We have a pipeline of Rs 51,000 crore. And not much stress we have because of personal loan, we don't have much, only Rs 6,500 crore.

items.quote: Two, three sectors, Sushil ji. One, green, you see, already green is everywhere, battery also, EV also, then solar power also. Transmission line also. I think this year transmission line we will see lot of this government PPP. And then data center, data center also we are seeing lot of demand in data center. I think last year road sector has been little slow, but we may expect this year some tract

items.quote: guidelines came only yesterday, and few things they have added. So, whatever we have calculated in the draft guidelines, I think impact will be a little higher than that. See, I can give some number, but that will not be very relevant because ultimately, next meeting, you will say, s

items.statement: Made Rs 310 crore standard asset provision for West Asia crisis prudently; no stress seen in SMA data
items.quote: We have made some provisions, although we are not seeing any stress because of the West Asia crisis, but we have made a provision of around Rs 310 crore keeping this crisis in view. But, as I told in the SMA data, we are not seeing any stress. This is purely prudently we have made this so that in case something happens, then we will have some cushion.

items.statement: No floating provisions held; standard asset provisioning ~Rs 500 crore this quarter; ECL impact assessment ongoing
items.quote: So, in NPA, in fact, we are not holding any floating provision, NPA whatever we are making only a specific account-wise provision. items.statement: Limited pricing levers: 50% loan book linked to external benchmark, MCLR formula-driven; focus on mid-corporate segment (Rs 50-500 cr) for better pricing
items.quote: If you ask me, very frankly, very few levers are left because see, almost 50% of loan book is linked to external benchmark. We have hardly any lever on that. Then only one thing remains, we take benefit of IT and try to, I mean, at l

items.statement: Retail term deposit rates cannot be reduced due to high bulk deposit rates; some banks increased retail term deposit rates in March
items.quote: No. See, retail term deposit also, we are not able to reduce any rate of interest on that. Because bulk is at elevated level, then you cannot keep very wide gap between retail term deposit and bulk. So, because of that, even retail term deposit will remain at this level. Or maybe a few of the banks you have noticed, in March few of the banks have increased retail term deposit rates.

items.statement: Digital spend budget roughly equivalent to employee cost
items.quote: Choksey ji, let me answer it in a relative manner, the budget will be more or less equivalent to the human cost, that means the salary and all those things we are paying to our employees. So, in that way you can definitely correlate.

items.statement: Treasury profit expected Rs 1,000-1,200 crore in FY27; AFS reserve swung from +Rs 400 crore in Q3 to -Rs 200 crore in Q4
items.quote: And still I expect that around, for the year I am saying, maybe around R s 1,000 crore, R s 1,200 crore profit we will earn through treasury.

name: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd

items.statement: Expect strong power demand growth in FY27 with peak demand rising further from recent 256 GW
items.quote: We believe that FY27 will see a strong growth in overall power demand as well as peak demand.

items.statement: Target INR 50,000 crore EBITDA conservatively by FY2031, potentially FY2030 if no issues arise
items.quote: So, Bharat Bhai, we should be in a position to achieve INR50,000 crore conservatively by FY 2031.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 near INR 25,000 crore and FY28 near INR 33,000 crore for expansion
items.quote: In FY26-27, we are adding Korba Phase-II of 1.32 GW, and, capex for FY26-27 will be near about INR25,000 crores, for our expansion. For FY27-28, it will be near about INR33,000 crores.

items.statement: Total expansion capacity tied up under long-term PPAs now stands at 13.3 GW including 1.6 GW Maharashtra DISCOM LOA
items.quote: With this, our total tie-up expansion capacity now stands at an impressive 13.3 gigawatts.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA INR 6,498 crore up 27% YoY; continuing EBITDA INR 5,573 crore up 9% YoY
items.quote: Reported EBITDA was INR6,498 crores, up 27% year-on-year versus the EBITDA for Q4 last year.

items.statement: New Maharashtra PPA tariff INR 5.30/unit comprising INR 4.11 capacity charge and INR 1.19 energy charge
items.quote: As regards to the tariff is concerned, it is INR5.30/unit, which consists of INR4.11 as the capacity charge and INR1.19 as the energy charge.

items.statement: Power demand revival from March with peak demand reaching 256 GW; FY27 expected strong growth
items.quote: Peak demand has recently reached 256 gigawatts, and it is expected to rise further in the current year.

items.statement: 95% of 18.15 GW operating capacity tied up under long/medium-term PPAs; merchant capacity reduced to 5%
items.quote: 95% of our operating capacity of 18.15 gigawatts is now tied up under long-term and medium-term PPAs.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation impacting labour and LPG availability causing conservative approach on Mahan commissioning
items.quote: Because of this ongoing geopolitical situation, which is slightly impacting the availability of labour and the availability of LPG, we are taking a conservative approach.

items.statement: Raised INR 7,500 crore secured NCDs in recent quarter; also raised interim funds from banks as corporate debt
items.quote: During the recent quarter, we successfully raised INR7,500 crores secured non- convertible debentures. We also have raised interim funds from banks in the form of corporate debt.

items.statement: Korba Phase-II 1.32 GW commissioning between June-September FY27; Mahan Phase-II 1.6 GW first unit Q4 FY27, second unit H1 FY28
items.quote: Korba will get commissioned something between June to September. The first unit will be in the second quarter of this year, and the second unit will get commissioned before the year-end. And as regards to Mahan is concerned, Mahan's first unit is likely to get commissioned in the last quarter of this year.

items.statement: Weighted average cost of borrowing currently about 8% from domestic capital markets and banks
items.quote: So recently, the rate getting from the market, is about 8%,and its either DCM or from domestic banks.

items.statement: Nuclear power SPVs incorporated; awaiting government rules notification before elaborating on capacity or timeline
items.quote: So far, the government of India has not notified the rules. So, we are only getting ourselves ready as and when the rules come, which will give us clarity on the type of size of capacity and how we will proceed.

items.statement: Bangladesh receivables outstanding reduced with regular payments; expert appointed for undisputed amount reconciliation
items.quote: As regards to collection is concerned, the outstanding has gone down. And therefore, we are getting regular payments from the Bangladesh.

items.statement: Jaiprakash resolution plan: Adani Power as implementing agency to take over 180 MW asset and 24% JPVL stake
items.quote: There is one asset within JAL, which has a small capacity at 180 MW. So that will be taken over by Adani Power as the implementing agency. Apart from that JAL is having 24% shareholding of JPVL, i.e. Jaiprakash Power Ventures.

items.statement: FY27 residential bookings guidance over INR39,000 crores, a 20% increase over FY26 guidance
items.quote: In financial year '27, we hope to grow residential bookings to over INR39,000 crores through the launch of a large number of exciting new projects combined with strong sustenance sales.

items.statement: FY27 collections guidance over INR24,000 crores, a 20% increase over FY26
items.quote: We expect to grow collections by 20% to over INR24,000 crores.

items.statement: Targeting 20% ROE by FY28 through faster execution and project delivery
items.quote: We remain extremely focused on delivering our return on equity target of 20% by financial year '28 by stepping up our speed on execution and project delivery, which will create rapid growth in operating cash flows as well.

items.statement: Added INR42,100 crores of future sales potential in FY26, achieving over 200% of guidance with 59% YoY growth
items.quote: Godrej Properties added INR42,100 crores of future sales potential through portfolio addition, achieving over 200% of guidance and delivering year-on-year growth of 59%.

items.statement: INR1,500 crores pending milestone-linked payments for FY26 BD deals
items.quote: Only some milestone-linked payments are pending. So around INR1,500 crores is what is pending for the deals which we have signed in '26.

items.statement: Imputed EBIT margin ~24.5% in FY26, slightly lower due to higher JV contribution (88% economic interest vs 93% prior year)

items.statement: Construction cost impact from Middle East conflict estimated at 5-6% max, translating to 0.1-0.2% quarterly margin impact, manageable via price hikes over 2-3 years
items.quote: I would say, give or take, cost impact would be between 5% to 6% at max. Again, in some projects could be even lower. From a margin point of view, again, project to project could differ. But give or take, every quarter, this is going to be something like 0.1% to 0.2% of margin impact.

items.statement: NCR sales dip in FY26 due to launch delays (Gurgaon approvals, Ashok Vihar); expect recovery to >INR10,000 crores in FY27 with key launches

So a large acquisition in Gurgaon that we've done. Unfortunately, we're not able to get the approvals within the year. That is now slated to be a Q1 of this financial year launch.

items.statement: AI disruption concerns overdone; Bangalore residential and office demand strong, supported by global capability center growth
items.quote: Our view is that the worry that AI is somehow going to lead to core residential demand is probably a little bit overdone. As we've seen both -- not only in terms of residential demand, office demand itself has been very strong and any slight softness in the IT sector has actually been more than made up so far in global capability center demand.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty (Middle East conflict) caused ~INR1,000 crores sales impact in late March; demand slightly better now but remains cautiously optimistic
items.quote: give or take, we could have probably done INR1,000-odd crores more and would have loved to even actually deliver 20% growth last year. That was sort of an internal target.

items.statement: Volume growth compounded at 20% over last 5 years vs 40% total sales growth; expect roughly equal split between volume and value growth going forward
items.quote: if you look at the last few years, Puneet, the volume growth over the last 5 years has compounded at 20% a year, excuse me, against the total sales growth of nearly 40% a year. So volumes have been a meaningful contributor. So I would exp ect a roughly eq ual split perhaps between volume and value for the overall growth

items.statement: No immediate plans to monetize annuity portfolio (INR230-250 crores share of ~INR1,000 crores potential); may consolidate share instead

items.quote: Board of Directors have recommended a total dividend of Rs. 60, which includes final dividend of Rs. 30 and a special dividend of another Rs. 30, this is subject to approval of shareholders.

items.statement: Busy Infotech FY26 billing was Rs. 170 crores with normalized growth of 43% YoY.
items.quote: In FY26, in total, we did Rs. 170 crores of billing. The normalised rate of growth that we have had year-on-year which excludes the impact of the change in the payout structu re that we have introduced is 24% and 43%, respectively.

items.statement: Silver monthly churn increased to ~7% from 5-6% pre-COVID; Silver annual churn increased to ~4% from 2-2.5%.
items.quote: Monthly side used to be 5% to 6%. Now we are running at 7%, about 2% per month we have deteriorated. And if you take the month-on-month decreasing value, I think 15% lesser retention, and this is pre -COVID versus post-COVID.

items.statement: Buyer verification (OTP/email) caused ~1% drop in traffic-to-enquiry conversion in recent months.
items.quote: So we are starting to do more buyer verification also, and that is leading to probably 1% of drop in the conversion from traffic to this.

items.statement: No guidance on net paying supplier additions until multiple quarters of continual success.
items.quote: So we'll continue to have no guidance on the net adds until we have multiple quarters of continual success.

items.statement: ARPU growing at 8-9% currently; price hikes take 1-3 years to fully reflect in ARPU due to rolling application to new subscribers.
items.quote: Currently, since the customer growth is hardly 1 - 2%, so most of the growth is coming from ARPU which is growing at 8 - 9%.

items.statement: Export business collections grew to Rs. 60-70 crores from Rs. 20-25 crores when purely domestic.
items.quote: So export, again, as we started sometime around 2020, become a separate business altogether with almost Rs. 50 - 60 crores of collections. It was always there even when we were purely domestic at maybe Rs. 20 - 25 crores, but now it has become Rs. 60 - 70 crores of business.

items.statement: Geopolitical events (war) and pricing pressure causing prolonged pain in SME gross additions.
items.quote: It took longer than what we expected, especially in March when the war also broke out. Otherwise, generally, February and March typically do a better job, which could not happen. So hopefully, this is going to continue a little longer with the pain in the market.

items.statement: EBITDA margin band updated to 23-25% after railway acquisition, down from prior 24-26% core business band
items.quote: We had already said that it will be 23 to 25 % after the railway acquisition. So that is the band. 24 to 26% is the band prior when we, the core business. I think now it is 23 to 25%, and that, I think we can say we should be able to continue being in that band.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin 24.4%, down 2.7% YoY due to 1.9% PLI base effect and 0.8% from product mix and commodity inflation
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was 311 crores, which is a growth of 32%. The EBITDA margin was 24.4%, which is lower by 2.7% compared to the same quarter last year. In this, there is a base effect of 1.9% due to fully PLI income accrued in the fourth quarter. Bala nce 0.8% impact is due to product mix and commodity price inflation

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 24.7%, down 2.7% YoY mainly from product mix change and higher fixed costs
items.quote: EBITDA for the year was 1,107 crores, which is a 13% growth. Margin was 24.7%, which is lower by 2.7% compared to the same period last year, and that's mainly on account of change in product mix and then to some extent, higher fixed costs.

items.statement: Commodity inflation (steel, aluminum, copper, freight, packaging, energy) pressuring margins; part not passed through and lag in pass-through will continue to impact margins foreseeable future
items.quote: Over the last 5 months, all major commodities for us, steel, aluminum, copper, have continued to move up. This has been further amplified by a sharp increase in freight, packaging, and energy prices. Frankly, almost everything linked to petrochemicals has become more expensive. And while a large part of this commodity inflation is pass through, 1) some parts are not passed through, and 2) there is

items.statement: Commodity price inflation impact on margins split roughly half from product mix and half from commodity lag; prices still trending up so impact continues until stabilization
items.quote: So, Gunjan, this 80 bps is actually almost half for the mix and half for the commodity prices, and, you're right, most of this would be, for the material price, and, that is a pass-through with a lag, so it is largely because of the lag effect. but you als o have to recognize that the commodity prices continue to trend up, so it's not as if, you know, this has stopped. So, if the prices stabilize

items.statement: Electrification momentum strengthening globally: EU BEV sales +45% YoY in March, India electric cars +65% and 2W +45% YoY in March, both >50% in April; North America best monthly BEV run rate since US subsidy cuts
items.quote: So in March, BEV sales grew by nearly 45% year on year in the EU. In India, electric cars and two -wheelers grew 65% and 45%, respectively year on year, in March. And both are trending above 50% in April as well. So we think it's a sustained trend of electrification growth across the board. Even North America saw its best monthly BEV run rate in March, ever since the US subsidy cuts for EV, which

items.statement: India policy push for electrification expected over next 18 months to reduce oil/gas dependence; consumer demand rising as TCO improves with inflated fuel prices for economic-use vehicles (3W, delivery, 2W, eLCV, buses)
items.quote: I think you should see over the next 18 months, a lot more policy push to reduce our country's oil and gas exposure. This is also the reason the currency remains weak. So there is a very, very high realization of how this dependence is bad for us. And a lot of work should happen in the next 18 months from the policy side. The consumer demand side also, I expect that, as more and more people realiz

items.statement: Net order book ₹237 billion at end Q4 FY26, EVs 70% of order book; added 31 new programs and 3 new customers during FY26
items.quote: So at the end of Q4 FY26, our net order book stands at 237 billion, with EVs accounting for 70% of the orderbook.

items.statement: Q4 added 7 non-EV differential gear programs worth ₹3 billion from existing customers; order momentum broad-based across powertrains, geographies, customer types
items.quote: So in Q4, we won 7 Non-EV differential gear programs, and all of them from existing customers, which totaled ₹3 billion addition to the orderbook. The remaining order wins came from either segments like starter motors and railways, Basically, the order momentum is broad-based. It is across powertrains, across geographies, and across customer types.

items.statement: Quick commerce NOV growth CAGR of 60% over three years
items.quote: We've given overall guidance of 60% CAGR and that would obviously mean some reasonable store expansion, but we're not planning to give out any specific number guidance on that.

items.statement: On track for 3,000 dark stores by March, no guidance beyond that
items.quote: On store addition, we're on track on our guidance for March of 3,000 stores. We remain firmly on track. We're not going to give any guidance beyond that.

items.statement: FY27 growth will not be 100%, no specific short-term guidance given
items.quote: Yes, it will not be 100%, but we are not guiding to a specific number. We need that flexibility in the medium term and short term to respond to how the market dynamics are.

items.statement: Quick commerce targeting 5-6% margin at steady state
items.quote: As we move to 5-6% margin that we are saying we will get to at some point, contribution margin will go up and on a year-on-year basis, we'll see that trend consistently.

items.statement: NCR quick commerce already at 5-6% margin implying 8-9% contribution margin
items.quote: We are not sharing that data point. I don't think it matters also, but broadly, it'll be somewhere in that range.

items.statement: June quarter acceleration driven by AOV reversal, fewer days in March quarter, and seasonality
items.quote: The only other factor will be seasonality. It's a different season so we see different consumption patterns and summer driving growth in certain categories.

items.statement: Maintaining pricing discipline in quick commerce despite market discounting
items.quote: We are very confident of maintaining our pricing discipline. We're not sure what competition will do.

items.statement: Platform fee increases applied broadly, discounts targeted to price-sensitive cohorts
items.quote: What we're trying to do essentially is increase the overall revenue per order by increasing the platform fee and then channel that revenue to select cohort of customers in select geographies where we're seeing growth.

items.statement: No plans to launch Toing-like model; Bistro remains small experiment
items.quote: At this point, we don't have any plans to do what Swiggy is doing with Toing. We're not clear on what problem it solves for consumers or for restaurants.

items.statement: No new categories planned for District; travel not a focus area
items.quote: We have no plans to add any more category to District than what we already have, and travel is not a focus area for us at this point.

items.statement: Competitive intensity remains high across all tiers; different players aggressive in different markets
items.quote: The competitive intensity is fairly high pretty much wherever everybody is. Akshant Goyal: Different set of players in different markets. Someone is aggressive somewhere at this point. For us, it's competitive everywhere

items.statement: Automation capex driven by ROCE framework; increasing directionally in warehouses
items.quote: We keep testing for that. We don't want to pursue automation for the sake of it. The framework is that the capex should have ROCE that we can track and that is visible.

items.statement: Food delivery incremental margins reinvested for growth, not margin percentage optimization
items.quote: If we can find ways of effectively reinvesting any incremental margin that we get in our business, or any business, we would do that because the objective is to optimize for growth of absolute profit and not the profit margin percentage.

items.statement: Fuel price increases generally passed to consumers without meaningful demand impact
items.quote: In the past, going by the last 12 to 18 months, experiences and examples like the GST hike happened, where we were fairly easily able to pass it on to consumers without too much impact on demand.

items.statement: Hyperpure included in overall billion-dollar profit guidance
items.quote: The statement that we have made includes all the businesses that we are in today, including Hyperpure. It might be the smallest, but it will still be meaningful and relevant.

items.statement: Targeting 10-12% volume growth in FY27, barring major war escalation
items.quote: we are targeting around 10% to 12% of volume growth from here on. And definitely considering the growth expectations from the various products that we are into, barring the war does not impact too much, we are confident to grow with the volume growth of 10% to 12%.

items.statement: ECH and CPVC capacity doubling on track for Q2 FY27 commissioning within budget
items.quote: Our capacity expansion projects of Epichlorohydrin and CPVC are progressing on track and within budget.

items.statement: New greenfield project under evaluation, expected to be announced this year for growth beyond FY29-30
items.quote: So definitely I'm sure that we will be freezing on something and announcing this year so that we can have a consistent growth beyond FY29, FY30 onwards.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin normalized at 23% due to better plant utilization and raw material prices
items.quote: Leading to our EBITDA margin has been normalized range of 23 % on account of better sweating of the plants and also normalized level of raw material prices.

items.statement: Management defers EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 but expects to maintain current range
items.quote: I would defer giving any guidance on the EBITDA margins. But what we have achieved so far, we would be maintaining in that range.

items.statement: Caustic soda ECU at INR30,000 in Q4 FY26, currently around INR37,000 due to war-related price increases
items.quote: current quarter, quarter 4 we have ended with the ECU of around INR30,000 and that has been there. And currently the ECU because of the war situation had gone up, like caustic soda prices have increased by almost 30 % to 35% compared to what it was before war.

items.statement: Domestic demand intact for 60% of product basket; 40% facing volume pressure from elevated prices
items.quote: because of the product basket that we are into where 60% of our product basket is something which goes into the basic things and where the demand is still intact even at elevated prices, so we are better off compared to the situation that and again there is a 40% of our product basket where the elevated prices bit of a

items.statement: Chlorine captive consumption at 75% currently, targeting 90-95% by FY28 after ECH/CPVC ramp-up
items.quote: Current chlorine captive consumption is around 75%. And as we are commissioning our ECH and CPVC capacity in the Quarter 2 of FY '27, and it will run at a lower utilizations initially because it will take time to ramp up that facility. So maybe in FY '28, once we kind of reach to the optimum utilization levels, at that

items.statement: Chlorotoluene plant commissioned March 2025, targeting 70-75% utilization by FY28 with sizeable FY27 contribution
items.quote: So optimum would be in the range of 70% to 75% utilization level, which we expect to reach in FY '28.

items.statement: West Asia conflict disrupting supply chains; stabilization expected to take 4-5 months after ceasefire
items.quote: considering the situations, the stabilize as well, like if there is a pause in the current situation, then also it will take at least four to five months of time for things to stabilize for the realizations of all the products to come down.

items.statement: INR depreciation caused mark-to-market loss on forex derivative, increasing FY26 interest cost to INR72 cr
items.quote: So, it was majorly because of one of the loan that where we had we had a mark-to-market impact. So, it's just a mark -to-market impact which has been there in the interest cost put together.

items.statement: FY26 capex spend INR394 cr, operating cash flow INR436 cr, net debt/EBITDA 0.9x
items.quote: During the year, we spent around INR394 crores on the ongoing capex and we have generated around INR436 crores from the operations.

items.statement: Guiding 25% revenue growth in FY27
items.quote: I'm confident of delivering 25% revenue growth in FY '27.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin similar to FY26 level in FY27
items.quote: We are confident in our ability to maintain EBITDA margin at a similar level in the coming year.

items.statement: FY26 capex INR195 crores; FY27 planned capex ~INR90 crores plus R&D centre
items.quote: For next year, our capex will be the sum of the spillover of FY '26 capex, which is around INR50 crores and around INR40 crores will be maintenance capex.

items.statement: Invested INR190 crores in Indichem JV in FY26
items.quote: Another major cash outlay during the year was our investment in South Korea joint venture, Indichem Inc. We have invested INR190 crores in this JV during the year FY '26.

items.statement: Demand momentum strong; new product inquiries healthy
items.quote: On the demand side, momentum remains strong. New product inquiries continue to come in at a healthy pace while demand for existing products remain robust.

items.statement: Electrolyte additive capacity 2,000 MT each for VC and FEC fully contracted for next 3 years
items.quote: We have 2,000 metric in capacity for both each. And as we mentioned during last commentary also that this plant is fully covered back by the customer contracts for all the capacities in next 3 years' time.

items.statement: Two new battery electrolyte products to commercialize in FY27
items.quote: We expect to bring two additional products to commercial scale in FY27, further strengthening our revenue visibility backed by long-term customer contracts.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin ~36%; expect similar in FY27
items.quote: Similar level as FY '26. Q4 is too ambitious.

items.statement: Gulf conflict disrupting feedstock supply chains and shipping; no production impact expected
items.quote: The chemical industry has once again navigating turbulent conditions driven by the ongoing conflict in the Gulf region, which has disrupted supply chain for key feedstocks and consequently pushed raw material prices higher.

items.statement: CDMO: 4 validated products each INR50-100 cr peak revenue; Fermion 10-year contract
items.value: INR50 crores to INR100 crores each
items.quote: We are expecting those products to be between INR50 crores to INR100 crores each at a peak level.

items.statement: Indichem JV plant completion advanced to H2 CY26; R&D centre sending samples
items.quote: It should get completed in second half of calendar year '26.

items.statement: Seasonality: H1 ~40% revenue, H2 ~60%; pattern expected to continue in FY27
items.quote: This pattern results in H1 contr ibuting around 40% of our top line, while H2 accounts for generally around 60

items.statement: Phasing out select commodity products; replacing with higher-value differentiated offerings
items.quote: We'll begin phasing out select commodity products this year, replacing them with a new product using same infrastructure with slight modification in calibrated phase manner.

items.statement: CDMO revenue target INR1,000 crores by FY28 intact
items.quote: Yes, that is the guidance, correct.

items.statement: Indichem JV expected ~1x revenue on INR200 cr capex; margins like BFC business
items.quote: We are expecting around 1x kind of revenue from this plant.

items.statement: Target positive full-year same-store sales growth (SSG) in FY27 after negative SSG in FY26
items.quote: First and foremost, we are committed to turning SSG positive and ending FY '27 with a positive full year same-store sales growth.

items.statement: Plan to close 50+ small stores in Q1 FY27 and migrate to larger 700+ sq ft EBOs
items.quote: Over the next 3 months in quarter 1, we plan to shut another 50 such small stores.

items.statement: Plan to launch 10-12 new bottom-wear products in FY27 targeting new purchase occasions
items.quote: Over FY '27, we plan to add 10 to 12 new refreshing products especially bottom-wear products for our customers, not just line extensions, but genuinely new formats that opens up new purchase occasions and customer cohorts.

items.statement: Expect gross margins to remain stable at 62.5-63.5% in FY27
items.quote: I think we'll maintain between that 62.5% and 63.5% gross margin, what we've been delivering.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin recovery from Q2 FY27 after store closures reduce costs by INR25+ crores
items.quote: From Q2 financials, you'll be able to see a significant increase in our EBITDA margins, which is currently at about 11.5% for the full year vis-a-vis we were close to 16.8% in the previous year.

items.statement: Demand environment improving; industry peers reporting positive demand commentary in Q4
items.quote: Quarter 4, when I speak to my peers, many retail companies, apparel companies have given positive commentary around demand scenario. So, I think from a demand perspective, probably it's not as weak as it was earlier, and we have seen improvement in demand in the industry.

items.statement: Daily Wear concept pilot at 10 stores as of March 2026; target 25-30 stores by end FY27
items.quote: By the end of FY '27, we plan to expand the Daily Wear concept to about 25 to 30 stores, which as on 31st March 2026 is 10 stores.

items.statement: ASP currently INR800-811; target to keep blended ASP under INR1,000 long-term
items.quote: Currently, our ASP is around that INR800. I think in the short term, it will be between INR800 and INR900. So we are very cognizant of that. We don't want to premiumize so much that our ASP starts crossing INR1,000 or beyond INR1,000.

items.statement: LFS channel declined 15-16% in Q4 FY26 (7% adjusted for credit note); expect stabilization and recovery in FY27
items.quote: If I adjust the INR5 crores, the 15% decline will come down to 7%. Now from a trajectory perspective, where we were at minus 30% in quarter 3, the minus 30% has become minus 7%. So the recovery has already started seeing in Q4 from an LFS perspective.

items.statement: Brand ambassador to be onboarded in June 2026 to amplify brand salience and store traction
items.quote: Looking ahead in June 2026, we will have a brand ambassador for our products. This is a significant step for Go Colors, one that we believe will meaningfully amplify our brand salience, support stronger top-of-the-mind awareness and generate improved traction at a store level.

items.statement: International expansion measured; first Middle East store opened in FY26 with encouraging early response
items.quote: Go Colors opened its first international store in the Middle East during FY '26, making a significant milestone in our brand's journey. This early response has been encouraging, and we are studying the unit economics and consumer responses carefully.

items.statement: Revenue will grow in FY27; no degrowth expected despite store rationalization
items.quote: We will not degrow in FY '27, Devanshu. The idea is to grow. And a lot of things, a lot of efforts have been happening in correcting the small stores, doing good marketing. We've signed a brand ambassador also. I think all these things are going to bring a positive result for us in FY '27. So there will definitely not

items.statement: Inventory days elevated to 4 months due to sales softness and Daily Wear pilot; expected to normalize to 3 months in FY27
items.quote: This inventory level what we have currently at 4 months; in FY '27, it will stabilize again back to 3 months, what was our previous number.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 18-20% YoY; EBITDA margin guided at 25-30%
items.quote: Now coming to guidance for FY27, we expect annual revenue growth to be around 18% to 20% and EBITDA margins to be in the range of 25% to 30%.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 29.7% vs 34.8% in FY25 due to strategic investments in ESOP, senior leadership, travel, events, and labor regulations
items.quote: Our EBITDA was at INR 48.3 crores and EBITDA margin stood at 29.7% in FY26 versus 34.8% in FY25. This was a conscious and planned investment phase, as we communicated in earlier calls.

items.statement: DFM product development expensed ~INR 2 cr in FY26; no further big investments planned in FY27; event spend to reduce by at least 60%
items.quote: On DFM development, if you want to quantify it, then you can consider approx. INR 2 crores was expensed in FY26, and we expect no further big investments on DFM development in FY27.

items.statement: Demand remains intact; conversions strong; some deal delays due to geopolitical issues (UAE/war) but orders now releasing
items.quote: Demand remains intact, and our execution momentum is strong. We remain confident of delivering sustainable growth while continuing to invest for scale.

items.statement: Clients migrating from SAP to Odoo to reduce costs; Odoo provides similar features at lower cost
items.quote: See, multiple customers are trying to reduce their cost, and they are trying to move to less costly solutions. So Odoo and SAP, both are doing mostly the same, both are providing mostly the same feature. And you know that SAP is super costly as compared to Odoo.

items.statement: 82% of revenue recurring; IT services core driver; product segment (DFM) small, developed in disciplined manner; focus shifting fully to services
items.quote: Our growth continues to be driven by a diversified services mix across ERP, cloud, data, AI, salesforce and enterprise transformation, with 82% of revenue being recurring, providing strong visibility and resilience.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty (war) caused deal delays in UAE; conservative margin guidance (25-30%) to absorb potential shocks
items.quote: Considering geopolitical factors, I'm trying to be conservative, and that's why I have given you the bracket. But if everything goes well all around the world, then it will be a good number.

items.statement: AI-first operating model: all engineers Claude-certified; AI agents used for coding, testing, deployment, workflow automation; 60-70% of customers already using AI-enhanced delivery
items.quote: We have already implemented this for multiple customers. As per our commentary, we are already using AI for at least 60% to 70% customers, and we have increased their output with the same number of the resources.

items.statement: Dividend payout to continue at 40-60% of profits; no acquisitions planned; net debt-free with INR 6.9 cr cash
items.quote: It will continue in the same manner, as we are not looking for any acquisitions or inorganic growth currently in the coming quarters. So it will continue in the same way.

items.statement: AUM growth of around 20% for FY27
items.quote: Now, as we stepped into a new financial year, we are geared up to get back on the track of growth and well -poised to achieve AUM growth of around 20% for the financial year 2027.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 1.7% to 1.75% for FY27
items.quote: At this point of time, we will probably be guiding you for a credit cost of 1.7% to 1.75% for the next financial year; depending on how the buckets trend over the year, this could look better from here, but our guidance will be about 1.7% to 1.75%.

items.statement: Steady-state credit cost of 1.5% to 1.6% for FY28-30
items.quote: So, we are probably looking at anywhere between 1.5% to 1.6% of credit cost as a steady -state number. I think we are confident about that.

items.statement: ROA guidance of 8.25% to 8.5% for FY27
items.quote: For this year, I think 8.25% to 8.5% is an ROA that we should be able to operate at.

items.statement: Steady-state ROA of 8% to 8.25%
items.quote: And on a fairly steady -state, also about 8% to 8.25% levels, we should be able to operate.

items.statement: Spread guidance of around 13.5% for FY27
items.quote: Our belief is that I think even for the current financial year, which is FY27, and thereafter, we should be able to operate at a spread of around 13.5%.

items.statement: Opex to AUM guidance of 7% to 7.25% for FY27
items.quote: Our sense is, I think it will largely remain around the 7% to 7.25% levels, and not show any big decline during the year despite the 20% growth that we'll achieve.

items.statement: Disbursement target of INR 6,500 crores to INR 7,000 crores for FY27
items.quote: And we should be able to get close to about INR6,500 crores to INR7,000 crores of disbursements in the coming year.

items.statement: Branch expansion of 60 to 75 branches in FY27
items.quote: So even for this financial year, we intend to open 60 to 75 branches.

items.statement: Yield compression of 30-40 bps expected over next 3-4 quarters as rate cuts pass through
items.quote: So, I would probably say about 30 - 40 basis points of further impact that may come in over the next three to four quarters.

items.statement: Incremental lending yield at 22.5%; book yield expected to settle at 22% to 22.25%
items.quote: We are today incrementally lending at around 22.5%. And factoring for some delinquencies and all that, the book yield should be closer to about 22% to 22.25%.

items.statement: No pricing change planned for FY27; current yields competitive for segment
items.quote: no issue from a pricing perspective, and it is not like we are -- we have been slow on disbursements because of pricing. The slowdown in disbursements is a conscious call given the challenges that we faced. And we don't really envisage at this point of time for any pricing drop to happen at least in

items.statement: Strong demand in core segment; pent-up demand after slow FY26
items.quote: And this is a segment where the demand is of the least concern because it's a very huge market out there. And we should be able to get close to about INR6,500 crores to INR7,000 crores of disbursements in the coming year.

items.statement: No material impact from geopolitical tensions; sub-1% portfolio exposure to potentially affected segments
items.quote: The proportion of that portfolio is firstly extremely small for us, sub-1%. And even on that, we are not seeing any alarm signals at this point of time.

items.statement: Raised $100 million from ADB; $50 million drawn in Q4, $50 million available for FY27
items.quote: We raised $100 million from Asian Development Bank, ADB, one of the largest development financial institutions across the globe during this quarter, which is a reinforcement of lenders' belief in Five-Star.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 spreads expected to continue at Q4 level of INR148/kg; full-year FY27 growth targeted at ~14-15% (similar to FY26)
items.quote: So at least in Q1, I believe that it will continue, what spreads we have received in Q4, it would continue at least in Q1.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR2,000 crores and EBITDA margin of 15-18% targeted between FY29-FY30
items.quote: So as for our internal guidance, we are sort of aiming for FY29 at least for the top line, maybe around FY30. So, you can say between FY29 to FY30 is when we are planning to achieve this, both for your top line guidance as well as margin guidance.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR100-120 crores including 10MW ground solar (~INR35 cr), knitting machines (~INR15 cr), PM MITRA Park land investment, and maintenance capex
items.quote: So FY27 capex plan will be between INR100 crores, INR120 crores. Primarily, there is one large investment on our on-ground solar. So, the cash outgo and the commissioning will happen this year.

items.statement: Export contribution at 14% of revenue in Q4; Europe demand steady, Bangladesh strong, US demand improved post tariff resolution; no direct US exports
items.quote: So, this quarter, it was almost about 14% of our top line came from exports. I want to clarify one part in your question. We do not export directly to U.S.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 spread improved to INR148/kg from INR123/kg in Q3; EBITDA margin rose from ~10% to 11.7%; FY27 EBITDA growth expected near FY26 level (+/-2%)
items.quote: Just to give you a number, our spread in Q3 was about INR123 per kilo, which has gone up to about INR148 kilo in Q4.

items.statement: Cotton prices rose from INR55,000/candy (Dec'25) to INR62,000/candy (Apr'26); company holds ~120 days cotton inventory procured at lower prices; purchases to taper down
items.quote: On the cotton front, prices moved upwards, rising from approximately INR55,000 per candy in December '25 to around INR62,000 currently.

items.statement: Domestic demand improved meaningfully in Q4; export demand boosted by US tariff resolution and India-EU FTA; China yarn demand tapered since March
items.quote: Domestic market conditions improved meaningfully during quarter 4 FY26. I am pleased to report that the quarter was a strong one for us across both volume and pricing.

items.statement: Fabric revenue target 15% of total in FY27 (up from 12% in FY26); 40 knitting machines to be installed (15 already, 25 more from Q3); 60% of yarn to be vertically integrated into fabric/processed fabric
items.quote: We are targeting almost 15% of our revenue to come from fabric. A large part of our knitted fabrics would be in house.

items.statement: Key risks: West Asia conflict disrupting trade routes/logistics, elevated fuel prices pressuring synthetic fabric costs, gas availability issues, inflationary pressure on processing costs, cotton price volatility
items.quote: Challenges remain in terms of on-going US-Iran conflict, which has disrupted traditional trade routes, resulting in shipment delays and elevated logistics cost.

items.statement: No buyback planned; INR350 crores of committed capex (from INR1,000 cr plan) to be deployed over next 3 years primarily in fabric/processing and PM MITRA Park
items.quote: We are as of now we are not looking at a buyback, but we are looking to deploy this cash what we generate and also see earlier we had a plan of about INR1,000 crores of investment. Out of that about INR675 crores is already deployed.

items.quote: I believe that our cost of funding can go down easily by 100 to 120 basis points once the rating improves.

items.statement: Expect similar strong growth in MTF book in coming periods due to largest broker position and strong balance sheet
items.quote: We expect a similar strong growth in the coming periods because we are the largest broker in terms of Industry cash brokerage revenue pie. Due to this, we will carry an edge in terms of higher growth for our MTF book.

items.statement: Expect brokerage line item to catch up in coming periods given regulatory impact is behind and volumes are up
items.quote: Now with a higher base in the current financial year over last financial year, we expect the brokerage line item to catch up for coming periods, given that the regulatory impact is behind and our volumes are up.

items.statement: Housing Finance business expected to witness strong growth over 2-3 years with strong capital adequacy and low leverage
items.quote: We expect Housing Finance business having formed a strong base and a very strong leadership team to witness strong growth over 2-3 years.

items.statement: Annuity revenue share at over 60% of total revenues and Asset Management and Private Wealth profitability share will continue to rise in FY27
items.quote: Over the last 3/5/10 years, our annuity stream of revenue has consistently gone up. They are now at over 60% of the total revenues . The Asset Management and Private Wealth Management Business share of profitability because of their annuity nature too have consistently gone up, and that trend will continue to rise in FY27.

items.statement: FY26 was a year of investments on all fronts - people, brand, and technology - to maintain leadership position
items.quote: Also, FY26 was a year of investments on all fronts in the group, be it people, brand or technology. We've not left any stone unturned to maintain our leadership position in our businesses.

items.statement: IB business completed 52 deals in FY26 with cumulative raise of ₹83,600 cr and fees income grew 39% YoY to ₹309 Cr
items.quote: Our IB business still has successfully completed 52 deals in FY26 with cumulative raise of ₹ 83,600 cr and our fees income delivered a strong 39% revenue growth YoY basis to ₹ 309 Cr.

items.statement: Operating profit after tax grew 16% YoY to ₹2,360 crores in FY26, Q4 grew 25% to ₹661 crores run rate
items.quote: Our operating profit after tax in the year FY26 grew by 16% YoY to ₹2,360 crores, led by a 33% growth in the profits of Asset and Private Wealth businesses.

items.statement: AMC AUM grew 34% YoY to ₹3.7 lakh crores with robust net flows of ₹70,000 crores, unique PANs crossed 1 Cr in Mar'26
items.quote: Our Asset Management and Private Wealth business continued momentum during the year with robust net flows of ₹70,000 crores and an AUM of ₹3.7 lakh crores, which is up by 34% year -on-year.

items.statement: AMC launched 5 new MF Active Products in FY26 increasing presence to 82% of Industry AUM, expect 8 funds to cross 3-year vintage by Mar'27 and 16 by Mar'28
items.quote: We launched 5 new MF Active Products in FY26 increasing our presence to 82% of Industry AUM. Importantly, only 6 of our funds have a vintage of over 3 years vs 42/29/26 funds with similar vintage in the case of top 3 peers. We expect 8 funds to cross 3 years vintage by Mar'27 and 16 funds by Mar '28.

items.statement: Alternates raised largest growth capital fund IBEF V close to $1 billion, fee accruing AUM grew 40% to ₹21K Crs, launching Private Credit fund of ₹3,000 Crs, Commercial RE Fund and Residential RE Fund Series VII
items.quote: We raised our largest growth capital fund IBEF V raising close to a billion dollars. This leads to 40% growth in fee accruing AUM from average AUM of ₹15k Crs to closing AUM of ₹21K Crs. items.statement: AMC fees unimpacted by TER changes, slightly improved for cohort; yield compression due to mix effect from faster-growing passives with lower retention
items.quote: Our fees as a consequence of the TER changes continued to remain unimpacted. In fact, they have slightly improved for our cohort of AUM as that category did not get impacted. items.statement: MTM loss of ~₹1,000 crores on investment book is notional, most recouped in April 2026; investment book collateralized with lenders and expanding at 40% per annum

items.statement: Long-term credit rating upgraded to AA+ with stable outlook, highest ever for non-bank domestic capital market player in India
