items.quote: we have done almost 80% of brownfield expansions. And now within one or two quarters, it will be finished. Then the capacity will go es to the 3,500 tons per month

items.statement: Price hikes of 60-70% of raw material cost increase implemented from May 1st; VAM prices doubled from INR 75-80 to INR 160-180
items.quote: Almost 60% - 70% (of) price rise (of raw material) we have taken. But from the 1st May

items.statement: Peers have taken 4-5% price hikes in April and ~10% from May 1st
items.quote: in April, they have started and 4% to 5% price rise started to taken and from the 1st May, it is almost 10% has taken

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margins expected to be impacted by VAM price surge; recovery expected within 2-3 months if geopolitical situation stabilizes
items.quote: this quarter may be affecting our gross margin because of the sudden price increase into the VAM

items.statement: Q4 volume growth of 16% YoY driven by genuine demand, not dealer stocking; tertiary offtake focus intensified
items.quote: Q4 is always been a heavy quarter in the business overall, right. So that is where -- so it is not because of the fear of price rise and all they have stocked the material

items.statement: OEM segment currently 6% of revenue, targeting 15% in 2-3 years with focus on metro markets
items.quote: we are assuming that after two, three years our revenue will be 85% into the retail and 15% around into the OEMs

items.statement: Receivables elevated at 150-160 days due to new state expansion; target to normalize to 110-120 days within 2-3 quarters
items.quote: we should aim for at least after 2 years that state should be very much stable, and we can at least maintain 12 0 days of debtor cycle

items.statement: NSE listing process underway, expected soon
items.quote: It is in process. We are into the process and very near, maybe it will be listed on the NSE

items.statement: April volumes strong as dealers pre-bought ahead of May price hikes
items.quote: April was good. And April, we can say about that because of the price rises going to in the May. So, dealers have that -- trying to get that benefits

items.statement: Reiterated guidance for sustained double-digit revenue and EBITDA growth in FY27
items.quote: we remain comfortable reiterating our guidance for sustained double -digit revenue and EBITDA growth

items.statement: Planned capex of ~INR 25 crores over next two years for labs and existing clients
items.quote: on the capex side, we would be doing, in the next two years, close to about INR 25 crores, just for existing clients, and this is more for just setting up the labs

items.statement: 95-98% of FY27 revenue expected from existing 75 active clients per their budgets
items.quote: if I had to give you a directional number, I would say 95% to 98% will come from existing clients, as per the budget from the 75 active clients that we have

items.statement: Demand outlook for digital and engineering services, especially AI projects, remains very positive
items.quote: the demand outlook for digital and engineering services, especially new initiatives in AI projects, continues to be very positive

items.statement: Board actively considering share buyback given attractive valuation and INR 127.3 cr net cash
items.quote: It's something the Board has been actively considering, and definitely, the price is very attractive, both for the company and for all the investors

items.statement: Dividend increased to INR 8/share (11th consecutive year), highest ever recommended
items.quote: we the Board, have looked at a capital allocation budget as well and recommended an increase in the dividend to INR 8 per share. This will be our 11th consecutive year of dividend, and this INR 8 per share will be the highest that the Board has recommended

items.statement: Guidance for FY27 volume growth at around 15% and EBITDA growth at around 15%
items.quote: So the guidance is very similar. Probably we are giving a guidance of both volume at around 15% and even EBITDA at around 15%.

items.statement: Domestic branded business targeting 25% volume growth going forward
items.quote: But we are still committed to driving 25% kind of volume growth, which means that the value growth also will be in the same lines.

items.statement: No major capex planned for next 2 years; only maintenance capex of INR25-35 crores
items.quote: So, there is no capex for '27. We didn't say there would be any capex. As we have been maintaining next 2 years, there will be some maintenance capex of maybe INR25 crores to INR30 crores, INR35 crores, but these are very small capex.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg improved on annual basis despite sequential dip; cost-plus model insulates margins from coffee price volatility
items.quote: But on an annual basis, in fact, the EBITDA per kilo has improved from previous year. So that's an improvement.

items.statement: B2C business EBITDA margin maintained at 4-5% with profits reinvested for growth
items.quote: As far as the profitability, I already mentioned that we probably are at around 4%, 5% EBITDA level. We'll keep the EBITDA levels there so that all the additional profits are plowed back into building the brand and growing the business.

items.statement: Green coffee prices stable currently; Brazilian crop may soften prices further in coming months
items.quote: As far as green coffee prices are concerned, they remain to be stable as of now, which is a good sign. The Brazilian crop is around the corner. And with the positive news of good supplies, we have a belief that the prices could further soften in the coming months.

items.statement: Freeze-dried coffee utilization higher than average; seeing better utilization for freeze-dried capacity
items.quote: We are seeing better utilization for freeze dried. So if that is happening much faster -- at a much faster rate, the utilization, we could look at not necessarily a capacity expansion, but maybe a strategic tie-up or things like that.

items.statement: Small packs proportion increased to around 20% from 15% last year, aiding profitability
items.quote: So largely, it is around 20% or so. It used to be -- and I'm talking about broad this thing because on a very small quarterly basis becomes difficult to assess. But largely, it is in that zone. If you remember, 2-3 quarters or, let's say, last year, we were talking about a number around 15% or so. So it has increased and that has also helped us improve our profitability.

items.statement: Middle East crisis poses supply disruption and energy cost challenges but managed well with no major disruption expected
items.quote: The Middle East crisis does pose a challenge with a bit of supply disruptions and energy price increase, but we have managed the situation well and do not see much of disruption going forward.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR1,073 crores; debt-to-equity at 0.5; net debt/EBITDA at 1.45; further reduction expected but working capital needs may offset
items.quote: The net debt as of 31st March is around INR1,073 crores, a reduction of more than INR750 crores from last year. Debt to equity is at 0.5 compared to 0.92 a year ago. Net debt to EBITDA is at 1.45 right now compare to 3.1 a year ago.

items.statement: D2C channel contributes 20-25% of domestic sales; strong market share on platforms
items.quote: And in a few of the platforms, we are also the number 2 player in the category. So we are doing extremely good approximately 20% to 25% of our sales come form the online channel, which is very good -- very good marker for the business that we're doing.

items.statement: International brand Percol at INR25-30 crores in UK; targeting INR100 crores in 2-3 years; evaluating US and Vietnam markets
items.quote: U.K., let's say, it's already a INR30 crores, INR25 crores, INR30 crores kind of revenue, we probably are looking to kind of get to INR100 crores within 2 years or 3 years or so.

items.statement: Malgudi snacks brand pilot in 100-150 stores showing good response; broader launch expected in couple of months
items.quote: So the response is quite good there. We have done as I told very small 100, 150 stores kind of a pilot. There is a lot of response on various aspects. People have liked the product. There are certain variants where we are doing some product tweaking as well because there was certain feedback. And hopefully, in a couple of months' time, you should be seeing a more broader launch at least with some

items.statement: Consolidated capacity utilization at 65% annually (70% last quarter); expected to reach 72-73% in FY27 and 80-85% in FY28 with 15% volume growth
items.quote: Yes. 65% will go to around 72%, 73%, If I were to be very specific.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing currently 7-7.5%; interest cost expected around INR100 crores next year with gross debt of INR1,200 crores
items.quote: So if you take INR1,200 crores at an average rate of 7.5%, it translates to close to INR90 crores, INR95 crores. So somewhere around INR100 crores would be an appropriate number is what I can give you.

items.statement: Exports 70% FOB based; CIF contracts absorb logistics cost increases; no major shipping route disruptions observed
items.quote: Most of it, almost if I take exports, 70% of our sales would be FOB based, right?

items.statement: Guided AUM growth of 35-40% for FY27 with commensurate disbursements
items.quote: We've given a guidance of AUM of 35 -40%. We could be probably a notch better, but it depends. We'll watch closely how this environment plans out. But directionally, I think we would like to look at a 35 -40% and commensurate disbursements along with it.

items.statement: NIM expanded 43 bps sequentially to 9.05% in Q4FY26, achieving 9% target in 3 quarters
items.quote: Our NIM has expanded sequentially by 43 basis points from an 8.62% in Q3FY26 to 9.05% in Q4FY26. In our Q1FY26 call, we had guided that we will restore 9% NIM levels in three to four quarters. Happy to report back that we have achieved the same in 3 quarters.

items.statement: Disbursement yield increased 40 bps sequentially, indicating pricing power
items.quote: A significant contributor to the NIM going forward is our disbursement yield, in my opinion, which has already gone up by 40 basis points. It is a milestone that underscores the successful integration of our new product verticals and digital businesses.

items.statement: ROA reached 1.81% in Q4FY26, up from 1.2% in Q3FY26 and 0.78% in Q4FY25
items.quote: Our ROA has moved to 1.81% this quarter versus 1. 2% last quarter. And if I compare it with the quarter ending March '25, it was around 0.78%. We believe it is the strongest evidence of our structural operating leverage.

items.statement: Six new businesses contributed 24% of Q4 disbursements vs 20% in Q3
items.quote: The 6 new businesses we've launched are responsible for this, contributing close to 24% disbursement in this quarter versus 20% last quarter.

items.statement: Gold loan Q4 disbursement ~₹819 crores; >90% branches in Tier 2/3 locations
items.quote: Total disbursement in Q4 is close to ₹819 crores, a fairly decent step up. More than 90% of branches are in Tier 2, Tier 3 locations.

items.statement: Education loans crossed ~₹900 crores disbursals in first year; 500+ consultants/partners; 20% instant sanctions
items.quote: As of March 2026, our education loan has crossed approximately ₹900 crores in disbursals, driven by a distribution network now of around 500 + consultants and strategic partners, firmly aligned with our original vision. We are also seeing a healthy traction in the instant sanction process, which now contributes to nearly 20% of total

items.statement: Credit cost declined to 2.51% in Q4FY26 from 2.62% in Q3FY26; 6MoB30+ improved to 1.05%
items.quote: There has been a quarter-on-quarter decline in credit cost from 2.62% to 2.51%. This improvement is further validated by our 6-month outcome, i.e. 6MoB30+, which continues to further trend positively. Our GNPA for Q4 stands at 1.44% versus 1.51% in Q3FY26.

items.statement: FY26 capex was INR 1,125 crore, in line with guidance.
items.quote: In line with the guidance given, the capex for the year was at about INR 1,125 crore.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected in the range of INR 700 crore to INR 800 crore.
items.quote: Our capex for FY27 is expected to be in the range of INR 700 crore to INR800 crore as we continue our journey to optimize capex and maximize the returns.

items.statement: Signed a backward integration contract with a global chemical company involving INR 200-250 crore capex over a residual 15-year period.
items.quote: First one being a backward integration initiative with a leading global chemical company, transitioning the relationship into a more integrated end-to-end manufacturing model with a capex of about INR 200-250 crore to cater to the requirement over the residual 15 -year contract period.

items.statement: Signed a $150 million multiyear supply agreement with a global agrochemical innovator extending through March 31, 2030, with no incremental capex.
items.quote: And the second one is a $150 million multiyear supply agreement with a global agrochemical innovator for a critical agrochemical intermediate used in crop protection formulations, extending through March 31, 2030.

items.statement: Overall demand environment for the product basket remained largely stable; Middle East shipment disruptions were proactively redirected to other geographies.
items.quote: The overall demand environment for our basket of products remained largely stable. While we ex perienced disruptions in the shipments to the Middle East, we were able to proactively redirect volumes to the other geographies, ensuring continuity in operations and minimizing the impact on overall volumes

items.statement: Middle East geopolitical tensions pose near-term risk to feedstock availability and product placement; full impact of disruptions to be felt in ongoing quarter.
items.quote: The specific situation in West Asia continues to pose near -term risk to the availability of certain critical feedstock and placement of key products in the Middle East.

items.statement: Energy application volumes down 4% QoQ due to lower Middle East exports; non-energy agrochemicals showed steady volume growth but margin pressure persists; polymers in strong growth phase driven by EV demand; MPDA underperforms due to China
items.quote: The volumes for the quarter were down 4% quarter -on-quarter, primarily driven by lower exports to the Middle East, which were impacted due to geopolitical disruptions.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 29% YoY in Q4 FY26 and 15% for full year FY26 despite continued margin pressure over a significant part of the portfolio.
items.quote: Overall, the performance reflects steady execution supported by volume growth, improving capacity utilization and benefits coming from operational efficiencies despite continued margin pressure over a significant part of the portfolio.

items.statement: Key raw material prices (benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene, methanol) went up over 60%; freight costs significantly increased due to higher export shipments and fuel rates.
items.quote: In particular, the prices of key raw materials such as benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene, methanol went up by over 60%.

items.statement: Zone IV projects (multipurpose plant, PEDA, calcium chloride, 5 chemistry blocks) to be commissioned in phased manner during FY27; delayed by 3-4 months due to labour constraints.
items.quote: On Zone IV projects, they are expected to be commissioned in a phased manner during the current financial year. Multipurpose plant and PEDA plants are actually under commissioning trials and should come on stream soon, while others will commission gradually in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Net debt expected to decline in FY27 given lower capex intensity, despite working capital expansion from elevated raw material prices.
items.quote: However, given the capex intensity is lower, we still anticipate the net debt to decline in the current year.

items.statement: Augene Superform JV on track for commissioning in H1 FY27 with focus on agrochemicals and coatings; circularity initiatives commissioning on track for CY26.
items.quote: Augene, the Superform joint venture is on track for commissioning in H1FY2 7 with an initial focus on agrochemical s and coating end markets. Our circularity initiatives also continue to gain momentum with commissioning on track for the CY26.

items.statement: Middle East revenue exposure is roughly 9-10% of annual revenue, dominantly in energy application; full impact of shipment disruption to be visible in coming quarter.
items.quote: So, on an yearly average basis, roughly 9% to 10% of our revenue came from Middle East, which is dominantly in energy application.

items.statement: Agrochemical margin recovery depends on Chinese industry conduct; if anti-involution stance persists and broadens, margin recovery could become more broad-based.
items.quote: I think the biggest driver to get back the margins in the agrochemical segment would be how Chinese industry evolves on this particular application.

items.statement: FY27 capex of INR 750-800 crore significantly allocated to Zone IV completion and new long-term contract (INR 200-250 crore), plus ~INR 150 crore annual maintenance.
items.quote: INR750 crore to INR800 crore, a significant part of it will still go in completion of Zone IV and part of it will also go to the new long-term contract, which we signed, right, where we announced total capex of INR200 crore to INR250 crore.

items.statement: China's anti-involution stance on PNCB/NCB chain products expected to yield benefits from Q1 FY27 onwards.
items.quote: The last quarter announcement of China's anti -involution stance and impact to products related to PNCB in the NCB chain should start seeing benefits from the Q1 FY2 7 onwards.

items.statement: Management targets to reduce net debt from current levels in the current financial year despite pricing scenario and planned capex intensity.
items.quote: Overall, at least the internal target is to reduce the net debt levels from the current levels in the current financial year despite the current pricing scenario and the capex intensity that is planned for the current year.

items.statement: Zone IV capex delayed by 3-4 months due to 35% reduction in contract labour availability and election-related migration.
items.quote: I think on the capex side, yes, we are behind compared to our original plan and that 3 to 4 months of delay will have an impact in terms of how much we were budgeting over the course of next 2 years, but we are figuring out strategies to mitigate that impact.

items.statement: EBITDA potential from MPP, Zone IV, and UPL JV unchanged; only realization timeline may shift due to capex delay.
items.quote: No, I think at this point in time, we are not changing the EBITDA potential from all of these initiatives. I think the only thing we are highlighting is on the capex -led growth, I think we have seen a slight delay in the project execution, and that might have an impact on realization of that EBITDA potential in the given time frame.

items.statement: Target net working capital days of 55-60 days; Zone IV not expected to materially change trajectory.
items.quote: Ideally, we would like to remain within 55 to 60 days kind of average levels. But as I mentioned, it does vary depending on the market situation. But from an objective standpoint, I think we like to target 55 to 60 days kind of levels.

items.statement: Tax rate expected in range of 9% to 15% for FY27 onwards due to IT depreciation benefits from Zone IV.
items.quote: But given the fact that we have Zone IV, which is getting commercialized and there is an IT depreciation, which is a significant part of deduction available, the tax rate will be in the range of around maybe 9% to 14%, 15% kind of stuff lateron.

items.statement: MMA demand outlook complex and volatile; no conclusive trend until Middle East situation settles.
items.quote: I do not think there is any conclusive trend at this point in time, which we can draw. And I do not think we will reach a stability until the situation in the Middle East is kind of directionally at least settled.

items.statement: Augene JV with Superform expected to commission in June-July and ramp to full utilization in current financial year; recycling JV to commission this calendar year but not contribute meaningfully yet.
items.quote: From a JV point of view, we expect Augene to commission within hopefully, June, July kind of time frame, which is the JV with Superform. And that should actually ramp up to a full utilization level within the current financial year. So that will start contributing meaningfully.

items.statement: West Asia war creates serious near-term challenge: >60% raw material price increase in 2 weeks and 10% revenue market shutdown.
items.quote: I think it is not easy to handle more than 60% increase in raw material pricing in a 2 weeks' time frame. It is not easy when 10% of your revenue, which is going to a market suddenly shuts, right? So, I think it is a challenge even today.

items.statement: Gross block expected to reach INR 9,500-10,000 crore by end of FY27 after Zone IV commissioning.
items.quote: End of FY2 7, we should be in the range of around INR 9,500 crore to INR10,000 crore. We do not have the exact number, but around that range.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA closed at roughly 3.6x (INR 4,300 crore net debt vs INR 1,172 crore EBITDA).
items.quote: I think we closed the year at roughly INR 1,172 and our net debt was around INR4,300 crore. Chetan Gandhi: Roughly 3.6x

items.statement: Raw material physical availability well covered for methanol (couple of months) and sulfur (few weeks via domestic contracts), but at increasingly higher cost.
items.quote: No. In terms of physical availability, we are well covered so far as far as both of these commodities that you mentioned. It does come at an increasingly higher cost to ensure that sort of all of our plants are fed 100% of the requirement.

items.statement: Partnership/JV momentum increasing despite West Asia conflict; repeat long-term contract from global major validates value proposition.
items.quote: In fact, we see momentum increasing because people are increasingly looking at more robust supply chains, more secure supply chain for their global requirements going forward. And we expect many such conversations to proceed and conclude in the coming financial year as well.

items.statement: FX revaluation loss of INR 39 crore on $87 million unhedged loan due to INR 5 depreciation; natural hedge via export portfolio but accounting mismatch.
items.quote: So, we have roughly around $87 million of an FX loan, which is unhedged and is open. Rupee depreciated by close to INR 5 from a level, I guess 31st December was at INR 89.8 or something and 31st March was at INR 94.8. So, there was a INR 5 depreciation on Indian rupee on $87 million of exposure.

items.statement: Domestic demand offsetting export pressure for dyes and pigments; global GDP slowdown risk to discretionary spend in India also monitored.
items.quote: That comment, Rohit, was specifically for dyes and pigments in the context of a particular product where there is a pressure in the global demand, but that is getting offset by the increase in the domestic demand.

items.statement: Bayer contract asset utilization to improve in coming financial year with steady Dicamba intermediate volumes using 50% of asset.
items.quote: I think as I mentioned in the last call, I think sort of 50% of that asset is used to manufacture one particular intermediate that goes into Dicamba. And there, we are seeing steady volumes right now. So it will definitely lead to a better utilization of that asset in the coming financial year.

items.statement: Cost and operating efficiency initiatives on track; most implemented initiatives to accrue fully in current year.
items.quote: Most of the initiatives on the costs that are implemented, they will start accruing fully in the current year. Operating leverage, all initiatives are on track. There is no delay in any of these.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR800-850 crores, conservatively guided at INR800 crores
items.quote: Now, so our target for the entire year is INR800 crores and that we are very confident to achieve.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target maintained at 29-31% for FY27
items.quote: Yes, we'll do our best to maintain the same margin or even increase the margin.

items.statement: Order book INR452 crores as of call date, 30-32% export mix
items.quote: As of now, we have an order book of almost INR452 crores.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin 21% vs 29% FY26 due to lower exports (higher margin) and oil price doubling in March
items.quote: In Q4, our total export was around INR52 crores and the domestic is around INR100 crores. And export we could not ship in the tune of almost like INR35 crores to INR40 crores in the month of March.

items.statement: Transformer oil prices doubled (100% increase) since February; other commodities up 10-25%; price hike discussions ongoing with customers, some agreed
items.quote: So oil prices have become almost double than what we used to buy in month of February. So February till today, it has increased to almost 100%. And all other commodity has increased in range of 10% to 25%.

items.statement: Price increase negotiations with customers underway; existing fixed-price orders being renegotiated under force majeure; new inquiries quoted at current RM costs
items.quote: We have approached almost all customers for the price increase, revision in price and the active dialogues are going on. I mean, some of the customers have already agreed for the price increase and with some customers we are still under discussion.

items.statement: Domestic demand firm: India commissioned 55 GW renewable capacity in FY26; US demand recovered after tariff reduced from 50% to 10%; Middle East logistics normalized from April
items.quote: India commissioned 55 gigawatts of renewable energy capacity in year '26, a record high and this sustained momentum continues to underpin strong order inflows in our domestic renewable transformer business.

items.statement: New facility will enable 220 kV / 160 MVA power transformers; PGCIL approvals to follow commissioning
items.quote: Yes, so the new facility what we are making will have a capacity to make transformers up to 160 MVA 220 kV class.

items.statement: Targeting INR400 crore+ revenue in Q1 FY27 and 35% revenue CAGR to hit INR5,000 crore by FY31
items.quote: We are targeting INR400 crores plus revenue for the quarter 1 FY27. And all our strategies in terms of pricing, marketing, branding, we want to achieve this number.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA per ton target of INR6,000-8,000 near term, moving to INR10,000-12,000 in 2-3 years
items.quote: So on a consol basis, you can assume that INR6,000, INR7,000, INR8,000 per ton then the journey towards INR10,000, INR11,000, INR12,000 per ton in next 2, 3 years.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance of ~INR100 crore for Kisan brownfield expansion to INR1,000 crore capacity and existing plant upgrades
items.quote: For FY27, the total capex requirement would be near about INR100 crore.

items.statement: Demand encouraging with low base; rural outperforming urban; agri demand good; construction projects spilled from Q4 driving Q1 pickup
items.quote: Demand is like April was good. It could have been better, but it was expected because of heavy March. May, June, it's a seasonal quarter for the industry. Demand from agri is good.

items.statement: PVC prices expected stable within +/-5% range near term; import duty returning July may trigger short-term import surge but channel cautious
items.quote: Prices, like I told before earlier, the prices should be right now on the lower side. It may go down by, let's say, 3% or 4%, not too much downward is there. Again, on the higher side, there is not too much scope also there.

items.statement: Channel inventory currently normal to below normal after March destocking; channel refilling seen in May-June
items.quote: Right now, the channel inventory after March stocking and then again, the prices fell down, the channel has maximum destock themselves, and they are running on a very low inventory.

items.statement: South India plant land acquisition to start after 1 year; plant commissioning ~18 months later, targeting FY28 end
items.quote: You can expect that South India plant will come somewhere in like FY28 end, towards FY28.

items.statement: Government infra spending remains low on ground despite payment release promises; volume confidence driven by core plumbing/agri and dealer additions
items.quote: Government infra still remains low, right, although a lot of promises have come towards like release of payment, etcetera, and kickstart the capex. But we have not seen anything significant coming on ground as of now.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR 3 per share for FY26
items.quote: Considering the robust performance, t he Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR 3 per share for the financial year 2025-2026

items.statement: FY27 capex budget around INR 9,000 crore, majorly for petchem project
items.quote: And I think you had also asked about the proposed CAPEX budget for the current financial year. So, it is around INR 9,000 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex capitalized INR 390 crore in Q4, balance INR 100 crore to be capitalized in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We have capitalized INR 390 crores and balance around INR 100 crores will be capitalized in the next quarter.

items.statement: FY26 actual cash capex INR 2,511 crore vs guided INR 3,000 crore, difference due to provisioning vs cash flow
items.quote: So, the provisioning are different and the cash what has been spent is INR 2,511 crore.

items.statement: Additional storage tank at Kochi estimated at INR 1,200 crore
items.quote: So, it is about around INR 1200 crores.

items.statement: March Dahej utilization 53%, Kochi slightly above 20%; April-May utilization similar to March levels
items.quote: So, the Dahej capacity utilization during March was around 53 % and Kochi was slightly more than 20%.

items.statement: Jan-Feb Dahej utilization averaged ~108%
items.quote: It was on an average of about 108%.

items.statement: Expect Qatar supply to resume within 3-4 weeks after conflict ends, possibly by first week of June
items.quote: We are in constant touch with Qatar Energy and we are hopeful that the moment this conflict comes to an end, within three to four weeks, supply should resume.

items.statement: New Exxon contract (0.5 mtpa) started in April; Equinor contract (Performance Chemiserve) first cargo expected 12th May; combined ~1 mtpa additional volume in FY27
items.quote: Roughly 1 million tons in this year.

items.statement: Force majeure on Qatar supply since March; time charter vessels aligned with SPA term; not liable for time charter costs during force majeure
items.quote: Yes, those time charter vessels are specifically hired for carrying cargo from Qatar to our terminals. So, once the supply resumes, these time charter vessels will be again engaged as being done earlier.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 regas revenue INR 879 crore, inventory gain INR 95 crore, trading gain INR 118 crore
items.quote: So, the regas revenue is INR 879 crores for this quarter. And the inventory gain is INR 95 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 IndAS impact: +INR 119 crore gross margin, -INR 91 crore forex, +INR 8 crore opex, -INR 77 crore depreciation, -INR 59 crore lease interest
items.quote: Yes, the IndAS impact is for the 4th Quarter, 119 positive at gross margin level. Then there is a FOREX loss of INR 91 crores and positive 8 crores at OPEX level. And then depreciation INR 77 crores and interest expense on lease liability INR 59 crores.

items.statement: UOP dues of INR 630 crore for CY22 received in Q4; provision reversal INR 550 crore offset by new provisions INR 35 crore (CY23) and INR 6 crore (CY24) and waiver INR 13 crore
items.quote: During the current quarter, the customers also made payment of outstanding Use of Pay dues amounting to INR 630 crore pertaining to calendar year 2022.

items.statement: Kochi terminal achieved highest ever annual throughput of 68 TBTU in FY26
items.quote: I am also happy to share that the Kochi terminal achieved its highest ever annual volume throughput of 68 TBTU during FY '25-'26, which is an encouraging milestone for the company.

items.statement: Petchem project on track; equipment sourced from Japan, Korea, China, Europe, US - not Gulf region
items.quote: So, far as the project activity for petrochemical plant is concerned, the project is absolutely on track because the capital equipment generally don't come from the Gulf region.

items.statement: Secured new orders worth Rs. 594 crores for four-year program life in Q4 FY26, with 56% from Automotive and 44% from Non-Automotive segments
items.quote: During the Q4, the Company secured new orders worth Rs. 594 crores for the program life of four years. 56% of these orders were from Automotive segment and balance 44% were from the Non-Automotive segment, reflecting continued progress in Company's diversification strategy.

items.statement: Order book for FY27 execution stands at Rs. 1,550 crores including forging and casting businesses
items.quote: So, it has been showcased that Rs. 1,550 crores of new orders will be executed in FY27. So, does that include castings also or is it only forgings stand-alone business that it is showing? Naresh Jalan: No, it is consolidated - forging and casting together

items.statement: Capex for FY27 limited to Rs. 300-400 crores including JV contribution, focus on debt reduction
items.quote: Sunny, this year we are looking at more of consolidation. I think with the contribution in JV, I think we are not looking at cap ex and maintenance. We are not looking at capex of more than Rs. 300 to Rs. 400 crores maximum to the tune of Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: Targeting debt reduction of Rs. 400-500 crores in FY27 backed by promoter funding and performance
items.quote: Certainly, we are looking at a quite significant debt reduction in this year on the back of promoter funding and good performance. All this, so we are looking to reduce the debt by at least Rs. 400 to Rs. 500 crores in this year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 17.1%, up ~220 bps quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: EBITDA excluding other income is Rs. 208.19 crores in Q4, higher by 111% year-on-year compared to EBITDA of Rs. 98.5 crores in Q4 FY25. On Q-on-Q basis, EBITDA was higher by 27% compared to Rs. 163.37 crores in Q3 FY26. The margin improved to 17.1%, higher by almost 2 20 basis points quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Expects margins to improve by 100-150 bps from current levels as utilization scales and energy cost pass-through materializes
items.quote: So, I think the current margin which we have been able to achieve in the fourth quarter, I think now it's here to stay and it we are going to do better margins than what we have achieved right now in this quarter. items.quote: No, as earlier also expressed, all our pricing is based on pass -ons. So, I think with a quarter lag, we pass on all the price increases of commodities. Basically, mainly for commodity for us is steel. Steel is pass-on for us every quarter.

items.statement: Railway revenue share grew to 7.5% in FY26 from 4.6% in FY25; targeting double-digit share in FY27
items.quote: As we had indicated, the Railway business has been a strong pillar of growth. We have taken steps to deepen our footprint and enhance capabilities in this segment in recent years. These are now paying dividends as the share of business from railways grown to 7.5% of revenue in this year against 4.6% a year ago.

items.statement: Casting business targeting 85-90% utilization in FY27, adding Rs. 400-500 crores revenue
items.quote: We expect another Rs. 400 to Rs. 500 crores of revenue for the full year from the casting business on that account.

items.statement: Wheel plant expected to generate Rs. 400-450 crores revenue in FY27
items.quote: But we should be anything between Rs. 400 crores to Rs. 450 crores roughly in terms of revenue from the wheel plant.

items.statement: Trailer axle business targeting Rs. 250 crores revenue and 10% market share in FY27, up from Rs. 120 crores and 4-5% share
items.quote: And I think this year, we are looking at almost doubling this business to Rs. 250 crores and to a market share of about 10%.

items.statement: Export mix expected to exceed 40% in next two years from current levels, driving margin improvement
items.quote: So, I think with the current trend in the overall overseas market and with the new order wins in the European market, we are expecting in next two years our export mix to significantly improve. And I think historically which was 60:40, I think we are looking at going above 40 in terms of our export volumes in the overall scenarios, current scenarios.

items.statement: No capex plan finalized for FY28 yet, discussing with customers on future capacity needs
items.quote: But we have not yet basi cally frozen any capex plan for FY 2028 right now. So still, we are talking to customers and getting their feedback in terms of what next to do in terms of the overall capacity requirements.

items.statement: Target to repay INR 140 crore debt annually for next 3 years, aiming to prepay more
items.quote: Our target will be to repay or to prepay a little more than this.

items.statement: No major capex planned for next 2 years
items.quote: No, we don't plan any major CAPEX now in next 2 years.

items.statement: Decent order book in place for international business
items.quote: And we have a decent order book right now and I am sure our team will work very hard to continue this kind of performance.

items.statement: Europe contract manufacturing margins to improve as MMP scale-ups complete
items.quote: more than top line growth that business is likely to give us better margins in the coming year because it could be manufactured in plants which have completed all its MMP scale ups

items.statement: Emerging markets (Africa) confidence high for next 2-3 years with strong portfolio and field force
items.quote: So, to answer your question in short , yes, the confidence level is pretty high for next 2-3 years on this business.

items.statement: US growth driven by solid orals (INR 12 crore sterile, rest oral solids) and new liquid oral launches planned
items.quote: Sterile is INR 12 crores and the rest is all oral solids.

items.statement: USFDA plant issue unresolved; future approvals at risk but current sales via second sites
items.quote: what will really impact us if the plant situation doesn't get resolved really is the future approvals which should be coming on time.

items.statement: Asset held for sale (land parcel) at book value INR 23 crore; expected to fetch more
items.quote: We should get more, but this is book value.

items.quote: At primary level for internal sales, for the year we have clocked INR 37 crores in India.

items.statement: Warren Remedies OTC revenue INR 120 crore for FY26 (Q4: INR 27.4 crore); API plant validation to take ~1 more year
items.quote: For the year it is 120, I think this quarter it is INR 27.4 crores.

items.statement: Domestic formulation revenue INR 1,739 crore in Q4 FY26, down 6% YoY due to weak season
items.quote: Revenues from domestic formulation business for the quarter are at INR 1,739 million as compared to INR 1,851 million.

items.statement: API revenue declined 23% YoY to INR 315 crore in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Revenues from API business for the quarter de-grew by 23% at INR 315 million as against INR 409 million.

items.statement: Pre-sales outlook of at least 20% growth on FY26 numbers, aiming for INR9,000 crores in FY27
items.quote: If the current sentiment and market conditions hold up, our outlook is that demand on ground will support a pre -sales outlook of at least 20% growth on our FY '26 numbers and aiming for INR9,000 crores.

items.statement: Residential launch pipeline of 11.6 million square feet with GDV of INR11,900 crores for FY27
items.quote: For FY27, the residential launch pipeline stands at 11.6 million square feet with a GDV of INR11,900 crores.

items.statement: Capital expenses of approximately INR6,000 crores over next 4 years for 10 million square feet commercial construction
items.quote: The capital expenses towards the construction of this 10 million square feet will be approximately INR6,000 crores spread over the ne xt 4 years, ranging between INR 1,200 crores to INR1,700 crores per annum.

items.statement: Added INR15,000 crores GDV across 13 million square feet in residential business development during FY26
items.quote: From a business development perspective, for the residential segment, we added INR15,000 crores of GDV across 13 million square feet in projects duri ng FY 26.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin at 28%; Real Estate EBITDA INR525 crores, Leasing EBITDA INR906 crores, Hospitality EBITDA INR207 crores

items.quote: While we are watchful of the macroeconomic uncertainty due to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and the broader implications of AI, the fundamental demand drivers in our core markets remain intact.

items.quote: Brigade's commercial leasing portfolio delivered stable performance in FY26, with cumulative leasing of approximately 1.1 million square feet across new leases, renewals, investor leasing and managed office transactions with sustained occupier preference for Grade A, amenity -rich and technology-enabled assets during the year. items.quote: FY '26 saw a 15% increase in revenue and EBITDA compared to FY '25. RevPAR growth of 6% was driven by a 7% improvement on ADR. Demand for FY '27 remains strongly anchored in domestic travel, with international travel expected to recover gradually.

items.quote: So the project is Brigade Stellaris that we just launched in Q4. That is a pretty high -end project. It's 284 units, and each unit is around INR6 crores plus. So far in Q4, what we did? items.statement: Total capex of INR 1,700 crores earmarked through FY29; INR 815 crores for existing businesses, balance for new verticals (lithium-ion, copper, steel, rubber). FY26 capex was INR 372 crores.

items.statement: Capex phasing: ~INR 600 crores in FY27, ~INR 700 crores in FY28, ~INR 400 crores in FY29. Copper capex ~INR 700 crores over next 3 years.
items.quote: So definitely the year wise if you see the breakup is close to INR 600 crores for next year and INR 700 odd crores in FY '28 and then around INR 400 crores for FY '29. So, this is a broad breakup of INR 1,700 crores

items.statement: No specific order book disclosed; management expects 40-50% copper volume growth in FY27 and 20-25% overall volume CAGR.
items.quote: So, volume numbers , overall, we are planning to grow at around 40 %-50% in copper in this year. So, it will be in the similar range over last year in copper also.

items.quote: Adjusted consolidated EBITDA for FY '26 stood at INR 452.48 crores reflecting a growth of 12% year-on-year with margins remaining healthy at 10.6%.

items.statement: Middle East disruption reduced value-added sales (10-12% of total) and increased inward logistics costs, pressuring Q4 EBITDA. Management expects near-term margin impact but is seeking alternative markets.
items.quote: So, because of this disruption, we could not sell that material to Middle East and therefore the value-added content or value-added products that we used to sell went down and therefore the EBITDA per ton also came down to some extent.

items.statement: Lead volume grew 7% in FY26 to 48,889 MT; aluminum volumes declined due to lack of hedging mechanism on MCX; volumes expected to pick up once hedging is live. Overall volume target 20-25% CAGR.
items.quote: The lead segment reported growth in sales of 7% to 48,889 metric ton per annum driven by capacity additions and stabilization.

items.statement: Value-added products contributed 42% of FY26 revenue, target 50% by Vision 2029. Copper acquisition (RMIL) adds value-added copper products (sheets, brass cups, foils) for electrical, automotive, coinage, ammunition.
items.quote: Value-added products contributed 42% to the overall revenue demonstrating steady progress towards Vision 2029 where the target is a 50% contribution from such offerings.

items.statement: Middle East conflict disrupting 10-12% of sales (value-added products) and increasing logistics costs; aluminum hedging mechanism pending MCX approval; 18% GST hindering formal sector battery collection.
items.quote: A lot of our material goes to the Middle East, around 10% to 12% of the total sales and most of these products that we sell to the Middle East are value-added products. So, because of this disruption, we could not sell that material to Middle East

items.statement: Capex of INR 1,700 crores to be funded from internal accruals; working capital debt expected to rise to INR 800-900 crores after copper recycling plant commissions (currently net debt INR 118 crores).
items.quote: So, debt should be working capital debt of around INR 800 crores to INR 900 crores after the copper coming in once the copper business starting say next year.

items.statement: Total installed capacity ~4.57 lakh MTPA; medium-term target >8 lakh MTPA by FY29. Mundra lead expansion of 80,300 MTPA commissioned Feb 2026 (INR 49 cr). Lithium-ion pilot 6,000 MTPA commissioned Jan 2026 (INR 14 cr). RMIL copper acquisiti
items.quote: Our expansion program is progressing broadly as planned, with total install capacity now at about 4.57 lakh metric ton per annum. We continue to work towards our medium-term target of scaling this up to over 8 lakh metric per annum by FY '29

items.statement: Lithium-ion battery recycling pilot (6,000 MTPA) is early stage; no meaningful revenue expected in FY27; volumes may appear in 2-3 years but not included in FY29 guidance.
items.quote: We are not expecting any major revenue in this year from lithium-ion battery recycling. But in the next 2 to 3 years, I mean you can see some volumes coming. But we are not considering any volume from lithium-ion battery till our FY '29 guidance.

items.statement: Working capital days ~90 in FY26 (elevated due to inventory build for new capacities); guided at 85-90 days going forward including copper business.
items.quote: But going forward, we see it with the copper business coming in and copper business, since that will be more imported one, so it should be close to 85 to 90 days going forward.

items.statement: Phagi lead expansion (45,000 MTPA) expected to commission in Q1 FY27 pending government approvals; Mundra rubber expansion in H1 FY27.
items.quote: It is going to happen in this Q1 only in Jaipur. Akhilesh: Any estimated timeline like end of Q1 or something? Yogesh Malhotra: So, we have already installed the capacities. We are just waiting for the government approvals which can come anywhere probably in the first half of this quarter

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% with EBITDA margin maintained and slight upward trend in EBITDA and net profit margin
items.quote: So, we expect the top line to be growing between 15 -20% around that time, and I'm again being conservative. But 15%, hopefully, yes. And the EBITDA margin would be maintained with the slightly upward trend in EBITDA as well as in the net profit margin.

items.statement: Cotton volume growth expected around 20% for FY27, paddy 20-25%, maize strong growth continuing
items.quote: We have maintained a conservative line on cotton, but I've always said that the cotton will be growing around 20%. It has proved what I made the statement last year, it has grown to 22%. As far as paddy is concerned, paddy has also grown beyond 20-25%.

items.statement: Minimal CapEx budget for plants and processing; strategy favors rentals over ownership; only land bank and vehicles as CapEx
items.quote: As a matter of policy, as a matter of strategy, Nath has not been investing much in CapEx. If you go through my balance sheet, so you will find that we have only land bank as CapEx, and we also have vehicles as CapEx because which we need for ensuring sales production and things like that.

items.statement: Uzbekistan JV contributed INR 15 crores in FY26, first revenue from international operations; Central Asia market ~USD 1 billion in 5-6 years
items.quote: FY26 marks the first year our Uzbekistan JV contributed almost INR 15 crores to our consolidated top line, a landmark achievement in our international expansion journey and a strong validation of our global growth strategy.

items.statement: Cotton-paddy combined portfolio now 58% of revenue mix, up from 52% in FY25; maize emerging as third pillar at 10.72%
items.quote: The cotton-paddy combined portfolio now accounts for 58% of our revenue mix, up from 52% in FY25, a testament to our steady market position in this critical crop.

items.statement: El Nino impact mitigated by geographic diversification, product portfolio across durations, and advance stock positioning at branches

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; cash and bank balance INR 707 million; inventory build-up funded by working capital debt
items.quote: Cash and bank balance stood at INR 707 million. Inventory increased to INR 4,446 million, in line with our planned scaled up for the upcoming season, reflecting our confidence in FY27 demand.

items.statement: Next-gen cotton pipeline includes products better than Sanket and Jumbo; competition now in-house; production stability expected over 2-3 years

items.quote: Plant Nutrition segment, the segment saw a decline of 18%. This is mainly due to China export restrictions, which disturb supply dynamics. We expect this to normalize in the coming year as supply-side pressure ease.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin of 10-12% sustainable in medium term with new alu-zinc line and export ramp-up
items.quote: we feel that an EBITDA margin of anywhere between 10% to 12% is possible and sustainable.

items.statement: Current order book stands at INR350-400 crores, largely from export customers, with customers ordering more in advance to build buffer

items.quote: EBITDA for Q4 FY '26 stood at INR15.64 crores with an EBITDA margin of 6.84%. The year-on-year softness in Q4 margin was entirely attributable to the extraordinary cost escalation in energy and raw materials triggered by the Middle East conflict.

items.statement: Successfully passed through 100% of incremental energy, raw material, consumable and freight costs to customers in new contracts since April 2026
items.quote: all the new orders and the new contracts that the company has been entering into with long-term customers, both domestic and international, we have been able to pass through the entire impact of the incremental costs.

items.statement: Expects robust demand environment in H1 FY27 with strong order visibility from domestic and export markets, assuming no further global conflict escalation
items.quote: We expect the demand environment to remain robust. And with the normalization of energy and raw material costs, assuming no further escalation in global conflicts, our margin recovery in H1 '27 should be meaningful.

items.quote: Pre-painted steel, our highest value product now constitutes 80% of total quantities sold in FY '26, up from 74% in FY '25.

items.quote: anything to do with government policies, external geopolitical conditions, GDP of the country, demand of the country, public sector and private sector projects in the country would -- all of these would define.

items.quote: it is too early to comment whether we will be wanting to raise any fund from the market or not for this project.

items.quote: we can anticipate anywhere between -- let's say, anywhere between INR300 crores to INR500 crores, in that range, of incremental revenue from the new capacity being installed.

items.quote: as a layman, I would say it's fair to assume that a premium of between INR3,000 to INR5,000 a ton is a ballpark that one can say is a fair premium over galvanized steel.

items.quote: we will definitely not breach a level of 2x, and we'll strive to actually be anywhere in the range of between 1x to 1.5x.

items.quote: We pretty much want to continue doing what we are doing with a 15% return profile. And with scale, that keeps us significant. I think that's very important to call out.

items.quote: Hopefully, within FY27, and I think SEBI has facilitated that by extending the DRHP validity to September 30.
