items.quote: As far as new markets is concerned, I think SIS is very focused on India at the moment. Our priority is consolidating market share and accelerating the solutioning aspect. So currently, there is no new international market that we are looking at.

items.statement: Reiterated revenue CAGR of ~75% over FY25-FY28 driven by Bokaro ramp-up and organic growth
items.quote: We reiterate our earlier guidance of a CAGR of approximately 75% over FY '25 to FY '28 period supported by the phased commissioning and ramp -up of Bokaro greenfield project along with continued organic growth across the existing business verticals.

items.statement: EBITDA and PAT CAGR guided at ~45% and ~40% respectively over FY25-FY28
items.quote: In line with the above guidance, operating EBITDA and PAT is expected to grow at a CAGR of nearly 45 % and 40% respectively over the same periods.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin to stabilize at 12-13% and PAT margin at 5-6% by FY28
items.quote: EBITDA and PAT margins are expected to gradually stabilize at around 12 % to 13% and 5% to 6% respectively by FY '28 as the benefits of integration scale and operating leverage begin to materialize.

items.statement: Bokaro greenfield project on track for phased commissioning starting Q1 FY27; cold trials by end of May, hot trials in June
items.quote: FY '26 has been a pivotal year operationally marked by strong progress on our greenfield downstream steel complex at Bokaro, which remains on track for phased commissioning starting quarter one FY '27.

items.statement: Total Bokaro project cost INR803 crores; debt-equity roughly 250-300 crores equity and balance debt
items.quote: So on a total cost of INR803 crores, our debt -equity is at roughly 250 to 300 of equity and balance of debt.

items.statement: Peak long-term debt expected in next 12-15 months; fair to assume INR700-800 crores by end of FY28
items.quote: That's fair. That's fair. That's a fair assumption.

items.statement: Bokaro saleable products: ~6 lakh tons at peak including color coating (2 lakh tons), galvanizing/Galvalume/ZAM (5-6 lakh tons), cold rolling (3-4 lakh tons), pickling (5-6 lakh tons)
items.quote: So if you look at saleable products, it'll be the differences because the highest value add is the color coat. So the leftover of about 3 to 4 lakh tons will be in the form of galvanized, Galvalume or ZAM. And if there is any other balance, it'll be in the form of FHCR or HRPO. So there is a trickle down, but the overa

items.statement: No long-term order book for Bokaro due to short order-to-delivery cycle (~2 weeks) and volatile input costs (zinc, aluminum, magnesium) making forward orders risky
items.quote: But a lot of these products are not long gestation sales periods, you typically have an order to delivery gap of maybe about two weeks. So the order book kind of becomes a little moot. The other factor being that because some of the components are highly volatile in nature, for example zinc or aluminum or magnesium goi

items.statement: Long-term spreads across HR, CR, GI, color coated segments are stable and positive; short-term aberrations not focused on
items.quote: So if you look at long -term averages, the spreads are fairly stable. There are short -term aberrations from time to time and in the steel industry , it's best not to focus on the short -term aberrations. I think long-term the spreads are positive.

items.statement: Targeting Bokaro working capital cycle of 30-40 days; all production under BMW brand; minimal B2C ad spend, focus on B2B
items.quote: So, we are targeting a working capital cycle of about 30 days in Bokaro. But I mean a lot of it will depend on where we buy the steel from, what is the product that we ultimately sell, how much inventory we need to carry on the FC side, etcetera. But I think it's fair to say between 30 to 40 days is comfortable.

items.statement: Base case IRR for Bokaro investment above 20%
items.quote: So, our base case for an investment is a 20%, so in this case it's safe to say it's above that.

items.statement: Blended ROCE expected to reach 15%+ post Bokaro commissioning
items.quote: So on a blended basis, we expect to reach 15 plus.

items.statement: Legacy business peak revenue estimated at INR800-900 crores at full utilization
items.quote: I think it's fair to assume between INR800 crores to INR900 crores.

items.statement: Net worth grown from INR1,000 crores to INR3,000+ crores over 4 years from accruals; sufficient capital to grow 20% in next couple of years
items.quote: Last 4 years, I think our net worth has gone from about INR1,000 crores to INR3,000-plus crores. And basically, all of it from accruals. So, I think we are running a profitable franchise, and we have enough we are -- all the cash is being used to reinvest in the business. So, we think that we have enough ammunition to

items.statement: Aim to increase wealth RM headcount in FY27; no specific number given
items.quote: Our focus is that we should increase the headcount for wealth RMs this year. I don't have a specific number in mind, but because last year had been a difficult year for recruitment.

items.statement: FPD AUM target to increase from INR52,000 crores; no specific number given
items.quote: And coming to asset growth, I think we are close to about INR52,000 crores. And I don't have a number in mind, but we have to increase it.

items.statement: Depreciation increased 20% YoY due to investment in branches and technology
items.quote: Depreciation increased 20% on account of investment in branches and technology.

items.statement: Net interest spread roughly 4%; MTF interest income ~INR160-170 crores in FY26
items.quote: Net interest margin, 18% -- no, 18%, 19%, I think the net interest spread is roughly about 4%.

items.statement: FPD AUM grew from INR31,000 crores to INR52,000 crores; mutual fund assets from INR14,000 crores to ~INR21,000 crores; HNI segment ~INR12,000 crores
items.quote: We have seen a growth in our FPD assets because it was about INR31,000 crores, and it has now become about INR52,000 crores. And we have seen all-round growth, both in mutual fund and other assets also and including our fixed income assets.

items.statement: Short-term impact from RBI regulations effective July 1 on broking business due to increased working capital and margin requirements; cost of F&O trades to increase for clients
items.quote: My view is that there will be a short-term impact for sure because of increased working capital requirements and margin requirements. And then over a period of time, the market finds its own level and goes back to that trend.

items.statement: Income tax search under Section 132; notice for ~INR56 crores for block period April 2018-Feb 2025; appeals filed; no material adverse impact expected
items.quote: We have got a notice which for roughly -- for both IIFL management and IIFL facilities for roughly about INR56 crores combined for the block period from April 1, 2018 up to February 3, 2025.

items.statement: Closed capital credit opportunities fund; raised INR500 crores
items.quote: We launched -- we closed our capital credit opportunities fund. We raised about INR500 crores and this is basically a risk-adjusted higher kind of fund.

items.statement: Board evaluating opportunities for acquisitions, new projects to enhance shareholder value; no definitive event requiring disclosure
items.quote: As a company, the Board continuously evaluates opportunities to enhance shareholder value, whether it's in terms of potential acquisition, new projects and other such and combination.

items.statement: SEBI regulations on domestic mutual fund yields: impact marginal as effective yield already aligned with regulator suggestion
items.quote: Our opinion or our learning is that the impact will be marginal because already effective yield was plus/minus the yield as suggested by the regulator.

items.statement: Operational PBT down 22% YoY in FY26 primarily due to steep increase in employee costs to INR687 crores
items.quote: Operational PBT was down 22%, and that is basically -- primarily driven by increase in the employee expenses.

items.statement: NIM expected to remain between 3.75% to 4%
items.quote: the general guidance which I hav e always given is that, it will be between 3.75% to 4%. We are right in the middle of it, som ewhere at 3.83% in Q4 FY 26

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio to remain 60-65% till end of FY2027, then decline from FY2028
items.quote: On the CTI, I would always say that we will be between 60% to 65% till end of FY2027. FY2028 onwards, the operative leverage will kick in.

items.statement: Loan growth target of around 25% for FY2027, dependent on deposit growth
items.quote: I think 25% is so mething that we will strive for. We will be disappointed if we do not do that part, that much at least

items.statement: ROA around 1.5% and ROE around 15% expected to sustain in FY2027
items.quote: I think a range of somewhere around 1.5% and 15% for ROA and ROE respectively will sustain.

items.statement: Meaningful retail asset growth to start from FY2028 onwards
items.quote: Our meaningful growth in retail assets will start from FY2028 onwards.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio target of 30% of total portfolio by 2030, with 5% as working capital loans
items.quote: Our eventual play is to bring gold loan to 30% of our portfolio by 2030. Out of that, at least 5% of that 30% will be working capital loan.

items.statement: NRI deposits target of at least 20% of total deposits in the long run
items.quote: In the long run, at least 20% of our deposits/liability must come from NRI and we have created a separate vertical structure for this.

items.statement: Implementing transaction banking systems (Vayana, Aurionpro, Oracle trade) in next 3-4 months
items.quote: We are also planning to imp lement the entire transaction banking systems in the next three to four months in the form of Vayana in supply chain finance, Aurion pro in CMS and trade products on the core itself from the Oracle

items.statement: Q4 FY2026 NIM at 3.83%, down 2-3 bps QoQ due to yield compression from repo rate cuts
items.quote: Our quarterly advance growth is 9% and the NIM has fallen by two or three basis points over Q3. On a year on year basis i.e., vis a vis Q4 FY 25, the NII is up by 25%.

items.statement: Gold loans increased to 53% of portfolio YoY, partly due to reclassification of loan against gold security
items.quote: Our gold portfolio increased by around 9% in the mix - from around 44% to around 53%. When you see on the retail side, the retail portfolio has exactly decreased by that mix.

items.statement: ECL transition impact not significant due to existing contingency provisions of Rs.210 crores
items.quote: The transition impact is not a significant number for us at the moment as we h ave some advantage because of the aggressive provisions that we make on th e NPAs and even on standard assets, we have this additional contingency provision created at the time of Covid which is above Rs.105 Crores

items.statement: SMA book at lowest level in last five quarters as of Q4 FY2026
items.quote: Almost at every busine ss or at a bank wide level, our SMA book has constantly been improving and as we are talking on Q4, the SMA book is lowest in the last five quarters

items.statement: SME/BLG growth deliberately kept at 2-3% YoY in FY2026 due to West Asia crisis and tariff issues
items.quote: SME and LAP together we call it BLG, which is Business Lending Group. That grew around 2% to 3% last year, year-on-year basis and this is something we did consciously because we saw a strange situation last year.

items.statement: SME growth to accelerate to 28-30% range in next two years once West Asia crisis clarity emerges
items.quote: Whatever happened, single-digit growth is given and hopefully we will be back to that 28%-30% growth range in the next two years.

items.statement: Deposit cost reduced 10 bps from Q1 FY2026 levels, wholesale deposit cost down over 30 bps
items.quote: If you look at our quarter wise deposit cost for the FY, it has been coming down, with significantly higher cost reduction in wholesale dep osits. If I remember correctly, our deposit cost came down by 10bps from Q1 levels. On the wholesale side, it came down by more than 30 bps or more

items.statement: Successfully migrated to new core banking system (Oracle) with 50+ surround systems in May 2025
items.quote: We have successfully migrated to the new core banking system with OGL, OFSAA and 50 and odd surround systems around it.

items.statement: Plan to open 150 showrooms across Kalyan, Candere and new regional brand in FY27
items.quote: During the ongoing financial year, we plan to open 150 showrooms across Kalyan, Candere and the new regional brand.

items.statement: Recommend 10% SSSG for 3-5 year projections despite recent 20-30% actuals
items.quote: If you are trying to put a number for the next 3 - 5 years, we usually don't guide more than 10% SSSG for next 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Candere to open 50-55 stores in FY27 similar to last year
items.quote: So, it will be in the similar line of the last financial year, 50-55.

items.statement: India PBT margin expected to stay in 5.5-5.6% range with possible slight improvement
items.quote: So now if you look at this financial year, meaning the previous financial year, the PBT India has been in the range of, what, 5.5% - 5.6%. I think that is here to stay.

items.statement: Candere gross margins in mid-30s due to over 70% studded ratio
items.quote: The gross margin store level Candere is in mid-30s because the studded ratio are more than 70%.

items.statement: Interest cost to reduce by INR30 crores in FY27 from non-GML debt repayment of INR300 crores
items.quote: Yes, because INR300 crores is what we have to now reduce the non-GML. So INR300 crores, if you put an approximate 9%, 10%, it's INR30 crores.

items.statement: INR20 crores one-off interest on advance tax in FY26 interest cost
items.quote: Yes, yes, INR20 crores.

items.statement: April started very well with strong Akshaya Tritiya sales and encouraging wedding demand momentum
items.quote: As we speak, April has started off very well. And even with high basis, we have been able to grow.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 may see slower wedding days due to Adhik-Maas but some preponement possible
items.quote: But yes, there is high possibility that those days can be slower than our usual wedding. But there are people who preponed their purchase also if there's an Adhik-Maas.

items.statement: Akshaya Tritiya coin sales lower than estimated unlike Dhanteras where they exceeded estimates
items.quote: Yes, the coin sales were lower than estimated, unlike Dhanteras where it was more than estimated.

items.statement: No gold supply issues despite Middle East tensions; banks supply via IIBX and domestic sources
items.quote: So, there is abundant supply of gold in the country, and we continue to receive regular inventory from our banks.

items.statement: Aim to make India non-GML debt-free in FY27, possibly by H1 if things go well
items.quote: Yes. So, we want to make it a non -GML debt-free in the running financial year. And yes, if things go really well, we might do it by H1 itself.

items.statement: New regional brand launch delayed waiting for post-election situation to settle in target state
items.quote: So, it is on, but the post-election dust has not been settled in the state where we want to open our new brand. So, we are just waiting for the dust to settle down, and we start our campaign.

items.statement: Middle East franchisee conversion with Arab investors underway but not materialized; no guidance given
items.quote: But we are focusing on a major franchisee expansion in the Middle East through Arab Investors. But nothing has materialized, but it's going in the right direction.

items.statement: Asset disposal timeline for first set of INR180 crores before September 2025; second set process started
items.quote: The time line set for the set no 1 asset disposal was before September of this year, which I think is going in the right direction. And we have also started process to release the second set of assets from the banks.

items.statement: Capital allocation: ~50% of cash for dividends, debt reduction, capex; balance for Candere and regional brand
items.quote: Yes. So close to 50% of the cash generated will be used for dividends and debt reduction, capex, etc. Balance 50%, we have to park some funds for Candere and the regional brand.

items.statement: Expect to outperform underlying industry growth by 1.5x to 2x in FY27 based on order book over 85% of forecasted revenue
items.quote: Based on our current strong performance, execution visibility and the current order book being over 85% of the FY27 forecasted revenue, we expect to outperform underlying industry growth by 1.5x to 2x in FY27.

items.statement: Target export revenue share of 14% to 15% of consolidated revenue by FY28
items.quote: We are working towards increasing share of exports in our consolidated revenue to 14% to 15% by FY 28, driven by deeper penetration in existing markets, entry into new geographies and the addition of new customers.

items.statement: Total capex of INR 260-270 crores over 3 years from FY26, with INR 80 crores spent in FY26 and balance in FY27-FY28
items.quote: So put together, there is an investment close to INR220 crores. Apart from that, we have the normal capex, which is around INR15 - 20 crores per annum. So on a 3-year basis, we could say INR260 crores, INR270 crores.

items.statement: Long-term sustainable EBITDA margin target of 27-28% with high growth trajectory
items.quote: But in the long term, I think that 27% - 28% sort of margins with a high growth trajectory is what you should expect from SJS.

items.statement: Decoplast chrome plating greenfield plant in Pune in final commissioning, will double capacity
items.quote: The new plant at Pune is complete for the chrome plating facility that we've added, where we are doubling capacity there. And so the plant is just in the final stages of commissioning.

items.statement: Full year FY27 EBITDA margin target around 23%, aiming for 25% over next couple of years
items.quote: I think this year, the full year target is to have an EBITDA margin of around 23% in terms of EBITDA. So -- and our aim is that ultimately, over the next couple of years, the EBITDA margin should reach to about 25% annually.

items.statement: Skid assemblies capacity expanding from 6,000 to 15,000 units per annum by next two quarters; peak utilization 75-80%
items.quote: Currently, we have scaled our skid assemblies capacity from 2,000 units per annum to 6,000 units per annum, and we are on track to further expand the same by the next two quarter to 15,000 skids per annum.

items.statement: Two robotic welding lines commissioned; new annealing furnace targeted for commissioning by end of this year
items.quote: have commissioned 2 robotic welding lines to enhance automation, precision and operational efficiency. In addition, we are also investing in advanced manufacturing capabilities, including a new annealing furnace facility targeted for commissioning by the end of this year

items.statement: Exclusive long-term contract with one supplier for skid assemblies; annual pipeline shared, broken into quarterly POs; order book not disclosed due to agreements
items.quote: we work on a long-term contract with our, with the suppliers with whom we have an exclusive contract. And they have given a pipeline for the entire year and then they break it down into quarterly POs.

items.statement: Skid assemblies sold 617 units (~INR21.2 cr) in last 4 months of FY26; targeting 60-70% utilization of 15,000 capacity by March FY27 (INR325-330 cr revenue at 75% utilization)
items.quote: In the last financial year, we achieved a strong traction in our skid assemblies business with the sales of 617 skid assemblies, which resulted in an overall sales of approximately INR21.2 crores, and this has been done over the last 4 months itself.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 23.86% (+326 bps YoY); FY26 EBITDA margin 22.6%; skid assembly margins in line with company average
items.quote: We have achieved an EBITDA margin of 23.86% in Q4, which also reflects our strong operating leverage and also is a result of the continued improvement in our product mix.

items.statement: Value-added products (assemblies, fittings, bellows) 52% of FY26 sales; domestic share rose to 31% from 26% driven by skid assemblies and Hyd-Air
items.quote: Our value -added product segment, which includes assemblies and fittings and bellows contributed 52% of the total sales. The domestic sales contribution has also increased to 31% from 26%.

items.statement: Metal bellows FY26 revenue INR8 cr (mostly Q3-Q4); ARR now ~INR12 cr; targeting 50-60% capacity utilization in 2-3 years (peak revenue ~INR80 cr)
items.quote: In the current year, on an annual basis, we did about INR 8 crores of business from the metal bellows section. And the majority of the business came in, in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Design finalization and stringent end-customer quality audits are current bottlenecks for skid assembly ramp-up; expect to streamline over next couple of months
items.quote: the main bottleneck is from the design aspect, where the design which was initially to be provided by the principal is actually now being done by our entire team. So designing of the skid assemblies is the critical aspect here.

items.statement: Income tax demand ~INR40 cr (FY18 assessment year reopened); management confident of reversal on appeal due to prior disclosures and time-bar issues
items.quote: We have already -- we had done the necessary disclosures in both our financials and our income tax return. So we are confident that this is something, which will be -- which would come in our favor in the appeal that we are going to file.

items.statement: US tariff on products reduced to 10-15% range from mid-February; no current tariff issues
items.quote: I think it's around 15%, but I will have to just double check. I think in the range of between 10% to 15%.

items.statement: International skid assembly supply targeted in FY27; open to partnerships beyond exclusive domestic partner
items.quote: our aim is to have or to start at least some supply of skid assemblies in the international market in the current financial year.

items.statement: New data center hose assemblies under development and customer approval; annealing furnace to support; sales expected from next quarter
items.quote: We have already started developing those products. It is under approval at the customers end. Also, our annealing plant that we are coming to commission would also contribute to this.

items.statement: Skid assembly ASP range INR3-3.25 lakh per unit; wide range due to varying data center specifications
items.quote: I would say to consider an average, I think INR3 lakhs to INR3.25 lakhs would be an average that we can consider in terms of the average selling price for skid assembly.

items.statement: Management guides for 20% AUM growth, 20% profit growth, and 17-18% disbursement growth in the short to medium term.
items.quote: As we go ahead, we would continue with similar guidance of 20% AUM, 20% profit and 17% to 18% disbursement growth.

items.statement: Management targets INR 50,000 crore AUM in three years, implying continued ~20% CAGR.
items.quote: If I look at the trajectory of numbers that I've guided 20% growth, if I look at 3 years from now, the next milestone, obviously in 3 years should be INR50,000.

items.statement: Added 5 branches in Q4 FY26 and 46 branches in FY26, taking total network to 626 branches across 22 states.
items.quote: We have added 5 new branches in quarter 4 and 46 branches in the full year, in line with our strategy, taking our total network to-date to -- as of March 31 to 626 branches across 22 states.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved by ~55 bps YoY to 35.9% in FY26, in line with guidance of ~50 bps reduction.
items.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio for FY '26 came in at 35.9% as compared to 36.4% in FY '25, an improvement of approximately 55 bps. This is in line with our guidance of dropping cost-to-income ratio by about 50 bps in the current financial year.

items.statement: Exit spread improved to 5.82% in March 2026 from 5.7% a year ago; management guides for 8-10 bps YoY spread compression.
items.quote: We have always guided that our spreads year-on-year will probably see some contraction to the extent of about 8 bps to 10 bps.

items.statement: Management expects cost of funds to remain stable for the next 2-3 quarters; would be happy to maintain current exit rate of 7.7%.
items.quote: If we are able to maintain 7.7% cost throughout the entire next year, I'll be very, very happy to be very honest.

items.statement: Demand remains stable and end-user driven, supported by first-time homebuyers and government schemes like PMAY; strong traction seen in multiple states.
items.quote: We believe demand in our segment will continue to remain stable and end user driven, supported by first-time homebuyers and increased penetration in underserved markets.

items.statement: LAP mix deliberately kept lower at ~25-26% of disbursements (vs typical 28-29%) due to caution on tariff and geopolitical issues; room to increase to 27-28% when appropriate.
items.quote: We did incrementally about 26% loan against property in Q4 FY26, and we want to maybe take it to about 27%,28% in the current quarter, and we'll wait out, as I said.

items.statement: No signs of stress from West Asia conflict; bounce rates stable for 6 quarters, customers largely in essential commodities, minimal NRI exposure.
items.quote: West Asia war or the current geopolitical issues, the first line of defense, and I always make this statement for us, the first line of defense is always if there was something to be going wrong, it would be the bounce rate increase or decrease in the bounce rate. Fortunately, the last -- the current month, 3 cycles of bounce rates have not seen any trend whatsoever.

items.statement: Management targets another ~50 bps reduction in cost-to-income ratio in FY27 driven by productivity gains and AI-driven models.
items.quote: We're looking at another 50 bps probably in the next financial year. What will be driving this is a combination of productivity, some of the projects that we have taken up on sales productivity, which will come from our AI-driven models that we will be able to deliver on productivity.

items.statement: GNPA improved sequentially by 30 bps to 1.08%; collection efficiency above 99.8%; Stage 2 assets improved by 30 bps; 1+ DPD improved by 78 bps sequentially.
items.quote: Asset quality remains pristine with gross NPA standing at 1.08%, a sequential improvement of 30 bps versus quarter 3 FY26. Collection efficiency continues to remain strong, above 99.8%, reflecting consistent on-the-ground execution.

items.statement: ESOP cost of INR 13.5 crores booked in Q4 FY26 and full year FY26 is a one-time charge; no impact expected in FY27.
items.quote: Also included in the manpower cost for quarter 4 FY '26 is an amount of INR13.5 crores, both in quarter 4 FY '26 and full year FY '26, which is the impact of fresh ESOPs that we have granted to employees in the quarter 4 of the current financial year. The impact of this is in the quarter 4 and full year is INR13.5 crores.

items.statement: Other income includes one-time items of INR 6-7 crores (IT refund INR 2.5 crores + old write-backs INR 3.5 crores).
items.quote: One was an IT refund of about INR2.5 crores that we have taken back to the P&L. And the second was some old write-backs that we had, which we had not done for a long time, and that is about to the extent of about INR3.5 crores. So put together, it is the extent -- in the range of about INR6 crores to INR7 crores that we had as a onetime, which is sitting in the fee income.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth projected at low to mid-teens with EBITDA margin expansion of 75-100 bps assuming stable regulations and macro conditions
items.value: low to mid-teen revenue growth; 75-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: In FY27, we project low to mid-teen revenue growth and as I have been explaining in the last meet and a few calls that I have had the privilege of addressing to you guys that EBITDA margin expansion will happen as committed between 75 to 100 basis points going forward, assuming stable regulations and macroeconomic conditions.

items.statement: Capex guided at INR400-425 crores for FY27
items.quote: Yes. So I think we guide around that INR400 crores rough number. I think we'll broadly be in that range of INR400 - 425-ish crores.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin improved 80 bps to 19.4% despite higher R&D spend
items.quote: EBITDA margins improved 80 bps to 19.4% reflecting improved utilization and productivity gains. The EBITDA margin improvement is despite the increase in R&D investments during the year.

items.statement: Raw material price increases from Middle East conflict partially baked into guidance; 1-2 quarters inventory buffers; pass-through evolving
items.quote: So I think it's a mix. I think the guidance we are guiding out includes the current what we are seeing in terms of the pricing.

items.statement: Domestic industry growth expected at 8-9% in FY27; Emcure targets low double-digit growth above industry
items.quote: I think we continue to expect industry growth to be around 8% to 9%, and for us, the target, is to grow faster than the industry – probably at low double-digits.

items.statement: In-licensing contributes ~15% of domestic sales; strategy remains organic-led but open to accretive in-licensing
items.quote: In-licensing makes up for the domestic about 15% of our sales.

items.statement: ARV order book remains robust in Rest of World markets supporting sustained growth
items.quote: In the rest of the world markets, we expect sustained growth led by non-ARV pipeline and robust ARV order book.

items.statement: Middle East conflict driving solvent shortages, higher freight and insurance costs; industry-wide issue; inventory buffers cover 1-2 quarters
items.quote: The solvents that we require for active pharmaceutical ingredients are not available and that is an industry-wide problem that we are facing. Even for that matter one must admit that the insurance cost and the freight cost have also gone up because of the longer route that is required to be taken.

items.statement: Zuventus integration on track from April; Q4 softness due to restructuring and attrition; field force ~4,000 MRs with 40% in Zuventus
items.quote: As you know, acute is largely a short-term treatment, right? So, if you have a gap in the field force, it does lead to a much higher sales drop than what you will see in the normal chronic business. Coming to your question on the field force, about 40% of the field force is in Zuventus for us.

items.statement: Semaglutide (Poviztra) early uptake promising after April price cut; rDNA biologic differentiation vs synthetic generics; 1,000 reps promoting
items.quote: Now with this price reduction, I think we have a real sweet spot in terms of the pricing vis-a-vis the generics. And of course, across specialties, there's close to 1,000 sales reps that are actively promoting this product.

items.statement: Europe business expected mid-teens CAGR over next 2 years driven by Amphotericin B scale-up
items.quote: In the near term, the growth, we do expect it to be stronger in Europe, especially as Amphotericin B gets launched. But yes, once it reaches the scale, so I think over the next 2 years, we do still expect mid-teens growth in the Europe business as a CAGR.

items.statement: Canada semaglutide launch via Dr. Reddy's partnership in Q2 FY27 for Quebec market; own filing also underway
items.quote: You'll be happy to know that our Mantra subsidiary in Quebec has partnered with Dr. Reddy's and we'll be launching the product hopefully sometime in Q2 and then ramp up from there.

items.statement: Employee expenses expected to grow ~10% in FY27
items.quote: Yes, we expect it to be around 10% next year.

items.statement: Roche nephrology in-licensing: no upfront payment; portfolio <INR50 crores annualized

items.quote: For some services which are very routine, low technology, low science, those kind of services price competition will always be there. But then there are some specialty services where the scientific input is very critical.

items.statement: FY27 constant currency revenue growth guided at 10-13% and EBIT margin at 12.25-12.75%
items.quote: We are guiding to constant currency growth for FY27 to be in the 10% to 13% range, and we are guiding for EBIT margin band of 12.25% to 12.75% for FY27.

items.statement: Debt increased by INR 200 crores in FY26 vs INR 700 crores in FY25; cash flow healthy, debt expected to decline; 40-50% of cash flow paid as dividend, 50% used for acquisitions/growth
items.quote: Last year the debt had increased by around INR700 crores, while the current year the debt increase is INR 200 crores. So it has been come down, we have actually repaid.

items.quote: Demand remains centered on regulatory compliance, financial and economic crimes, customer experience, and cost efficiency, and we are seeing strong pull for our AI and automation-led, outcome-oriented transformation offerings.

items.statement: Shift to agentic operating model: revenue per employee up 12% over 2 years; revenue growth materially faster than headcount growth; attrition improved to 29.7% down ~6pp over 8 quarters
items.quote: Over the last two years, our revenue per employee has gone up by 12%. Our revenue growth over the last two years has been materially faster than our headcount growth and we expect that gap to widen as agentic operations scale.

items.statement: New commercial constructs: platform fee plus per-interaction pricing with outcome accountability; K-shaped growth dynamic where higher value per interaction drives greater volume allocation
items.quote: This is not a chatbot. It's a governed autonomous collector with outcome accountability through a platform fee plus per interaction pricing, where higher value per interaction can drive greater volume allocation, supporting a K-shaped growth dynamic.

items.statement: Domestic motorcycle industry growth expected to slow to 7-9% in near term from 20% in Q4, driven by 125cc+ and 150cc+ segments growing at twice industry rate
items.quote: This is bound to slow down the mot orcycle category from its rocking 20% growth in Q4 to we estimate 7% to 9% in the near term. But having said that, the great thing from our point of view is that we expect this growth to come almost entirely from the 125cc plus segment and even more so from the 150cc plus segment, which should grow at twice the industry rate.

items.statement: Exports targeting 220,000 units per month in Q1 FY27, up from 200,000 levels, despite Gulf region loss
items.quote: We are looking at moving the exports needle to 2,20,000 units per month this quarter, up from the 2,00,000 levels. And this, despite the loss of business in the Gulf region, we are, of course, hoping that there will be no further disruptions due to the geopolitical issues in the Middle East.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 commodity cost inflation estimated at 3.5-4% of revenue; pricing actions cover ~40% of impact; currency at INR 94-95 provides cushion
items.quote: Taken together, we are currently estimating a material cost inflation impact of approximately 3.5% to 4% of revenue. And this is from an overall portfolio perspective. It will, of course, vary across models and segments. But this is based on the current outlook. And as you would imagine, it is very volatile and dynamic and the situation could change. So, the 3.5% - 4% of revenue that I'm calling o

items.statement: Price hikes taken from 1st April covering ~40% of commodity inflation impact; further pricing actions possible but will be choiceful

This is bound to slow down the mot orcycle category from its rocking 20% growth in Q4 to we estimate 7% to 9% in the near term.

items.statement: Chetak EV retail crossed 1 lakh units in Q4 (March 50,000+); market share ~23%; unserviced demand spillover from March-April due to 10-15% supply chain impairment
items.quote: In quarter 4, Chetak crossed the 1 lakh retail mark for the very first time in a single quarter, the highest ever quarterly retails for the brand. March '26 was the largest mon th with retails touching 50,000 plus levels. Market share has moved up to almost 23%, a gain of 170 basis points sequentially.

items.statement: Supply chain difficulties (LPG shortage, manpower, outbound logistics) impairing ability to service demand by 10-15%; commodity inflation volatile and event-driven; Middle East geopolitical risk to exports
items.quote: Supply chain difficulties in terms of the LPG shortage, manpower availability and outbound logistics to overseas markets have impaired availability to service demand by about 10% to 15%. Hopefully, these will start to resolve themselves over a period of time. The cost environment is seeing a potential rise during the quarter of about 3% to 5%, driven by the metal complex.

items.quote: Lastly, the Board of Directors at its meeting earlier today approved a payout of 100% of the profits that we have made last year in recognition of the 100 years milestone of the Bajaj family in India and with Bajaj Auto being the flagship company that star ted it all. his will be split as follows a final dividend of INR150 per share that will aggregate to INR4,192 crores and the balance of about I

items.quote: Sequentially, we look to hold margin flat, essentially supported by favorable currency, richer mix and operating leverage. items.statement: 3-wheeler industry growth 25%+ in Q4 and April driven by structural demand from non-metro mobility, road network expansion, shared mobility, women workforce participation; capacity expansion underway for larger format 3Ws
items.quote: The industry growth in 3 -wheelers in quarter 4 total was 25% plus. In April, it was 25% plus again. And you are very right. A lot of this was because of the EVs, which are growing. items.quote: As for KTM, the focus in 2026 continues to be to drive along with the Executive Board and through them, the broad -based turnaround plan covering work streams on portfolio priorities, product development, go -to-market, supply chain, including sourcing, org anizational and structure simplification with a view to rationalizing fixed costs. I expect the results of this to start showing up in the lat

items.quote: To give you a sense of numbers, AUM has r eached nearly INR19,000 crores, roughly doubling in the course of the year, and disbursements for the year were a tad under INR15,000 crores. items.statement: Aspiration to consistently deliver 20%+ AUM growth and outperform industry
items.quote: Our aspiration clearly is to consistently deliver 20% -plus AUM growth, largely to outperform industry.

items.quote: We continue to maintain our guidance on keeping credit costs under check and below 25 bps on a sustainable basis.

items.statement: Opex to AUM ratio target below 3% on a 2-to-3-year platform
items.quote: I think on a 2-to-3-year platform, yes. We are shooting for something below 3%.

items.quote: We maintain that once we reach a double size of the balance sheet, it will be somewhere 2.75% opex to AUM ratio.

items.quote: The cumulative 125 basis repo cut by RBI has improved affordability, creating strong tailwinds for the segment, which is affordable housing.

items.statement: Focus on rebuilding direct sourcing muscle through CSC, website, app and referral program; indirect channels continue as important part of ecosystem
items.quote: We just want to continue building our own strengths, which is direct sourcing through channels like CSC, develop our digital avenues, which is the website, our own app, which has a referral program.

items.statement: No concentration risk; diversified retail book; monitoring 5-6 profiles potentially affected by Middle East situation but no impact seen yet
items.quote: It's a very diversified book over a period of time. And hence, that's the strength of the retail business. There's no concentration risk at all.

items.quote: During FY26, we also successfully secured commitment of ~Rs. 975 crores, USD 108 million, from a marquee multinational financial institution at a very competitive cost.

items.statement: Added 31 branches in Q4, total network 435 branches across 15 states; expansion focused on Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat
items.quote: During the last quarter, we added 31 branches, bringing our total network to 435 branches across 15 states.

items.statement: AUM grew 15% Y-o-Y to Rs. 234.5 billion; disbursements grew 11% to Rs. 67.8 billion for FY26
items.quote: Our AUM at the end of FY26 stood at Rs. 234.5 billion, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 15%, while disbursements for the year grew 11% at Rs. 67.8 billion.

items.statement: Target AUM of INR 6,500 crores by March 2027 (FY27 end)
items.quote: I spoke of, March '27, we are likely to exit at INR6,500 crores of AUM.

items.statement: Target disbursement of INR 500 crores/month for next 3-4 months, then INR 550-600 crores/month
items.quote: we want to retain at that level for at least next three-four months and then aim for about INR550 crores to about INR600 crores as we progress

items.statement: Cost of borrowings expected below 12.5% blended for FY27
items.quote: overall for the year, we believe it should be, below 12.5%.

items.quote: NIM contracted to 9.9% compared to 11.1% largely on the impact of cost of borrowings which we have seen in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Yield improved to 22.8% in Q4 from 22.4% in Q3; incremental disbursement yield ~25.25%
items.quote: Yield for the quarter got positive impact because of this movement into better portfolio mix. So, it is at 22.8% compared to 22.4% in Q3.

items.statement: Opex target 7-8% of AUM in medium term; current INR 160 crores/quarter can optimize further without cutting corners
items.quote: in the medium term, it should come down to about 7% to 8% opex to AUM, and in the near term, can INR160 crores come down? That's what we are aiming for.

items.statement: Customer satisfaction score improved from 22% in Q3 to 71% in Q4; targeting 95% by end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: our score, which was about 22% in Q3 has gone up to 71%. We are still not very happy, we are aiming for a 95% score either before the end of this quarter or early next quarter

items.statement: Merger with CFL subsidiary expected to complete in 5-6 months
items.quote: On the merger front, the process has begun, might take another 5-6 months, we are working on it.

items.statement: Spread guidance maintained at 5% to 5.25% portfolio level
items.quote: Our aim remains to deliver a spread at a portfolio level in our guided range of 5% to 5.25%.

items.quote: Our branch strategy is to add about 30 to 40 branches every year. So that is what we are planning.

items.quote: Net interest margin for Q4 stood at 5.9%, while there was a modest sequential compression of 10bps, NIM remains robust and continues to reflect the strength of our business model.

items.statement: PLR cut of 10bps in January, no further PLR cuts planned in near term
items.quote: We have already done with the 10 basis points in January. So we will want to stay put for now.

items.statement: Demand improved from October onwards, April disbursements strong, no impact from Middle East crisis observed
items.quote: The demand also started improving from October onwards. So all these things kind of came together in the last two quarters and that helped us deliver these good results.

items.quote: We are looking at somewhere between 15% to 20% loan against property. We are somewhere in the middle of that 16% or 17%. So the ratio of housing to LAP will broadly remain in the same ballpark, which is about 80% -20%.

items.statement: No visible impact from Middle East crisis on collections or demand as of April

items.statement: AI implementation focused on cost productivity first, origination impact gradual, agents live for income assessment and bank statement analysis

items.quote: It should get addressed this quarter. Some progress has been made in the first month of April. And by the end of May, hopefully, all the issues should get addressed. So I think June should be a normal month.

items.statement: Operating cost to assets expected to remain range-bound at 2.6% to 2.7%
items.quote: As we continue to invest for growth, we expect this ratio to remain broadly range-bound within 2.6% to 2.7%.

items.statement: CRAR at 44.1% (Tier I 43.8%) post QIP, net worth INR4,357 crores, book value INR418/share
items.quote: As of Mar'26, our Capital to risk-weighted assets ratio (CRAR) stood at 44.1% with Tier I at 43.8%.

items.statement: Write-offs INR36 crores for FY26, auctioning 50-100 units monthly (~1,000 annually)
items.quote: Total write-off has been – this year has been about INR36 crores.

items.statement: Management guides for approximately 30% growth and historically beats that guidance.
items.quote: We always guide about 30%, we always beat that guidance.

items.statement: Term insurance riders attachment (critical illness, accidental protection) has increased post-September due to 18% price reduction from GST changes.
items.quote: But people have been buying a little bit more of the riders. So, things like a critical illness rider, the attachment of that has gone up; some of the accidental protection riders, their attachment has gone up.

items.statement: Conversion rates have increased post-September as customers are more aware of insurance value.
items.quote: Both of these changes are dwarfed by a different change, which is the fact that our conversion rate has gone up. So, for the people who are coming, more of them are buying.

items.quote: I'm happy to share that the Board has approved the 100% acquisition of Citelum India Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of the French government, marking our foray i nto the smart lighting and urban infrastructure space.

items.quote: The margin profile of the corporate sector also has increased over the period of time that we saw, which in the post -pandemic era. So -- and of course, it depends on the service delivery capability.

items.statement: Government segment awarded 17 new contracts in FY26 and 2 in Q4 FY26 with profitability-first approach
items.quote: The government segment recorded 2 new contracts awarded during Q4 FY '26 and 17 new contracts awarded on a full year basis, reflecting this measured and profitability-first approach.

items.statement: Debt-equity comfortable at 0.22; loan and advances at INR146.45 crores expected to reduce meaningfully near term

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR1.50 per equity share (face value INR10) for FY26
items.quote: I am happy to share that Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR1.50 per equity share of face value of INR10 for the financial year '26, subject to approval of shareholders.

items.statement: Taskmaster B2C platform revenue INR46 lakhs in FY26; no 2-3 year guidance given as still in pilot phase
items.quote: Currently -- the Taskmaster currently has -- it is a start-up. So, it has posted a revenue of about INR46 -- in this year, INR46 lakhs. We are building it.

items.statement: Bioenzyme technology commercialization under pilot projects with VPRC; no fixed commercial cost or timeline yet
items.quote: Currently, as you know, we have a strategic association with VPRC, Vishnu Prasad Research Center, in Chennai. And we are doing various pilot projects with their enzymes. So, this is -- we're already running these pilots in Mira -Bhayandar and Vasai Virar gar bage dumps.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at minimum 15% with renewable sector contributing 20-25% of total revenue
items.quote: For Financial Year '27, we are guiding 15% minimum revenue growth with renewable sector contributing close to 20% to 25% of the total revenue, further building up our diversification.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance sustained at 11-12.5% range
items.quote: EBITDA margins expected to sustain between 11% to 12.5% and order inflow guidance of minimum INR5,500 crores.

items.quote: Total order inflow for the year stood at INR11,332 crores, significantly surpassing our annual guidance of INR5,000 crores for Financial Year 26.

items.statement: Cost escalation compensated by authorities on monthly basis per new government circular
items.quote: The increased cost is already compensated by the department; they already come up with the circular for compensating the escalation part and earlier it was linked to 3 months and now it has been linked to monthly basis.

items.quote: Our standalone debt-to-equity stood at 0.2x as on March 31, 2026. On a consolidated basis, it stood at 0.6.

items.quote: From a strategic standpoint, we made a conscious decision to accept relatively tighter margins in data centre orders, solar orders, and semiconductor projects to establish credentials and build a strong pipeline of orders.

items.quote: We are about 23 solar active hot leads available, number one. Number 2, we have Waree reference getting established. We have Satvik and Gupin getting established. IMR will add more to those names. And there is a very beautiful large order which is about to happen.

items.quote: From a financial standpoint, in FY26, we reported a consolidated total income of 221.72 crores up 46.93% year on year from 150.90 crores last year, with a EBITDA at 23.16 crores, growing 28.31% year on year from 18.5 18.05 crores.

items.statement: Management projects 35-40% revenue growth for FY27 and targets EBITDA margin of 10-10.5%.
items.quote: We grew about 40% last year in terms of revenue, and we have historically mentioned that we will be looking for 40% growth for the next two years. So, yes, the projected revenue growth is about 35% to 40%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin sweet spot is 10-10.5%; Q4 adjusted for INR 5 cr ECL provision was 10-10.2%.
items.quote: No, so we would maintain an EBITDA of around 10 % to 10.5%. That is our sweet spot, and we will keep our consistent growth and numbers in the area.

items.statement: Targets Contract Manufacturing revenue share of 55-60% and Services share of 9-10% in FY27.
items.quote: I think it would be a fair assumption. We will be looking to target about 55% to 60% contribution from Contract Manufacturing and Services I think somewhere around 9% to 10% that we have really maintained historically as well.

items.statement: Plans to invest INR 25-50 cr in FY27 for capacity deposits across vendor and customer side.
items.quote: We will look to invest more in this financial year, maybe about INR 25 crores to 50 crores, depending on the opportunities that we get.

items.statement: Current asset base provides revenue predictability of INR 6,000+ cr over next 5 years; annual capacity of 9 MT (INR 900-1,000 cr).
items.quote: The current asset base actually gives us a revenue predictability of more than INR 6,000 crores for the next five years.

items.quote: Our aim is in Q1, we should be able to predict around 85% to 90% of our top line and similarly of the bottom line as well.

items.statement: Raw material cost inflation is fully passed through; steel price changes do not impact profitability.
items.quote: For us, it is a clear pass -through. Our business model is such, if steel is sold at 90,000 and if the market is at 95 ,000, so for us, it is a complete pass -through.

items.statement: Took additional INR 5 cr expected credit loss provision in Q4 FY26 as conservative measure on receivable risk.
items.quote: We have taken an additional expected credit loss of about INR 5 crores. This is in line with taking a more conservative approach in terms of the receivable risk that we generally take in our balance sheet.

items.statement: Secured INR 30 cr working capital sanction; targeting INR 100-150 cr total facilities to bridge payables-receivables gap.
items.quote: We got a INR 30 crores sanction from one of the banks, and this is what we have mentioned before also that we will be going for about INR 100 crores to INR 150 crores of working capital facilities.

items.quote: Revenues from asphalt increased to INR 30 crores in Q4 2026, growing 88% sequentially. More importantly, active customers in this category nearly doubled during the quarter to 28 customers.

items.statement: Targets peak Contract Manufacturing utilization of 75-80%+ in FY27; current annualized utilization 65-70%.
items.quote: We will be looking to reach a peak utilization of more than 75% to 80% in this financial year itself.

items.quote: With the acquisition having closed, we are comfortable that revenues will cross INR 1,000–1,050 crores in FY27.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin target of 25–30% for core organic business

items.statement: Organic platform NRR 114% in FY26; inorganic NRR 94%; blended 110%

items.statement: Fulfillment margin has scope to improve over next two quarters alongside ad revenue growth.
items.quote: I think there is still in addition to ad revenues improving there is still some scope to increase our inaudible 50:05 margins which might happen over the next two quarters.

items.quote: Almost a doubling of frequency has happened from a baseline perspective in the last three years.

items.statement: Prepaid share increasing, reducing COD; BNPL still early, not yet a major driver.

items.quote: Second, as our volumes increase in the ecosystem, that density increase across the board, be it last mile, middle mile, all the legs, also leads to cost improvement.

items.statement: Ad product ROAS among industry best, multiples of global peers; seller budgets more than doubled YoY.
items.quote: Our return on ad spend continues to be one of the industry best. In fact, multiples of what other e-commerce players kind of offer in India or anywhere else in the globe.

items.statement: Valmo sort-centre automation planned over next few years; may use partner capex or own based on payback.

items.statement: Seller concentration decreasing as more sellers become active and larger; Pareto base expanding rapidly.
items.quote: the concentration on sellers continues to kind of reduce as we have more and more sellers who kind of become active as well as larger on the platform.

items.quote: We expect our credit growth to be 1% or 2% over the industry growth.

items.quote: With respect to margins, we expect that NIMs to be in the range of 3.75% to 3.8% for the full year, though we are at 4% plus at the exit quarter of this year.

items.quote: Given the current macroeconomic environment and the anticipated effects on the net interest margins discussed earlier, we expect the ROA for the full year to be between 1.7% to 1.8%.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to be less than 1% for FY27
items.quote: Credit cost, I can think around less than 1% we can think of.

items.statement: GNPA expected <1.5% and net NPA <1% for FY27
items.quote: GNPA is expected to be less than 1.5% and net NPA to be less than 1% for the full year.

items.quote: Slippages would be expected to be below 1% of the asset book.

items.statement: LCR to be maintained around 115% to 120% for FY27
items.quote: LCR would be maintained around 115% to 120%.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio to remain below 50% for FY27
items.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio would be below 50% as we have been continuously planning, and we'll endeavor to retain that way.

items.quote: With respect to branch expansion, we are planning to open 50 branches. Out of that 38 will be regular and 7 will be liteand another 5, we are going to shortlist shortly.

items.quote: The cost of deposits reduced by 13 basis points on a sequential basis as a major part of the deposits repriced during the year. The yield on advances increased by 16 basis points during the quarter.

items.statement: Fixed rate loan book increased from 23% to 29% of total book in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our fixed rate loan book, which was at 23% in the total book at the end of December has now increased to 29% at the end of March '26.

items.quote: We have launched the products for 7.2%. So we need to pay something more on the senior citizens also. items.quote: We have provided prudentially INR163 crores, I repeat INR163 crores is a onetime towards sectors identified that may get affected due to ongoing geopolitical tensions.

items.quote: As I was mentioning in my guidance, we started seeing the lower level of utilization in the working capital. 2% to 3%, it is down across the sectors, many sectors, it is there.

items.quote: The jewel loans portfolio encompassing all verticals accounts for 30% of the bank's overall portfolio. We maintain an internal cap of 35%.

items.quote: I would really refrain from giving any -- I mean, any kind of guidance, you know better than that how indeterminate it is, whatever guidance we may give.

items.quote: Looking at this kind of trajectory that we're having today, it's quite possible that INR 15,000 crores instead of FY '28 may kind of slip over to FY '29.

items.quote: This year, we should be spending INR 1,200-odd crores for construction.

items.quote: Overall, I could say roughly about INR 60,000 crores of projects we are at this point, kind of pursuing.

items.quote: we have about INR 70,000 crores, INR 72,000 crores of GDV today, of which about -- how much is launched about close to 30,000. I think it's all laid out in our presentation ~31,700 we have launched.

items.statement: Premium and luxury segments outperform while affordable and mid-income demand softened
items.quote: However, premium and luxury segments continue to outperform while affordable and mid-income demand softened.

items.quote: Further, pricing has shown a healthy growth across all the four regions, Y-o-Y growth, MMR 7.4%, Bengaluru 13.9%, NCR 8.5% and Pune 6%.

items.quote: mostly, we attempt to collect at least 65% to 70% by the time we finish the structure of the building.

items.quote: Approvals are largely based on two things. One is the environmental and the NGT. So those are pretty indeterminate things.

items.quote: Yes. So because of oil prices and disruption in supply chains, there has been an impact on cost. But being a very prudent planners, we have already taken it in our contingency measures, etc.

items.statement: ITC transaction expected to conclude this quarter after CCI approval received
items.quote: Now certain state-level approvals are pending, and we expect to conclude the transaction in this quarter.

items.quote: We achieved presales of INR 4,288 crores, reflecting a robust 69% Q-o-Q increase. Collection for Q4 FY '26 remained healthy at INR 994 crores, and we recorded area sales of 3 million square feet, making an impressive 75% Q-o-Q growth.

items.quote: For the full year FY '26, we closed with a pre-sales of INR 8,136 crores, collections of INR 3,341 crores and area sold of 5.5 million square feet reflecting the depth, resilience and stability of our business.

items.quote: The only challenge what we find is the Rs.400 crores number which we had communicated as a part of a couple of years plan, that actually gets bit derailed because of the pricing pressures which we are seeing both in the commodity segment and more importantly on the specialty segment.

items.statement: Net debt of Rs.71 crore to become net cash positive in FY27 with Rs.130 crore scheduled repayment
items.quote: See, our scheduled debt repayment for next year is again Rs. 130 crores. So, obviously we will be debt-free, because we have Rs. 71 crores of net debt. So, net debt obviously will be debt-free.

items.statement: Next growth capex focused on specialty/niche chemicals; holding back announcement until geopolitical uncertainty clears
items.quote: The CAPEXES which will come for growth predominantly as of now our thought process is to make it in the specialty segment or in the niche segment with related chemistries. items.statement: Solar power expansion paused awaiting regulatory clarity on TANGEDCO banking rules and geopolitical stability
items.quote: We are waiting for a clarification on that because entire dynamics will depend on extent to which we are able to offset the renewable over the TNEB rates.

items.quote: Despite volume increase in both C-PVC and SIOP, the significant reduction in NR by 22% in C-PVC with no consumerate reduction in PVC input prices resulted in PVC-C-PVC spread contraction and consequently margins.

items.statement: Basic chemicals EBITDA margin improved to 3.5% from 1.3% driven by better utilization and renewable energy benefits
items.quote: The basic chemical margins improved to 3.5% over 1.3% last year.

items.statement: Caustic soda Q4 realization ~$350/t; current Q1 realization north of $400/t due to Southeast Asia supply disruptions
items.quote: In Q4 I think it was around $350. And as we talk in Q1 the realization is in the north of $400.

items.quote: See, today the import price is in the vicinity of about $250.

items.quote: The spreads have improved. It has gone back to the pre-war. What has happened is that that there was a spike in the PVC prices in the month of March. So, pass-over was not happening in the CPVC.

items.quote: Yes, there has been a demand dip because of the lower offtake from the sectors that you have mentioned, but there has been no production curtailment because of the demand dip that we have seen.

items.statement: Synthetic rutile margin improvement driven by shifting export mix away from China to higher-paying ex-China customers
items.quote: When we are exporting into China, we do not get those prices. When we export into our existing customers who have been taking ex of China, their prices are better off.

items.statement: VCM feedstock supply from Middle East paused due to Gulf War; procuring at higher cost difficult to pass through to PVC prices
items.quote: Because of the gulf war that supply which has been the closest logistically is not coming. So, our contracts were all put on pause. items.statement: Record FY26 volumes in C-PVC (50kt capacity), SIOP and synthetic rutile; C-PVC capacity expanded from 20kt to 50kt commissioned on time, within budget
items.quote: We achieved our highest ever sales volumes in C-PVC, synthetic iron oxide pigment and synthetic rutile.

items.statement: Current quarter expected to be slightly better or equivalent to Q4 FY26; KPIs are EBITDA, revenue, positive cash flow, working capital control
items.quote: the current quarter is going to be slightly better or equivalent to last quarter. And our KPI remains EBITDA, revenue and positive cash flow.

items.statement: Knitting expansion of 92 crore under execution adding printing capacity; modernisation capex for old asset replacement ongoing; no major new capex planned
items.quote: we are having ₹92 crores of expansion in our knitting business. We are adding printing as one of the segments. So, as a result of this new CAPEX, we may also add EBITDA in the 3rd and 4th quarters

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 7.1% in FY26 from 4.8% in FY25 (231 bps expansion); Q4 FY26 margin stable at 7.4% QoQ, up 115 bps YoY; target double-digit EBITDA margin
items.quote: EBITDA stood at ₹327 crores, from ₹233 crores, registering a strong growth of 40.5% year-over-year, with margins improving to 7.1% from 4.8%, an expansion of 231 basis points.

items.statement: Knitting expansion expected to improve EBITDA by 3-4% from current levels once fully implemented in Q3 FY27
