items.quote: availability of gas is there, but the cost has significantly gone for upward revision. So, that is a challenge, and we expect this to resolve.

items.statement: Board approved preferential issue of 24.7 lakh Convertible Warrants (~36 crore) to promoter group LNJ Textile Advisory LLP in April 2026
items.quote: our Board of Directors in April approved a proposal for the infusion of equity through the preferential issue of 24.7 lakh Convertible Warrants, which are equivalent to almost 36 crore

items.statement: Capital allocation disciplined with focus on projects offering 1-3 year payback, particularly modernisation and productivity improvement
items.quote: capital allocation would remain disciplined, with a strong focus on capital expenditure projects that offer shorter payback periods of one to three years, particularly in the area of modernisation and productivity improvement

items.statement: Core business organic growth target of 16-18% YoY maintained for FY27
items.quote: As you know, during the last couple of quarters, as part of GREAVES.NEXT strategy, I have said that our growth ambition in the midterm is between 16% to 18%. So, we continue to hold that.

items.statement: Core business EBITDA margin target of 13-15% maintained as business scales
items.quote: Once again, we have said that we will maintain 13% to 15% EBITDA margins as we scale the business.

items.statement: Capex of INR 500-700 crore over next 5 years focused on product development, capability enhancement, and international expansion
items.quote: So, after the revamp of the strategy and launch of GREAVES.NEXT, we earmarked INR 500 crores to INR 700 crores of CAPEX. This CAPEX will be focused in three major areas.

items.statement: Secured single largest institutional order worth INR 35 crore for end-to-end genset delivery including long-term maintenance
items.quote: We also secured our single largest institutional order worth INR 35 crores. This covers end-to-end delivery, including supply, installation, commissioning and long-term maintenance.

items.statement: Aftermarket grew 35% YoY in FY26; retailer onboarding target of 3,000 by FY27 from ~350 currently
items.quote: We accelerated the retailer engagement, onboarding approximately 350 retailers with a clear roadmap to scale this to 3,000 by FY '27.

items.statement: Energy Solutions outlook strong supported by infrastructure growth, industrial expansion, and reliable power demand
items.quote: The overall outlook for India's genset market remains strong. This is supported by infrastructure growth, industrial expansion and an increasing demand for reliable power.

items.statement: Commodity cost pressures in aluminum, copper, platinum; passthrough mechanism activated in Q1 FY27
items.quote: However, there is a passthrough mechanism, which we have already activated in Q1. So, therefore, we do see some recovery on account of price.

items.statement: Greaves Finance AUM at INR 521 crore as of March 2026; group cash balance healthy
items.quote: The Greaves Finance Limited, the total asset under management for the financing business stood at INR 521 crores as on March '26. Our balance sheet continues to remain strong with a healthy cash balance.

items.statement: Expects 5-10% volume growth next year, cautious optimism on better times ahead
items.quote: We expect that the next year will be like a normal year, which is about 5% to 10% growth rate, but there is too much uncertainty in the future.

items.statement: Planned capex for FY27 around INR80-90 crores for completing Dahej project and maintenance
items.quote: So around -- it will be around INR80 crores to INR90 crores.

items.statement: Pharma 50-60% of sales, agro 15-20%, total 70-75%
items.quote: Maybe between 50% and 60% of our sales are to pharma and another maybe 15%, 20% to agro. Total, it's about 70%, 75%.

items.statement: Margins temporarily improved in March due to inventory lag, expects better margins going forward but not dramatic
items.quote: We are optimistic that I think we have seen the bottom. So probably the margins going forward will be a little better than what we have experienced in the last year.

items.statement: Ammonia price doubled from INR50 to over INR100/kg, passed on to customers, prices unlikely to return to pre-February levels soon
items.quote: Like ammonia, as you said, we were in the region of about INR50 a kg and now we are over INR100 a kg. So obviously, the cost of production has risen, and we have had to pass it on to customers.

items.statement: No demand slowdown seen yet in pharma, some concern in agro due to monsoon/El Nino
items.quote: Well, at the moment, we haven't seen anything, but there is a little bit of concern that they could be affected, not pharma as much as agro because they expect this monsoon also with the El Nino and all, there is some concern.

items.statement: Kurkumbh project delayed, mechanical completion by end June, commissioning early next quarter
items.quote: Mechanical completion is going to be completed somewhere at the end of June.

items.statement: War-related supply chain uncertainty continues, ammonia sourcing improved but future uncertain
items.quote: But of course, the future remains a little uncertain as long as the war continues, which we hope will get resolved soon.

items.statement: Methylamine overcapacity with 4 players (RCF, Balaji, Aarti, Alkyl), ethylamine capacity sufficient for 4-5 years
items.quote: Methylamines, there is an overhang of capacity because a new player has come in. So there's RCF, Balaji, Aarti and us now. So there is a bit of overcapacity of methylamines.

items.statement: Acetonitrile price ~INR200/kg vs INR140-150 last year, acetic acid also risen considerably
items.quote: Today, I think we are at about, what INR250. Kanchan Shinde: INR200. Kirat Patel: A bit over INR200 now per kg. But then acetic acid has also risen considerably

items.statement: Peptide/acetonitrile demand optimistic but early days, acetonitrile market ~30,000 tons, peptide maybe 10%
items.quote: The acetonitrile market is about 30,000 tons or so. And this will be maybe 10% of the whole. So something will go up, something will go down. So the total market is not disrupted by it.

items.statement: R&D pipeline has ~12 projects at various stages, 1-2 may commercialize, policy to announce only after market launch
items.quote: At any point in time, we are probably over a dozen projects working on it, probably more. But at various stages, some are right at the preliminary research stage.

items.statement: Ammonia contracts now short-term due to high prices, nobody willing to commit long-term
items.quote: At the moment, the ammonia contracts are all short term because prices are high and nobody is willing to commit well, it's not day-to-day, but it's fairly short compared to what we used to do earlier.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement expected next year but not necessarily sustained annually
items.quote: Definitely, I think we do foresee some improvement in our margins in the next year. But will it continue growing, that's a separate question altogether.

items.statement: Green ammonia alternative 3-5 years away, coal gasification methanol by-product being pushed by government
items.quote: I think it will happen. It will take a little time. It will be 3 to 5 years before anything breakthroughs happen.

items.statement: FY26 volume and value flat (+/-1%), volume down ~1%, price down ~1%, combined ~2% drop
items.quote: It's been basically flat volume and value, plus-minus 1% either way prices have dropped 1% and volume has probably dropped 1%. So the combination is about 2% drop.

items.statement: Expect healthy volume growth in FY27 above industry average due to low base from FY26 decline
items.quote: we certainly look forward to a positive growth. And it should be in access to the industry average because we had a bad year last year. So, for us, it is a low base on which we have to grow this year. So, we expect healthy growth over last year.

items.statement: Capex on hold; will evaluate after first two quarters of FY27 before deciding on further expansion
items.quote: No, we are putting CAPEX on hold because we have already invested for all the developments and we will observe first two quarters as I told you last time before we decide for the further CAPEX plans.

items.statement: Building products margin 14-18%; agriculture margin 8-10% depending on season
items.quote: Normally, agriculture would have about 8% to 9% margin, or 10%, it depends on time of the year, while building product offers from 14% to 18%.

items.statement: May see inventory gains in Q1 FY27 due to volatile petrochemical prices from geopolitical issues
items.quote: going forward in Q1 also, as things are very volatile today, it is difficult to predict. But still, we may see some advantage on inventory side.

items.statement: Agriculture and building product demand back to normal after initial war-related disruption
items.quote: Demand for agriculture and building products were impacted immediately after the war broke out because of the sudden very high increase in the raw material and finished goods prices. But now they have settled. So, demand is again back to almost average normal.

items.statement: Expanding CPVC capacity; OPVC not on agenda; CPVC offers better margins and is focus for growth
items.quote: CPVC we are expanding. OPVC is not on our agenda at this moment.

items.statement: Government withdrew import duty on PVC and polymers until end of June due to war-related supply challenges
items.quote: Government of India has withdrawn import duty on PVC and all other polymers till the period of end of June up to 1st July.

items.statement: Trade receivables declined to INR 28 crores from INR 48 crores due to reduced institutional sales in Q4
items.quote: our outstanding are mostly towards institution. And you must have seen in the Q4, we have reduced our institutional sales as per our projections given to you. So, this is why the outstandings have declined.

items.statement: Targeting substantial revenue increase in FY27 and aim to reach INR 1000 crore revenue target previously guided
items.quote: we should be able to aim substantial increase over last year. And we will definitely target towards our guidance. That is what we had said earlier.

items.statement: Second manufacturing plant timeline undecided; will wait for first two quarters of FY27 to decide
items.quote: No. As I said earlier in the question, we will wait for first two quarters to make up our mind when and how, where.

items.statement: Loan growth target of 15-16% for FY27, matching industry if higher
items.quote: we are still aiming to get between 15% and 16%. But if the industry were to do higher than that, we will match industry.

items.statement: NIM drivers are asset mix shift to Retail/MSME, rate hikes, and revenue-focused goal setting
items.quote: The NIM drivers for us are largely change in asset mix, is the biggest driver. So, if we can get more larger proportion of our book to be Retail and MSME, automatically NIMs open up

items.statement: 60-65% of deposits due for repricing in FY27, expected to favor NIM
items.quote: we have almost say 60 to 65% of our deposit is due for repricing during this financial year, considering the average tenor of our deposits

items.statement: Target to reduce corporate book from 38% to ~33% of total, ultra-short corporate from ~20-25% to ~10%
items.quote: corporate goes down from 38 to 33 and within the corporate the ultra -short duration goes down from roughly 20% or 25% of our book down to perhaps 10% of the book

items.statement: Gold loan risk managed via Value at Risk framework with portfolio caps; 30-day moving average with 25-50% standard deviation applied
items.quote: we are using the Value at Risk framework, and we've built a mechanism by which we actually measure this risk. And using Value at Risk, we can see periods of volatility

items.statement: Credit costs at trough (3 bps this quarter); expect slippages and credit costs to trend up due to geopolitical stresses
items.quote: My own view is that we've seen the trough when it comes to credit cost. Credit cost for this quarter was three basis points. I don't think a credit cost can be lower than this

items.statement: Expense growth expected as bank invests in distribution and technology after reaching efficiency frontier
items.quote: we've reached a point where expenses cannot be kept at this level indefinitely and we will have to start doing a little bit of investment both in distribution, a little bit more investment in technology

items.statement: Portfolio buyouts ~INR2,000 crores; shifting preference to pass-through certificates over buyouts
items.quote: Our total portfolio buyout across products is roughly in the order of magnitude of about INR2,000 crores at the end of the last quarter

items.statement: MSME grew 15% YoY; sequential dip due to write-offs, no material stress visible
items.quote: MSME has grown 15% year -on-year. And we are quite happy with it

items.statement: CEO succession search underway; new incumbent expected before or immediately after Sep 30 term end
items.quote: the process will conclude and letters will be written to the RB I in due time for RBI to make its decisions and convey them to the Board in such a fashion that the new incumbent can be in position when required, which is, my term ends on the 30th of September

items.statement: ECL transition not expected to have material one-time or steady-state impact given low SMA (0.6%) and high PCR (80%)
items.quote: we don’t estimate any material impact over there, mainly because of few factors that if you see our numbers, SMA numbers, is on a declining trend and is close to 0.6% of our total book

items.statement: Cost of deposits rose 3 bps in Q4 due to slight repricing for growth; future repricing of high-cost deposits to favor NIM
items.quote: we have slightly moved the deposit rate considering the deposit growth. So if you see our deposit prices compared with the market rates, we were little lower than the other competitors

items.statement: No floating provisions held for ECL transition; capital adequacy at 19.66% with Tier-1 at 18.76%
items.quote: currently we are not holding any floating provision in our books. So, what we expect is that based on the current estimate, we don't estimate any material impact over there

items.statement: Management does not provide revenue guidance for FY27 due to market volatility
items.quote: Now going forward, as you know, Girish, we do not give ou t guidance. But if you look at the investments that we have made, we've gotten a large number of leaders who have come in at the leadership level

items.statement: Demand environment remains soft with macroeconomic headwinds and client-specific issues causing revenue erosion
items.quote: our performance during the quarter and year under review reflects a ve ry soft demand environment due to sustained macroeconomic headwinds, leading to some client -specific issues and as a result, erosion of

items.statement: Q4 FY26 TCV deal signings of $208 million, up 3% sequentially, second consecutive quarter above $200 million
items.quote: We've signed deals worth $208 million TCV during Q4, which is 3% higher than what we signed in Q3 of FY '26

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 18.5%, up 30 bps QoQ; full year FY26 EBITDA margin 16.3%, up 333 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q4 increased to 18.5%, which is an expansion of 30 basis points quarter-on-quarter

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin expected to be upward of 15% as investments in sales, leadership, AI capabilities and productivity benefits pressure margins
items.quote: I continue to believe, that our steady state margins that we should expect is going to be upward of 15% and there will be an erosion from where we are today, obviously, because of these investments

items.statement: Sales team strength expected to increase 30-40% YoY by middle of FY27 with significant hiring in US and Europe across verticals
items.quote: By the middle of FY '27, I reckon that our sales team strength would have gone up by 30% to 40% on a year-on-year basis

items.statement: AI deals require upfront productivity commitments causing near-term revenue deflation but expected to catch up in future quarters
items.quote: Now what happens in an AI deal is we have to commit to the savings and underwrite some of the savings right up front, which is why you see revenue deflation in the immediate and the medium term

items.statement: Market uncertainty and volatility from trade, tariffs and geopolitics make demand outlook unpredictable
items.quote: the developments related to trade, tariffs and geopolitics have made the situation even more volatile

items.statement: Revenue shift from traditional services to AI-oriented work in BFSI vertical; spending pool stable but mix changing
items.quote: The spending remains to be strong. Only the shift of the spending pool is moving from the more traditional side of the businesses to more AI-oriented work

items.statement: Walked away from low-margin, non-strategic deals impacting ~200 bps of FY26 growth; rationalized tail accounts
items.quote: at least 200 basis points of growth roughly went away because we walked away from low-margin, non-strategic deals

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin included ~340 bps one-off benefits: 170 bps forex tailwind, 170 bps from lower provisions, leave encashment and equity compensation
items.quote: the forex tailwind gave us a 170-basis point benefit. And the other items that I talked about gave us another 170 points benefit. So it's about a 340-point benefit that we got in the fourth quarter

items.statement: Life Sciences MedTech client-specific operational issue believed to be behind; manufacturing facing macro headwinds
items.quote: I intuitively feel that the bad news in both manufacturing and med devices sector is behind us

items.statement: ETR expected to settle closer to historical levels starting FY27 after elevated FY26 due to US federal tax provision
items.quote: The elevated ETR due to incremental U.S. tax, as I had called out on our earlier calls, was limited and will be limited to FY '26, and we expect ETR to settle closer to our historical ETR level starting FY '27

items.statement: Board proposed final dividend of INR 4 per share; full year dividend INR 6.50 per share; cash and equivalents INR 2,637.3 crore
items.quote: the Board of Directors has proposed a final dividend of INR 4 per share, subject to shareholders' approval. This, combined with the interim dividend paid out after our Q2 Board meeting, takes our overall dividend for the full financial year to INR 6.50 per share

items.statement: ERP business challenged historically; new 25-year SAP veteran leader hired to drive improvement; system of records not going away
items.quote: We strongly believe our ERP business will only continue to improve from here. System of records is not going away

items.statement: Larger competitors bidding for mid-sized deals in AI-driven outcome-based models creating competitive intensity
items.quote: we are ab solutely seeing larger players also bidding for midsized deals. But equally, it also is an opportunity for smaller-sized companies

items.statement: Expect lower percentage EBITDA margins in Q1 and Q2 FY27 due to crude oil inflation, but higher revenue growth and absolute EBITDA at reasonably good levels
items.quote: This quarter and next quarter, I expect some pressure on EBITDA percentage margin, but we are seeing upside in a variety of other areas.

items.statement: Indonesia expected to deliver mid-single-digit volume growth and high single-digit value growth going forward
items.quote: So, I think what we will get in Indonesia is kind of mid-single-digit volume, high single-digit value going forward.

items.statement: Africa business expected to deliver strong performance in FY27 with FMCG growth drivers continuing to compound
items.quote: I expect Africa performance to be quite strong, on Monday, we'll explain to you that there are some underlying drivers in FMCG, which are driving bulk of the growth in Africa, and those will continue to compound in FY27.

items.statement: Consolidated blended raw material inflation currently at 7% to 9% at spot prices of USD 100-105 Brent and 4,500 MYR palm oil
items.quote: I think we put that out in our result 7% to 9% is what we're seeing.

items.statement: Price hikes taken in April: soaps 5%, detergents 6-7%, household insecticide 4-5%
items.quote: In soaps, we have taken our prices by 5%. In detergents, we have taken up prices again by 6% or 7%, which is now a meaningful part of our business, maybe 7%. In household insecticide, we have taken up prices again by 4%, 5%.

items.statement: India standalone business delivered 8% underlying volume growth and 10% sales growth in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our standalone business delivered an excellent quarter, driven by 8% underlying volume growth and 10% sales growth.

items.statement: Indonesia delivered 4% underlying volume growth for second consecutive quarter with pricing pressures largely bottomed out
items.quote: In Indonesia, the pricing pressures we have been calling out over the last several quarters have now largely bottomed out, and we are seeing increasingly clear signs of stabilization. The business delivered 4% underlying volume growth and 3% sales growth.

items.statement: Home Care growing faster than Personal Care; air freshener business seeing explosive global growth manufactured in India
items.quote: I think, firstly, our Home Care business salience is increasing every quarter and it's becoming bigger and bigger on the back of some of these things. So that is one. The second is there has been a lot of explosive growth globally on our air freshener

items.statement: Godrej Fab ARR at INR 500 crores GSV in Q4, broken even in Q4, national rollout beyond South India
items.quote: I think our ARR is about on GSV terms, about INR500 crores in quarter 4 and maybe INR450 crores in NSV terms. So, it's very, of course, internally look at our gross sales value is about INR500 crores.

items.statement: Crude oil at USD 100-110 expected to cause 3-4 months of margin pressure before pricing catches up across all categories
items.quote: So, it may take 3 to 4 months again, of a little bit of a dip in percentage margins. But unlike in the case of very sharp palm oil prices were even if I have a 6% -7% inflation because of palm oil, it affects only one category and then that become s really hard to take our price

items.statement: El Nino weather pattern may create volatile Q1 for household insecticide but FY24 El Nino year was reasonably good overall
items.quote: As far as weather goes, if the predictions of El Nino are right, there will be impact and Q1 will be a difficult quarter for HI because for a good quarter when it's hot and reasonably wet, actually, it's reasonably good for Q2 and Q3 should be okay.

items.statement: State-of-the-art pet food plant set up in Nasik, volumes shipped, category seen as long burn with potential to become big business in few years
items.quote: We've set up a state-of-the-art plant in Nasik, and we've shipped our volumes from there. So, the more we understand this category. Firstly, is going to be a long burn. There's going to be a lot of value to feel that I'll again share this on Monday, but we do feel that this is a category that has a good odd for us to really become a big business in a few years' time.

items.statement: Revenue presentation changed from Q4 FY26 to net off customer-related spends per ICAI EAC opinion; no impact on absolute EBITDA, PAT, cash flow
items.quote: The impact is straightforward, revenue from operations and the corresponding lines within other expenses both reduced by the same amount period after period. There is no impact whatsoever on absolute EBITDA, PAT, profit after tax, total liquidity, or cash flow.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin at 20.1%, up 276 bps YoY and 180 bps QoQ; EBITDA net of RSU expense at 19%
items.quote: The adjusted EBITDA, adjusted for RSU expenses and non-recurring costs, stood at INR 115.7 crore or $12.6 million, which is an EBITDA percentage of 20.1%.

items.statement: Management maintains EBITDA margin guidance in 17%+ range; Q1 at 20.1% includes FX benefit, core margin ~19%
items.quote: We have continued to maintain our margins in a very healthy range, as we had guided in the +17% margin, kind of a range.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month ACV wins increased to $82.5M from $76.5M last quarter, showing positive deal momentum
items.quote: We had $76.5 million of ACV on a TTM basis last quarter. We are reporting $82.5 million of ACV wins this quarter.

items.statement: AI-driven demand expanding; ~29% of revenue from AI/AI-enabled services; strong deal momentum in SDLC, modernization, business workflows
items.quote: approximately 29% of our revenue today comes from AI and AI-enabled services.

items.statement: Fixed-price revenue mix rising from ~10% in 2024 to ~15-16% in 2025; shift toward outcome-based pricing with AI transformations
items.quote: Last year, as in 2024, has already probably changed to maybe closer to 15% or 16% in 2025, and we believe that it will continue to move in the favor of fixed price as we go along.

items.statement: Deliberate bench investment in AI/data talent (~2-2.5% utilization dip to 80.5%) to build COE and EXIQO AI studio
items.quote: there's a deliberate decrease in utilization as a result of which, for creating that COE and the deliberate bench on both data and AI talent, thus bringing our utilization down to about 80.5%.

items.statement: Frontier model vendors (Anthropic/OpenAI) partnering with PE to target mid-market; seen as validation of people-centric AI approach, not pure tool play
items.quote: It validates that AI is fundamentally a people problem, not a tools problem. Because if it was only tools, then those frontier companies have already released the tools.

items.statement: No formal forward guidance provided; high confidence in organic and combined growth trajectory; EBITDA maintenance expected
items.quote: while we don't provide any forward guidance and flavors, but very high confidence that both organically, as well as combined entities, we are on the right trajectory for doing what we promised to our investors to continue to grow the organization.

items.statement: Novigo acquisition fully integrated; restated annual revenue ~$21-22M vs original $32M due to accounting policy alignment (gross to net)
items.quote: That restated will stand at about $21-$22 million a year.

items.statement: Token costs for client delivery borne by client (100% pass-through); internal token costs for training/R&D absorbed by company
items.quote: token cost for output delivered to the client is usually, I would say, in almost 100% cases borne by the client, either they provide us subscription to the front end model that they are subscribed to, or we would do it, but we will pass on the costs.

items.statement: New CRO Farooq Ahmad onboarded (Bay Area, 30 yrs tech experience) to strengthen North America tech sales and go-to-market
items.quote: we recently onboarded Farooq Ahmad as our Chief Revenue Officer. He is going to be leading our sales engine, strengthen the go-to-market approach, and lead the key growth initiatives across key markets, especially focusing on North America in the tech space.

items.statement: SG&A dropped to INR 91.4 crore from INR 114.3 crore QoQ due to AR provision reversal; normalized run-rate ~INR 110-115 crore
items.quote: SG&A expenses decreased by INR 22.9 crore from INR 114.3 crore in last quarter to INR 91.4 crore this quarter. This is mainly due to reversal of conservative AR provision on account of realization in this quarter.

items.statement: Middle East crisis impacted Novigo in Q1; expected to be behind them, contributing to positive growth ahead
items.quote: They obviously were also impacted by the Middle East crisis to some extent in Q1. So, that hopefully will be a thing behind us, and then that will contribute to positive growth in that front as well.

items.statement: P&A segment targets 50% total growth by FY29; no piecemeal FY27 guidance given
items.quote: we are totally committed to delivering the F '29 objective, which we said that we are going to ultimately work towards managing a 50% total growth on our P&A portfolio, and we are totally committed to that.

items.statement: Manufacturing EBITDA per liter guided at INR5-7 for FY27, same as FY26 range
items.quote: INR5 to INR7 is our guidance for the EBITDA per liter. That's the range in which it will remain for the year.

items.statement: Bulk alcohol annual volume guidance ~200 million liters; growth expected on top from UP capacity
items.quote: INR20 crores is our annual guidance. And on top of that is UP. So yes, there is going to be growth on top of the INR20 crores.

items.statement: No immediate need for external fundraise; internal accruals and debt optimization to fund FY27 plan
items.quote: this year, we do not see a need to achieve the business plan given some of the operational improvements and leverage we've been able to get.

items.statement: Annual debt outflow reduced from INR67 cr to INR14 cr projected for FY27, unlocking INR53 cr liquidity
items.quote: we have systematically reduced our annual debt outflow from INR67 crores per annum to just INR14 crores projected for FY27. This action alone unlocks INR53 crores of direct liquidity in the coming year.

items.statement: Blended interest rate reduced by 50 bps through refinancing and treasury management
items.quote: Through this refinancing and broader treasury management, we have driven down our blended rate of interest, combining all forms of borrowing by a full 50 basis points.

items.statement: Ethanol and ENA export orders visible; Q4 exported 3.7 million liters ENA
items.quote: In Q4, we started this journey and exported 3.7 million liters.

items.statement: Ethanol demand expected to stay strong due to higher blending mandates and flex-fuel push
items.quote: Over the last few months, we've seen oil marketing companies, Government of India start preparing towards higher ethanol blends. And I believe flex fuel mandates for new cars is also on the angle. So overall, ethanol demands are going to be quite strong going forward.

items.statement: P&A revenue grew 27% YoY to INR164 cr, volumes up 31% to 1.19M cases in FY26; underlying growth ex-Delhi 58%
items.quote: When we isolate and remove the Delhi anomaly from the data, our P&A business grew at an exceptional 58% year-on-year.

items.statement: Regular & Others FY26 revenue INR900 cr (+4%), volumes 15.7M cases, EBITDA INR158 cr (+12%); portfolio reset in WB & Haryana complete
items.quote: For the full year FY26, revenue was INR900 crores, up 4% with volumes at 15.7 million cases and EBITDA delivering a 12% expansion to INR158 crores.

items.statement: Geopolitical-driven cost pressure on glass, PET, logistics; mitigation underway, impact expected modest
items.quote: we have quickly geared up and a lot of efficiency measures are already up and about. While we see that there will be an impact, but the way we see most of the impact, we should be able to neutralize.

items.statement: Bihar prohibition policy monitored; first-mover advantage if market reopens due to existing manufacturing footprint
items.quote: We are actively monitoring the legislative landscape and policy regarding prohibition. If or when that market reopens, the first-mover advantage should be significant because we have a fully operational footprint in the state.

items.statement: Q4 manufacturing inventory buildup from ENA shift and permissions delay to liquidate in Q1 FY27
items.quote: This inventory buildup will get liquidated in Q1.

items.statement: P&A segment revenue target is INR500 crore by FY29, not INR1,000 crore
items.quote: The number for P&A is INR500 crores, not INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Manufacturing EBITDA guidance maintained at INR5-7 per liter regardless of ethanol/ENA mix
items.quote: Our guidance remains between INR5 and INR7 a liter regardless of ENA or ethanol.

items.statement: R&O margin target 16-18%; Q4 at 18% seen as high end, expect slight decline due to UP mix
items.quote: Our target in this space is 16% to 18%. So it will be a little bit lower than that for sure.

items.statement: Rajasthan price increase of INR30 per case secured for FY27; no increase in UP or Haryana yet
items.quote: This year also, we've got a price increase in Rajasthan to the extent of INR30 a case.

items.statement: UP and Rajasthan combined grew 7% in FY26; expect higher growth in FY27 driven by UP brand launches
items.quote: Rajasthan plus UP last year give us 7% growth. I believe in the coming year, Rajasthan plus UP will give us higher than 7% growth.

items.statement: Bulk volume target well over 20 crore liters in FY27 (20 crore from existing units + ~2 crore from UP)
items.quote: Well over 20 crores will be the target for this year.

items.statement: West Bengal re-entry timing uncertain; license shift in progress, relaunch with new portfolio planned
items.quote: In West Bengal, our license is in process, and it's very difficult to commit a particular quarter when everything gets kicked off and signed off.

items.statement: Equity capital raise put on hold; expansion funded from internal cash flows; residual cash to repay debt
items.quote: The plan for capital raise -- equity capital raise has been put on hold. We are able to manage our expansion based on our internal cash flow.

items.statement: Net debt at INR627 crore as of Q4 FY26; R&O working capital 5-6 days; interest cost expected INR14-15 crore/quarter post-refinancing
items.quote: So the net debt business for the company is at INR627 crores. That's the net debt.

items.statement: Capex for next year estimated at INR170-180 crores
items.quote: For the next year, the capex is estimated at roughly around INR170 crores, INR180 crores.

items.statement: Store expansion guidance remains 13-15% area addition annually net of closures
items.quote: The guidance for the next year remains the same at 13% to 15% area addition every year, net of 1% or 2% mistakes that may need closures year-on-year.

items.statement: Capex per store remains INR1.3-1.4 crores; higher average due to refurbishments and tech
items.quote: Our capex per store still remains around INR1.3 crores, INR1.4 crores.

items.statement: Gross margin decreased 1% YoY due to inventory provision and lower LimeRoad commission
items.quote: On the margin front, gross margins actually for the quarter decreased year-on-year by 1%.

items.statement: Yarn prices up 10-15%, translating to 5-7% apparel cost impact; passing 1-2% to consumers

items.statement: Crude up 30-35% led to 8-9% yarn cost increase and 3-4% garment cost for polyester products
items.quote: If the overall crude prices that we see has grown by almost 30%, 35%, it has translated to almost cost of 10% -- 8% or 9% in yarn cost, and which has resulted into 3% to 4% of apparel or garment cost.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment healthy but crude-led inflation could impact need-based basket
items.quote: So the consumer may find it difficult to manage their inflation and that could be a reality. And that is what we are caring about, that all of our consumers who are largely need-based consumers whose their income, but one respite we are able to see is the increase in minimum wages or the overall earning capabilities that is going to increase by the government.

items.statement: Polyester mix 70-75% for forward season; cotton ~50% in summer
items.quote: But when we are moving towards the forward season and the winterish season, the polyester mix goes up. That is why your polyester mix would be around 70%, 75% of the total sourcing that we are doing in the forward period.

items.statement: Fabric needs blocked 50-60% till December for forthcoming 6-7 months
items.quote: They have almost blo cked 50% to 60% of our needs or our total demand till December. So there is already a blocking which has happened for the forthcoming 6, 7 months

items.statement: Labour cost rise in Haryana/Noida could be detrimental; raw material availability challenges persist
items.quote: I see there are constraints in terms of the overall inflation, overall labour cost also going up because what happened recently in Haryana, or Noida and all of this certainly has led to a little bit of -- could lead to a little bit rise in the labour cost that again coul d be detrimental

items.statement: LimeRoad marketplace profitable at CM3 high single digits; losses cut ~70% YoY
items.quote: LimeRoad loss -- marketplace loss reduced significantly year-on-year, continuing the sustained improvement in the operating metrics for the online marketplace business. The marketplace business remains profitable at CM3 levels in high single digits.

items.statement: Full year PAT grew 6x to INR124 crores at 3.3% margin, approaching pre-COVID 4-4.5% levels
items.quote: As a culmination of all the improvements and efforts on a full year basis, PAT has grown by 6x to INR124 crores, reflecting consistency rather than quarter specific effects. This is our highest ever PAT and the PAT percentage at 3.3% is also now almost reaching the similar levels of PAT of around 4%, 4.5% that we used to enjoy pre-COVID.

items.statement: Medium-term ROC target 18-20%+; currently ~14.5%
items.quote: So I think we have been always working towards acquiring around 15% to 18% of ROC giving. So right now we are around 14.5% we want to go to 18% and then maybe 20% and above 20%.

items.statement: Rent expense target 6-7.5% of sales; currently ~8%
items.quote: So I think we should be hovering and then we should be comfortable around say 6%, 7% to 7.5% and 7% is the ballpark figure which we want to come up with.

items.statement: FY27 AUM growth guided at 20.0-25.0%
items.quote: For FY27, we are guiding an AUM growth of 20.0-25.0%, NIM of 12.8-13.2%, cost to income of 33.0-35.0%, credit cost of 3.0-4.0%, ROA of 4.0-4.8%, and an ROE of 16.0-20.0%.

items.statement: MFI portfolio growth assumed at 10-12% for FY27
items.quote: So our assumption is around 10-12%.

items.statement: Retail finance share expected to reach 24-25% by FY27 end
items.quote: It should hit somewhere around 24-25%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 NIM expanded 35 bps QoQ to 14.2%
items.quote: NIMs expanded by 35 bps QoQ to 14.2% in Q4.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing declined to 9.2% in Q4 FY26, marginal cost at 8.9%
items.quote: Cost of borrowing further declined to 9.2% in Q4, marking a total 60 bps reduction during the year. Our marginal cost of borrowing continued to remain around 8.9% in Q4.

items.statement: Added 9.8 lakh borrowers in FY26, 38% new-to-credit; net addition of 4 lakh+ after write-offs
items.quote: We continue to scale borrower acquisition with 3.3 Lakh borrowers added in Q4, while 9.8 Lakh borrowers added in FY26, of which 38% were new to credit.

items.statement: Retail finance AUM share rose to 18.1% in March 2026 from 5.9% a year ago
items.quote: The share of retail finance increased to 18.1% as of March 2026, up from 5.9% a year ago.

items.statement: New ECL model added INR 39 Cr provision in Q4 for West Asia crisis; Stage 1 ECL at 1.63%
items.quote: Considering the ongoing West Asia crisis, th e new ECL model has incorporated a higher weightage for major external event scenario resulting in an additional provisioning of INR 39 Crore in Q4

items.statement: Credit cost guidance range widened to 3-4% to absorb macro uncertainties and normative PAR accretion
items.quote: The broader range, what we have picked from 3.0-4.0%, it is primarily to take into account all these evolving externalities, because we need to see how, what is going to be the actual fallout of the global issues.

items.statement: Expects mid-double-digit revenue growth in FY27 with 30-40 bps EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: We are reasonably confident of sustaining mid double-digit growth in fiscal '27 with 30 to 40 basis points of EBITDA margin expansion.

items.statement: Online B2C expected to sustain 20%+ growth rate going forward
items.quote: Yes. for us, online B2C, like I said, continues to remain solid, and we expect that over the years, this should continue to be at 20% plus.

items.statement: Gross margin target of high-50s percentage over next 2-3 years
items.quote: We have directionally been working on delivering towards the high 50s, and that's what we will go towards the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Plans 1.5 lakh net sq ft retail space addition in FY27
items.quote: So we expect to drive about 1.5 lakhs net square feet addition over the next fiscal year across our portfolio.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps YoY; full-year FY26 EBITDA margin at 13.4%, up 40 bps
items.quote: EBITDA margin is at 13.4%, up 40 basis points year-on-year

items.statement: Will selectively implement price increases while safeguarding growth; sourcing predominantly India-based and deepening further
items.quote: We intend to double down on our cost control measures, and we will selectively implement price increase while safeguarding growth.

items.statement: Adjacent categories (footwear, innerwear) now 24% of business, grew 25% in FY26; will continue scaling womenswear
items.quote: Other categories (beyond men's apparel ) now contribute 24% of our business and were a meaningful growth driver.

items.statement: Net debt zero target delayed 9-12 months due to Flipkart transaction borrowing; primary objective to reduce term loan debt
items.quote: I think apart from that, we have been quite efficient. Hence this basically changes our goal of becoming a net debt zero Company in about maybe in 9 to 12 months.

items.statement: Expects 7-8% like-for-like growth in FY27 with equal split from pricing and volume; rest from expansion/upsizing
items.quote: We are expecting to see about 7% to 8% of like -for-like and the rest of it to come from an expansion, upsizing, etc.

items.statement: Store closures to continue at ~5% of fleet annually across brands; not concentrated in any single brand
items.quote: We should see approximately about 5% closures going forward. And I wouldn't say it's higher in one brand over the other.

items.statement: Flying Machine repositioned as unisex denim-anchored youth brand; clocked 70% B2C growth and double-digit retail LTL in Q4
items.quote: Flying Machine clocked retail LTL of double digits and a B2C growth of 70%.

items.statement: Expect 30%+ growth rate in solutions and products
items.quote: We believe this growth, we expect to be 30% on this, even though it's a small part, as we said, initially we start with 20 25%. We'll grow with 30% plus growth rate in these solutions and products

items.statement: Closed $349 million worth of increments in Q4
items.quote: The key highlight, if you want to ask me, is the 349 million worth increments closed during the quarter

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin at 20.8%, Q4 at 20.6%
items.quote: EBITDA growth margin is for the year 20.8%. And for this quarter, 20.6%.

items.statement: 21% of total pipeline now in products and solutions
items.quote: It's a 21% of the total pipeline is already into products and solutions, so it will, It basically gives us a very encouraging sign

items.statement: 9% year-on-year growth with OEM clients
items.quote: It's a 9% year-on-year growth with OEM clients, which has been our strategy.

items.statement: AI-led transformation causing near-term cannibalization in some areas
items.quote: AI-led transformation led to near-term cannibalization in some areas. In some cases, but over the period, not over the period, we see a larger opportunity with AI-based solution

items.statement: Lower than expected growth in middleware and autonomous driving due to delayed architecture programs
items.quote: Lower than expected growth in middleware and autonomous driving. And one of the important reason for this is Many New architecture programs have been delayed.

items.quote: For one of our clients, and I'll tell you it is a public news, Honda, they basically cancelled all their new platform programs And that had an impact on us, and it was very recently, because it happened in the April month

items.statement: Target wallet share of 15-20% among top 25 clients for FY26
items.quote: If you take the overall wallet share of KPIT among our top 25 clients is about 10% as of last year. That we grew by 10% to 12% year-on-year Now, the goal for this year is whether we can push that up to more than 15 to 20%.

items.statement: More than 80% of new contracts are fixed price in nature
items.quote: More than 80% of our new contracts are ﬁxed price in nature. That's something that we have driven very diligently over the last couple of years

items.statement: Converting four largest clients to outcome-based model this quarter, next four next quarter targeting 75%+ overall
items.quote: We'll be converting four of our largest clients in that model in this quarter, and we'll take the next four in the next quarter. And that will pretty much take us north of 75% overall, in terms of having outcome-based and ﬁxed price

items.statement: Added 13 new clients including 4 truck OEMs and 6 off-highway OEMs across 4 countries
items.quote: We have now built enough muscles and AI solutions and products do help us substantially. So unlike any other year in the past, we added 13 clients.

items.statement: Truck market expected to pick up in second half of 2026 with pre-buying
items.quote: There will be a pre-buying that will happen in the second half of 2026 And we believe that the truck business will pick up a little bit. The European market as well as North America market is likely to pick up in the second half of 2026.

items.statement: Strategic external investments of $400 million in M&A to create full stack story
items.quote: We have made strategic external investment of $400 million in M&AS, and I will tell you later how it actually stacks, create the full stack story

items.statement: FY27 revenue environment positive; two largest SDV programs ending but revenue largely compensated by new accounts; solid growth expected from trucks, off-highway, USA, India (doubling), China; 30% YoY revenue growth in solutions and produc
items.quote: I must say that all across we are seeing a good traction. I think we have some little bit of a few issues to tackle in the early part of the year, but we are seeing a very positive environment FY27.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 20.5% to 21.2% post increased investment in AI solutions, products competency development and new markets
items.quote: EBITDA 20.5 to 21.2 post increasing investment in AI solutions and products competency development and new markets.

items.statement: Medium-term target: solutions and products revenue share to reach 50% (from 15% in FY26) in 3 years; EBITDA margin target 22% to 24%
items.quote: Again, go back to the old days 50% revenue share to be achieved from solutions and product. This is very important. And See, the revenue part, which is in FY26, which is 85% of our, this 15% is solution and product, which will move to 60% in 3 years. And this is in terms of 40%. So we expect the EBITDA to be between 22% to 24% from where we are today.

items.statement: Annualized sustainable double-digit growth opportunity in medium term; aim for leadership in new adjacencies within 4 years
items.quote: We have opportunity for annualized sustainable double-digit growth. And I can tell you that I have been a little We want to be… make sure that we do not want to overcommit.

items.statement: Five levers to improve efficiency and margins: per-person revenue/contribution growth, outcome-based model, reusable solutions/assets, products-led approach in new markets, and AI-driven internal efficiency
items.quote: Over the last three years, consistently per person revenue and per person contribution for KPIT has gone up And we believe that it will continue to go up in future.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by higher gross contribution from solutions/products, shift to fixed-price AI-infused solutions, and internal AI efficiency in SG&A
items.quote: The margin growth will come through As we said, we believe that We will be in a position to increase our gross contribution signiﬁcantly through our approach of solutions and products Of course, you know the products typically the gross margins will be much higher.

items.statement: Positive FY27 environment across geographies; solid growth expected in trucks, off-highway, USA, India (doubling), China; connected vehicles, after-sales, autonomous driving to see substantial growth
items.quote: Solid growth is expected from trucks and oƯ-highway, USA, India. India, we will be Almost doubling, it's a small base, but doubling the revenue and China, which is also, again, have grown reasonably well Connected vehicles, after sales, and autonomous driving which we are expecting growth, which these are the areas where we will have substantial growth

items.statement: Passenger car software spend to increase FY26-30 despite near-term reset; Europe cutting costs but creating outsourcing opportunity; North America investing in future programs; India, China, Korea, Japan spend rising
items.quote: The overall people are cutting costs, right, especially in Europe, and you know there are it's not necessarily R&D spend. The cost is going down so that they can continue to spend money where it matters to them from future perspective.

items.statement: Solutions and products revenue to grow 30% YoY in FY27; target 50% revenue share in 3 years (from 15% in FY26); nonlinear growth expected via conversion of fixed-price to AI-infused solutions and product scaling
items.quote: We expect 30% year-on-year revenue growth in solution and products, and we hope it will increase over the period.

items.statement: Products-led approach in new markets (India, Southeast Asia, Africa) for cost-effective, profitable entry; Qorix middleware platform to ramp in trucks/off-highway and new architecture programs in 1-2 years
items.quote: In the new markets, whether it's India, China, Southeast Asia and Africa. Unlike the Western world where we started with services and then sort of we are in the process of graduating to solutions and products, we'll take the products and solutions ﬁrst approach to the new market

items.statement: Two large SDV programs ending in FY27: one planned ramp-down (impact in Q1), one surprise EV program cancellation ($15B hit to OEM); no other abrupt program ends foreseen
items.quote: The other one was a surprise, not only to us, but to the rest of the world, when that OEM decided to stop their EV programs The launch of this, and they decided to take a$ 15 billion hit, one-time hit right on their balance sheet.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict (oil prices) may impact truck business faster than passenger car if sustained beyond 3-6 months; clients currently focused on cost rationalization, no spending cuts yet
items.quote: We have not seen the impact on the OEMs yet because of the conﬂict that we are seeing at this point in time. We'll see when it gets resolved. I think if it continues beyond three to six months, it'll have repercussions, you That will be macro.

items.statement: TCV wins jumped significantly in Q4 FY26 on back of off-highway commercial and traditional clients; stronger traction vs last year; multi-year deals create quarterly variability but positive yearly trend
items.quote: It has come on the back of oƯ highway commercial and few other strong wins we had and also other our traditional clients also So it's not it's a process, I think it just worked out during this quarter.

items.statement: India revenue ~4% currently, doubling in FY27; target dominant role as India becomes 3rd/2nd largest auto market; China revenue similar to India (~4%), not disclosed separately
items.quote: Right now, we are about 4% of our revenues are from India and they will increase substantially. The share will go up and we do believe If it is going to be the third largest market. That's why we are doubling down.

items.statement: Cymotive acquisition: cybersecurity expertise in millions of vehicles; leveraging for other OEMs as AI/quantum threats grow; Cariad consolidation moved work to KPIT India
items.quote: The biggest advantage to that is it is in many millions of vehicles already Which gives us a conﬁdence or other OEMs will get there.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected to be double-digit, most probably in the mid-teens, assuming current aluminum prices
items.quote: It is truly double digit, most probably, in the mid-teens, I would say. That is what is the expectation for the growth.

items.statement: Stationary engine order book of $100 million finalized, targeting that revenue by FY29-30
items.quote: The stationary engine side is the order book is for the first $100 million is finalized and is with us. So as slated earlier -- as stated earlier, I would say, we will be able to reach that $100 million sort of revenue in '29, '30.

items.statement: FY27 capex decision to be made in September; FY28 capex depends on FY27 performance; monitoring net debt to EBITDA
items.quote: On FY 2027 itself, we are not very clear about the capex as today because we have taken some interim requirements. But September we have to decide on the capex even for FY 2027. FY 2028 depends on the performance of FY 2027.

items.statement: Sunbeam aluminum margins at single-digit; restructuring underway with exit of unprofitable customers/products; traction expected from Q2 FY26
items.quote: We are just lacking behind on the margin-wise with a single, still at single-digit for various reasons. We are on the right track that we are exiting customers where it's not profitable, exiti ng subsegments of the business with same customers where it's not profitable totally or even selling one portion of the low- value business which is around INR30 crore per year

items.statement: Aluminum price pass-through enforced; declining supply where pass-through not agreed; resetting legacy prices across aluminum plants

items.quote: Frankly speaking, we are focusing on value-added products like casting and machining. We are not interested really to do only the casting portion.

items.quote: What is worrying us more is not the debt, as I mentioned. What is worrying us the inflationary manpower cost, which is very difficult to pass on to customer.

items.quote: The greenfield project is already on. The civil construction is on, and the plant will be commissioned by December. So next year it will be in operation.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA currently 2.43x; targeting <2x in current year, then further down to 1.5x
items.quote: we are already at 2.43 net debt to EBITDA. We are looking at, going forward, it'll be less than 2, I would say, in the coming, the current year itself, totally. And then it'll go down furt her to 1.5

items.quote: If you're going at this rate, no. Because the future capex in this year will again spoil the margins. Whatever gains we are making on the installed capacity.

items.statement: Targeting FY27 PAT of over ₹300 crores (2x FY26 PAT)
items.quote: that's the kind of a target that we have in mind. So with the credit cycle in the MFI industry behind our back, I think that's the kind of number that we are targeting as a bank

items.statement: Targeting cost-to-income ratio of 67-68% for FY27

items.quote: Approximately 80% of our order book carries cell price pass-through clauses, insulating the P&L from any input volatility.

items.quote: The aforesaid capex programs shall be met with a disciplined mix of debt and equity. Capital prudence is non-negotiable. items.statement: FY27 production 7.5-8 GW (6 GW non-DCR, 2 GW DCR); DCR offtake ramps H2 FY27 post June 2026 mandate
items.quote: FY27 collectively with the 6-gigawatt module coming is expected to produce collectively for the company as a whole some 8 gigawatts, of which as we discussed 2 gigawatts will be on the DCR front and the balance 6 on the non-DCR.

items.statement: BESS target 15 GWh by FY30: 5 GWh pack assembly by Mar 2027, 7.5 GWh cell FY29, 7.5 GWh cell FY30
items.quote: The journey for the 15 gigawatt-hour BESS capacity has also kick-started wherein a 5 gigawatt-hour cell-to-pack facility is scheduled to commission by March 27, followed by the first phase of 7.5 gigawatt-hour of battery cell manufacturing to commission in FY 29 and the second phase in FY30.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of INR 150 crore minimum, with internal estimate of INR 160-165 crore
items.quote: We are estimating more than INR 160 crores to INR 165 crores. But you know, the fair bet is 150 is definitely we will achieve.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target of INR 220-230 crore, aiming for 200+ crore
items.quote: We will be doing more than 200 plus crores in FY '28, sir. It will be around 200 to 250 somewhere in between like INR 220-230 crores definitely we will be achieving.

items.statement: PAT margin guidance of 16-17% for FY27 and next 3-4 years
items.quote: So, in that, keeping all that in mind, we are estimating around 16% to 17% PAT.

items.statement: Printing capacity sufficient up to INR 250 crore revenue; warehouse capacity up to INR 300 crore; no major capex needed except notebook machine already purchased
items.quote: So, up to INR 250 crores, we don't have to buy even CAPEX. And our own warehouse, we have around 1,50,000 square feet of warehouse, which is company-owned, our own property. So, this particular space can handle up to INR 300 crores of turnover, sir.

items.statement: E-commerce platform scaled from 3 pilot schools to 50 schools in FY26, generating INR 20 crore; targeting 150 schools in FY27 for INR 50-60 crore
items.quote: Going forward, next year, with 150 schools, we are estimating around INR 50 crores to INR 60 crores of turnover. Just from the 150 schools, which we are trying to close.

items.statement: Uniform business carries ~50% EBITDA margin; scaling uniforms will lift overall margins
items.quote: What we noticed is that the uniform margins are close to 50%. So, when we scale it up, how much will that change in percentages, we need to calculate.

items.statement: Geographic expansion from 10 to 15 states in FY26; targeting all 28 states and 8 UTs in next 3 years
items.quote: In the next 3 years, my target is to get into all the 28 states and 8 union territories of the country.

items.statement: NCERT-aligned workbooks for Classes 6-8 saw strong adoption; pilot of 10,000 copies each sold 40,000 requiring 4 reprints
items.quote: So, we did a pilot print of 10,000 copies each, and we sold around 40,000. So, we had to reprint the product four times.

items.statement: No dividend planned for FY26; may consider after reaching internal targets next year
items.quote: Right now, we are a growing company. Maybe we will probably declare next year after once we reach a certain target which are there in our mind. But this year, no dividend.

items.statement: E-commerce platform (Pelican Edu Supply) processes ~22-23% of total revenue; enables faster working capital cycle via direct parent payments
items.quote: If I am telling that I have generated INR 20 crores of revenue out of the INR 91 crores from technology, that is close to 20%, right? Around 22%-23% of, we are generating from the technology.

items.statement: Notebook manufacturing capacity of 10 tons/day installed; 80% of capacity already booked via orders
items.quote: So, let's say, our notebook, we will be doing around 10 tons capacity per day, out of which 80% capacity we already have procured orders.

items.statement: Jewellery growth guidance of 15-20% CAGR over next 3-5 years
items.quote: I think this is the general guidance that we have given that we should be able to sustain this kind of a growth irrespective of gold rate because it's intrinsic to what we kind of try to achieve irrespective of the gold rate.

items.statement: Jewellery growth guidance of 15-20% CAGR over next 3-5 years reiterated by MD
items.quote: Therefore, the 15% to 20% is something that we ought to do, you know. If we don't do that much, we won't be doing justice to all these tailwinds.

items.statement: Jewellery margin sustainability depends on gold price; 10-20 bps pressure visible
items.quote: So, I would not give you a good assurance that this is sustainable. A lot of things are going on. And maybe we will have more informed view to guide a little bit about this.

items.statement: Margin sustainability easier if gold price stable; improvement possible
items.quote: Sustainability of margin would become far easier if gold rate remains where it is. And then we will see whether there is an opportunity to improve or what.

items.statement: Q4 buyer growth 8% vs flat prior; driven by wedding preponement, diamond festival, exchange campaign
items.quote: So, very clearly, we have seen resurgence in buyer growth in Quarter 4 and what we have reported is 8% versus a flattish for the period prior to that.

items.statement: Exchange program sustaining; expected to drive buyer growth forward
items.quote: We think so. We believe so. That's why we are sustaining the investment behind exchange. It's very relevant for wedding buyers.

items.statement: Gold loan cost not increasing; tenure extended to 270 days
items.quote: No, not yet. Actually, now, if you would recall, gold loan tenure has been increased from 180 to 270 days. And I think we are working on that, and we are successful in starting that also.

items.statement: Analog watches ~85-90% of watch division revenue; overall watch growth 14%
items.quote: Within overall business. Analog within the watch is around 85%. Now closer to 90%.

items.statement: beYon LGD expansion to 10-12 stores in 2-3 cities in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We are at two stores currently and hopefully we will get a bunch of stores in place well in Quarter 1 itself.

items.statement: Gold supply covered for Q1; exchange program and plan Bs ready
items.quote: We are pretty much quite covered for Quarter 1. And also our gold exchange program is very, very successfully being run from the last Quarter 3 onwards.

items.statement: GCC situation unpredictable; Damas Q4 loss ₹82 cr due to March disruption
items.quote: March month was quite disturbed in the GCC, where not only Damas is present, but our Tanishq also is present. So, all those things have kind of come in the Q4 in the form of loss of ₹82 crores.

items.statement: Unallocated loss ₹140 cr in Q4 due to ₹100-120 cr special employee reward
items.quote: And this year also the good performance has been celebrated by sharing that with all the employees and all the people connected with Titan. So, it is about ₹100- ₹120 crores roughly.

items.statement: Transfer pricing adjustment ₹80+ cr in standalone; nullifies in consolidated
items.quote: We formalized that from '25-26, where we are now treating our all subsidiaries as low-risk distributor. And that Titan as a parent company is in a way ensuring that a certain amount of basic profit is there and that transfer pricing adjustment in the standalone books is about ₹80 crores plus minus.

items.statement: Ticket size benefit from gold price inflation in Q1-Q2 FY27; H2 depends on gold trajectory
items.quote: So, therefore, in that sense, if you were to compare, let's say, Quarter 1 versus Quarter 1 of last year, just the increase in gold rate will give us a certain ticket size benefit in Quarter 1 and Quarter 2.

items.statement: CaratLane Q4 margin 8.4% due to revenue impact from ERP migration; FY margin ~10%
items.quote: Yes, it is because the Revenue was one big factor. And also, we have continued our investment on our campaigns in order to generate a lot more awareness among customers.

items.statement: Taneira focusing on same-store growth, buyer growth, stock turns, sell-throughs; sub-₹10k price band push
items.quote: One is, of course, same-store growth, buyer growth. And thirdly, we will be looking at these stock turns as well as the sell-throughs of product merchandise that has been brought in.

items.statement: Expect high-single digit top-line growth with EBITDA margins around 25% in FY27
items.quote: As mentioned in our earlier interactions, we expect to grow our top line high-single digits with margins at around 25% in FY27, despite increased headwinds from an uncertain geopolitical environment.

items.statement: Confirmed high-single digit revenue growth in Rupee terms and EBITDA margin around 25% for FY27
items.quote: That's correct. We did say that we would be looking at around about 25%, or in the vicinity of that for the full year and of course high-single digit number in terms of overall sales growth.

items.statement: Expect R&D spend around 8% of sales in FY27
items.quote: We expect R&D to be around 8% of sales for the next fiscal.

items.statement: Expect effective tax rate of 25-26% in FY27 due to phasing out of domestic incentives
items.quote: For FY27, we expect the ETR to be about 25% - 26% due to the phasing out of incentives on some of our domestic facilities.

items.statement: India formulations business to continue outperforming IPM by 1.2x to 1.3x
items.quote: We remain confident that our India formulations business will continue to outperform IPM by 1.2x to 1.3x going forward, supported by salesforce of about 12,000 people and a pipeline of more than 80 new product launches over the coming years including innovative in-house and in-licensed products.

items.statement: Plan to launch about 20 products in India in FY27
items.quote: We launched 15 products in FY26 and plan to launch about 20 products in FY27.

items.statement: Chronic segment target increased to 70% of India portfolio in next five years
items.quote: The chronic segment now accounts for 66% of our portfolio up from 64% in FY25, and we have set ourselves a target to increase this share to 70% in the next five years.

items.statement: US business to launch 50+ products over next three years including 10 exclusive first-to-files, 4 biosimilars, 2-3 505(b)(2)s
items.quote: In the next three years we expect to launch 50 plus products in the US with 10 exclusive first to files, four biosimilars as well as two to three 505(b)(2)s.

items.statement: US base business grew supported by higher volumes offsetting low-single digit price erosion

items.statement: Management expects FY27 volume growth in mid-single digits, close to 20 million tons, with EBITDA similar to FY26 range
items.quote: I said close to close to 20 million tons, I did not give a specific number. I said mid-single digit in terms of volume.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR900 crores; total capex for 6 million ton expansion is INR4,753 crores including GST (INR4,300 crores net)
items.quote: For FY '27 it is INR900 crores. And our capacity addition by FY '29 will be 6 million tons, from 21.5 to 27.5.

items.quote: out landed cost for Bikram is going to be in the region of 1 to 1.05. And the current prices of domestic coal maybe around 1.45. So that will give you a sense of the cost arbitrage that we will get from Bikram coal block.

items.statement: Peak net debt expected at INR4,000 crores during capex cycle; debt-to-EBITDA not to exceed 2.5x
items.quote: In this capex cycle, our expectation is that the peak net debt should be in the range of INR4,000 crores.

items.quote: with Kundanganj coming on stream, we expect the incentives to go up to around INR130 crores.

items.quote: We consciously started building up stocks because of the geopolitical situation. We were anticipating some tightness in so far as the price of the coal is concerned, for coal and the fuel is concerned.

items.statement: Expect double-digit revenue growth of 12% to 14% in FY27
items.quote: We remain fairly confident that we will again deliver double-digit growth between 12%, let's say, and 14% in the FY '27 fiscal.

items.statement: Expect 60-plus hotel openings across brands and geographies in FY27
items.quote: In FY '27, we expect 60 -plus hotel openings across brands and geographies.

items.statement: Recent acquisitions expected to contribute over INR250 crores incremental revenue in FY27
items.quote: Our recent acquisitions are expected to contribute over INR250 crores in incremental revenue.

items.statement: Ginger brand to have 250 hotels under development or in operation by end of FY27
items.quote: We expect the Ginger brand itself to have a total portfolio of 250 hotels either under development or in operation at the end of FY '27.

items.statement: Annual capex of INR1,000 crores to INR1,200 crores to strengthen existing and build new competitive advantages
items.quote: Even going forward, we will continue to invest INR1,000 crores to INR1,200 crores annually to strengthen our existing competitive advantages and at the same time, build new ones.

items.statement: FY26 capex over INR1,000 crores with INR650 crores for renovations, maintenance and digital, rest for greenfield projects
items.quote: IHCL in FY '25 -'26 spent over INR1,000 crores towards capex, out of which around INR650 crores was used for renovations, routine maintenance and digital initiatives, while the rest half was used towards greenfield projects.

items.statement: Pipeline remains strong at 31,000-plus keys, largely capital-light
items.quote: Our pipeline remains strong at 31,000-plus keys and continues to be largely capital light.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin of 35% in FY26 reflecting operating discipline and structural efficiency
items.quote: Even as we invested meaningfully for future growth, we delivered EBITDA margin of 35%, reflecting operating discipline and structural efficiency.

items.statement: Stand-alone EBITDA margin expanded 120 bps to 45.1% in FY26
items.quote: On a stand-alone basis, revenue grew 10% year -on-year to INR5,640 crores, EBITDA grew 13% year-on-year to INR2,543 crores, yielding EBITDA margin of 45.1%, an expansion of 120 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Like-for-like RevPAR growth expected at high single digits (7-9%) on sustained basis
items.quote: On a sustained basis, high single digits, let's say, anywhere starting from 7-ish going up 8%, 9% depending on the hotel and the region and the quarter you pick.

items.statement: Domestic demand resilient, international travel subdued due to West Asia conflict
items.quote: Domestic has been pretty resilient. And even in the month of April, domestic has actually done quite well. It's pacing quite well, keeping in mind that international travel is kind of subdued right now.

items.statement: Goa showing north of 25% growth in April across all hotels, Kerala and Chennai could improve
items.quote: Goa, we have seen almost in the month of April north of 25% growth in all our hotels. Some have gone to 30% and beyond. So, averaging at 25%. Goa is definitely back since the last few months, March and April, and the trend is not changing.

items.statement: New businesses vertical grew 25% in FY26 to INR753 crores revenue, 31% CAGR over 4 years
items.quote: Our new businesses vertical comprising Ginger, Qmin, Ama, Stays & Trails and Tree of Life delivered 25% growth in FY '26. This resulted in a consolidated revenue of INR753 crores.

items.statement: West Asia conflict caused INR40-50 crores revenue impact on consolidated basis, near INR100 crores on enterprise basis in Q4
items.quote: We did see some loss of revenues in some of our hotels internationally, including London. And that's what we tried to summarize also on the slide on impact of the West Asia conflict, about INR40 crores to INR50 crores of revenue on the consol basis and almost close to INR100 crores on an enterprise basis.

items.statement: Board proposed dividend of INR3.25 per share (25% of consolidated PAT), up 44% from FY25, including INR0.50 special dividend for 125th AGM
items.quote: the Board has p roposed a dividend equivalent to 25% of consolidated PAT amounting to INR3.25 per equity share, subject to shareholders' approval. This includes a one -time special dividend of INR0.50 per share to commemorate IHCL's landmark 125th AGM

items.statement: Management stopped giving volume guidance due to geopolitical uncertainties but expects growth
items.quote: So we stopped giving guidance due to the geopolitical scenarios and uncertainties. But we are, of course, expecting growth, but we don't give guidance on that.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected between INR1,500-1,800 crores
items.quote: In this financial year, between INR1,500 crores to INR1,800 crores.

items.statement: Board approved additional INR2,000 crores capex for capacity expansion, AI automation and sustainability
items.quote: The Board of Directors has approved an additional capex of INR2,000 crores, which will support capacity expansion and infrastructure development across both OHT and on-highway tyre categories, AI enabled automation across on-highway tyre category, and also the company's sustainability initiatives.

items.statement: Maintenance capex of ~INR200 crores per year extra
items.quote: This is only project. And maintenance is about INR200-odd crores every year, which will be extra, which is also in the past has been always mentioned extra.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin 22.9%, FY26 margin 22.7%, near-term margin pressure expected due to raw material costs
items.quote: So at this moment, we are seeing the pressure to come. We are evaluating the situation and see how much we can pass on. But at this moment, we may have some price pressures, margin pressures.

items.statement: Price hikes of 3-5% taken across geographies, targeting additional 2% this month, may take further hikes
items.quote: So price hike, we have taken between 3% to 5% already across various geographies, and we are targeting around 2% in this very month, towards the end of this month. And we'll continue to watch this, and maybe we may have to take further price hikes.

items.statement: Freight cost 4.5-5% of revenue in Q4, expected to increase marginally
items.quote: It was about 4.5% to 5%, and we expect it to go up marginally, the way things are, subject to no further disruption.

items.statement: Europe H2 recovery driven by easing channel inventories, Americas improving traction, India sustained momentum
items.quote: From an end market perspective, in Europe, H2 showed good recovery over H1, driven by easing in channel inventories. Similarly, in the Americas market, we are witnessing improving traction supported by higher channel activity.

items.statement: Moving towards high-end radialized products like IF/VF technology to improve mix
items.quote: So we are moving more towards the high-end radialized products, the specialized products like IF/VF technology products. So we are working on those as a product mix.

items.statement: Channel inventory at normal levels, no restocking opportunity seen
items.quote: No, we see it at normal levels.

items.statement: Median EBITDA margin target raised to high single digit (~9%) from ~7-8%; bad year 6.5-7%, good year 10-11%
items.quote: Our objective is to take the median towards a high single digit, which is about 9%. So, that in a bad year like this, our EBITDA will be around 6.5%-7%, and in a good year, we will even cross 10% or 11%.

items.statement: Cow flush started in South/West regions; volumes improving but not yet surplus to soften prices; milk volume growth 1% YoY Q4, 2% FY26; VAP volume growth 18-22.5% YoY
items.quote: As we speak now, we are already seeing supply side improved in regions of dominant cow milk availability. So, you can say that the cow milk flush has started and we are seeing the volumes being increasingly available.

items.quote: in the first year, we are expecting the utilization to be around 35% to 40%. And we had mentioned that it will take us about six to seven years to utilize this facility completely.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 13.76% driven by higher volumes, better realizations and operational efficiency
items.quote: Operating EBITDA stood at INR 55 crores , up 42% year -on-year with EBITDA margins which have improved to 13.76, which is driven by higher volumes, better realizations and enhanced operational efficiency.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 12.31% supported by strong volume growth, improved margins and higher capacity utilization
items.quote: Operating EBITDA reached a new peak at INR 177 crores, up 42% year-on-year. EBITDA margins expanded to 12.31% for the year supported by strong volume growth, improved margins and higher capacity utilization.

items.statement: Major NBR capacity expansion to double capacity expected by Q1 FY28; no major capacity coming in FY27

items.statement: Board approved new R&D center with planned spend of INR 20-25 crores on infrastructure
items.quote: We are building a new R&D center this year for which we have got approval from the board and we are going to spend somewhere between INR 20 crores to INR 25 crores, building a new R&D center.

items.statement: Nitrile latex running at 90-100% capacity utilization in Q4; expect to continue at full utilization
items.quote: We are running at almost full 100% capacity utilization now for Nitrile latex. And at least going forward, we expect to run at full 100% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Expect low double-digit volume growth for FY27 if demand sustains, despite high capacity utilization
items.quote: I think, as I said, the whole world is a little very uncertain right now, but if the demand is there and we do have capacity to grow by another in double- digits, low double-digits in volume for the whole year.

items.statement: Raw material prices increased ~70% in Q4 tracking crude; covered till end of June but Strait of Hormuz closure creates uncertainty
items.quote: We have seen the crude prices have gone up by about 70% in a couple of months. So that is about, round about the increase we are also looking at in raw material prices.

items.quote: Short answer is yes, absolutely. I think that is a big worry because in the long run, I don't know these kinds of high energy prices and high petrochemical prices, I don't know the, or nobody knows, I don't think anyone can predict what the demand destruction will be.

items.quote: As of March 31st, we have a total debt of about INR 90 crores. And our investments and cash bank balances are INR 160-odd crores.
