items.statement: International air freight rates increased ~15% since March 2025 due to geopolitical supply constraints
items.quote: As I'm talking to you from March, 15%, international rates have increased. So, rates are hardening.

items.statement: No immediate plans for warehousing or asset-heavy capex; current operations yield higher ROCE than warehouse business
items.quote: Our current operations are giving us more ROCE than if we venture into the warehouse operation. So that is the process going on but never say never.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict causing supply issues and rate hardening, but company maintains momentum with 60+ airline relationships
items.quote: Unfortunately, there is -- supply issues are there. But since we have -- we are operating with more than 60 airlines.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR0.40 per share (30% of PAT) for FY26
items.quote: The Board has also recommended a final dividend of INR0.40 per equity share for 2025-2026. It is basically 30% of our profit after tax.

items.statement: Actively pursuing redevelopment of non-core property with adjacent landowners; meeting scheduled next week to maximize value
items.quote: As early as next week also, we're going to have a meeting for that only. And rest assured, we are actively pursuing that matter.

items.statement: Rajpat Logistics to operate asset-light trucking model for select top corporates with minimal receivables risk
items.quote: We are an asset light company, and we will continue to be an asset light company. So, we will not own any trucks, but we will leverage our network.

items.statement: Expects 10-14% growth in international business for FY27, possibly up to 15%
items.quote: Yes, we expect 10 to 14% growth in our international business this year, as per our current business plan. Last year there was 4% growth, this year we expect 10 to 14%. Maybe even 15%.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at INR 120 crores, including land acquisition
items.quote: No, it'll be closer INR 120 crores and the reason for that is we're also looking at land.

items.statement: Total announced capex of INR 240 crores over next 18 months (INR 200 crores projects + INR 40 crores land)
items.quote: So I mean, you know, you need to factor all that in that it's a total announcement of 240 crores.

items.statement: Major capacity enhancement projects commissioning from June-July 2026 through Q1 2028; partial benefits from current quarter
items.quote: We expect commissioning of major enhancement projects starting from June -July and continuing through this financial year and beyond up to the first quarter of 2028.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 19.5% from 18.3% driven by structural initiatives
items.quote: EBITDA increased by 19% year-on-year to INR267 crores and margins expanded to 19.5% from 18.3% in this financial year.

items.statement: Targets maintaining EBITDA margin consistently between 18-21% over next five years including industrial business
items.quote: Will it average out to what we have over the next five years? Will it pan out and be in line with our aspirational goal of maintaining profitability consistently between 18% and 21%? Yes.

items.statement: No internal risks identified; well-positioned to navigate external challenges with strong management and owner-driven governance
items.quote: I mean, nothing beyond what other companies or the environment faces , as we don't have any internal risk whatsoever.

items.statement: Domestic business resilient despite global challenges; export demand impacted but international business grew 4% in FY26
items.quote: While export demand was impacted, NRB and its subsidiaries remain more resilient than many of those around us. Our international business did grow over the previous year to a little over 4%.

items.statement: Inventory reduced by over INR 20 crores despite significant sales growth; position considered close to optimal
items.quote: Nevertheless, we believe that there was and will continue to be scope for improvement, and our inventories at the end of the year were in fact lower by over INR20 crores, even though our sales rose significantly.

items.statement: Loan growth guidance upsized to 12-14% for FY27 from previous 11-13%
items.quote: The loan growth earlier we had given a guidance of 11 to 13 %, now we are upsizing that to 12 to 14 %.

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance raised to 10-12% for FY27 from previous 9-11%
items.quote: Deposit growth guidance for the last year was 9 to 11 %, that we are improving to 10 to 12 %.

items.statement: NIM guidance set at 2.75-2.95% for full year FY27
items.quote: The NIM guidance has been 2.75 to 2.95% for the full year.

items.statement: ROA guidance maintained at above 1% for FY27
items.quote: ROA, as we always say, the ROA is going to be more than 1 %

items.statement: Slippage ratio guidance maintained at 1-1.25% for FY27 considering geopolitical issues
items.quote: the slippage ratio we continue to maintain at 1 to 1.25 % considering the geopolitical issue that we are going to have

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY27 set at less than 0.60% for full year
items.quote: The credit cost for the full year is going to be less than 0.60%.

items.statement: Plan to raise Rs 6,000 crores via AT-1 and Tier 2 bonds in FY27
items.quote: we have announced that we are going to raise Rs. 6000 crores in the form of AT-1 or Tier 2 in this financial year.

items.statement: Enabling provision for Rs 8,500 crores equity capital raise over 2-3 years up to FY28
items.quote: we have enabling provision of raising almost Rs. 8500 crores of equity capital over a period of 2-3 years. That is still FY28.

items.statement: Technology spend was Rs 4,500 crores in FY26 (opex+capex), may upsize due to cyber/AI threats
items.quote: we had around Rs. 4,500 crores as the spend, both Opex and Capex put together in technology

items.statement: RAM advances share increased to 61% of loan book
items.quote: the business model continued to be RAM focused. So, RAM growth has been good and the RAM percentage has gone to 61 %.

items.statement: Domestic NIM improved to 3.04% in Q4 FY26 from 2.79% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: the NIM has improved vis-a-vis the last quarter from 2.79% to 2.89% with the domestic NIM at 3.04%.

items.statement: ECLGS scheme expected to enable Rs 12,000+ crores disbursement to MSMEs (20% of working capital book)
items.quote: Based on the 20% of that, we are expecting Rs. 12,000 plus crores is the impact which you can disperse because of the ECLGS scheme.

items.statement: No immediate impact on domestic or international book from West Asia conflict; monitoring closely
items.quote: As of today, we don't see anything on the global book also because of the geopolitical impact in global book.

items.statement: Pension fund subsidiary setup expected in 6-9 months post regulatory approvals
items.quote: On the pension fund 6 to 9 months, whereas the standalone PD, the PD is already operational from 1st April 2026.

items.statement: Hiring plan of 6-7,000 employees for FY27, expecting net addition of 4-5,000 headcount
items.quote: year also the hiring plan continue to be the similarly 6 to 7,000 employees. But sometimes whatever your hiring plan, people don't join once you offer. Some of them do not join. So, in that way, I think we'll be adding something around 4 to 5,000 headcounts in this year

items.statement: Expects overall industry growth of 14-16% and aims to do better; targets 13-15% growth in all critical parameters annually
items.quote: We do hope that 14 % to 15% to 16% growth for overall industry, not only for IOB, is very much feasible and we can do better than that.

items.statement: Targets around 3,600 crores of NPA recovery for FY27, down from over 4,000 crores previously due to lower NPA stock
items.quote: Now because stock has come down, the outstanding NPA numbers have come down. So, this year we are targeting around 3600 crores of recovery.

items.statement: Expects to maintain global NIM in the range of 3.30% to 3.35%
items.quote: Yes, 3.2, I think. Global it is 3.21, domestic it is 3.32. We expect to maintain at this range between 3.30 to 3.35.

items.statement: Anticipates total ECL impact of around 3,000 crores; has already provided 1,750 crores and plans to front-load the full requirement by April 2027
items.quote: And as per our calculation, we anticipate that the total impact of ECL, the new guideline which has been given by the regulator, it is going to be around 3000 crores.

items.statement: Expects additional funding of 8,000 to 10,000 crores through ECLGS 5.0 scheme valid until March 2027
items.quote: Our broad assessment is that around 8,000 to 10,000 crores of additional funding can happen through this ECLS mode this is valid up to March 27

items.statement: Cost of deposits decreased to 4.97% from 5.08%; cost of funds decreased to 5.09% from 5.24%
items.quote: As regards performance ratios, I have to talk about the cost of deposits. It came down to 4.97% as of 31st March 2026 when compared to 5.08% as of 31st March 2025.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved by 220 bps to 44.94% from 47.14%
items.quote: Cost to income came down by 220 bps and it stood at 44.94 as of 31st March 2026 when compared to 47.14 as of 31st March 2025.

items.statement: SMA ratio improved to 4.92% from 6.70%; no stress seen from West Asia crisis so far
items.quote: March ‘25 our SMA percentage to total credit used to be 6.70 last year. And as in March ‘26, it came down to 4.92%.

items.statement: RAM (Retail, Agri, MSME) constitutes 83% of domestic advances; retail grew 45%, agri ~40%, MSME 13% YoY
items.quote: Regarding the share of domestic advances, 83% of domestic advances constitute RAM, and remaining 17 percent constitutes corporate and others.

items.statement: Jewel loans form ~30% of total credit portfolio; 70% are agriculture jewel loans with zero NPA/SMA
items.quote: Almost 70% of the jevel loan will be agriculture. The remaining will be classified as retail and MSME. And of our total credit portfolio, around 30% is jewel loan.

items.statement: Overseas NPAs are legacy accounts from 2015-17 with negligible fresh slippages in last three years; all in various court stages
items.quote: These NP accounts in overseas center, they are legacy accounts very old ones because recent slippages last three years. There have not been many as far as slippage is concerned.

items.statement: Agriculture portfolio is largely jewel-backed in Tamil Nadu and southern regions, not pure crop loans, so monsoon risk is mitigated
items.quote: In that geography in which we generally operate, mostly operate, there is agriculture jewel loans, backed by jewel. It's not pure crop loan.

items.statement: Technology investment increasing year-on-year up to 15%; AI being deployed as full-fledged system for automation, fraud monitoring, and mule account detection
items.quote: In fact, our technology investment is increasing year on year, up to 15%. So, we are fully aligned with what is happening in the industry.

items.statement: Plans to revive QIP to create public float after previous attempt was dropped due to West Asia crisis
items.quote: But this year again, we'll be back with that. So let us see. That creating a float in the system, that is a challenge, and we are working on it.

items.statement: Digital transactions at 96%; ~21-22% of retail loans sourced fully digitally with delinquencies comparable to branch-sourced loans
items.quote: 96% of our transactions are happening through digitally. Year on year, and quarter on quarter we are improving on that.

items.statement: ROA baseline set at above 1.20%; current ROA at 1.23% for FY26
items.quote: Our baseline is that ROA at any point of time should be above 1.20. That is the baseline. Above that, of course, we will try to do better.

items.statement: Overall revenue growth expected at 18-20% in FY27
items.quote: So, with the demand trend continuing to grow upward, we expect the overall growth of around 18% to 20% next year.

items.statement: Sanitaryware revenue growth expected at 12% in FY27 driven by 7% volume and 5-6% price impact
items.quote: In sanitaryware segment, we expect 12% growth driven by favourable volume impact of 7% and price impact of 5% to 6%.

items.statement: Faucetware revenue growth expected at 18% in FY27 driven by 10-12% volume and 8% price impact
items.quote: And similarly in case of faucetware, we expect a growth of 18% which is going to be driven by favourable volume impact of 10% to 12% and price impact of 8%.

items.statement: Faucetware volume growth expected at 10-12% and sanitaryware at 7-8% in FY27
items.quote: Going forward in FY27, we expect that faucetware should continue to grow at 10% to 12% in volumes, and sanitaryware should be in the range of, you can say, 7% to 8% in FY27 also.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to sustain at 14-15% if demand trend continues
items.quote: We see that if this this trend continues, we will be able to sustain the EBITDA margins at around 14% to 15%.

items.statement: Price increases of 12% in sanitaryware and 16% in faucetware implemented over two months to offset brass cost rise
items.quote: So, effectively over a period of two months, we have taken a price increase of 12% in the case of sanitaryware and 16% in the case of faucetware.

items.statement: Faucetware capacity expansion to 5 lakh pieces per month with minimal capex of INR 4-5 crore operational from Q4 FY27
items.quote: We are further increasing this capacity from 4.30 lakh per unit to 5 lakh per unit by debottlenecking and by putting some efforts within the brownfield setup that we have built earlier with a minimal capex of around INR 4 crore to INR 5 crore.

items.statement: Senator and Polipluz combined revenue target of INR 70-80 crore in FY27 vs INR 19 crore in FY26
items.quote: Total, we expect that these two brands taken together should give us roughly INR 70 to INR 80 crore.

items.statement: Retail demand recovery seen from Q3 FY26 sustaining through Q4 and April, expected to continue in FY27
items.quote: Since Q3 of the current financial year, we have started seeing an improvement in the retail demand, and we saw this sustaining through Q4 also. If we see the month of April also, we have seen a good surge in retail; it has continued in the current quarter also.

items.statement: Greenfield sanitaryware plant construction evaluation to begin in coming quarters; first phase estimated at INR 150 crore plus INR 27 crore land already purchased
items.quote: The greenfield project was initially estimated at around INR 130 crore, of which land portion has already been purchased, that is at INR 27 crore. And considering the two years' inflation, so our understanding is when we are going to construct the first phase, if we conclude in terms of construction this year, then it will cost around INR 150 crore.

items.statement: Declared dividend of INR 75 per share (1,500% of face value) from cash reserves of INR 853 crore
items.quote: So, this time, we have given a healthy dividend, declared a healthy dividend payout, which is now INR 75 per share, almost 1,500% of the face value.

items.statement: Project business share stabilized at 39-40%, expected to remain at 40% with retail at 60% going forward
items.quote: With the improvement in retail demand, we expect that this percentage should now remain stable. So, going forward, we expect that the proportion of retail and project should now remain stable at 60% for retail and 40% for the project business.

items.statement: Brass prices increased 29-30% YoY; price increases have largely covered cost impact with 1-2% gap to be managed via discount control
items.quote: Typically, if I see, the price increase has been 30% over the last one year. And if I assume that it constitutes something like 60% of my brass constitutes 60% of my cost. So, the effective impact on my COGS would be in the region of 18%. And I have taken a price increase of 16%.

items.statement: Advances growth guidance for FY27 is 11% to 12%
items.quote: Actually, bank has a tradition of giving some conservative numbers because GDP growth is projected at 6.9%. And we have seen what earlier guidance has been given by us. And accordingly, it has been projected.

items.statement: NIM guidance for FY27 is 2.5% to 2.6%
items.quote: So, we presume that it will hover around 2.5 to 2.6 here.

items.statement: ROA guidance for FY27 is more than 1%
items.quote: That is why we have given it our return on asset more than 1%.

items.statement: PSLC income guidance for FY27 is around Rs 3,000 crore
items.quote: No, no. It is 3,000. It will be around 3,000.

items.statement: Digital transaction volume grew to Rs 1,204 crore in FY26 from Rs 940 crore in FY25
items.quote: For the last year the number was 1,204 crores digital transaction. Prior to that that was 940 crores. So good impressive growth has been seen.

items.statement: Corporate sanctioned but undisbursed pipeline is around Rs 20,000 crore; additional undisbursed corporate is around Rs 20,000 crore
items.quote: So corporate demands are already NBG that is sanctioned by us. So, we have to finalize the proposals. That is lined up at around 20,000 crores. Another undisbursed corporate is around roughly about 20,000 crores.

items.statement: NIM improved 9 bps QoQ in Q4 FY26 and 1 bps for full year FY26
items.quote: In this quarter, our NIM improvement was 9 basis point. So, already we are very, very, because our credit growth is very high at 15.30.

items.statement: Retail term deposit rates raised 30-35 bps in Dec/Jan to attract retail deposits over bulk deposits
items.quote: Why we had raised because our retail term deposit even after raising was much cheaper than the bulk deposit rate and the idea behind to have a more flow in retail term deposit rather than bulk deposit.

items.statement: ECL implementation expected to require Rs 10,000 crore total provision; can be staggered over 4 years; bank can absorb in first year with 1% CRAR impact
items.quote: Total requirement will be 10,000. And it can be staggered to 4 years. And our profit is in the range of 19,000 to 20,000 crores. So, bank is in a very, very good position to absorb the entire in the first go itself.

items.statement: SMA book reduced to Rs 33,728 crore (2.75% of advances) from Rs 40,481 crore in Mar-25; slippage ratio 0.69%
items.quote: In December, in absolute terms, the outstanding was 35,604. This year it is 33,000. In March, this is 33,728. So, although my credit is growing at 15%.

items.statement: Slippages in Q4 FY26 were Rs 2,771 crore: MSME Rs 1,333 cr, Agriculture Rs 886 cr, Retail Rs 431 cr, Corporate Rs 80 cr, Gold loan Rs 41 cr
items.quote: Segmental, I can tell you, 2,771 is the total slippage that has happened in this quarter. Out of which, 1,333 is for MSME. Agriculture is 886. Corporate 80. Gold loan 41. Retail some 431 crores.

items.statement: Capital raise may be considered if needed; board approval pending; decision expected within couple of months
items.quote: If the need be, if need required, we will go for capital raising. And since it has not moved to the board, once board permissions, then I will share it with you. I think within couple of months, we will share that number with you.

items.statement: Target RAM to corporate mix of 60:40; currently at 59:41; retail to grow within RAM
items.quote: We endeavour to reach at 60-40. 59 RAM and 40 corporate.

items.statement: LCR at 118%, well above regulatory minimum of 100%
items.quote: So, LCR was 118%. It is much above the regulatory level of 100%.

items.statement: Proposed dividend of 210% of paid-up capital (Rs 4.20 per share) for FY26
items.quote: We are proposing a dividend of 210 percent of paid up capital and our share face value price is 2. So, the proposed dividend is Rs. 4.20 per share.

items.statement: FY27 performance to improve progressively with new products scaling meaningfully in second half
items.quote: As we look ahead to FY '27, we expect to increasingly benefit from the foundations that have been laid with performance improving progressively as the year unfolds, especially as our new products scale up meaningfully in the second half.

items.statement: Major investment phase substantially complete; no large greenfield capex needed for FY27-28
items.quote: As we stand today, this major investment phase is substantially complete. The emphasis now is on improving utilization, expanding margins and driving steady improvement in return on capital employed.

items.statement: Malaysia drug product Line 2 operational soon; drug substance doubling by end of FY27
items.quote: The DP has happened. The Line 2 has is getting qualified as we are speaking and will get operational soon. DS, the drug substance doubling will happen towards the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Biosimilars EBITDA margin 26% in Q4 FY26, up from operating leverage and mix
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at ₹720 crores, representing growth of 33% on a year-on-year basis. This translates into an EBITDA margin of 26%.

items.statement: Generics EBITDA margin 8% in Q4 FY26, up ~300 bps sequentially from Q3
items.quote: EBITDA margins were at 8% , improved nearly 300 basis points over Q3 of this fiscal, driven by higher volumes and operating leverage.

items.statement: Full annualized interest cost savings from deleveraging visible from FY27
items.quote: Importantly, interest cost savings have begun to accrue, and the full annualized benefit will be visible from FY '27, further supporting profitability and cash generation.

items.statement: Biosimilars revenue grew 12% YoY in Q4 FY26 to ₹2,756 crores; FY26 revenue up 16% YoY
items.quote: Biosimilars revenue for Q4 FY '26 stood at ₹2,756 crores, representing a 12% year-on-year increase, driven primarily by advanced markets.

items.statement: Insulin franchise crossed $300M in FY26; Adalimumab beyond $250M; Pegfilgrastim and Trastuzumab ~$200M each
items.quote: Insulin now has crossed $300 million this year. So that's the bracket that it has crossed and that includes Glargine, Aspart, human insulin, DS and DP. So total insulin franchise is now beyond $300 million.

items.statement: Yesintek (ustekinumab) gaining traction in US with expanding formulary coverage; market share ~20% as of Feb
items.quote: We've seen tremendous success with our biosimilar ustekinumab, which continues to gain market share. And in fact, if you've seen the IQVIA numbers as of February and the overall market is close to a fifth already.

items.statement: Free cash flow first claim to reduce net debt; net debt $1.1-1.2B subject to working capital
items.quote: If you remember in March '25, including structured instruments, we had, in fact, more than $1.5 billion of net debt. That's down to $1.1 billion now. So, it will hover between $1.1 billion to $1.2 billion subject to working capital.

items.statement: Interest cost reduced from ~₹300 cr/qtr to ~₹210-220 cr/qtr; ~₹70-75 cr/qtr savings
items.quote: If you remember, first quarter of FY'26, we had booked INR280 crores in that quarter. It was trending upwards to INR300 crores. And from those levels, now we are down to about INR210 crores, INR220 crores.

items.statement: Biosimilars geographic split roughly 75% advanced markets (40% NA, 35% Europe), 25% emerging
items.quote: If I give you a split, it's been roughly North America at 40%, 35% in Europe and 25% emerging markets. You see sometimes a little bit of a shift between North America and Europe.

items.statement: Generics gross margins in early 40s%; split ~2/3 API, 1/3 formulations; GLP-1 <10% of FY26 revenue
items.quote: The gross margins are in early 40s, and that's two -third API, one-third generics, that's kind of a split today. And as you know, the GLP -1 revenues, which was about less than 10% of the overall business last year in FY '26.

items.statement: Biosimilars R&D at 7% of revenue in Q4 FY26; FDA guidance changes cut development cost 50% and timeline 3-4 years
items.quote: R&D investments for the quarter stood at 7% of revenues, reaffirming our ongoing commitment to innovation and pipeline advancement.

items.statement: Ongoing capex of ~INR1,100 crores to commercialize in H2 FY27, adding 35M meters fabric and 22,000 tons spinning capacity.
items.quote: As regards to the present ongoing capex, the plan is progressing very well. It is expected to commercialize in second half of FY '27.

items.statement: Renewable power capex (75 MW including PPAs) expected operational by H2 FY27; targeting 50-55% of power needs from renewables.
items.quote: The renewable power capex is also progressing as per schedule and expected to be operational in the second half.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 124 bps QoQ to 15.17% on improved realization, efficiency and cost savings.
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 15.17% against previous quarter margin of 13.93% and Q4 '25 margins of 14.30%.

items.statement: Yarn spreads increased from INR110/kg in Q3 to INR120-125/kg currently; fabric prices improving with a lag.
items.quote: The last quarter spreads were about INR110 a kg and now it is about INR125 -- around INR120 to INR125, depending on different counts.

items.statement: Export demand steady at ~100M kg/year; management expects 5-10% incremental international demand from China.
items.quote: We can think about a slight increase, maybe about 5% to 10% going more towards -- because of the increase in demand coming in from China.

items.statement: Domestic and export demand both improved in Q4; FTAs with UK and EU expected to drive strong order inflows and sourcing diversification to India.
items.quote: Already various customers from Europe have started inquiring and planning to diversify their sourcing from India, looking into these FTAs.

items.statement: Revenue expected to grow 30-35% from current levels driven by capex (INR1,000+ cr incremental revenue) and 5-7% price normalization.
items.quote: We expect that we should be -- from here onwards, we should be easily able to add 30% to 35% of our -- to our existing revenue numbers.

items.statement: West Asia conflict increased sea freight 75-80% to Europe and transit time by 2 weeks; most freight passed on via FOB sales.
items.quote: Sea freight cost, there is an increase, especially for the Europe, there is an increase of about 75% to 80% increase in comparison to what was there in the month of February.

items.statement: Industry requesting permanent removal of cotton import duty; government dialogue ongoing but no timeline committed.
items.quote: We have been requesting the Finance Ministry as well as Textile Ministry and Agriculture Ministry to remove the duty for complete forever.

items.statement: Peak total debt expected at INR1,900-2,000 crores post capex; funded via internal accruals and debt at blended cost ~6.5%.
items.quote: Our peak debt -- means our peak debt depends upon our working capital, but our normal total debt, we are expecting to be less than -- in the range of about INR1,900 crores to INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Fabric revenue share 22% (woven ~18%, knitted ~4%); new capex fully integrated for finished fabrics to improve value-added mix.
items.quote: The new expansion is completely integrated. And whatever capacity we are putting on the woven side is also for the finished fabrics.

items.statement: Renewable energy savings expected at INR30-35 crores in FY27 and INR50 crores annually once fully operational.
items.quote: During this year itself, we expect that we will have a saving of around INR30 crores to INR35 crores.

items.statement: Management reaffirmed guidance to double AUM, income and net profit over the next three fiscal years (FY27-FY29).
items.quote: Yes, absolutely. So we last quarter showcased how we are going to do it and this quarter on a full year basis, we have reaffirmed the guidance, so we are sticking with the same guidance for the upcoming three fiscal years.

items.statement: NIM target maintained at 6.5% for FY27 despite achieving 6.83% in FY26.
items.quote: We continue to say that we are going to maintain the same 6.5% sort of a NIM level even in the upcoming financial year as against the 6.83 that we are doing, so our target remains the same and we hope you overachieve the NIM in the upcoming financial year too.

items.statement: Added 427 new touchpoints in Q4 FY26, taking total network to 5,299 across 22 states.
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 427 new touch points, taking our total network to 5,299 touchpoints across 22 states, comprising 422 branches, 3381 distribution points and 1,496 business correspondents.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing moderated to 10.22% in FY26, supporting NIM expansion.
items.quote: At the same time, our cost of borrowing moderated to 10.22%, reflecting continued progress in liability optimization and funding diversification.

items.statement: AUM grew 17% YoY to Rs 61,009 million; disbursements for Q4 FY26 stood at Rs 13,440 million.
items.quote: Our Assets Under Management increased to Rs.61,009 million, registering 17% year-on-year growth, reflecting steady expansion across income generation loan and MSME lending segments. Disbursements for the quarter stood at Rs.13,440 million indicating sustained borrower demand and healthy sourcing momentum.

items.statement: Demand for small-ticket credit remains healthy and broad-based across micro-entrepreneurs and small businesses in Tier-3/4/5 geographies.
items.quote: Demand for small-ticket credit remains healthy and broad-based, supported by working capital needs of micro-entrepreneurs and small businesses, rising economic activity across informal and semi-formal segments and the growing acceptance of formal credit channels even in India's Tier-3, 4, and 5 geographies.

items.statement: No concentrated exposure to exporters affected by Middle East tensions; LCC segment may face some difficulty but Paisalo not impacted.
items.quote: We do not have any large concentrated exposure on any of our borrowers, which are largely dependent on getting proceeds from there. So from that point of view, we are considerably better looking.

items.statement: Completed maiden ECB issuance of USD $15 million; achieved dual AA stable rating.
items.quote: We completed our maiden ECB issuance of USD $15 million, a historic milestone that reflects growing international investor confidence in Paisalo's credit story and opens a new and diversified avenue of long-term funding. We also reinforced our credit standing through dual rating of AA stable.

items.statement: Headcount reduced 3% in FY26 despite AUM growth and branch expansion, indicating productivity gains from AI/tech investments.
items.quote: Despite meaningful expansion in our branch network and strong double-digit AUM growth in FY26, headcount was down 3% during the year, an early but tangible sign that our technology and AI investments are translating into real productivity gains and a more efficient cost structure.

items.statement: Co-lending with SBI: one method expected live in Q1 FY27, second by end of Q1 or early Q2 FY27.
items.quote: One of the methods we are expecting it to get live within this quarter itself while the second process we are awaiting the bank's confirmation on their compliance of the RBI circular. So I am expecting that the second one also should get live in by the end of the quarter one of the new fiscal year or early next quarter

items.statement: Actively scouting for inorganic growth opportunities and partners.
items.quote: Yes, we have that on the plans. We are actively scouting for opportunities and partners to help us in the same.

items.statement: GNPA and NNPA improved to 0.76% and 0.61% respectively in Q4 FY26; collection efficiency at 98.5%.
items.quote: Asset quality remained healthy and stable during the quarter, with GNPA and NNPA improving to 0.76% and 0.61% respectively, underscoring the strength of our underwriting and collection framework.

items.statement: FY27 entered from position of strength with sustained demand, improving funding efficiency, pristine asset quality and robust risk framework.
items.quote: With sustained demand across our core segments, improving funding efficiency, pristine asset quality and a robust risk and operating framework, Paisalo has entered FY27 from a position of strength.

items.statement: Targets maintaining EBITDA margin around 24% for FY27
items.quote: So, we believe that the maintaining of this number, this margin should be achievable.

items.statement: FY26 capex of INR 140 crore used to buy rented properties for printing presses and offices
items.quote: Largely with this money is going into buying out the existing properties, what we have rental.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 66 bps to 28% on like-for-like basis excluding election impact
items.quote: EBITDA margin expansion of 66 bps to a robust 28% in FY 2026.

items.statement: Newsprint cost averaged INR 49,000/ton in Q4 FY26, up from INR 48,000/ton in FY25
items.quote: In quarter 4, this number has become INR49,000 and going forward, we believe this number will further go up maybe by 6% to 8% going forward in the quarter 1 itself.

items.statement: Expects newsprint prices to rise 6-8% in Q1 FY27 based on forward orders
items.quote: In the Q1, we believe this should -- this may -- actually not may, this has already gone up by 7%, 8% because we have the forward order with us.

items.statement: April 2026 ad revenue showed double-digit growth; real estate, jewelry, healthcare grew double-digit in FY26
items.quote: Auto had a single-digit growth. Real estate at a double digit, jewelry at a double digit, healthcare at a double digit.

items.statement: Digital MAUs at 20 million as of March 2026; expanding into Uttar Pradesh market
items.quote: As of March 2026, our news apps recorded around 20 million monthly active users, maintaining Dainik Bhaskar's leadership position as the number one Hindi and Gujarati news app.

items.statement: Circulation copies declined ~2% to 39 lakh in Q4 FY26 due to delivery boy shortages and market shrinkage
items.quote: Quarter 4 copies are almost 39 lakhs.

items.statement: Government ad revenue share stable at ~17-18%; no change in promoter holding plan beyond 75%
items.quote: Same number. One percentage here and there.

items.statement: Radio: 7 new stations launched in FY26, all EBITDA positive within 3 months; total 37 cities
items.quote: My FM expanded its network with 7 new stations entering our presence now to 37 cities across India. I'm happy to share that all new 7 stations have become EBITDA positive within 3 months' time only.

items.statement: No plans for acquisitions or buyback; board evaluating tax-efficient cash deployment
items.quote: Certainly, we'll be looking at thinking that what is the best tax-efficient manner to do with the cash.

items.statement: Dividend policy unchanged; board evaluating tax-efficient cash usage instead of payout
items.quote: There is no change in the policy. I think Board is evaluating more tax-efficient manner to use the cash.

items.statement: Targets 15% growth for rail segment, 5% for CFS, and 15% for Snowman over 3-5 years assuming fewer disruptions
items.quote: we would be trying to target a 15% growth for the rail segment. CFS is probably around 5%. Snowman also, we're targeting about a 15% growth.

items.statement: Snowman INR1,000 crore revenue target deferred to FY29 from earlier FY28 expectation
items.quote: Maybe more realistic is FY '29.

items.statement: Snowman targets 15% EBITDA margin at INR1,000 crore revenue implying INR150 crore EBITDA
items.quote: Our target would be that something like at INR1,000 crores. It's a 15% EBITDA margin on a blended basis, and we have a INR150 crores EBITDA.

items.statement: Jaipur ICD would require INR70 crore over 1-1.5 years if approved; additional INR125 crore for electric reach stackers, EVs, 3 rakes, and new warehouse
items.quote: Jaipur, if it comes in, then that will be another INR70 crores to be spread across 1 year, 1.5 years over there. Other than that, we are also buying electric reach stackers, electric vehicles. Also, we've just placed our first order. We're buying three rakes as well. So, all this will add up to an additional about INR1

items.statement: Snowman FY27 capex guideline around INR50 crore for BTS, one owned warehouse, land, and vehicles
items.quote: Maybe around INR50 crores capex is the guideline for FY '27.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 rail realizations and margins down 4-5% YoY due to volume decline, domestic business mix, empty container costs, train stabling costs, and year-end accounting
items.quote: on a normal basis, suppose this wasn't there, then we would go back to our previous quarter's numbers, but it's very hard to predict right now what will happen.

items.statement: Snowman warehousing pricing positive; passing through cost increases including Haryana wage law changes; determined to hike prices at every contract renewal
items.quote: It's quite positive. I mean the industry is moving and responding to the price increases. We have had a couple of price increases required this year and with Haryana changing the wage laws and all, that has been passed through and the customers have accepted that.

items.statement: Volumes remain subdued due to West Asia conflict impacting US, Europe, Middle East trade routes; April similar to March; no clarity on recovery timeline
items.quote: The trend is continuing right now. So, volumes remain a bit subdued, and there's no clarity also on when things will pick up exactly. So, it's a wait-and-watch kind of situation.

items.statement: Gateway standalone gross debt reduced to INR170 crore; no plan to increase Snowman stake; capex plans and dividends to utilize cash flows
items.quote: we're not looking to increase our stake in Snowman in the near term. So there would be use for it, and we'll continue like dividend, we've said that is also going to be part of it.

items.statement: Expect mid- to high-teens revenue growth in FY27, driven 75% by volume and 25% by mix, with no price increases planned
items.quote: I would say a mid- to high teens is a good growth expectation for next year, of which I expect volume growth to be the maximum driver, right? I would say almost 75% of the revenue will come from volume and maybe about 25% from mix. We have no intention at this point in time to increase prices.

items.statement: Steady-state consolidated gross margin expected around 73% to 74%, barring abnormal reagent price hikes
items.quote: So, I think you can expect the steady-state margins for the business to be around 73% to 74%, barring any abnormal price hike in reagents that may come out as a consequence of the war or the supply chain side.

items.statement: Expect full-year FY27 EBITDA margin to be stable at FY26 levels (reported ~32%, normalized ~34%) as operating leverage is reinvested in growth
items.quote: For the full year, I think we delivered roughly about 32% reported EBITDA and a normalized EBITDA at around 34%. I expect that to be stable into the next year.

items.statement: FY26 total capitalization ~INR35 crores including 7 new labs and genomics; FY27 capex expected in INR40 crores range (maintenance plus expansion)
items.quote: Maintenance capex is roughly about INR40 crores with new expansion and all of that. We expect the capex to be in that range.

items.statement: Franchisee additions running at ~500 per quarter (ex-Q3), targeting ~1,500 annually; mature franchisee revenue scales 1x, 2.5x, 3.5x, 4x, 5x over 5 years
items.quote: I expect about 500 per quarter is -- because we have resourced that way, right? The constraint is not at the demand side. The constraint is our ability to onboard and scale up the franchisees to make them successful.

items.statement: Specialty testing (allergy, genomics, histopathology, etc.) currently ~2% of revenue; target 15-20% of mix in 3 years, in line with competitors
items.quote: Our competitors specialty mix is roughly about 15% to 20%. I anticipate in 3 years reaching that level within Thyrocare as well.

items.statement: Specialty tests to be priced disruptively (e.g., INR1,000 vs routine INR30-40); gross margin % lower but absolute margin per test higher; no routine price hikes planned
items.quote: We always come in with a disruptive pricing. So to that extent, the percentage gross margin in Specialty will be lower. But of course, given our realization per test is only INR30 to INR40, specialty test can be in the INR1,000, right?

items.statement: Insurance segment grew ~45% YoY in FY26; partnership business normalized to 32% YoY growth after one-off Maha Kumbh boost in Q4 FY25 (~INR4 crores)
items.quote: If I look at the year-on-year growth for the insurance business, we started very aggressively last year, but year-on-year, we've grown at almost 45%, right, in the insurance space.

items.statement: Reagent supply chain not routed via Middle East; 2-3 months inventory held; vendors requesting price increases due to dollar, largely mitigated by volume discounts so far
items.quote: Of course, with the dollar being where it is, right, many of our vendors has come back requesting for price increases. But given our volume growth, we have been able to mitigate a large part of that.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated gross margin 74.7% (+113 bps YoY) driven by vendor negotiations and volume discounts; Tanzania not yet breakeven (quarterly loss <INR1 crore)
items.quote: Our consolidated gross margin has improved to 74.7%, an increase of over 113 basis points year -on-year. This was largely driven by better negotiations and a strong growth in test volumes, which has helped improving

items.statement: Genomics launched May 1 starting with NIPT in top 10 North India cities; ~40-person specialty sales team deployed; capex for specialty ~INR5-8 crores, main investment is opex and disruptive pricing
items.quote: See, the capex investments would not be much. They would be in the tune of about INR5 crores to INR8 crores, right? The real investments are on the opex side. We've put a team of, I think, about 40 people on the Specialty side.

items.statement: Allied consumables/diagnostics launch details to be disclosed by June-July; strategy leverages Thyrocare's scale as large consumer to launch own brand
items.quote: I would like to keep it internal to the company for the next 1 or 2 quarters because we are just working on the overall launch plan. So, I think it will become clear to you by June or July of what segments we are entering into, right?

items.statement: Tax rate expected to normalize to 28-29% going forward from ~23-24% in FY26 (deferred tax timing difference)
items.quote: And going forward, we expect our tax rate of 28% to 29%.

items.statement: Processed 210 million tests in FY26 (+23% YoY) and served 19.2 million patients (+15% YoY); Q4 FY26 test volume growth ~29% driven by competitive biochemistry pricing
items.quote: We processed 210 million tests in FY '26, which grew by 23% year-on-year. It's important to contextualize that this volume is higher than some of our biggest competitors combined.

items.statement: Aarogyam ~33% of mix, growing ~20% YoY; Jaanch ~2% of revenue, growing 66% YoY; franchisee base 80% Tier 2+ and 20% urban/metro
items.quote: Aarogyam will be about 33% of our overall mix and year-on-year growth it would have grown at about 19%, 20%. So, that is the wellness mix. Jaanch is also in my opinion, considered wellness. That is only 2% of our revenue today, but grew at 66% year-on-year.

items.statement: New Age business to contribute 20-25% of revenue in 3-5 years, targeting INR1,000 cr portfolio as part of INR10,000 cr roadmap
items.quote: In the next 3 to 5 years, we see this business contributing to around 20% to 25% of the overall revenues.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance of INR60-70 cr for cheese capacity expansion, lactose plant upgrade and other projects
items.quote: we can fairly assume INR60 crores to INR70 crores of capital expenditure

items.statement: Q4 FY26 gross margin expanded to 28% vs 25.9% in Q3 and 26.7% YoY despite 15% milk price inflation
items.quote: we were able to expand our gross margins to 28% in Q4

items.statement: Milk prices at INR42/litre, up 15% YoY and 4% QoQ; company passed on cost via calibrated pricing and mix
items.quote: The commodity witnessed inflation of 15% year-on-year and 4% sequentially during Q4 FY26 with average milk prices at INR42 per litre.

items.statement: Core categories target double-digit volume growth; Ghee strong, Paneer/Cheese impacted by pricing tweaks and export decline
items.quote: Overall, we are looking at a double -digit volume growth for core categories. That's what we aspire to.

items.statement: New Age business (Avvatar, Pride of Cows) grew 91% YoY, now 10% of revenue; crossed INR100 cr quarterly for 2 consecutive quarters
items.quote: Our new age business has emerged as a strong growth engine, crossing INR100 crores in quarterly revenue for the second consecutive quarter, and growing over 100% year -on-year in Q4.

items.statement: Milk prices expected stable for 3-4 months; any energy price spike or El Nino could increase feed/logistics costs
items.quote: What I think the prices should be stable for next 2, 3 months until something big happens in energy prices

items.statement: Cheese capacity expansion from 60 to 80 MT via adjacency capex; plan to reach 120 MT without greenfield
items.quote: the overall plan is that we increase our capacity of cheese from 60 metric tons to 80 metric tons and then we take it ahead

items.statement: New Age business EBITDA margins nearly double company average; blended EBITDA target double-digit in coming years
items.quote: we are fairly confident that we will inch up to double-digit margins

items.statement: Dubai subsidiary incorporated, bank account opened; first ODI investment on hold due to geopolitical uncertainty
items.quote: we have got even the bank account opened in quarter 4. But having said that, the first ODI has not gone into it.

items.statement: Employee cost elevated due to ESOP (INR5 cr), director remuneration hike (INR9 cr), and talent strengthening; sustainable run-rate ~INR45-46 cr/quarter
items.quote: roughly you can eliminate almost what I gave you the numbers around INR7.5 crores, INR8 crores as exceptional items. Balance will be the regular number.

items.statement: Inventory at INR730 cr, up INR150 cr purely from rate variance (milk inflation); quantitative variance near zero, no channel buildup
items.quote: the inventory has increased by almost INR150-odd crores and purely on account of rate variance at the overall level

items.statement: Distribution expansion adding ~30,000 GT outlets/quarter; focus on North/South India where underpenetrated; organized shift from unbranded aiding share gains
items.quote: we are adding every quarter about 30,000 outlets as per GT is concerned in terms of all across India

items.statement: Volume growth expected to exceed 10% in FY27 if current enablers persist
items.quote: if I have clocked 8.25 overall volume growth this year, it should be certainly more than that. We should be able to cross double digit if this remains for a longer time, and we are able to see.

items.statement: Endeavor to maintain EBITDA above INR8 per SCM in FY27
items.quote: maybe our wish and endeavor could be we will maintain more than INR8 EBITDA per SCM, but we'll have to consider multiple factors before we decide to do any price changes.

items.statement: Capex guidance around INR1,200 crores for FY27, potentially slightly higher
items.quote: Certainly, it will be whatever we have been giving, INR1,200 crores range. It can be a little more than that if we are able to do and see

items.statement: Near-term CNG margins lower as cost increase not fully passed through
items.quote: Specifically in case of CNG, complete pass-through could not be done.

items.statement: CNG price increased by INR1 on 22nd April 2026; further hikes possible if high costs persist
items.quote: we have already taken a price increase on 22nd of April, INR1, okay. And let us see how the alternate fuel prices move , specifically for CNG since you asked. We will take the call.

items.statement: DPNG price hike of INR1 on 22nd April 2026 covers APM cost increase from Kirit Parikh circular and exchange rate impact
items.quote: So $0.25 plus there is an upside in the cost due to exchange rate. So considering both these, we have taken a hike of INR1* on 22nd April 2026 . Before that also, there was some hike, but a little earlier than this.

items.statement: DPNG demand accelerating due to LPG supply issues and government mandate to switch within 3 months
items.quote: wherever there is a gas connection available if somebody is using LPG, that will not be allowed beyond 3 months, and he has to mandatorily opt for PNG. So, in our view, that will help us grow our domestic customers also high compared to what we have done in the past

items.statement: Commercial PNG registrations surging from hundreds to thousands due to LPG shortage
items.quote: On the commercial side, there is a good potential for increase because the situation of LPG is not very good. So a lot of demand is there for pipe gas even at a premium. So we are getting a lot of registrations. I mean previously, the registrations would number in 100s. Now they're coming in 1000s.

items.statement: Industrial & commercial volume split in Q4: ~0.57 mmscmd industrial, ~0.15 mmscmd commercial (curtailed at 80%)
items.quote: I think Mr. Wagle already said 0.57 was industry. And if my total was 0.719, balance is commercial. So, this is for this quarter.

items.statement: LNG supply disruptions from West Asia crisis curtailing industrial/commercial supply to ~80%; Henry Hub supply cut to 50% in March
items.quote: Our LNG supplies are disrupted due to West Asia crisis and hence supply to industrial and commercial customers is curtailed to approximately 80% as per tariff time to time, impacting the volumes adversely.

items.statement: Pooled gas pricing opaque; spot LNG ranging $11.5-$14 per mmBtu sourced via IGX/aggregators
items.quote: As far as pricing, I think it is available in the public domain. It is ranging between $11.5 to $13, sometimes $14. And that keeps on changing depending on the volumes available, depending on the time at which we are trying to approach the market.

items.statement: Final dividend of INR18 per share (180%) approved; total FY26 dividend INR30 per share including interim
items.quote: I'm happy to announce that Board has approved a final dividend subject to the approval of shareholders at the AGM at the rate of 180%, that is INR18 per equity share for the current financial year. Thus, including interim dividend already paid at the rate of INR12, total dividend is INR30 per share for the financial year 2025-'26.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA INR1,451 crores vs INR1,570 crores prior year; PAT INR847 crores vs INR1,041 crores
items.quote: EBITDA from operations for the financial year 2025 -'26 is INR1,451 crores compared to previous financial year EBITDA of INR1,570 crores. Net profit after tax for FY 2025 -'26 is INR847 crores compared to net profit after tax for the previous financial year of INR1,041 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 overall volume 4.672 mmscmd (+1.12% QoQ, +6.15% YoY); CNG 3.349, DPNG 0.605, I&C 0.719 mmscmd
items.quote: During the quarter, we achieved overall average sales volume of 4.672 mmscmd as against 4.620 mmscmd in the previous quarter, which is an increase of 1.12%. Current quarter volumes consist of CNG volume of 3.349 mmscmd, DPNG volume of 0.605 mmscmd and 0.719 mmscmd of gas was supplied to the industrial and commercial customers.

items.statement: March industrial volume loss ~1.25-1.3 lakh scmd (~20-22%) vs February average of 5.75 lakh scmd
items.quote: Overall, in the month of March, we lost about 1.25 lakh, 1.3 lakh scmd out of, let's say, Feb average of 5.75. About 20%, 22% volume we lost.

items.statement: Target AUM of INR500-550 crores for FY27, aiming for INR3,000 crores by FY30
items.quote: So this year if we are project projecting to projections about let's to reach about INR500 crores of an AUM or INR550 crores when we double the numbers from here

items.statement: Plan to double branch network to 50 branches by FY27 end or mid-CY27
items.quote: Have a branch spread of about close to 50 branches by the year-end financial year end next year and mid of calendar year next year

items.statement: Investing in technology, AI-driven underwriting, digital wallet RedPay launch in 12 months, and PPI license NOC received
items.quote: Over the next 12 months, we plan to launch a digital wallet, named RedPay, which will enable smoother disbursement, repayments, and customer transactions within our ecosystem

items.statement: Strong borrowing pipeline of INR400-450 crores from lenders for current financial year
items.quote: We see a strong pipeline for this year where we are raising money through lenders about close to INR400 to INR450 crores

items.statement: Current NIM ~10.75-11%, target to maintain at current levels with secured mix shift and cost of funds reduction
items.quote: Our NIM today stands at 10.75% around close to 11% right now, net interest margin. If we maintain our 75% to 80% book in my secured lending and my average cost keep borrowing goes down, I keep maintaining my NIM at the level that we are today

items.statement: Current cost of funds 13-14%, target to reduce to 11-12% in FY27, further to 10.25-10.5% over 2-3 years
items.quote: Our current cost of fund is right now about close to 13% to 14%, right? We want to take down so between 11% to 12%

items.statement: Shift to 80% secured MSME lending, 15-20% digital lending, JLG book to be fully run down by end of next calendar year
items.quote: 80% of my lending will be in MSME secured percent. Between 15% to 20% will be my digital lending

items.statement: Strong MSME credit demand in North India tier-2 cities, finance minister budgeted INR5 lakh crores for MSME lending
items.quote: This year also our finance minister has budgeted about INR5 lakh crores towards MSME lending, right? So that means there is immense value that a medium borrower still is alive

items.statement: Net NPA 0.74% in FY26 vs 0.31% in FY25, increase attributed to JLG book and regional issues; secured book 90+ DPD only INR65-70 lakhs
items.quote: Our net NPA stood at 0.74% in FY2026, compared to 0.31% FY2025, far better than what the market is performing on the asset contributors

items.statement: Raised INR25 crores equity via CCD last month; targeting public sector bank onboarding for cheaper funds
items.quote: Last month we raised approximately INR25 crores of equity through CCD, Compulsorily Convertible Debentures

items.statement: Collection efficiency 95-96% (0-month), 97-98% (0+ month); in-house legal team, branch-level collection responsibility
items.quote: From a collection efficiency point of view, we are around today 95% to 96% of collection efficiency if a zero month is considered. If a zero plus month is considered, I am at 97%, 98%

items.statement: Advances growth target of around 25% for FY27
items.quote: For FY27, we plan to accelerate both branch and digital infrastructure, in line with the asset growth objective of around 25%.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 1.4% to 1.5% of average gross loan book for FY27
items.quote: Guidance FY27. Grow the advances by around 25%, expect credit cost to moderate to 1.4% to 1.5% of the average GLB, and reach ROA of around 1.6%.

items.statement: NIM guidance for FY27 at around 8.5%, similar to Q4 FY26 exit level
items.quote: I would fina lly like to give the guidance of NIM around 8.5%.

items.statement: Opex to ATA ratio expected to be 20-30 bps above FY26 due to investments
items.value: 20 to 30 basis points above financial year '26
items.quote: The opex to ATA ratio would be 20 to 30 basis points above financial year '26 due to the investments that we are making for the future growth.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio to remain at FY26 levels despite investments
items.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio, despite the investments that we are going to do will continue to remain at the same percentages as we had in the preceding financial year, which is for FY'24 (Correction: removal of word) FY'25/'26.

items.statement: Investments in digital, AI, analytics, cloud-led platform, and branch infrastructure
items.quote: Our digital, AI, and analytics investments will continue to better align with our existing and new customer needs, strengthening our data foundation through a cloud -led platform.

items.statement: Secured portfolio mix target of a little upwards of 56% by end of FY27
items.quote: For this year, I can only guide that our secured portfolio would be a little upwards of 56%.

items.statement: Expect cost of funds benefit of around 30 bps from deposit repricing
items.quote: Benefit of around 30 basis points.

items.statement: No plan to change retail TD or bulk TD rates; will watch competition
items.quote: We have no plan as of now to reprice our retail TD or bulk TD. We will wait and watch this space, and we'll be competitive in the market.

items.statement: SA cost of funds expected to reduce by 25-30 bps from April rate cuts on 10L-10Cr bucket
items.quote: So around 25 to 30 bps reduction will happen as we go along from here.

items.statement: No plan to change MFI lending rates at this point
items.quote: In the MFI book, we are also not thinking of changing interest rates at this point in time. We want to hold on to what we are charging at this point in time.

items.statement: Micro banking disbursement growth guided at less than 10% (higher single digit) for FY27
items.quote: So as far as the micro banking business is concerned, we would be growing it at less than 10%, I would say, a higher single -digit number.

items.statement: Secured book growth planned at around 40% for FY27
items.quote: Yes, 40% is something that we have already planned. So 10% on unsecured, 40% on secured and therefore, 25% average.

items.statement: Board approved equity capital raise up to INR 2,000 crores in H2 FY27
items.quote: Our plan is to do it in the second half of the current financial year, depending on the suitability of the circumstances.

name: Aptus Value Housing Finance India Ltd

items.statement: No specific SSG guidance for FY27; focus on improving footfalls, conversion, ASPs, and basket size
items.quote: So while I can't give you a particular guidance on what SSG do we aim to achieve for the next financial year, what I can tell you is that anything and everything which we should be doing as a company to achieve better SSG numbers is something which we are targeting.

items.statement: Gross store additions of ~1 lakh sq ft in FY26; net addition ~4,200 sq ft after rationalization
items.quote: So we added about 1 lakh -odd square feet at a gross level in the last financial year.

items.statement: Twamev EBO pipeline active; 8 stores currently, targeting 5-6 more signings; openings lag 18-20 months due to build-to-suit
items.quote: So I hope that we will actually end the financial year with a lot of signed Twamev EBOs, but openings might be staggered over the next financial year and maybe a few in first 2 quarters of financial year '28 or '29 as well.

items.statement: Gross margin ~65.7% FY26, ~65% Q4; 150 bps contraction attributed to GST rate change from Sep'25
items.quote: So the gap which we are seeing, Sameer, it is majorly on account of GST only, which has impacted our revenue and gross margin as well.

items.statement: Fabric cost impact ~50-150 bps on COGS (INR 1-1.5 per INR 100 MRP); expect to absorb over time via new collections, no price hikes on existing SKUs
items.quote: So in our case, we do anticipate about 50 to 150 basis point increase in the total sort of this number, which is, let's say, on a INR 100 product, we can see an impact of INR 1 to INR 1.5 on the cost.

items.statement: March FY26 very strong; April decent; May impacted by Adhik Maas; June expected strong with July weddings; consumer sentiment turned neutral after war in late Feb
items.quote: Overall, April has also been decent as a follow-up to March. But what is interesting now to see is how would May work for us, given that there is Adhik Maas, but June should again then be exciting, given weddings in July.

items.statement: ASP upgrade target 3-3.5% per category via collection upgrades (e.g., kurtas from INR 4,000 to 4,500); cross-sell Manyavar to Mohey/Twamev; new stores carry more Mohey
items.quote: So we will not be taking any price h ikes in existing products, but the goal would be to upgrade our collection. So for example, if Manyavar's core kurtas -- the best kurtas exist today at INR4,000, some of the new collection that we make will be in the INR4,500 bracket, to give you an example

items.statement: High rentals in new markets (1.3-1.4x expected) delaying store signings; competition consolidating but new entrants still adding stores; war impacting consumer sentiment
items.quote: So that is the kind of fight we're having across the country where we want to get stores at very good rental levels, and it's being very difficult to find those stores.

items.statement: Retail sales INR 2,008 cr FY26 (+6.1%), SSG 2.7%; Q4 retail sales INR 561 cr (+7.8%), SSG 4.6%; revenue INR 1,436 cr (+3.5%), EBITDA 44.3%, PAT 26.2%; cash conversion ~98%
items.quote: FY26 marked an important milestone for the Company as retail sales of our customers crossed the INR 2,000 crores mark, reaching INR 2,008 crores and reflecting a growth of 6.1% over FY25.

items.statement: 5-6% retail area underperforming (vs normal 2-3% closure rate); new stores 85% higher revenue/sq ft vs closed stores; net openings positive in FY27 but focus remains SSG
items.quote: Right now, we would have about 5% to 6% retail area that falls in that category, which we don't love.

items.statement: Dividend policy historically ~50% of profits; reviewing capital allocation, decision expected by next earnings call
items.quote: Up until now, what we've been doing in the history of the Company after IPO is that we've been doing about 50% profits as dividends.

items.statement: AI deployment across functions (marketing, supply chain, product); agentic AI analyzing 20,000 Google keywords autonomously; early results promising
items.quote: But now we've created an AI system that is analysing all 20,000 keywords and making changes on its own. So those efficiencies, which would never exist are now possible, and we are literally working on training every member of our team to understand AI and start deploying agents across the Company.

items.statement: Consumer retention project targeting 90 lakh existing customers; first focused effort on repeat purchases
items.quote: As a Company, we had never focused on working on the existing consumers. So right now, we have almost 90 lakh consumers with their data in the Company. So one big goal that we have for the year is how can we call back a lot of these consumers again this financial year.

items.statement: Manyavar kurta pilot stores (1,000 sq ft) planned in high-throughput Bangalore neighborhoods; no Diwas physical stores planned; quick commerce not feasible as platforms want own warehouses
items.quote: So this is something which we are actively working on where there are a lot of opportunities in, let's say, high-throughput neighbourhoods of Bangalore, where we want to open a 1,000 square feet Manyavar store, but we want to do it in a slightly differentiated manner where we primarily keep kurtas and jackets as categories.

items.statement: FY27 volume expected to cross 250 MMSCM with double-digit growth, up from 223.67 MMSCM in FY26
