items.statement: Boeing T-7 program: INR75 cr executed in FY26, INR70 cr remaining for FY27
items.quote: we did approximately INR75 crores this year on that program and we're left with another INR70 crores for this financial year

items.statement: Semiconductor & space revenue targeting 300-400% YoY growth in FY27
items.quote: for both the space and the semiconductor this year we're looking at a significant growth. We're looking at close to a 300% to 400% growth on our revenue from the previous year

items.statement: Commercial aerospace RFPs expected by Q2 FY27; orders larger scale than defense/space
items.quote: we're hoping that we shall get some RFPs by the second quarter of this financial year. So we should be getting some RFPs and requirements and opportunities by the second quarter

items.statement: Leased additional 210,000 sq ft facility near existing ops for space & semiconductor migration
items.quote: we have taken a strategic decision to lease an additional facility of approximately 210,000 square feet in close proximity to our existing operations instead of constructing a new facility

items.statement: Inventory coverage improved from 10 to 7.67 months; target 4 months to reduce working capital pressure
items.quote: Inventory coverage improved significantly from 10 months historically to 7.67 months, demonstrating enhanced capital efficiency. As our s cale increases and demand planning continues to strengthen, we firmly believe and confirm that inventory coverage will reduce further in the coming years

items.statement: Employee cost ~15% of revenue in FY26; expecting improvement in FY27
items.quote: Around 15% of our revenue goes into employee cost. You've seen that in our P&L. We're looking at an improvisation in this year as we scale up too

items.statement: FY27 new launches pipeline of 5 million sq ft with GDV of INR 7,800 crores
items.quote: For FY ’27, we have an exciting pipeline of new launches of 5 million square feet, amounting to a total GD V of INR 7,800 crores

items.statement: FY27 delivery target of roughly 5.5 million sq ft
items.quote: We have a target of delivering roughly 5.5 million square feet in FY '27.

items.statement: FY27 launch sales target of 20%-25% at launch, expecting INR 1,800-2,000 crores from new launches
items.quote: We plan to achieve, as we do in all our launches, approximately 20%,-25% sales at launch and that is the target we have for this year also.

items.statement: Net debt not to exceed March 2026 level of INR 8,100 crores; debt-to-equity ratio to be lower than 2x in FY27
items.quote: But at the same time, it will be ensured that the net debt level surely doe s not go beyond what it is today as of March’26. For March’27, it does not go up. However, we would attempt to reduce it marginally at the absolute level, but not substantially. So, our debt-to-equity ratio for FY’27, we will be, of course, issuing a proper guidance a little later, but it will be lower than 2x for sure

items.statement: Refinanced INR 3,500 crores debt since listing, achieving 120 bps reduction in blended cost of debt and INR 125 crores annualized savings
items.quote: Since our listing, we have leveraged our strength and strengthened our market position to refinance approximately INR 3,500 crores of debt. These results are tangible. We have achieved an interest rate delta of 3.5% of these facilities, leading to a 120 basis points drop in our overall blended cost of debt, total debt. This optimization alone adds approximately around INR 125 crores to our annuali

items.statement: Plan to refinance another INR 1,300 crores in coming quarter
items.quote: Looking ahead, we have an active pipeline for further optimization. We expect to refinance another around INR 1,300 crores in the coming quarter.

items.statement: Total future inflows across portfolio approximately INR 57,000 crores including INR 27,000 crores from ongoing projects and INR 30,000 crores from ready-to-move-in and forthcoming launches
items.quote: In addition, our ready-to-move-in projects and forthcoming launches together add approximately INR 30,000 crores, so total future inflows across the portfolio is about INR 57,000 crores.

items.statement: FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin 30%, Q4 margin 36%; new project margins 20-25% at revenue level, 25-30% cash flow level
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA for Q4 reached INR 612 crores, with margin expanding to a very healthy 36% for the full year. Adjusted EBITDA stood at INR 1,022 crores, reflecting a 30% margin.

items.statement: Robust walk-ins and conversions in April 2026; Worli project sold INR 400 crores in Q4 FY26; no drastic change in footfalls despite geopolitical concerns
items.quote: Till now, our walk-ins have been robust in April also. As the lifecycle of our projects are at maturity and mid-level, we are seeing a good robust walk-ins yet and conversion, we do not see an issue till now.

items.statement: Construction cost escalation 2-4% but manageable given sales value; geopolitical situation being monitored
items.quote: The construction costs have increased, but it is 2% to 4% of the construction cost and it should not have an impact on us looking at the total value of sales. The geopolitical crisis and the little Indian narrative also, we have to wait and watch how it is.

items.statement: FY26 pre-sales INR 5,280 crores (up 17%), collections INR 4,960 crores (up 34%); 4-year pre-sales CAGR 26%, collections CAGR 33%
items.quote: FY26 pre - sales reached INR 5,280 crores, up 17%, while collections grew by 34% to INR 4,960 crores. The consistency of our p erformance is best reflected in our multi -year trends. Our four -year pre- sales compounded annual growth rate stands at 26%, while our collections compounded annual growth rate of 33% continue to outpace sales

items.statement: FY26 OCF INR 1,500 crores (100% level) and INR 1,002 crores (pro-rata); construction spend INR 1,916 crores (100%) and INR 1,512 crores (pro-rata)
items.quote: OCF generated for the full year was Rs.1,500 crores. Adhidev Chattopadhyay: Okay. Chandrashekhar Joglekar: At the 100% share level. And at the proportionate level, it was INR 1,000 crores. INR 1,002 precisely

items.statement: Unsold inventory in ongoing projects INR 22,000 crores; expected to reach INR 30,000 crores with new launches and liquidate over 4-6 years
items.quote: So, the inventory of ongoing projects which we need to sell is out of the balance value, unsold inventory, which is of bas ically INR 22,000

items.statement: New business development: Shri Mahalakshmi Cooperative Housing Society redevelopment in Andheri West, 0.4 million sq ft carpet area, GDV ~INR 1,400 crores
items.quote: I am pleased to share that we have secured a development agreement for the redevelopment of Shri Mahalakshmi Cooperative Housing Society. This project is situated on a prime 3 acre land parcel just off Veera Desai Road in Andheri West, one of Mumbai's most sought-after residential and commercial hubs. With the potential carpet area of approximately 0.4 million square feet, we estimate the gross de

items.statement: Cash balance INR 1,062 crores as of March 2026; not more than 20% locked in RERA accounts
items.quote: Today our cash balance as of March'26 has been around INR 1062 crores. Out of which not more than 20% is locked into the RERA account. Rest of the cash is available for the projects freely.

items.statement: FY26 revenue INR 3,436 crores (up 54% YoY); Q4 revenue INR 1,694 crores (nearly 3x YoY); FY26 PAT INR 80 crores, Q4 PAT INR 194 crores
items.quote: We reported revenue from operations of INR 1,694 crores, a nearly three-fold increase from the INR 601 crore reported in the same period last year. This propelled our full-year revenue to INR 3,436 crores, representing a 54% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Expects steady-state EBITDA margins of 15-16% going forward
items.quote: So going forward, if you say, we expect our EBITDA to be similar to around 15% to 16%.

items.statement: Committed INR39.53 crore via purchase orders for greenfield expansion as of March 2026
items.quote: As of the end of this March, we have already committed INR39.53 crores via purchase orders of our greenfield expansion project.

items.statement: Total capex for new 35,000 MT facility is INR76 crore excluding land
items.quote: So the total capex for the new capacity is about INR76 crores and this is without the land.

items.statement: Trial production at new Vizianagaram plant expected Nov-Dec FY27, commercial production from Q4 FY27
items.quote: So, we look at commencing with trial productions in November or December of FY27 and commercial production from Q4 of FY27.

items.statement: Targets 15% capacity utilization at new plant in FY27, 65-70% in FY28, 85-90% thereafter
items.quote: So I think we should look at somewhere around 15% of capacity utilization in FY27. Then in FY28, we are looking at 65% to 70% of capacity utilization and then reaching at 85%-90% utilization rate by the next fiscal.

items.statement: New plant peak revenue potential INR475 crore at 85% utilization; existing plant expects 20-22% revenue growth
items.quote: So, our peak would be about INR475 crores at a 85% utilization rate.

items.statement: 78% revenue from repeat institutional customers; unable to onboard new customers due to capacity constraints
items.quote: However, I would like to share that our revenue is -- repeat revenue is coming nearly 78% from our existing customers, which highlights that there is a very high demand for our product in the market and we are not able to cater to new customers.

items.statement: H2 FY26 margin compression due to RCN price spike, forex (~10.5% depreciation), and shipping disruptions
items.quote: While H2 saw some margins compression due to a spike in raw cashew nuts prices, forex, and global shipping disruptions, we maintained a double-digit EBITDA margin for the full year.

items.statement: Initiating currency hedging and longer-term shipping contracts to mitigate forex and freight cost risks
items.quote: We are already talking to the banks for the hedging mechanism so that we can hedge some currency risk. And then we are already talking to the shipping lines to do some longer-term contracts so that we can also hedge some of our shipping cost.

items.statement: Whole kernel recovery improved to 70:30 (wholes:pieces) after technology upgrade in Nov 2023
items.quote: Yes, so our wholes recovery as compared to pieces recovery is now at about 70:30. 70 being wholes and 30 being pieces.

items.statement: No firm orders for new capacity yet; institutional customers give only 1-3 month visibility
items.quote: So, actually we don't have any existing orders because these institutional customers, they give you visibility only for -- the visibility ranges from one month to sometimes three months, so we are still away from that period.

items.statement: Royal Mewa brand grew 6.5x in FY26; marketing focus on digital/social media without compromising margins
items.quote: Furthermore, our brand Royal Mewa is no longer just a pilot project. It grew over 6.5 times this year.

items.statement: IPO raised INR74.45 crore; INR57 crore allocated to new facility, INR10.42 crore to general corporate purposes
items.quote: Our successful IPO through which we raised INR74.45 crores is being primarily utilized towards setting up of our second processing facility in Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh.

items.statement: Expect historical revenue growth rates to continue in the next year; no specific revenue guidance given
items.quote: We do not have specific revenue guidance at this point in time, but we expect that our historical revenue growth rates are a good indication of where we should be growing in the next year as well.

items.statement: Target 60% of revenue from output, outcome, or license-based contracts in 2-3 years, up from ~40% today
items.quote: We expect to get to 60% of our revenue to be output, outcome, or license based in the next two to three years. That is the trajectory. Today, it is about 20 points lower than that.

items.statement: Aim to grow license-driven revenue from 3% to 20% of total revenue by 2030
items.quote: We want to take that license driven revenue from 3% to 20% by 2030, and which will be quite significant in terms of also margin expansion.

items.statement: Q4 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin reached 22.1%, up 189 bps year-over-year
items.quote: In Q4 2026, gross margin expansion along with 140 bps of reduction in SG&A contributed to adjusted EBITDA expansion of 189 bps year-over-year to 22.1%.

items.statement: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin was 17.6% after expensing 4.1% of revenue on R&D
items.quote: For the FY2026 adjusted EBITDA was 17.6% versus 17.4% in the previous year. While our gross margin expanded by 93 bps, growth investments in relationship management for key clients and opening new offices led to 96 bps uptick in SG&A as a percentage of revenue versus the previous year.

items.statement: Output/outcome-based pricing carries 5-7 percentage points higher gross margin than input-based; license-driven gross margin is 25-30 points higher
items.quote: There is a 5- to 7-point difference between input-driven pricing versus output-driven, outcome-driven pricing. 5- to 7-point of additional gross margin are there in output and outcome compared to input and there is a 25-to-30-point difference between that and the license-driven gross margin.

items.statement: Expect to shift engagements toward outcome, output, and license-driven models for higher margins
items.quote: We have seen that anything that is priced as linked to outputs, outcomes, or as license has a much stronger margin profile and also sustainable. And so we expect to move our engagements into more outcome driven, more output driven, and more license-driven.

items.statement: Enterprise AI takeoff expected this year and next few years; growth rate should be robust but tempered by macro uncertainties
items.period: this year and the next few years
items.quote: We expect, enterprise AI to take off substantially in this year and the next few years. There is always some friction between what is possible versus what the enterprises are willing to implement right now.

items.statement: TMT vertical client-specific issues expected to work out; better performance expected in next few quarters
items.quote: We expect these client-specific growth issues to have worked themselves out through this year, and therefore, we expect to do better in the TMT vertical in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Qure.ai has a phenomenal order pipeline and strong order book as of April 2026; expected to recover and do better than last year
items.quote: And today, as of April 2026, Qure is sitting on a phenomenal order pipeline and a very, very strong order book. They are not just going to recover from all the setbacks from the last year, but do even better than that.

items.statement: Fractal Alpha (Asper and Analytics Vidhya) grew 41% in FY2026; segment losses narrowed from INR 26 crore to INR 15 crore
items.quote: Fractal Alpha revenues grew by 41% year-over-year. Asper grew by 31% and Analytics Vidhya by 49%. Gross margin for Fractal Alpha expanded by 143 bps year-over-year. Our losses in the segment for the same period ha ve come down by 43% while investments in sales and R&D have continued

items.statement: Cogentiq platform chosen by a Mag7 company after three-month evaluation for marketing transformation
items.quote: For example, one of the largest Mag7 technology company did a full evaluation, three-month evaluation, of all the agentic platforms out there and decided to choose Cogentiq and work with it in their overall marketing transformation.

items.statement: R&D investment increased 48% to INR 212 crore in FY2026; INR 134 crore (4.1% of revenue) expensed in P&L
items.quote: In FY2026, we spent INR 212 crore on R&D investments, 48% higher than the previous year. Out of this INR 212 crore, INR 134 crore, or 4.1% of the revenue, was expensed in the P&L.

items.statement: Macro uncertainties (trade, geopolitical) temper extreme enterprise AI excitement; net result is balanced outlook
items.quote: It is very interesting that there is a tremendous, tremendous need to get enterprise AI right inside companies. We have never seen this level of excitement and need for this, and it is yet tempered with all the other geopolitical situations that are happening.

items.statement: Repaid long-term debt in April 2026 using IPO proceeds; company is now debt-free
items.quote: In April, we used these proceeds to repay our long-term debt as we had committed at the time of the offering. Fractal is now debt free.

items.statement: Expects 25-30% same-store sales growth (SSG) for FY27, driven by existing SIS stores and new EBOs.
items.quote: I am expecting 25% to 30%, but if gold prices shoot up just like last year, it again can match with the previous year's SSG growth.

items.statement: Expects top-line revenue growth of 25-30% for FY27, primarily driven by SIS SSG and new store additions.
items.quote: I expect top-line growth also to get maintained around 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Plans to open 15 new EBOs over 24 months using IPO proceeds; 1 store already opened, 6-7 in FY27, remaining in FY28.
items.quote: Out of these 14, 6 to 7 will take place in current financial year and remaining will be in next financial year. Because we have mentioned in DRHP, RHP prospectus that this is a project for 24 months' period.

items.statement: EBO capex estimated at INR20-25 crores per store; INR287 crores from IPO proceeds earmarked for store expansion and working capital.
items.quote: When it's a EBO which we are setting, it requires around INR20 crores to INR25 crores per EBO. So that expansion will have better numbers at lower capex.

items.statement: No order book disclosed; business is B2C retail with no order backlog.
items.quote: We are doing exclusively diamond jewellery only. We have got no mix of the plain gold jewellery or anything.

items.statement: Sees structural demand tailwinds: rising incomes, urbanization, shift to organized/branded jewellery, and growing diamond acceptance across occasions.
items.quote: Backed by these favourable tailwinds along with our differential business model, strong parentage, and scalable retail strategy, we believe PNGS Reva is well-positioned to capitalize on this opportunity and deliver sustainable long-term growth.

items.statement: Product mix: 60-70% lower ticket (entry/everyday), 20-25% medium, 10-12% high-ticket bridal/occasion wear. Average bill size INR1.2 lakhs in FY26 (up 41% YoY).
items.quote: As far as current year ending for which we are referring the results, that is FY26, the average bill size value or average order value is INR1,20,000. Y-o-Y growth is 41%.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamonds not seen as long-term threat due to lack of resale value; natural diamonds viewed as wealth/inheritance assets.
items.quote: So with our buyback policy, natural diamond has got rarity and increasing value over a period, so I am not thinking that is a threat for me.

items.statement: No equity dilution expected for next 2-3 years; growth funded via internal accruals (INR64 cr added this year) and existing debt headroom (INR150-200 cr unused sanctions).
items.quote: I don't primarily expect any dilution of the equity, but after getting settled by 2030, I will be expanding out of the borrowings in future.

items.statement: Inventory turnover at 1.31x in FY26; expected to stabilize at 1.25-1.35x despite new EBO additions due to SIS SSG offset.
items.quote: Hardly, this means this is 1.31, if that were the case, it would fall between 1.25 and 1.35.

items.statement: Marketing spend ~3-4% of top-line annually; INR2 cr per new EBO spread over 12-18 months for BTL/ATL/social media.
items.quote: And brand as such we will be spending around 3% to 4% every year on the top-line.

items.statement: Gold price increases may compress gross margin % but absolute margin rupees maintained; no hedging due to high MCX cost, relies on natural hedging (same-day cover) and surplus gold recycling.
items.quote: Gross margin percentage basis it may contract, but in absolute value, it will get maintained. And as a person, I more believe in the absolute value rather than percentage.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 is 18.5% to 20% with sequential quarter-on-quarter improvement, key improvement in H2, excluding Lanreotide contribution
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY '27, supported by our ramp-up of new launches and investments that we've made across our manufacturing facilities and ongoing expense optimization initiatives. We expect the EBITDA margins to be in the range of 18.5% to 20% and this would be actually achieved with a sequential improvement quarter-on-quarter with the key improvement being in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Targeting $1 billion exit run rate in North America by end of FY27, not full-year revenue, driven by respiratory and peptide launches
items.quote: In North America, we will concentrate on enhancing our commercial execution and accelerating new product introductions. And our aim is to cross $1 billion mark as a run rate towards the end of this financial year, i.e., FY '27.

items.statement: Confident of delivering strong double-digit and market-beating growth in India for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: Yes. So we are confident that we'll be able to deliver a strong double-digit growth as well as a market beating growth in FY '27, '28.

items.statement: Capex cycle increased steadily over last 3 years, will probably reduce after another year as capacity built for planned products, then focus shifts to productivity
items.quote: Then we have capex, which we have increased steadily over the last 3 years. So this cycle will probably reduce after another year or so because we've built enough capacity for the products that we want to supply.

items.statement: India chronic mix at 60% per IQVIA MAT March '26; Foracort surpassed INR 1,000 crores revenue; Dytor at INR 650 crores with 25% YoY growth; 33 brands >INR 100 crores, 23 in top 300
items.quote: Our chronic mix stands at 60% as per IQVIA MAT March '26. Foracort, our leading inhalation brand surpassed the revenue of INR1,000 crores, reaffirming its position as a respiratory market leader. Meanwhile, Dytor, our cardiac brand, has established itself as a -- as a INR 650 crores brand, delivering 25% Y -o-Y growth.

items.statement: U.S. pipeline of nearly 40-50 products to be filed over next 3 years, including 12 first-to-files and 8 B2 opportunities; 5 respiratory assets filed, 4 expected commercialization in FY27; 8 peptides/complex generics filed with launches FY27
items.quote: We remain very confident in our U.S. business outlook, which is supported by a pipeline of nearly 40 to 50 products to be filed over the next 3 years. And this includes 12 first to files and 8 B2 opportunities that we are targeting.

items.statement: Geopolitical war situation causing some operating expense impact in Q4, more impact expected as revenue inventory consumed in future quarters; monitoring closely but near quarters not meaningful
items.quote: In addition, we have started to see some impact of ongoing geopolitical situation within the operating expenses, which we are closely monitoring. In the near quarters, we don't see a meaningful impact. But in the future quarters as the revenue inventory gets consumed, you'll see that impact coming through.

items.statement: Generic Ventolin approved with CGT, 6-month exclusivity expected; no cannibalization with other albuterol variants; significant uptick expected; ramp-up in H2 FY27
items.quote: We have CGT on the generic Ventolin. So we will actually be exclusive for a 6 -month period. And we expect a signifi cant uptick. There is no cannibalization that will happen on the other variant, which is a generic to another variant of same molecule.

items.statement: AI-led transformation across quality, regulatory, corporate functions, R&D for faster decision-making and productivity benefits; investing in data and technology foundations
items.quote: We have invested in robust data and technology foundations, which allows us to sca le this up in a structured and sustainable way and also in a very timely fashion. So we will be focusing a lot on driving efficiency, productivity and better decision-making with the help of AI over the coming months to coming years.

items.statement: Biosimilar strategy: predominantly in-house with 2 assets under development (1 in clinical trial under IND), adding 1-2 assets/year targeting 6-8 in-house assets over 5-8 years; limited in-licensing for near-term opportunities; JV with Kemw
items.quote: Yes. So we have predominantly an in- house strategy where we have 2 assets currently under development for developed markets. One of them is already under clinical trial under an IND of U.S. We will be adding 1 to 2 assets each year, which will then, therefore, start resulting into a pipeline of 6 to 8 in-house assets over the next 5 to 8 years.

items.statement: Lanreotide supply disruption: partner remediation efforts underway, reinspection needed; alternate U.S. manufacturing site identified, targeting filing by early next calendar year or Q4 FY27; expect return from FY28 perspective
items.quote: we have the partner who is working on the remediation efforts. And that's in full swing, and we are helping them as much as possible on navigating that part. So I think maybe by next quarter, we'll have closer visibility on their e xact remediation time lines, which will also include a reinspection from the FDA. So that we can come back and guide after a quarter. But in parallel, we have also iden

items.statement: Target 15% volume growth in FY27 across pig iron, casting, steel and tube
items.quote: I definitely look for ward that we should succeed in getting at least 15% growth once again

items.statement: Solapur foundry to reach 5,000 tons/month average in FY27 for 60,000 tons annual production
items.quote: We should average out close to 5,000 in this year itself, '26-'27.

items.statement: Oliver Engineering to reach 24,000-25,000 tons annual production in FY27 from 17,000 tons in FY26
items.quote: From 17,000 to 24,000 or 25,000, 7,000, 8,000 tons extra production and sales from Oliver is possible, feasible.

items.statement: Tube volume growth target 10-11% in FY27 with sales realization recovery of 5-6%
items.quote: I expect that both domestic and export orders in the oil and gas segment should be better and robust. And at the same time, even the other applications, the progress of orders is supporting our expansion plans.

items.statement: Annual capex of INR600-700 crores planned for FY27 and FY28 across pig iron, foundry, steel and tube
items.quote: We'll continue to invest at the rate of about INR600 crores to INR700 crores every year.

items.statement: Baramati tube expansion project investment INR500+ crores to complete within 1.5 years
items.quote: Investment for that plant could be plus of INR500 crores, it would be part of our capex plan of about INR600 crores, INR700 crores per year.

items.statement: Hiriyur blast furnace upgrade investment INR125-150 crores to increase capacity to 2,50,000-3,00,000 tons/year
items.quote: I also mentioned that we would like to invest, not very huge, but about INR125 crores to INR150 crores in Hiriyur to upgrade the blast furnace to take it to, 2,50,000, 3,00,000 metric ton per annum capacity

items.statement: Commissioning 35 MW solar and 25 MW wind power by September 2025 for green energy
items.quote: We are pushing hard to commission another 35 megawatts of solar power plant by July, August and another 25 megawatts of wind power maybe by September.

items.statement: Current EBITDA margin just above 12.5%, target 15% EBITDA margin
items.quote: I expect that we are just above 12.5% of EBITDA. And I would say that our effort will continue. I have been talking about that we are comfortable only when we are at 15% EBITDA.

items.statement: Casting demand robust from auto and tractor sectors, new customer additions including export orders
items.quote: Demand for casting remains robust from auto sector as well as the tractor sector. We have also now we have gone ahead and we will be commissioning sixth foundry.

items.statement: Shift to complex castings (blocks, heads) and machining value addition targeting INR100 crores machining revenue
items.quote: Our portfolio of housing has not grown much, tractor housings. I would say that all our new order bookings are at better pricing than conventional tractor housings or tractor crankcases.

items.statement: Commodity price volatility, war situation, currency (USD/INR 95), coal cost increase $25/ton
items.quote: Dollar has gone to INR95 and coal prices on an average have gone up by about $25 per ton of coal. So some factoring will happen to the cost.

items.statement: Merger of Oliver Engineering into KFIL expected to close in next couple of months for FY26 benefit
items.quote: we are working for merger of Oliver into Kirloskar Ferrous Industries. we look forward to close it in the next couple of months so that we can have the benefit of merger for the year '25-'26 itself.

items.statement: Management stays committed to EBITDA margin corridor of 20% to 24% for FY27
items.quote: As far as we are concerned, at this moment, I would say we have guided a corridor of 20% to 24%. We stay committed to that guidance.

items.statement: Management plans to expand underlying volume growth by about 100 bps year-on-year in FY27
items.quote: So therefore yes, I think this about 100-odd bps expansion as we go forward is something we are planning for and we would like to deliver.

items.statement: Capex guidance maintained at 3% to 5% of revenue; spent INR 570 crores in FY26 vs INR 430 crores in FY25
items.quote: Our capex tends to be actually 3% to 5% of our revenue turnover. I think Sandeep also alluded to it in his opening commentary and last year, we have come in at about the median of that number or an average of that number.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin expanded 280 bps YoY to 23.4%; consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 310 bps YoY
items.quote: And EBITDA margin at 23.4% expanded by 280 bps versus same period last year. And for the quarter, EBITDA grew by 31.1%.

items.statement: Weighted average raw material basket inflation at 40% to 50% at current replacement prices; VAM prices around $1,800 per tonne
items.quote: I think inflation is real on our weighted average raw material basket, inflation is anywhere between 40% to 50%. And therefore, we are looking at that.

items.statement: Price increases of 4-5% taken in April and 7-8% in early May at blended company level; Fevicol division saw ~12-15% increase
items.quote: I think Sudhanshu mentioned at a company level, we have taken in April around 4% to 5%. And in early May, another 7% to 8%. And these are blended at company level.

items.statement: Urban demand buoyancy observed in Q4 FY26; management expects demand to sustain if West Asia conflict resolves in May
items.quote: I can use. So basically, in the case of scenario 1, I think we are going with the hypothesis that the demand buoyancy which India saw in the last quarter of FY26 will more or less sustain

items.statement: Nina Percept waterproofing has very healthy order book; execution impacted by pollution-related construction restrictions in Q4
items.quote: We have a very, very healthy order book. I think what happens in winter period, particularly end of Q3, beginning of Q4 is that because of this pollution restrictions, a lot of construction sites don't get permission to do work.

items.statement: Fevicol delivered double-digit volume growth in Q4; Roff and Dr. Fixit grew at higher end of growth band; core and growth brands both contributed
items.quote: Our core businesses delivered well, especially Fevicol delivered a double-digit growth in the quarter that went by. So you are absolutely right. And it is a combination of basically the portfolio in general is firing quite uniformly in this case.

items.statement: VAM constituted less than 10% of raw material consumption in FY26; Q4 FY26 VAM price was around $840 per tonne
items.quote: If you look at last year, it would be less than 10% and I'm expressly calling out that if you look at FY '25-26, VAM would be under 10% of our raw material consumption for the company.

items.statement: Total volume growth (tonnage) is multiples of underlying volume growth due to mix shift toward lower-value products like Roff

items.quote: We enter FY27 with an order book exceeding 1800 crores and a healthy pipeline across all segments.

items.statement: 68-72% of the INR 1,800 crore order book is executable in FY27, subject to Middle East and supply chain constraints.

items.statement: No significant margin dip planned despite higher upfront investments; Q4 EBITDA margin was 19%, full year 20.02% within guided 20-21% range.
items.quote: We are not planning on any significant margin dip because the scale of the orders increases.

items.statement: Working capital pressure expected in FY27 from large contracts (INR 350 crore hyperscaler deal, others); estimated transient increase of INR 200-250 crores.
items.quote: I feel like the INR 200 crores – INR 250 crore sort of number is the right number.

items.statement: Contribution margins improving as company owns full stack (hardware, software, services) in Transit and Data Centers; end-state margins higher at maturity.
items.quote: The reason we get into that owning every point on the value chain is because we do see that the economics of the business fundamentally changes when you own every point on the value chain.

items.statement: Rebuilding entire Banking stack with AI-native agentic architecture (Aurion AI); launched AI-native trade finance platform; series of AI-native apps to follow within couple of quarters.
items.quote: We are rebuilding the Banking stack with Aurion AI, starting with a fully AI-native trade finance platform on agentic architecture that we announced a few weeks back.

items.statement: Pharma revenue target INR 50-55 crore for FY27, up from INR 34.4 crore in FY26
items.quote: INR55 crores is our target for the next financial year '26-'27. We hit almost INR34.4 crores for the current financial year. So we have taken a 50% growth to reach somewhere around close to between INR50 crores and INR55 crores for the Pharma.

items.statement: Capex budget reduced to INR 80-85 crore for FY27 from INR 120 crore in FY26, focusing on brownfield expansions
items.quote: And we hope to control this capex to INR80 crores, INR85 crores in the next year, that is '26-'27 as we will be going only for brownfield expansions now onwards.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg target 42.5-43 for FY27, up from 40.7 in FY26, driven by Hyderabad consolidation and capacity utilization improvement
items.quote: FY '27, as I expected, we are aiming at, at least 42 to 43, 42.5 could be a good estimate for the full year.

items.statement: Full cost pass-through achieved; gross margins of 46-47% expected to be maintained
items.quote: Certainly, we have passed on the entire price rise to the clients across the segments. And they also appreciated that the reality -- ground realities and even some of them have reduced the period of raw material fluctuation.

items.statement: Paint segment volume growth 13.5% in FY26; ABG grew 60% YoY in Q4, Asian Paints recovered 17% in Q4; expects strong double-digit growth to continue
items.quote: I think it will continue to grow at this level, but the way they are aggressively marketing and aggressively ramping up their production capacities, I think we will certainly be in a strong double digits for next couple of years.

items.statement: Food & FMCG grew 15-18% in FY26; targets 20%+ growth in FY27 driven by Panipat ramp-up and new client additions
items.quote: I'm sure it will be looking at least 20% growth in the food and FMCG, including the North numbers for the next financial year.

items.statement: Capacity to reach 67,000-70,000 MTPA by end FY27 from 63,000 currently; Pharma capacity expanding from 1,500 to 2,500 tons
items.quote: By end of this financial year, that is '26-'27, probably we will be somewhere around 67,000, 68,000, maybe close to 70,000 tons.

items.statement: Lubes segment lost BPCL (INR 14-15 crore revenue) due to L1 tender pricing; expects no further PSU losses, stable at current levels
items.quote: We lost a client BPCL towards the end of last financial year, who used to -- I mean, which used to contribute about a significant amount of sale. But due to tendering system and public sector, they go only by L1 basis.

items.statement: New Pharma plant land acquired at Sultanpur; construction to start soon, commercial production by end FY27 or Jan 2028
items.quote: I think it will go into commercial production only by beginning of next financial year, I mean, next calendar year. It may take at least 8-9 months to complete the construction once the land is handed over.

items.statement: Panipat thin-wall capacity doubling with 4 new machines in July; current utilization 20-25%, targeting 40-50% next year
items.quote: Currently, I think it is about 1,200 tons or 900 to -- sorry, 1,000 tons. It will become 2,000 tons Food and FMCG there. And Qpack also we're adding a little bit.

items.statement: EBITDA target INR 210 crore for FY27, up 20% from INR 173 crore in FY26
items.quote: We are aiming at, at least INR210 crores EBITDA for next financial year, up from INR173, that's 20% price.

items.statement: Commissioned 9.9 MW wind capacity in FY26 (6.6 MW March 2026, 3.3 MW April 2026); constructing 17.6 MW solar to be commissioned in Q1 FY27 and full production by Q2 FY27
items.quote: We have successfully added 9.9 megawatts of wind capacity in this fiscal. 6.6 was added in end of March '26 and 3.3 in April '26. We are also in the process of constructing 17.6 megawatts of solar capacity, which will be commissioned in Q1 and probably will enter full production during the course of Q2.

items.statement: Credit rating and outlook enhanced for key subsidiaries during FY26; financial and liquidity position improving
items.quote: The financial and liquidity position of the company is improving and the credit rating and outlook have also been enhanced for its key subsidiaries during the course of this year.

items.statement: Depreciation increased ~INR 1 cr due to new asset capitalization; new wind assets have free O&M first year; interest on new loans to impact going forward
items.quote: Depreciation is around INR 1 crore on account of this higher capitalization. But in terms of O&M, normally new assets, the first year is free O&M. items.quote: But given the circumstances and the market of steel remain in similar situation, we'll be able to deliver a 10% to 15% EBITDA per ton growth as well.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA per ton of INR4,500-4,800 in FY27
items.quote: So from INR3,900 levels, we should be touching somewhere close to INR4,500 to INR4,800 for this financial year.

items.statement: Export contribution target of 15% of sales
items.quote: Our total export guidance or export target for the company is to reach export contribution of 15%.

items.quote: So the total plan for capex is close to INR100 crores and INR120 crores for this full financial year.

items.statement: Targeting 2 million tons exit capacity by FY27, majority capex already done
items.quote: To reach a capacity of 2 million tons by FY27, yes, that's the intact target. That is still intact.

items.statement: Value-added products share at 27% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: It was around 27% total value-added products for Q4.

items.statement: Color-coated and GT pipes capacity of 7 lakh tons at Mangaon to come online by end of H1 FY27
items.quote: We are adding cold rolling complex in which we'll be entering into value-added products such as color-coated pipes and GT pipes, and the total capacity outlay for that is 7 lakh tons.

items.statement: Demand supportive across infrastructure, construction, industrial; market pickup seen after election-related slowdown
items.quote: Demand from infrastructure, industrial and construction-related segments continue to remain supportive, and the company remains focused on strengthening its market presence across these segments.

items.quote: Given in this quarter or next quarter, if the copper prices are stable, we'll be able to deliver close to 10% to 15% EBITDA margins.

items.quote: So, for this full year, we should be targeting close to INR150 crores to INR200 crores of top-line in the company.

items.quote: We should be drifting close to 25% to 30% ROCE for the next years, given that a lot of our assets are not sweating and a lot of capex is happening.

items.quote: So, regarding the capex allocations, we are not planning any large capex in this financial year. There could be certain sustaining capex, about some INR35 crores to INR40 crores in the financial year.

items.statement: Chennai Park depreciation ~INR13 crore for 4 months; full-year FY27 incremental ~INR45-50 crore

items.quote: Our stand-alone GNPA stands at 3.1% as of March '26. Our X bucket collection efficiency is 99.9%. Stage 3 coverage has improved to 73% from 67% in December '25. items.statement: Added 392 new branches in FY26; now present in 1 lakh+ villages and 550+ districts
items.quote: We have 392 new branches added in FY26, a seasoned field team present in over 1 lakh villages and 550-plus districts.

items.quote: We are having robust order book for smartphones and also in advanced discussion with them for adding other product categories in the JV.

items.statement: Strong demand in Tier-2/3 cities; Agra adding INR5 crores/month revenue since Feb 2026; Bathinda at 65-70% occupancy
items.quote: Agra we started from Feb 2026. It is, that it's already adding close to INR5 crores in our top line per month.

items.statement: High-end specialties revenue share 56.9% (+316 bps YoY); oncology revenue 6.5% of FY26 top line vs 5% prior year
items.quote: Approximately 56.9% of our revenue has been coming from the high-end specialties, which is an improvement of 316 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Debtor days 129 in FY26 (down from 161); government receivables 92% of total; target <100 days dependent on government process acceleration
items.quote: Debtor days have reduced significantly from 161 days in FY '25 to 129 days in FY '26, this reflecting the improved collection discipline, greater efficiency in government claim processing, and a continued focus on payor mix management.

items.statement: No major debt raise planned; INR314 crores FDs + INR100 crores cash + INR330 crores annual OCF fund growth; small debt only if large acquisition arises
items.quote: We may go for a small debt, but not the major one, because we have enough money with us.

items.statement: Long-term ambition to double bed capacity to 10,000+ by FY33 from 5,460 in FY28
items.quote: Between FY '28 to FY'33, we are hoping that we'll probably be able to double this strength of 5,460 to nearly 10,000 plus.

items.statement: Expects FY27 to be better than FY26 on revenue, margins, cash flow and balance sheet with large debt repayment
items.quote: So all in all, despite some of these headwinds, we think company should do better in FY '27 compared to '26 on all parameters. By and large, the revenue, the margins, the cash flow, all 3 parameters and balance sheet should definitely become far better than what it is today with a large chunk of repayment.

items.statement: Targets domestic retail business growth above 15% in FY27
items.quote: So our target is that the retail business should grow more than 15%, right? And that was in the current quarter also in the whole year, but we ended up at 13% because of lack of sales in March because of the shock.

items.statement: Invested INR140 crores in beverage bottling lines in Dec-Mar quarters; discussing 3 more lines for FY27
items.quote: So the bottling beverage business, we have invested approximately INR140 crores over the last couple of quarters, December and March quarter. And the first project is already online. It's working.

items.statement: Overall EBITDA margin improved to 13.2% in Q4 FY26 from 12.8% YoY; Hi-Tech margin at 19.8% vs 17.5%
items.quote: We have been able to improve the margin. Overall margin came at 13.2% as against 12.8% across all the divisions. Within individual businesses, Hi-Tech came out at 19.8% as against last year same period, 17.5%.

items.statement: Polymer prices spiked 50-60% in March then partially retreated; PVC down to ~10% above Feb levels, polyethylene still ~40% up
items.quote: And we saw that between 20th February to sometimes in 25th of March, prices had gone up substantially, resulting into almost -- at one point, there were more than 50% increase in the raw material prices within a space of about 20 days. And on polyethylene side, it was, in fact, 60% increase.

items.statement: Hi-Tech (drip, tissue culture) grew 20% in FY26 driving margin expansion; beverage lines started; tomato processing plant to start Jan FY27
items.quote: But within that 11%, you would see that the Hi-Tech business grew more than 20%. So that has been really heartening to see that the business which is most profitable, grew at the best rate.

items.statement: Cautious on FY27 due to unpredictable raw material prices, geopolitical/export uncertainty, and debt repayments due Sept 2026 and Mar 2027
items.quote: In overall scene, we are cautious right now, right, because of this unpredictable scenario related to major raw materials which we have in terms of the plastics, which we use in drip and pipe business.

items.statement: Targets PAT positive in FY27 after adjusting for one-time tax regime change and NCD unwinding impacts
items.quote: For FY '27, right, our plan right now is to be PAT positive. But I want to just bring attention to one part, right? That's a pain felt by us also, right, that whether you are unpaid employees of the banks after doing all the work.

items.statement: Tomato processing plant with Japanese partner expected to start in January FY27 (tomato season)
items.quote: The other business which we are working on a collaboration with the Japanese company, it's about tomato processing. That plant would start sometimes, I think, January. That is the next mango season -- sorry, tomato season when that comes through.

items.statement: Expects stronger demand for water management products in coming months due to below-normal monsoon forecast
items.quote: And we expect that over the next few months, as this is expected also to be -- monsoon is expected to be lower than normal. We expect stronger demand for water management products from farmers.

items.statement: Operating cash flow post working capital was ~INR600 crores in FY26 (76% of EBITDA); targets 4-figure cash flow in FY27 via receivables recovery
items.quote: And that's important to know because that is what our really focus is going forward next year also that almost -- if you look at for the whole FY '26, whatever EBITDA we generated, almost about 76% was operating cash flow post working capital change was created in that to -- in north of about INR600 crores

items.statement: Sterling expects to cross 95 resorts and 4,500 rooms in 2027 with 20+ sign-ups in pipeline
items.quote: We expect to cross 95 resorts and 4,500 rooms in 2027, with more than 20 sign-ups in our pipeline actively coming on board.

items.statement: Demerger of Sterling Holiday Resorts expected to complete by Q1 FY28
items.quote: We expect this process to get completed by Q1 of FY '28, which was the original timeline that we had intimated.

items.statement: Sterling maintains EBITDA margin 31%+ and PBT margin 21% with debt-free balance sheet
items.quote: Importantly, we have achieved this while maintaining healthy profitability metrics with an EBITDA margins of 31% and over and PBT margins of 21% combined with a debt-free balance sheet.

items.statement: Travel segment 5% EBIT margin target intact despite short-haul shift and geopolitical headwinds
items.quote: I would think the 5% that we have said is our objective to get to is not getting disturbed.

items.statement: Airfares surged 30-50% on most westbound routes due to geopolitical tensions
items.quote: We are seeing airfares surge by 30% to 50% on most westbound routes.

items.statement: Prepaid forex card expanded to 28 global currencies from 12 in Dec 2025; float at INR 16bn on USD 764mn load volumes
items.quote: A noteworthy development on our prepaid forex card is that it has expanded today to 28 global currencies, from 12 that we were operating in December of 2025.

items.statement: Middle East conflict caused 50% revenue decline in Desert Adventures; DEI Q4 EBIT negative INR 10cr vs +INR 7cr YoY
items.quote: The largest impact of the geopolitical instability is visible in the number for our Desert Adventures operations in the Middle East, which declined by 50% in the quarter.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 0.50 per INR 1 face value share for FY26
items.quote: Our Board of Directors have recommended a dividend of INR 0.50 to INR 1 face value share, subject to approval of the shareholders.

items.statement: Expect to sustain and accelerate top-line growth in India and Europe
items.quote: Despite the tough macroeconomic environment, we expect to sustain and accelerate top-line growth in India and Europe.

items.statement: FY27 CapEx outlined at INR 35 billion with nearly 80% towards growth and capacity expansion
items.quote: For FY'27, we have outlined a CapEx of INR 35 billion, with nearly 80% towards growth and capacity expansion projects.

items.statement: Close to INR 3,000 crores of FY27 CapEx in India for truck and car tyre capacity expansion
items.quote: Close to INR 3,000 crores out of the INR 3,500 crores would be in India, where we are expanding capacity both in truck and car tyres.

items.statement: India margins under pressure from increased costs, offsetting through price increases
items.quote: As for India, the margins will remain under pressure on account of the increased cost as we attempt to offset them through price increases.

items.statement: Europe margins expected to improve in H2 FY27 after Enschede plant closure stabilisation
items.quote: So in H2 of FY '27, the positive impact of margins as we become more cost competitive for our European operations should start flowing in.

items.statement: Raw material costs expected to rise in high teens sequentially; announced price increases of 6% to 8% for current quarter
items.quote: Raw material costs are expected to rise in high teens on a sequential basis. And we have already announced price increases of 6 % to 8% for this current quarter.

items.statement: At least a couple more rounds of price increases needed to negate cost push; Q2 raw material inflation could be marginally higher than Q1
items.quote: We've taken about half the price increase that is needed. So at least a couple of more rounds of price increases would be needed to negate all the cost pus h that is there

items.statement: Demand remains strong across categories and channels; April showing equally strong volume growth, momentum expected through Q1
items.quote: In terms of outlook, demand remains strong across categories and channels, with April already showing equally strong volume growth, and we expect the same momentum to continue through Q1.

items.statement: Europe expects better growth momentum in Q1; April positive for all segments
items.quote: In terms of outlook, we expect a better growth moment um in Q1. April has already been positive for all segments

items.statement: Geopolitical developments in West Asia adding significant volatility to raw material, energy, and logistics costs impacting near-term margins
items.quote: Geopolitical developments in West Asia have added significant volatility to raw material, energy, and logistics costs, which will impact margins in near term.

items.statement: Continued inflation on fuel, tyre, and other materials could impact overall GDP and demand in second half of FY27
items.quote: if the continued inflation, both on the fuel side, t yre, and other materials continue, there would be some impact on the overall GDP and hence the demand

items.statement: Agri/OHT contribution about 12% of Europe revenues; OE piece about half of that, may lose some OE business from Enschede closure
items.quote: The agri-contribution overall was about 12% of our revenues. And within that, the OE piece would be about half of it. So let's say 5%, 6%.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA improved from 3.2x to 0.4x at consolidated level; India net debt to EBITDA improved from 1.1x to 0.7x
items.quote: On a consol level, our net debt to EBITDA ratio has significantly improved from 3.2 times multiple to 0.4 times in 2026 March.

items.statement: Transition to concessional tax regime effective FY27 reduces applicable tax rate from 34% to 25%; deferred tax liabilities provided positive net impact of almost INR 570+ crores
items.quote: Following the enactment of the Finance Act 2026, we decided to transition to the concessional tax regime effective FY '27. With this transition, our applicable tax rate reduces from 34% to 25%.

items.statement: Enschede plant closure on track; last day June 30th; non-cash write-off of EUR 43 million taken on fixed assets this quarter
items.quote: The closure of the Enschede plant production remains on track. And as mentioned earlier, we have assessed now the fixed assets at the plant as we enter into the last month, and a non-cash write-off of EUR 43 million has been taken on the fixed assets this quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 25% YoY in Q1 CY26 driven by sales mix and operational efficiency
items.quote: EBITDA improved by 25%, 24.8% like year-on-year, first quarter last year versus this year quarter 1.

items.statement: EBIT margin excluding prior-period depreciation charge improved to 27.8% in Q1 CY26
items.quote: If I exclude the exceptional item of depreciation, it has actually gone up to 27.8%, which is consistent with the growth that we have seen in the EBITDA.

items.statement: EBIT margin at 8% of sales in Q1 CY26 excluding prior-period depreciation charge
items.quote: Then we are at 8% EBIT for the quarter, which is in line with the EBIT that we have demonstrated in the quarter 4 last year and almost 1.7% or 170 basis points higher versus the quarter 1 of last year.

items.statement: Low to medium double-digit raw material cost impact seen; most costs passed through to customers with minimal margin impact
items.quote: I think overall, we have probably low to medium double-digit raw material impact on our products overall. The good news there is, firstly, there's no issue with availability.

items.statement: Price pass-through implemented swiftly; future orders locked in with new pricing by end of March
items.quote: In fact, by end of March, we had almost all our future orders locked in with the new pricing.

items.statement: Demand growing at usual industry rates of 5-7% annually; large MNC customers growing 2-5%, regional customers faster
items.quote: usually 6%, 5% to 7% is the increase every year. Some customers increase more. Some customers do less. For example, the large customers that we play in, usually, they are less, maybe 2% to 3% to 5%.

items.statement: Focus on higher-value business aligned with innovation, premiumization and sustainability; selective participation in value-aligned segments
items.quote: We are going after higher-value business, which is also consistent with our strategy and our strength in terms of the innovation leader in the industry.

items.statement: Solar captive electricity project at Khopoli plant signed and being executed; expected to go live in next few months with benefits in H2
items.quote: I'm also happy to report that we actually engaged in a formal agreement for developing a solar captive electricity project in our Khopoli plant. So that's been signed. It's being executed now, and we expect to go live in the next few months.

items.statement: Capital spent on solvent cooling equipment across plants to reduce solvent consumption
items.quote: We've installed a lot of equipment. We spent some capital in solvent cooling, for example.

items.statement: No inorganic opportunities currently on radar; focus on organic growth aligned with value proposition
items.quote: So I think the short answer is not at the moment. But if something comes up, we would definitely look at that. But right now, it's not in our radar at the moment.

items.statement: Daman property put up for sale after curtailing operations there
items.quote: So we have a property in Daman, which we have actually put up on sale. So we have curtailed our operations there and it's related to that.

items.statement: ECB loan from parent partially repaid; remaining portion to be paid by June 2027 per RBI guidelines
items.quote: A part of it still remains, which has to be paid over a period of time as prescribed, by June '27.

items.statement: Next reporting end of July for Q2 CY26 results
items.quote: I think in terms of reporting, I think you've seen our calendar, our next reporting is going to be end of July, and we'll talk to you a bit more on our results in second quarter.

items.statement: Interest on income tax refund of INR 6.5 crores received in Q1 CY26
items.quote: So it's about INR 6.5 crores that we have received.

items.statement: Retention via dynamic pricing: lower rates, higher limits, faster UX for repeat borrowers
items.quote: once they basically come onto our platform, show that, you know, they're a good customer making repayments on time, we basically, you know, try and essentially, next time when they come to our platform, you know, reduce the pricing for them

items.statement: Received marketing and manufacturing licenses for H9N2 Avian Influenza vaccine, strengthening biological portfolio in poultry segment
items.quote: During the quarter, we also received both the marketing and manufacturing licenses for H9N2 Avian Influenza vaccine. This is an important milestone for Hester and further strengthens our biological portfolio in the poultry segment.

items.statement: Capitalized Fill-Finish and BSL-3 facilities; undertaking optimization initiatives for BSL-3 to improve utilization efficiency and operating cost
items.quote: During the year, we capitalized our Fill-Finish as well as BSL-3 facilities, as a part of our broader manufacturing and infrastructure expansion initiative.

items.statement: Will calibrate price actions wherever required to manage periodic cost pressures from raw material inflation
items.quote: While these may create periodic cost pressures, we continue to focus on operational efficiency and calibrate price actions wherever required.

items.statement: Aims to return to 50-50 revenue mix between Poultry and Animal Healthcare from current 70-30 skew; R&D pipeline focused on Animal Health biologicals
items.quote: There has been a time, I think, 2 years ago where both were almost 50%, 50%, and that is what we are aiming at where we are not hyper-dependent on any one division.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR 70 crores from INR 102 crores; debt-to-equity at 0.19x, considered comfortable; no immediate need for fresh debt
items.quote: Currently, sir, the debt is around INR70 crores, right? It's reduced from INR102 crores, okay? So I think this is - the debt to equity is currently 0.19 times from what it has reduced. So I think this is quite comfortable for us at this level.

items.statement: Africa sales invoiced in USD for cross-border transactions and local currency for domestic sales; participating in Tanzania livestock vaccination drive discussions
items.quote: Invoicing to the other countries in U.S. dollars and for the local, it is a local currency.

items.statement: Petcare segment scaling gradually across selected therapeutic and supplement products; no commercialized pet vaccines yet
items.quote: The Petcare segment continues to scale gradually across selected therapeutic and supplement products and remains a long-term strategic focus area for us.

items.statement: Regulatory requirements evolving globally may necessitate future capex; cannot foresee exact investment needed for compliance
items.quote: Regulatory processes are time and again evolved from the drug department and one has to comply. And it is an evolving process all over the world. So it is difficult to hypothesize and tell what could come from the drug department.

items.statement: Poultry segment achieved INR 65 crore quarterly revenue with 30%+ margins in Q4; management aims to sustain this trend but acknowledges external forces
items.quote: Sir, so now only concern is that whether this is a one-off considering high broiler prices in the fourth quarter? Or sir, you see this trend continuing of INR 65 crores quarterly revenue in the poultry segment with like 30s margins?

items.statement: Write-offs of INR 6.5 crore for bad debts in FY26 vs INR 2.4 crore last year; CFO expects reduction going forward
items.quote: See, this is Ashish. Now one is mainly there is again the provision of debtors as required, and there are a few old debts, which were non-recovered, which are identified and written off. So it comprises of that.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of INR 250 crores and EBITDA margin target of 15%
items.quote: This quarter itself we have done INR 59 crores. So, multiplying by 4, you will see INR 240 crores is easily feasible. So, given some growth here and there, hitting INR 250 crores I think is certainly possible.

items.statement: EBITDA margin projected to improve from 11% to at least 15% in FY27
items.quote: I think EBITDA margin should move from 11% to at least 15% is our projection.

items.statement: Nashik office construction expected to complete by end of FY27, saving INR 2-2.5 crores annually from FY28
items.quote: Hopefully, in June, we will be raking the ground. And by the end of the financial year, the building should be up and ready. So, probably the cost savings of around INR 2 crores - INR 2.5 crores per annum can accrue in the next financial year, 2027-2028.

items.statement: CES order book grew ~70% YoY to ~$5 million; MES order book declined to $0.25 million
items.quote: CES orders have shot up from actually, it was $2.5 million when we started the year. In June 24 last year, the work on hand was $2.84 million. Today, the work on hand is close to $5 million. So, there is a jump of almost 60%-70%.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin target 15-16% for FY27 after MES restructuring and productivity gains
items.quote: Our engineering services from India, now that we have curtailed the excess staff in MES, both the MES and civil from India, that's our core business, standalone business, will certainly go up by at least 15%-20% and EBITDA in the region of 15%-16%.

items.statement: Structural design target increased from 10% to 30-40% of civil revenues in 3-4 years via organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: I wish to see in 3-4 years at least 30%-40% of our revenues coming from design.

items.statement: AI seen as limited threat; may reduce headcount 5-10% but not disrupt engineering services business model
items.quote: AI has no role as far as designing and detailing is concerned because it is not easy to just make an AI-based construction. Nobody would take a risk at least for the next 5-10 years in my opinion.

items.statement: Beryl acquisition completed Nov 2025, contributed INR 23 crores revenue in 5 months; 40-person team retained fully
items.quote: Beryl standalone, they have done a turnover of INR 11 crores in Q3. So, total is INR 22 crores. Yes, INR 22.9 crores. So, almost INR 23 crores.

items.statement: General Price Increase (GPI) from 1 Jan 2026 provided positive impact, helping mitigate year-on-year inflation; ultimate realization of price increase will be more than 4% but varies by product and customer negotiation timing.
items.quote: Yes. So we did GPI from 1st of January, and it has been a little better than what we had last year as such. So it has provided a positive impact, helping us to mitigate the impact of the year -on-year inflation levels as such.

items.statement: Price increase realization will ultimately be more than 4%, though it varies by product and certain key customers take a month or two longer to renegotiate.
items.quote: So, the ultimate realization of profit would be more than 4%, the price increase. But again, it will depend on product to product.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin varies quarter-on-quarter due to peak seasonality and capacity balancing; focus is on yearly margin rather than quarterly, with no specific forward guidance given.
items.quote: So we...our focus is normally to ensure a year-on-year yearly margin. So while we try to operate at an efficiency when the loads are low, the focus is on also building up capacity in case of the peak loads.

items.statement: PBT margin guidance of 7-8% remains a target to achieve as soon as possible, but no specific timeline provided; effort is to maximize in peak and optimize in other quarters.
items.quote: As soon as possible, that's what we'll track. But otherwise, any specific guidance will be like forward-looking. But yes, the effort is always to maximize in the peak and optimize in the other quarters.

items.statement: Consolidated FY26 capex was INR 360 crores, including INR 200 crores for aircraft maintenance (engine/C/D checks); standalone capex was INR 120 crores.
items.quote: So if you look at the consol numbers, our capex for the year is almost INR 360 crores, whereas standalone, it is INR 120 crores. In consol, out of INR 360 crores, INR 200 crores is mainly coming from aircraft.

items.statement: Aircraft maintenance capex of INR 100-150 crores annually is recurring for current fleet; ground capex (INR 120 crores standalone) includes IT, automation, MHE, and lease assets (ROU), with no major expansion capex planned for FY27.
items.quote: Yes, sSo it can be INR 100 crores in 1 year or maybe another INR 200 crores in another year. So typically, INR 100 crores to INR 150 crores every year, even in...without any new capacity addition in aircraft, this will be a part of capital expenditure.

items.statement: E-commerce on ground remains the key growth driver; e-commerce on air has been steady. Ground continues to grow faster than air.
items.quote: E-commerce, especially e-commerce on ground continues to be our growth driver, including the surface on ground as such. While the e -commerce on air has been steady, not very much too much growth over there.

items.statement: Revenue mix FY26: Air 60%, Ground 40%; B2B 70.3%, B2C 29.7% (largely e-commerce). B2C split: Air e-com 17%, Surface e-com 12% of total revenue.
items.quote: The mix has been between air and ground, 60:40.

items.statement: B2C is 29.7% of revenue and is largely e-commerce; split within B2C is 17% air e-com and 12% surface e-com.
items.quote: So between air and surface, it would be like 17% to 12% ...17%: 12% out of this 29.7%.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 volume growth: Air (multimodal) ~8.8%, Ground ~6.9%; ground growth rate slowed vs FY25 due to customer composition changes and lower shipment weight.
items.quote: The rates have gone up by about 8.8% and in ground 6.9%.

items.statement: ATF price increases from March 2026 will impact financials from April, but fuel surcharge mechanism (linked to Brent and currency) largely neutralizes profitability impact.
items.quote: So the impact in the financials will come starting from April. As you know, we have a fuel surcharge mechanism where any increase or drop in Brent is largely compensated or neutralized with the...between ATF and fuel surcharge.

items.statement: Freighter pallet utilization ~85% overall (90-95% on main sectors); one-third of air cargo moves on commercial airlines, two-thirds on own aircraft.
items.quote: So it continues to be at around 85% on a pallet utilization level. We use a good amount of commercial air capacity as well. And we tend to fly the flights only when we have good load.

items.statement: No significant charter opportunities from West Asia crisis currently; domestic charters continue on ad-hoc basis.
items.quote: So, we may not see that ...as of now, at least we don't have that big indication of new opportunities coming for charters because the passenger airlines also are ...I mean, it's moving internationally.

items.statement: FY27 capex focused on automation (sorters, MHE), IT hardware/applications, renewal/replacement, and organic growth expansion; no new segment or major expansion capex planned.
items.quote: No, not as a segment or a new line of business as of now. But then this is largely in automation, so putting up sorters or MHE, material handling equipment and also IT -related spend.

items.statement: Management avoids forward volume growth guidance for FY27, emphasizing capacity optimization and balancing volume vs price to protect absolute profitability and service quality.
items.quote: Without really giving color of forward-looking statement, but this is a business which is largely a network business distributed all across India. So any significant upsurge or even shortfall in margin can impact either service quality or the profitability either way.

items.statement: Ground is growth engine but has variable cost structure (middle/first/last mile), so volume growth may not dramatically improve profitability unlike air where asset investment yields better incremental returns.
items.quote: However, with ground, largely the costs are also variable. I mean all the middle mile, the lanes all are variable. Even the first mile, last mile are largely variable.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected at INR375-400 crores
items.quote: So next year, I mean, financial year '27, we expect around INR375 crores to INR400 crores of overall capex, which will be spent across new projects as well as renovation of some of our high-value cinemas.

items.statement: FY27 capex split: INR225-250 crores new projects, INR80-100 crores renovation, balance maintenance and IT
items.quote: Roughly around about INR225 crores to INR250 crores we will spend on new projects, which will be across payments which are due for projects which are under fit-out as well as new handovers that will take within the year. And about INR80 crores to INR100 crores will be spent on renovation and the balance we will spend on maintenance and IT related capex.

items.statement: Signed capital-light pipeline of 138 screens (52 FOCO, 86 asset-light) to be executed over next 18 months
items.quote: Overall, I think going forward, we have about 138 screens, which are signed under capital-light, of which 52 are under FOCO model and about 86 are unde r asset-light. So that's one. Second, in terms of going forward, our rental cost, of course, in capital-light model and franchisee model is going to be lower as compared to cinemas where we invest our entire capex and that appears in our P&L

items.statement: FY27 screen additions ~120 screens with 55-60% under capital-light formats
items.quote: And the percentage of screens opening in FOCO and asset-light model will -- was 55% this year. It will continue to be between 55% to 60%.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 14.4% from 8.4% in FY25
items.quote: On an IND AS 116 adjusted basis, FY26 revenues was a record of INR6,742 crores, up 16% year-on-year. EBITDA before exceptional items doubled to INR968 crores with margins expanding from 8.4% to 14.4%, reflecting both strong revenue growth and the cost discipline we have sustained for several years.

items.statement: FY27 content pipeline broad and diverse across Hindi, English and regional cinema giving strong confidence
items.quote: Looking ahead, FY27 content pipeline is broad and diverse across Hindi, English and regional cinema, giving us strong confidence in the trajectory.

items.statement: FY26 ATP INR280 (up 8%), SPH INR147 (up 10%); Q4 ATP INR315, SPH INR165
items.quote: ATP for the year stood at INR280, which is up by 8% compared to previous year and SPH at INR147 compared -- up by 10% , both record highs. In Q4, ATP touched INR315 and SPH INR165.

items.statement: Management sees no direct impact from macro headwinds (West Asia crisis, fuel prices) as cinema is small-ticket discretionary spend that historically benefits in challenging times
items.quote: But having said that, we -- history has shown that cinema being still a very small ticket size, if you look at PVR, ATP is INR280. And overall, if you look at India, India is -- maybe the average ticket price is somewhere between INR100 and INR150 maybe if you look at all the single screens, multiplexes, which are there. It's still a very -- and our average transaction size is 2 to 2.5 when people

items.statement: Gross debt to be reduced from INR760 crores to ~INR500 crores; net cash position expected in near term
items.quote: Our gross debt as of 31st March is ar ound INR760 crores, and we intend to bring it down to about INR500 crores levels. And in the last year, we've prepaid a lot of our term loans. We will continue to prepay some of the term loans and some loans will -- with the flux of time, will get reduced. So we want to bring it down to about INR500 crores levels at a gross debt

items.statement: Smart screen pilot launches by mid-July; 28-30 smart screens targeted in FY27 with 30-40% lower per-screen capex
items.quote: Yes. I think by July 15, a couple of pilots will open. I think we're calling them pilots. We're very confident because the se are in good cities. Good deals have been signed by the developers. Demographic studies have been done. So by July 15 or mid-July, at least 2 of them are open, and we're hoping to open close to 28 to 30 screens under this model.

items.statement: FOCO model: management fee 10-14% of cinema top line, no capex or opex borne by PVR-INOX
items.quote: on the FOCO model, we only book the management fee. We don't consolidate the P&L of the property. The P&L is retained by the landlor d. And the management fee varies between 10% to 14% of the top line of the cinema

items.statement: Asset-light model: developer contributes 40-80% capex; PVR-INOX capitalizes balance, consolidates full P&L, pays yield as rental expense
items.quote: On the asset-light model, where there is a contribution coming from the landlord anywhere between 40% to 80% of the overall cinema capex. Depending on how much the developer contributes, we work out an arrangement of yield on his investment. So the balance capex, which comes to our account, which is, let's say, 40%, 50% is something that we capitalize in our books and gets recorded as ROU assets a

items.statement: Advertising growth projected in H2 FY27 driven by mega titles in Oct-Dec period; on track for projected growth path
