items.statement: Expects at least 20% year-on-year profitability growth for the next 2-3 years
items.quote: we expect that at least in the profitability terms, we should be clocking 20% growth year-on-year in the coming 2, 3 years, what we envisage

items.statement: Targets 2x-3x annual growth in Adhikari lending business
items.quote: we can see this business growing from an x factor point of view, like we are hoping that this business can grow 2x to 3x every year

items.statement: Aims to reduce Adhikari loan interest rates from 32-36% towards 24-26% over time
items.quote: the vision is to go down to close to 24%, 26% and directionally keep moving lower to reduce cost of borrowing

items.statement: Expects UPI Cash Point to reach 50% of AEPS volumes in 1-2 years
items.quote: we envisage that this product with our presence will have almost in next 1 to 2 years, there will be a 50% of what we are doing in AEPS

items.statement: Gross margin grew 13% YoY to INR 201.2 crores on 10.5% GTV growth due to high-margin product mix
items.quote: Against a 10.5% growth in GTV, we have seen a 13% growth in gross margin. This is because of the reason that the new products that we are introducing, for example, credit, insurance, banking, which includes CASA, these are high-margin products

items.statement: Q4 FY26 gross margin INR 48.6 crores, down INR 3 crores QoQ due to subsidy cycles and year-end adjustments
items.quote: quarter 4, we have a gross margin of INR48.6 crores, which is INR3 crores down from the previous quarter. That's one point we have mentioned it out that's about the subsidy cycle in the quarter 3 versus quarter 4

items.statement: AEPS cash withdrawal GTV grew 16% YoY vs industry 9%, market share up to 18.4%
items.quote: we have seen a growth of almost 16% in the Spice Money GTVs. And against that, the off-us AEPS industry has grown by 9%. So this growth where Spice Money has outpaced the industry has led to an increase in our market share from a 17.27% in the last financial year to 18.4% in financial year '26

items.statement: BBPS collections share rose from 9% to 13% of total collections GTV; targeting migration from CMS to BBPS
items.quote: The BBPS business used to contribute approximately 9% of overall collection GTV in the Q4 of financial year '25, while it has now started to contribute almost 13% of our overall collections GTV in the latest quarter

items.statement: Macro uncertainty may impact discretionary spending but essential payments platform provides resilience; government subsidies may support AEPS volumes
items.quote: we are hoping that when there are these external shocks, as an essential payments platform, we'll be able to hopefully see lesser impact

items.statement: Merger of Spice Money into DiGiSPICE approved by NCLT first motion; targeting direct listing within FY27
items.quote: The merger application was placed before the honorable NCLT, where our first motion has been accepted. And now we are moving towards convening a meeting of our shareholders for approval of the merger and then moving towards second motion. So like I said that we are hoping that within this financial year, we can close t

items.statement: Medium-term standalone revenue growth target of 25% to 30% CAGR and EBITDA margin target of 13% to 15% maintained for FY27 and beyond
items.quote: So as we said, we -- in the medium-term, we continue to work towards a 25% to 30% growth rate. And we feel we are continuing along those lines, and we should be in line with those expectations. And similarly, as I mentioned, 13% to 15% EBITDA is what we're working towards, and we maintain that target.

items.statement: Standalone order book closed FY26 at approximately INR 1,645 crores, up around 23% year-on-year
items.quote: We closed the year with a standalone order book of approximately INR 1,645 crores, representing a growth of around 23% year-on-year and providing strong visibility for the coming years.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 expected to be INR 40 crores to INR 45 crores, with roughly 50% or slightly higher allocated to BTS segment R&D capabilities
items.quote: And on the capex, the question is around what kind of capex we are looking for in the next fiscal year, it will be in the order of, I would say, about INR 40 crores, equally more or less 50% or could be slightly higher on the BTS segment in terms of the R&D capabilities. But otherwise it will be INR 40 crores to INR 45 crores you can expect.

items.statement: FY26 standalone EBITDA margin was 12.42%, slightly below 13-15% target due to EMS product mix; improvement expected in FY27 as mix improves
items.quote: Yes, it was -- first of all, I think just in terms of our broad guidance, we're targeting to be in the range of 13% to 15% at a combined level and we are slightly below that for the full year, basically because of the product mix in the E MS business

items.statement: BTS segment carries ~20% EBITDA margin; EMS segment pegged at 9-10% (occasionally 11%) due to cost-plus contract manufacturing model
items.quote: So in general, the BTS segment, we carry a margin profile of around 20% at EBITDA level, whereas the EMS segment across industries, I would say it is fairly pegged at between 9% and 10% or in some cases, if we get lucky, briefly, it will be at ar ound 11%, then it will again get reset due to the price pressure because we operate on a cost -plus basis, right, largely, it's a contract manufacturing

items.statement: Strong customer traction and increasing strategic relevance across Defense, Aerospace, Industrial, Electrification, and Semiconductor segments for medium to long-term outlook
items.quote: We remain optimistic about the medium to long-term outlook across Defense, Aerospace, Industrial and Electrification, Semiconductor segments, where we continue to see strong customer traction and increasing strategic relevance.

items.statement: BTS revenue grew ~37% YoY in FY26 driven by space payloads, radar subsystems, land/missile programs; EMS revenue grew ~21% YoY driven by semiconductor equipment OEM ramp-up and new wins in industrial, electrification, grid automation, defen
items.quote: In our build-to-specification business, FY26 was a particularly strong year with revenue growth of approximately 37% year-on-year. The growth was primarily driven by strong execution across space-based payload programs, radar subsystems, subsystems for land and missile programs, and other strategic defense and aerospace platforms.

items.statement: BTS order inflows in FY26 were over INR 400 crores; order book grew over 2.3x in last 3 years at 32% CAGR for BTS and 1.7x at 20% CAGR at entity level; trajectory expected to continue
items.quote: So on the BTS business, which is what we focus as order heavy business. So there, we booked over INR 400 crores in the current year. And EMS, of course, it's an order-cum-forecast that we report only the firm orders, as you know. And in terms -- so that's on the order. And while as far as the order book closures, if you will see consistently, we've been growing in terms of order book that we carry

items.statement: Supply chain bottlenecks emerging in EMS, notably copper clad laminate (PCB lead times) and memory components due to AI data center demand; proactive mitigation underway but monitoring closely
items.quote: Yes, supply chain bottlenecks are clearly an emerging theme in the EMS part of the business I think it's not only the copper clad laminate, which essentially affects the PCB lead times. But beyond this, I think some of the other impacts that we've also seen is on specific component categories like memories, where there is also a lot of demand and pull coming in because of the AI data center build-

items.statement: No major supply disruptions from Middle East war; only short-term logistics delays at end of Q4 FY26
items.quote: No, we don't see any short -- we had certain short-term impacts at the end of Q4 because of some logistics delays as a result of the war. But I would say we are not seeing any major supply disruptions directly as a result of the Middle East war right now.

items.statement: No further exceptional losses expected from European subsidiaries in FY27 consolidated financials; balance sheet carries over INR 100 crores excess liabilities over assets
items.quote: But at that point in time also, as we explained, the balance sheet carries much larger liabilities, over INR 100 crores excess over assets. So we don't expect any write-down coming in hitting the consolidated books. Moreover, we'll also be evaluating the point in time of cessation of control in terms of having a necessity to consolidate. So if that event gets triggered in Q1, then Q1, we would not

items.statement: HAL UHM AESA radar program total opportunity exceeds INR 570 crores over lifecycle; Phase 1 development ~INR 67 crores over 2 years; Phase 2 production ~INR 500+ crores execution through FY30-FY31
items.quote: Yes. So the INR 570 crores order is basically divided into 2 phases. This is -- the first phase is the development phase that accounts for about INR 66 crores -- INR 67 crores or so. And the second phase is the remainder about INR 500-plus crores. This is without tax or anything. So the development phase of this is expected to be done in basically in 2 years. So we've 2 years from the date of the

items.statement: Virupaksha radar development order < INR 10 crores for 2 subsystems (antenna array, exciter-receiver); Space debris tracking radar order ~INR 30 crores for one long-range high-power ground-based system
items.quote: Virupaksha, just to clarify what we have won is there are broadly speaking 4 critical subsystems that get integrated into a full radar. We have won 2 of the higher-value subsystems, which is the antenna array and the exciter-receiver. And it's, I would say relatively small development contract less than INR 10 crores. The second one, which is a space debris tracking radar, which is a long-range ra

items.statement: Semiconductor equipment EMS growth broadly in line with expectations, driven by anchor customer; preliminary discussions with a couple of other semiconductor customers underway
items.quote: Yes. I think we are progressing quite well, I would say, broadly in line with our expectations for the growth from this customer segment. Yes, today is largely driven by a key anchor customer in this segment. And we have begun discussions with a couple of other customers here. But I would say it's still in preliminary stages. The major growth is really coming from the anchor customer.

items.statement: Targeting 13-15% combined EBITDA margin over next 2-3 years; improvement from operating leverage and mix; BTS-EMS revenue mix may shift moderately toward BTS but not significantly different from current
items.quote: And that should be coming basically from some operating leverage also as we see the growth kicking in. But yes, over time, depending on the year, depending on the mix, you may see some improvement beyond that on the margins. But directionally, this 13% to 15% for the next 2, 3 years is where we feel we'll be.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR925-1,000 crores contingent on Middle East situation improving within 1-2 months
items.quote: So the guidance on the revenue, we've said INR925 crores to INR1,000 crores. That's the kind of band which we are looking at. And we feel fairly confident of being able to achieve it provided the geopolitical situations improve.

items.statement: Surat greenfield Phase 1 started March 2026; Phase 2 (pizza base line) in Q3 FY27; total Surat investment ~INR100 crores
items.quote: Surat total investment in Surat with Phase 2 completion will be a little above INR100 crores.

items.statement: FY27 capex of INR20-25 crores for Surat Phase 2 line, balance payments, and Nadiad/Nashik debottlenecking
items.quote: This will be roughly around INR20 crores to INR25 crores this year, we will be still spending on capex.

items.statement: Truly Indian brand in ~3,000 US stores across Costco, Raley's, Safeway-Albertsons, Whole Foods; 2-3 rotations in some Costco divisions
items.quote: We now service close to 3,000 stores across the U.S. markets.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 17.4% in Q4 FY26 (up 190bps); standalone 24.3% (up 260bps); FY27 guidance to maintain high-teen EBITDAs
items.quote: We feel fairly confident that we will maintain these high-teen EBITDAs, which we've been giving guidance for.

items.statement: Freight costs increased 3-4% of revenue in March (aberration month); toned down in April; expect ~1% impact going forward
items.quote: I think you can very well add roughly around 1 percentage basis points in terms of the freight of what we spent right now.

items.statement: Ashoka brand targeting 30-35% growth in FY27 via deeper penetration, new markets, new products
items.quote: We expect the Ashoka brand to grow close to 30%, 35% in this fiscal year.

items.statement: Truly Indian brand targeting INR75-80 crores in FY27 (vs ~$4-4.5M in FY26) driven by distribution expansion and repeat orders
items.quote: Our estimate is if everything goes well, we are looking at anywhere between INR75 crores to INR80 crores on Truly Indian for this year.

items.statement: Middle East (GCC) ~15% of revenue impacted 80-85% in March-April due to shipping disruption; no shipments in March
items.quote: So I would say the GCC business has been impacted by at least about 80%, 85% for us.

items.statement: Q4 growth driven 60-65% by volume, rest by product mix and rupee depreciation; no price increases taken
items.quote: So I would say the growth is more 60%, 65% towards the volume growth. There has been some benefit with the devaluation, but majority of the growth has come through with volume growth.

items.statement: PLI incentive INR16 crores in FY26; final year of scheme in FY27 with similar amount expected
items.quote: So from a PLI perspective, for the full year, our number is roughly around INR16 crores for FY '26.

items.statement: Surat facility to contribute INR40-50 crores in FY27; full capacity potential INR200-250 crores by Year 3
items.quote: So we expect in terms of revenue around INR40 crores to INR50 crores contribution from the Surat facility in this fiscal year. At its full capacity, the Surat plant will give us upwards of INR200 crores in top line.

items.statement: Poultry volume growth expected at 7-8% industry rate; layer chicks target 5 crore+ in FY27 vs 4.57 crore in FY26; broiler chicks and CBF targeting 2-5% growth
items.quote: Our growth is coming to 7% to 8% as an industry. And we do expect that, that growth is likely to happen in Venky's also.

items.statement: Oil Seed division expects Q1-Q2 FY27 performance equivalent or better than Q4 FY26; Q3 depends on new crop and El Nino impact
items.quote: Up to September, I think we'll be doing equivalent, if not better than this quarter.

items.statement: Oil Seed division deferring new capex for 1 year to strengthen existing 3 units/4 plants; Animal Health new therapeutic plant at 35-40% utilization with room to grow
items.quote: Right now, we would like next 1 year for these units, all 3 units where we have the 4 plants to be strong enough to sustain any volatility in the future so that we ensure the consistent performance.

items.statement: Poultry Q4 FY26 operating margin ~14% driven by broiler realization and input costs; management expects similar future performance subject to ingredient prices
items.quote: With regard to quarter 4, the main attributing factor was broiler realization and, of course, input costs. So that is the reason why the percentage and the overall absolute profit was higher.

items.statement: Animal Health Products EBITDA margin 29% in Q4 FY26; full year FY27 expected to sustain 22-23%+ despite raw material cost pressure in Q2-Q3
items.quote: For whole year, I think it will sustain 22%, 23% and above, and we are likely to see the improvement in the top line also.

items.statement: Oil Seed EBIT margin improved to 5.3% in Q4 FY26; driven by capacity utilization rising to 65-70% (target 80% in FY27) and outside sales increasing to 60-65% of revenue
items.quote: Capacity utilization today is around 65% to 70%. And this year, we expect to be around 80%.

items.statement: Feed cost average INR31,658/ton in FY26; broiler feed ~INR39,000/ton in Q3; maize/soya prices expected volatile due to crude oil, ethanol policy, biodiesel demand
items.quote: As for raw material prices are concerned, I think it's going to be a little bit volatile in coming months. for one thing, the crude oil prices are very high.

items.statement: Broiler realization INR102.67/kg in Q4 FY26, ~INR97-100 in April FY27, falling to INR90-93 by mid-May; DOC realization INR51.32 in Q4, INR38-39 in April; layer chick stable INR45-49
items.quote: In April, as far as the prices of broiler is concerned, it is ranging somewhere around INR97, INR98, or say INR100 is round figure.

items.statement: Poultry demand strong: non-veg share of poultry risen from 35-40% to >55%; consistent placement by integrators reducing volatility; industry growth 7-8%
items.quote: If you see overall pie graph of non-veg segment, earlier, poultry was having 35% to 40% in non-veg segment. Now it is crossing more than 55%.

items.statement: Animal Health shifting to natural solutions, therapeutics (new plant), expanded distribution (6-7 day nationwide reach); exports tiny (<2-3%) but growing
items.quote: We started developing a lot of products for the natural solutions, which is into those kind of growth promoters, which was natural.

items.statement: Oil Seed increasing outside sales from 20% to target 33% of DOC production; outside revenue target 60-65% vs 35% in-house; reduces group dependence
items.quote: We are trying to increase it to 1/3 of our production of a DOC. So that means our dependence on the group will become lower and our 60% to 65% revenue will be coming out from the outside the group only.

items.statement: CCI investigation notice received regarding parent breeding farm practices; Venky's India Limited not directly affected as it doesn't deal in those products
items.quote: This CCI investigation is regarding certain practices in the parent companies or the parent breeding farms in which Venky's as such, do not deal in those products.

items.statement: Maize/soya price volatility expected due to global factors (Brazil/Argentina cheaper), crude oil, ethanol policy; but availability sufficient
items.quote: The price is there, which are fluctuating in nature, but we don't see much impact on that because of the global factors.

items.statement: No plans to increase debt or working capital limits; sufficient working capital (INR160 cr) and inventory in place; receivables down to INR544 cr from INR553 cr despite higher turnover
items.quote: There is -- at the moment, there is no -- I mean, planning to enhance the capital or liability in any other way, maybe term loan section or the working capital section, no plans to increase the liability as such.

items.statement: Board approved INR 217 crore for renewable power at Bharuch plant, increasing RE capacity from 50.4 MW to 98.4 MW, completion by Q1 FY28.
items.quote: Our Board has approved capital expenditure of INR 217 crore towards obtaining approximately INR 48 crore of additional renewable power supply for our Bharuch plant and related infrastructure development, thereby taking the total RE power provision for Bharuch plant from the present peak of 50.4 megawatts to 98.4 megawa

items.statement: Board approved INR 101 crore to expand epoxy formulated resins capacity by 36 KTPA to 50 KTPA, commissioning by Q2 FY28.
items.quote: The Board has further approved INR101 crore for the expansion of epoxy-led formulated resins capacity by 36 kilotons per year, increasing the total formulated resins capacity to 50 KTPA. The same is expected to be commissioned by Q2 financial year '28.

items.statement: Overall FY27 capex guidance range of INR 1,000-1,200 crore including approved and pipeline projects.
items.quote: So that should be in the range of around INR1,000-INR1,200 crore including the normal capex as of now, which has been let us say approved by the board, but we have few projects in the pipeline as well.

items.statement: Fenesta Building Systems order book up 15% year-on-year.
items.quote: The order book is up by 15%.

items.statement: Fenesta margin reduction due to scale and product mix shift towards newer categories is as planned.
items.quote: Margin reduction reflecting increased scale and shifts in the product mix towards newer categories is as planned.

items.statement: Chemicals PBDIT flat at INR 163 crore in Q4 FY26 due to elevated fixed costs from expansion and stabilization.
items.quote: PBDIT for the quarter was flat at INR163 crore due to elevated fixed costs associated with business expansion and stabilization.

items.statement: Vinyl PBDIT improved 68% to INR 39 crore in Q4 FY26 led by higher prices, lower energy costs, and better efficiencies.
items.quote: PBDIT for the segment improved by 68% to INR39 crore led by higher prices and further supported by lower energy costs and better operating efficiencies.

items.statement: Sugar and ethanol PBDIT down 18% to INR 207 crore in Q4 FY26 due to 8% higher cane cost; inventory valued at INR 3,876/quintal.
items.quote: PBDIT for the segment came in at 18% lower at INR207 crore owing to the higher cost of production of sugar due to the increased cane price by 8%. Sugar inventory was lower at 32.2 lakh quintals as against 39.9 lakh quintals last year. The inventory is valued at INR3,876 per quintal.

items.statement: Current ECU (electrochemical unit) realization at INR 32,000-33,000 per metric ton for lye.
items.quote: The current ECU is in the range of INR32,000 to INR33,000 per metric ton.

items.statement: PVC prices currently ranging INR 81-82/kg; volatile due to China dumping, West Asia conflict, and import duty changes.
items.quote: Our prices are ranging between 81 -82 in that range right now. But you know China dumping can come in at any time. We do not know at what price and what is their policy behind it. So it is very uncertain.

items.statement: Fenesta seeing good demand with record order book; retail cost pass-through difficult but institutional contracts have tolerance-based pass-through.
items.quote: Now in terms of your second question on demand, I think we are seeing good demand even now. If you see our Q4 numbers also, they were pretty good. So, we have had record order book. So, demand is pretty good right now.

items.statement: ECH plant commissioned April 2026, running at 60-70% utilization, ramping up; 70-75% of ECH sold in market, rest captively consumed.
items.quote: Now actually the plant is running at close to 60% to 70% capacity utilization and we a re ramping up the capacity. The product approval from customers has been coming in regularly and so we expect a steady ramp-up in the coming next quarter or two.

items.statement: Raised funds via sustainability-linked NCDs from IFC in March 2026, integrating ESG targets into capital structure.
items.quote: Further, in March 2026, we have raised funds through the sustainability -linked non -convertible debentures from the International Finance Corporation, IFC. This partnership is more than a financial transaction. It is a global validation of our ESG roadmap.

items.statement: Ethanol sector viability at risk: OMC allocations only 1,100 crore litres vs 1,900 crore capacity; sugarcane-based feedstock restricted to 28%; policy misalignment with cane costs.
items.quote: Against a national capacity of ~1900 crore litres, OMC allocations stand at just about 1100 crore litres, with share of sugarcane-based feedstocks restricted to a mere 28%. This penalizes integrated players who invested in distillation capacities based on stable blending assumptions.

items.statement: CEO targets 25% revenue growth for FY27 but emphasizes uncertainty and will assess quarter-by-quarter; aims to maintain 12-14% operational EBITDA margin
items.quote: What we want to achieve is 25%. But to tell you specifically where we will end up is quite difficult. Even all the uncertainty is in front of us.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA margin improved 220 bps to 13.4% in FY26; management guides 12-14% range for FY27
items.quote: We are positive that we will be able to operate between 12% to 14%.

items.statement: April and May demand strong with growth in both tractors and tillers; monsoon at 92% LPA but spatial distribution and timing critical
items.quote: Looking at April and May so far the demand is continuing to be good. The company has done well in last month. April normally is a lower month compared to the other months of the year. However, we have grown both in the tractors and the tiller space in April.

items.statement: Zetor tractor exports targeting 1,000 units in FY27; aim 5,000-6,000 units by FY30 with new variants launching this year
items.quote: We are targeting thousand numbers this year.

items.statement: Investing in technology, global expansion (US market entry by end of 2027), and evaluating inorganic opportunities in adjacencies
items.quote: Two, three directions that we are working on in utilizing those funds. Number one, we continue to invest in technology. We continue to invest in global growth.

items.statement: Price increase taken end of April across power tillers and tractors; commodity and fuel inflation rising, full pass-through difficult but operational efficiencies buffering impact
items.quote: We have taken a price increase towards end of April. We are watching this closely. If this continues to grow or inflation continues to sustain, it will be difficult to pass on the entire inflation to the consumer.

items.statement: Electric weeder and tiller launched; all-India rollout planned for early Q2 FY27 after real-world testing
items.quote: We are intending to do a all India wide launch across India in early Q2 of this year.

items.statement: Retail finance penetration target 20% in FY27 (up from 10% in FY26) via Project Chatrapati village-level expansion
items.quote: We want to grow it to 20% retail finance this financial year.

items.statement: Inventory disciplined at 36 days; receivables reduced from 75 to 51 days with further improvement targeted via TOC supply chain and SRM digitization
items.quote: We are at about 36 days of inventory. In FY25 we had taken receivables to about 75 days. We have brought it down this year to 51 days.

items.statement: Music vertical revenue CAGR guidance of 20-23% with annual EBITDA margin of 60-65%
items.quote: For the music vertical, which is licensed music, artist management and retail, all combined, we continue with our medium-term guidance of 20-23% CAGR in terms of revenue with our annual EBITDA guidance for this vertical being anything between 60-65%.

items.statement: New content budget for FY27 expected between INR 300-350 crores
items.quote: It's also part of the presentation that we are expecting our new content budget to be anything between INR 300-350 crores this year. That's a range it will be in.

items.statement: FY27 music lineup includes Love & War, Naagzilla, Rajinikanth's next Tamil film, Sivakarthikeyan's Seyon, Nani's Paradise
items.quote: Our overall lineup for FY27 includes the delayed and now scheduled album of Love & War of Mr. Bhansali, Dharma productions starring Kartik Aaryan called Naagzilla, Rajinikanth's next Tamil film, Sivakarthikeyan's Tamil film Seyon, Nani's Telugu expected blockbuster Paradise, amongst others.

items.statement: Video vertical (TV/short format) net margins typically 8-18% with minimal capital allocation
items.quote: That business typically, if it's run well, should always be a profitable business. And in the past, we have always been profitable in that part of the business. You're looking at margins that are anything between 8- 18% Net Margin.

items.statement: Refused to acquire Dhurandhar 2 music as producer expectations did not fit five-year payback guideline
items.quote: The expectations of the producer just did not fit into a five-year payback guideline. And we said no. And I'm proud to share our position actually stands vindicated today.

items.statement: Punjabi music strategy revamped with combined recorded music and live events deals; expects results in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Now we have been able to crack a model whereby we are working with more and more artists in a fashion that we do a combined deal with them, both for the recorded music as well as doing live events with the same artists. This is where Saregama starts getting uniquely placed compared to all other peers in that market because we're the only guys who are playing across both recorded music and live.

items.statement: AI-generated content currently seeing no traction; labels working with platforms to ensure no royalty value assigned to pure AI content
items.quote: But the fact of life is, it's seeing no traction and all the music labels globally and in India are working very closely with the leading three global streaming platforms, making it very clear that when the content pool is going to get distributed across the labels, no value should get assigned to content which is getting generated purely or through AI.

items.statement: UN40 music festival launched in Q4 FY26 with 12,000 footfalls and 8 sponsors; expected to break even by FY28
items.quote: We generated 12,000 footfalls along with 8 sponsor brands coming on board. And remember, this is season 1 of this festival. We plan to nurture this festival further and make it even bigger in FY27. We expect this IP to break even by FY28.

items.statement: Bhansali Productions strategic investment secures exclusive A and B+ Hindi film music for 24-30 months at predictable cost
items.quote: This, in turn, ensures that Saregama secures our A and B+ Hindi film music album requirement for the next 24 to 30 months. We won't have to go hunting in the market for it.

items.statement: Pocket Aces reached breakeven in FY26; profitability expected to improve further
items.quote: As promised, Pocket Aces has reached breakeven this year. We are committed to it. Pocket Aces team was committed to it, and I'm very proud that we finally went out there and delivered to what we have promised. The company has started making money, and we believe that as we will go forward, the profitability of the company will start going up.

items.statement: Live events revenue INR 62 crores in FY26; FY25 had one-off Diljit Dosanjh tour; Carvaan Live concerts and US tours planned for FY27
items.quote: Overall, live events vertical during the year saw a revenue of INR 62 crores. I accept that this revenue number is far lower than FY25. But please keep in mind, FY25 had a one -off event, which was Diljit Dosanjh's India tour. These kinds of tours don't happen at that frequency. So, if I remove that one-off revenue out, even the live vertical has seen growth this year.

items.statement: Video vertical declined 44% to INR 108 crores by design due to winding down Yoodlee film production; focus shifting to TV serials and short-format digital content
items.quote: On an annual basis, the video vertical has declined by 44% to INR 108 crores. Let me very clearly state this. This decline is by design and has not happened by chance. We have shared this with many of you guys in the past that early last year, we took a conscious call that we will wind down our own in-house film production business that we were doing under the Yoodlee brand name.

items.statement: Music catalogue of 180,000 songs growing at 5,500 new releases per year; viewed as inflation-linked infrastructure asset compounding over decades
items.quote: We at Saregama with 180,000 song catalogue growing at 5,500 new releases per year, is exactly the kind of asset that compounds value over decades.

items.statement: Projects 20-23% CAGR for music vertical over next 3-5 years
items.quote: So, in the current scenario, looking at the subscription growth rate that is happening for the music vertical of ours, which added re tail also to it. We are projecting a 20-23% CAGR over the next 3-5 years

items.statement: Expects music net margins to improve 300-500 bps over 3-5 years
items.quote: Yes, over the next 3-5 years, you should have 300-500 bps increase coming on our music business, everything else remaining as it is.

items.statement: Confirms INR 1,000 crore content investment across FY25-FY27
items.quote: FY25, '26, '27 was INR 1,000 crores odd, and we will be in that ballpark in that space only.

items.statement: Plans linear increase in content investment post FY27 at high single to low double digit YoY
items.value: high single digit to low double-digit percentage increase
items.quote: So, as you go forward, you can look at anything in terms of very high single digit to a very low double-digit percentage increase on a YoY basis.

items.statement: TV and digital series business typically delivers 8-18% net margin with minimal capital allocation

So 60% would typically be from the Indian Railways, which is cost-plus model. And 40% we are looking forward to earning from the diversified field.

items.statement: Management expects 25-30% year-on-year revenue growth for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: So with the current trend that is going on, we are quite optimistic that this trajectory of growth that has been witnessed in past few years should keep continuing. But our sense is that it could be more than 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Order book consistently revolving at INR3,000+ crores providing multi-year revenue visibility
items.quote: Our order book remains robust, revolving consistently over INR3,000 crores, providing multiyear revenue visibility and reinforcing confidence in our long-term growth outlook.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to be maintained at 44-45% year-on-year with minor variation
items.quote: So EBITDA would be -- remain on growth trajectory only. And probably what we believe is we should be able to maintain EBITDA of 44%, 45% year-on-year. It may vary 1% or 2% here and there, but no major movement.

items.statement: Strategic priorities: PEC contracts, higher capacity drilling rigs (2,000 HP), and offshore fleet expansion
items.quote: See, if we talk about top 3 priorities, of course, PEC is one. Second priority for us is higher capacity drilling rigs. And third priority definitely to add a fleet into offshore segment as well.

items.statement: PEC contracts have free gas price mechanism; higher gas prices increase order book value
items.quote: Yes, definitely. Because in PEC, we are having a free gas price mechanism. And as you rightly said, with increase in gas price, this order book can increase upward.

items.statement: New 2,000 HP drilling rig capex estimated at INR100-120 crores, funded through internal accruals and debt
items.quote: So our primary estimate is the rig can be of around INR100 crores or INR100 crores to INR120 crores, but that depends on the availability of equipment as well.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of INR500-600 crores submitted; new PEC tender (15-year) recently received but not yet bid
items.quote: It's close to around INR500 crores, INR600-odd crores.

items.statement: Dolphin Offshore expected FY27 revenue of INR150 crores with ~60% EBITDA margin on single asset
items.quote: But with the single assets which we are already operating, we are expecting top line of around INR150 crores from this financial year and the current FY27 with EBITDA of almost 60%.

items.statement: QIP plan cancelled due to improved cash flows
items.quote: No. So we have decided not to go ahead with QIP.

items.statement: Long-term vision: company could double in 3-5 years given government push and market share in onshore services
items.quote: But barring that, now that government has a great move, on this sector, it won't be surprised company could even get double in next 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Management confident of sustaining EBITDA margins in the 30% to 32% range going forward
items.quote: we remain confident in the strength of our business fundamentals and our ability to sustain EBITDA margins in the range of 30% to 32% going forward.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR540 crores funded entirely through internal accruals
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY27, we plan to incur a capex of about INR540 crores, which includes carryover commitments from FY26 as well as fresh capital investments. Importantly, this entire capex will be funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: Solapur Phase 1 expected to be operational in Q2 of this year
items.quote: On the capex front, Solapur Phase 1 is progressing as planned and is expected to be operational in Q2 of this year.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 360 bps to 33.6%, highest in history
items.quote: We delivered EBITDA margins of 33.6%, expanding by 360 basis points, highlighting the inherent strength and operating efficiency of our business.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 34.4%, up 230 bps year-on-year
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter was 34.4%, up 230 basis points year -on-year.

items.statement: Price erosion of 5.5% on non-GPL, non-CDMO base business
items.quote: So on that, the price erosion is about 5.5% is what we have seen on the non-GPL, non-CDMO.

items.statement: Raw material cost increases (solvents, freight) being passed through to customers with green light received
items.quote: most customers are agreeable to take on that added cost, whether it relates to freight or relates to material costs. So we don't expect an impact.

items.statement: Demand visibility is pretty good across geographies and segments
items.quote: demand visibility is pretty good. So we'll have to see how the whole margin thing shapes up.

items.statement: Non-GPL contribution increased from 59% in FY22 to 71% in FY26, expected to continue rising
items.quote: This is reflected in the strong and consistent performance of our non-GPL segment, whose contribution to the overall business has steadily increased over the years from 59% in FY 22 to 71% in FY 26

items.statement: Chronic therapies contributed 67% to FY26 revenue, outgrowing acute segment
items.quote: Chronic therapies continue to outgrow acute segment and contributed 67% to the top line in FY26.

items.statement: CDMO business recovered from Q3 FY26; expect to close 2 new deals in early second half of FY27
items.quote: As far as new projects go, we hope to close 2 new deals in the second half early second half of this year.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflicts and supply chain constraints create uncertainty; freight and solvent costs rising
items.quote: Given the ongoing geopolitical conflicts and uncertainties around global demand, we continue to remain watchful of the external environment.

items.statement: High potent API pipeline: 28 products (12 validated, 7 advanced, 9 in development); revenue contribution not significant until patent expiries from 2028
items.quote: So see, the only contribution that we get is from the sale of exhibit batch quantities because like I explained, the patent expiries are not going to happen until early 2028

items.statement: R&D spend at 3.6% of sales in FY26; expected to reach ~4% in next 1-2 years then settle
items.quote: As far as settling down, I don't think we'll cross 4%, right? We'll probably be at 4% in the next year or 2. And then it should settle down.

items.statement: Capacity expansion from 1,198 KL in FY24 to planned 2,690 KL by FY28; Solapur Phase 1: 370 KL BI block + 120 KL API block
items.quote: The capacity we are adding today will take us from 1,198 KL in FY 24 to a planned 2,690 KL by FY28, positioning the company to drive sustained growth well beyond FY28.

items.statement: Net debt-free with INR782 crores cash and equivalents as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: As of 31st March 2026, our cash and cash equivalents stood at INR782 crores

items.statement: Expects 15-17% revenue growth in FY27 and high-teen growth in FY28, excluding potential recovery of lost US business
items.quote: for fiscal 2027, what we expect as on date is maybe a mid-teen growth, 15% to 17% growth, something like that. And again, same kind of growth would be there or maybe a bit on a higher -- a high-teen growth in the fiscal 2028.

items.statement: Expects US order flows to resume meaningfully from Q1 FY27 as tariffs normalize
items.quote: With duties now normalizing, we expect U.S. order flows to resume meaningfully from Q1 of current fiscal, that is FY 2027.

items.statement: Annual capex of INR 30-40 crores minimum plus maintenance capex; broadly INR 50 crores per year for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: there would be there a minimum INR30 crores to INR40 crores bare minimum capex plus maintenance capex, etcetera, that would require for a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Monthly dispatch schedule of INR 115-125 crores for H1 FY27; expects INR 160-165 crores incremental revenue in FY27 from order book ramp-up
items.quote: on an average, INR115 crores to INR125 crores dispatches planned for this first half on a monthly basis.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded to 51.5% in FY26 from 49.4% in FY25 due to product mix shift and raw material management; expects normalized gross margin range of 49-53%
items.quote: our gross margin expanded meaningfully from 49.4% to 51.5% in fiscal 2026, reflecting the positive shift in product mix towards higher-value machine auto components and a better raw material management.

items.statement: Expects operating EBITDA margin not less than 20.5-21% on conservative basis, with potential improvement from scale benefits
items.quote: I expect on a conservative way, operating EBITDA would not be less than 20.5%, 21% kind of thing. And with the incremental growth, further it may improve because maybe I'll be getting the benefit of scale of economy and fixed cost absorption.

items.statement: Quarterly raw material cost pass-through with majority of overseas customers; half-yearly with a few customers
items.quote: With the majority of our overseas customers, we have a quarterly pass-on for the raw material cost. Maybe with a couple of customers, it's on a half yearly base kind of thing.

items.statement: Container availability delays of 2-3 weeks and extended transit times; managing with premium payments and inventory buffering
items.quote: there is a delay of maybe two to three weeks on availability of container and maybe a bit of extended transit days also. But we try to manage our inventory at warehouse and consignment stock.

items.statement: Board approved buyback of 1 crore shares at INR 180/share (INR 180 crores); promoters not participating; considering dividend but preserving cash for capex and uncertainties
items.quote: In April 2026, our Board approved a buyback of 1 crores shares at INR180 per share, aggregating to INR180 crores. The promoters /promoters group has chosen not to participate, ensuring that full benefit of this buyback flows directly to all public shareholders.

items.statement: Fully settled Right of Recompense obligation of INR 101 crores on March 31, 2026; now debt-free with no legacy obligations
items.quote: In March 2026, precisely on 31 st of March 2026, Rolex Rings has honored its Right of Recompense obligation in full, making total payment of INR101 crores to our consortium lenders.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 62-63%; forging equipment at 80-85% utilization in certain product ranges requiring capex
items.quote: My utilization is almost same what we had, as you have seen that my top line is almost at same -- this thing. So, we are in the range of 62% to 63% of utilization of my available or achievable capacity.

items.statement: Expect to add 200-225 net new stores in FY27, with KFC contributing 100-110 stores
items.quote: We expect to add approximately 200 to 225 net new stores in FY27 as DIL. KFC is expected to contribute 100 to 110 stores of these additions with the balance being driven by Costa Coffee, Biryani By Kilo and international businesses.

items.statement: Merger with Sapphire Foods on track for completion by end of current financial year
items.quote: We continue to expect completion of the merger by end of the current financial year.

items.statement: Tech-related changes will be managed within existing budgets including Yum! charges
items.quote: As I said during the call where we announced the merger, we will be able to manage all the tech-related changes within our existing budgets, including whatever charges we pay to the Yum!.

items.statement: KFC brand contribution margin improved to 17.0% in Q4 FY26 with brand contribution growing nearly 20% YoY to INR 99 crore
items.quote: Brand contribution grew nearly 20% year-on-year to reach INR 99 crore with brand contribution margins improving to 17.0% for the quarter.

items.statement: International business brand contribution margin reached 17.7% with brand contribution of INR 89 crore in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Improved gross margins and operating leverage drove brand contribution margins to 17.7%, with brand contribution reaching INR 89 crore.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin at 68.8% and brand contribution at 14.1% improved YoY in FY26
items.quote: Both gross ma rgin at 68.8% and brand contribution at 14.1% improved on a year-on-year basis

items.statement: KFC menu price increase was less than 0.5 percentage point on portfolio basis in recent quarter
items.quote: There was a very small correction. So, on a portfolio basis, I would say it was maybe less than 0.5 percentage point.

items.statement: Elevated coffee and cocoa prices led to 1.2% YoY decline in gross margins for Franchise Brands portfolio
items.quote: Elevated coffee and cocoa prices, however, impacted input costs and led to a 1.2% year-on-year decline in gross margins.

items.statement: KFC delivered 4.9% positive SSSG in Q4 FY26, strongest in 14 quarters, with nearly 15% YoY growth
items.quote: KFC delivered a positive SSSG of 4.9% for the quarter, the stron gest performance in the last 14 quarters, reaffirming both the resilience of the brand and the long-term opportunity in the market

items.statement: KFC SSSG trends maintained in first 45 days of current quarter in line with previous quarter
items.quote: If at all, in the quarter, almost 45 days have gone by, we have seen that we are able to maintain the current SSSG trends in line with the previous quarter.

items.statement: Pizza Hut SSSG at -3.7% in Q4 FY26 but improved sequentially with ADS stable at ~INR 30,000 per store per day
items.quote: While SSSG was at minus 3.7%, the SSSG performance improved on a sequential basis, with ADS remaining stable at ~INR30,000 per store per day.

items.statement: Biryani By Kilo turned brand contribution positive and initiated measured offline expansion via Express formats
items.quote: With Biryani By Kilo now achieving positive brand contribution, we have initiated measured expansion in the offline channels by way of test launch of smaller Express formats.

items.statement: Gas crisis continues in some parts of country; evaluating electrical equipment and dual-fuel options to mitigate future impact
items.quote: The gas crisis continues to be an issue in some parts of the country, and we are still not fully out of it. We are monitoring the situation very closely and continue to effectively manage the situation.

items.statement: Macro uncertainties and geopolitical tensions remain; small-scale players under pressure aids consolidation
items.quote: Because remember that any of such geopolitical situations, they put more pressure on the small-scale players, which kind of helps us consolidate further.

items.statement: Discontinuing Tea Live brand in India and Thailand next quarter after testing
items.quote: Having tested Tea Live in India and Thailand, we have decided to discontinue the brand, and the same will happen in the next quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 29-30% and PAT margin 19-20% for FY27
items.quote: We hope to keep margins stable between the 29% to 30% EBITDA margins as well as in the PAT around 19% to 20%.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR3,000-3,500 million for Site 5 and new R&D site
items.quote: The total capex for financial year '26 was INR3,838 million and the capex expected for financial year '27 is INR3,000 million to INR3,500 million.

items.statement: Remaining capex across Site 5 and R&D expansion ~INR1,500-1,600 crores over next 4 years
items.quote: It will be approximately all put together, the Site 5 is the major site and the Site 1 where we are expanding the R&D. So all put together, it will be approximately INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores, all in next 4 years.

items.statement: 3 new LSM products (2 pharma, 1 agro) from Site 5 to commission by May-end/early June; validation done, orders in hand
items.quote: There are 3 new large-scale manufacturing products, 2 in pharmaceutical and one agrochemical from Site 5, which will be commissioned by May end or starting of June 1st week. Validation batches are done and orders are already in hand.

items.statement: LSM pricing up >20% YoY and 18% QoQ in Q4; sustained in April-May; medium-term sustainable
items.quote: Pricing has been exceptionally strong over 20% year-on-year and 18% quarter-on-quarter in Q4. We believe this pricing environment is sustainable in the medium term.

items.statement: No demand disruption from oil market conflict; steady demand across products; no hoarding
items.quote: We have seen a steady demand in all our products as such. So there is no hoarding of material happening in this instance during this war.

items.statement: Target 70% revenue from CRAMS+CEM, 30% LSM over next 3-4 years; currently 55% CRAMS+CEM
items.quote: We are very confident of achieving our vision of 70% of revenues coming from CRAMS and contract exclusive manufacturing business models by fiscal year '30.

items.statement: Fire at external warehouse near Site 1 on Mar 11 '26 caused INR70M inventory provision; Site 2 fire claim settlement expected by end Q1 FY27
items.quote: Further, a provision for loss of inventory on account of fire at an external warehouse near Site 1 on March 11, '26 a mounting to INR70 million has been provided in Q4 of financial year '26.

items.statement: Debt to increase by INR200-250 crores in FY27 as QIP funds deployed; sequential drawdown
items.quote: Approximately by end of financial year '27, you can expect INR200 crores to INR250 crores additional in the debt, not more than that.

items.statement: Site 5: 4 of 16 blocks built, 2 ready for commercial production; 4 more blocks excavation started; 20 blocks total across Site 5 and Site 5+
items.quote: We have already completed the construction of 4 blocks. Two blocks are already ready to run. So water trials and solvent trials are ongoing. I think we'll have a good news very soon when we start the commercial production on 2 production blocks.

items.statement: Semiconductor materials: Phase 1 target 400 tonnes at $40-50/kg; opportunity seen tripling by 2030
items.quote: We are looking at producing on the first phase of 400 tonnes of particular set of molecules and where the average price would be $40 to $50 per kilo.

items.statement: Expecting margins to bounce back to previous levels in FY27
items.quote: No, no, we'll bounce back to our previous levels.

items.statement: Total portfolio 7.5 lakh sq ft with 4.92 lakh sq ft booked and 2.40 lakh sq ft available inventory
items.quote: Our total project portfolio consists of 7.5 lakh square feet, out of which 4.92 is booked and 2.40 lakh available inventory.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with capital employed around INR 80-90 crores as of March 31
items.quote: It will be upwards around INR80, INR90 crores.

items.statement: Dombivli hospital expected to achieve EBITDA breakeven by end of 2 years of operation (calendar year end 2027-28)
items.quote: So, end of 2 years, we should expect an EBITDA breakeven.

items.statement: Average capex of INR1.5 crores per bed across 1,700 new beds in current expansion cycle
items.quote: Across the 4 hospitals in this cycle, from Dombivli all the way to BKC, the 1,700 beds will come up at an average cost of around INR1.5 crores per bed.

items.statement: INR500 crores deployed in capex in FY26; gross debt INR500 crores, cash INR545 crores; net cash positive
items.quote: we deployed around INR500 crores in capex this year, Dombivli, BKC land payment , and ongoing Pune and Mira Road projects. And yet on a net basis, we are still cash positive. The gross debt stood at around INR500 crores, while the cash on hand was around INR545 crores.

items.statement: Internal accruals over next 4-5 years plus debt at under 3x EBITDA sufficient to fund all announced projects including BKC
items.quote: Our current view is that the internal accruals over the next 4 -odd years, combined with debt at under 3 times EBITDA, should be sufficient to fund everything that we have announced.

items.statement: Pune South on track to open in calendar year 2028; Mira Road excavation expected to begin by end of year; BKC land allotted, 25% paid, regulatory clearances underway
items.quote: Pune South is on track to open in calendar year '28, as we had committed. Mira Road has completed its architectural drawings and is undergoing regulatory clearances. We expect excavation to begin by the end of the year.

items.statement: Dombivli EBITDA burn estimated at INR2-3 crores per month on average for the year
items.quote: So, we have said between INR2 crores to INR3 crores a month on an average for the whole year.

items.statement: ARPOB grew 11.7% to INR67,700 driven by Indore case mix improvement and insurance price renewals after 2-year period
items.quote: Indore maturing and improving in case mix is definitely adding to the ARPOB. And we have had a couple of renewals from the insurance company, which happened once in 2 years, so, some price increase that has kicke d in after a 2- year period as well, so a combination of some inflationary price growth and case mix

items.statement: Thane occupancy ~75%, Pune ~65%, Indore 45-50%; base business growth driven by inflation-linked pricing at Thane, occupancy plus inflation at Pune, all drivers at Indore
items.quote: For Thane, the occupancy has been around 75%; Pune, close to 65% and Indore is between 45% and 50%, because of the added capacity that we did last year.

items.statement: Key cost risk is depreciating rupee increasing capex costs; consumable costs linked to global supply chains being monitored
items.quote: On the cost side, the only thing that I am watching out for very keenly is the depreciating rupee and the cost of capex, so that is kind of a national reality. So that is something if the situation does not come under good control, returns to really balloon.

items.statement: Insurance revenues 55.4% of mix, government 1%; Indore case mix improving with new bed occupancy ramp-up
items.quote: The insurance revenues now make up 55.4% of our revenue mix, while government stands at just 1%.

items.statement: Thane expansion approvals expected sometime in current financial year; scope and scale to be disclosed after final approvals
items.quote: I think sometime in this financial year, we should have the approvals with us. And once I have them, I will be happy to inform everyone about the exact scope and scale of expansion.

items.statement: Remaining 75% of BKC land cost to be paid in current financial year (FY27)
items.quote: It should be paid in this financial year. Everything will be paid in this financial year.

items.statement: Indore Phase 2 expansion (111 beds) to be considered once occupancy crosses 60%
items.quote: Once the occupancy crosses 60% or near 60%, then we will think about the next phase of bed addition.

items.statement: Dombivli fixed costs will increase over next couple of years as more doctors are hired for the large facility
items.quote: So yes, I think you should expect more fixed costs.

items.statement: No focus on international medical tourism; model caters to local residential communities within 45-minute driving distance
items.quote: our model is catering to local residential communities and all our hospitals are designed such that the capacity is sufficient to cater to the immediate 45 -minute driving distance community

items.statement: FY27 new launches target in excess of INR150 billion
items.quote: as a culmination of -- as a best estimate basis, if we see the year going forward, we are estimating that we'll do new launches in excess of INR150 billion.

items.statement: FY27 sales target nearing INR100 billion
items.quote: In addition, we expect to do sales which are nearing INR100 billion.

items.statement: FY27 revenue recognition target INR50 billion
items.quote: Completion and collection go hand-in-hand and hence, we've kept a target of INR50 billion for both of these metrics, revenue recognition of INR50 billion

items.statement: FY27 collections target crossing INR50 billion
items.quote: And even collections, we are expecting it to cross INR50 billion in the year to come.

items.statement: FY27 completion target INR60-65 billion
items.quote: which means we'll have to do completions in the range of INR60 billion to INR65 billion.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA target INR1,000-1,500 crores
items.quote: The number for the current year, I think, should be in between INR1,000 crores to INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: JV capex INR3,500-4,000 crores over 4-4.5 years, Signature share ~INR1,500-2,000 crores
items.quote: about 5.5 million square feet, you should assume capex in the range of about INR3,500 crores to INR4,000-odd crores should happen by both the parties put together over the next 4 to 4.5 years.

items.statement: Recent launches sold 40%+ (INR4,000+ crores of INR10,000 crores launches)
items.quote: Put together, if we did launches of INR10,000-odd crores, I think we've sold -- we've done sales in excess of INR4,000 crores for entire bucket put together.

items.statement: Per sq ft realization crossed INR15,000, up 20%+ YoY; expect normative inflationary increase in FY27
items.quote: per square foot realization crossed INR15,000 mark, which is, of course, a 20% plus realization on a per square foot basis vis-a-vis the previous year.

items.statement: Will not push prices but will capture market-driven increases
items.quote: We are not going to push that sale prices up. But yes, I think if market forces help us to price the product at a higher price, then of course, we are going to grab that price increase for the company.

items.statement: Global headwinds uncertain but full year and 2-3 launches provide confidence
items.quote: There are certain global headwinds right now. No one can predict how that's going to pan out for the country or for the region, but yes, assuming the dust settles over some time, I think we have full year and with these two or three launches, we are fairly hopeful of doing what we are guiding towards.

items.statement: Net debt near zero (~INR2 billion); JV debt stays off consolidated balance sheet
items.quote: net debt is actually down to a near 0 level. It's just 2 billion, could have been positive or minus 2, but by and large, this is almost down to a 0 level net debt position.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 17% to 20% for FY27
items.quote: At consolidated level with the planned capacity expansion and the current demand trends, we expect revenue to grow by 17% to 20% in FY27.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR250 crores to INR275 crores for FY27
items.quote: Therefore, despite the current geopolitical and regulatory uncertainties, we have lined up a capex plan between INR250 crores to INR275 crores for FY27.

items.statement: Total capex for 45-acre plant development estimated at INR850 crores to INR1,000 crores over next 3-odd years
items.quote: So eventually, the total investment in this plant over the next - - considering we bou ght this land in June -- sorry, January 2023 to another 3 -odd years of complete development, would be close to INR850 crores to INR1,000 crores

items.statement: EBITDA margin for FY26 at 17.3%, at higher end of guidance
items.quote: We are pleased to report an EBITDA growth on an absolute basis of 15.5% for the full year to INR402.6 crores with EBITDA margin at the higher end of our guidance. The EBITDA margin softened to 17.3% as compared to 18.2% in FY25.

items.statement: Raw material cost inflation of 15% to 20% weighted average; pricing actions of 4% to 5% passed on so far
items.quote: On an average, we have seen our raw material cost increase by approximately 15% to 17%, while the pricing actions taken so far are around 4% to 5%, which naturally creates a near-term gap.

items.statement: Raw material basket: ~40% direct crude linkage, ~30% indirect linkage, rest minimal impact
items.quote: One would be about -- which has a direct link to crude and its derivatives, which would be roughly about 40-odd percent, then there is about 30%, which is indirect linkage.

items.statement: Domestic demand remains buoyant; exports delivered steady double-digit growth despite global uncertainties
items.quote: the demand scenario in the domestic market continues to remain buoyant and was a key contributor to growth, underpin ned by strong entr enched distribution network, robust brand equity and a well-diversified product portfolio

items.statement: Higher Uniclan contribution and e-commerce mix in baby hygiene compressed EBITDA margin despite stable gross margins
items.quote: The main reason was increased contribution from e-commerce sales in our baby hygiene business, which is done through Uniclan. The e-commerce business has a slightly higher selling and distribution cost structure, including digital marketing spends.

items.statement: Near-term margin pressure expected in Q1 FY27 due to raw material cost inflation outpacing pricing actions
items.quote: But given the current commodity environment and the volatility aris ing, we do expect margins in Q1 to remain slightly under pressure versus the corresponding period last year

items.statement: First building of 45-acre facility on track for completion in June 2027; commercial production expected end of Q2 FY27
items.quote: As a part of the phased development of our 45-acre facility, the first building is on track for completion in June 2027 with commercial production expected to commence towards the end of Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Uniclan FY26 revenue INR203 crores, EBITDA margin 8.6%; targeting 20% growth and 10% EBITDA margin long-term
items.quote: So, FY26 on a full year basis, we've done a revenue of around INR203 crores at Uniclan. This represents close to -- for Uniclan, this represents close to a 23% growth over their base year revenue. In terms of margins, the margins have been around 8.6%.

items.statement: Seven SpA JV formation expected to complete before end of June 2026
items.quote: In terms of our JV formation with Seven SpA, we are in the process of formation of the joint venture entity, and this should be completed before the end of June 2026.

items.statement: SKIDO Q4 revenue INR4.5 crores, up 60%+ YoY; FY26 revenue INR14 crores vs INR9 crores prior year
items.quote: So SKIDOs revenue for the quarter was about INR4.5 crores as compared to INR 2.8 crores in the same period previous year, which is a 60-plus percent year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Manufacturing footprint to double from ~2 million sq ft to ~4 million sq ft over next few years as 45-acre plant develops
items.quote: Today, our operations are spread across close to 2 million square feet of built-up area. And what we are constructing in 45 acres, eventually once all the phases of construction are over, would be again close to 2 million. So, in a way, it would be doubling our reach in terms of manufacturing infrastructure in the next few years.

items.statement: Direct distribution target of ~225,000 stationery stores out of 300,000-350,000 total universe; cross-sell via Uniclan kirana network
items.quote: So, our universe to target would be about direct target, direct reach about 225,000 stationery stores. And by that time, I think our distribution through Uniclan in the general merchant outlet would have also reached a substantial point, which is basically into Kirana stores.

items.statement: Capex funding through internal accruals and potential additional debt; no free cash flow generated in FY26 due to higher capex
items.quote: If there are free cash flows available, we'll definitely want to utilize them for capital expenditure rather than distributing it as higher than our stated policy of 10% of stand-alone profits to be distributed as dividend. So for that. And there's a lot of headway available to take a little bit of additional debt if required.

items.statement: Targets Critical Power exports to reach 20% of revenue in FY27 from 15% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We are really trying to increase that to 20% in FY '27, and this rise of 10% to 15% in Quarter 4 is just a trajectory on that journey

items.statement: Targets INR 50 crore BESS revenue in FY27 from pilot stage
items.quote: this year, we have kept an internal target of scaling from pilot stage orders to north of INR 50 crores of business

items.statement: Standalone gross margin expanded to 27% in Q4 FY26 driven by richer EVSE mix and fewer low-margin lithium batteries
items.quote: Standalone gross margin in Q4 expanded to 27%, an improvement, significant improvement year-on-year, driven by a richer EVSE mix, fewer lower margin lithium batteries

items.statement: BharatNet project margins slightly lower in Q4 due to fixed government contract pricing amid commodity cost increases
items.quote: because of the fixed nature of pricing in these government contracts some slight low, the contribution margin in Q4 is slightly lesser than in Q3 because of some of the price increases due to geopolitical situation

items.statement: FY26 revenue INR972.9 cr, EBITDA INR97.9 cr, PAT INR68.6 cr; Q4 revenue INR286.2 cr (+27.6% YoY), EBITDA INR26.8 cr, PAT INR18.9 cr
items.quote: For FY26, the revenue stood at INR972.9 crores, EBITDA stood at INR97.9 crores, and the PAT stood at INR68.6 crores. For the fourth quarter, we saw continued momentum across all our key customer segments, with revenue for Q4 at INR286.2 crores, up 27.6% year-on-year, EBITDA at INR26.8 crores, and PAT at INR18.9 crores.

items.statement: Dahej Phase 1 commissioning targeted in H1 FY27; brownfield debottlenecking at Naidupeta to complete by Dec 2026; combined capacity to exceed 115,000 MTPA by 2029
items.quote: We continue to target the commissioning of Phase 1 of the zinc oxide production as per plan. Once operational and stabilized, the Dahej facility will become a pivotal contributor to our overall capacity build-up and also to our growth plans.

items.statement: Very healthy order book and demand projection for May-June; June projections almost at par with April-May
items.quote: even as we speak the months of May, June, we have a very, very healthy order book and a very healthy demand projection. So, currently we are not witnessing any slowdown from the tire industry and what we hear that the demand for tires is quite strong in the market and even our projections what they have given for the m

items.statement: Current EBITDA margin 10-11%; target blended margin 13-14% with higher value-added products from Dahej; Q4 margin 10.26% impacted by 150bps from energy/raw material spike in March
items.quote: So, you see our current EBITDA margins are usually in the 10% to 11% range, and as we've mentioned before, higher value-added products would help increase the blended margins to the 13% to 14% range.

items.statement: All incremental costs (raw material, energy, freight) from March transparently passed on to customers effective 1st April 2026; pricing directly linked to LME with direct pass-on model
items.quote: In line with our long-standing pricing philosophy, all of these incremental costs, including higher freight, energy, and other ancillary costs, have been transparently passed on to all our customers with effect from 1st April 2026 itself.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict disrupted supply chains in March (Middle East import freeze, Europe shipment delays); secured raw material via scale, balance sheet, supplier relationships; temporary ceramic plant shutdowns in Morbi due to gas shortag
items.quote: There is no denying the fact that the war has impacted virtually every industrial supply chain across the world, and zinc dross, our primary raw material, has been no exception. However, this is precisely the kind of environment in which JGC strength comes to the fore.

items.statement: Solar Phase 1 at Naidupeta commissioned in FY26 (~INR2 cr capex, 3-3.5 yr payback); further renewable investments planned at Naidupeta and Dahej; export contribution 10-15% of sales; zinc oxide is 3.5-5% of tire compound by weight, 1-1.5% o
items.quote: we've spent roughly about INR2 crores or so in the solar power project and the payback period for the project is about three to three and a half years. So, the return on the capital employed is fairly high and it also leads to significant reductions in the energy cost.

items.statement: Consolidated top line growth expected in mid-teens range for FY27
items.quote: Overall, we expect the top line growth at a consolidated level to be in the range of mid- teens at the backdrop of higher investment in further scaling up ICONiQ White, arrest de-growth of the other 3 millennial brand and establishment of super premium to luxury portfolio of ABD Maestro.

items.statement: P&A category expected to grow at high teens by FY28
items.quote: Through a combination of above, we expect P&A category to grow at high teens by FY28.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be equal to or better than FY26 overall margin of 14.4%
items.quote: The guidance that we are giving is that the FY27 overall margins, we should be hold on to the FY26, if not better it.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target increased to 18% by FY28 from previous 17% guidance
items.quote: Our guidance was 17% EBITDA margin by FY28. If you would notice, we have increased by 100 basis points to 18%, and we will stay with that guidance.

items.statement: Phase 1 and Phase 2 backward integration projects expected to contribute ~300 bps EBITDA margin enhancement by FY28 and incremental ~100 bps by FY29
items.value: 300 bps by FY28, 100 bps by FY29
items.quote: Phase 1 and Phase 2 initiatives are expected to contribute approximately 300 basis points towards EBITDA margin enhancement by FY28, and an incremental margin improvement of nearly 100 basis points by FY29.

items.statement: Malt Distillery in Telangana expected operational H1 FY27; ENA distillery expansion in Maharashtra expected operational H1 FY28
items.quote: Malt Distilleryproject in Telangana is expected to become operational during H1 FY27. Similarly, ENA distillery expansion project in Maharashtra is expected to become operational during H1 FY28.

items.statement: Gross margin target of 48-50% over next 3 years from current ~45%
items.quote: From a level of 45% it would be my endeavour that over the next 3 years, we take it to 48% to 50% because gross margins in the alcobev space in India are still very low, and I think there is huge potential.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to cross 20% over next 3 years with 50% gross margin
items.quote: Premiumization is the name of the game. EBITDA margin, hopefully with a 50% gross margin, I think should cross the 20% mark easily over the next 3 years.

items.statement: Telangana price increase expected in Q2 FY27, better to plan from H2 perspective
items.quote: We are hopeful that in Q2 sometime, this price increase should come through, but better to plan from an H2 perspective.

items.statement: UK FTA benefits expected to kick in from Q2 FY27
items.quote: As we understand, Q2 looks like a distinct possibility that the FTA will come in place.

items.statement: ESOP charge of ₹5-6 crores per quarter expected in FY27
items.quote: I think, on a quarterly basis, you could see a number of about ₹5 crores to ₹6 crores.

items.statement: Mass premium and other category expected to grow low to mid-single digits
items.quote: Through a combination of above, we expect mass premium and other category to grow by low to mid-single digits.

items.statement: P&A volume contribution target >50% and value contribution 70-75% over next 3 years
items.quote: The Premium and above segment, I believe that it should cross the 50% mark as far as volume is concerned. And as far as value is concerned, it should be between 70% to 75% mark.

items.statement: ABD Maestro targeting ₹100+ crores revenue in FY27 with 2 new brand launches, travel retail and international expansion
items.quote: As far as ABD Maestro is concerned, we are hoping to cross ₹100 crores mark soon in terms of annual.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty and war-related disruption impacting input costs and exports in near term
items.quote: As we get into Q2 and H2, 3 or 4 things are going to happen. FTA should kick in, the Telangana price increase should kick in. The capex benefit should kick in, the season should kick in. So, what we'll see is some bit of margin contraction in Q1, early Q2.

items.statement: UP bottling plant expected H2 FY27 to save ₹27 franchise fee per case on large volume base
items.quote: Our bottling unit that we are planning to put in UP, we have fairly large volume base there now. The ₹27 franchise fee will not be applicable. This will happen sometime in H2.

items.statement: Expect double-digit volume growth in CDMO for H1 FY27 with API prices at current levels
items.quote: At least for the H1, we see a strong volume growth and the API prices, I think, should remain at current levels.

items.statement: Target double-digit top line growth in domestic formulation business for FY27
items.quote: We expect to be double-digit top line growth in the domestic formulation business.

items.statement: Expect double-digit growth in international branded formulation business for FY27 with sustained margin profile
items.quote: This year, we expect to do a double-digit growth in that segment as well, and the margins should sustain -- the margin profile should sustain.

items.statement: API business losses to reduce sharply in FY27 but full year may remain negative
items.quote: We expect the losses to come down sharply. We expect that while the full year would still remain negative, this will be sizably lower and would have a significantly lower drag on our P&L.

items.statement: Trade generics to remain at similar revenue and EBITDA levels without meaningful contribution
items.quote: This is expected to remain -- as we mentioned in the opening statement, this is expected to remain at similar levels of revenue with similar levels of EBITDA.

items.statement: Zambia contract: $25 million per year for FY27 and FY28 from Indian facilities
items.quote: Zambia will flow in into our CDMO revenues. So this will be, as we said, a $25 million, which at today's rate will be INR230-odd crores addition to our top line, which we expect to deliver in Q2, Q3 sequentially as we roll out the orders and get confirmed purchase orders.

items.statement: European CDMO contract: EUR35 million per year on MAT basis for six years till 2032
items.quote: Broadly, this is how it is, EUR35 million for the next six years till 2032.

items.statement: FY26 capex was INR222 crores; FY27 capex target is INR300 crores
items.quote: FY26, we did a capex of INR222 crores. And this year, we are targeting to keep our capex to INR300 crores.

items.statement: CDMO margins expected to remain at current profile (13-14%) for FY27
items.quote: Similar margin profile what we currently have.

items.statement: European CDMO contract margins expected to be similar or high teens
items.quote: It should be similar or high teens. So this is what we expect.

items.statement: CDMO base margins expected to improve once European and Zambia contracts are in full swing
items.quote: We can think through that the base margins for the business once both of these contracts are in full swing will improve.

items.statement: API prices crashed 20-25% as a basket over FY26; recently risen single high-digits but still below April 2025 levels
items.quote: The whole of the year, the API prices crashed by about 20%, 25% as a basket.? Due to the current ongoing global Akums Drugs & geopolitical situation, the API prices have slightly gone up, single high-digits, they have gone up as a

items.statement: CDMO model is percent margin on input cost; absolute margins fluctuate with API prices
items.quote: This model is a percent margins on the input cost. So, the input cost then depending on the product type, the dosage form and so on, the percent margin is applied on top of it.

items.statement: CDMO volume growth >25% in H2 FY26 driven by existing customers; similar double-digit growth visible in May for Q1 FY27
items.quote: What we have seen, as we also discussed this in Q3, this is primarily led from existing customers only. So, this is not new geographies or new customers. So, what we are seeing is increased demand for existing brands from the existing customers only.

items.statement: New injectable facility utilization in early teens; significant ramp-up expected in FY27
items.quote: New facility, we are still ramping up. The utilization is in early teens. And we expect that this year, we will have a significant ramp-up in the injectable facility.

items.statement: GLP market entry under evaluation; pricing volatility and API partner selection are key considerations
items.quote: We are still evaluating when to enter, at which states to enter, given if you also have read some news last week when we have been witnessing in the industry itself, the pricing still remains very volatile and going down south.

items.statement: FY27 revenue projected between Rs 2,150-2,200 crore, up from Rs 1,898 crore in FY26
items.quote: I think we are projected 15%, but I think we should be somewhere between Rs. 2,150 crores to Rs. 2,200 crores, which is very good.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target of Rs 2,500 crore reaffirmed
items.quote: And Rs. 2,500 crores for 27-28 as projected some years ago.

items.statement: Gujarat PEB plant Phase 1 operational by July 2026, Phase 2 by year-end; Andhra heavy structure plant Phase 1 by July-August 2026, Phases 2-3 accelerated to end of FY27
items.quote: As promised, both the pre-engineered building plant in Gujarat will be in play by July this year, and the heavy structure plant will also be in two phases in July and August.
