items.statement: Heavy structure capacity to reach 40,000 tons by March-April 2027 and 60,000 tons by November-December 2027
items.quote: heavy structure will add in this year, maybe by next March, we will have about 40,000 tons, 20,000 tons is already going in line by August, and 20,000 tons more hopefully by March, April next year. That will make it 40,000 tons and the plan currently is to add it to 60,000 tons by next November or December.

items.statement: Order book stands at over Rs 1,700 crore, up Rs 40-50 crore from last disclosure; Rs 102 crore order announced recently to be booked next quarter
items.quote: Our order book is over Rs. 1,700 crores right now compared to what it was in April. It is Rs. 40 crores, Rs. 50 crores higher than what it was last time we declared it. After that, as you know, we have announced another Rs. 102 crore order that we have received, but that will go into the next quarter.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin steady at 9.3% despite provisions and extra costs
items.quote: The total revenue for FY '26 is Rs. 1,898 crores compared to Rs. 1,453 crores, a growth of 31%. EBITDA Rs. 176 crores from Rs, 136 crores, 29% growth, very healthy. EBITDA margin steady at 9.3% in spite of these provisions that we had to make and the extra costs we had to incur.

items.quote: Pipeline 1 would be about Rs. 700 crores to Rs. 800 crores, where orders would get finalized within the next 60 days. That would be approximately Rs. 800 crores to Rs. 900 crores currently. So, those are very serious at a serious stage. items.statement: Dividend of Rs 12.5 per share (125% of face value) recommended for FY26
items.quote: the directors have recommended a final dividend as of last year, Rs. 12.5, 125% of the share value.

items.quote: See, HSS segment, we were not going to give a very major figure in anything because till we get into the market and till we start selling and till we see, like they say, the taste of the pudding is in the eating. items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15% maintained, HSS contribution to be revised after plant commissioning
items.quote: You see, if everything goes in order, I think this year, we should be able to sell about 10,000 to 12,000 tons because the production will happen in July by the time we get into commercial production supply.

items.statement: Gujarat HSS plant Phase-1 commercial production by July 2026, Phase-2 to follow shortly after
items.quote: Trial production Wil start in June, and commercial production will start by July. We are very much on track, except that we lost that one month in the beginning.

items.statement: Fundraise via QIP or other route in next 2-3 months primarily for HSS plant Phase-2 and 3 acceleration
items.quote: We are going to raise funds. As we said, we are exploring, while we did take approval for QIP, we are exploring as to what s the best way to raise the fund when we require it.

items.statement: Order book at Rs 1,700 crore as of 30 April 2026, executable in ~9 months, primarily PEB
items.quote: Rs. 1,700 crores. As of 30th April 2026, it is Rs. 1,700 crores? Yes. To be executed in about 9 months, yes.

items.statement: FY27 PAT margin expected at 7-7.5%, similar to current levels despite growth investments
items.quote: Yes, 7% to 7.5%. Yes, net. By what, we don't know.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target >10% long-term, currently ~9.3% (9.7% ex one-offs), driven by value-chain move and productivity
items.quote: I think the chances of being on the upside is very high, that we should grow. And that is the target. I mean, 9%, 9.5%, 10%, I don't think is a very good margin for a company which does all that we do.

items.statement: Steel price volatility averages out over 4 quarters; each job uniquely priced with forward cost estimates
items.quote: We don't have an automatic formula that just price everything at Rs. 60 or Rs. 70. No. We price every job as a unique individual job, where we see what are the materials required?

items.statement: Export revenue target Rs 100 crore in FY27 (currently Rs 30-35 crore in hand), North America JV to ramp over 1-1.5 years
items.quote: If [ were to make a very wild guess, I would say that our aim should be to get at least Rs. 100 crores of orders. In export, that would be our aim.

items.statement: Key risk is manpower shortage at sites and plants; addressing via better worker care, automation and robotics
items.quote: I think the biggest challenge that India will face, and then of course everybody will face, is the manpower. So, I think how well prepared we are to pick up that challenge.

items.statement: Tax rate normalized to ~25% from FY27 after one-time 27% hit in Q4 FY26 due to Section 145A method change
items.quote: But going forward, it will be back to normal. So, instead of, say, 25% tax as we should have paid or 24% we paid last year, I think it went up to about 27%.

items.statement: Working capital improvement focus: tightening payment terms, higher advances, milestone-based collections for large orders
items.quote: So, we are also tightening up the processes at the time we are taking orders to make sure that the payments come faster and the customers do meet their milestones.

items.statement: Sixth PEB plant land acquired; combined PEB capacity Rs 3,000 cr + HSS Rs 500 cr by FY27-28 end
items.quote: We have bought the land recently for the second PEB plant, if we want to have it. We bought the land last month next to our existing land.

items.statement: Management does not provide growth guidance
items.quote: We generally don't give growth guidance I think this is we've typically helped you guys to plot how to look at the business, how it will scale, etc. But we have decided not to give guidance on our numbers.

items.statement: West Asia conflict expected to create short-term drag on trade movement and growth
items.quote: we believe that the west Asia conflict which is a widespread conflict not only for us but for the whole Indian economy w ill have short- term headwinds with anticipated drag on trade movement and which obviously because most of our revenue comes from flow throughs but we continue to climb on our revenues that will be consistent but maybe create a drag on our short-term

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin stabilized around 31% after peaking at 36% in Q1 FY26 due to growth business investments
items.quote: I think we peaked in terms of profitability say back in say Q1 of FY26 almost 36% of say adjusted EBITDA margin and now we have sort of stabilized around 31% odd.

items.statement: Stepped up investments in core businesses and growth businesses including AI for super loads

items.statement: Vehicle finance assets managed by partners at ~600 crores, ~10% on own books
items.quote: Close to 600 crores is the assets managed by our partners overall in our books. About 10 percentage is basically on our books.

items.statement: Intercity truck movement showing drag in April-May after inventory clearance till March
items.quote: Because intercity trucks typically sit at the top end of the value chain and mostly till March, I think there was a lot of inventory stocks which would definitely move but going into April and May we're finding some kind of drag on it in taking off.

items.statement: Tolling GTV grew 27% YoY vs NETC CV industry growth of 16%, representing ~90% of payments GTV
items.quote: The GTV of tolling for us in the last full year grew at about 27% on a year-on-year basis in a very matured and penetrated industry largely driven by a strong product play and a distribution play.

items.statement: AIS device sales doubled in Q4 FY26 driven by mandates across 10 states
items.quote: The sales of the AIS vertical doubled during the last quarter which was largely driven by mandates and largely driven by a strong distribution and a product play.

items.statement: Super loads mature hubs (Bangalore, Hyderabad) showing strong unit economics; 10 new cities growing faster than established ones
items.quote: Our mature or let's say our first hubs of Bangalore and Hyderabad, we continue to scale, continue to double down and these continue to show signs of strength from a unit economics from a scale perspective. items.statement: Vehicle finance business expected to exit investment mode and start generating cash flows by end of FY27
items.quote: Vehicle finance business probably by the end of this financial year would no longer be in the investment mode and would start probably churning cash flows which will also enable us to move that into a core business kind of a trajectory from a narrative perspective.

items.statement: OMC loyalty program suspension temporarily impacting fuel business; similar hiccups occurred in past and recovered
items.quote: One small narrative on that which is a very direct impact is as you know that we have a fuel business which is basically built on top of the loyalty program which OMC's work on and they have suspended their loyalty program temporarily. items.statement: All businesses contribution margin positive; growth businesses negative at EBITDA level due to scaling investments
items.quote: So, most or all our businesses across regardless they are new or experiments or whatever we are always contribution margin positive. We make money on every order we do so if orders scale our profitability converges.

items.quote: Basically, the whole framework of MLFF is on prepaid collection. That's point number one, right? items.quote: a recent quarter basis there the growth in profitability is 30% on a year-on-year basis and we delivered 50.2 crores of adjusted EBITDA in the last quarter. items.statement: FY26 Gross Income ~715 crores (55% YoY), Adjusted EBITDA ~190 crores (84% YoY), PAT 160 crores, Free cash flow 185-190 crores

On a EBITDA basis we have done close to 190 crores which is a 84% growth on a year-on-year basis. This is our first full year of profitability at a PAT level. We have done 160 crores in PAT in the full year financial FY 25-26.

items.statement: Monthly transacting customers grew 13% YoY to 8.2 lakh; power users (2+ services) grew 22% YoY
items.quote: We grew in our transacting customers by 13% on a year -on-year basis to close to 8.2 lakh monthly transacting customers across the whole year. Users who use more than two services who are our power users, we've compounded at 22% year on year.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated EBITDA target north of INR 500 crores
items.quote: I would say that we did a consol EBITDA of about INR 280 crores FY26. We are looking at north of INR 500 crores for the FY27 EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Punjab Phase 2 expansion targeting commissioning by end of FY27
items.quote: Now that we are done with Phase 1, we have now put all our energy and all our focus on the Phase 2 expansion. We are working with the people, the entire project team as well as the operational team on that basis. items.quote: As such after the Phase 2, if you realize we still have the cotton expansion that is coming up in MP where we should be on the ground post the monsoons. items.statement: Technical yarn capacity doubling at Silvassa from 9,000 to 18,000 MTPA, commissioning by end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: As communicated earlier, we are progressing with the doubling of our technical yarn capacity at Silvassa from 9,000 metric tons per annum to 18,000 metric tons per annum, which we believe will further strengthen our position in higher value textile applications.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improvement expected in FY27 as Punjab stabilizes and product mix improves
items.quote: We anticipate this will translate into stronger operating margins, better absorption of depreciation and interest cost and healthier free cash flow generation over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Punjab facility gross margins expected to improve substantially from Q2 FY27 as supply chain settles and value-added mix increases
items.quote: Yes, see once we ramp up fully, I mean we are ramped up fully, but once we settle the supply chain and the product line-up everything, you will from the second quarter FY27, you will see the substantial change in that.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through underway after war-related volatility; polyester spreads cautiously constructive
items.quote: But because whenever there is a high volatility, it becomes a little difficult to pass on immediately, which stabilizes over a period of time. That is exactly what happened and we have passed on now in the process of passing on the entire hike of raw materials.

items.statement: Domestic yarn demand robust post-war volatility; long-term structural drivers from man-made fiber shift remain intact
items.quote: Demand scenario, the last quarter after the war, yes, downstream people also because of the volatility in the crude prices and the raw material prices were a little disturbed. But they are back to base and we see very robust demand coming in now also.

items.statement: Peak gross debt at INR 1,500 crores; targeting INR 100-125 crores annual repayment with no major new debt planned
items.quote: This is our peak gross debt level and we are expecting a payouts of close to INR 100 to INR 125 crores every year. And we don't plan to take any big debt in the near future.

items.statement: Gas cost at Silvassa up 50-60% but only 6-7% of operational cost; Punjab uses agri-waste unaffected by gas prices
items.quote: As far as Silvassa is concerned, yes, we use gas for heating. There definitely the cost of gas has gone up by about 60%, 50% to 60% of the cost of gas. So that is affecting our cost of heating at Silvassa but not at the Punjab facility.

items.statement: FY27 capex ~INR350 cr: INR90 cr for pump/motor automation & capacity; rest for solar module expansion to 2.1 GW + backward integration
items.quote: By the end of this year, I think we will infuse around INR350 crores of total capex this year in FY27.

items.statement: SteriPort capacity expansion from 6.6 crore to 12 crore bottles/year expected operational by 20th June 2026
items.quote: With utilization levels remaining healthy, we are now expanding capacity from 6.6 crore bottles per year to roughly 12 crore bottles per year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 24-25% for FY27 driven by SteriPort expansion (27% margin) and solar savings
items.quote: The new product line is expected to have about 27% EBITDA margin only for SteriPort. So combining the new and the existing, on an average basis we will be expecting between 24% to 25% EBITDA margin going forward.

items.statement: PAT margin expected to improve from 5% to 8-9% as debt repayment reduces finance costs
items.quote: Once we leverage in the current year then going forward, it will be improving by at least 3%.

items.statement: Polymer prices up 60-70%; price increase of INR 1.25-1.75/bottle (5-6% on selling price) implemented with no resistance
items.quote: We are witnessing roughly 60% to 70% increase in input cost, both the grades: polyethylene and polypropylene. And the impact per container would vary from roughly INR1.25 to INR1.75.

items.statement: SteriPort contributes 42% of revenue; SVP portfolio (inhalation, preservative-free ophthalmics) contributes 20% of SVP revenue
items.quote: Our SteriPort platform, a product that continues to gain strong traction in the market, contributes nearly 42% of the revenue from operations.

items.statement: No long-term contracts with hospital chains; pricing is one-sided favoring buyers, but price increases passed through immediately
items.quote: In Indian context, the contracts typically tend to be one-sided. If we enter into a contract with a hospital chain like say, Apollo, if it favors them then they will trigger all the covenants, but if it is working against them then probably they would stop buying from you.

items.statement: Debt reduced from INR 234 crores to INR 204 crores post March 2026; 90% borrowing now at single-digit rates; further INR 30-40 crores debt replacement planned

items.statement: Comfort Click became EPS accretive in Q4 FY26

items.statement: Seasonal portfolio recovery expected from May onwards
items.quote: So we see recovery from May onwards.

items.statement: Seasonal portfolio expected to deliver consistent double-digit growth over 3-4 years
items.quote: So we are quite hopeful that it should come back on track and over a three to four -year period should deliver a consistent double-digit growth.

items.statement: Organized channel saliency improved to 30% in FY26 from 24% in FY25
items.quote: As per the internal data, the domestic business continued to witness a steady shift towards organized channel, with saliency improving to 30% in financial year '26 from 24% in financial year '25.

items.statement: Quick commerce contributes 7-8% of total domestic business
items.quote: Quick commerce will be 7%-8%.

items.statement: Comfort Click amortization in Q4 FY26 will continue at similar level for full year
items.quote: Amortization, you know, what you see the number in this quarter, the quarter 4, will almost be on the similar line because that captures the full quarter's amortization.

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions had limited impact with proactive mitigation
items.quote: The ongoing geopolitical disruptions has had a limited impact on the company wi th proactive mitigation measures in place.

items.statement: Tax rate for FY27-28 will be in 25% bracket; FY27 mix of cash and deferred tax asset
items.quote: So FY 27- 28 will be in the 25% bracket. But 26-27, it will be kind of cash plus deferred tax asset used. So the mix of two.

items.statement: Operating leverage to play out on entire business ex-Comfort Click
items.quote: As far as operating leverage is concerned, it is likely to play out on the entire business ex - Comfort Click, because as we told earlier also that Comfort Click is largely variable spend business.

items.statement: Comfort Click like-for-like growth of 31.4% in Q4 FY26 and 29.5% in FY26
items.quote: The international business, including Comfort Click business, delivered a like -to-like growth of 29.5%.

items.statement: Commodity input costs showed divergent trends across categories
items.quote: Commodity input costs showed divergent trends across categories, while structural growth drivers remained intact.

items.statement: Rural demand recovery outpaced gradual urban improvement
items.quote: During the quarter, consumption trends remained steady, supported by a sustained recovery in rural demand, which continued to outpace the gradual improvement in urban markets.

items.statement: RiteBite Max Protein expanded into RTD beverage, ghee jaggery bar, and Korean flavor chips
items.quote: Under the RiteBite Max Protein franchise, we expanded its offering with the launch of Max Protein Ultimate Protein Boost Ready -to-Drink beverage, Max Protein Roots Ghee Jaggery Bar and Korean flavor chips with multiple flavors.

items.statement: No plans to divest slow-growing product categories
items.quote: I think our allocation of funds are appropriate to the brand. So I don't see any major changes. I think all brands have appropriate funding required. So there's no other plans or any other changes to the business.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected around 11% plus/minus 50 basis points
items.quote: the ongoing challenges and initial costs in the newly commissioned plants, we continue to expect an annual EBITDA margin of around 11% plus/minus 50 basis points

items.statement: FY27 total capex planned at approximately INR 1,750 crores
items.quote: For FY27, we have planned a total capital expenditure of approximately INR 1,750 crores, comprising of around INR 650 crores towards sustaining capex and around INR 1,100 crores towards growth capex and balance towards land acquisition.

items.statement: New 2-wheeler lighting order with annual peak value of approximately INR 450 crores, SOP in H2 FY28
items.quote: A key highlight during the quarter was the receipt of a significant new order for unserved models, with an annual peak value of approximately INR 450 crores for the supply of 2-wheeler lighting products, with SOP scheduled in second half of FY 28.

items.statement: New seating export orders with expected annual peak value of approximately INR 390 crores from 3 new customers in Europe and North America, supplies from FY28
items.quote: Building on this traction, the business secured new export orders with an expected annual peak value of approximately INR 390 c rores from 3 new customers from Europe and North America in the CV segment. Supplies for these programs are expected to commence in FY28

items.statement: Sunroof order book potential over INR 350 crores after additional INR 85 crore order
items.quote: Further strengthening our order book, we secured an additional order wi th an annual peak value of estimated to be INR 85 crores, taking the total sunroof order book potential to over INR 350 crores

items.statement: IVI order of INR 600 crores estimated peak annual value, SOP Q3 FY29, part of Denso JV
items.quote: Our in-house R&D center has developed a competitive Android-based IVI platform, enabling us to secure a sizable order of INR 600 crores estimated peak annual value compared to our FY26 JV revenues of INR 846 crores.

items.statement: 2-wheeler display unit order with estimated annual peak value around INR 200 crores, production from Q4 FY27
items.quote: Additionally, CREAT, our R&D center has developed a silver box display unit for 2-wheeler applications for which we have secured an order with an estimated annual peak value of around INR 200 crores. Production for this program is expected to commence in Q4 FY27.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 11.3%, gross margin compression of almost 1% due to new businesses and commodity impact
items.quote: In terms of margin, yes, you are right. There is a gross margin compression of almost 1%.

items.statement: Commodity price impact expected to be sizable in coming quarters; discussing shorter pass-through cycles with customers
items.quote: But to your point, yes, there will be expected to be an impact in the coming quarters, which are expected to be sizable. But we are currently in the process of discussing with our customers that our customers have been very supportive.

items.statement: Aluminum pass-through impact roughly 4% to 5% for Q4 FY26 in casting business
items.quote: In terms of casting, the growth is 18%. The impact of aluminum pass-through was roughly around 4% to 5% for the quarter.

items.statement: Labor cost increase impact almost a couple of hundred crores for Haryana and Gujarat
items.quote: So the impact is obviously quite significant. It's almost like a couple of hundred crores for what we call Haryana and Gujarat.

items.statement: Near-term moderation in alloy wheel penetration due to customer vehicle mix shift to entry-level models and steel wheel adoption
items.quote: From a demand standpoint, we are seeing some near-term moderation in alloy wheel penetration in our customers. This was primaril y led by shift in our customers' vehicle mix with stronger growth in entry level of the models, where alloy wheel adoption remains relatively lower

items.statement: 2-wheeler alloy wheel penetration around 70%, 4-wheeler alloy wheel penetration around 40%
items.quote: In terms of penetration trends, the 2-wheeler alloy wheel penetration is somewhere around 70% and 4-wheeler EV alloy wheel penetration is somewhere around 40%.

items.statement: Green mobility segment grew 25% YoY in Q4 to INR 423 crores, 8% of consolidated revenue
items.quote: Showing immediate momentum, the green mobility segment achieved a robust 25% year-on-year revenue growth in the quarter, reaching INR 423 crores and contributing 8% to the company's total consol revenues.

items.statement: EV powertrain plant at Khed City Phase 1 commissioning planned for H2 FY27; new Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar plant approved with INR 550 crores investment, commissioning by Q2 FY28
items.quote: The construction of the new greenfield facility for our high-voltage EV powertrain components under our subsidiary, Uno Minda Auto Innovations Private Limited is progressing on schedule, with Phase 1 commis sioning planned for the second half of FY27

items.statement: Enabling resolution for INR 2,500 crores fundraising approved, mix of instruments, no specific plan currently
items.quote: So Neel, if that's the only question, I'm assuming, this is only an enabling resolution we take every year. Even last year, we have done it. And this is a mix of all the instruments. It is not necessarily equity. It also covers NCDs and some other borrowings.

items.statement: FY27 iron ore mining guidance of 4-4.25 million tons production, 3.4 million tons net usable for pellets
items.quote: this year, we will be doing about 4 million to 4.25 million tons of iron ore production. And end of Q3, early Q4, we should be able to hit the rated capacity target of 6 million tons.

items.statement: FY27 pellet production guidance of 4 million tons with 3 million tons merchant sales
items.quote: pellet guidance for this year is 4 million tons. The iron ore volume, net usable iron ore for the pellet is at 3.4 million tons.

items.statement: 1 million ton integrated steel plant capex revised to INR 7,000 crores with construction starting October 2026
items.quote: The current CAPEX given as INR 7,000 crores is very much on the practical side. We have done a thorough study with the equipment suppliers and basis that we have shared the details with the stakeholders.

items.statement: 20 GW BESS project first line commissioning by March 2027, 5-6 GW output in FY28, scaling to 17-18 GW by year 3
items.quote: we should be able to commission the first line by end of Q4, which is March '27. So, first year, FY '28, we expect to do a 5 to 6 Gigawatt of output, which is hardly at about 30%-40%. Second year, we want to scale it to about 70%, which is at about 12, 13 Gigawatts, 14 Gigawatts. And from third year onwards, we expect to do about 17, 18 Gigawatts.

items.statement: Iron ore landed cost guidance INR 3,000-3,200/ton for FY27, substantial reduction expected post-monsoon from Q3-Q4
items.quote: this year, the guidance will be in the similar level, which is about INR 3,000-3,200 levels. But Q3-Q4 onwards, we can see a substantial reduction in the pricing of mining.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 prices softened ~10% across supply chain post end of April vs Q4 levels
items.quote: Q1, the pricing was pretty much at the same levels of Q4 for the first half of Q1. But the second half of Q1, say, end of April, early May, the prices have softened a bit almost by 10% across the supply chain.

items.statement: Imported coal prices to increase 15-20% from Q2 FY27 due to freight and currency impact
items.quote: Q2 onwards, because of the war impact, the sea freight has gone up substantially from $15-$16, it is almost crossed $22. Dollar is up from 93-94 levels to 97 levels. So, there is a substantial impact on the imported coal price from Q2 onwards, at least by 15%-20%.

items.statement: Export pellet market being explored as domestic demand weak, delta between domestic and export pricing now <$10/ton
items.quote: today, the Indian prices are about INR 9,500. And with the dollar inflation, today, if you want to export, we can easily achieve more than INR 9,000 ex-plant. So, the delta is now hardly less than $10 between domestic pricing and the export pricing.

items.statement: Transportation cost rising due to diesel escalation, planning EV fleet of 350 trucks (INR 350 cr capex) to reduce costs
items.quote: of iron ore we need to move at the full capacity, we need to deploy more than about 300 trucks or about 350 trucks at the full capacity. Aman Kothari: 300, okay. Abhishek Agrawal: Yes, 350 trucks. So, at a full site CAPEX should be more than about INR 350 crores

items.statement: Solar capacity expansion from 165 MW to 540 MW, 25 MW commissioned recently, additional 100 MW by July 2026
items.quote: In addition to current 165 Megawatt, the company has commissioned solar power capacity of 25 Megawatt yesterday only and additional 100 Megawatt is expected to be commissioned by July '26.

items.statement: Closing order book grew 8% YoY to ₹20.54 billion with export orders contributing 51%
items.quote: The healthy order inflows across the key and high value segments during Q4 FY '26 resulted in our closing outstanding order book increasing by 8% year-on-year to ₹20.54 billion.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 order booking grew 19% YoY to ₹7.54 billion with export orders at record ₹5.16 billion (174% YoY growth)
items.quote: On the order booking front, Q4 FY '26 recorded a 19% year-on-year growth with total order booking of ₹7.54 billion, which is underpinned by traction across both the domestic and international markets and a favourable segment mix.

items.statement: Management expects minimum growth indicated by 9% order book growth, avoids giving direct revenue guidance
items.quote: Well, we shy away from giving direct giving guidance, but what we do have is a growth in the enquiry closing order book by about 9%. And so that gives you an indication of the minimum growth that we would like to anticipate.

items.statement: Enquiry book nearly doubled YoY to ~18 GW for product segment; India enquiry book up ~100% to ~7 GW; North America up ~1000% to ~3 GW
items.quote: The overall order book mix also witnessed a meaningful improvement, supported by a strong scale -up of the aftermarket business, which improved during the year. We're happy to talk about this subsequently in the question-and-answers.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin 24.2%; Q4 margin compression due to lower aftermarket mix (25% vs 33%), strategic NTPC order (~3% PBT), and ₹8.5 crore MTM loss
items.quote: Operationally, we continue to maintain healthy profitability during the year. EBITDA stood at ₹5.27 billion with margins of 24.2%, while profit before tax before exceptional items stood at ₹4.9 billion, which remained broadly stable year -on-year with margins of 22.5%.

items.statement: Commodity price increases (copper, aluminium, steel) mitigated by rate contracts, diversified supplier base, and partial pass-through to customers; no significant margin impact expected
items.quote: We have rate contracts which are long-term. They also insulate us with some of those escalations. Besides when we take particular orders, which are of a large magnitude, we are extra cautious in terms of negotiating very good supplier rates.

items.statement: Export revenue share rose to 58% in FY26 (48% in FY25) and 60% in Q4 FY26; aftermarket declined as % of sales; API expected to revert to 10%+ of order booking and revenue
items.quote: Export revenue remained a key growth driver, increasing 30% year -on-year and contributing 58% of our overall revenue compared to 48% in the previous year. At the same time, Aftermarket as a percentage of sales did decline on a year -on-year basis.

items.statement: Investing significantly more into AI movement to be technologically ready for disruption across industries and markets
items.quote: We will be investing significantly more into the movement into AI. We think that we need to be technologically ready for any disruption that will occur both within industries, within companies as well as in the market in general.

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions (India-Pakistan, West Asia, US tariffs) impacted H1 FY26 order booking and revenue; FY27 expected to be back-ended due to execution profile
items.quote: As I've said in our previous conference calls, we started off the year with the conflict between India and Pakistan, which had an impact not only in terms of order booking, some very large orders which we were anticipating in the API segment, which could have been delivered during the year.

items.statement: US enquiry pipeline driven by data centres (combined cycle), biomass, pulp & paper, geothermal, small modular reactors; conversions delayed by permitting timelines
items.quote: So especially in U.S. demand is coming in addition to the combined cycle applications for the data centres, areas where we are seeing a good traction is biomass plants is one thing. Pulp and paper enquiries are picking up and Geothermal.

items.statement: US subsidiary lost ~₹8 crore in FY26 but Q4 profitable; expects breakeven or positive in FY27, profitability from FY28 with scale and overhead absorption
items.quote: Though the full year itself, as you will see from the annual report when it's out and the subsidiary accounts still had a loss of about ₹8 odd crores in that subsidiary. In the coming year, we anticipate not only for that to reverse, but for it to be profitable.

items.statement: Geothermal and ORC seen as large future markets; CO2 energy storage depends on pilot project validation; MVR/heat pump to remain small but high-margin
items.quote: But when I look forward in terms of in the next couple of years or next three, four years, the Geothermal market will be a large market for us. It will contribute very meaningfully. I think the ORC market will also be large for us.

items.statement: Domestic market grew ~35% in FY26 (~3,400 MW); broad-based across steel, cement, oil & gas, sugar, ethanol, process cogeneration, waste heat recovery
items.quote: Marketwise, domestic market around 35%, it has grown. That is the one data point when it comes to domestic market.

items.statement: Receivables at ₹6.39 billion (84 days vs 49 days) due to March-skewed billing; significant amount already liquidated; FY27 year-end receivables may remain similar due to back-ended execution
items.quote: The average trade receivable days stood at 84 days versus 49 days as of the 31st of March 2025. While we see that this receivable level is high and as I have commented, we believe that this receivable level will significantly be diluted during the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: FY27 expected to be back-ended like FY26; double-digit growth not explicitly guided but minimum growth indicated by 9% order book growth
items.quote: But if you look at it historically, it will again be a back -ended H2 year for us.

items.statement: NTPC strategic order ~2/3 executed at ~3% PBT margin; MTM loss of ₹8.5 crore in Q4 to be adjusted in subsequent quarters
items.quote: We also had a mark-to-market loss given the high volatility of rupee during the end of the quarter, which also led to a recognition of over ₹8.5 crores as a loss on a M2M basis.

items.statement: FY27 gross margin improvement target of 40-50 bps YoY; EBITDA margin improvement target of 50-75 bps YoY
items.value: 40-50 bps gross margin; 50-75 bps EBITDA margin
items.quote: we are anticipating an average 40 to 50 basis point improvement in the gross margin in the next 1 or 2 years, every year. So we remain at that number. So if this year, if all goes well, we should see gross margin improvement of this order. I think slightly more than that 50 to 75 basis point we are targeting that it sh

items.statement: Mid-single-digit revenue growth outlook for FY27; profit growth targeted at close to 10%
items.quote: we're maintaining mid-single-digit growth outlook for the current year and then close to about 10% or so plus broad growth in the profits.

items.statement: Capex during FY26 reduced by more than half compared to FY25, reflecting disciplined capital allocation
items.quote: Capex during the year was almost reduced by more than half compared to FY 2025, reflecting disciplined capital allocation.

items.statement: BCG-led cost transformation (Project PULSE) targeting ₹40-50 crores annual procurement savings and similar opex savings; AI-enabled digital platform being institutionalized
items.value: ₹40-50 crores procurement savings; similar opex savings
items.quote: As I recall, we had foreseen on that annually about ₹40 crores to ₹50 crores, we should be able to save in our procurement and a similar number in our opex as well. So I think we are well on track.

items.statement: Top 10 customers expected to grow 7-8% in FY27; new verticals in North America to drive growth above average
items.quote: across our top 10 clients, we should see growth more in the vicinity of about 7-8%, slightly lower than the average. It is the new verticals that will fire the growth. It is in North America, that would be firing the growth.

items.statement: New vertical investments reduced 27% in FY26 to ~₹120 crores; targeting ₹80 crores in FY27 and ₹50-60 crores recurring annually thereafter
items.quote: We've actually brought it down by 27%, and we had said we will be able to bring it down to about ₹80 crores in FY 2027. We remain positive that we will be able to bring it to ₹80 crores, beyond that ₹50 crores to ₹60 crores every year is going to be a recurring investment.

items.statement: Expects 6-7% tonnage growth in FY27 with at least 2% sequential quarterly growth
items.quote: In terms of volume growth, we are expecting to grow at least around 6% to 7% for the full year basis. And we are expecting that at least around 2% quarterly growth on a sequential basis even for the financial year '27.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 21.4%, down 190bps YoY due to higher lorry hire, salary and maintenance costs
items.quote: On profitability, the EBITDA margin stood at around 21.4%, down by around 190 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: New branches contributed 1-1.5% tonnage in Q4; expects 2-3% from new branches and 4% from existing in FY27
items.quote: on a full year basis, again, we are expecting that if we open gradually of 100 numbers, we're expecting that on a full year basis, these branches may contribute around 2% to 3% in the tonnage.

items.statement: No exposure to bus business; promoter has separate bus company
items.quote: Currently, we are not into bus business. This company is -- the promoter and another company is having the bus business.

items.statement: Western DFC not a risk as commodities carried not linked to railway services
items.quote: DFC is directly related to the full truckload. So, the commodity what we are carrying is not directly linked with the railway services.

items.statement: Targets year-on-year EBITDA growth of over 20% for FY27.
items.quote: So we will be able to maintain year-on-year EBITDA growth of over 20% for FY27.

items.statement: Expects positive headcount on both half-year and full-year basis in FY27.
items.quote: However, on a half year basis as well as a full year basis, we will be positive.

items.statement: Targets bottom-line growth upwards of 20%.
items.quote: And also on the bottom line, we are targeting upwards of 20% growth.

items.statement: Entered FY27 with about 20,000 open positions, 15-20% higher than same point previous quarter.
items.quote: We entered the new fiscal year with about 20,000 open positions.

items.statement: Enterprise segment margin outlook is flattish; relies on operating leverage.
items.quote: And with respect to margins, the outlook is a bit flattish.

items.statement: Received INR180 crore PF demand notice; confident of winning based on legal opinions and NOC.
items.quote: And there is a demand of about INR180 crores pertaining to how the process or the offsetting of profits and loss were done in the PF Trust level.

items.statement: Board approved buyback of up to 25% of free reserves at INR1,600 per share from free cash.
items.quote: On capital allocation, the Board has approved a buyback of up to 25% of free reserves at a price of INR1,600 per share to be funded from our existing free cash.

items.statement: Focus on scaling higher-margin businesses like Specialised Staffing and Degree Apprenticeship.
items.quote: Accelerating the scale of higher-margin businesses, especially TeamLease Digital and our Degree Apprenticeship business is a priority.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected to remain similar to FY26 India capex of ~₹800 crores.
items.quote: We expect capital expenditure in FY 27 to remain similar to FY 26.

items.statement: ABS volumes to grow 100-150% in FY27 vs FY26.
items.quote: So I think the growth can be 100% to 150% compared to last year.

items.statement: AURIC Shendra plant to cross ₹200 crores revenue this year.
items.quote: We are planning to cross ₹ 200 crores this year from AURIC Shendra plant.

items.statement: Driveshaft business to cross ₹100 crores in FY27.
items.quote: With the above, the driveshaft business will cross ₹100 crores in this financial year.

items.statement: Inverted front fork monthly sales to reach 100,000 units by end of FY27.
items.quote: With increasing OEM offtake, we are adding assembly lines which will take our monthly sales of inverted front forks from 60,000 units to 75,000 units per month, by June 2026 and to 100,000 units per month by the end of FY 27.

items.statement: 3W brake assembly volumes to double from 0.6 million to 1.2 million units per annum by end of FY27.
items.quote: We are also progressing with the planned increase in our 3W brake assembly volumes, which will double from 0.6 million to 1.2 million units per annum by end of this year.

items.statement: 4W revenue contribution to reach 10% soon.
items.quote: Our plan is to reach 10% soon, but the question in the 10% is because it may look as a lower number, but the sales in 2W are also growing.

items.statement: ABS capacity expansion of 12 lakh units per annum, SOP September 2026.
items.quote: Work has commenced on this expansion of 12 lakh units per annum, with SOP expected in September 2026.

items.statement: New Chennai disc brake plant capacity: 3 million assemblies and 4 million discs per annum.
items.value: 3 million disc brake assemblies per annum and 4 million discs per annum
items.quote: The Chennai plant will have a capacity of 3 million disc brake assemblies per annum and 4 million discs per annum, which is part of our total 7.6 million disc brake assemblies and 8.6 million brake discs per annum planned at Endurance.

items.statement: AURIC Shendra cumulative orders peak annual business potential ₹513 crores, peak by FY29.
items.quote: Cumulative orders will translate into peak annual business potential of ₹513 crores. These orders are from a large US EV OEM for automotive as well as non-auto applications, from Jaguar Land Rover, as well as from Yazaki and Valeo for electric platforms of Mahindra and Tata Motors. SOP for key programs is expected to b

items.statement: Maxwell cumulative orders won ₹247 crores per annum, peaking in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: At Maxwell, we have won ₹56 crores of new business in FY 26, which has taken the total cumulative orders won to ₹247 crores per annum, which will peak in Q 2 of the next financial year.

items.statement: Electronics division expected to grow around 40% in FY27
items.quote: Continuing the strong growth momentum, this division is expected to grow by around 40% in FY '27.

items.statement: Railway division expected to grow 30% to 35% for both FY27 and FY28
items.quote: backed by strong order book visibility of INR2,600 crores plus and product portfolio expansion, we remain optimistic of division's growth of 30% to 35% for both FY '27 and FY '28.

items.statement: Consolidated margin pressure of 50 to 100 bps expected, temporary in nature
items.quote: To sum up, we expect a margin pressure of 50 to 100 bps at consolidated level, which is of temporary in nature and expected to normalize as macro environment improves.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected around INR1,800-2,000 crores overall, cash outflow INR1,100-1,200 crores
items.quote: So FY '27, we are expecting that one is Ascent and one is the other than Ascent. Ascent will be around INR1200-odd crores, including the capitalized portion out of this INR547 crores. And apart from that, there will be around INR700 crores to INR800 crores capex in all the other entities put together.

items.statement: FY28 cash outflow for capex expected around INR1,400-1,500 crores
items.quote: So it will be same because in '28, our new Ascent-K circuit larger capex will happen. There also we'll have a better -- much larger pay terms from the capex suppliers. So you can expect a similar or a little higher around INR1,400 crores, INR1,500 crores of cash outflow for the capex in terms of cash.

items.statement: Electronics division margins expected in 9.5% to 10% range in FY27
items.quote: And the margins, what we are expecting right now should be in the range of 9.5% to 10% range.

items.statement: Railway division margins expected in 16% to 17% range
items.quote: But the margins in the railway side, we expect in the range of 16% to 17%.

items.statement: Copper clad laminate prices increased more than 60% in last 1 year, still increasing
items.quote: For bare PCB businesses, there has been increase in input cost of copper clad laminate. Prices has increased by more than 60% in last 1 year and still increasing.

items.statement: Gold prices increased approximately 60% in last 1 year, still increasing
items.quote: Gold prices have also increased by approximately 60% in last 1 year and prices still continue to increase.

items.statement: PCB business gets price increases with 2-quarter lag due to Tier 2 position
items.quote: But in the PCB business, we are Tier 2. We don't supply directly to Maruti or Hyundai, we supply to Tier 1 guys, and that's where the inventory has to be taken care at 2 levels. And hence, the lag in the PCB business to increase the cost is about 2 quarters.

items.statement: RAC industry expected to grow 12% to 13% in FY27, Q1 expected around 20% growth
items.quote: On the complete year side, we are estimating a growth of somewhere around 12% to 13% on the complete year.

items.statement: Electronics division revenue mix: PCBA ~INR2,281 crores, PCB ~INR600 crores, Power Electronics & Industrial Automation remainder
items.quote: PCBA is INR2,281 crores, almost INR2,300 crores and then total on the other side is about INR596 crores, which is Power-One, Unitronics and Shogini and Ascent clocks crossed INR402 crores. So almost about INR1,000 crores is the other, out of which if you see Shogini plus PCB will be about INR500 crores -- around INR600 crores is PCB.

items.statement: Minimum wage increased 35% in Haryana and 22% in UP, other states may follow
items.quote: Basically, first factor is the minimum wage increase, which happened of 35% in Haryana, which led to riots in Noida and UP government also in turn increased minimum wages to about 22%.

items.statement: Indian Railway contracts are fixed price with no pass-through mechanism
items.quote: On Indian Railway, contracts are fixed term contracts. They don't negotiate because these are tender documents.

items.statement: Ascent-K Circuits HDI PCB facility construction to commence by June 2026, trial production by Q3 FY28
items.quote: On the way forward, Ascent-K Circuits, HDI PCB manufacturing facility is set to commence its construction by June of '26. With trial production expected by quarter 3 FY '28, this will be a state-of-the-art facility strategically located near new Noida Airport.

items.statement: Targets INR1,500 crores revenue by FY28, driven by 85-90% utilization and special project.
items.quote: we are expecting to utilize our assets by FY '28 by optimal, when we say optimal, 85% to 90% that will drive us. Also in FY '28, the special project where we got the advance which will come in commercial operation. So that will also add to it, and that gives us confidence.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin at least 2-3% higher than FY26, targeting ~20%.
items.quote: we are expecting at least 2%, 3% higher EBITDA compared to the what we had, purely because of the operational efficiencies when we are driving up the utilization beyond 70%, we should able to rationalize a lot of cost.

items.statement: Targets over 75% capacity utilization in FY27, up from ~60% in FY26.
items.quote: we target over 75% utilization in FY '27, supporting EBITDA margin expansion.

items.statement: Expects 35-45% volume growth in FY27.
items.quote: We already said that we will grow by about 15% on capacity utilization and volumes are between 35% to 45%, volume growth also will happen in FY27.

items.statement: Plans INR125 crores capex in FY27, fully funded by internal accruals, at Pakhajan.
items.quote: For FY '27, the company has planned a capex of INR125 crores, which will be completely funded through internal accruals.
