items.statement: Raipur insurance empanelment delays expected to complete next quarter, aiding ramp-up.
items.quote: We expect the empanelment’s to be complete in the next quarter, post which we will see a significant improvement in the numbers as well.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR13,500 crores with EBITDA margin 7-7.5% and PAT margin 4%
items.quote: maintaining a guidance of INR13,500 crores revenue along with an EBITDA margin of 7% to 7.5% and a PAT margin of 4% for FY27

items.statement: Guidance may be updated next quarter depending on market situation
items.quote: However, depending on how the market situation evolves during the ongoing quarter, we will update the guidance if required in the next quarter.

items.statement: Plan to open 5 COCO stores (2 legacy, 3 LiteStyle) and 20 FOCO stores in FY27, all outside Maharashtra
items.quote: So, in our outlook, we have planned for 5 COCO stores, 2 PNG legacy stores and 3 LiteStyle stores. The locations which we are venturing into is in Gurgaon, strengthening our position in Lucknow, and we have also venturing into Gujarat.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 gross margin 9.7%, down 230 bps YoY due to higher gold bars/coins mix, lower studded ratio, and promotional discounts
items.quote: Gross margin stood at 9.7%. The moderation in Q4 FY26 was primarily driven by higher share of gold bars and coins, a lower stud jewellery mix in the overall sales mix, and a target customer acquisition discounts in the new markets and a bit of the gains on the unhedged portion which are coming in the sales.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 gross margin 12%, EBITDA margin 6.6%, PAT margin 3.8%
items.quote: Gross profit grew 83% year-on-year to INR1,302 crores with gross margin expanding by 280 bps to 12% on a yearly level, reflecting structural improvement in the product mix.

items.statement: Gold bars/coins gross margin 0.5-1%, plain gold jewellery 12.5-13%, franchise gross margin 2.5-3%
items.quote: So, the we on the gold bar and coins we operate on a very thin margins in the range of half a percent to 1%. And on the normal jewellery on the gold jewellery which is not studded, which is not non-studded jewellery is in the range of 12% to 13%.

items.statement: Gold bars/coins share 40% in Q4 FY26 (up from 28% YoY), full-year FY26 32%; expect to normalize to ~25% in FY27
items.quote: But I think this year it should again stabilize back to the 25% or even lower levels, and that is what we have been always saying that, you know, this year is going to be a year of a lot of new jewellery being bought using old jewellery and bars and coins as a category this year will see a slowdown.

items.statement: Old gold exchange 40% of business in FY26, targeting 50%+ in FY27; make-to-order 30-35%
items.quote: So old gold today is around 40% of our entire business, and we expecting that this the old gold trend picks up, we should be at around 50% plus, as far as old jewellery to new jewellery is concerned.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 gold volume +27% YoY, silver +37%, diamond +125%; same-store sales growth 86% YoY
items.quote: Despite the sharp run in gold prices, we saw positive traction in volume. Gold grew 27% year-on-year by volume in in Q4, silver volumes rose 37% year-on-year, and diamond volumes rose an exceptional 125% year-on-year.

items.statement: Import duty hike expected to reduce bars/coins demand, shift consumers to jewellery via old gold exchange
items.quote: Import duty hike primarily would have an impact on the bars and coin sale. Like I mentioned before, I - we don't see an impact much on the jewellery side. So, if you look at our business in terms of sales, you know, there'll be a portion of bars and coins which would - which we see a

items.statement: Hedging at 67% in Q4 FY26 (up from 57% YoY), targeting 80% in FY27 to eliminate margin volatility
items.quote: Further, we plan to take it to 80% to remove the complete volatility in the margins.

items.statement: QIP enabling resolution valid till August 2026; promoter shareholding reduction deadline September 2027 (3 years post-listing)
items.quote: See, I mean, in terms of progress, like I said, there is an enabling board resolution which is till end of August. So that is where we are. We haven't really thought on, you know, going ahead on that front at this point of time.

items.statement: Retail revenue target INR9,800 crores in FY27 (23% growth), driven by 5-10% SSSG for mature stores and ramp-up of new stores
items.quote: So, in particular, retail, we have closed down the year at around INR8,000 crores. And the next year targets and the guidance for the retail, which we have taken under in our AOP, is around INR9,800 crores, which is a 23% increase.

items.statement: Non-Maharashtra stores contribute 10% of revenue; make-to-order 22% outside Maharashtra vs 30-32% in Maharashtra
items.quote: make-to-order is a is a little lower there than compared to Maharashtra, but still it's a good proportion, around 22% of the entire sales outside Maharashtra are make-to-order, while in Maharashtra the number is at 30% to 32

items.statement: New stores in UP, Bihar, MP achieving annualized stock turns of 1x in first year vs 0.8x guidance
items.quote: So, like our guidance we had projected around 0.8x stock turn for the year one, so we have we have surpassed the guidance and all the stores in primary UP, Bihar, and MP are doing annualised stock turns of 1x in the first year itself.

items.statement: Plans further capex of INR100 crores in FY27, calibrated to market conditions and EXIM normalization.
items.quote: Seeing better opportunities, our intention is a further capex of INR100 crores in this FY27, which remains linked to strong customer demand and will be calibrated to market conditions as year goes on, including the pace of EXIM normalization.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins to sequentially improve and return to around 7% seen at start of FY25.
items.quote: The EBITDA margins which are 4.6%, 4.7%, we hope to bring it back to where we were starting FY25 which is around almost 7% and even higher the year earlier.

items.statement: Targets debtor days below 120 in the current financial year.
items.quote: We are targeting to bring our debtor days to below 120 in this current financial year.

items.statement: Expects EXIM situation to improve or rationalize within this quarter, with green shoots from this month.
items.quote: My gut feel is that the situation especially in the EXIM side should start improving or rationalizing itself within this quarter.

items.statement: Sees top and bottom line sequentially improving from this quarter, with bottom line recuperating.
items.quote: I feel fairly confident that from here both the top and the bottom line should start showing a sequential improvement.

items.statement: Pivoted EXIM business toward East Coast exports to buffer West Coast disruptions.
items.quote: We've pivoted on our EXIM side more to our East Coast exports to sort of buffer the hits that are happening on the West, that's something we cannot control, but obviously a highly profitable business that we can't do.

items.statement: Domestic volumes expected to rise from this month, driven by Morbi multimodal park and Western seacoast clients.
items.quote: The volumes have been subdued, but we expect it to start rising from this month onwards.

items.statement: Order book remains strong with pedigreed customers; domestic and East Coast EXIM pipelines robust.
items.quote: The order books remain very strong, the domestic pipelines are good and the Exim pipeline especially on the East Coast are very robust.

items.statement: FY26 capex deployed over INR70 crores on specialized containers, handling equipment, and vehicles.
items.quote: Total capex deployed in FY26 was over INR70 crores, including in specialized TEUs, handling equipment such as reach stackers, commercial vehicles, all completely aligned to our customers' requirements and operating needs.

items.statement: Procured 161 specialized containers in FY26; similar orders in pipeline for FY27.
items.quote: Your company procured 161 specialized containers during FY26 and we have similar orders in pipelines for FY27 as well.

items.statement: EXIM volumes fell 11% in Q4 versus 40% industry decline due to Middle East crisis.
items.quote: Luckily for our company, we have been very resilient in this regard, with our EXIM container movement dropping less than 11% compared to the 40% overall.

items.statement: Insurance premiums rose by USD1,200 for 20ft and USD2,400 for 40ft containers; war risk surcharges nearly doubling ocean freight.
items.value: USD1,200 for 20 feet and 2400 USD for 40 feet
items.quote: The war has resulted in insurance premium going up by USD1,200 for 20 feet and 2400 USD for 40 feet in some cases.

items.statement: IPO funds: under INR100 crores still to be deployed; INR92 crores of IPO funds remain for FY27 capex.
items.quote: We used the capex mostly for domestic and this year also the Exim that we've planned is a INR100 crores of which we have INR92 from our IPO funds still to be deployed.

items.statement: Expects FY27 revenue growth >20% on capacity additions and order inflows.
items.quote: We expect revenue to grow by more than 20%, supported by capacity additions and strong order inflows, and increased contribution from high-margin engineered products.

items.statement: Long-term target of INR650+ crore revenue with 15-16% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: Our long-term inspiration remains to build a INR650 crores plus revenue platform with sustainable EBITDA margins in the range of 15% to 16%.

items.statement: No additional capex needed up to INR800-900 crore revenue.
items.quote: I think that the capex that we are doing, the INR100 crores capex that we have indicated should be enough to propel us to INR800 crores to INR900 crores in the coming years.

items.statement: Order book ~INR200 crore as of 30 Apr 2026; 80-90% executable in FY27.
items.quote: Our order book remains healthy at approximately INR200 crores as of 30th April 2026, providing strong visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Passes on raw material price hikes to customers with a lag; fixed-price contracts cause margin fluctuation.
items.quote: Also, the volatility in the raw material prices, we are able to pass it on to the customers for all the subsequent contracts that we are executing for them.

items.statement: No demand slowdown from West Asia crisis; projects not on hold.
items.quote: We don't see any slowdown happening as of now. So, none of the projects have gone under hold.

items.statement: Raw material volatility (tungsten, nickel, cobalt) impacts margins; fixed-price contracts bear brunt.
items.quote: Of course, if the prices go up, we take a margin hit in these contracts. But subsequently, whatever we are quoting for new contracts, the prices go up.

items.statement: Railway developmental orders execution 6-9 months; substantial revenue from next year.
items.quote: So, we expect the execution to take anywhere between, since they are developmental orders, we expect the execution to take anywhere between six to nine months.

items.statement: No revenue from Tejorup (defense) this year or next; prototype development ongoing.
items.quote: I don't think and I don't foresee any revenue coming in from Tejorup in this financial year. And also, I think, nothing significant coming in the next financial year.

items.statement: International sales to grow >20% YoY, targeting 15% of revenue.
items.quote: We expect the international revenue to go up to 15% in the next, in this year and the next year.

items.statement: Debtor days target 80-90 days, inventory days 60-65 days.
items.quote: No, our target would be anywhere between 80 to 90. We are targeting 80 to 85, actually, and inventory days of 60 to 65.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 32,500 crores with 13% overseas component
items.quote: In the overall order book, at this point in time, the overseas component is around 13%.

items.statement: Secured INR 4,125 crores new orders in FY26 plus INR 3,800 crores variation orders
items.quote: Coming to order inflows during the financial year, we secured new orders worth INR 4,125 crores, excluding approximately INR 3,800 crores of variation and change orders received on existing projects.

items.statement: Order booking guidance of INR 30,000 crores for FY27 with INR 15,000 crores already visible
items.quote: Having a certainty of about INR 15,000 crores order including L1 in the current financial year, we expect to book another INR 15,000 crores of more orders, making a total order booking guidance of INR 30,000 crores for the current financial year.

items.statement: No revenue growth or EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 due to geopolitical uncertainty and elongated award cycles
items.quote: At this stage, considering the continued uncertainty in the geopolitical environment, elongated award cycles and ongoing project-related developments, we believe it would be prudent to wait for greater visibility before providing specific revenue growth or EBITDA m argin guidance for FY27

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance of INR 725 crores
items.quote: So, FY27, we are looking at a CAPEX of around INR 725 crores.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin at 11.7% down from 12.8% in FY25
items.quote: For the overall year, the absolute number of EBITDA was INR 1439 crore which is 11.7% as compared to last year's INR 1662 crore which is 12.8%.

items.statement: Q4 provisions of INR 160 crores including ECL matrix change and arbitration provision
items.quote: In Q4, across all projects, we have done a provision close to INR 160-odd crores.

items.statement: FY26 total provisions of INR 325 crores with INR 260-265 crores one-time costs in Q4
items.quote: FY26, the number is close to INR 325 crores.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of INR 4 lakh crores for next two years with 70% domestic and 30% overseas
items.quote: Our bid pipeline remains healthy for the next two years, which we track. It's close to INR 4 lakh crores, which we are tracking across segments, and out of that, 70% is domestic and 30% is from the overseas market.

items.statement: Overseas projects contribute 30% of turnover despite being 13% of order book
items.quote: Even though it is around 13% in the overall order book, but during the year turnover, almost 30% is coming from the overseas market.

items.statement: Payment delays from customers impacted Q4 execution and forced choice between growth and liquidity preservation
items.quote: we decided to balance between funding projects and maintaining liquidity. So, we funded projects up to a limit but we had not gone beyond a point to avoid overexposure to any customer

items.statement: Geopolitical developments and POL supply chain disruptions severely impacted overseas project execution in March
items.quote: After the war, there were Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants (POL) and gas-related issues in projects consumables and logistic-related challenges. Especially, this was in the overseas market which kind of marred the planned progress.

items.statement: Croatia railway rehabilitation project L1 formalities expected to conclude shortly
items.quote: I am pleased to share that we have received a proposal for the rehabilitation and construction of the railway line project in Croatia for which we were declared L1 last year. We expect the related formalities to conclude shortly.

items.statement: Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail C2 project TBM assembly progressing, tunneling to commence before end of next quarter
items.quote: We expect tunneling operations to commence before the end of next quarter.

items.statement: FY26 capex of INR 1,069 crores with INR 700 crores in Q4
items.quote: So, in FY26, we have incurred a CAPEX of INR 1069. And this number was in December, this number was around INR 370 odd crores. So, in Q4, we have done close to INR 700 crores.

items.statement: Management declines to give revenue guidance for FY27 due to long gestation projects and geopolitical uncertainty.
items.quote: Therefore, it is based on the expected order, based on the current order, giving a guidance, especially till uncertainty remains in the geopolitical situation, will be inappropriate

items.statement: Order inflow guidance of INR 30,000 crores for FY27; INR 8,000 crores already received, INR 7,000 crores at L1, balance INR 15,000 crores with visibility.
items.quote: New order inflow, we have indicated INR 30,000 crores, out of which we have already received INR 8,000 crores and another about INR 7,000 crores were L1 and further INR 15,000 crores.

items.statement: Confirmed INR 8,000 crores orders comprise INR 373 crores DMRC and INR 7,544 crores Croatia; Croatia not yet in order book.
items.quote: INR 373 crores of DMRC and INR 7,544 of Croatia are the orders in that INR 8,000.

items.statement: L1 orders include Vadhvan Port ~INR 5,300 crores and one other project making up ~INR 15,000 crores L1 total.
items.quote: Another two orders were only L1, where Vadhvan is the public knowledge and it's around INR 5,300 crores. There is one more job where we are L1, which is the rest of the amount.

items.statement: FY27 depreciation similar to FY26 plus incremental from ~INR 1,000 crores TBM capex additions.
items.quote: FY27, it will be the similar number, maybe marginally it will be up from because you yourself have said that these CAPEX, whatever TBM, we have added INR 1000 odd crore.

items.statement: Domestic projects have escalation formulas covering cost increases (90% to >100%); international mostly fixed-price but Croatia has pass-through beyond 10% cost increase.
items.quote: All our domestic projects have an escalation formula. The formula could vary from customer-to-customer, but it has got an escalation formula consisting of steel, cement, labor, fuel, other factors, and all that.

items.statement: Receivables elevated at 143 days; targeting ~120 days by unlocking ~INR 1,000 crores stuck payments before June.
items.quote: We are looking at those liquidation, maybe say by June, we should see a sizable liquidation in the range of say INR 1000 odd crores.

items.statement: Collection issues widespread across government projects (central and state); UP Jal Jeevan Mission and Gabon specifically cited.
items.quote: Specific project, if we have to talk about, we have already talked about UP Jal Jeevan Mission Project and we have tried to explain that there, contrary to the contract condition, the customer has taken a stand that whoever is completing the final connection

items.statement: Debt to drop sizably in FY27; gross debt/equity ~0.65x, net debt/equity <0.5x; targeting FY25 levels.
items.quote: But one thing for sure we can tell you that for this financial year FY27, we will see a sizable drop in the debt number. And that's what we have stated also that debt, we have al ways tried to maintain it at a level which is comfo rtable to

items.statement: Gabon bank guarantee invoked; project 92% complete, no margin recognized, expenses fully provided.
items.quote: Gabon, so, Gabon, we have already paid that bank guarantee invocation. And in that contract, anyways, we were not recognizing any margin and whatever was to be provided, we have already provided for the expenses.

items.statement: Minimum wage and Labor Code increases already factored; labor availability issues but no protests at sites.
items.quote: Whatever minimum wages and Labor Code related increases, we have already factored all that. So, we are going ahead as per the revised code.

items.statement: Croatia railway project funding fully approved by ECB; road projects cancelled due to bids 20-45% above estimates.
items.quote: ECB has already approved the entire amount, and funds are already there with them. Therefore, we don't find any issues.

items.statement: Pune Ring Road rebid expected in current quarter (by June); Nagpur-Gondia rebid timing depends on land acquisition.
items.quote: We expect Pune Ring Road could come for bidding in the current quarter itself towards the June or so, because Pune Ring Road, the land acquisition is almost completed.

items.statement: Arbitration interest income INR 19 crores, other interest INR 61 crores in FY26 other income of INR 374 crores.
items.quote: So, that is the arbitration interest is INR 19 crore and other interest is INR 61 crores.

items.statement: Expects to end FY27 with over 1 million sq ft operational area.
items.value: more than a million operational area
items.quote: So all these center, all these signed off centres and the additional centres that we are signing off will be developed and we will be ending the year with more than a million operational area.

items.statement: Managed office share to rise to 70% of portfolio, co-working 30%.
items.quote: I think will be 70% managed office and 30% of the co-working, which over a period of next three to four years will come down to 90% of managed office and 10% of co-working.

items.statement: Managed office growing at 30-40% annually vs co-working at 10%.
items.quote: So probably in co-working, we are growing at the rate of 10% every year, but in managed office, we are growing at the rate of 30, 40% per year.

items.statement: FY27 will see significant growth; full benefit of 10 lakh sq ft in FY28.
items.quote: So all this leads to not all 10 lakh contributing to the revenue in financial year 27, but you will get the benefit of these 10 lakh square feet in the financial year, 27, 28 entirely.

items.statement: Plans to sustain current growth momentum for at least five years.
items.quote: We have an internal plan which we intend to implement and this kind of growth momentum. we want to sustain for at least this five-year period that you have mentioned.

items.statement: Will convert accounts to Ind AS in FY27.
items.quote: We are going to soon getting our accounts converted to index in this financial year itself.

items.statement: Expects to enroll first GCC client very soon; participating in RFPs.
items.quote: We have been getting a lot of requirements and recently we have started participating in the RFPs as well. And if everything goes the way it is going, we will be enrolling the first GCC client with us very, very soon.

items.statement: Co-working ~30% margin, managed ~25%, back-to-back ~20%.
items.quote: Even if that matters, that maybe the coworking has a profit percentage of near about 30%. I'm just quotin g an example, not in real terms. Managed office will have a profit percentage of maybe 25%. And when we'll talk about back -to-back, that will have a profit percentage of maybe 20%.

items.statement: No dynamic pricing; manual pricing to achieve 85-95% occupancy.
items.quote: We cannot do automation in terms of pricing and dynamic pricing. But yes, from the launch of the centre to getting a certain percentage of occupancy, we have a little bit of variation and probably, you know, those lucrative pricing.

items.statement: Industry is commodity-like; scale needed to survive consolidation.
items.quote: But this is a commodity business. And if you don't become very big, very fast in a commodity business, it is very, very less probable to sustain and survive in the market.

items.statement: Aims to be one of the biggest in next three years.
items.quote: We will be one of the biggest in next three years. That is what I can assure you today.

items.statement: Plans to expand into Bangalore, Pune, and Hyderabad.
items.quote: similar kind of strategy we are going to replicate in cities like Bangalore, Pune and Hyderabad to have the similar kind of impact that we have in NCR market now.

items.statement: New centers take 3 months to set up, 6 months to stabilize.
items.quote: It's a 3 months investment cycle for establishing the center . Prior to that, we do the design and the development of the concept. And once the centre is ready, let's say after the end of second month, We start marketing the center

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected early to mid-teens, double-digit.
items.quote: Yes, early to mid-teens. Now coming to the FY31, look, our FY31 goal was INR 8400 crores, of which we had highlighted that about 1700 crores will come from inorganic route.

items.statement: 100 bps EBITDA margin expansion by exit FY27.
items.quote: We are looking at a strong 100-basis point expansion by the time we exit FY27.

items.statement: FY31 revenue target INR 8,400 crores (~USD 1 billion), 14-15% organic CAGR.
items.quote: We have built a resilient foundation aligned tightly with our “3x3 Strategy” to scale to USD 1 billion, or approximately INR 8,400 crores, by FY31 and we are exiting the year with powerful momentum.

items.statement: FY27 cash deployment ~INR 100 crores, INR 70-80 crores maintenance capex, INR 15-20 crores leasehold.
items.quote: So, we have typically around INR 100 crores of cash deployment, typically around INR 70-80 crores into my maintenance CAPEX. And typically, this year, like this year, and FY26-27, we have two large leasehold premises, which we are also moving into. So, around 15-20 crores into that.

items.statement: Q4 TCV bookings INR 620 crores, second consecutive 600+ quarter.
items.quote: Our commercial engine is firing on all cylinders. Sales momentum remained exceptionally healthy in Q4, with TCV bookings of INR 620 crores. This marks our second consecutive quarter of 600-plus TCV, providing us with high revenue visibility heading into the new fiscal year.

items.statement: FY26 TCV bookings INR 2,355 crores, 114 new logos added.
items.quote: For the full year, TCV bookings stood at INR 2,355 crores, with 114 new logos added during FY26.

items.statement: Tech and Digital revenue grew 27.2% YoY to INR 249 crores, 31% of total.
items.quote: Our Tech and Digital revenues climbed 5.8% quarter-on-quarter and 27.2% year- on- year to INR 249 crores. This segment now accounts for 31% of our total revenue mix up from previous quarters, proving our rapid transition to higher-value technology-led services.

items.statement: International revenue grew 16.4% YoY to INR 304 crores, 38.1% of total.
items.quote: Our international footprint expanded 4.3% sequentially and 16. 4% year -on-year to INR 304 crores, lifting our international mix to 38.1% of revenue.

items.statement: Healthcare vertical targeted to be 12-15% of revenue by FY31, $120-150 million.
items.quote: By 2031, we believe that healthcare will be 12 to 15 % of our revenue mix. So, that means we are looking at about $120 to $150 million.

items.statement: Wage code compliance absorbed INR 4 crores one-time impact in Q4, no margin compression.
items.quote: Importantly, this is after absorbing approximately INR 4 crores of one-time impact from the implementation of the new wage code.

items.statement: Evaluating six acquisition targets, two advanced, hopeful of at least one acquisition this year.
items.quote: In fact, as we speak, we are evaluating about six potential targets, two at an advanced stage. But given that we are a value investor, whatever acquisition that we make will have to pass through the lens of our value thesis. We are hopeful that this year we will be able to make at least one acquisition.

items.statement: Steady-state depreciation guided at ~INR 60 crores quarterly.
items.quote: Overall depreciation, if that was the question, they take around INR 60 odd crores.

items.statement: Normalized OCF conversion target ~70% of EBITDA.
items.quote: But on an overall basis, you should assume around 70% of cash conversion from the EBITDA.

items.statement: FY26 adjusted PAT margin 2.3%, baseline for future improvement.
items.quote: After adjusting for exceptional items of 65 crores relating to demerger-related costs, the new Labor Code for the past service cost and the wage restructuring impact, the FY26 adjusted PAT margins to 2.3%.

items.statement: Organic revenue growth guidance for FY27 is 15-16%.
items.quote: So organic growth in terms of revenue our guidance is 15% to 16%.

items.statement: Organic EBITDA margin expected around 4% in FY27.
items.quote: Organically, we've touched 4% EBITDA. So that's the range of EBITDA that we want to be from an organic businesses.

items.statement: With acquisitions, EBITDA margin to jump to 5%.
items.quote: With these two acquisitions, the EBITDA margins jump from 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Inorganic revenue addition of INR 800 crores annualized from acquisitions.
items.quote: And to top it up, another INR 800 crores comes from the inorganic route.

items.statement: Expect to cross INR 100 crores PAT with acquisitions integrated.
items.quote: we should cross on an annualized basis a INR 100 crores PAT company with both these acquisitions integrated well.

items.statement: foundit to achieve EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27.
items.quote: we are on that trajectory of an internally aligned of taking the company to a EBITDA break-even company by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: STEAG acquisition enterprise value INR 180 crores, with INR 140 crores cash.
items.quote: STEAG acquisition, we're going to pay enterprise value of INR 180 crores. We got almost INR 140 crores of cash in the business.

items.statement: FY26 secured 164 new contracts with ACV INR 459 crores.
items.quote: In FY26, we have secured new 164 contracts with a total annual contract value of INR 459 crores.

items.statement: STEAG to add 90-100 bps to pro forma EBITDA margins.
items.quote: the acquisitions of STEAG India is expected to add nearly 20% to our top line and improve our pro forma EBITDA margins for the year by approximately 90 basis to 100 basis points.

items.statement: LSG Sky Chefs has mid-to-high teens EBITDA margins.
items.quote: EBITDA margins of this business are in mid -to-high-teens, which would augment our margins further.

items.statement: Telecom segment growth muted due to delayed capex by operators.
items.quote: the overall segment growth was muted due to delay in planned capital expenditure from leading telecom operators

items.statement: Post-acquisition, high-margin telecom and industrial share to rise from 19% to 33%.
items.quote: Post-acquisition, the share of our high margin telecom and industrial verticals would grow from 19% to 33% of revenues.

items.statement: Q1 seasonally soft for food and telecom due to summer holidays.
items.quote: Quarter ones would be an exception, because two of our high-margin businesses, which is food and telecom, have a seasonality effect in quarter ones.

items.statement: STEAG acquisition funded primarily through debt and internal accruals.
items.quote: We plan to fund this acquisition primarily through debt and internal accruals.

items.statement: Management aspires to deliver around 20% revenue growth long-term but refrains from giving specific FY27 guidance.
items.quote: Historically, if you look at it last 10 years, our revenue growth has been around 20% level. Even when we started last year, we said that we'll be delivering about 20%, but then the course-corrected and then we delivered about 15% revenue growth.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain EBITDA margins in the 38-40% range going forward.
items.quote: We've delivered so far, and we'll continue to deliver those numbers going forward as well.

items.statement: Unit 4 Phase 1 capex of ~Rs 1,200 crores across FY27 and FY28, aiming completion by March 2028.
items.quote: In Phase 1 of that expansion, and we are looking at investing almost about Rs. 1,200 odd crores across two years, this year FY27 and in FY28. We aim to complete the Phase 1 expansion by March '28 financial year.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at roughly Rs 700 crores, FY28 at ~Rs 500 crores.
items.quote: Roughly about Rs. 700 crores and then post that will be about Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: No order book concept in specialty ingredients; it is a flow business. CRDMO has dedicated manufacturing with lead times.
items.quote: We don't have order book sort of a concept in specialty ingredients, because we manufacture and then we try to sell to the customers who are already taking the product across multiple geographies and across multiple product categories.

items.statement: Backward integration of an intermediate improved material margins in Q3/Q4 FY26.
items.quote: That integration is complete. We source the raw material, manufacture the intermediates, manufacture the API and supply to the customer, and we are not reliant on any external source. The backward integration had helped us in terms of improving our material margins, which has moved up over Q3 and Q4 of last year.

items.statement: Destocking largely behind; customers now restocking, expected positive impact on top and bottom line.
items.quote: The destocking that had to happen has already happened. So, this year, everything will be in the positive territory, they are restocking now. That part is behind us.

items.statement: Biotech funding recovered ~50% YoY in first four months; early-stage project inquiries increasing.
items.quote: Biotech funding has been recovering, and I think till about April, the four months, it's gone up by about 50-odd percent YoY. So, there's a recovery, which has happened on the biotech funding side, and we are also seeing that with respect to the requests, which is coming in on the early-stage development projects.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Commercial ~60%, Late-stage/Phase 3 ~14%, R&D ~8-9%, Specialty Ingredients ~17%.
items.quote: Commercial is about 60% and 14%. R&D is about 8 % to 9% of our business, and the balance is specialty ingredients. Specialty ingredients is about 17% of our business. That's the breakdown.

items.statement: Phase 3 pipeline stands at 10 molecules, all from emerging biotech, mixed across ADC, peptides, oligos, biotransformation.
items.quote: In terms of the additions, which have happened in Phase 3, all of them are non-lateral. These are molecules where we were working with them on early Phase 2, and they have moved to Phase 3. All of them are emerging biotech.

items.statement: Four molecules commercialized in FY26; three launched by biotechs, one with big pharma; current contribution ~8-9% of revenue.
items.quote: Ballpark, the current contribution from these four molecules will be in the range of closer to about 8% to 9% of our revenues. So, when I talked about commercial molecules being about 60% of our revenues, 8 odd percentage ballpark will be from these new molecules, which had been launched.

items.statement: No impact from US pharma tariffs; big pharma have separate arrangements, biotechs taking it with equanimity.
items.quote: No, it hasn't had any impact on us. If you look at the nature of our business, most of our commercial products are with the big pharma, and they have entered into separate arrangements with respect to the tariff part with the administration.

items.statement: AI seen as aid in discovery and route optimization; manufacturing (83% of business) remains protected but AI may optimize plants.
items.quote: But at the end of the day, somebody has to get into the plant and manufacture, and that's 83% of our business, it's a very high percentage of our business. We feel that we are a little protected, manufacturing still has to be done. But there are areas where it will start to optimize your plants with better use of AI.

items.statement: Unit 4 Phase 1 adds ~365 KL custom synthesis and 100 KL fermentation, doubling custom synthesis and adding 50% fermentation capacity.
items.value: 365 kiloliters custom synthesis and 100 kiloliters fermentation
items.quote: This will add close to about 365 kiloliters of custom synthesis capacity and 100 kilolite rs of fermentation vis-à-vis our current capacity which is 425 kiloliters custom synthesis and 180 kiloliters fermentation. We are more or less doubling on custom synthesis and adding 50% more on the fermentation side

items.statement: Unit 3 now fully operational; expected to turn positive territory in FY27.
items.quote: Unit 3 is already turning around and it's going to be in the positive territory this year.

items.statement: Actively scouting acquisitions in India and abroad but will only pursue right asset at right quality.
items.quote: We are actively searching. Unfortunately, we haven't come across the right candidate, and I've said this ad nauseam and I'll repeat it again, we will not do an acquisition for the sake of an acquisition. It has to make sense and it must be the right asset.

items.statement: Targets INR1,000 crores revenue by FY28; FY27 will be a significant step.
items.quote: Our target of INR1,000 crores revenue by financial year '28 is firmly on track. Financial year '27 will be a significant and visible step towards that milestone.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR600 crores is achievable.
items.quote: Yes, it is very much achievable. We are on line.

items.statement: Current unexecuted order book stands at INR825 crores.
items.quote: Our order book as of now stands around INR825 crores and we have already participated on the various other tenders whereby we expect some reasonable and sizeable orders to come in during the course of this year.

items.statement: Tenders under evaluation worth INR1,225 crores; expected order inflow INR200-300 crores.
items.quote: The total tenders which are at various stages of evaluation is around INR1,225 crores. Over and above and our strike rate somewhere goes around 20% to it stays between 20% to 30%. So we can say around 200 to 300 out of these we are going to book.

items.statement: INR3,000 crores of tenders identified for bidding in next two months.
items.quote: And around INR3,000 odd tenders we have already identified for which bidding, bid preparation is undergoing and we will be bidding in a month or in next two months.

items.statement: Confident of maintaining FY26 margins in FY27.
items.quote: We are very much confident of maintaining the same.

items.statement: FPI business has better margins than EPC; higher FPI share improves consolidated margins.
items.quote: Yes, you are very right. FPI, the more is the contribution from FPI, the better will be the margins.

items.statement: Targets FPI to contribute ~10% of total revenue, possibly more by FY28.
items.quote: Yes, we are very much hopeful that the contribution in FY '28 may be even better than 10%.

items.statement: No fund-raising planned; arranging INR300-350 crores credit lines for FY28 growth.
items.quote: We are for INR1,000 crores, we are making arrangements for a credit limit of around INR300 crores, INR300 crores to INR350 crores, mix of both fund-based and non-fund-based.

items.statement: No immediate fund-raising plans; may explore if valuations are good.
items.quote: As on date, we do not envisage any need of raising any funds from the market. But again, now if there is some very good decent valuation and if it is in the interest of stakeholders, definitely we can explore.

items.statement: Majority of orders have price variation clause, protecting against commodity price fluctuations.
items.quote: Yes, Deepak, majority of our orders are with price variation clause. Like if there is any change in the commodity prices, the same gets, you know, passed on to the customer.

items.statement: Expects at least one large SCADA-type project order in FY27.
items.quote: But yes, in this financial year, we expect similar such project, at least one similar such project in this financial year.

items.quote: Now we are working on, you know, making some arrangements and doing some things so that we can avoid this concentration of revenues in the last month of the year.

items.statement: Compact FPI to be launched by Q2 FY27.
items.quote: Latest by Q2, we will be able to, you know, launch this FPI into the market.

items.statement: Targets 60-70% CAGR revenue growth in FY27 and subsequent years
items.quote: In the medium term, we are confident to achieve 60% to 70% CAGR growth in the upcoming financial year, that is FY 2026-27, and relatively the next years as well.

items.statement: Aims to maintain Q4 FY26 EBITDA ~35% and PAT ~20-23% margins in FY27
items.quote: So, for the next financial year, FY2026-27, we are trying to continue with the Q4 performance. So, the PAT that we have achieved in the Q4 was between 20% to 23%, I guess, and then EBITDA was approximately 35%. So, we are trying to maintain the same values in the upcoming year.

items.quote: Today, across our structural and architectural business segments, our current active order book stands at approximately Rs. 25 crores.

items.quote: So usually, our order book keeps building throughout the year. So, it's not like at the start of the year, but every month we have added almost Rs. 4 crores to Rs. 5 crores of order book in the last year.

items.quote: Now what we are targeting is $45 to $60 per hour even. And that's why we are optimistic that going forward our project prices will increase comparatively.

items.quote: Now we have added architectural design as well as interior design, both the services into our existing portfolio.

items.quote: We have taken deviation in the object issue from office buying office premises. So, Rs. 5 crores we have made provision for this kind of acquisitions only.

items.quote: There has been no change into our business so far. There was a critical situation in last few months globally, but that has not impacted in any sense to our business.

items.quote: We would anticipate that going forward there will be much larger offtake of machines. Much more offtake of machines. And we have even said that almost 24 months since the slowdown has happened in textile. This is something which we were looking forward to.

items.quote: I would say we would see a net interest cost of not more than INR 70-odd crores for the full financial year.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 15.5-16.5%, may restore to 16.5-17.5% if global uncertainties cease.
items.quote: Considering the current situation, the EBITDA guidance for the full financial year '26, '27 will be in the range of 15.5% to 16.5%. However, if the global uncertainties cease over the next few weeks, a couple of months, the guidance will be restored to 16.5% to 17.5%.

items.statement: 20% revenue growth guidance for next 2 years, backed by order book.
items.quote: Over the next 2 years, we are seeing that -- we are giving a guidance of 20% revenue growth year-on-year. And the order book, which currently company has, completely backs up this guidance with some headroom for betterment.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow target INR4,500-5,000 crores, well on track.
items.quote: I'll give you a range of INR4,500 crores to INR5,000 crores, and we are well on track to achieve that.

items.statement: FY27 capex target ~INR165 crores mainly for aluminum formwork and jump-form.
items.quote: For the current financial year, our target towards capex, mainly coming from aluminum formwork, jump-form will be close to about INR165 crores.

items.statement: FY27 target to realize INR50 crores from sale of noncore assets.
items.quote: The company is expected to realize INR50 crores in FY '27 from sale of noncore assets.

items.statement: FY27 revenue from CIDCO expected INR500-600 crores, MHADA INR350-400 crores.
items.value: INR500 crores to INR600 crores; INR350 crores to INR400 crores
items.quote: We should be close to INR500 crores to INR600 crores in CIDCO, and we should be close to INR350 crores to INR400 crores in MHADA.

items.statement: FY26 revenue loss ~INR125 crores due to labor migration and environmental issues.
items.quote: In the whole of financial year, it will be about INR125 crores.

items.statement: Net debt currently less than INR170 crores, reduction to continue over next 2 years.
items.quote: So, the net debt is approximately as on today, as I speak to you, less than INR170 crores.

items.statement: Order book standalone INR13,498 crores as of March 31, 2026; public 57%, private 43%.
items.quote: Order book on standalone basis stood at INR13,498 crores as on 31st March '26. Public sector accounts for 57%, while private sector accounts for 43% of the total order book.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow expected: Q1 >INR1,000 crores, Q2 similar, Q3+Q4 INR2,500-3,000 crores.
items.value: INR1,000 crores; INR2,500 crores to INR3,000 crores
items.quote: We do expect in the quarter 1 orders closed in excess of about INR1,000 crores. Quarter 2 will be a similar number. Quarter 3 and quarter 4 will be about INR3,000 crores, so between INR2,500 crores to INR3,000 crores, thereby -- which we will be achieving the full year guidance of about INR4,500 crores to INR5,000 cror

items.statement: Targets INR500 crores revenue, requiring over 30% growth over next 4-5 years.
items.quote: In short, the target is INR500 crores, and we feel we are getting into a position with our new products also getting accepted in the market to grow at a higher rate compared to our previous few years where we grew in the mid-20s.

items.statement: SaaS business targeting approximately 35% ARR growth.
items.quote: For our SaaS business, we are targeting an ARR growth rate of approximately 35% and we expect the SupTech business with a combination of one-time revenues plus recurring revenues to move a at a lower rate, but there could be surprises as we go forward.

items.statement: SupTech business expected to grow at lower rate than SaaS, with possible lumpy revenues.
items.quote: And we see the SupTech platform going at a good clip, may not be matching the SaaS growth revenues. But here, there is the possibility of getting lumpy revenues as well.

items.statement: Aims to remain EBITDA positive while growing business, balancing customer acquisition costs with SupTech profits.
items.quote: We don't want to be doing this in EBITDA negative mode. We want to make sure that we remain EBITDA positive and still grow the business.

items.statement: Sales and marketing spend at 1.1-1.2x net ARR, may increase slightly but not indiscriminately.
items.quote: We are at about 1.1, 1.2 levels. We might go a little higher than that, but we don't want to be spending indiscriminately.

items.statement: Prolonged Middle East crisis could delay SupTech pipeline, potential impact post June.
items.quote: It is possible that a prolonged Middle East crisis might have a possible adverse impact on the SupTech pipeline. Having said that, so far, we have not seen any indications along these lines, but it will be fair to factor in this possibility if the crisis goes well beyond the first quarter of this financial year.

items.statement: SaaS business predominantly Europe and U.S. focused, sees no significant impact from Middle East crisis.
items.quote: On the SaaS business part, which is enterprise-oriented business, we don't see much of an impact, because our SaaS business is predominantly Europe and U.S. focused and to some smaller extent, India as well.

items.statement: Expanding SupTech product suite with risk-based supervision, licensing, and decision management modules.
items.quote: We are also expanding this product suite to offer more end-to-end features for the regulatory customers, which include risk-based supervision, licensing and decision management and a few other modules as well.

items.statement: Cash at INR155 crores, net worth INR200 crores, book value INR98 post TaxTech divestment.
items.quote: Post the TaxTech divestment, our balance sheet has strengthened considerably and cash right now in the books is at around INR155 crores as on March 31st, while the net worth has moved to INR200 crores from INR76 crores as at March 31st, 2025, and the book value has gone up as well to about INR98 from INR37.

items.statement: DataTech business spun off into subsidiary for sharper focus.
items.quote: Now, we also mentioned in our press release that our fledgling DataTech business, we have spun off in the subsidiary to give it sharper focus.

items.statement: MSME loan facilitation pilot started February, 3 lenders onboarded, early stage.
items.quote: The loan facilitation we have rolled out starting from February on a pilot basis. Now we are slowly increasing the number of lenders, and we are also reaching out to MSMEs in a calibrated fashion.

items.statement: Internal target for MSME monetization earlier than a couple of years.
items.quote: Our internal target is a little bit earlier than that.

items.statement: Days receivable comfortable at 75-80 days, may improve with enterprise SaaS growth.
items.quote: Yes. I would say that 75 to 80 days is what we would be comfortable. But if the enterprise SaaS revenues really gallop going forward, it could further improve, but we need to wait for that.

items.statement: Exploring inorganic opportunities in adjacencies to enhance RegTech footprint, disciplined approach.
items.quote: We'll be open to evaluating opportunities, particularly in adjacencies that could enhance our RegTech footprint. Early days, but we are just on a wait-and-watch mode, even now.

items.statement: Standalone revenue guidance for FY27 is INR 875-950 crore excluding battery chemicals
items.quote: We remain confident of achieving revenues in the range of INR 875 to INR 950 crore in FY27 on a standalone basis, considering full production from MPP-5 from Q2 FY26 onwards.

items.statement: Battery chemicals revenue guidance for FY27 is INR 300 crore plus, mostly in H2
items.quote: The electrolyte salt and electrolyte, the Neogen Ionics revenue potential we had mentioned last year to be INR 300 crore plus. The same remains the current guidance also.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue target for FY29 is INR 3,700-4,200 crore
items.quote: With the existing capacity, we can have revenue of around INR 3,700 to INR 4,200 crore plus based on the projections which we have made till now.

items.statement: Dahej Phase 1 budgeted at INR 428 crore, completion by February 2027; Pakhajan Phase 2 revised cost INR 1,367 crore, completion by March 2027
items.quote: Under this updated schedule, the Dahej Phase 1 project is budgeted at INR 428 crore and is firmly on track for completion by February 2027. Concurrently, the revised cost for Pakhajan Phase 2 stands at INR 1,367 crore and expected completion is by March 2027.

items.statement: FY27 capex outflow expected around INR 800 crore including balance battery capex and standalone
items.quote: FY27 we would complete with the balance CAPEX which could be around INR 600 crore/INR 700 crore. Plus maybe about INR 100-odd crore in Neogen. So, total together at around INR 800 crore.

items.statement: Three US electrolyte makers completed site audits, awaiting final commercial clearances; provisional approvals from additional global customers for lithium electrolyte salts
items.quote: Encouragingly, we have received provisional approval from additional global customers for lithium electrolyte salts, while final site audits for multiple US-based electrolyte makers have also been completed and are currently awaiting final commercial clearances.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin sustained at 17.8% in Q4 FY26 despite expansion overheads and supply chain disruptions
items.quote: EBITDA margin sustained at 17.8% despite expansion-related overheads, geopolitical-led supply chain disruptions, and temporary costs associated with the Dahej replacement facility and toll manufacturing arrangements.

items.statement: Strategic pass-through mechanism protected core profitability despite elevated input costs including packaging and logistics
items.quote: While input costs, including packaging material and logistics-related expenses, remained elevated during the quarter, our strategic pass-through mechanism helped protect our core profitability.

items.statement: Improving demand visibility for India's giga-scale ACC battery ecosystem and strong international interest for non-FEOC compliant supply chain
items.quote: We continue to witness improving demand visibility for India's giga-scale ACC battery manufacturing ecosystem, alongside strong international interest for non-FEOC compliant supply chain.

items.statement: Organic Chemicals revenue split: bromine derivatives 40-45%, advanced intermediates 30%, organolithium and lithium balance
items.quote: I think bromine derivatives was about 40-45% of the revenue. The advanced intermediates was about 30% of the revenue. The organolithium and lithium together were the balance.

items.statement: ROCE target for battery materials projects maintained at 18-20% despite revised capex
items.quote: So, when we put together the revised model also, the return remains at 18% to 20% - 20% being the base target on the salt side and with electrolyte, as I said, we are finalizing it, but effectively we should be targeting 18% to 20% ROCE, even after the revised capex.

items.statement: Gross block for Neogen Ionics expected at INR 1,700-1,800 crore by end of FY27; standalone gross block INR 450-550 crore
items.quote: gross block of Neogen Ionics would be around INR 1,700 crore to INR 1,800 crore at the end of FY27 as most of the CAPEX will be completed. Rohit Nagraj: And for standalone, and on a consolidated basis? Dr. Harin Kanani: Gopi, standalone would be like somewhere around INR 450 crore to 550 crore

items.statement: Peak debt expected to remain unchanged despite capex increase due to promoter equity and Morita JV funding
items.quote: Since we have already raised INR 160 crore equity which has come in from the promoter as well as $20 million from our JV partner which was not factored in during the initial discussion, the peak debt will not change. Will remain the same as earlier.

items.statement: Expect revenue growth in low to mid-teens for FY27 supported by OSAM full-year contribution, Africa trajectory, and 8-9% organic India growth
items.quote: We expect revenue growth to be in the low to mid -teens, supported by OSAM's full year contribution, Africa continuing on its current trajectory, and an 8% to 9% organic growth in our India business.

items.statement: Expect gradual gross margin recovery of 50 to 100 basis points over FY26 levels as procurement normalizes and pricing actions take effect
items.quote: are expecting a gradual gross margin recovery of 50 to 100 basis points over FY26 levels as procurement normalizes and our pricing actions take effect

items.statement: Maharashtra project expected to start commercial operations by end of FY27 with INR106 crores deployed cumulatively across FY25 and FY26 against total project envelope of INR280 crores
items.quote: Our Maharashtra project is progressing as per the scheduled timelines and is expected to start commercial operations by the end of FY27. The work is under progress and INR106 crore s worth of capex has already been deployed cumulatively across '25 and '26.

items.statement: Uganda greenfield expansion on 70 acres with total capex budgeted around INR60 crores including land and plant to be completed by year-end 2029
items.quote: On the Uganda expansion plan, we acquired 70 acres of land parcel for a greenfield expansion. Total capex budgeted for this project is currently around INR60 crore s, including land as well as the plant. It will be executed in a phased manner and will be completed by year-end of '29.

items.statement: FY27 capex projected at INR130 crores standalone plus INR180 crores for Maharashtra project
items.quote: Management: Maharashtra out of INR280 crores, INR20 crores we have spent in FY25, INR86 crores we spent in FY26 and balance INR180 crores we're planned to spend in FY27.

items.statement: Africa business targeting 15% to 18% of consolidated revenue by FY28 supported by Phase 2 expansion in Uganda
items.quote: We see Africa scaling towards 15% to 18% of consolidated revenue by FY28, supported by a Phase 2 expansion in Uganda, which will include pasteurized milk and milk products that will be sold in Uganda.

items.statement: Targeting VAP contribution closer to 32% to 34% driven by curd, paneer, and ice cream once planned expansion stabilizes
items.quote: Once our planned expansion fully stabilizes, our planned expansion directionally we are confident that the VAP mix will improve further. This growth will be delivered by curd, paneer, and ice cream, and broadly we are targeting closer to 32% to 34% in terms of VAP contribution.

items.statement: Average procurement cost in Q4 FY26 was INR41 per liter vs INR38.7 previous quarter and INR37.4 in Q4 FY25; average milk sales price was INR58.4 per liter vs INR57.7 previous quarter
items.value: INR41 per liter procurement, INR58.4 per liter sales
items.quote: The average procurement cost in Q4 FY26 stood at INR41 per liter as against INR38.7 per liter in the previous quarter and INR37.4 per liter in Q4 FY25. However, we did not entirely pass on this increase in cost to the consumers. Our average milk sales price for the quarter stood at INR58.4 per liter, which was INR57.7 per liter in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Packaging material costs increased 30% year-on-year; fuel price increase of INR3 per liter currently being absorbed with 0.25% margin impact
items.quote: So I think packaging material as a number has gone up by 30%. Most of the plastics that are there and we use a lot of the plastic, it's gone up by 30%.

items.statement: Milk supply improving with Maharashtra and Karnataka showing significant upward growth in procurement; expecting procurement prices to drop by INR1.5 to INR2 in coming quarters
items.quote: We're expecting that the procurement prices should come down to the INR1.5 to INR2 and because of the product mix improvement, our realization is on the higher side.

items.statement: Standalone India EBITDA margin was approximately 6% to 7% on full-year basis; Q4 represented cyclical trough with recovery expected from Q1 FY27
items.quote: On a 9-month basis [Wrongly said, please read it as Full Year Basis] , our stand -alone India EBITDA margin was approximately 6% to 7%. In Q4, represented a cyclical throw , we expect this to begin to recover in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Uncertainty around fuel prices (USD60 to USD120 per barrel could mean 25-30% fuel cost increase), packaging costs, and weather/El Niño impact on procurement
items.quote: None of us are certain about where this price of fuel will be stopped becau se if you look at it and people and this is my view and please correct me if I'm wrong USD60 to USD 120 in my simple mathematics for barrel means it's a 100% price increase, which should translate even to a 25% or 30% increase for us on fuel, which is not yet shown

items.statement: Effective tax rate to return to normal 25-27% range post completion of favorable tax orders received in FY26
items.quote: Effective tax rate will return to the normal 25 to 27 range post completion of the favorable tax orders we received in FY26.

items.statement: Capital allocation priority: 1) fund growth capex (Maharashtra, Uganda, regular capex) from internal accruals, 2) regular dividends, 3) selective bolt-on acquisitions with procurement/distribution synergies
items.quote: Our priority order is first fund growth capex where Maharashtra, Uganda, and our current regular capex are both covered from our internal accruals. Second, regular dividends. Third, selective bolt-on acquisitions where we see procurement or distribution synergies.

items.statement: VAP grew 21% year-on-year excluding bulk sales; curd sales volume grew 15.4% and curd sales grew 19.1% year-on-year
items.value: 21% VAP growth, 15.4% curd volume growth, 19.1% curd sales growth
items.quote: Excluding bulk sales, VAP delivered growth of 21% on year - on-year basis. Curd sales volume reported a healthy growth of 15.4% on year-on-year and stood at 442 million metric tons in terms of value. Curd sales grew by 19.1% on year -on-year basis.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance: 12-13% high visibility, targeting 18-20% with investments.
items.quote: we have a reasonable level of confidence in terms of high visibility pipeline and order book to deliver about 12% to 13% of growth

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 21-22% due to upfront investments in AI CoE and Databricks leadership.
items.quote: what we planned for is an EBITDA between 21% to 22% for the revenue growth that we will deliver primarily on account of some of these upfront investments

items.statement: Technology vertical expected to grow 5-8% YoY in FY27 after adjusting for losses.
items.quote: technology vertical for this year, our sense is that it should be between 5% to 8% growth on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Consumer vertical expected to grow 18-22% in FY27.
items.quote: Consumer should, our sense is right now, should grow anywhere between 18% to 22%.

items.statement: BFSI expected to grow at least 40% in FY27.
items.quote: BFSI, obviously, the growth rates for the next year will come down compared to the previous year. But our sense is they should grow at least at about 40% for the next year

items.statement: Databricks portfolio expected to grow 60%+ in FY27.
items.quote: the expectation is that the Databricks portfolio of work will continue to grow at about 60% plus.

items.statement: Largest tech account shrinkage was $6.5-7M; targeting 95% of last year's revenue from this client in FY27.
items.quote: the total value of shrinkage was closer to about $6.5 million to $7 million.

items.statement: AI-led projects have gross margins of 55-58% vs overall 50.8%.
items.quote: we are seeing that the gross margins on those projects are definitely higher at about 55% to 58%.

items.statement: No deflation in T&M pricing; clients pay more for AI work but expect higher productivity.
items.quote: there is no deflation on the way it works is that clients continue to engage our people. In fact, in many instances, they will be willing to pay a bit more.

items.statement: 28% of FY26 revenue from primary AI (traditional, generative, agentic) visible to clients; another 21% AI under the hood.
items.quote: about 28% of our revenues for last year involves one of these three, where the AI aspect is clear and visible to the client

items.statement: Technology vertical headwinds from client consolidation and insourcing; new leader prefers internal FTEs over vendors.
items.quote: their preferred model is to work with internal full-time employees as opposed to work with the vendors.

items.statement: Plan to increase fixed-bid/outcome-based contracts from 20% to capture AI productivity benefits.
items.quote: the plan though is to shift a bit more to both milestone and deliverable based as well as outcome-based. So that 20% that Raj referred to, we want to bump it up

items.statement: Databricks ecosystem revenue was ~$17.5M in FY26, up from ~$12M in FY25.
items.quote: on a full year basis, our revenue from the Databricks ecosystem put together is closer to about $17.5 million.

items.statement: BFSI practice grew over 80% in FY26; ended year with ~$18M revenue.
items.quote: the BFSI practice grew in excess of about 80% compared to the year before.

items.statement: Confident of 25% growth in FY27, based on order book conversion and pipeline.
items.quote: So, one way to look at it is see that whether it is 18% or 20% of the open order getting converted, I'm talking from an analyst angle only. If that number, let's say, is 20%, then 20% of INR1,700 crores is almost like INR350 crores. And then the current year also, we saw how much we could convert right away. Something,

items.statement: INR120 crores allocated for organic growth in FY26, including government, IoT, and IP creation.
items.quote: So overall, what we have done the capital allocation in FY26 was INR120 crores for organic growth. This organic growth included the growth in the government business, it's included in the IoT business. It included in creating intellectual property.

items.statement: IoT-led EBITDA margin increased to 16% in FY26, targeting further expansion.
items.quote: So, let's hope that this -- over the course of year, I think we increased EBITDA from 14% to 16%. Last quarter, of course, Stellar was 33% -- but over the course of the year, that was the number -- and we are hoping to increase that 16% in this year.

items.statement: Government business expected to see significant growth in FY27 due to strong order book and pipeline.
items.quote: But we saw a strong Q4, that's the inflection point that we have seen. And so the government business itself should see a significant growth in this year.

items.statement: IoT business expected to see significant growth in FY27 and coming years with dedicated management focus.
items.quote: So as we keep growing IoT business and you will see a very good growth in the IoT in this year and the coming years because we have now a full clear management focused on growing the IoT business.

items.statement: Government receivables increased, but no bad debt and collections are strong.
items.quote: One of the reasons we are actually moving on two fronts in the government. One part, as Rohan has been saying, we have almost -- if not really fully, but almost zero bad debt in the government. That is very important for us to note. The collection period might be higher. But that's again a nature of that beast.

items.statement: Final dividend of INR3.50 per share declared for FY26.
items.quote: The Board was pleased to express its gratitude to all the shareholders by declaring a final dividend for FY26 of INR3.50 per equity share of INR2 each at the rate of 175%.

items.statement: Aim to hold margins at least in FY27 while stepping up revenue growth
items.quote: Our key focus in FY27 is on stepping up revenue growth while at least holding margins.

items.statement: Expect acceleration and step-up in growth in FY27 versus FY26
items.quote: FY27, as we see today, short of any black swan events coming our way, we do see an acceleration and a step-up in growth of what we delivered in FY26.

items.statement: Implemented calibrated price increase of 6-7% on average in April 2025
items.quote: In response to rising costs, we implemented a calibrated price increase of 6% to 7% on an average in April, and we will re main agile as the situation

items.statement: Price increase addresses cost inflation to a large extent; competition also raised prices
items.quote: Our pricing actions, along with our interventions on our efficiency programs, etc., that in our view, kind of addresses to a very large extent, the cost inflation that is there.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin of 13.2% in Q4 FY26, highest ever; full year margin 12.2%, up 55 bps
items.quote: For the full year, adjusted EBITDA stood at INR 332 crores with margin of 12.2%, up 55 basis points over the previous year.

items.statement: Capex increased to INR 84 crores in FY26 from INR 55 crores in FY25
items.quote: This is despite a step-up in capex from INR 55 crores in FY25 to INR 84 crores in FY26.

items.statement: Early indicators show price increase landed well with no material impact on sell-outs or downtrading
items.quote: The early indicators that we have seen is that the price increase has landed well, and we do not see any impact as of now on sellouts or on tertiary sales.

items.statement: Robotics to reach INR 1,000 crores by FY30; air purifiers grew 2.7x in FY26; softeners and filters scaling
items.quote: As we mentioned in the Investor Day, we expect it to reach more than INR1,000 crores for us by FY30.

items.statement: AMC bookings grew double digits for fourth consecutive quarter; multi-year mix increased significantly
items.quote: We've had the fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth in bookings, in AMC bookings. And therefore, that momentum has sustained.

items.statement: Input cost inflation and currency pressure persist with no end in sight; drought risk to water purifiers seen as immaterial
items.quote: Input cost pressures are real with no end in sigh t yet. We have a number of initiatives in progress aimed at mitigating its

items.statement: Net cash surplus of INR 443 crores; free cash flow INR 237 crores (148% of PAT)
items.quote: In FY26, we further strengthened our balance sheet, ending the year with a net cash surplus of INR 443 crores, and we generated a free cash flow of INR 237 crores, representing 148% of reported PAT.

items.statement: Robotics manufacturing shifting from imported FG to SKD assembly at Dixon over next 3-4 months
items.quote: As we come closer to September, you will start seeing the manufacturing and assembly migrate to Dixon over the next 3-4 months.

items.statement: Water purifier category grew at 3-year CAGR over 12%; expect acceleration due to low penetration and rising awareness
items.quote: The category has grown at a 3-year CAGR of over 12%, and we remain confident of its growth trajectory stepping up as we go forward.

items.statement: Gross margins range-bound at 58-60% over last 3 years; input cost pressures may create headwinds in FY27
items.quote: Our gross margins have remained range bound at 58% to around 60% over the last 3 years now. This is a reflection of our balanced portfolio, mix management and the well-institutionalized COGS program.

items.statement: Service revenue growth to step up in FY27 driven by AMC booking momentum and filter opportunity
items.quote: Going ahead, we do expect that impact to continue in the coming quarters as well. I think one important call out that I would have is that you will see this impact very, very clearly when we release our annual report.

items.statement: Company confident of growing around mid-teens in FY27
items.quote: We are confident that will continue to grow around mid-teens in FY27.

items.statement: Capex of around Rs. 400 Cr planned for FY27
items.quote: For next year growth of mid-teens, we need to invest around RS.400 Cr which we shall be investing in this year also.

items.statement: Export orders in hand, targeting 20% export growth in FY27 if geopolitical situation remains reasonable
items.quote: This year we are very confident of growing at 20%, provided the geopolitical situation remains reasonable, which we are as an optimist, which we feel that it shall be sorted out soon rather than later.

items.statement: Aim to sustain current EBITDA margin level and improve gradually in subsequent quarters
items.quote: Our aim is to sustain current level of EBITDA margins and continue our efforts to improve gradually in the subsequent quarters, depending upon the growth of the two-wheeler industry and geopolitical environment.

items.statement: Aluminium price increases passed on to OEM and aftermarket customers from April onwards
items.quote: Everything has been corrected April onwards and all these aluminium price rises which has happened in April also, they have been passed on to the customer both on the aftermarket front as well as to our OEM customers.

items.statement: OEM customers continuing with original production schedules showing nice growth in FY27
items.quote: As far outlook of the two-wheeler industry is concerned, our all our OEM customers they are carrying on with their original production schedules which shows a nice growth in this year also and none of the supplies have been affected by the raw materials or anything.

items.statement: Alloy wheel revenue expected Rs. 90-100 Cr in FY27 and Rs. 220 Cr in FY28
items.quote: FY27 we are expecting revenue of around Rs. 90 - Rs. 100 Cr and FY28 will be about Rs. 220 Cr.

items.statement: Alloy wheel supplies to Japanese customer to begin in H2 FY27; sunroof supplies also on track for H2 FY27
items.quote: The alloy wheel supplies to the Japanese customer in the beginning of the H2, so this current year you'll see much higher capacity utilization in the Karoli plant also.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict in West Asia disrupting supply chains and creating volatility in energy, commodity and currency markets
items.quote: After 28th February, 2026, geopolitical conflict in West Asia has disrupted the global economy, posing an unprecedented challenge in supply chain, creating undue volatility in energy, commodity and currency across the globe and it has started affecting Indian economy as well.

items.statement: Strategic reduction in low-margin wheel assembly business complete; revenue will be nil from April 2026
items.quote: Another key update, strategic reduction in low margin wheel assembly business is now complete. From 1st April 2026, wheel assembly revenue will be nil.

items.statement: 9.9 MW solar plant at Sirsa operational since April 2025; 11.55 MW Bikaner plant expected to commission in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our second captive solar plant of 11.55 megawatt in Bikaner, Rajasthan is progressing well and is expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY27, this reflects ASK's special focus on green energy.

items.statement: Independent aftermarket grew 24.7% in FY26 driven by GST reduction from 28% to 18%; expects good growth to continue in FY27
items.quote: Happy to share that our independent aftermarket has grown by 24.7% in FY26. We still remain optimistic that the geopolitical situation shall normalize soon, and the growth trajectory of our sector shall be maintained.

items.statement: Capex breakup: Rs. 40-50 Cr maintenance, rest for new plant capacities
items.quote: Capex breakup is very little is the maintenance budget, that's about Rs.40 to Rs. 50 Cr, rest is all the capex for the new plant capacities, which we keep on adding.

items.statement: Wage increases by state governments creating input cost pressure; confident OEMs will compensate
items.quote: Recent developments in geopolitical scenario and significant increase in minimum wages by some of the state governments has created an input cost pressure on the industry. The customers have been requested to support, and we are confident that all our prestigious OEMs will compensate this input cost escalation.

items.statement: Bangalore plant at 90% capacity utilization; Karoli plant at 65% utilization, expected to increase with alloy wheel supplies
items.quote: Very, very happy to share that Bangalore we have reached 90% capacity utilization that we set up last year, our 18th plant and the third plant in Bengaluru. The Bangalore all capacities are full now. In the Karoli plant, the capacities utilization is still 65%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 orders expected at 40,000-45,000 and consolidated revenue at 500-550 crores, nearly double Q4 level
items.quote: Looking ahead to Q1 FY27, we expect 40,000 to 45,000 orders and consolidated revenue of 500 to 550 crores, nearly double of the Q4 level.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated gross margin reached 38.5%, up from 34.3% in Q3 and 13.7% in Q4 FY25; excluding PLI gross margin was 33.5%
items.quote: In Q4 for 2025-26, consolidated gross margins reached 38.5%, up from 34.3% in Q3 and 13.7% in Q4, similar quarter as last year. Excluding PLI gross margins was 33.5%.

items.statement: Management expects gross margins to remain a strong structural advantage and incrementally increase over the long term, despite near-term commodity pressures and growth investments
items.quote: And over the longer term also, we can actually expect gross margins to incrementally keep going up. Obviously, in the short term, there will be commodity pressures, as well as some of this gross margin in the last month or two we've invested into aggressive growth.

items.statement: Auto business requires only ~50 crores annual maintenance capex; Cell business capex for 6 GWh largely done with payouts in Q1/Q2 FY27, no further capex until subsidiary raises capital
items.quote: Vipul, again, I will tell you rule of thumb maintenance CapEx will be some ₹50 crores annually. I'll just add one more nuance. We do have some R&D which we capitalize, about 20% -30% of our overall R&D expenses. That will keep coming in. But in terms of PPE CapEx, that'll be below ₹50 crores a year.

items.statement: Current inventory at 3-4 days, auto backlog exists, demand increased meaningfully in recent weeks, volumes expected to rise another 10-20% near term as delivery timelines improve
items.quote: we are actually rig ht now, not on 31st March, but right now in the current May period, running at a very low inventory level in our network. That’s because demand has increased so much that people are buying whatever they can find in the network from us. Our inventory, free inventory days is actually down to 3 -4 days and we have auto backlog now

items.statement: EV demand has gone up meaningfully in last few weeks; April registrations up 20% MoM while industry declined >22%; May trending 14,000-15,000 registrations; broad-based recovery across regions
items.quote: April registrations were up 20% month-on-month, while the broader E two-wheeler industry declined by more than 22%.

items.statement: Bikes (Roadster) now 15% of April gross orders with 50%+ market share in electric motorcycles; portfolio includes up to 9.1 kWh battery and 500+ km certified range using Bharat 4680 cells
items.value: 15% of gross orders; 50%+ EV bike market share
items.quote: Motorcycles are India's largest two-wheeler category and EV penetration remains very low. Ola now has 50% market share in electric motorcycles, and bikes contributed 15% of April gross orders.

items.statement: Adjusted operating EBITDA breakeven achievable at 20,000-25,000 units/month with ~35%+ gross margins, ~1.4 lakh ASP, ~50,000 gross profit/vehicle, and 300-350 crores monthly OpEx
items.quote: With the reset OpEx base and current gross margin structure, adjusted operating EBITDA breakeven is ach ievable at around 20,000 to 25,000 units per month, subject to pricing mix and commodity conditions

items.statement: Asset base (1M units auto capacity + 6 GWh Gigafactory phase 1) can support 15,000-20,000 crores annual revenue across Auto and Cell without meaningful incremental capex
items.quote: Together, the asset base can support approximately 15,000 to 20,000 crores of annual revenue scale across Auto and Cell without needing meaningful incremental CapEx.

items.statement: Gigafactory at 2.5 GWh operational, installation up to 6 GWh largely complete with commercialization expected by end of Q1 FY27; plan to expand to 20 GWh by next year via separate capital raise at cell entity
items.quote: The Gigafactory is now entering the scale phase. We currently have 2.5 GWh operational capacity. Installation up to 6 GWh is largely complete with commercialization expected to be completed by the end of this quarter.

items.statement: Plan to transition full vehicle portfolio to own Bharat 4680 cells by September 2026; currently 15% of orders on own cells
items.quote: We plan to transition the full vehicle portfolio to our own cells by September 2026.

items.statement: Own cell production already cheaper on BOM cost vs imports at low volumes; expect 10-15% cost advantage including Gigafactory overheads at 6 GWh scale
items.quote: I do expect, as we scale up our Gigafactory towards the 6 GWh over the course of this year, we will get a 10%-15% advantage on building our own cell, including the operational overheads of the Gigafactory.

items.statement: Warranty costs dropped from 500+ crores in FY25 to 59 crores in FY26 (70% lower on Gen 3 vs Gen 2); service stats down 88%, same-day closures ~87%, part dependency down 69%
items.quote: In FY25, we had a 500 plus crore of warranty costs, in FY26, it's only 60 crores, 59 crores to be accurate. So what we've been sharing with you guys on our Gen 3 platform being by far the industry leader, is validated by our warranty costs in FY26.
