items.statement: Plan to raise capital at cell subsidiary level to fund expansion from 6 GWh to 20 GWh; significant inbound interest from private equity players
items.quote: And we are actually going to be expanding that 6 to 20 GWh by next year, but only by raising capital separately at the cell entity, which also we have a lot of inbound interest from private equity players, given the leadership of this asset that we have created.

items.statement: Auto business generated 213 crores CFO and 173 crores free cash flow in Q4 FY26; consolidated CFO 91 crores; first operating cash flow positive quarter
items.value: 213 crores Auto CFO; 173 crores Auto FCF; 91 crores consolidated CFO
items.quote: Q4 was the first operating cash flow positive quarter. Consolidated CFO was 91 crores, supported by strong gross margins, PLI inflows, lower OpEx and tighter working capital discipline. The Auto business delivered 213 crores of CFO and 173 crores of free cash flow in Q4.

items.statement: Consolidated OpEx (including lease) to move toward ~350 crores over next couple of quarters from 428 crores in Q4 FY26; OpEx ~90% fixed, high operating leverage
items.quote: We expect OpEx to move towards approximatel y 350 crores. We actually spoke about in our last year Shareholders’ Letter also over the next couple of quarters, as the full benefit of 26 actions flow

items.statement: Cell production to start in H2 FY27, reaching 6 GW by June-July 2027.
items.quote: So we believe that in the second half of the year beginning, we'll be able to start our cell production and then ramp up. So we are very, very close to our cell production start of 2.4 gigawatt.

items.statement: FY27 capex for expansion is about INR 1,700 crores, funded by debt and equity.
items.quote: So, for FY27, our capex requirement for this expansion is about 1,700 crores. So it will be a mix of debt -equity.

items.statement: FY28 capex for 6 GW ingot project expected INR 1,800-2,000 crores.
items.quote: So we see around 1,800 crore to 2,000 crore capex will be required in FY28 as well.

items.statement: Confirmed order book at 5.89 GW, about INR 8,000 crores, execution over 18 months.
items.quote: Our confirmed order book remains robust at approximately 5.89 gigawatt, as of March 2026, providing strong forward revenue visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Margins to be stable and healthy in FY27, improving significantly in H2.
items.quote: So, overall, we see that the margins will be quite healthy and stable for FY27.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 margins to be softer due to war and commodity fluctuations.
items.quote: And we expect that the first quarter, because this war still continues. The first quarter will be a little softer, because there's high fluctuation, which is really extraordinary fluctuations both in, you know, the US dollars and commodities and oil prices, and all these are key components in manufacturing.

items.statement: Some orders allow cost pass-through, others require absorption due to fixed-price contracts.
items.quote: So it depends from order to order. For some of the orders, we will be able to pass on that, you know, change and for other, we will have to absorb some of some of that compression.

items.statement: Cell market is seller's market with high demand, especially retail segment.
items.quote: So it is more like a seller's market right now for solar cells , and there is very high demand in the retail segment, especially in the PM Surya Ghar and the KUSUM segment.

items.statement: Initially focus on retail segment for cells, then enter C&I and utility by Q3/Q4 FY27.
items.quote: So initially, we will be focusing on the retail segment, and we believe that because we have gone in with the same set of equipment and technical know -how, the technical staff will also be coming along with it. So we are very confident that we'll be able to stabilize our efficiencies in a very short period of time , w

items.statement: Commodity price increases, rupee depreciation, and war impact input costs and margins.
items.quote: So the major reasons for the decrease in EBITDA are, as you rightly mentioned, correct, because there was an increase in commodity pricing, which really impacted our input costs across the value chain.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio to remain between 1 and 1.5 times.
items.quote: Our current debt-equity is 0.65, but we feel that our debt -equity will remain at around 1.1 -- between 1 and 1.5 times ratio, not more than that.

items.statement: Encapsulant capacity expanded to 5 GW, with 5-10% cost savings from in-house production.
items.quote: The savings which we get from our internal manufacturing are between 5% to 10%, depending on, you know, what prices we are able to secure the raw material, but it gives us an added advantage.

items.statement: EPC revenue contribution was 3-4% of top line in FY26, expected to remain same in FY27.
items.quote: Our EPC contribution was about 150 megawatt, which is about 3% -4% of our bottom line. We only take EPCs that are profitable and have a high margin, because that is not our core business.

items.statement: Normalized copper EBITDA expected to stabilize at INR30,000-32,000 per ton on steady state basis
items.quote: So, for forward guidance, I'm sure about excluding the exceptional tailwind of quarter three FY '26 and a confluence of one-time headwinds in quarter four FY '26, the management expects normalized EBITDA to stabilize at approximately INR32,000 to INR30,000 on a steady state basis.

items.statement: Lead volume growth expected 10-15%, copper volume growth potential beyond 15% for FY27
items.quote: Lead and copper, as we see the trends coming in and if we don't let the international disturbances overpower the trends, a regular growth in two digits is always expected.

items.statement: Total FY27 capex estimated at INR115-120 crores across copper value-added phase 2, antimony, plastic recycling, Ahmedabad JV and Kuwait projects
items.quote: So, this all put together plus the phase two of the copper value-added project will be around INR115 to INR120 crores.

items.statement: Copper downstream projects (anode to busbar) have potential to increase EBITDA margin by 2-4% and add INR22-45 per kg incremental EBITDA
items.quote: Copper downstream project has potential to further increase the EBITDA margin from 2% to 4%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 copper EBITDA per ton compressed by ~INR24,000-24,500 due to formula drop (~INR18,000-18,500) and war-related logistics (~INR6,000)
items.quote: With respect to the war situation, EBITDA per ton got impacted for around INR6,000 per ton. And with respect to the higher LME and drop in formula, it was nearing approx INR18,000 to INR18,500 per ton.

items.statement: China-driven exceptional buying in Q3 FY26 created tailwind that reversed in Q4; LME surge from $10,000 to $14,000 impacted realization formulas
items.quote: This year copper was extraordinary rallied and the bullish trend in copper and the price went up to skyrocket from US $10,000 to $14,000. And because of that, a 40% increase in copper, the formula has impacted very big way.

items.statement: Geopolitical shipping disruptions via Iran corridor delayed Kuwait machinery dispatch and stranded containers at UAE ports; hedging covers price risk on stuck material
items.quote: Certain imported machinery deliveries witnessed temporary delays due to the geopolitical situation relating to Iran shipping

items.statement: Dedicated plastic recycling unit targeted operational by Q3 FY27 with estimated capex of INR15 crores on 6-acre land
items.quote: The new unit is targeted to become operational by quarter three financial year '27 and will entail an estimated capex of around INR15 crores.

items.statement: Copper anode production commenced March 2026 at 800 MT/month; second furnace (800 MT/month) expected Q1 FY27; cathode phase 1 by Q2 FY27, phase 2 by Q3 FY27 (1,500 MT/month); wire rod by Aug 2026 (600 MT/month); bus bar by Sep 2026 (1,500 M
items.quote: I am pleased to share that copper anode production has already commenced in March 2026 with an initial installed capacity of 800 metric ton per month. The second furnace with an additional 800 metric ton per month capacity is currently in the advanced stag e of installation and is expected to be commissioned during quarter one financial year '27

items.statement: FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 5.9% from 5.7%; PAT margin expanded to 3.6% from 3.5%
items.quote: EBITDA margins also improved to approximately 5.9% in FY '26 as compared to 5.7% in FY '25, supported by better operating leverage, improved product mix, and stable operational execution.

items.statement: Management implementing long-term hedging formula mechanism to eliminate formula volatility impact on sale price; copper contracts shifting from 30-60 day to long-term
items.quote: So in the future we will be working on a long-term hedging formula mechanism where the price of the formula which varies up and down won't affect our sale price.

items.statement: Ahmedabad JV (Jain C&Y Circular Solutions) processing of electric motor and cable scrap to commence Sep 2026; machinery installation completion targeted Dec 2026
items.quote: Processing of electric motor scrap and cable scrap is expected to commence from September 2026 onwards. Installation of the planned machinery and equipment is targeted for completion by December 2026.

items.statement: Kuwait battery recycling venture civil construction complete; machinery ready at supplier; dispatch delayed 30-day notice pending shipping route normalization
items.quote: Civil construction at the site has been completed and the ordered machinery is ready at the supplier's facility. However, due to disruption in shipping routes arising from Iran-related geopolitical situation, dispatches have been temporarily delayed.

items.statement: Lead capacity utilization at 97-100%, copper at 65%, aluminium at 35% for FY26; copper utilization to rise with new capacities over 2-3 years
items.quote: So the copper, presently we are utilizing around 65% of the total installed capacity, while lead we are almost close to 97% to 100%, and aluminum is around 35% of the installed capacity.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of INR500 crores: INR375 crores used for debt repayment, INR16.4 crores for IPO expenses, balance for general corporate purposes
items.quote: From the primary issue of around INR500 crores, approximately INR375 crores was utilized towards repayment of the debts, while the balance amount was earmarked for general corporate purposes including the IPO expenses.

items.statement: Operating cash flow negative INR600 crores in FY26 due to volume/price-driven working capital increase; expected to turn positive from Q2 FY27 as inventory days reduce below 60
items.quote: Now coming to your second question with respect to when it will become a positive. Yes, in a longer term we expect that we have already reduced the stock from comparing from Q3 to Q4 we have reduced the stock content and which will be our further policy to reduce the stock so that the working capital cycle which is around presently 66 days which should come down further below 60. So once that is a

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of INR 210 crores, 45%+ growth over FY26.
items.quote: Our FY27 revenue target is INR 210 crores, a 45% plus growth on FY26.

items.statement: FY27 PAT expected around INR 24-25 crores on INR 210 crores revenue.
items.quote: So, it will be around INR 24-25 crores on INR 210 crores of business.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue outlook around INR 92 crores, H2 around INR 99 crores.
items.value: INR 92 crores H1, INR 99 crores H2
items.quote: Adding new recurring means and project work, H1 outlook is around INR 92 crores and H2 estimate is INR 99 crores.

items.statement: Entered FY27 with INR 159 crore assured recurring revenue at INR 13.5 crore per month.
items.value: INR 159 crores, INR 13.5 crores per month
items.quote: We entered FY27 with INR 159 crore in assured recurring revenue at INR 13.5 crore per month, a 35% MRR step-up before even we won a single new deal, if I don't consider any new deal in the current year.

items.statement: Current contracted base and visible pipeline of INR 190 crores for FY27.
items.quote: Current outlook based on contracted base and visible pipeline is INR 190 crores.

items.statement: FY27 margin recovery via higher-margin AI/security mix, utilization to 88%, operating leverage.
items.quote: Our FY ‘27 margin recovery plan is built on three levers. First, improving our services mix towards higher margin, AI and security work. Second, driving billable utilization from 84% towards 88%. And third, operational leverage as new hires reach full productivity.

items.statement: FY27 PAT margin expected similar to FY26, around INR 24-25 crores.
items.quote: See, we are targeting a 45% growth in our top-line revenue and equivalent increase in our PAT margin. So, that will be around the same, if not more.

items.statement: No cost escalation risk; AWS prices stable, hardware price inflation is a tailwind for cloud migration.
items.quote: No, there is no cost surprise.

items.statement: AI to be meaningful contributor in FY27 and primary growth engine from FY28.
items.quote: AI will be a meaningful contributor in FY27, and our primary growth engine from FY28 onwards.

items.statement: Targeting 5% of revenue from AI and cybersecurity combined in FY27.
items.quote: And our target for this year, both AI and cybersecurity put together, we are targeting about 5% revenue from this.

items.statement: No major manpower cost increase; INR 17 crore to INR 18.5-19 crore plus INR 1.5 crore new hires.
items.quote: Yes. So, there will be, on the existing manpower only, the INR 17 crore would, with the appraisals in place, it will go up to INR 18.5 or 19 crore. And then, there would be about a few, like I said, a few resources here and there, which would get added on.

items.statement: Dubai contract and gaming client exit removed INR 7.5 crores revenue; headcount added INR 6 crores cost.
items.value: INR 7.5 crores revenue, INR 6 crores cost
items.quote: The Dubai contract decision removed approximately INR 4 crores from the top line. The mandatory gaming client exit removed a further INR 3.5 crores. Together, that is INR 7.5 crores of revenue that was either foregone or withdrawn. Simultaneously, our headcount investment added approximately INR 6 crores in annual cost

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; global expansion to be funded by revenue from those geographies.
items.quote: So, we will start like that so that our initial cost of business acquisition is low and as we acquire more customers, as we build our revenue, we expect that revenue and the profit which gets generated from those particular geographies to fund our future expansion and growth in those regions.

items.statement: Debtor days improved from 72 to 62; FY27 target below 55 days.
items.quote: Debtor days, we have improved 14% from 72 days to 62 days with the FY ‘27 target below 55.

items.statement: Targets FY27 revenue of INR450-500 crores, with H1 target of INR200+ crores.
items.quote: Our target for this year is to achieve INR450 crores plus, and we are focused on that.

items.statement: Aims to become a INR1,000+ crore company in three years.
items.quote: maximum in three years we want to become a 1,000-plus company.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin above 15%, with potential 1-2% improvement.
items.quote: The target is to go above 15%, but it depends a lot on the situation and how price variations hit us.

items.statement: Aims for standardized EBITDA margin above 18% for CT PT products.
items.quote: But standardized we will almost want to work above 18% EBITDA.

items.statement: Current order book of INR237 crores plus INR125 crores fresh orders.
items.quote: We have approximately 237 crores orders. And we have already pre-ordered new add-ons of the 125 cr.

items.statement: Plans INR25 crores capex from IPO proceeds for machinery and facilities.
items.quote: Right now, our first target is the INR25 crores capex we mentioned during the IPO.

items.statement: Capex in SMC, FRP, and engineering units to enable revenue above INR750 crores.
items.quote: if our full-fledged, if we want, revenue above INR750 crores can come.

items.statement: Passes on copper and steel costs; takes short orders to manage resin fluctuations.
items.quote: For copper and steel, we pass on the costs because it depends on the situation at the time of supply.

items.statement: Includes 5% price escalation clause in orders to pass on fluctuations.
items.quote: if the fluctuation is like this, if it is more than 5%, then we will pass it on.

items.statement: Expects significant boom in utilities and electrical industry over next 5 years.
items.quote: for the next 5 years, there will be a significant boom in the industry because a lot of new infrastructure development is happening in India

items.statement: Shifts focus to higher-margin products like CTPT, busducts, and meter cubicles.
items.quote: we have started taking orders for products like CTPT, busducts, and meter cubicles, which are high-value items. These have much better EBITDA margins compared to SMC.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation causes raw material price fluctuations, impacting margins.
items.quote: Right now, it is a fluctuating market due to geopolitics.

items.statement: No immediate need for debt or equity; may consider after September based on situation.
items.quote: right now we have a cash fund because the IPO has just happened. So, according to that, right now, if we can maintain the working capital cycle better, then perhaps there will be no requirement this year.

items.statement: Working capital cycle sustainable at 40-45 days per government MSME rules.
items.quote: our cycle will either improve or stay at 40 to 45 days as per the government rules, the MSME rules.

items.statement: Expects 50%+ revenue growth in FY27, matching historical performance.
items.quote: Whatever historical performance we have shown in the last three fiscals, with the same performance we will grow in this fiscal '27 as well.

items.statement: Expects to maintain EBITDA margin 12-13% and PAT margin 8-9%.
items.quote: We are expecting to maintain an EBITDA between 12% to 13% and PAT margin of 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Order book of INR 621 crores to be executed over 12-24 months, average 18 months.
items.quote: Sir, generally our timeline is 12 to 24 months, so averaging it, our timeline is 18 months. So roughly it is completed in 18 months, sir.

items.statement: Win ratio of 30-40% expected to continue.
items.quote: Madam, our win ratio is 30 to 40%. Okay. We will move ahead with the same ratio, madam.

items.statement: Purchase orders have price variation clauses to pass on cost increases.
items.quote: Sir, all our purchase orders, almost all our POs have price variation calculations. The price that varies according to the scenario gets compensated for us in the price variation clause.

items.statement: H1 typically 35% and H2 65% of annual revenue.
items.quote: Generally H1 is 35 and H2 is around 65.

items.statement: Retention money around INR 66 crores as of March 2026.
items.quote: And talking about March '26 numbers, around INR 66 crores is in retention currently.

items.statement: Participated in DISCOM distribution tenders, results next month.
items.quote: Madam, we have participated in DISCOM distribution in our tender pipeline. Its result will come in the next month, madam.

items.statement: Capex to substantially reduce over next two years, less than half of past levels.
items.quote: Next capex will substantially come down. It will be less than half what we have been doing in the past.

items.statement: Price increases of 3-10% taken in Q4, similar in April, further announced in May.
items.quote: We have -- Consumer Products, our price increases have ranged from anywhere from 3% to 10% in quarter 4, and we have already taken a price increase in the same range in April.

items.statement: Lighting EBIT margin may stay close to current levels as gains reinvested in growth.
items.quote: So at the EBIT level, it may be close to where we are but whatever advantage we'll get in terms of margins or the momentum, we'll spend that behind to build momentum further.

items.statement: Consumer Products margin recovery uncertain due to war-related inflation and competitive pressures.
items.quote: Difficult to say exact margin, and I tell you why because there is another factor which is affecting the cost of our products is the war -related inflation.

items.statement: Consumer Products expected to bounce back next financial year.
items.quote: However, we expect the vertical to bounce back in the next financial year.

items.statement: Lighting Solutions momentum expected to continue into next year.
items.quote: We are confident of carrying this momentum into next year.

items.statement: Wires category launched, expected to be strong growth driver for next few quarters.
items.quote: We are confident this business will grow in future and will emerge as one of the strong growth drivers for the next few quarters.

items.statement: War sentiment, continued price hikes, and patchy summer remain key headwinds.
items.quote: However, sentiment concerns arising out of war, continued price hikes and patchy summer remains key headwinds.

items.statement: Not all cost inflation can be passed on; need to stay competitive.
items.quote: But we are using all the levers to see that we deliver a good margin. However, we do believe we have to also see we stay competitive in the market. And in that context, maybe whatever is left, not everything, we'll be able to pass on to consumers.

items.statement: Working capital expected to remain negative next year.
items.quote: So we have been operating at negative working capital for the past 2 years, and we -- the expectation is to continue on those same lines for the next year as well, and we endeavor to achieve that as well.

items.statement: Plan to bridge BLDC fan gap in next 12 months to accelerate growth.
items.quote: In the next 12 months, our plan is to bridge this gap. And this is where we believe the acceleration of growth will happen.

items.statement: Step up investment behind brands and innovations in next 12 months.
items.quote: So you will see a step up in that in the next 12 months, our investment behind brands and investment behind innovations.

items.statement: Dividend of INR 3 per share recommended for FY26.
items.quote: Further, in celebration of 100 years of Bajaj Group, the Board of Directors have decided to maintain a dividend rate same as last year and accordingly approved -- recommended a final dividend of INR 3 a share, that's 150% of face value of INR 2 each on equity shares for the financial year ending 31st March 2026.

items.statement: Management aims to return EBITDA margins to around 10% in FY27, though worst cost impact may not be over.
items.quote: So, it will be our endeavor to go back to the guided number of around 10%.

items.statement: Peak revenue at current price realizations seen at INR 1200-1250 crore excluding Mahad ramp-up.
items.quote: But that should very easily be anywhere between INR 1200 crores to INR 1250 crores.

items.statement: Mahad at current capacity to add around INR 50 crore additional revenue in FY27 on conservative basis.
items.quote: At the current capacity, it will be around INR 50 crores additional revenue.

items.statement: Mahad optimum utilization top line seen at INR 60-65 crore as Evermoss prices have increased.
items.quote: Around INR 60 crores to INR 65 crores because the prices has already increased.

items.statement: Mahad expected to reach 75-80% utilization in next one year, becoming EBITDA neutral and contributing.
items.quote: we are very confident that in the next one year, we should be in a position to achieve utilization of the plant which is anywhere between 75% to 80%

items.statement: Mahad plant capex was about INR 90 crore; capacity can be doubled with INR 12-15 crore more.
items.value: INR 90 crore; INR 12 crores to INR 15 crores
items.quote: initially we have invested around INR 90 crore approx. And this capacity can be easily doubled by adding INR 12 crores to INR 15 crores of CAPEX.

items.statement: Mahad ramp-up continues to drag consolidated EBITDA margins by 1-1.5% as previously guided.
items.quote: Mahad continues to be in its ramp-up phase and continues to be a drag on our consolidated EBITDA margins to the extent of between 1% to 1.5% as we have guided in the past few quarters.

items.statement: Input cost shock from gum turpentine, CST, alpha-pinene at all-time highs; situation may worsen before normalizing.
items.quote: Gum turpentine, CST and alpha-pinene prices continue to go up in the last two quarters and currently are at their all-time highest ever.

items.statement: Tariff overhang on India-US trade eased; gradual recovery in North America order flow expected.
items.quote: The tariffs overhang on the India-US trade has eased compared to the earlier part of FY ’25-26 and that should support a gradual recovery in order flow from North America.

items.statement: RFQ cycles for H2 FY26 constructive on volumes though pricing remains tight.
items.quote: RFQ cycles for the second half of FY ’26 are looking constructive on volumes though pricing continues to remain tight.

items.statement: Revenue split across three divisions expected to remain broadly one-third each.
items.quote: we always have a guidance that the three divisions normally have split revenues of 33%:33%:33% broadly.

items.statement: Expects consolidated EBITDA margin to exceed 10% over next three years, with mid-path by early next year.
items.quote: we are aiming right now, we have an EBITDA at around consolidated at around 3% and it will go step by step, not by way over what we are aiming is really be at more than 10% over the next three years and achieving already probably to be in the middle of the path beginning of next year.

items.statement: Expects margin improvement from next quarter as recent orders translate into results.
items.quote: So we expect from the next quarter on improvement in margins due to the fact that the orders we have registered on Q1 and also the one we got in the second half of the year in 2025 will start to, let's say, translate into positive results.

items.statement: Standalone order book at ~INR13 billion as of March 2026, up 101% YoY.
items.quote: As on March 2026, our stand alone order book stands at approximately INR13 billion and reflects a 101% year-on-year increase.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at ~INR33 billion; majority executable over three years.
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the consolidated order book stands at approximately INR33 billion.

items.statement: Secured order from JSW Steel for CGL project valued at ~INR4.4-4.7 billion.
items.quote: We have also secured an order from JSW Steel for a CGL project valued at approximately INR4.4 billion to INR4.7 billion.

items.statement: Expects positive order pipeline trend over next 24 months, driven by India, China, green steel, JVD.
items.quote: our opinion is that the trend will be positive in the next 24 months. We expect more orders coming in, especially from number one, the Indian market, which is extremely dynamic and still investing heavily to double the capacity of the country for 2030..

items.statement: Targets value services to be 30-35% of mix over next 3-5 years.
items.quote: We see that we are over the next three to five years we are looking to be at around ideally 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Investing in rolls coating facility at Taloja, expected to be commissioned shortly.
items.quote: We remain committed to investing in this segment, including the rolls coating facility at Taloja, which is expected to be commissioned shortly.

items.statement: Board still exploring fundraise options; another board meeting in 2-3 weeks.
items.quote: Board is still exploring options. So, we have another Board which is evaluating the options and we have another board foreseen in the next two to three weeks to come to better answers.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in Middle East could cause short-term volatility in industrial sectors globally.
items.quote: At the same time, geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are creating uncertainty across energy markets, logistics, and commodity flows, which could lead to short -term volatility in the industrial sectors globally.

items.statement: US business consolidation may be delayed to end of year or slightly postponed due to technical issues.
items.quote: USA is we are still here also we are still investigating. There are some technical issues on incorporating, not incorporating, on consolidating USA. So, either we are able to achieve that by the end of the year or maybe it will be discussion on maybe postponing s lightly, but not so much.

items.statement: Volteron has no revenue yet; strategy under evaluation for JCIL contribution.
items.quote: So Volteron has no revenue yet due to the fact that it is ready for commercialization only since few weeks. So we are reshaping completely the Volteron strategy right now and especially we are conducting a reflection on how JCIL will contribute and benefi t from the Volteron deployment in the future.

items.statement: Cost structure aligning from West to India and China over 18 months to drive synergies.
items.quote: Going forward, the cost structure is gradually aligning from the West towards India and China, which is expected to drive operational synergies and efficiency improvements over time, improving the margin trajectory.

items.statement: Novelis long-term EBITDA per ton guidance of $600 remains intact
items.quote: Importantly, our long-term guidance of $600 per ton remains intact, supported by accelerated execution of our $350 million to $400 million structural cost reduction program.

items.statement: Novelis targets $350-400 million structural cost reduction by FY28 exit
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain committed to our 3-year goal of permanently reducing our cost structure by $350 million to $400 million by FY 28 exit.

items.statement: Novelis FY26 exit savings run rate reached $200 million
items.quote: Back in April 2025, we set an FY26 exit savings run rate target of $75 million, which we raised last quarter to $125 million. With another quarter of solid execution behind us, that run rate is now $200 million.

items.statement: India capex FY27 about INR12,000 crores; Novelis capex FY27 $2.3-2.4 billion
items.quote: In FY 27, the India capex will be about INR12,000 crores, and the Novelis capex will be between, I think, Dev has already announced on the call about 2.3 billion to 2.4 billion, largely Bay Minette.

items.statement: India capex FY28 estimated INR15,000-17,000 crores; consolidated capex lower than FY26
items.quote: India capex, Pinakin, INR 12,000 crores this year, next year will be, I don't know, INR 15,000 crores to INR17,000 crores, but it's not going to be at the same level as Bay Minette was. So, I do think the consol capex of the two will be lower.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt peak expected INR80,000-90,000 crores over next 2 years
items.quote: So consolidated net debt peak should be between INR80,000 crores and INR90,000 crores over the next 2 years.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated capex INR31,619 crores, up 47% year-on-year
items.quote: At the same time, we continue to invest aggressively in future growth with capital expenditures of INR31,619 crores, up 47% year-on-year.

items.statement: India upstream aluminium EBITDA $1,756 per ton, margin 48% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: This helped us deliver an EBITDA of $1,756 per ton this quarter. EBITDA margins were at 48% and continued to be among the best in the global industry.

items.statement: Novelis adjusted EBITDA $543 per ton in Q4 FY26, up 5% year-on-year
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter stood at $498 million or $543 per ton, reflecting a 5% year-on-year.

items.statement: India aluminium cost expected to increase 5% in Q1 FY27 vs Q4 FY26, driven by furnace oil, CP coke, pitch
items.quote: So I think in Q1, we are anticipating a 5% increase over Q4, and the majority is driven by furnace oil. Furnace oil prices have really gone up high, followed by CP coke and pitch, but furnace oil being the biggest one.

items.statement: India aluminium demand Q4 FY26 ~1.6 million tons, up ~9% year-on-year
items.quote: In Q4 FY26, aluminium demand is estimated around 1.6 million tons, reflecting an approximately 9% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: India copper demand Q4 FY26 402 KT, up 10% year-on-year
items.quote: In the domestic copper market demand this quarter, including domestic supply, scrap and imports and imports excluding rose by 10% year-on-year, reaching 402 KT compared to 364 KT in the same period last year.

items.statement: Global aluminium deficit widened to 1.5 million tons for CY26 due to West Asia conflict; supply response expected medium term
items.quote: This is expected to tighten availability, particularly through Q2 and Q3 of calendar year '26. As a result, t he market has moved from an earlier expectation of 0.3 million tons deficit to 1.5 million tons deficit for calendar year '26

items.statement: Sustainable PBT margin expected at 11-12% in near term
items.quote: Now talking about the sustainable margin, we could be looking at 11-12% kind of margin in the near future, while obviously in long term, the focus would be on improving it further, but the sustainable margin will be that.

items.statement: INR 500 crores investment planned from FY26 to FY28, with INR 200 crores in FY27
items.quote: So, from '26 to '28, we have around INR 500 crores investment, which will go through each year. This year, '26, will be around INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Aftermarket price hikes started; OEM pass-through discussions ongoing with a couple of customers
items.quote: So that is on the way starting with the aftermarket. And as per agreement with OEM, whatever increase in steel price and something happens, we get it. As of now, we have taken only from a couple of customers and similar discussions are happening with some other OEMs.

items.statement: Order book extends to 2030 with wins in EV motors and wheel hub bearings for launches in FY26-27
items.quote: And some of the listing that we have done here is primarily the wins that we have with electric motors and also some of the wheel hub bearings, primarily the new launches that are upcoming into the '26-'27 financial year. So, this represents quite a strong portfolio and the order book going up to about 2030, basically.

items.statement: EV share currently 6% in 2-wheelers and 4% in passenger vehicles; EV product performance much higher than ICE
items.quote: Yes. I mean the current 2-wheeler is about 6% and then the passenger vehicles is about 4%. Krupa, specific to what you mentioned, certainly the performance of the electric vehicle products is much, much higher than the ICE vehicles.

items.statement: Demerger-related costs minimal in Q4 and not expected going forward
items.quote: We don't have much of the demerger-related costs in Q4 and going forward also, we don't see any demerger-related costs specifically to be in our future.

items.statement: Royalty and trademark fees unchanged from pre-demerger levels
items.quote: Now as far as royalty is concerned, there is no change in any royalty or trademark fees from the earlier settlement. So, it remains the same, how it was pre-demerger.

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 15.3% in FY26, expected to return to 16-19% range soon
items.quote: The EBITDA margin, which you mentioned, okay, so last financial year, if you look at it, it's about 15.3%. So okay, slightly lower than the previous year, what 16%, something you were mentioning for automotive. But we hope it we should be back to the level very soon.

items.statement: New product lines coming at Haridwar plant in FY27 to address capacity shortage
items.quote: And we have limited capacity, which we are anyway working on, as I said, already two new product lines are coming in our Haridwar this year only.

items.statement: Automotive production trending upward for passenger, commercial, 2- and 3-wheelers; iron and steel production up 9.7% YoY in Q4
items.quote: Automotive production has been an upward trend during last q uarter for the passenger vehicle, commercial vehicle as well as 2 and 3 -wheelers. Iron and steel production was highest during Q4 financial year 2026 with 9.7% year -over-year growth

items.statement: White space identified in unitized wheel bearings for SCV/LCV and low-friction transmissions for CAFE-3 norms
items.quote: White space for us is the unitized bearings for the wheel application in the SCV segment and also in the light commercial vehicle, if I had to call out those as an area that we can do significantly well, and we are doing well there. And specifically, the n ew generation transmissions that are coming in for the CAFE-3 norms with our portfolio of low friction, low- weight assortment, that's a space

items.statement: Trading from SKF Industrial due to automotive capacity constraints; expected to reduce as new capacity comes online
items.quote: Because of that, Industrial is we are kind of trading from industrial. About EBITDA, see, this is true that in automotive, we have more localized product. But if you see automotive, it's very price-sensitive market, especially OEM.

items.statement: Focus on margin recovery, sustainable growth, and strengthening customer partnerships
items.quote: As we move forward, our priorities are clear margin recovery, sustainable growth and strengthening partnership with customers and stakeholders.

items.statement: Expects FY27 revenue of INR1,450-1,500 crores, led by Fabric and Garment momentum.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain optimistic about the company's growth trajectory and expect revenues between the range of INR1,450 crores to INR1,500 crores in FY 2027, this in spite of all of the headwinds.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin expected 10.5-11%; near-term may dip as raw material costs are passed on.
items.quote: At the EBITDA level, we expect margins to remain between the range of 10.5% to 11% over the medium-term. Near-term margins may go down as the raw material costs are being passed on.

items.statement: Plans FY27 capex of INR135-140 crores across segments, including sustainability and infrastructure.
items.quote: The capex has been planned around INR135 crores to INR140 crores. And so we will be utilizing this across all the segments.

items.statement: Aims to raise Fabric and Garment share of revenue to nearly 70% over medium term.
items.quote: Our strategic objective remains to further increase our contribution from the Fabric and Garment business to nearly 70% over the medium-term, which we believe will support stronger margin resilience, stickiness to the customers, and improve the overall quality of our revenues.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 may be subdued; Garment momentum expected to improve from Q2 onwards.
items.quote: While quarter one may remain relatively subdued, we do expect business momentum to improve progressively in the Garment business from the second quarter onwards.

items.statement: Targets 20% revenue growth in both Garment and Fabric businesses next year.
items.quote: And we are also targeting growth in the Fabric business next year to the extent of another 20%. So, that's aggressive targets we have set, let's see how much we can achieve.

items.statement: Middle East exposure ~INR100 crores; expects INR10-20 crores reduction in FY27.
items.quote: About INR100 crores to the Middle East. So, we expect maybe about INR10 crores, INR20 crores reduction could happen.

items.statement: Garment division has healthy order book; capacity utilization rose to 72% in FY26 from ~50%.
items.quote: The capacity utilization overall in the Garment business went up to 72% for FY26 compared to maybe 50% or so in FY 2025. The strong performance is supported by a healthy order book, improved execution, and we are hopeful for a strong business momentum towards the final quarter of the new financial year.

items.statement: Garment division projects 18-20% growth for next year.
items.quote: Next year, we are projecting the Garment division is projecting around 18% to 20% growth.

items.statement: Labor shortages in spinning persist into Q1 FY27, impacting capacity utilization.
items.quote: Lower utilization levels during the quarter were primarily due to the labor shortages, particularly in spinning and these challenges have continued to persist during the initial phase of quarter one FY 2027.

items.statement: D2C brand One Mile sales ~INR15 lakhs/month; plans to raise separate funds once sales reach INR1 crore/month.
items.quote: I think that the average sales is now at about INR15 lakhs per month, no more. So, it's still small. As the sales come up, we will, at some point, we want to get it to a level of about INR1 crore a month before we try to raise some funds for this brand separately.

items.statement: Board recommended 20% dividend on face value, total payout INR3.42 crores.
items.quote: I am very pleased to share that the Board of Directors has again recommended a dividend of 20% on face value, translating into a total payout of INR3.42 crores to the shareholders.

items.statement: Long-term debt to reduce from FY2028 onwards; no reduction in FY2027 due to planned capex.
items.quote: But from FY 2028 onwards, you will see a reduction happening in the long-term.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR82 per share for FY26
items.quote: the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR82 per share for the fiscal year.

items.statement: INR958 crore brownfield expansion at Cheyyar facility to reach ~2 million units annual capacity by Q2 FY28
items.quote: INR 958 crores brownfield expansion at our Cheyyar facility in Tamil Nadu to further strengthen our manufacturing capacity. This will take us our annual capacity to almost 2 million units and cases.

items.statement: Greenfield facility planned in Andhra Pradesh for ~2 million units capacity for long-term growth
items.quote: we have also signed up with Andhra Pradesh government for the greenfield project that's kicking in over about 2 million capacity.

items.statement: Royal Enfield dealer and depot inventory at 7-8 days due to temporary manpower and LPG issues, now back on track
items.quote: currently, Royal Enfield, the inventory levels are almost about 7, 8 days, primarily because in the month of May, you know there are issues on the manpower availability due to elections and LPG shortages.

items.statement: Royal Enfield domestic sales grew 23% to 1.1 million units in FY26; April 2026 sales up 57% YoY to 1.04 lakh units
items.quote: Financial year '26, we sold most about 1.11 million motorcycles in India. And there was a solid growth of about 23% over the last financial year. In the month of April 2026, we sold about 1.04 lakh motorcycles, which is actually a 57% growth over the last year.

items.statement: Premium motorcycle segment grew from ~70k/month in 2022-23 to ~1.1 lakh/month; Royal Enfield holds ~90k share and outgrew segment
items.quote: the entire premium motorcycle in 2022, '23, the market size was only almost 70,000, now it has gone to almost about 1.1 lakh per month. And in that time till now in the 1.1 lakh, we are almost about 90,000 plus.

items.statement: Q4 commodity cost impact 90 bps; 70 bps passed via Jan price hike, 20 bps via cost reduction and mix
items.quote: Overall, because of the increase in commodity costs, we've had a total of about 90 basis points in the quarter. We were -- we took a price increase in January and the blended price increase was about 70 basis points. And remaining 20 basis points, we were able to address it through value driven cost reduction as well as model price variance mix.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 incremental commodity headwind 3-3.5% on material cost; 1.75% price hike taken in April covering ~50%; balance via value engineering, austerity, pre-buy
items.quote: it is almost about 3 to 3.5 percentage on the material cost level impact is expected. And what we have done anticipating this and started working on first is before the price increase, we intensified our value engineering. We intensified our cost reduction exercises, some of the austerity measures because it's a war situation, we also have to be prepared for it. And we also did a pricing increase

items.statement: Flying Flea C6 launched in Bangalore April 2026; deliberate city-by-city rollout; initial feedback incredible
items.quote: We ended the year by starting a new journey with the launch of Flying Flea C6, as was mentioned, alongside the opening of our first Flying Flea store in Bangalore in April 2026. The feedback on the FF C6 has been incredible, and we are taking a deliberate city-by-city approach.

items.statement: EML to invest up to INR750 crore for 50% stake in 50-50 JV with Volvo Financial Services India (AUM INR1,806 crore)
items.quote: our investment in this will be up to INR750 crores for the 50% stake in this Volvo Financial Services India. Volvo Financial Services India is in operation here in India for last more than 10 years, and they have assets under management of INR1,806 crores.

items.statement: Capacity expansion investment of INR 958 crores started in April to take overall capacity to 2 million in phases at Cheyyar facility.
items.quote: And the investment which was also clear INR958 crores in April, that has started, and that will take us the overall capacity in phases to 2 million for future because the growth momentum is continuing.

items.statement: Greenfield project MoU signed with Andhra Pradesh government for 261 acres of land for future capacity beyond 2 million.
items.quote: Typically, it will be somewhere around 24 to 30 months window, that's where we will come out with a new plant fully operational.

items.statement: Royal Enfield capacity to increase from 1.4 million to 1.6 million with 500 per day module kicking in from July for festive season.
items.quote: Our capacity declared was about 1.4 million, and we said with the 500 module, which we started off anticipating the growth, that's going to kick in from July because we had to be prepared for festive season.

items.statement: Royal Enfield grew almost 37% in April with top 10 cities growing 24% plus and rural growth continuing.
items.quote: In fact, in the month of April, we grew by almost about 37%. That's what I mentioned. And if I have to tell you about top 10 cities, in top 10 cities, we have grown almost about 24% plus.

items.statement: Brazil grew almost 71% last year, became number 2 in middleweight, and is now a focus as next big market after India.
items.quote: In fact, last year, we grew by almost 71% compared to the previous year. And in Brazil, we have become the number 2 in the middleweight and our product, Guerrilla 450 has won the motorcycle of the year.

items.statement: Europe is a market adjustment year with degrowth and pre-registered OBD2B vehicles not cleared, causing fresh billing delays.
items.quote: Europe continued to degrow. In a degrowing market, we are maintaining our market share. But I must tell you, in Europe, I call it as market adjustment year.

items.statement: VECV announced appropriate price increases of 2% across various vehicles from 1st April to offset commodity inflation of 3-3.5%.
items.quote: We also announced appropriate price increases for that, which is to tune of 2% various vehicles. So that has been announced from 1st April.

items.statement: Commodity pressure expected in range of 3% to 3.5% in first quarter and continuing for the year.
items.quote: I think the commodity pressure is exactly same as what Govind has mentioned. I think we are sailing the same boat. So, which is expected to be in the range of 3% to 3.5% and that's in the first quarter.

items.statement: First-time buyers increasing with 30% of consumers below age 25; replacement cycle yet to kick in but growing in double digits.
items.quote: First-time buyers are going up. In fact, as I mentioned, 30% of our consumers are below the age group of 25. So the first-time buyer percentage is also going up.

items.statement: Election-related manpower migration, LPG availability, commodity and power issues caused 2-3 weeks disturbance in both businesses, now settling.
items.quote: Two things I think in both the businesses, we are also hearing more from that is because of the election there is migrated workmen movement from here and there. That has caused a disturbance and LPG availability was causing an issue.

items.statement: Vehicle finance JV to invest up to INR 750 crores additional capital; existing net worth INR 500 crores, debt-equity at 3x, targeting 5-6x leverage.
items.quote: We are now going to put up to INR750 crores into the balance sheet and they already have net worth of around INR500 crores and their current debt equity is only around 3.

items.statement: VECV has reasonably good order book in electric bus segment across 9m, 12m, 13.5m buses for public and private demand.
items.quote: And we go by the current order book, our current demand, but we have a reasonably good order book business right now.

items.statement: Flying Flea electric motorcycle launched in Bangalore in one store, city-by-city rollout planned; test ride inquiries very good.
items.quote: We have launched the product. Now booking has just started. We had gone into Bangalore only in one store, slowly, we are building up because we know we are not in a rush.

items.statement: Bullet 650 dispatch already started; S6 and other EICMA products on track with no delays.
items.quote: A bullet 650 is on the cards. It's just going to come because that I can share it with you because the dispatch is already started.

items.statement: VECV expects MHCV industry growth to continue if economy grows and infrastructure investments continue; April industry sales extremely well.
items.quote: If the Indian economy continues to grow, if we suppose government is able to continue to make infrastructure investments and the economy grows, then there is no reason why the CV industry will not grow.

items.statement: International markets cautiously optimistic; US tariff issues only 3% of total market, Europe degrowing but maintaining share.
items.quote: Currently, what is happening in the macro, most of the markets, especially United States, you all know, and there are tariff issues, confusions, which are all getting settled, but that's only about 3% of the total market for us.

items.statement: Digital business achieved positive EBITDA in FY26, meeting guidance given at start of year
items.quote: For the full year FY26, a strong revenue growth was seen at 53%. With a balanced cost structure, it resulted in delivering a positive EBITDA in FY26 compared to a loss of INR5,480 million in the previous year. This also marked the first year in which our digital business has delivered a positive EBITDA on a comparable basis, achieving the guidance which we had given at the start of the year.

items.statement: ZEE5 at optimum investment level; may increase slightly but won't impact EBITDA materially
items.quote: I believe that we are at optimum level of investments on the ZEE5 or the digital front. At some point in time, we may choose to up our investments, but they will not move the needle to the extent that it will start impacting our EBITDA line.

items.statement: Board approved INR20 crore investment in CORE Private Limited for Live business and up to INR116 crore in Phantom Digital Effects Limited for AVGC capabilities
items.quote: Firstly, an investment of INR20 crores was approved in respect of CORE Private Limited, CORE stands for Culture of Real Experiences. So, this will help drive our Live business. Secondly, an investment of up to INR116 crores was also approved, as Punit mentioned, in Phantom Digital Effects Limited

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin at 6.9% in Q4 FY26; would have been similar to Q3 excluding one-offs and lower ad revenue from Middle East conflict
items.quote: With a 7% decline in operating revenue and optimizing our other fixed costs during the quarter, our adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 6.9%. Further, we had higher costs due to legal expenses in quarter 4. Excluding these one-offs and lower advertising revenue on account of the Middle East conflict, our margins would have been similar to quarter 3.

items.statement: Revised movie amortization policy to 50% in first 2 years, balance 50% over next 3 years (previously straight-line over 5 years)
items.quote: We've had a look at the various patterns of consumption, and we have changed that estimate to make it more front-ended to increase it to 50% in the first 2 years and then the balance in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Advertising revenue declined 4% YoY in Q4 due to Middle East conflict impacting March; adjusted for March impact, would have seen low single-digit growth
items.quote: On the advertising front, we did witness healthy traction in the initial months of Jan and Feb. However, March was severely impacted with the ongoing Middle East conflict where advertisers have held back their spends in the end of the quarter. As a result, our overall advertising revenues declined 4% year-on-year.

items.statement: Digital revenue grew 71% YoY to INR4,700 million in Q4 FY26, highest ever; full year FY26 growth 53% with positive EBITDA vs loss of INR5,480 million prior year
items.quote: We witnessed continued momentum in our revenues, which grew 71% year-on-year basis for Q4 FY26 to INR4,700 million. This quarter has also marked our highest ever revenues in the digital business. For the full year FY26, a strong revenue growth was seen at 53%.

items.statement: Prolonged West Asia crisis creating challenging advertising environment in near term; advertisers adopting cautious approach
items.quote: While the advertising environment looks challenging in the immediate near term amidst the prolonged West Asia crisis, we do believe that the investments in strategic levers during the financial year '26, along with our digital proposition, positions us well from a medium-term perspective.

items.statement: Network share increased 80 bps YoY to 17.4% in Q4; Zee TV GRP growth 40% YoY with 21% stronger performance than closest competitor for 26 weeks
items.quote: As we look at the viewership share, as Punit also mentioned, we exited the month of March with a network share of more than 18%, while for the quarter, it stood at 17.4%, a gain of 80 basis points on a year-on-year basis. Our flagship Hindi GEC Zee TV has witnessed higher GRP with nearly 21% stronger performance than its closest competitors for 26 weeks straight.

items.statement: Music business: 217 billion total video views, 176 million YouTube subscribers, 20,000+ song library; profitability healthy, expanding across language markets
items.quote: During the year, we have garnered over 217 billion total video views with more than 176 million subscribers on YouTube. This performance was driven by our new age music catalog and a rich library of over 20,000 songs. Profitability in the music business remains healthy, and we continue to diversify our catalogue across additional language markets.

items.statement: Employee cost optimization: reduced to 9% of revenue target (from current lower levels), achieved through role evaluation and manpower rationalization over 1 year
items.quote: If you go back 4, 5 years before the pandemic, we used to operate at 9% people cost to revenue, and we are trying to bring it back to that, and that's what our objective is going to be.

items.statement: Cash and treasury investments at INR27.6 billion as of March 2026 (cash INR7.5B, FDs INR7.8B, MFs INR12.3B)
items.quote: Cash and treasury investments as of March 2026 stood at a healthy INR27.6 billion, comprising of cash balance of INR7.5 billion, fixed deposits and other treasury investments of INR7.8 billion and mutual fund investments of INR12.3 billion.

items.statement: Content inventory advances and deposits at INR67.6 billion as of March 2026, down INR2.8 billion YoY due to optimized fresh acquisitions and accelerated amortization
items.quote: As a result of the above and optimized fresh acquisitions, the content inventory advances and deposits as of March '26 stood at INR67.6 billion, down by INR2.8 billion on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: ZEE5 digital ad revenue growing extremely handsomely QoQ and YoY, moving toward 50-50 ad-subscription balance in medium term
items.quote: the good news, which is what I can tell you is it continues to grow extremely handsomely on a quarter-on-quarter basis, and it is moving into the territory of us with our aspiration of becoming ad and subscription more like balance of 50-50 in the medium term.

items.statement: Provision for doubtful debts of ~INR70 crore made conservatively at year-end based on debtor aging; amounts considered collectible
items.quote: These are made on a conservative basis, Umang, and they are all collectible, but we make these provisions especially at the end of the year, taking into account the age of the debtors and receivables, and we make these provisions.

items.statement: Publication business expected to grow ~15% in each of first two years of curriculum change cycle.
items.quote: Now with respect to growth, at least in the first 2 years, we are clearly seeing growth of around 15% in a single year.

items.statement: Domestic stationery revenue expected to grow ~15% in FY27 including new categories.
items.quote: So in domestic stationery business, we are expecting growth of 1-5, 15%, including our new category in launches that we have already done so far. So we are expecting around 15% growth.

items.statement: Export stationery growth guided at higher single-digit 8-9% for FY27 due to tariff uncertainty.
items.quote: So I would say single higher-digit growth will be an estimation, around 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Stationery EBITDA margin expected ~9% in current year post brand expenses, improving to 9.5-10% next year.
items.quote: So we should be making around 9% margin in the current year post these expenses. And in the subsequent year, around 9.5% to 10% versus around 13-odd percent that we are making on a regular basis.

items.statement: Publication EBIT margin expected at least 200 bps better than last year on double-digit revenue growth.
items.quote: So there will be at least 200 basis points better margin than the current year -- than the last year.

items.statement: India capex minimal at INR25-30 crores; UAE project on hold due to geopolitical tensions.
items.quote: So it would be just hardly INR25 crores, INR30 crores of investments.

items.statement: South Gujarat plant total investment INR65 crores including land; asset turnover 1x first year, 2x second, 2.5x thereafter.
items.quote: So altogether, we have invested INR65 crores, including buying of a land.

items.statement: Export price reductions reversed; margins to normalize with less than 100 bps impact for full year.
items.quote: But for the year, it will be hardly impacted in not even 100 basis points. It will be more or less lesser than that.

items.statement: Paper prices up ~8% from lowest level; no further increases expected for 3-4 months.
items.quote: So the paper that we use in last 1 quarter, we have seen around 8% jump from its lowest level that it had gone down last year.

items.statement: Scaling non-paper stationery and digital commerce; paper capacity ~80% utilized, outsourcing non-paper initially.
items.quote: On paper capacity, I would say we are quite highly utilized. So on an annual basis, I can say around 80%.

items.statement: Export growth may be reduced by 5-7% due to inflation impact on US customers.
items.quote: But nevertheless, we all may discount by around 5% to 7% impact, which we have to reduce from our growth expectation on a conservative basis.

items.statement: Indiannica to merge with Navneet for cost synergies; awaiting approvals.
items.quote: So we have filed for -- rather we have decided to merge it with Navneet and the major reason being that a lot of cost that are duplicated at both the locations and both the companies individually gets reduced.

items.statement: No plans to demerge stationery and publishing businesses currently.
items.quote: So as on date, the numbers are not that big even for stationery independently. So there are no plans right now, no thoughts also right now to demerge the business.

items.statement: Management believes the company is in a position to achieve upwards of 20% growth in FY27.

items.statement: Smart meter shunt revenue grew ~33% to ~70 crore in FY26.
items.quote: almost 33% growth in shunt, from the energy meters, which is around, 70 crore odd rupees.

items.statement: US shunt customer revenue expected to return to peak levels in FY27 and surpass in FY28, all in higher-margin component form.
items.quote: we expect that in this year and the year after, we expect numbers to reach, and then probably in the year after that, to go beyond what its highest numbers were when we used to supply those larger volumes of strip two or three years ago to them. So we expect the business to come back to those levels, or almost back to those levels, at least in this year, and then probably surpass it next FY27-28.

items.statement: No substantial growth capex needed beyond 10-15 crore annual maintenance and automation capex.
items.quote: Yes. So, there's no substantial capex required, but still, as we mentioned earlier also, we need some maintenance capex along with some automation capex, which is in the range of, 10 to 15 crore year-on-year. So, we are not yet seeing any substantial amount which needs to be deployed for expansion.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded ~250 bps to 22.9% in FY26 driven by better realisations, mix, operating leverage and cost discipline.
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by around 250 basis points to 22.9%, which demonstrates that growth was supported by better realisations, improved product mix, operating leverage and continued cost discipline.

items.statement: Shunt realization improved 10-12% as component mix rose from 55% to 65% of supply.
items.quote: earlier we used to supply regarding 55% in component, which goes up to 65% in year-on-year. And that is yielding almost 10-12% improved realization, as per the previous, per kg shunt realization.

items.statement: Standalone revenue grew despite stable volumes due to better realisation and higher-value component contribution.
items.quote: On a standalone basis, revenue grew despite broadly stable product volumes, indicating better average realisation and increasing contribution from higher-value components. This is consistent with our long-term direction of reducing dependence on lower value-added strip-led supply and increasing our presence in engineered components and assemblies.

items.statement: US customer concentration peaked at 38-39%, fell to 13-14%, expected to stabilize at 16-18% even if volumes recover.
items.quote: From its peak, it's come down from nearly 38-39%, It came down to about 13-14%. And now, when it goes back to those levels, it will come back to an 18-19% level, at the most. Most likely, it should be less than that, but I'm saying even if their volumes do go up as expected, it will not go beyond that number. Maybe 16% to 18%.

items.statement: Metallor JV converted to 100% subsidiary in 2023 after partner exited parent business.
items.quote: this is no longer a JV, it's a 100% subsidiary of Shivalik, and this used to be a JV until 2023, And, at that time, the JV partner was exiting their overall, the parent company business, and as a result, we had the opportunity to buy their equity in the business, and now it's a wholly owned subsidiary.

items.statement: Confident of improved top-line and bottom-line in FY27, subject to no prolonged Middle East conflict impact.

items.quote: We have incurred a cumulative capex of INR27 crores in FY’26 and plan to close FY’27 with an additional capex of around INR10 crores.

items.quote: In Canada, it will be something in the region of about CAD 4 million, which is roughly about INR25 crores or INR30 crores currently, right?

items.statement: Operating margin expected to improve automatically as volumes increase without major overhead expansion.
items.quote: There will be, because as we increase the volume, the operating margin automatically will improve because we are not focusing on any major overhead expansion.

items.statement: Quickmill expects much better FY27 performance with focus on export markets outside North America.

items.statement: Textile industry is in a much better phase than 12 months ago, driving demand for machinery.
items.quote: the textile industry is going through a much better phase than what it was, say, 12 months ago.

items.statement: FY27 guidance subject to no further adverse impact from prolonged Middle East conflict on global and Indian economy.
items.quote: However, this is subject to not having any further impact, if any, on the global and Indian economy in the event of a prolonged conflict in the Middle East.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio at 0.28x, intends to sustain this level going forward.
items.quote: our debt-to-equity ratio now comfortably at 0.28x, a level we intend to sustain going forward.

items.statement: Management endeavors to deliver mid-20s EBITDA margin going forward with aim to improve further
items.quote: We continue to maintain that we endeavor to deliver mid -20s kind of margin going forward with an endeavor to improve further wherever there are areas of improvement.

items.quote: As we have seen these things move and as we have stated earlier, achieving a INR 500 crore – INR 600 crore top line is when you would see these things move into a positive phase.
