items.statement: Capex for FY27 expected to be similar to FY26 levels
items.quote: Like for the current year already, it's available. So we don't see any significant capex growth than last year. It will continue to sustain.

items.statement: NorUDCA has healthy order book for upcoming quarters
items.quote: Our Novel product, NorUDCA, which was launched in India in the previous quarter, continues to gain traction, and the strong reception has tran slated directly into a healthy order book for the upcoming quarters

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement driven by operating leverage; 35% target ambitious but not immediate
items.quote: As far as EBITDA margins are concerned, Kiran, the fact is that as the business grows, a bit of operational leverage does kick in, right? But obviously 35% is an ambitious target, which we would be working towards achieving. But we can't really say that it would be achieved immediately because whilst we grow the business, we also have to spend more for growing the business.

items.statement: Raw material and solvent prices have increased significantly but availability is not an issue
items.quote: yes, we don't see any major challenges on that, but only the prices have gone up significantly. So that is the only thing, but availability is there, no problem.

items.statement: Focus on complex differentiated products, vertical integration, and CDMO across API, formulations, biologics and ADCs
items.quote: We are building a highly differentiated pharmaceutical platform spanning across complex APIs, specialty formulations, biologics and ADCs with integrated CDMO capabilities.

items.statement: Jadcherla USFDA audit observations addressed, re-audit pending; no revenue impact expected as US focus shifted to third-party CMOs
items.quote: So we have very complex differentiated products, which we want to launch. So our major focus on U.S. will be from third-party CMOs. There is no issue with the FDA. It's just that the facility when the audit happened, the FDA has given some observations. We have done the compliance. And now we are again waiting for the reaudit of that.

items.statement: Aflibercept licensing income higher than Adalimumab; major milestones expected in FY27 on launch and one-year completion
items.quote: So, we have received only a few milestones in last few financial years. But a major part of milestone will be received in the current financial year on launch and then on one year completion. And the licensing income Is higher than Adalimumab.

items.statement: CDMO revenue approximately INR110 crores in API and similar in biologics for FY26
items.quote: For the full year on the API side of the business, we have clocked approximately around INR110 crores of CDMO business. And we are also doing similar CDMO business on the biologics side also.

items.statement: Oncology breakthrough molecule for innovator expected to be meaningful in FY28
items.quote: Yes, we expect it should be meaningful in FY28.

items.statement: NorUDCA Europe and ROW launch expected FY29; ROW revenues may start FY28
items.quote: Even NorUDCA would be in FY29 for Europe, but if I tell you about ROW market, we will start seeing revenues in FY28 in ROW markets.

items.statement: Nivolumab, ADC product and 2 NBE programs entering human global studies in FY27; Europe/ROW commercial revenues expected FY29
items.quote: I think in the current financial year, Nivolumab . ADC product and 2 NBE products, will be entering human global studies in current financial year. We expect sometime in FY29, the commercial revenues to start in from Europe and ROW.

items.statement: Adjusted ROCE excluding biologics and albumin investments improved from 4% in FY23 to 17.4% in FY26
items.quote: where our adjusted ROCE, excluding investments made in high -growth potential businesses like biologics and albumin, has seen a significant improvement from 4% in FY23 to 17.4% in FY26.

items.statement: Net debt increased to INR613 crores from INR550 crores; capex of INR361 crores in FY26 funded primarily by internal accruals
items.quote: On the debt front, our net debt for the year increased to INR613 crores from INR550 crores in the previous year, which is in line with the growth in our business operations. And our capex of INR361 crores in FY26 was primarily funded by internal accruals and deployed in key verticals of API, CDMO and albumin facility.

items.statement: Order book at March 2026 is INR 1,044.31 crore, up from INR 656.68 crore in December 2025.
items.quote: The order book position is INR 1,044.31 crore including INR 899.44 crore of product business, and INR 144.87 crores of project and services business.

items.statement: Order book rose to upwards of INR 1,000 crore in FY26 versus around INR 600 crore last financial year.
items.quote: If you talk about order book, we are sitting at the close of March, 2026 in the upwards of INR 1,000 crores as compared to last financial year of around INR 600 crores.

items.statement: Robust order book will positively impact revenue for quite a few quarters, with revenue recognition lagging due to implementation cycles.
items.quote: But however, this robust order book is going to definitely positively impact in positive terms for quite a few quarters.

items.statement: Revenue from new orders may not reflect immediately, possibly taking one or two quarters due to implementation cycles.
items.quote: So that is why you are saying it might not be immediately reflective in revenue, maybe in immediate one or two quarters, but definitely once the implementation is done, we should see that revenue flowing in our books.

items.statement: New orders majorly from India and US, with a few from other geographies.
items.quote: And if we talk about geographies from where we have got this order, happy to share that one of the order which we have booked is from US, and most of the orders are from India.

items.statement: Added seven new logos in FY26 versus three in FY25, showing promising trajectory.
items.quote: So, we have added seven new logos this year. In financial year FY26 versus three logos in FY25, so trajectory is promising, and moving in the right direction.

items.statement: Japan market active discussions with top banks; results may come in upcoming quarter.
items.quote: So we have been making a conscious effort to tap some of the top Japanese banks, and there are some active discussions which are currently on, and we might see some results in upcoming quarter, because it takes time actually to get that the required level of confidence on the new product.

items.statement: Focus on co-lending, gold loan, and finance against security as key lines of business for investment.
items.quote: And even in this current GA, which is getting released, both this line of businesses are being strengthened, be it co-lending, be it gold loan, and we have also strengthening the finance against security as going to be the potential line of business, as we have understood the market.

items.statement: Deals are hybrid model, mostly long-term, with some subscription-based revenue.
items.quote: A part of the revenue definitely is subscription-based fees as well. But ours, it is a hybrid model on which we work. And most of the deals are long term deals.

items.statement: Bajaj Finance left due to strategic investment in a competitor, not pricing or software issues.
items.quote: Okay so Bajaj Finance is not because of any other reason, but I would say they have been, on their own invested in a company which is a competitor to us so that was a strategic reason with which this decision was taken.

items.statement: No significant customer loss or movement in modules or complete exit over last three years.
items.quote: There is no significant loss or movement from any of our customers in terms of either module or moving out completely.

items.statement: Some Middle East orders postponed due to war situation.
items.quote: And, additionally, there were a few orders, at least couple of them which got postponed from Middle East because of the war situation.

items.statement: Headcount approx. 2,000, stable over last few quarters.
items.quote: So head count at the end of the quarter was approx. 2,000, and which is pretty much same as maintained across last few quarters if you see.

items.statement: Sales team grew by 40-50 executives in last two years; new Chief Business Officer onboarded.
items.quote: This has led to a growth of about a headcount of anywhere between 40 to 50 sales executives in the team, and this is across all sales domains.

items.statement: Expects H1 FY27 stable for export-oriented watch component business, with growth more visible in H2.
items.quote: Even though Swiss watches continue to face headwinds in several markets, we expect H1 FY27, that is this year, to remain relatively stable for the export -oriented business, with growth being more visible during the second half of the year.

items.statement: Bracelets business to continue good revenue growth this year and next, but margins may moderate near term.
items.quote: Based on current visibility, we expect the Bracelets business to continue delivering good revenue growth in this financial year and the next financial year, though margins may be moderated in the near term due to lower price points of newer customers, which are fueling growth.

items.statement: Bracelets and Precision Engineering to grow at about 25% CAGR medium to long term; watch components less.
items.quote: But in the medium and long term, both these businesses we believe they will grow at abo ut 25% CAGR. The watch component business will probably grow a little bit less than that.

items.statement: Ornapac packaging expected to become profitable in H2 of current financial year.
items.quote: While the business currently is showing a loss at its ramp-up stage, we expect the division to become profitable during the second half of the current financial year.

items.statement: Favre-Leuba sales expected to more than double in FY27 with expanded global footprint.
items.quote: We expect to more than double the sales in FY27 and greatly expand our global footprint with exciting new product launches.

items.statement: Planned capex of approximately INR50 crores across businesses in FY27, including maintenance and growth.
items.quote: From an overall capital allocation perspective, we have planned capex of approximately INR50 crores across businesses during FY27.

items.statement: Major part of FY27 capex for Precision Engineering and bracelet; Eigen capex to commission in 3-4 months.
items.quote: Going forward, for the next year, when we have shared that approximately INR50 crores is planned to be invested in the capex, it is spread over all the businesses. But the major part will be for the Precision Engineering and the bracelet.

items.statement: No great change expected in margin picture over this year; margins to remain stable.
items.quote: What we can say is that we do not expect any great change in the margin picture over this year.

items.statement: Ethos has room to pass on 7-8% price increase due to Swiss franc appreciation, to improve margins.
items.quote: I think averagely, there is a room for improvement of 7%, -8% easily over there right now. We are definitely 7%- 8% below what we need to be right now in general.

items.statement: Domestic business expected to remain robust with healthy demand and localization opportunities.
items.quote: We expect the domestic business to continue to remain robust, supported by healthy demand trends and incr easing localization opportunities within India, which will show up in our growth numbers.

items.statement: Ethos to launch new format targeting INR25,000 to INR2 lakh price point, expanding beyond luxury.
items.quote: We will also be launching a format. We believe that the threat from wearables is over, and that allows us a lot of expansion back in a price point between INR25,000 and INR2 lakhs.

items.statement: Global economic uncertainty and weak luxury demand in China/Europe may impact inventory planning and procurement.
items.quote: The global watch industry also operated in a challenging environment during the year, weak consumer demand in key luxury markets, particularly China and certain parts of Europe, continue t o weigh on industry growth, while global brands remained cautious inventory planning and procurement decisions amid uncertain macro

items.statement: Bracelet capacity utilization at 75-80% this year; expanding to 110,000-120,000 units in 12 months.
items.quote: But if I were to say that, I think we are going to expand from the current or from the original level of about 75,000 over the next 12 months to about 110,000 to 120,000.

items.statement: Ethos aims to double boutique network in next 3 years, focusing on company-owned stores.
items.quote: I do believe that if things go well, we should be doubling our network of boutiques in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Expect double-digit volume growth in FY27 with incremental 2.5 million tons or more
items.quote: So we should be in FY 27, we should also be growing in a double -digit growth. So we expect the market to grow, say, around 6% to 8%. And as far as our volumes are concerned, so as we said, we should get incremental definitely 2.5 million tons incremental volume, maybe more.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR3,500-4,000 crores; FY28 at INR1,500-2,000 crores
items.quote: For this year, the capex should be in the range of INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores. Amit: Okay. And next year? Ajay Saraogi: Next year, it would be INR1,500 crores to INR2,000 crores

items.statement: Jaisalmer integrated unit cost INR3,630 crores, INR742 crores spent by March, commissioning H1 FY28
items.quote: The project cost for this -- for the integrated unit is expected around INR3,630 crores, and we have already spent about INR742 crores up to March. We expect the commissioning in H1 of FY28.

items.statement: Target INR50 per ton cost savings in FY27 from green power and AFR in existing operations
items.quote: We see another INR50 which we should get in this fiscal, mainly coming -- mainly driven by, a, on the green power and some -- and on AFR in the South and the North plants.

items.statement: Passed on ~INR10 per bag price increase in April-May covering ~18% of cost inflation
items.quote: So we could say that because you had inventory and other things in the month of April in the May, we would have on an averag e a price increase of about INR 10 a bag. So INR10 would mean, say, 18% less of that.

items.statement: No regulatory issues foreseen for Punjab grinding unit; land acquired, orders placed, commissioning H1 FY28
items.quote: As of now, I mean it's very difficult to say, but we are -- we don't foresee I mean wherever -- what we have identified that there should be any issues. But if there are, we will inform everyone. But as of now, there are no issues.

items.statement: Green power share to reach ~55% in FY27 from ~52%; 80 MW in process
items.quote: FY '27, it should increase by 2%, 3% because we are -- some approvals from the state government and from the [ group 0:49:26 ] power, the listing is there. I think this should be closer to 55% by FY '27.

items.statement: Employee cost FY27 to rise 12-14% YoY from INR937 crores base due to increments and new plants
items.quote: So we do expect that from the whole year num ber of INR937 crores, there could be about 12% to 14% increase year-on-year.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA 1.45x, net debt/equity 0.48x as of March 2026; gross debt INR5,136 crores
items.quote: The net debt to EBITDA is 1.45. The equity is INR6,961 crores. The net debt to equity is 0.48. These are the major highlights.

items.statement: Panna project saving INR200-300 crores vs INR2,850 crores budget; railway siding spillover remains
items.quote: What is happening in case of Panna, there is some spillover capex and expenditure remaining to the railway siding. Number two, I'm happy to inform that out of INR2,850 crores, there would be a good amount, at least INR200 crores to INR250 crores saving -- about INR300 crores saving in Panna.

items.statement: Management refrains from giving annual FY27 guidance; will provide guidance by middle of Q2 FY27
items.quote: We would like to wait middle end of quarter 2 to put a number to it.

items.statement: Long-term revenue target of INR6,000-6,200 crores by FY29 or latest by FY30 remains on track
items.quote: We should be on track to attaining this INR6,000 crores plus in FY '29 or latest by FY '30 because there are certain other things on the annual, which will also aid us in achieving this.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at INR200 crores including land, defense plant, and maintenance; new tower crane factory of INR400+ crores need-based
items.quote: So I think including land, our capex for this year should all be put together should be close to INR200 crores. And we also intend to make a new tower crane factory where we envisage a capex of upwards of INR400 crores.

items.statement: Defense order book of INR575 crores pending execution; expect INR200-220 crores revenue from defense in FY27
items.quote: We have about INR575 crores order book pending in defense. That will happen. Some exports will also increase. But to put a number to it at this juncture would not be prudent.

items.statement: Target to sustain EBITDA margin (ex-other income) in 15-16% range through calibrated price actions
items.quote: We are hopeful that we should be able to sustain our margin profile, EBITDA without other income in the range of around 15% to 16%.

items.statement: Price increases of 1% in Jan, ~4% on May 1, and 5% from June 1; total 9-10% so far, may need 11-14% to offset steel-led cost inflation
items.quote: We've already increased our prices. I'll talk of the calendar year in January, we took a 1%, 1.5% general inflation price increase. And only on 1st of May, we've again increased our prices by close to about 4%, maybe a little more. And from 1st of June onwards, we are again pushing in a price increase of another 5%. This will bring the total to 9% to 10%. But I think looking at the overall cost in

items.statement: Q1 FY27 demand strong; tower crane order books full; expect growth in backhoe loaders, material handling, and hydra cranes recovery
items.quote: As of now, things are looking good. But what happens in Q2, Q3, I think middle end of Q2 is a precise time we should be able to guide even on an annual guidance.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks (West Asia conflict, crude oil spike, rupee depreciation) causing input cost volatility and demand uncertainty; anti-dumping duties on Chinese cranes not yet notified by Finance Ministry
items.quote: At the same time, we remain mindful of the evolving geopolitical environment, which could lead to temporary supply chain disruptions and demand side hyperinflation and input cost volatility.

items.statement: Other income negative in Q4 due to mark-to-market losses on investments; expect recovery to INR20-35 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Most probably we should be hopeful that it would get back in the range of anywhere between INR20 crores to INR35 crores, right Luthra?

items.statement: Blended capacity utilization at ~60% for cranes, metal handling, construction equipment; tower crane capacity 950-1,000 units
items.quote: Our blended capacity utilization for cranes, metal handling and construction equipment stands at around 60%, which provides us with enough headroom to capitalize on any immediate demand uptick in the future.

items.statement: Export and defense revenue target 10-15% of crane/construction equipment segment (currently ~9%); FY27 target ~5-6% defense, ~6-7% exports
items.quote: Within this year itself, hopefully, we should be doing close to about 5% to 6% revenue contribution from defense and about 6%, 7% from export. So that will take us anywhere between 11% to 13% plus with respect to our -- within the Cranes and Construction Equipment segment.

items.statement: Chinese competitors' costs rising 8-10% due to local assembly; ACE sees competitive advantage but anti-dumping duties not yet implemented
items.quote: So their costs are going to go upside by 8% to 10%, which will make us more competitive but the costs are going up because of trying to do local manufacturing.

items.statement: QRSAM missile program orders received; building prototypes for two integration companies; material handling for ammunition loading/unloading only
items.quote: We have got a couple of orders for -- this is called QRSAM, quick response surface to air missile. And we are currently working on building protos for two different integration companies for the same program who have been allotted to work on that.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected 27-30%, subject to Middle East war headwinds.
items.quote: We are confident of achieving a long-term growth in the -- in revenue in excess of 20%, with revenue this year expected to cross 27% to 30% for the year, subject to the headwinds with respect to the economic conditions on account of the war in the Middle East.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow guidance INR3,000 crores.
items.quote: So order inflow guidance for FY '27 is about INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected around 14% for FY27, long-term target 14%.
items.quote: The long-term EBITDA guidance continues to be in excess of 13% and with higher-margin business, like I said earlier, of signaling and Africa, we expect this to be 100 points better at around the 14% mark for the full year.

items.statement: Average annual capex INR70-75 crores for next couple of years, including HAM contract.
items.quote: So I would say, on an average for the next couple of years, capex would be, including the HAM contract, would be about INR70 crores / INR75 crores.

items.statement: Total order book INR4,476 crores, ~3.5x FY26 revenues.
items.quote: Our total order book stands at INR4,476 crores, which is approximately 3.5 times our FY '26 revenues.

items.statement: Signaling business margin ~20%, revenue expected INR120-130 crores in FY27.
items.quote: The signaling business has a margin profile of almost 20% compared to the 13% / 14% for the traditional infra business that we were doing. We expect that business to have a revenue this year of almost INR120 crores / INR130 crores.

items.statement: Signaling order inflow expected INR150-200 crores in FY27.
items.quote: We anticipate -- we do expect almost INR150 crores to INR200 crores of order inflows in this financial year.

items.statement: May execution strong, labor back; H1 FY27 to catch up on delayed revenues.
items.quote: We anticipate this to be adjusted in the first half. Like I said to the previous question, to the previous person lady that we expect, April to be slightly subdued on account of elections again, but -- so the first quarter, we'll not do the full catch-up, but the first half, we will do the full catch-up.

items.statement: Middle East war and currency volatility are key risks to growth targets.
items.quote: 40% is even better, but that, I think, is -- you do have to be mindful of the economic situation with respect to war in the Middle East and also how the currency is playing out, because at the end of the day, you are relying on government payments for the public capex.

items.statement: Alcon acquisition completed; merger with GPT approved, expected this financial year.
items.quote: This merger is with the appointed date of April 1, 2026 and is expected to be completed in this financial year, subject to regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue INR414.7 crores, up 8.9% YoY.
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, revenues for the fourth quarter -- for the quarter stood at INR414.7 crores compared to INR380.7 crores, representing a growth of 8.9% year-on-year.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated PAT INR97.3 crores, up 21.5% YoY.
items.quote: In terms of the PAT numbers, the consolidated PAT for FY '26 stood at INR97.3 crores, a growth of 21.5% from INR80 crores last year.

items.statement: Board declared third interim dividend INR1/share; total FY26 dividend INR2.75/share.
items.quote: I'm happy to also note that the Board has declared a third-interim dividend of INR1 per share, taking the total dividend payout for the year to INR2.75 per share that is 27.5%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected at 15% or more, potentially reaching INR600 crores.
items.quote: Yes, absolutely, sir. How are you?

items.statement: FY28 revenue could reach INR700 crores if growth continues.
items.quote: Absolutely right, subject to Mr. Trump's behavior.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to improve by 15-16% with revenue increase, despite new restaurant costs.
items.quote: So we would be able to improve to the extent of 15%, 16% over a percentage increase on EBITDA numbers with the increase in revenues because of the front-end cost of the new restaurants, which would continue to open over the next 2 years.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR40 crores for renovations and new stores.
items.quote: This would be INR40 crores.

items.statement: INR32 crores for 8 new restaurants and INR5 crores for QSR/confectionery in FY27.
items.quote: INR 32 crores approximately for the restaurants and rest around INR 5 crores for the QSR and confectionery.

items.statement: Focus on seven key brands; no expansion of other brands despite profitability.
items.quote: The focus brands currently remain to be Mainland China, Asia Kitchen, Haka, Gong, Siciliana, Walters and Sweet Bengal.

items.statement: Mitigating LPG/PNG supply risk by shifting to induction woks; 78% of chain converted, targeting 100% in 20 days.
items.quote: So we are prepared to 78%. We are going to 100% in exactly 20 days. So we are fully prepared to ensure that the show must go on.

items.statement: Cash on books at INR162.48 crores; net cash INR103 crores as of March end.
items.quote: Sir, INR 162.48 crores.

items.statement: Targets Rs 5,000 crore disbursements and Rs 18,000 crore AUM for FY27.
items.value: Rs.5000 Crores disbursement, Rs.18,000 Crores AUM
items.quote: Current year, the target we want to achieve a disbursement of approximately Rs.5000 Crores disbursement and I am expecting a prepayment as well as repayment of about Rs.2940 Crores, out of Rs.2940 Crores approximately Rs.2060 Crores will go to AUM, remaining used to set off my prepayments as well as repayments. So, my

items.statement: Expects to achieve Rs 25,000 crore AUM in two years, i.e., FY29.
items.quote: Two years down the line, yes, we will be in a position to achieve Rs.25,000 Crores AUM.

items.statement: Aims to maintain spread of 3.2-3.25% in FY27, lower than previous quarters.
items.quote: For current financial year, we would like to maintain a spread of in and around 3.2%to 3.25%.

items.statement: NHB refinance of Rs 600 crore expected to reduce cost of funds by 10-15 bps.
items.quote: My guess is we will get a cost benefit of in and around 10-basis to 15-basis points immediately.

items.statement: Stage 2 assets targeted to reduce below 5% by end of FY27.
items.quote: So going forward, we can reduce the stage 2 accounts below 5% before the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Expects growth from non-TN states, especially Karnataka, Andhra, Telangana, Maharashtra, MP, Rajasthan.
items.quote: So my non-TN is poised to give me good numbers for this year.

items.statement: Plans to maintain quarterly disbursement momentum above Rs 1,000 crore.
items.quote: We want to maintain the momentum, we want to maintain the trend of doing more than Rs.1000 Crores in a quarter. This trend will continue.

items.statement: Plans to continue higher dividend trend, not one-off.
items.quote: Continue this, we want to maintain this trend. It is not a one-off thing like what I discussed in my concall. As a management, we want to continue this trend.

items.statement: CSR spending to be 2-3% of average profit going forward, down from 5%.
items.quote: My idea is about 2% to 3%, not more than that.

items.statement: Plans inorganic book purchase of Rs 25-30 crore in FY27.
items.quote: We may do in this financial year about Rs.25 Crores to Rs.30 Crores, not more than that.

items.statement: Reduced benchmark rate twice in FY26, by 10 bps each, impacting yield.
items.quote: July 1 we have reduced 10-basis points and again February 1 we have reduced our 10 basis points.

items.statement: Prepayments and BT Out remain a challenge due to vintage book and customer profile.
items.quote: For a 25 year of old Company pre-payment, pre-closures, it is very difficult to avoid. Market also is very competitive.

items.statement: Expects non-TN states to contribute significantly from Q2 FY27.
items.quote: If not in Q1, at least in Q2, I am looking at a much, much higher contribution from non-TN states, Rajiv.

items.statement: No immediate reduction in bank borrowing costs expected; maintaining cost of funds challenging.
items.quote: My guess is next quarter, I am not expecting any reduction in cost of funds and maintaining this cost of funds will be really challenging.

items.statement: Medium-term revenue growth estimate remains close to 15%
items.quote: And in the medium term, our estimate remains close to the 15% growth projections that we had given earlier.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion of 200+ beds over next 24 months at average cost of INR 45 lakh per bed
items.quote: So on these are all brownfield expansion and average cost is about INR 45 lakh per bed. So that is about INR90-100 crore for 200 beds.

items.statement: Plan to add 1,000 beds by FY30 with 400 from greenfield and 600 from brownfield
items.quote: So, we have maintained that we will be adding about 1,000 beds by FY30. 400 of those beds will come through Greenfield expansion and about 600 through the Brownfield expansion.

items.statement: Confident of delivering margin expansion estimate shared earlier, with Q4 margin up 90 bps YoY
items.quote: And with the measures that we have taken and that we will continue to take both on the quality of revenue side and other things that I mentioned earlier, and on the cost side, the margin expansion is achievable and we have demonstrated that over the last two quarters.

items.statement: Margin expansion opportunities identified across clusters, primarily from West and East as South is mature at 25%+ margins
items.quote: I think we have identified opportunities for margin expansion across clusters. But largely, I think it will come from West and East more, because South is a mature cluster with margins already 25% plus.

items.statement: Inherent demand growing rapidly due to higher cancer incidence
items.quote: Secondly, there is an inherent demand that is being generated in the market, you know, quite rapidly because of higher incidence of cancer.

items.statement: Payor mix improved favorably by 100 basis points over last couple of quarters
items.quote: So this last couple of quarters, we have seen the payor mix move up favourably by 100 basis points.

items.statement: Medical value travel impacted by Middle East conflict, being worked on aggressively
items.quote: There was also a factor of the Middle East conflict impacting the medical value travel to our West and South cluster, which additionally impacted the revenue growth.

items.statement: Rights issue of INR425 crore completed, net debt reduced to 1.4x, internal ceiling at 2.5x net debt to EBITDA
items.quote: The net debt to EBITDA ratio has, come down favourably. Earlier it was 2.2 x, 2.3x. It is come down to 1.4x as of today and this gives us enough headroom to invest in capacity addition, expansion, brownfield, technology additions and all.

items.statement: Milann fertility business sold to Inviga Healthcare Fund at enterprise valuation of INR63 crore, expected to close in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The transaction values Milann at an enterprise valuation of INR63 crore. The equity consideration for 100% of the business, including certain transition services support is INR37.6 crore, of which 75% will be received upfront at closing and the balance 25% over 18 months.

items.statement: MR-Linac at North Bangalore facility on pay-per-use basis for asset-light model
items.quote: So, Anubhav, MR-Linac is on a pay-per-use basis to create an asset-light model for us.

items.statement: Existing hospitals with expansions to deliver 75-80% of growth for next couple of years
items.quote: I think for the next couple of years, our existing hospitals with expansion within them will deliver at least 75% to 80% of our growth and the rest will come from newer centers.

items.quote: we have consistently maintained that we would target a 20% CAGR in terms of revenue growth, and the capacities that are coming online, even the one that has come online in the last quarter of the FY26, we have more coming online this year, so all of this will help us achieve that 20% revenue CAGR.

items.statement: Aims for 40% EBITDA margin in medium term, driven by efficiency, argon recovery, operating leverage.
items.quote: our long-term EBITDA margin aspiration is 40%.

items.statement: Plans to invest entire INR 250 crore capex target over FY27.
items.quote: we expect to utilize the entire amount over the course of the year.

items.statement: Merchant capacity to increase from 900 to 1,130 TPD; on-site from 700 to 1,000 TPD in 12 months.
items.quote: We expect this to go up from 900 to about 1,130 and the on-site to go up from about 700 to about 1,000 in over the next 12 months.

items.statement: Argon revenue share expected to reach ~15% long term.
items.quote: I think slightly longer term if we look at it, we can touch somewhere around 15% is what we expect.

items.statement: Argon prices recovered in Q4 and expected to remain robust with steel demand.
items.quote: the pricing has recovered from the Q3 lows, and we expect it to remain robust with significant demand coming in from the steel sector.

items.statement: Power cost as percentage of revenue to reduce due to renewables and efficient plants.
items.quote: I can tell you that absolutely you're right that this power cost, the percentage that it cost overall, power cost will keep reducing

items.statement: No excessive capacity or price war expected due to long-term contracts and demand growth.
items.quote: we don't really foresee that there is excessive capacity coming in or that there will be a downward pressure on the pricing.

items.statement: Project engineering vertical expected muted growth due to internal focus.
items.quote: we don't expect significant growth from the project engineering vertical, largely because of the fact that we have significant expansion plans of our own

items.statement: New merchant plants ramp up over 18 months, revenue increasing quarterly for 6-8 quarters.
items.quote: For the merchant plants, we expect the ramp-up to take about 18 odd months from the date of commissioning.

items.statement: Signed long-term PPA for wind-solar hybrid to supply 55-60% power to one unit.
items.quote: We've recently signed up, I think just a couple of quarters ago, a long-term PPA for a wind-solar hybrid plant which will give about 55 to 60% of our power demand for one of our units

items.statement: Grid power cost is 50-60% higher than PPA pricing.
items.quote: The grid pricing is about 50 to 60% higher than the PPA pricing

items.statement: Transportation cost minimized by delivering within 300-400 km radius.
items.quote: we prefer to deliver within a radius of about, let's say, 300 to 400 kilometers from our plant.

items.statement: Specialty gases facility planned at west-central India plant for solar cell manufacturing.
items.quote: this facility is planned within our west-central India plant. And so that plant will also have this facility where we'll be able to debulk and distribute these specialty gases.

items.statement: FY27 volume growth guidance mid-teens to high-teens excluding North plant
items.quote: So in FY27, what we forecasted is our performance would be in the mid -teens. That was the guidance that we had given, mid-teens to high-teens. And we maintain our stance o n that. This number is excluding the North, and we are actually working towards hitting that

items.statement: Nagaur plant utilization guidance 50-60% for full year FY27
items.quote: had given was 50% to 60% utilization for the full year. This is the first month of operation, I think we'll be in a better position and a little more confident of our performance at the end of Q1. That's when we discuss the numbers in a little more detail. But we maintain our guidance of 50% to 60% utilization for the full year of 2.5 million ton grinding capacity

items.statement: Capex guidance INR2,300 crores for FY27 and INR2,200 crores for FY28
items.quote: As far as the guidance for FY27 and FY28 are concerned, we intend to spend about INR2,300 crores in FY27 and about INR2,200 crores in FY28. So this is the guidance we are giving as far as the capex is concerned.

items.statement: Additional 2.5 MTPA grinding at Nagaur approved with INR430 crores investment commissioning by Q4 FY28
items.quote: The estimated investment for this project is INR430 crores, and this unit is expected to commission by quarter 4 of FY28.

items.statement: GGBS volume target around 7 million tons for FY27
items.quote: So we probably are targeting kind of 7 million ton of volumes of GGBS this year. Is that fair over 6.5 million ton of volume from GGBS? Nilesh Narwekar: Yes, it is around the same number

items.statement: Cement realization Q4 FY26 INR4,673 per ton up 4.8% QoQ; GGBS realization INR3,682 per ton slight QoQ improvement
items.quote: On product ASP, cement realizations for quarter 4 FY '26 was at INR4,673 per ton, increase of 4.8% quarter-on-quarter with increases across all regions that we operate in. GGBS realization for quarter 4 FY '26 was at INR 3,682 per ton, slight improvement on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: April 2026 demand soft due to inflation, labor shortage, elections; improving in May and normalizing
items.quote: The demand environment in April '26 has been relatively soft due to the inflationary pressures arising from the Middle East war situation. To add to that, shortage of labo ur and impact of elections in some of our key states of Tamil Nadu, Ker ala, West Bengal have played out. But we continue to be optimistic from here on with the activity coming back to

items.statement: Trade mix improved to 51% in Q4 FY26 vs 47% in Q3; clinker factor 51% industry lowest
items.quote: Within cement, the trade mix improved to 51% versus 47% in Q3. Our clinker to cement factor remained one of the lowest in the industry at 51% in quarter 4 FY '26.

items.statement: West Asia crisis creates near-term uncertainty for economic growth and cement demand; monitoring and prepared to react
items.quote: Having said that, as all of you know, the West Asia crisis brings with it certain issues for the cement industry, namely packing bags, imported fuel and more recently, the petrol and diesel costs have gone up. This creates a near -term uncertainty for overall economi c growth and for the demand outlook for cement industry as a

items.statement: Punjab plant EC delayed due to elections; shifting 2.5 MTPA grinding to Nagaur instead
items.quote: Please keep in mind that there are elections due in Punjab sometime in Feb next year. So things are a bit slow on the government side. So we expect this EC to be a bit delayed. As and when that happens, we will take a call on the second line probably in Rajasthan.

items.statement: UAE grinding unit commissioning delayed to end April 2027 due to war
items.quote: No, because of this war, it's delayed by a month. So, we are hoping by April '27 end that should be commissioned.

items.statement: FY28 target consolidated turnover INR1,100 crores and EBITDA margin 16-18%.
items.quote: For the next year, our guidance remains at a consolidated INR1,100 crores of turnover and our EBITDA margins would be in the range of about 16% to 18%.

items.statement: No FY27 guidance due to geopolitical uncertainty; may provide in a quarter or two.
items.quote: So it'll be difficult for us to give a FY ‘27 guidance at this stage. As we have discussed throughout this call, it'll be much better placed probably a quarter or maybe two quarters from now for us to give you an FY ‘27 guidance.

items.statement: Dahej project capex ~INR270 crores; INR260 crores incurred and substantially capitalized.
items.quote: Out of the total planned capex of approximately INR270 crores for the Dahej project, nearly INR260 crores has already been incurred and substantially capitalized.

items.statement: Dahej peak revenue potential ~INR800 crores, asset turn 3-3.5x.
items.quote: We are expecting an asset turn of this of the capex to be about 3, 3.5 times. So the peak potential revenue is about INR800 crores from the new Dahej unit.

items.statement: Phenol raw material price surge and supply delays impacted near-term production timelines; plant production-ready.
items.quote: On the phenol derivative side, while the plant remains production-ready, ongoing geopolitical issues have significantly increased prices and impacted the availability of the key petrochemical raw material such as phenol, which in turn has impacted the near-term production timelines.

items.statement: Business momentum back; order and deal flows returning after tariff clarity.
items.quote: So now going forward, there could be a fair amount of comparison and the business momentum is back. We are seeing order and deal flows come through.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 gross margin 23.4% standalone, 30.5% consolidated; EBITDA margin 13.4% standalone, 14.2% consolidated.
items.quote: Gross profit margins improved sequentially to 23.4% on a stand-alone basis and 30.5% on a consolidated basis. Similarly, EBITDA stood at INR15 crores on a standalone basis compared to INR8 crores in the Q3 FY ‘26, registering a sequential growth of 98%.

items.statement: Non-mint products, especially clove and derivatives, gaining traction per diversification strategy.
items.quote: Additionally, the company also witnessed improved traction across non-mint product, particularly clove and its derivatives, in line with its diversification strategy.

items.statement: FY27 could be better than FY26, closer to FY25, due to tariff clarity and new capacity.
items.quote: FY ‘27 should be more or less in line in terms of how we are scaling up and much better and closer to FY ‘25 versus FY ‘26.

items.statement: GST headwind resolved; business normalized to pre-GST levels.
items.quote: So the GST on the headwind the that had come is past us and we've seen the situation getting back to normal and we're back to what it was prior to the whole GST situation kicking in.

items.statement: Phenol vertical ramp-up expected in Q1 and Q2 of following year as prices stabilize.
items.period: Q1 and Q2 of following year
items.quote: And as a result of which, I believe the clarity is on its on the horizon and by Q1 and Q2 of the following years, we'll have better ramp-up of these phenol verticals.

items.statement: Anisole internal consumption vs market sale planned 50-50; no margin guidance yet.
items.quote: So internal consumption of Anisole, we internally thought of like a 50-50, like selling or internally consuming it.

items.statement: Plant qualification audits for CMO/CDMO expected to complete in next two quarters.
items.quote: We believe a significant portion of this activity in terms of qualification of the plant will get over in the next two quarters.

items.statement: FY26 export-import split: 44% export, 56% domestic.
items.quote: So we can come back to you on the exact U.S. numbers, but this year domestically we've done better, like the export-import split is 44% export and 56% domestic for FY ‘26.

items.statement: Expects FY27 revenue run rate of INR330-350 crores with cash EBIT margin of 21-22%.
items.quote: So next year, at a revenue run rate of 330 to 350 Crores, we expect to have a cash EBIT of 21 to 22 percentage.

items.statement: Plans to invest INR200-225 crores over next two years to expand operational area to 3 million sq ft by FY28.
items.quote: we are planning to invest roughly INR200 crores to INR225 crores in the next two years of time frame, which practically would empower us to reach from current 1.2 million square feet to 3 million square feet of operational area by FY28.

items.statement: Board approved INR35 crores preferential issue, with INR15 crores from promoters and INR20 crores from non-promoters.
items.quote: our board recently approved a preferential issue of INR35 crores, which was largely to fund the growth and take up a 4.5 lakh square feet with Winston as an asset. Out of this INR35 crores, INR15 crores had been subscribed directly by the promoter and promoter group through convertible warrants, and additional INR20 Cr

items.statement: Expects INR110-120 crores liquidity in Q1 FY27 from monetization of subsidiary holding.
items.quote: Q1 FY27, we are anticipating a significant capital event through monetization of our holding in one of our subsidiaries, wherein we are building almost 0.5 million square feet. That capital event would result into a liquidity of INR110 crores to INR120 crores within DevX.

items.statement: Board approved NCD issuance of INR100 crores at 11-12% interest, to be issued as properties are ready.
items.quote: We are looking to kind of issue debentures in the range of 11 to 12 percentage.

items.statement: Capital One asset pre-leased with 95% occupancy, expected monthly revenue run rate of INR2.65-2.75 crores from Q1 FY27.
items.value: INR2.65 crores to INR2.75 crores per month
items.quote: The asset is EBITDA positive from day one, and we would be achieving a revenue run rate of INR2.65 crores to INR2.75 crores per month. The revenue from this center would be reflecting in our books from Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Signed 8.1 lakh sq ft development management asset, committing INR100 crores over four years for INR120 crores annual revenue.
items.quote: The second asset is 8.1 lakh square feet, which also starts our development management journey in the city. We have committed an investment of INR100 crores across four years, which will ultimately help us achieve an annualized revenue of INR120 crores with 80 percentage occupancy and 8,500 seats.

items.statement: Signed 4.5 lakh sq ft under straight lease model in Ambli-Bopal corridor, funded through preferential issue.
items.quote: Recently, in this last quarter, we also signed 4.5 Lakh square feet in an asset called under Stright lease model Ambli–Bopal corridor, funded through a preferential issue.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin for FY26 was 60.5%, up from 59.8% last year.
items.quote: And our margin, EBITDA margin, has been achieved at 60.5 percentage, which last year was 59.8 percentage.

items.statement: Normalized Cash EBIT for FY26 was INR36.55 crores, 21.38% margin, exceeding industry 15-18%.
items.quote: So normalized Cash EBIT for FY26 is INR36.55 crores, which is 21.38 percentage margin. At an industry parlance, 15 to 18 percentage is assumed to be a better outcome.

items.statement: 65% of revenue from enterprise clients on built-to-suit contracts with average lock-in of 34 months.
items.quote: On client side, 65 percentage of our revenue comes from enterprise clients, which is on built-to-suit contracts.

items.statement: Client retention was 99.7% with negligible churn; over 100 clients present in multiple cities.
items.quote: The client retention is unheard of. We have a 99.7 percentage retention this year, almost negligible 0.003 percentage of churn that we achieved last year.

items.statement: Development management fees range INR300-500 per sq ft over 2-4 years, generating INR12-20 crores for 4 lakh sq ft asset.
items.value: INR300 to INR500 per square feet
items.quote: The revenue that we generate is a per square feet revenue which ranges anywhere between INR300 to INR500 per square feet, which spans across two years to four years of time frame.

items.statement: Noida asset shut down due to poor maintenance by landowner, impacting Q4 revenue.
items.quote: The Noida asset was typically operated by a land owner which was going through a very difficult phase. And the common area maintenance was their responsibility. And the asset was not being able to maintained or managed by them. And we were not happy with the services that were being rendered to us.

items.statement: Expects 20-22% revenue growth over medium term, with profitability growth outpacing top line.
items.quote: So, we expect to grow at around 20% to 22% over the medium term and profitability growth should outpace the top line.

items.statement: Phase-1 ink manufacturing capex of INR 40-45 crore targeted for FY27.
items.quote: Our ink, the plan in Phase-1 is targeted for FY27, takes in in-house production to 150 ton a month with CAPEX of around INR 40 crores to INR 45 crore.

items.statement: Phase-2 ink manufacturing capex of INR 20-25 crore targeted for FY28.
items.quote: Phase-2 is targeted for FY28, takes total in-house capacity up to 500 tons a month with additional INR 20 crores to INR 25 crore of CAPEX.

items.statement: Ink expansion capex to be funded 25% internal accrual, 75% bank debt.
items.quote: So, 25% of the total CAPEX, that will be done by the internal accrual and 75% will go with the bank debt.

items.statement: Near-term EBITDA margin sustainable at 14-16%, will improve with in-house ink manufacturing.
items.quote: Otherwise, as I normally say, this is the margin range that we are operating around 14% to 16% which is a sustainable margin range.

items.statement: Long-term target of 1000 tons per month ink capacity across multiple ink types.
items.quote: Phase-3 is a longer-term target for 1000 tons a month across sublimation, reactive, disperse, pigment inks.

items.statement: India digital textile printing at 7-8% penetration, significant growth expected over next 5-10 years.
items.quote: So, India is in very early stage. So, for the next 5 to 10 years, if we see then the volumetric growth in terms of machines will be there.

items.statement: Sublimation paper realization was INR 5.6 per meter last year.
items.quote: So, let's say, right now, the last year, what the realization we got was the INR 5.6 per meter.

items.statement: Ink realization expected at INR 200-300 per liter.
items.quote: But if we talk about the realization, then we can assume around, let's say, INR 200 to INR 300 per liter.

items.statement: Operating cash flow negative due to MSME payment compliance and Konica Minolta advance payment terms; normalized in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: But I am pleased to share that collections have been strong in Q1 FY27 and the position has normalized now.

items.statement: Recurring revenue from ink, paper, spares was 50.25% of total revenue in FY26.
items.quote: Recurring revenue from ink, sublimation paper, spare part, that contributed roughly 50.25% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Ink manufacturing production to start by end of FY27, revenue realization in next financial year.
items.quote: So, production should start by the end of the year, and maybe we can have the realization of that into the next financial year.

items.statement: Management will wait until after Q1 FY27 to provide formal guidance due to geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty.
items.quote: However, now considering the geopolitical situation and also the uncertainty, we would like to probably wait until Q1, where we get a better grip of the situation, better visibility, and maybe in a position to give a guidance after Q1.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR 160-200 crores for FY27 across Payment Solutions, IoT, and modernization, partially funded by IPO proceeds.
items.quote: On the capex side, we have a plan of investing close to about INR 160 crores to INR 200-odd crores through the year across Payment Solutions and IoT business verticals, as well as overall modernization, of which some funds would come in from the IPO fund.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 330 bps YoY to 30.8% driven by operating leverage, improved mix, cost absorption, and procurement efficiencies.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter came in at approximately INR 125 crores, with an EBITDA margin of 30.8%, an increase of 330 bps Y-o-Y. EBITDA margin expansion was supported by stronger operating leverage, improved business mix, better cost absorption, procurement efficiencies, and structurally improved margins across operating segments.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin improved 204 bps YoY to 27.4% despite flat revenue.
items.quote: EBITDA came at INR 394 crores with an EBITDA margin of 27.4%, an increase of 204 bps Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Metal cards contribute ~4% of Payment Solutions revenue; management expects this share to improve in FY27.
items.quote: Yes. I would say right now, the metal card overall in our payment solution business contributes close to about 4% in the payment. Chintan Shah: Okay. Pragnyat Lalwani: And we see that hopefully to improve in the coming year

items.statement: IoT Solutions grew 45% YoY in FY26; management expects growth upward of 47% in FY27 driven by RFID, SIM, and eSIM traction.
items.quote: We expect that numbers should be definitely better than what this year was. We should be definitely growing upward of 47% in the IoT business.

items.statement: Won multi-year tender from leading PSU bank worth INR 8.7 crores over the tender period.
items.quote: In this quarter, we won a multi-year tender from a leading PSU bank, which represents approximately INR 8.7 crores in revenue over the tender period.

items.statement: Navi Mumbai and Kundli facilities operational in Q4 FY26; Nagpur and Bengaluru facilities still under construction.
items.quote: We would like to update that our Navi Mumbai and Kundli facilities have become operational in Q4 of FY '26, while the Nagpur and Bengaluru facilities are still under construction.

items.statement: Procurement optimization yielded 7-8% savings on top 50% raw material categories consumed in FY26.
items.quote: These kind s of sourcing optimization initiatives have caused about 7% to 8% savings at the material consumed level for the full year

items.statement: Management cites geopolitical uncertainty, supply chain disruptions, currency volatility, and demand conditions as key risks for FY27.
items.quote: As we look ahead to FY '27, we remain cautiously optimistic while being mindful of global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties, including supply chain disruptions, currency volatility, and broader demand conditions.

items.statement: IPO proceeds utilization INR 405 crores of INR 600 crores by end FY26; balance INR 195 crores (including unutilized IPO funds) to be deployed in subsequent periods.
items.quote: Of the total IPO and pre-IPO funds of almost INR 600 crores, we have utilized INR 405 crores as at the end of FY '26 and the balance INR 195 crores is planned to be utilized in subsequent periods.

items.statement: Management aims to continue working towards double-digit growth performance in the near term despite West Asia conflict and Kerala restructuring.
items.quote: Our goal is to continue to work towards a double-digit growth performance, and we are pretty confident that we will move towards that in the near-term.

items.statement: Expect another round of price increases in Q1 FY27 and will take calibrated price increases as needed based on input cost inflation.
items.quote: We expect to take another round of price increases in quarter one of FY27. We're obviously watching the situation and the environment very carefully and will take appropriate calibrated price increases as the need arises depending upon what kind of input cost increases, we see.

items.statement: Project BOLT launched to accelerate digital commerce with investments in organization structure, capabilities, consumer insights, and technology dashboards.
items.quote: Project BOLT is designed to systematically scale up this opportunity and is built on three key pillars. First, we are developing a dedicated digital commerce playbook anchored around people, process, and technology to bring sharper execution and consistency across platforms.

items.statement: GCC region grew 11.8% in Q4 and represents 70% of international business; supply chains have adequate stocks despite shipment delays.
items.quote: We delivered a 11.8% growth in GCC, which represents 70% of our international business, reinforcing the strength of our franchise in the region.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 16.9% from 14.4% in FY23; underlying margin expansion of 100 bps excluding PLI impact.
items.quote: EBITDA margins, increasing from 14.4% in 2023 to 16.9% in FY26, reflecting our sharp focus on premiumization, cost discipline, and a favourable product mix.

items.statement: Spice prices reversed deflationary trend with 6.5% uptick in Q4; chili up 20-30%, coriander up 10-15%; calibrated price increases taken in Q4 (~4% blended) with more expected in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: As we exit the year, we are seeing a recovery in spice prices, with quarter 4 showing an 6.5% uptick versus the lows that we were seen earlier in the years, indicating the beginning of an inflationary cycle.

items.statement: Domestic volume growth accelerated to 5.9% in FY26 (highest in 4 years); Q4 domestic volume growth 2.2% (6.5% ex-Kerala); digital commerce grew 38% in FY26.
items.quote: From 1.8% in FY23, we've scaled this up to 5.9% in FY26, demonstrating the strength of our brands and continued focus on driving consumption-led growth.

items.statement: Convenience Foods grew 6.4% in Q4 with double-digit growth in Meals and Sweets; Breakfast flat due to quick commerce platform restructuring.
items.quote: Convenience Foods grew by 6.4% in quarter 4, driven by double-digit growth in the Sweets and Meals portfolio. The Breakfast portfolio remained steady during the quarter, impacted by a temporary slowdown in two quick commerce platforms undergoing internal restructuring and is expected to normalize going forward.

items.statement: West Asia conflict causing elevated freight costs, port closures, and transit delays; Kerala distribution restructuring to impact next 2 quarters; US tariff uncertainty normalizing but inventory flush needed.
items.quote: The West Asia conflict has introduced volatility, leading to input cost pressures and intermittent supply chain disruptions. Despite these near-term uncertainty, the macroeconomic environment remains broadly conducive, and we are well-positioned to navigate these evolving dynamics.

items.statement: Eastern distribution restructuring in Kerala started in Q4 FY26; 2 of 3 phases implemented, final phase by Jan 2027; aims to improve spices coverage, accelerate convenience food, and build dedicated modern trade structure.
items.quote: we are starting to -- you know, we've already implemented two out of the three phases. One phase has already been implemented, another phase will be implemented by the end of May, and then the final phase will take at least two more quarters ahead of us. So I would imagine that by last quarter, if not first of January 2027, you will see that the full project will be -- the full restructuring will

items.statement: Digital commerce grew 38% in FY26 to 8.7% of domestic revenue; 38% of digital sales from non-South markets; 21% repeat rate on D2C.
items.quote: On a full-year basis, we've achieved a strong 38% growth in FY26, clearly reflecting the structural scaling of this channel. This momentum is also translated into increased contribution, with digital commerce now accounting for 8.7% of our domestic revenues, up from 6.6% last year.

items.statement: Cash surplus of INR 600 crores as of March 31, 2026; board decided to retain cash for future growth investments instead of dividend payout.
items.quote: As of 31st March 2026, the company maintained a healthy cash surplus of INR 600 crores, providing strong financial flexibility to fund strategic initiatives and drive long-term growth.

items.statement: PLI income zero in FY26 due to deflation missing CAGR thresholds; FY27 is final year of scheme, recognition depends on meeting thresholds.
items.quote: FY27 is the last year of the PLI scheme. It is still early days, so clearly if we meet the threshold, we will start to recognize it, but it's early days and difficult to comment at this stage.

items.statement: Eastern convenience food profitability improved with value-added products like 5-minute breakfast and new Madhuram range; ranges differ from MTR and target Malayali diaspora.
items.quote: the earlier Eastern's convenience food business had much lower margins, but with the value-added concepts that we are launching under Eastern, which is the five -minute breakfast and the new Madhuram range that w e put into the market, the profitability is much, much better than what it was earlier

items.statement: Wet batter portfolio expanded to Hyderabad after stabilizing business model; outbound travel/airline partnerships not currently pursued but suggestion noted.
items.quote: We have now established stability as far as the business model is concerned and the earning model of the business is concerned and therefore, we are ready to extend the product to one more additional city. So we've now taken it to Hyderabad and we will see the performance how it does from here on.

items.statement: Operating margin guidance raised to 7-10% from earlier 6-8%, depending on external scenarios and demand.
items.quote: But given our focus on reducing cost and also reducing our power rates through hybrid power and renewable power, we now feel that depending on the external scenarios and demand, our operating margin could be in the range of 7% to 10%.

items.statement: FY27 capex outlay over Rs. 100 crores for value-added products, Mother Yarn expansion, power reduction, waste reduction, and fire risk mitigation.
items.quote: As far as other projects are concerned, we are expecting a total CAPEX outlay of over Rs. 100 crores, primarily going into value-added products, expansion of Mother Yarn project capacity, and also for various reduction of our power consumption as well as reduction of waste for improvement of our operating margins and e

items.statement: PTCF commercial sales expected from FY27, most likely second half.
items.quote: We are hopeful that the commercial sales would start in FY '27, most likely second half of FY '27.

items.statement: Raw material price increases passed through to customers, with rare exceptions where production was declined.
items.quote: So the pass-through to a large extent, which started in March, has continued based on the pricing of raw materials which prevailed in the, up to, I mean, April and May.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic on demand growth due to geopolitical situation, elevated crude prices, and inflation.
items.quote: Due to continuously changing geopolitical situations, elevated crude oil prices and persistent inflation, we continue to remain cautiously optimistic about demand growth in coming quarters.

items.statement: Chinese imports at low prices persist in commodity products; favorable anti-dumping ruling received, awaiting Finance Ministry notification.
items.quote: While Chinese import at very low prices persists in commodity products, we are encouraged that the DGTR has issued a favorable anti-dumping ruling. We now await final notification from the Finance Ministry.

items.statement: Renewable energy share to increase from 36% in FY26 to 48% post additional capacity commissioning in FY27.
items.quote: I can give you an estimate of our current, for the FY '26, our renewable content on the total power consumption was about 36%. Post our commissioning of additional renewable power, it should go up to about 48%.

items.statement: Value-added products yield about 20% additional margin over commodity products after conversion costs.
items.quote: Since we report all, I mean, in a single segment, I will not be able to give volumes, but on an average, about 20% additional margin we realize after the additional cost that we do in converting these into value-added products.

items.statement: FY27 volume target to repeat Q4 plus volumes, dependent on external factors; focus on maximum capacity utilization.
items.quote: We would ideally want to have repeat our Q4 plus volumes, but this is all dependent on so many external factors. But the focus is to keep on utilizing maximum capacities, and that also improves our margin because it helps in better spreading of our fixed costs.

items.statement: Capacity to increase by 2 to 2.5 KT from FY27 capex; other investments add value but not capacity.
items.quote: So, c apacity would go up by about 2 to 2.5 KT, you can say, for the project that would get commissioned. Others are mostly adding value, so the capacity will not go up, but the value addition will go up.

items.statement: Radialization in truck and bus segment has stabilized at 60%; nylon reinforcement growth expected marginal at 1-2%.
items.quote: We expect only marginal growth of maximum 1 % to 2%. But we also do not expect a significant fall now, since it is now reaching a level where normally it is more stabilized.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on NFY could impact prices by 10-30% of current FOB value, favorable for domestic industry.
items.quote: So, what has come out as a notification talks of between about 70 cents to, I mean, depending on the product and the country, it is varying from about 20 cents to 80 cents. items.statement: Online business contributed INR5 crores in FY26, expected to scale 2-3x in current year.
items.quote: Now the most encouraging development is to see the strong traction in online business, which contributed approximately INR5 crores during FY26 and is expected to scale meaningfully as consumer preference increasingly shift towards digital home.

items.statement: Marketing development spend benchmarked at 10% of sales.
items.quote: So total, that we have marketing development, we have benchmarked at it about 10% -- to 10% of our sales, and we are sticking to that.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to sustain and progressively improve to north of 21% in FY27
items.quote: We expect EBITDA margins to sustain and progressively improve to north of 21%, reflecting the scale of our operations, execution capabilities and leveraging the new business lever.

items.statement: U.S. business aiming to touch $2 billion revenue milestone over the near term
items.quote: With these initiatives, our U.S. business is aiming to touch the $2 billion revenue milestone over the near term.

items.statement: Europe formulations targeting minimum double-digit growth in constant currency
items.quote: So, we are definitely trying to achieve the double digit growth. And, of course, considering the current geopolitical situations, we have taken it bit conservatively but we are confident it will be minimum double digit.

items.statement: Net CapEx for Q4 FY26 was $82 million and for full year FY26 around $341 million
items.quote: Net CapEx for the quarter is $82 million and for the year around $341 million, which includes capacity enhancement projects and plant expenses and CMO project.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin at 20.4%, Q4 FY26 at 20.3%
items.quote: For FY26, revenues stood at ₹33,653 crores, while EBITDA came in at ₹6,856 crores, translating into a healthy EBITDA margin of 20.4%.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 61.3% in Q4 FY26, up 153 bps quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Gross margin stood at 61.3%, increased by 153 bps quarter on quarter.

items.statement: Ex-gRevlimid, full-year revenue growth was 9.5% and Q4 year-on-year growth was 15.3%
items.quote: Ex-gRevlimid, our full-year revenue growth was 9.5%.

items.statement: Europe formulations achieved €1 billion annual revenue milestone in FY26
items.quote: For the full year, European formulations achieved a significant milestone of €1 billion revenue in terms of annual revenues.

items.statement: Growth markets revenue grew 25% year-on-year in Q4 FY26 to ₹980 crores
items.quote: For the quarter, growth markets revenue stood at ₹980 crores with a year-on-year growth of 25% and quarter-on-quarter growth of 13%.

items.statement: Pen-G plant power and fuel consumption increased operating costs; expected to continue but offset by lower raw material cost
items.quote: But what is the main factor which has increased the cost, is predominantly power and fuel consumption, for the Pen-G plant which has taken off very significantly in the last quarter.

items.statement: Pen-G and 6-APA incurred ~₹200 crores EBITDA loss in FY25; expected profitable contribution in FY27
items.quote: Last year as a whole, we would have incurred around ₹200 crores plus EBITDA loss on account of Pen-G and 6-APA (Lyfius & Qule).

items.statement: China OSD facility expected to achieve low double-digit EBITDA margin in FY27
items.quote: At least we are working to achieve a low double-digit EBITDA margin for the year. That is what we are trying to do there.

items.statement: Biosimilars CDMO Unit-1 commissioning by end of 2026, steady revenues from 2028; Unit-2 revenues from 2031
items.quote: So, a steady stream of revenues, to answer your question, would begin in Unit-1 from 2028. With respect to the recent Product Schedule three that I have signed, and we have informed the exchanges about, that is a greenfield drug substance manufacturing facility. We expect to close the commissioning of the facility in 2029. Two years from then, 2031, would be the start of revenues from Unit-2.

items.statement: Lannett acquisition expected to close by early Q2 FY27
items.quote: We will probably close by Q2 of the current fiscal. You know, what we did not factor in was the government closure for 76 days between February and April.

items.statement: Biosimilars portfolio targeting 7-8 products in Europe/growth markets and 2-3 in US by 2030
items.quote: By 2030, we are looking at biosimilars business having 7 -8 products in Eu rope and growth markets, plus potentially 2-3 products in the

items.statement: TheraNym CDMO signed 3 product schedules with MSD; both commercial assets, supplies to start in emerging markets and Europe
items.quote: So, we signed about 3 product schedules, which means that we signed for 3 products. Right now, technology transfer of 1 product, a new biological entity is happening. This is a product that is already commercial.

items.statement: Consolidated business expected to grow low double digits with margins in 38% to 40% range for FY2027
items.quote: Look, we expect that the business will grow in the sort of low double digits and we expect margins to remain in the 38% to 40% range.

items.statement: H2 FY2027 EBITDA margin expected in 17% to 18% range as Montreal production stabilizes
items.quote: H2 margins would be in the range of 17% to 18%.

items.statement: FY2027 capex similar to FY2026 Rs.1,668 Crores; key projects Spokane Line 4, Montreal Line 5, PET pharmacies
items.quote: FY2026, we have done a capex of Rs.1,668 Crores. In FY2027, we are looking at a similar capex to FY2026.

items.statement: Line 3 tech transfer revenue expected $60-80M in FY2027; margins similar to FY2026 initially
items.quote: So the answer is yes, we expect to generate approximately $60 million to $80 million in revenue from Line 3 as we move into FY2027, predominantly coming from the tech transfers of the products that I mentioned.

items.statement: Ruby-Fill market growing ~10% with share gains; generator annuity model every 6-7 weeks
items.quote: Ruby-Fill® is in a very good place because the market is growing at roughly 10% and together with the market growing, our market share is also growing.

items.statement: API custom manufacturing revenue mix to drive utilization and profitability; revenues kicking in FY2027
items.quote: You should see revenues kicking in FY2027 and additional revenues will also drive the margin profile for the API business.

items.statement: Generics business at double-digit EBITDA margin; targeting ~15% margin per 2030 vision
items.quote: So we are now at double digit EBITDA margin in our generics business. I think looking forward we expect again the sustained progress towards our 2030 vision. So, you should expect the margin to be close to 15%.

items.statement: SPECT cold kits shortage reduces H1 FY2027 revenue by ~$14M; supply normalizes H2 FY2027
items.quote: Just to give you a sense, the revenue impact in H1 is about $14 million on SPECT. So it is a pretty big number, right?

items.statement: Tax rate ~33% with unshielded expenses; expected to decline as PBT grows from Line 3/4 margins
items.quote: Our tax rate is around 33%. We have some unshielded expenses due to which tax rate is higher than 33%. It shall continue to go down as absolute PBT continues to go up.

items.statement: No new capex foreseen for next 12-18 months beyond Line 3,4,5 and PET manufacturing
items.quote: We do not foresee any capex over the next two years other than the investments we have already spent out, which is basically line 3, line 4, line 5, and PET manufacturing.

items.statement: Management targets same ~30% consolidated revenue growth in FY27 as FY26.
items.quote: So, as we already indicated, the group will deliver or expect to deliver and is internally targeting a 30% growth on its overall consolidated revenue.

items.statement: Crane rental business expected to grow another 30% year-on-year.
items.quote: And we are positive that going forward, we will see another 30% growth in our crane rental business.

items.statement: FY27 capex: INR 190 cr India plus INR 200 cr KSA, plus INR 123 cr spillover.
items.value: INR 190 crores in India and around INR 200 crores in KSA
items.quote: Adding on to this, we have announced -- our board has approved another capex of INR 190 crores in India and around INR 200 crores in KSA.

items.statement: Middle East FY27 capex ~INR 320 cr: INR 120 cr spillover plus INR 200 cr new cranes.
items.quote: So this year, we are forecasting to spend approximately INR 320 crores in the Middle East, and specifically for the Saudi Arabia and Qatar.

items.statement: Consolidated order book INR 1,053 cr as of May, fully executable in FY27.
items.quote: So, the order book of INR 1,053 crores is fully executable this year.

items.statement: Inquiry pipeline expanded to almost INR 4,000 crores.
items.quote: And what is further exciting is our inquiry pipeline, which has expanded to almost INR 4,000 crores.

items.statement: KSA EBITDA profile benchmarked 40-45%, targeting 45-48% via lean cost structure.
items.quote: But we believe because of our 3.5 years -- of decades, our technical operating and efficiency factors that we can deliver in the country and our capability to operate as a leaner cost structure, we can push that EBITDA profile to 45% to 48%.

items.statement: 50% of clients supply fuel free; for balance 50%, price increase discussions in advanced stage.
items.quote: No. So 50% of our clients give us free supply of fuel. And for the balance 50%, we are already in advanced stage of discussions with the client for a price increase.

items.statement: India yield ~2.1% expected to be maintained with plus/minus 5% deviation.
items.quote: So, our yield in the last financial year has been around 2.1%. And we foresee maintaining the same with a plus/minus 5% deviation.

items.statement: KSA utilization 85-90% and yield above 4.5% despite West Asia situation.
items.quote: In the current situation in West Asia, we are still able to derive a utilization in the range of 85% to 90% and a yield which is upwards of 4.5%.

items.statement: KSA inquiry pipeline ~$50 million over next 24 months.
items.quote: We have an enquiry pipeline of nearly $50 million in the next 24 months.

items.statement: Supply chain disruption may postpone KSA capex if shipping lines to region continue.
items.quote: If the shipping lines to the region continue to be, then there may be a postponement of capex.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting to asset-light E&C; no blended EBITDA margin target, BU-level P&L.
items.quote: And therefore, we do not target a blended EBITDA margin. We drive BU level P&L.

items.statement: Net debt to rise slightly due to higher capex but maintained at certain levels.
items.quote: So definitely, it will go up, but we'll maintain it at certain levels. And this is definitely going to be a little up considering the capex we have done.

items.statement: Order book reached all-time high of Rs.15,109 crores as on 31st March 2026
items.quote: Company order book position has reached its all-time high and stands at Rs.15,109 crores as on 31st March 2026, as compared to Rs.11,717 crores as on 31st March 2025.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance for FY27 is around Rs.8,000 crores, aiming to sustain FY26 levels
items.quote: Order inflow will stick to the existing numbers, which we have achieved around Rs.8,000 crores. We will try to maintain and sustain the same.

items.statement: Consultancy margin maintained at 20-25%, LSTK margin at 5-7% for FY27
items.quote: We are continuously maintaining our consultancy margin in the range of 20% to 25% percent and in the LSTK business around 5% to 7%.

items.statement: Middle East showing slowdown in greenfield projects, focus on revamp; Africa emerging as alternative
items.quote: In the Middle east part wherein we are serving there, we have seen a little bit of slowdown. The focus is more on the revamp of the facilities because of the damages what happened and the new projects are a little bit on the slower side.

items.statement: Middle East constitutes 10-15% of current order book
items.quote: You can say 10% to 15%, around.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected at minimum 10-15% for FY27
items.quote: Just now only two months have been passed and we are expecting minimum 10% to 15% increase in the revenue.

items.statement: Infra business contributed ~25% of order inflow in FY26
items.quote: For this year, it is around 25% in the order inflow.

items.statement: Dangote refinery order $360M, fertilizer $70M for 4 lines, execution over ~4-5 years
items.quote: For refinery, we were awarded for $360 million, and for fertilizer, we were given $70 million.

items.quote: The decision-making from the client side is delayed, because naturally, the focus has shifted on the revamping of the damaged facilities and awarding of the new projects is a little bit slower on the side.

items.statement: Coal gasification projects picking up pace with VGF increase; private and PSU projects moving
items.quote: The projects which were slowing down in between a s they were in the previous rounds, looks like the market is pushing for the coal gasification project

items.statement: Consultancy growth conservatively 15-20% CAGR over next 2-3 years
items.quote: Consultancy, on t he conservative side should be 15 %-20%. We should accept that. It should be in the same range

items.statement: IOCL Paradip Phase-II award expected by Q4 FY27 after feasibility completion
