items.statement: Saudi Aramco long-term agreement signed for in-kingdom services; out-of-kingdom agreement pending
items.quote: We have recently signed a long-term agreement with Saudi Aramco for the in-kingdom services. We are about to sign another agreement with them for out-of-kingdom services, which will be signed because of this Bakr id time.

items.statement: No employee cost impact from 8th Pay Commission in FY27-FY28 as it applies to central government first
items.quote: We do not see anything. That is for the central government as of now. Public sectors will come later.

items.statement: Domestic consultancy enquiries unchanged; no uptick post Middle East conflict
items.quote: We have not seen any change in domestic enquiries for us, at least, I have told earlier also. So, for us, consultancy is a regular business. It is the same.

items.statement: AI initiatives used internally for engineering processes, costing, and data access; digitalization department created
items.quote: AI initiatives are generally used for our internal, like, engineering processes and costing purposes, not specifically for the selling purposes, but our internal processes, we are trying to improve like the costing system is there, we have generated AI utilizing this, we can extract the data quite fast.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR 2,600-2,800 crores; ethanol INR 1,800-1,900 crores; grain INR 800 crores; mineral INR 100 crores.
items.quote: For FY27, we are definitely looking at about INR 2,600 to INR 2,800 crores of revenue, which I am expecting that about INR 1,800 crores to INR 1,900 crores should come from the ethanol segment, based on further allocations, about INR 800 crores we are targeting to get from the grain segment, and about INR 100 crores fr

items.quote: And if I talk about the EBITDA margins, definitely looking at about 10% to 12% EBITDA margins in this financial year.

items.statement: Current ethanol order book 18 crore liters; targeting at least 22 crore liters within FY27.

items.quote: As the next tender cycles, namely C2 and C3, come in, we are confident that we will be able to increase this order book from 18 crore liters to at least 22 crore liters within this financial year.

items.statement: Fresh capex of about INR 500 crores starting FY28, spread over 2-3 years, for specialty chemicals.
items.quote: We are looking at a mega project in that area, maybe looking at a capex of about INR 500 crores going forward, which will mostly be in the grain processing segment in the specialty chemical division.

items.statement: Grain processing segment targeting 5% EBITDA margin in FY27, about INR 40 crores on INR 800 crores revenue.
items.quote: So, in FY27, I definitely have a target of being able to achieve about 5% EBITDA on this segment, which will amount to about INR 40 crores at the EBITDA level on a revenue of INR 800 crores.

items.statement: Expects to sustain current quarterly ethanol margins for next 2-3 years, supported by FCI rice availability and soft maize prices.
items.quote: We are very confident that we will be able to sustain these margins over the next two to three years and continue delivering similar EBITDA levels on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Maize prices currently INR 19-22/kg; expected to remain in this range for the whole year.
items.quote: So, currently, prices are ranging between INR 19 and INR 22, depending on the region.

items.statement: Ethanol segment to lead revenue and profitability for next 2-3 years; mix to change after new capex.
items.quote: But until then, I'm expecting ethanol segment to be leading the revenue as well as the profitability for next two to three years.

items.statement: INR 500 crores capex to be funded by debt and equity; may require fundraising, options being evaluated.
items.quote: So yes, it is going to be a combination of both debt and equity funding. It may also require some fundraising, and we are currently evaluating all available options.

items.statement: Exports are small (~INR 100 crores sorbitol); not significantly exposed to Chinese pricing or export volatility.
items.quote: Actually, our exports are quite small as compared to the overall revenue basket. We are currently exporting sorbitol worth about INR 100 crores to various countries, which is still a relatively small share of the business.

items.statement: Expects to be debt-free by FY29, excluding long-term Assam plant loan continuing till FY32.
items.quote: Definitely, we could be a debt-free company by FY29. I am confident of that. But our long-term debt will continue till FY30.

items.statement: PLI due between Assam and MP is about INR 30 crores per annum; MP for 7 years, Assam for 3 years.
items.quote: The total PLI due between Assam, and MP is about INR 30 crores per annum.

items.statement: Expects INR 5 crores capital subsidy in Q1 FY27 for Assam plant; PLI by end of year.
items.quote: In quarter one, we are expecting an additional INR 5 crores capital subsidy underneath policy for our Assam plant, and the PLIs should come by the end of the year.

items.statement: Long-term vision to take company revenue to around INR 5,000 crores in next four years.
items.quote: Our vision for the next four years is to take the company’s revenue to around INR 5,000 crores.

items.statement: Expects double-digit revenue growth overall, not just higher single digits.
items.quote: Yes, we are looking at double-digit growth, obviously.

items.statement: All three businesses to contribute to growth via new customer acquisition and deep selling.
items.quote: So, we expect all the three businesses to contribute for growth in FY27.

items.statement: SMT line utilization expected to increase from current 30-40%.
items.quote: Currently, the utilization is in the range of 30 % to 40% and we expect this to go up in the coming year. That is the current year, FY27.

items.statement: EMS external customer revenue to grow further; pipeline and prototype orders to fructify.
items.quote: So, we expect this to grow further in next year because we have a pipeline of customers with whom we are working closely and we have got a few prototype orders also from a few customers. So, all this will fructify in FY27.

items.statement: Margin improvement seen as structural, not temporary, but quarterly volatility may continue.
items.quote: But, however, we believe the margin improvement is structural rather than temporary, supported by the operational efficiencies and volume growth and disciplined execution. However, the quarterly volatility may continue due to industry dynamics.

items.statement: Cost control to remain ongoing agenda to improve margins in future years.
items.quote: So, that has helped us to have a better performance, and we expect that a similar kind of cost control will be our ongoing agenda so that we continue to improve the margin in the future years also.

items.statement: Plans regular FY27 capex for business as usual and tooling; already invested Rs. 40 crores in expansion.
items.quote: As I mentioned in the earlier calls, we have already invested Rs. 40 crores in all our expansion projects, which is the factory expansion EMS. In addition to that, we will have a regular CAPEX, which will keep on continuing year-on-year.

items.statement: Memory price increases delay order execution short-term but long-term customers will pay market price.
items.quote: See, in the short run, it has the impact on converting order into execution. But in the long run, I think customers will have to take the bite and buy the products at whatever market price, because that is what is happening in reality also.

items.statement: Memory prices increased by double or triple; product cost impact proportional to memory share.
items.quote: And the price increases, like it increases by double, triple, like whatever handheld devices and all we are mentioning. All those devices need memory.

items.statement: Good demand in BFSI, warehouse and logistics for products; IT products, Auto and Power Electronics for CSS.
items.quote: We are seeing good demand in BFSI and warehouse and logistics sector for our product business. And for our Customer Support Services, it is the IT products and the Auto and Power Electronics segments. These are the segments which are giving us the growth.

items.statement: Good demand growth in handheld devices and 2D scanners for manufacturing and logistics.
items.quote: It is mainly the handheld devices and 2D scanners which are used in the manufacturing and logistics sector. We are seeing that as the entire manufacturing is growing in India and subsequently there is a resultant growth in the logistics sector as well, we are seeing a good demand growth in this segment.

items.statement: EMS focus on high-complex, mid-volume products in Auto, Power Electronics, Industrial Electronics, Defense.
items.quote: We are looking at mainly high -complex, mid-volume products with higher profitability. And those products are predominantly in the segments like Auto, Power Electronics, Industrial Electronics, and Defense Systems .

items.statement: Supply chain challenges and memory price increases caused inventory buildup and receivable delays, raising debt-to-equity.
items.quote: I think you are aware of the overall supply chain challenges which the industry is facing and there is an increase in memory prices and all. So, to address those things, we have to increase our inventory levels from our normal plan and even on the receivable side, we are seeing that there is a minor delay or that the c

items.statement: Reduced authorized service partners from 700+ to 500+ due to exiting non-profitable geographies.
items.quote: A few of the geographies, it is not profitable to provide this service in remote like Northeast and all those kind of locations. So, we need to exit from those kind of locations so we did this kind of reorganization in the last six months.

items.statement: Management declined to provide FY27 segment guidance due to fluid geopolitical situation
items.quote: Actually, the present situation is so, I think, fluid, it will not be right on our part to give you anything right now, but maybe by next time, we will be in a better position to -- till now whatever we have projected, we have been able to mostly achieve.

items.statement: Plywood capacity expanding 30% in FY27 via Hoshiarpur plant (48,000 CBM) and brownfield expansions at Kandla, Chennai, Guwahati
items.quote: Current capacity at Plywood is 4,06,000 as on March '26. And we are coming up with new capacity of Hoshiarpur, which is 48,000 CBM, which is going to come up in the second half of this year. Apart from that, we are having a brownfield expansion at our different factories, which is Kandla, Chennai and Guwahati, which will add another 20% of this particular capacity.

items.statement: MDF brownfield expansion at Badvel plant adding 60,000-70,000 CBM to be completed by end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: In Q1 of this financial year, we are doing a brownfield expansion in our South plant that will unlock about 60,000, 70,000 cubic meters per year of additional capacity. So that is ongoing currently and will get completed by the end of the quarter.

items.statement: UP plywood plant land acquired, capex to start late FY27 or Q1 FY28, commissioning targeted Q1 FY28-29
items.quote: The UP plant is a bit delayed. So we are looking at -- actually, we had earlier projected that we will be making capex in this year, but it seems because we've just got the land, so I think the capex of the same would start probably towards the end of this year, maybe Feb, March or maybe even Q1 next year, and it will be ready in Q1 '28 -'29.

items.statement: MDF steady-state EBITDA margin target is high-teens, driven by operational improvements, brownfield efficiencies, and value-added product mix
items.quote: Our strong belief is that this is a high-teens EBITDA business in steady state. And there are 2, 3 reasons for it. One, a lot of operational improvement on the plant side that we do in regular course is likely to kick in again next year as well.

items.statement: MDF and industry took 15% price increase to cover chemical cost inflation; early days to see how much sticks
items.quote: Given the disruption in chemicals and supply chain, so on and so forth, we and the industry have taken a 15% price increase, which barely actually covers the cost that has gone up on account of chemicals disruption. It is very early days to see how much of it sticks.

items.statement: Plywood took 7% price increase in April due to imported timber and chemical cost increases
items.quote: Yes. So actually, there is no challenge per se in getting the material. But yes, prices have increased, and we have taken a 7% price rise already in the month of April due to these reasons because we are so import heavy as well as our chemicals, which are imported as well.

items.statement: Plywood demand continues post price increase; secondary offtake stable, no drop observed
items.quote: Whenever we do a price increase, we expect that things will fall, but we have -- we are not seeing any drop in our secondary. So that, to me, shows that there might be some holding with the big dealers. But because we have such a wide expansion, and we actually run routes on a daily basis when it comes to feeding smaller dealers, I feel that demand is continuing even post the price increase curren

items.statement: MDF demand stable and healthy; usual seasonal correction from Q4 exuberance but no fundamental weakening
items.quote: Look, for us also, demand has been quite stable. Usually, April, May as compared to Q4, of course, there's a little bit of correction that happens from the Q4 exuberance. But in general, we don't see any fundamental weakening of demand. So it's quite stable and healthy.

items.statement: Plywood outsourcing (Sainik MR, ~8% of revenue) to be brought fully in-house by April 2026 as Hoshiarpur and internal expansions come online
items.quote: We want to actually make it a complete 100% in-house production. We are hoping that by the time there is an internal expansion next year, April, and Hoshiarpur. So once Hoshiarpur comes, we will start moving a lot of our Sainik MR, which is the only product we outsource in-house. And by the time we are here next year, we would probably make it 100% in-house.

items.statement: Forex exposure limited to INR 600 crores, predominantly long-term debt on imported machinery; mark-to-market loss in FY26 due to currency appreciation; no increase in forex exposure planned
items.quote: Our total forex is within INR600 crores. Over the course of the past 2 decades, we have benefited substantially because of a natural interest hedge, as you are aware. One year, yes, there's been a start loss. This is predominantly due to the fact that currencies appreciated beyond what anyone could have imagined.

items.statement: Long-term debt to EBITDA not to exceed 1:1 going forward; working capital debt supports 19% growth
items.quote: Long-term debt, I don't think we'll exceed 1:1 EBITDA going forward.

items.statement: Century Ports (KPD-1 West) commenced commercial operations in Q4 FY26; expected to be cash positive from Q1 FY27; operated as separate profit center with no cost savings to Century Ply
items.quote: We will be cash positive in Q1 FY '27 from the Port business.

Of this 176 MW coming from renewables would be on a standalone basis and 9,381 MW would be coming from the JVs and the subsidiaries.

items.quote: In FY2 6, we have incurred a group capex of INR49,068 crores as compared to INR44,636 crores in the previous year. While on the stand-alone basis, NTPC has incurred capex of INR28,462 crores in FY26 as compared to INR22,965 crores in the previous year

items.statement: NTPC Group has over 34 GW under construction: 16.5 GW coal, 2.6 GW hydro, 15 GW renewable
items.quote: NTPC Group currently has over 34 GW of capacity under construction, comprising 16.5 GW of coal-based capacity, about 2.6 GW of hydro capacity and 15 GW of renewable energy capacity providing a strong foundation for near- to medium-term growth.

items.statement: NGEL EBITDA margin remains at 87% in FY26; operating EBITDA grew 29% to INR 2,475 crores
items.quote: Consolidated revenue from operations increased by 29% to INR2,858 crores in FY26, while operating EBITDA grew by 29% to INR2,475 crores. EBITDA margin remains at 87%.

items.statement: FY27 renewable connectivity: 57% firm, 38% T-GNA; FY28: 88% firm, 3% T-GNA, 9% untied; FY29: 84% firm, 16% untied
items.quote: See, as far as FY27 is concerned, we have the firm connectivity of 57% and T-GNA of 38%. As far as FY28 is concerned, whatever CODs are expected in FY28, we have a projected firm connectivity of 88% and 3% would be coming from the T -GNA, remaining 9% is so mething which we are yet to tie-up. FY29, 84% we have firm connection and remaining 16%, we'll have to work on the connectivity

items.statement: NTPC Group installed capacity 89,108 MW as of 31 March 2026; added 9,618 MW in FY26 (1,823 MW NTPC, 7,795 MW JV/subsidiaries), highest ever annual addition
items.quote: As on 31 March 2026, NTPC Group installed capacity stood at 89,108 MW. During the year, we have added 9,618 MW of capacity. NTPC contributed 1,823 MW and JVs and subsidiaries contributed 7,795 MW, making the highest ever annual capacity addition since inception.

items.statement: NTPC Group RE capacity 12,068 MW as of date; NGEL added 4,225 MW in FY26 vs 2,977 MW in FY25; 490 MW added in FY27 to date
items.quote: During FY26, NTPC Group added 4,738 MW of RE capacity. Out of this, NGEL added 4,225 MW compared to 2,977 MW added in FY25. In addition, 490 MW have been added in FY27 till date, taking the total installed renewable energy capacity of NTPC group to 12,068 MW.

items.statement: Pump storage pipeline: NTPC Group 18,010 MW (NTPC 4,800 MW, THDC 6,800 MW, NEEPCO 1,600 MW); 1 GW already commissioned; targeting 3-5 GW completion by 2032-33
items.quote: Broadly, NTPC is working on 4,800 MW of PSPs. This is primarily to be executed through JV and subsidiary. THDC and NEEPCO, which are the hydro subsidiaries, they are working on 13,210 MW. So that puts the NTPC Group broad plan at 18,010 MW. Now out of the above, COD has been declared in the FY26 itself for 750 MW, that is the THDC Tehri PSP. And COD declaration of 250 MW has been done in the curre

items.statement: FY27 overall business growth guided at around 15%, deposit growth 10-15%, advances growth 15-20%
items.quote: The overall position I ha ve given, I will stand firm on it with the overall business growth of around 15% and maintaining we want to have the deposit growth between 10% to 15% and advanced growth of 15% to 20

items.statement: CASA ratio target maintained at 33% plus for FY27
items.quote: While focusing on CASA, we have assured that 33% plus, we want to maintain 33% -plus of CASA percentage.

items.statement: ROA guidance maintained at 1% plus for FY27
items.quote: ROA, I was telling 1% plus. 1% plus may be anything. So 1% plus, I will still hold on to it.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio guided at 52-53% for FY27
items.quote: it further. It wil l be between 52% and 53%. Once the costs are under control and the business is running smoothly, we will certainly work on further improvements

items.statement: NIM target maintained at 3% plus; management believes NIM has bottomed out
items.quote: As I was telling in the beginning, if you have seen, I am working on that 3% plus NIM. I will be working on it.

items.statement: ECL implementation impact estimated at 1-1.5% overall, spread over 4-5 years at 25-30 bps per year
items.quote: I believe the guidelines which has now come, which is available to spread over to the next 5 years and we have studied the impact also maybe around 1% to 1.5% overall will be there.

items.statement: Loan book mix: 55% EBLR linked to T-bill, 2.31% EBLR linked to G-Sec, 5.59% MCLR, 0.31% base rate as of March 2026
items.quote: To be very frank with you, base rate is 0.31%, MCLR 5.59% at the end of March '26. Then EBLR linked to G-Sec 2.31%, EBLR linked to T-bill rate 55%.

items.statement: Advances growth strategy: monthly targets set at 5% in first 3 months, 8% next 3, 9% next 3, 10% next 2, 14% last month for FY27
items.quote: We have this time changed our strategy that growth should come every month rather. Out of the growth percentage, we said 5% in first 3 months, that is, 15%, next 3 months 8%, next 3 months 9%, next 2 months 10%, and last month 14%.

items.statement: IBPC and Food Credit portfolio reduced from INR4,057 crores to INR1,707 crores in FY26; INR2,350 crores replaced with higher-yielding loans
items.quote: IBPC and Food Credit portfolio, which was at INR4,057 crores as of March 31, '25 has been brought down to INR1,707 crores as of 31st March '26. Accordingly, around INR2,350 crores have been replaced during FY '25-'26.

items.statement: Recovery target set at 50% of NPA book and 50% of technically written-off book (INR2,500 crores) for FY27
items.value: 50% of NPA and technical write-off book
items.quote: What quantum, what number, our aim is always to recover 50% of the book of NPA, 50% of the technical written-off.

items.statement: Major IT solutions planned for completion in FY27: loan originating system revamp with collateral management, DevSecOps implementation, HRMS revamp, Treasury revamp, BHIM 3.0
items.quote: A few major solutions that are planned for completion in FY '26-'27 are loan originating system revamp with collateral management, implementation of DevSecOps, HRMS revamp, Treasury revamp and BHIM 3.0.

items.statement: Cost of funds improved 8 bps QoQ to 5.38% in Q4 FY26; further improvement expected from bulk deposit reduction and CASA buildup
items.quote: Cost of Funds stood at 5.38% for Q4 FY '26, as compared to 5.46% for Q3 FY '26, registering an 8 basis points improvement.

items.statement: Yield on advances increased 7 bps QoQ to 8.78% in Q4 FY26; further strengthening expected from retail growth and corporate portfolio stabilization
items.quote: Yield on advances for Q4 FY '26 stood at 8.78%, as compared to 8.71% in Q3 FY '26, recording a 7 basis points increase.

items.statement: RAM (Retail, Agri, MSME) grew 4% QoQ to INR51,197 crores; mid-corporate advances grew ~13% QoQ in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our overall strategy is to continue our focus on growing ; Retail, Agri and MSME, that is RAM, which has grown from INR49,152 crores as on December '25 to INR51,197 crores as on March '26.

items.statement: Standard restructured advances reduced 7% QoQ to INR806.44 crores; PCR excluding technical write-offs improved to 65.39%
items.quote: Standard restructured advances as on 31st March '26 was INR806.44 crores, as compared to INR867.95 crores as on 31st December '25, recording a 7% Q -on-Q reduction.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25% year-over-year.
items.quote: So, from a guidance perspective, I would try to give anywhere between 20% to 25% growth.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin 12.5-13% in short term, 15% long term.
items.quote: So short term, we should be able to do 12.5%, 13% and on the longer term, we should be able to be 15%.

items.statement: Won Mumbai government contract worth Rs 150-200 crore, announcement in 2-3 weeks.
items.quote: It should be to the tune of about anywhere between Rs. 150 crore to Rs. 200 crore.

items.statement: Maharashtra pipeline over Rs 2,000 crore; two large contracts worth Rs 600 crore each upcoming.
items.quote: If I look at Maharashtra as a state, we have close to about Rs. 2,000 crore plus worth of pipeline coming up only in the state of Maharashtra, for which we are very keen on bidding and getting major contracts out of this.

items.statement: Q4 new orders and renewals secured around Rs 166 crore.
items.quote: We secured around Rs. 166 crore in new orders and renewals during this period, reflecting continued demand for our capabilities across digital transformation, infrastructure modernization, managed Services and AI-led Solutions.

items.statement: Government business expected to rebound in FY27 and FY28.
items.quote: At the same time, Government business continues to remain an important and strategic component of our revenue mix, and we anticipate a meaningful rebound in this segment during FY '27, '28.

items.statement: Aim for Services to be 75-80% of revenue for consistency.
items.quote: But if you ask me personally, I would want our Services business to keep on growing and take about 75% to 80% of our top line revenue because that gives a lot of consistency from a growth perspective because most of the Services contracts are signed for 5 years.

items.statement: Western Railway project dropped due to 25-30% equipment cost increase; retender expected mid-July.
items.quote: So that Western Railway project , unfortunately, we had to let it go because by the time the pricing was about to open, the equipment procurement cost went up by 25%, 30%.

items.statement: Audit qualifications to be fully resolved in next 2 quarters after RBI approval.
items.quote: So in next 2 quarters, we should be able to get a clean sheet coming in from everywhere.

items.statement: Long-term aspiration to scale business 10x over next decade, implying 20-25% CAGR.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we aspire to scale the business 10x over the next decade, which would imply a compounded annual trajectory growth of approximately 20% to 25%.

items.statement: FY27 tax rate expected around 25%, with some deferred tax benefit.
items.quote: It should be 25%, maybe 1%, 2% or 3% here or there, depending upon the deferred tax we get.

items.statement: AI implementation reduces resource count by 20-25% in 6-12 months.
items.quote: So, we see definitely a reduction on the resource count for any customer close to 20%, 25% in a matter of 6 months or a year.

items.statement: Store additions of 230-250 restaurants planned for the year
items.quote: we would open similar to about 230 to 250 kind of restaurants this year.

items.statement: Capex per store reduced by 20% over nearly three years
items.quote: our capex per store has actually reduced year-on-year, and almost nearly 3 years in a row by 20%, right? So it has come down by 20%.

items.statement: Energy cost inflation hitting 100-120 bps, pricing increase of 120 bps passed on
items.quote: energy is definitely the tune of 100 to 120 basis points, that hit we are already beginning to see come into the P&L.

items.statement: Labour Code impact ~20 bps, minimum wage increases across 11 states add 20-30 bps
items.quote: Labour Code is absolutely write-up of about 20-odd bps. But the minimum wage increases that we have seen across some of the states that have already gone live over 11 states out of 29 have already announced, and we'll wait and see some more, but that's another 20, 30 bps, which is there.

items.statement: Long-term margin improvement target of 200 bps maintained despite near-term pressure
items.quote: In the letter also we have said the long-term margin guidance on 200 bps holds and we'll try as quickly to get to that elevated number.

items.statement: Minimum order value reduced from Rs 149 to Rs 99 to gain market share
items.quote: We have very consciously taken a call to reduce minimum order value from Rs.149 to Rs. 99.

items.statement: Q1 like-for-like growth already better than Q4; annual 5-7% target maintained
items.quote: SSSG, we've given a commentary already, right, on Q1 and the longer term or the annual number, 5% to 7% remains. The quarter 1, we've already done better than Q4.

items.statement: Near-term margin pressure from energy, labor, commodity inflation; duration uncertain
items.quote: short-term pressure exist. Now will it be for a quarter, 2 quarters, 3 quarters, I think, at this stage, is anybody's guess, right?

items.statement: Premium product launches (Big Big Pizza, Sourdough) and wastage reduction driving gross margin improvement
items.quote: by conscious effort of wastage reduction, launch of premium products, mix changes and calibrated price increases, we have increased the margin, that bit has happened.

items.statement: Large fleet portion is electric, providing advantage versus peers on fuel cost
items.quote: the large part of our fleet is actually electric right? I think, therefore, we believe we have an advantage versus the rest of the market.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20% for FY27.
items.quote: As we have said, we are targeting 20% of revenue growth we are looking at.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance of INR8,000-10,000 crores for FY27.
items.quote: So order book guidance, as I said, it is INR8,000 c rores to INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 9.5-10.5% for FY27.
items.quote: Our estimation for FY '27 based on the order book which we have, we will be in the range of 9.5% to 10.5% for next year.

items.statement: Capex plan of approximately INR100 crores for FY27.
items.quote: We're planning approximately around INR100 crores o f capex, which includes certain capex on the international projects also.

items.statement: Monetization of 4 HAM assets by June 2026, expecting INR750+ crores.
items.quote: So to continue on that, out of the 6 projects, 4 we are definitely targeting by June end, which will typically bring in cash of around INR750-plus crores.

items.statement: Monetization of remaining 2 HAM assets by December 2026, expecting INR400 crores.
items.quote: And the balance we expect by December, which should bring in another INR400 crores.

items.statement: Working capital expected to normalize to 110-120 days post September.
items.quote: we believe that we should go back to the old norms of 110 to 120 days, this is more of a transitory as in the last call also, we had said there was some buildup of receivables in our Power division, which probably by end of June and September quarter, most of things would get cleared.

items.statement: Debt level expected to be INR500-600 crores by March 2027.
items.quote: And we believe that the debt level will be in the range of INR500 crores to INR600 crores by March '27 also, keeping all almost similar kind of turnover with a 20% jump.

items.statement: Balance HAM equity investment of INR325 crores, with INR175 crores in FY27.
items.quote: So on the equity side, the balance investment to be made in the HAM projects is around INR325 crores.

items.statement: Deferred consideration of INR550 crores expected in 24-36 months.
items.quote: And there are certain deferred consideration, which is based on toll extension, which is approximately INR550 crores, which will come in the next 1 or 2 years' time.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 was INR67 crores, with Q4 at INR16 crores.
items.quote: Q4, so total capex for the year was, INR67 crores, of which Q4 was INR16 crores.

items.statement: Effective tax on HAM asset sales expected at 6-7%.
items.quote: So effective tax on al l the put together would be in the range of 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Target to grow revenue at least 50% more than industry growth; if industry grows ~10%, Minda Corp aims for 15%+ revenue growth
items.quote: While we don't give future outlook in terms of revenue guidance, but our guiding principle has been that we want to grow our business at least 50% more than the industry growth. So if the industry grows about 10%, so we should look at revenue growth in Minda Corporation to the tune of 15% plus.

items.statement: Long-term vision to deliver INR 17,500 crores top line with 12.5% EBITDA margin by FY30 on a consolidated group basis
items.quote: Yes. So we have kept the long-term vision in mind for 2030 to deliver INR 17,500 crores top line with 12.5% EBITDA margin. And the whole group is working towards achieving those stated numbers.

items.statement: Capex expected in the range of INR 400-450 crores for FY27
items.quote: So our capex has been in the range of INR 350 crores to INR 400 crores. And this year also, we expect to be in that range, maybe 10% plus of that, close to about INR 400 crores, INR 450 crores capex we are expecting for fiscal year 2026-27.

items.statement: Lifetime order book of INR 10,000 crores recorded in FY26 with ~20% from exports; execution timeline 48-60 months
items.quote: We recorded a lifetime order book of INR 10,000 crores, contributing about 20% from exports order.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 lifetime order book of INR 3,500 crores with multiple platform-level instrument cluster orders from leading OEMs
items.quote: Our lifetime order book recorded INR 3,500 crores during the quarter. And along with that, we have secured multiple platform-level instrument cluster orders from several leading OEMs.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin at 11.7%, up 29 bps YoY; Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 11.9%, up 37 bps YoY
items.quote: For the full year, the revenue grew at 22.3%, despite macro and micro challenging economic environment we operated. EBITDA margin stood at 11.7%, expanding our margin by 29 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Commodity costs (copper, zinc, aluminum) escalated 30-40% in FY26; most contracts on pass-through basis so margin impact limited but no profit on escalation
items.quote: And when I look at across our main commodity, whether it is copper, zinc and aluminum, throughout the year, we saw escalation anywhere between 30% to 40% and most of our contracts with our customers are on pass-through basis.

items.statement: CV segment expected to continue growth driven by infrastructure development, highways, airports and logistics demand
items.quote: Commercial Vehicle is expected to do well in the coming quarters as well as in the years.

items.statement: Premiumization and new products contributed ~12-13% of the 29% YoY revenue growth in Q4 FY26
items.quote: When it comes to the factor of new products or premiumization, that has led to, you can say, somewhere about, out of 29%, you can say somewhere about 12% to 13% of growth has come from premiumization of new product addition.

items.statement: Wiring harness kit value increasing ~20% annually on average across products and segments due to premiumization and system solutions
items.quote: If I look at the wiring harness space, you can say somewhere about every year in totality on an average about 20% increase in the kit value is seen across products, across segments.

items.statement: Commodity inflation unlikely to cool off in next quarter unless geopolitical situation improves; commodity cycles historically move on uptrend every 3 years
items.quote: But looking at last 20, 30 years, we always found that after every alternative 3 years, commodity cycle moves on an uptrend basis. So unless and until the geopolitical situation improves, we don't see this cooling off at least in the next quarter or so.

items.statement: Minda VAST consolidation into Minda Corp from FY27; VAST did ~INR 500 crores revenue with ~7% EBITDA margin in FY26, >90% PV revenue
items.quote: From a Minda VAST perspective, last year, they did about, give or take, INR 500 crores revenue with an EBITDA margin of about 7%. We expect the EBITDA performance to improve in the current fiscal year with the improvement in top line as well.

items.statement: Turntide JV established March 2026; SOP for motor controllers and electronics in 5-6 months; axial flux motor orders under advanced discussion
items.quote: As I mentioned, we've already won orders when it comes to the motor controllers as well as the other electronic space. So that is going to start SOP in about 5 to 6 months.

items.statement: Toyodenso JV for switches to commence operations in Q4 FY27; FY28 ramp-up year, FY29 first peak year
items.quote: When it comes to the switches, which is coming again into the mass production by March this year, so the FY28 will be the ramp-up year, I would say. So the first peak year would be, let's say, FY29 for the switches joint venture.

items.statement: Sunroof JV lifetime orders INR 350 crores; mass production starting in next 4-5 months; FY28 first full year revenue
items.quote: So yes, for sunroof, we have received the lifetime order of about INR 350 crores last year. We are getting into the mass production in the next 4 to 5 months. So yes, FY28 will be the first full year revenue.

items.statement: Flash Electronics FY26 revenue INR 1,803 crores, EBITDA INR 310 crores (17.2% margin), PAT INR 137 crores (7.6% margin)
items.quote: Flash has continued to deliver strong performance with revenues of INR 1,803 crores in FY26 with an EBITDA of INR 310 crores and a margin of 17.2%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 outlook positive with several high-profile releases; confident of continuing last year's momentum.
items.quote: The outlook for the upcoming quarter remains positive, with several high-profile releases, including “Peddi”, “Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai”, “Welcome to the Jungle”, “Sarpanch”, “Cocktail 2” etc. With this robust lineup, we remain confident about continuing with the momentum of last year.

items.statement: Caravan business fully shut down; assets already disposed, realizing about INR 2-3 crores.
items.quote: We have already disposed of the assets, and these vans were quite old, more than 10 years old. So the amount of realization on that front totally would have been around INR 2 crores to INR 3 crores.

items.statement: Caravan business discontinued due to inconsistent pipeline; may operate via third-party tie-ups with no cost.
items.quote: Secondly, on the Caravan front, we have discontinued the Caravan business operations because there was significant inconsistency in the business pipeline.

items.statement: Ad revenue-sharing ratio should gradually decline as revenues scale up; ~80% of sharing expense is minimum-guarantee based.
items.quote: Therefore, nearly 80% of the revenue-sharing expense falls into this category, and that is the reason why, as revenues scale up, the sharing ratio should gradually decline.

items.statement: Ad-sharing with theatres rose to 50-60% from legacy 30-35% due to multiplex-heavy network; not losing pricing power.
items.quote: So, I think that’s a very valid observation regarding ad-sharing increasing from the earlier 30–35% range, which used to be our legacy percentage, to now being in the 50% –60% range.

items.statement: Where UFO invests in infrastructure, sharing percentage is lower, typically 35% to 45% depending on revenues.
items.quote: One, where we invest in the infrastructure, in which case the sharing percentage is relatively lower and typically ranges between 35% to 45%, depending on revenues.

items.statement: Consolidated DSO rose to 147 days in FY26 from 121 days in FY25, largely due to Dhurandhar receivables.
items.quote: To give you some perspective on DSOs, or Days Sales Outstanding, the consolidated DSO for the current year stands at 147 days, compared to 121 days in FY25, and this increase is largely attributable to the reasons I just mentioned.

items.statement: Net cash improved from INR 48.3 crores to INR 59 crores during the year despite working capital getting tied up.
items.quote: Our net cash has improved from INR 48.3 crores to INR 59 crores during the year, despite nearly INR 11 crores getting further tied up in working capital.

items.statement: Company will maintain both cash and debt on books; debt funds theatre equipment via LC converted to loan.
items.quote: The debt is taken specifically to fund the expensive equipment installed in theatres. Typically, we open a n LC, which subsequently gets converted into a loan.

items.statement: Company may reward shareholders with excess cash again once profitability turnaround sustains.
items.quote: And obviously, whenever excess cash is not required and there is an opportunity to reward shareholders, as we have done in the past, we will continue to ev aluate that.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 saw improving theatrical momentum; March strongest led by Dhurandhar: The Revenge.
items.quote: March was clearly the strongest month of the quarter, led by the exceptional success of “Dhurandhar: The Revenge”, which emerged as one of the biggest box office successes of the year.

items.statement: UFO network contributes 40-45% of footfalls for major blockbusters; got ~30% ad revenue share for Dhurandhar.
items.quote: For example, for any major blockbuster movie, the UFO network contributes nearly 40 –45% of the overall footfalls. However, historically, we were not receiving a proportionate share of advertising revenues associated with those movies.

items.statement: Employee cost rise largely due to ~INR 9 crores variable payouts after better profitability; costs under continuous monitoring.
items.quote: If you refer to Slide 18 of the investor presentation, we have highlighted that, on a full -year basis, there has been a variable payout of around INR 9 crores during the current year.

items.statement: VPF and CDC revenues declined in Q4 due to blank February and blockbuster clustering; full-year both grew.
items.quote: CDC and VPF revenues have gone down . So, that observation is correct for Q4. However, if you look at the full -year performance, revenues in both the CDC as well as VPF categories have increased.

items.statement: Management expects 10% to 12% cement volume growth in FY27 on FY26 base of ~5.3 million tons
items.quote: What we are looking for in the coming year is about 10% to 12% growth. So, I think that is what we are expecting. Yes, so I think it should be -- the volume that we di d, which is about 5.3 million and 10% to 12% growth on that

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at INR600-700 crores; FY28 capex estimated at INR1,500 crores for Nimbol, Bihar and Haryana grinding units
items.quote: So, I think the estimate for FY27 will be about INR600 crores to INR700 crores given we follow these timelines. Harsh Mittal: And in FY28, sir? Tushar Bhajanka: In FY28, I think the estimate would be about INR1,500 crores

items.statement: Subsidy income expected to decline by INR40-50 crores per quarter in FY27 vs FY26; full year FY27 subsidy estimated at INR145-150 crores
items.quote: So current year, we have done INR184 crores of subsidy. So what Tushar ji is saying INR40 crores to INR50 crores, somewhere in the INR145 crores to INR150 crores sort of thing you can estimate for the coming year.

items.statement: Fuel cost per GCV expected to rise INR0.10-0.15 in Q1 FY27 due to rake diversion to power plants; may normalize by Q3-Q4
items.quote: So, I think there would be an impact of, I think, about INR 0.10 to INR0.15 per GCV cost in coal. I think that should be a short-term increase. I don't think it should be a long-term structural increase, but there will be increase because of all the rakes being diverted and then we have to arrange coal from elsewhere and then that increases the cost.

items.statement: Cement prices increased INR6-7 per bag in Northeast and INR10 per bag outside Northeast in April-May vs March exit
items.value: INR6 to INR7 per bag (Northeast), INR10 per bag (outside)
items.quote: Northeast, I think it may be about INR6 to INR7. Outside Northeast was about INR10.

items.statement: April demand sluggish due to elections in Assam and West Bengal; pickup seen in May; too early to predict full year trend
items.quote: So, the current scenario right now, because of April, there was elections in April and May in Assam and also West Bengal. So, I think the demand was a bit sluggish because of that. I think we do see a pickup in May. April was a bit sluggish. So, it's -- like what you said, I think it's too soon to probably predict how the year would go.

items.statement: Premium cement share was 15.1% in Q4 FY26; trade share 78% in Q4 vs 81% last year; clinker factor 66.2% in Q4
items.quote: The premium cement share for this quarter was 15.1%.

items.statement: Bihar grinding unit (~2 mt) expected Q1-Q2 FY29; Rajasthan clinker (3.3 mt) + split grinding (5 mt) targeting H1 FY29; Jorhat grinding (2 mt) and Umrangso clinker later
items.quote: Yes. So, I think it means like first quarter of FY29 or second quarter of FY29, right? So around that time, we should be getting the Bihar grinding unit. And we have -- what we have done is that we prioritized Nimbol, Haryana and Bihar. And then we have also, of course, applied for permissions and everything in Umrangso and in Jorhat.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton expected INR1,500-1,700 for next 2-3 years (Northeast only); post-Rajasthan long-term blended EBITDA per ton seen at INR1,300-1,400
items.quote: I think in this -- I think for the next 2, 3 years till when we get the Rajasthan project, I think the EBITDA is -- because it is only in Northeast sales, the EBITDA should be between INR1,500 to INR1,700, right, at least. And once we get the Rajasthan, of course, for the first 1 year, because we'll be absorbing fixed costs and because we'll be ramping up our sales, the EBITDA per ton may fall. Bu

items.statement: New competition (Shree, Ambuja, JK Lakshmi) entering Northeast in 3-4 years; may create price pressure for 1-2 years but should normalize as players seek returns on high capex
items.quote: See, in the long run, like once they do come in, I think there will be a significant pressure in the market, right, because everyone will be running and running for the same capacity -- sorry, for the same market and the market is relatively small, right? So even a 3-million-ton plant in a big market makes a big impact. So, I think people who then are coming in, they also need to then think, right

items.statement: Board approved fund raise in Q3 FY26 but not yet executed; will consider QIP when net debt/EBITDA reaches 1.5x; decision pending
items.quote: Yes. I think that decision we still not have taken at the Board level. We have, of course, taken the permission for raising money in the Board. I think in quarter 3, we did that. But we haven't planned it also because the markets were, of course, a bit weak as well, right? So, I think whenever we do, we'll inform in advance and then, of course, we'll do it.

items.statement: AAC block revenue INR17 crores in Q4, INR43 crores in FY26; targeting INR150 crores in FY27 including AAC, RMC and allied products at 7-8% margin initially
items.quote: We are targe ting about INR 150 crores. This includes AAC, RMC and allied products. And I think the margin that we're looking at is about 7% to 8% to start with. And then gradually, we'd like to expand on the margin. Right now, we're trying to create the market first

items.statement: West Asia crisis impact estimated at INR250-300 per ton in H1 FY27 mainly from packing bags and fuel cost; price hikes of INR7 (NE) and INR10 (North Bengal) partially offset

items.quote: Yes, we've already, in fact, we've paid back a little bit more in the last month. Around close to INR2 crores we've already repaid.

items.statement: Management says AI is nascent and not impacting radiology business; radiologist still required to sign reports.
items.quote: So, AI is very, very nascent right now in our business. I would say that, especially in radiology, wherein x-rays and some CTs, etc., are starting to get reported. But you still require a radiologist to sign the report at the end of the day. So, right now, AI is not impacting at all.

items.statement: Targets 1.2 million tonnes steel volume in FY27 and 1.4 million tonnes in FY28.
items.quote: We are targeting a 1.2 million tonnes total steel volume for FY27 and a 1.4 million tonnes in FY28 steel volumes.

items.statement: Plans non-steel revenue of INR 750 crore in FY27 and INR 925 crore in FY28.
items.quote: We plan on achieving INR 750 crore in FY27, a 25% increase compared to FY26 and INR 925 crore in FY28.

items.statement: Targets e-commerce revenue of INR 35 crore in FY27 and INR 50 crore in FY28.
items.quote: We are optimistic on scaling up this division and are targeting revenues of INR 35 crore in FY27 and INR 50 crore in FY28.

items.statement: Aims to grow steel tubes and pipes volume from 6.9 lakh tonnes in FY26 to 1 million tonnes in three years.
items.quote: We aspire to grow from 6.9 lakh tonnes in FY26 to 1 million tonnes in the next three years in steel tubes and pipes.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin of 3.3-3.5% for FY27.
items.quote: We are looking at in the region of the same, around 3.3 to 3.5.

items.statement: Aspires to achieve 4% EBITDA margin in the medium term, likely by FY29.
items.quote: In the medium to long term, we aspire to take our EBITDA margins to around 4%, up from 3.35% in FY26, driven by gradual product mix improvement, growing share of value-added steel categories and operating leverage as we increase our scale of operations.

items.statement: Targets 20% revenue growth for FY27.
items.quote: Yes, it will be in the range of around 20%.

items.statement: Plans to add 7-10 new fulfilment centers/stores in FY27 with capex of INR 15-20 crore.
items.quote: We plan to add 7 to 10 new fulfilment centers/stores in FY27.

items.statement: Aims to increase non-steel share from under 10% to 15-20% in 4-5 years.
items.quote: Currently, we are at a little under 10%. Definitely, our internal target is to take it up to the 15% to 20% is our target.

items.statement: Expects Q1 FY27 to be slow but recovery from June onwards.
items.quote: Definitely, I would say the 1st Quarter may be slightly slow. But I am actually hoping for recovery in June itself.

items.statement: Notes tile prices increased 10-15% due to gas price rise and supply disruptions.
items.quote: It went up by about 10% to 15% was the kind of increase in the pricing at that point of time.

items.statement: Steel price volatility impacts inventory gains/losses; Q4 FY26 had INR 15 crore gain.
items.quote: Inventory gain in Q4 was close to around INR 15 crores, number one.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 had INR 16 crore one-time costs including demerger, rent, and bad debt.
items.quote: In Q4, we had around INR 16 crores of additional cost due to a demerger cost, additional rental expense. There are some bad debt provisions were there.

items.statement: Will keep growing the business at over 20% year-over-year on a top line basis
items.quote: we will keep growing the business at over 20% year -over-year on a top line basis

items.statement: Capex expected in the range of INR500 crores to INR600 crores for next year
items.quote: we believe the capex will be somewhere in the range of INR500 crores to INR600 crores for next year

items.statement: Locked-in core revenue of INR2,940 crores, up 34% year-on-year against locked-in rental cost of INR986 crores
items.quote: remaining locked-in core revenue now at INR2,940 crores, up 34% year-on-year against a locked-in rental cost of only INR986 crores

items.statement: FY27 opens with INR1,885 crores of core revenue already locked in
items.quote: FY '27 opens with the strongest opening position of INR1,885 crores of core revenue already locked in

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin of 23.2% expanded by 231 basis points year-on-year and 218 basis points quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Q4 EBITDA of INR164.7 crores at 23.2%, up 42.8% year -on-year and 22.4% sequentially. EBITDA margin of 23.2% expanded by 231 basis points year -on-year and 218 basis points quarter-on-quarter

items.statement: Sold close to 48,000 desks (3.3 million sq ft) in FY26, highest ever 12-month velocity, up 20% from last year
items.quote: This year, we sold close to about 48,000desks , which is almost 3.3 million square foot of leasing, our highest ever 12-month velocity, up 20% from last year

items.statement: Revenue to rent multiple held at 2.6x and total revenue to rent at 3x while growing volumes
items.quote: pricing held revenue to rent at 2.6x and total revenue to rent at 3x, meaning we grew volumes without giving up pricing

items.statement: Capex for FY26 was INR456 crores; free cash flow after capex was INR129 crores, up 286% year-on-year
items.quote: Capex for the year was INR456 crores. Free cash flow after capex was INR129 crores for the year. That's up 286% year -on-year

items.statement: Rent per sq ft increased only 0.9% over the year; operating expenses per sq ft stayed flat despite inflation
items.quote: Rent per square foot only increased 0.9% over the year. Operating expenses per square foot stayed flat despite inflation

items.statement: Target to remain higher than 85% occupancy even as new buildings are added through FY27
items.quote: the goal and the idea is to remain higher than 85% even as we bring on all of these new buildings as we exit the year

items.statement: 36% capacity growth already locked in, signed and contracted before FY27 begins
items.quote: From where we stand today, there's about a 36% capacity growth already locked in, signed and contracted before FY '27 even begins

items.statement: Launched Rivet, a standalone design and build business with no WeWork center commitment required, capital-light, no lease liability
items.quote: Rivet is a stand-alone design and build business for enterprises, landlords and developers with no WeWork center commitment required. It is the same in -house capability that we ha ve delivered our own 8.6 million square foot, which is now offered to the market

items.statement: GCCs contribute roughly 40% of existing member base and closer to 50% of new sales in the last year
items.quote: GCCs right now contribute roughly about like 40% of our existing member base, I think of new sales, maybe closer to 50% in this last year

items.statement: Net new store additions for FY27 expected around FY26 levels (542 net new stores in FY26)
items.quote: On operating outlook, net new store additions for FY27 are expected to be around FY26 levels.

items.statement: Long-term steady-state EBITDA pre-Ind AS margin expectation remains approximately 25%
items.quote: Our long -term steady -state EBITDA pre -Ind AS margin expectation remains unchanged to approximately 25%.

items.statement: India EBITDA pre-Ind AS margin reached 15.3% in Q4 FY26, up 6 percentage points YoY
items.quote: India EBITDA pre-Ind AS 116 margin reached 15.3% in Q4, which is a 6 percentage points margin expansion over the 9% that we had clocked in Q4 last year.

items.statement: International EBITDA pre-Ind AS margin reached 9.2% in Q4 FY26, up from 8.1% YoY; full year margin 7%, up 3.4 percentage points YoY
items.quote: Our international EBITDA (pre-Ind AS 116) margin reached 9.2% in Q4, up from 8.1% in Q4 last year. The key thing to note here is that full year EBITDA margin reached 7%, which is a 3.4 percentage improvement from 3.6% that we delivered in FY25.

items.statement: India product margin held steady at 64% in Q4 FY26 despite rupee depreciation
items.quote: Product margin was held steady at 64%, because the rupee depreciation absorbed all the benefits of vertical integration and premiumization.

items.statement: India eye tests grew 50% YoY to 6 million in Q4 FY26; global eye tests 6.8 million, up 45% YoY
items.quote: In terms of operational metrics, India revenue growth was primarily volume -driven with eyewear units growing 24.3% year -on-year in Q4 to 7.9 million units. The volume growth was powered by a 50% increase in eye tests to 6 million in the quarter.

items.statement: India Same Store Sales Growth 24% and Same Pincode Sales Growth 31% in Q4 FY26; international growth 35% largely same-store led
items.quote: In Q4, India delivered Same Store Sales Growth of 24% with Same Pincode Sales Growth of 31%. Similarly, international growth of 35% was also largely same-store led.

items.statement: Operating cash flow of ₹887 crores in FY26 funded 603 net new stores and manufacturing investment including Hyderabad facility
items.quote: We generated operating cash flows of ₹887 crores in FY26, which is about 91% of our reported EBITDA (pre-IndAS 116). This fully funded our store capex of 603 net new stores while also investing in manufacturing, including the new Hyderabad facility.

items.statement: Meller sunglasses launched across 1,000+ stores in India, Middle East, Southeast Asia, and soon Japan; scaling beyond plan with stockouts in multiple markets
items.quote: We have now launched the brand in India across 1,000+ stores. We launched the brand in Middle East. We have launched the brand in Southeast Asia across all Lenskart stores. We are now about to launch the brand in Japan also.

items.statement: B by Lenskart smart glasses launched in Q4 with over 30,000 waitlist customers; multiple smart eyewear product launches planned in FY27
items.quote: In Q4, we launched B by Lenskart with over 30,000 customers joining the waitlist already and increasing every day. Smart glasses are a multi -year journey and with our stores, optometry network, and prescription capability, we have a structural advantage.

items.statement: Currency depreciation (rupee) is biggest variable; Hyderabad and Thailand JV are structural answers to reduce import dependence over time
items.quote: Currency, of course, is the biggest variable. Rupee depreciation on imports is a headwind, but since 42% of our business is international and we continue to do more vertical integration, this has been offset so far. I think Hyderabad and Thailand JV are structural answers , which will reduce import dependence over time.

items.statement: No material impact on Indian or international demand from geopolitical issues; eye health is non-discretionary and category proved resilient in Middle East disturbance
items.quote: As far as demand is concerned, so far no material impact on Indian demand, I would say, or international. Domestic consumption -driven eye health is non -discretionary, I would say, and we saw that. I mean, it's difficult to predict these things, but I'll give you example of Middle East where we saw disturbance, but we saw the eyewear category was quite resilient.

items.statement: KSA business ahead of where UAE was at same two-year stage; continuing to open stores and bullish on trajectory
items.quote: We are about two year in the journey of KSA. We still stay bullish. We are continuing to open stores. When I look at where UAE was two years into the journey, KSA is far ahead.

items.statement: Remote optometry stores expanded 3.7x to 623 in India; Gold active members reached 8.8 million, up 29.5% YoY
items.quote: Remote optometry stores expanded 3.7 times in a single year to 623 stores. Gold active members reaching 8.8 million are up 29.5% year -on-year.

items.statement: Maintain revenue CAGR guidance of 15% to 20% over the next three to four years; no annual guidance given
items.quote: We will want to maintain a revenue CAGR guidance of 15% to 20% over a period of three to four years. We'll not be giving any annual guidance.

items.statement: Continue to maintain medium-term guidance of delivering 15% to 20% CAGR growth over the next three to four years
items.quote: Based on these levers, we continue to maintain our medium-term guidance of delivering 15% to 20% CAGR growth over the next three to four years.

items.statement: Capital allocation was INR165 crores in FY26 compared to INR113 crores in FY25
items.quote: Our capital allocation was INR165 crores in FY '26 compared to INR113 crores in FY '25.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margins improved by 100 basis points from 22.8% in FY25 to 23.8% in FY26
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margins improved by 100 basis points from 22.8% in FY '25 to 23.8% in FY '26, led by platform capabilities in international geographies.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin reduced from 24.6% to 20.9% due to a one-time ECL provision of INR10 crores; excluding this, margin would be 25%
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR55.4 crores compared to INR54 crores in the same period last year. One thing to note, margins reduced from 24.6% to 20.9%, due to a one-time ECL provision of INR10 crores.

items.statement: RPT improved 13.3% to INR2,598 in FY26 driven by international mix shift (32% to 42%), favorable forex (Philippines peso +5%, Uzbek currency +7%), and Philippines price increase of 58% in Oct 2024
items.quote: For FY '26, RPT stood at INR2,598 compared to INR2,292 in FY '25, registering a growth of 13.3%. RPT improvement was primarily driven by three factors. First, international mix going from 32% to 42%.

items.statement: Dialysis population in India projected to grow from 3 lakh to 5.2 lakh by 2029 at 13% CAGR; only 7% of 12.4 crore CKD patients diagnosed
items.quote: The dialysis population is projected to grow from three lakhs to 5.2 lakhs by 2029, a CAGR of 13%, which would be served by 5,500 clinics that are unevenly distributed.

items.statement: International revenue mix increased from 32% to 42% in FY26; Philippines price increased 58% in Oct 2024 with full-year impact in FY26
items.quote: First, international mix going from 32% to 42%. As you know, our price point in India is the lowest at $22 versus internationally, Philippines is at $111 and Uzbek is at $60.

items.statement: Two PPP contracts up for renewal in calendar 2026: a small two-clinic contract in Uttarakhand and an Andhra Pradesh phase later in the year; no certainty of renewal
items.quote: In this calendar year, we have two contracts that we are expecting to come for renewal. One is a small contract for just two clinics in Uttarakhand. That's in the process. And then later part of the year, we should get Andhra Pradesh, one of the phases for renewal.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia JV in investment phase; participated in NUPCO tender but no business yet; large Ministry of Health and Defense tender at EOI stage, moving to RFP in a couple of quarters; first clinic in Riyadh launching within two months
items.quote: A NUPCO tender came out a year ago, in which we participated and came out strong, but NUPCO was not the end user of the service, hence it has not translated into business yet. This takes time. The good news is the large Ministry of Health and Ministry of Defense dialysis tender has recently been issued with clear visibility of patient volume. Right now, it is on the EOI stage, but it will soon mov

items.statement: Active guests grew 11.8% to 36,981 as of March 2026; treatments grew 16.6% to 38.4 lakh sessions in FY26
items.quote: As of March 2026, our active guest counts stood at 36,981 compared to 33,076, as of March 2025, representing a healthy growth of 11.8%.

items.statement: Revenue grew 32.2% to INR998.8 crores in FY26; adjusted EBITDA grew 37.6% to INR238.1 crores; adjusted PAT grew 74.6% to INR128.3 crores
items.quote: Revenue for FY '26 stood at INR998.8 crores compared to INR755.8 crores in FY '25, reflecting a healthy year-on-year growth of 32.2%.

items.statement: Pre-tax ROCE improved from 19.9% to 22.8% in FY26 despite 50% higher capital allocation; working capital days improved from 92 to 83; AR days reduced from 130 to 116
items.quote: Despite almost 50% increase in capital allocation, our annual pre-tax ROCE improved from 22.8% compared to 19.9% in the previous year, reflecting the strength of India platform and our ability to realize the benefits of India platform both in India as well as international market through disciplined execution at scale.

items.statement: Generated INR233 crores operating cash flow and INR68 crores free cash flow in FY26; cash balance of INR500 crores
items.quote: In FY '26, we generated INR233 crores of operating cash flow and despite deploying a capital of INR165 crores in growing the business, we still generated INR68 crores of free cash flow. Currently, we hold INR500 crores of cash and we will remain disciplined in deploying capital in a ROCE accretive manner.

items.statement: Plan to add 40-50 clinics per year in India and 12-15 clinics per year in Philippines; majority of India additions are captive units
items.quote: We've been adding 40 to 50 clinics on year-on-year basis in India and we expect and we continue to do so, we expect to do that similarly. And also in Philippines, we are looking at adding 12 to 15 clinics in this year and the years to come.

items.statement: Reformmed.AI application implemented in 50 clinics to monitor core operational elements; will expand to entire network over time
items.quote: Our team at NephroPlus has created Reformmed.AI application to effectively monitor numerous core operational elements across a distributed dialysis network. This has already been implemented successfully in 50 clinics at NephroPlus as of today, and of course, we'll be expanding this to our entire network over a period of time.

items.statement: Gross new clinic additions target of 40-50 in India and 12-15 in Philippines for next year, excluding large PPP or acquisitions
items.quote: As I said that in India, we are fairly confident of delivering a 40 to 50 range of gross new clinics and Philippines of 12 to 15 range.

items.statement: FY2026 capex was INR165 crores, up 50% from INR116 crores in FY2025; no capex guidance given for FY2027 but cash of INR500 crores available
items.quote: I think in terms of capex, in FY 2026, we had a capex of INR165 crores compared to INR116 crores the year before. So, our capex almost grew by 50% in FY 2026 compared to FY 2025.

items.statement: Capex per bed: India INR10-11 lakhs (3.5-4 yr payback), Philippines INR40-45 lakhs (1-1.5 yr payback), Uzbekistan INR18-20 lakhs (1-1.5 yr payback)
items.quote: The capex per bed in India is about INR10 lakhs to INR11 lakhs with a payback period of about three and a half, four years. Philippines, it is INR40 lakhs to INR45 lakhs with a payback period of one, one and a half years.

items.statement: RPT increased 13.3% from INR2,292 to INR2,598 driven by international mix shift (32% to 42%), forex gains (PHP +5%, UZS +7%), and Philippines price hike of 58% in Oct 2024
items.quote: The RPT went from INR2,292 to INR2,598, which is about 13.3% increase. As I mentioned in my opening remarks, there are three key drivers.

items.statement: No large price increase expected in coming year; RPT changes will come from geography mix as international expansion continues
items.quote: So, in this coming year, we are not expecting any large price increase, but RPT change will be a factor of geography mix.

items.statement: Treatment volume grew 17% YoY; center count variability makes treatment volume the better metric for modeling
items.quote: And as we can see, the treatment volume has grown by 17% year-on-year and that's the metric that you should look at because the center has too much variability.

items.statement: International revenue mix rose from 32% to 42% of treatments, driving higher blended RPT
items.quote: One is obviously the international mix going from 32% to 42%. With the higher price point internationally, that's driving the higher RPT.

items.statement: Uttarakhand PPP contract at renewal tender stage; decision expected in 2-4 months but could extend; operations continue meanwhile
items.quote: PPP contract in Uttarakhand right now is at the renewal stage where the tendering is happening, so it is not renewed at the moment. We'll get clarity in that in some days, few days.

items.statement: Saudi JV in investment phase; new tender at EOI stage, clarity in 1-2 quarters; INR3 cr loss share this quarter
items.quote: Saudi, as we mentioned, we are on the in the investment phase and there is just recently a new contract or new tender which has been just released and it's at the EOI stage, which will take couple of quarters to take shape.

items.statement: Other expenses rose due to INR10 cr ECL provision (quarterly), IT/platform investment, international BD hiring, and R&M accounting change from capex to opex
items.quote: The other expense has predominantly moved by the ECL provision of INR10 crores that I previously mentioned. That was the primary driver of the other expense movement this quarter.

items.statement: Philippines acquisition pipeline: 12-15 roll-ups planned in coming year; recent acquisition 600-800 sessions/month, ~15 beds; long tail of 550-600 unorganized clinics
items.quote: We had done as I said we would be looking at doing a 10 -- anything between 12 to 15 roll-ups in the Philippines in the coming year as well.

items.statement: Competitive advantage in talent: India and Philippines are global nurse/paramedic suppliers; NephroPlus has training academies (Enpidia) in both countries
items.quote: Globally, India and Philippines are the supplier for nurses and the paramedic staff. And we have a strong hold in both these geographies.

items.statement: Targets FY27 turnover of INR200 crores, ~40-45% growth over FY26, driven by capacity doubling.
items.quote: We are targeting a turnover of INR200 crores in FY27, which will translate into a growth of approximately 40%-45% over FY26 figures.

items.statement: Expects FY28 turnover of more than INR300 crores.
items.quote: So, in the next financial year, we are expecting turnover of more than INR300 crores.

items.statement: Current order book ~INR200 crores, 50% product and 50% project, to be executed within FY27.
items.quote: Our current order book stood at approximately INR200 crores, which provides strong revenue visibility for the coming period and reflects continued customer confidence and deep business momentum.

items.statement: Already booked INR44 crores of orders in current financial year so far.
items.quote: So, next financial year, I mean, the order booking for the current financial year so far, we have booked order of INR44 crores already.

items.statement: Total capex since last year ~INR8 crores, including INR1 crore from IPO proceeds; capacity to reach 18,000 MT by Sep 2026.
items.quote: So, the total capex since last year would be approximately INR8 crores.

items.statement: Expects 1-2 percentage points higher margin in FY27 due to economies of scale.
items.quote: We can also scale from a larger turnover and expecting 1 or 2 percentage points higher margin this year.

items.statement: Service margin ~10% higher than manufacturing; service ~20%, product ~10%.
items.quote: The margin in services is approximately 10% higher than just in the manufacturing field.

items.statement: FY26 revenue split: ~50% service (project execution) and ~50% product sales.
items.quote: 50% is product and 50% is project.

items.statement: Long-term demand outlook for geotechnical and infrastructure solutions remains strong.
items.quote: We believe the long -term demand outlook for geotechnical and infrastructure solutions remains strong, and we are well-positioned to participate in this growth opportunity.

items.statement: Insulates from steel/polymer price fluctuations by booking large orders with suppliers; can renegotiate product prices if drastic.
items.quote: So, they cannot stop their production once they are into it. It becomes very costly if they have to stop their production. So, if they have a big customer giving a big, large order, they will book it and keep, and then they will do that backward purchase.

items.statement: INR15 crores of work in progress could not be billed in FY26, causing revenue shortfall.
items.quote: There is a work in progress in our project amounting to approximately INR15 crores, which could not get built during the financial year.

items.statement: Finance cost expected to remain around INR4.7 crores in FY27; debt-equity ratio ~0.7.
items.quote: And the finance cost this year has been INR4.7 crores. And we expect it to be around this level only.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity to reach 18,000 MT by Sep 2026, translating to ~INR200 crores product sale potential.
items.quote: So, 18,000 tons will give us a turnover of INR180 crores.

items.statement: Aspiration to continue healthy top-line growth trajectory of last 3 years while balancing fiscal responsibility; no prescriptive FY27 guidance given
items.quote: our aspiration is to kind of continue on the trajectory that we have been in the last 3 years

items.statement: PAT margin of 5% in FY26 is not steady state; there is headroom and upside
items.quote: I think our current margin levels are not steady state, if that's the question you're asking. There is headroom and upside and you've seen that.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to ~10% in FY26 from 2% in FY25; Q4 margin doubled to 10%
items.quote: adjusted EBITDA improved 800 basis points from 2% in FY25 to about 10% in FY 26. In Q4, the margin doubled from 5% to 10%.

items.statement: Gross margin held steady at ~69% full-year over last 3 years despite quarterly lumpiness; AI cost impact minor
items.quote: if you look at our gross margin over the last 3 years, we've got lumpiness in quarters, but full year is held steady at about 69%, with minor improvements.

items.statement: Volume growth offsets modest CPM pressure; net tailwind expected on monetization segment
items.quote: we see the volumes as a net sort of tailwind that will offset modest pressure on the CPM side. So, we've not seen anything beyond that yet.

items.statement: Monetized impressions grew ~62% YoY while monetization revenue grew 36% YoY; volume uptick more than offsets CPM pressure
items.quote: If you saw the impression growth that was roughly 62% year-over-year, revenue growth was still 36% year-over-year in the segment.

items.statement: NEWSPULSE first agentic AI product signed first paid customer; tens of POCs running with traditional news networks
items.quote: NEWSPULSE, our first agentic product, signed our first paid customer. It's early, but it is the first data point that AI work has been talking about is starting to convert and not just trials.

items.statement: Three segments all grew >25%: Streaming Unification 26% to INR 838 Cr, Monetization 36% to INR 381 Cr, Cloud Modernization 32% to INR 286 Cr
items.quote: Streaming unification grew 26% to INR 838 crores. Monetization and marketplace grew 36% to INR 381 crores and cloud modernization grew 32% to INR286 crores.

items.statement: No credible competition seen for Amagi's glass-to-glass platform with AI strategy; market dynamic but no disruption visible today
items.quote: I think that there is no competition that we see today as we speak.

items.statement: Cash balance INR 1,664 Cr (INR 907 Cr FY25 exit + IPO proceeds + operating cash); actively scanning for capability-driven acquisitions but no deal size committed
items.quote: cash in the bank, it's about INR 1,664 crores. And out of which INR 907 crores was FY25 exit, the rest of it is what is the IPO proceeds plus continued operating cash generation that we're doing.

items.statement: Net revenue retention 126% in FY26 (122% FY24, 127% FY25); $1M+ customers grew from 28 to 35
items.quote: Net revenue retention is a very important metric for us because it captures how existing customers expand with us over time. For starters, this is similar to the same-store sales metric, which is typically used. It has remained pretty healthy in the last 3 consecutive years, 122% in FY24, 127% in FY25 and 126% in FY26.

items.statement: Dollar-based NRR still north of 120% after FX adjustment; consistently in 120-125% range
items.quote: our sort of dollar-based NRR would be around -- still north of 120%. And so again, we've been in the 120% to 125% ZIP code consistently for a while now like we said.

items.statement: Revenue phasing: Q1 ~22% of FY revenue, 11% of EBITDA; H1 ~45% revenue, 37% EBITDA; H2 ~55% revenue, 63% EBITDA
items.quote: based on FY'25 and '26 average, Q1 represented about 22% of full year revenue and about 11% of adjusted EBITDA. Just for context, revenue in the first half was roughly 45% of full year revenue and second half is 55%. Similarly, at an EBITDA level, we are at about 37% for first half and 63%.

items.statement: Cost base: ~50% USD-denominated (30% direct cost + 20% sales) vs USD revenue; net FX tailwind; occasional transactional hedging only
items.quote: From a cost lens, the direct cost, which is roughly 30% and about another sort of 20% is sort of USD denominated for the sales teams. So, on $100 revenue you're talking about $50 of U.S.-denominated sort of cost.

items.statement: Adjusted operating cash flow INR 60 Cr (+80% YoY); free cash flow INR 38 Cr (+29% YoY); cash conversion priority as profitability scales
items.quote: adjusted operating cash flow, excluding onetime items relating to IPO and share buyback went up from INR 34 crores to INR 60 crores, up 80% year-over-year. On the right, you see that free cash flow improved from INR 29 crores to INR 38 crores, up 29% as well.

items.statement: Dedicated line for contract manufacturing agreement to be commissioned by July 2026.
items.quote: The commissioning of our dedicated line to cater to the contract manufacturing agreement is on track and expected to be completed by July 2026.

items.statement: Plan to launch one more biocide product in H2 FY27.
items.quote: Also, we plan to launch one more biocide product in the second half of this financial year, which will enhance our product offerings and strengthen our market position in this segment.

items.statement: Largely passed on raw material price increases in April and May.
items.quote: I can confirm that we have been largely able to pass on the input price increases in the month of April and May.

items.statement: Uncertainty in agrochemical intermediates demand due to possible suboptimal monsoon per El Nino forecasts.
items.quote: However, there is uncertainty about agrochemical intermediates demand going forward on account of the possibility of suboptimal monsoon as per the El Nino forecasts.

items.statement: Demand environment turned in Q4 FY26; momentum carried into Q4.
items.quote: However, the demand environment had begun to turn in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Final dividend of INR13.75 per share declared.
items.quote: I am happy to mention that the Board has declared a final dividend of INR13.75 per equity share, which is 275% of the face value of INR5 per share.

items.statement: Anti-dumping investigation findings expected by September 2026.
items.quote: However, considering that the investigation was initiated in September 2025, in normal course, we should expect some findings to be released by September 2026.

items.statement: Prices from China have increased due to VAT refund withdrawal and global input cost rise.
items.quote: So, yes, the prices have gone up. In general, we are seeing an increase in prices of products from China, and you know, this is due to a combination of factors, which is withdrawal of VAT refund as well as the input costs are globally increasing, including in China.

items.statement: Agrochemical intermediate proportion expected to reduce; new business value and margin accretive.
items.quote: But as we have shared, you know, whatever additional business that we are bringing in in terms of growth and due to which, you know, the agrochemical proportion, agrochemical intermediate proportion is expected to reduce going forward, the additional business coming in will be value and margin accretive.

items.statement: Domestic market share in phosphonates is 50-55%.
items.quote: Our domestic market share varies; it's in the range of 50% to 55%.

items.statement: Capacity utilization currently 65-85% depending on product.
items.quote: So, typically our current capacity utilization levels are in the range of 65% to 85%, depends on the product.

items.statement: Exports are 20% of revenue; US and EU are larger markets.
items.quote: Yes, so you know, the exports, the US, EU are the larger markets for us.

items.statement: Order intake up 20% YoY to INR 3,714 crores; opening backlog up 34% on April 1
