items.quote: We propose to spend approximately INR400 crores in FY27 towards Vizag greenfield, completion of Mahad and other additions in Ambernath.

items.statement: Mahad backward integration plant to go onstream in FY27 with slow ramp-up, full impact after a year
items.quote: Yes, we will -- the plant will go onstream this year, and we will start consuming the quantities that we produce, but we plan a slow ramp-up. So the full impact maybe will come after a year.

items.statement: PI segment inventory destocking complete, shipments rolling out at optimum capacity
items.quote: whatever destocking had to happen has happened, and the plant has been now running to optimum capacity and the shipments have started rolling out.

items.statement: Tracking ~20 active RFPs in PI/CDMO segment, 2 expected to commercialize in current year
items.quote: Within the PI and CDMO segment, we have been tracking approximately 20 active RFPs, primarily across chronic therapeutic areas, including intermediates linked to GLP -1 programs and peptide building blocks. Encouragingly, we believe that 2 of these opportun ities are expected to move into the commercialization phase during the current year

items.statement: Expect 3-4 new contrast media product launches in FY27 expanding advanced intermediates participation
items.quote: In the contrast media segment, we expect 3 to 4 new product launches during the current year, further expanding our participation across advanced intermediates within this space.

items.statement: High-intensity sweetener product under validation, trial quantities expected in coming quarters
items.quote: In the high-intensity sweetener segment, one high-volume product is currently under validation and we expect trial quantities to be shipped over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Discussions encouraging with select customers on pricing pass-through based on geopolitical situation
items.quote: The discussions are encouraging with select customers on pricing and pass-through based on current geopolitical situation.

items.statement: Margin outlook for FY27 uncertain due to evolving cost structures, logistics costs, crude oil impact; will update after Q1
items.quote: Actually, the cost structures are evolving. We need to actually watch how the Q1 cost structures pan out. We will be in a better position to talk about it during the Q1 results.

items.statement: Customer warning letter risk assessed as business as usual, no supply disruption foreseen in coming quarters
items.quote: From my side, I think it's business as usual in this particular segment. And we don't see -- foresee any disruption in the coming quarters also.

items.statement: No immediate fundraise planned; debt-free with INR400 crores liquid assets, accelerating capex from internal liquidity
items.quote: I think from a company standpoint, given the liquidity it has, I think we are going -- rather accelerating our capex plan. So we are well positioned as a debt-free company.

items.statement: Coworking and allied services revenue expected to grow 25-27% in FY27.
items.quote: our Coworking and Allied segment is expected to grow in the range of 25% to 28% (Correct number: 25% to 27%, previously stated on call) in FY '27.

items.statement: Awfis Transform revenue expected to grow 22-25% in FY27.
items.quote: Awfis Transform is expected to grow in the range of 20% to 23% (Correct Number: 22% to 25%,previously stated on call) over FY '26 levels.

items.statement: Total revenue growth expected at approximately 25-27% for FY27.
items.quote: Together, this total will constitute a revenue growth of approximately 25% to 27% for the full year.

items.statement: Gross seat additions planned at 22,000-25,000 seats in FY27.
items.quote: And what we expect to do is probably around 22,000 to 25,000 gross seats translating closer to 1.25 million square feet.

items.statement: INR130 crores of Transform mandates already won, to be delivered over next 6-7 months.
items.quote: The pipeline going into FY '27 is materially stronger with INR130 crores of mandates already won in delivery across the next 6 to 7 months.

items.statement: 14 major GCC mandates closed in FY26; 6 committed for FY27 and 7 in advanced discussions.
items.quote: We closed 14 major GCC mandates in FY ‘26 with 6 already committed for FY '27 and another 7 in advanced stages of discussion.

items.statement: Mature center occupancy at 84%, aiming for 200 bps increase over next couple of quarters.
items.quote: Broadly in this kind of a cohort, we would prefer that at least we have a couple of 100 basis point increase over the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: 5% seat closure churn not expected to recur annually.
items.quote: So broadly, we don't expect this percentage of seat closure across every year.

items.statement: Lease escalations typically 15% after first 3 years.
items.quote: typically, the way the leases work is that for the first 3 years is fixed, then it's a 15% escalation.

items.statement: Developer partnerships expected to become meaningful supply pillar in FY27 and FY28.
items.quote: We expect these partnerships to become a meaningful supply pillar in FY '27 and '28.

items.statement: Pre-committed over 4 lakh sq ft under managed aggregation through Q2 FY28.
items.quote: We have already pre-committed over 4 lakh square feet under our MA model through Q2 FY '28.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 growth expected to benefit from absence of Maha Kumbh base effect that impacted Q4 FY26
items.quote: Q1 FY '27 doesn't have the same base effect as Q4 FY '26. And therefore, we expect that to start showing up in terms of growth.

items.statement: Domestic demand trends remain strong in peak summer season; international travel affected by Middle East situation and higher fares
items.quote: we do see that demand trends continue to remain strong, at least for domestic. International continues to be affected somewhat, right, because of the Middle East situation as well as the fares

items.statement: Buses largest by contribution margin in Q4; flights largest by GTV; trains remain strategic franchise with 62% OTA market share
items.quote: In Q4, flights became our largest vertical by GTV, while buses became our largest vertical by contribution margin. Trains meanwhile continue to remain a very large strategic and profitable franchise for us.

items.statement: Train business faces near-term headwinds from policy changes (Tatkal timing, waitlist reduction) until new PRS system rolls out later this year
items.quote: Trains may continue to see some near-term headwinds until the underlying frequent policy changes stabilize or the new PRS system gets rolled out later this year

items.statement: AI infrastructure costs capitalized with 5-year amortization; includes foundational orchestration layer and platform capabilities
items.quote: it will be 5 years. And as the product, as the infrastructure layer comes up, it will be a 5-year amortization.

items.statement: Prosus fundraise proceeds being deployed over several years for AI investments, hotels build-out, and potential M&A; no rush on timeline
items.quote: We have time right now as in timelines are, we've still got a couple of years left for that. We don't want to rush into anything.

items.statement: ixigo NEXT launched as AI-native operating layer with voice intelligence, traveller context, real-time supply intelligence, and proprietary intelligence stack
items.quote: ixigo NEXT is not just a chatbot. It's not even a separate AI tab. It's not an assistant bolted onto a legacy app. It is fundamentally a new operating layer for travel.

items.statement: Fuel price increases passed through in flights and buses; buses in 'goldilocks zone' as take-rate business benefits from moderate fare increases
items.quote: flights are very sensitive to the price, a large part of the fuel price is passed through. In buses, this also happens, but buses, because it's a take rate business, it's actually, in some sense, a bit more beneficial

items.statement: AI systems handled 4.35M customer queries end-to-end; 81.5% voice and 91.1% chat conversations resolved by autonomous AI agents
items.quote: Our AI systems handled 4.35 million customer queries end-to-end, 81.5% of voice conversations and 91.1% of chat conversations with our customers were resolved by autonomous AI agents.

items.statement: Focus on absolute contribution margin and EBITDA rupee growth; willing to sacrifice 1-2% contribution margin for market share in flights and buses
items.quote: We are focused on the absolute number in contribution, the rupee number for contribution margin and rupee number for EBITDA. And we believe that growth will continue happening even while we invest in new businesses like hotels.

items.statement: Hotels Extranet HELLO launched for direct hotel onboarding; will disclose hotels separately only after product-market fit, operational maturity, and meaningful scale achieved
items.quote: we will start disclosing hotels separately only once we believe the business has reached the right level of product-market fit, operational maturity, and meaningful scale.

items.statement: Flight volumes impacted on Middle East and European routes; domestic growth and higher international fares offset GTV impact
items.quote: on the internatio nal side, we would have seen some impact, obviously, on Middle East and some of the European routes, etcetera. But then domestic growth more than covered up for it

items.statement: Company becoming AI-native: systems AI-readable, APIs AI-accessible, workflows AI-compatible, internal processes AI-native to accelerate product velocity
items.quote: We made our systems AI-readable. Our API is AI-accessible, our workflow is AI-compatible. Our internal process is AI-native. Because once the factory itself is reinvented, product velocity changes dramatically.

items.statement: Company expects overall revenue growth of around 20–25% for FY27.
items.quote: The company expects to achieve overall revenue growth of around 20–25% for financial year 2026–27.

items.statement: Tractor revenue expected to grow around 25–30% in FY27.
items.quote: Tractor revenue is expected to grow around 25–30%.

items.statement: Crane revenue from existing plant expected to grow around 15–20% in FY27.
items.quote: Crane revenue of existing plant is expected to grow around 15–20%.

items.statement: FY27 operating EBITDA margin expected around 12.5%.
items.quote: Ma'am, we are expecting the margin in the range of around 12.5% operating EBITDA.

items.statement: Tractor business steady-state EBIT margin expected around 10%.
items.quote: Around 10% at EBIT level.

items.statement: Total capex for new crane project around ₹70+ crore; ₹25 crore already spent.
items.quote: The total capex is around ₹70-plus crore, out of which we have already done around ₹25 crore till date.

items.statement: New pick-and-carry crane plant to start commercial production in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: The project work has regained momentum during the current quarter and the project is expected to start commercial production in the second quarter of financial year 2026–27.

items.statement: Tower crane commercial production to commence in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: Now that the testing is complete, we are fully geared for commercial production, commencing in Q2.

items.statement: Tower crane order book in single digits; deliveries to start Q2 FY27.
items.quote: As of now, we have recently started marketing, and we already have a small order book, so we've got some orders from the market already and the deliveries are supposed to start at Q2 beginning.

items.statement: Expects 60–80 tower crane units in next six months at ₹60–70 lakh ASP.
items.quote: we are expecting around 60 to 80 numbers in the next six months time.

items.statement: Emission norm cost pass-through to customers to continue from next quarter.
items.quote: Yes, yes, definitely. The market takes a little time.

items.statement: Other costs expected to normalize to 11–12% of revenue going forward.
items.quote: Going forward, it should hover in the range of around 11–12%, sir. Going forward, around 11–12% is what we are expecting.

items.statement: Working capital days expected to come under 200 days by FY28–29.
items.quote: It should come under 200 days.

items.statement: Internal plan of minimum 25% average growth; new crane plant 70–80% utilized by FY29–30.
items.quote: Around 25% average growth, minimum this is the internal plan. From the existing plant, until we utilize the whole capacity. And for the new crane plant, we expect that in FY29–30 at least around 70% to 80% utilization of the crane plant, because we are putting up a new plant of huge crane capacity.

items.statement: B2B revenue contribution expected to reach 35% in next three years.
items.quote: This could reach up to 35%, sir.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to increase to 3% in about two years (FY28).
items.quote: It can increase up to 3%, sir.

items.statement: Timeline to reach 3% EBITDA margin is about two years, consider FY28.
items.quote: About two years, consider ‘28, sir.

items.statement: Insurance and buyback revenue currently 2-3%, target 10% by FY26.
items.quote: So, our goal for ‘26 is to take it up to 10% first.

items.statement: Insurance and buyback revenue currently running at 2% to 3%.
items.quote: It is running at 2% to 3%, sir.

items.statement: MOP margin stays around 9% to 10%.
items.quote: We suggested that with every phone, our MOP margin stays around 9% to 10%.

items.statement: Store opening expense is INR4 lakh to INR5 lakhs.
items.quote: We incur an expense of INR4 lakh to INR5 lakhs on it.

items.statement: Average store turnover is around 25 to 30 lakhs per month.
items.quote: And on average, a store's turnover is around 25 to 30 lakhs.

items.statement: Store break-even time is minimum six to twelve months.
items.quote: Sir, minimum you can assume six to twelve months.

items.statement: Inventory managed at 28 to 30 days stock via ERP.
items.quote: So we manage with a 28 to 30 days stock inventory, and it's a complete ERP based on sales, we call it DOS.

items.statement: Added 100 plus stores since IPO.
items.quote: We have added 100 plus stores since the IPO, sir.

items.statement: Expected revenue growth of around 17%-18% for next financial year with broadly similar EBITDA margins.
items.quote: We believe the company is well positioned to continue its growth momentum in the next financial year with an expected revenue growth of around 17%-18% while maintaining EBITDA margins at broadly similar levels.

items.statement: Capacity expansion of 1.5 million units by Q2 FY27, with second phase of 1.5 million units over subsequent 15-18 months.
items.quote: we remain on track to increase our manufacturing capacity by 1.5 million units by Q2 financial year '27. Following this expansion, the second phase comprises of an additional 1.5 million units is expected over the subsequent 15 -18 months.

items.statement: Implemented calibrated price increases averaging 8%-9% from 1st April 2026 to offset rising input costs.
items.quote: To safeguard margins against rising input costs, we have implemented calibrated price increases across our portfolio and distribution channels, averaging around 8 %-9% from 1st April 2026.

items.statement: Exports expected to grow to 23%-24% of total revenues in current year, eventually reaching 30% in 2-3 years.
items.quote: We expect this to grow close to about 23% to 24% in the current year. And eventually this will go to close to 30% in 2 to 3 years of our total revenues.

items.statement: Gross margin pressure expected in Q1 FY27 due to raw material volatility, but recovery in subsequent quarters.
items.quote: But this quarter we will see a pressure on the gross margins.

items.statement: Demand remains strong internationally and in India despite price increases, with no demand pressures seen.
items.quote: No, the demand still remains very, very strong internationally and in India as well, because I think the dealers and the customers were expecting a bigger price increase because everybody knew the price change which was happening, the cost change which was happening for us.

items.statement: Unorganized market may shrink from 25-30% to 10-15% in 2-3 years due to cost pressures, benefiting organized players.
items.quote: my idea is unorganized is about 25 % to 30%, not more than 30% for sure, but not less than 20% as well and this, my idea is the next maybe 3 years might trim down to about 10% to 15%.

items.statement: New riding jackets and Bluetooth communication systems expected to begin commercial sales from H2 FY27.
items.quote: We anticipate commercial sa les of these products to begin from H2 financial year '27, further strengthening our premium product portfolio and increasing consumer engagement across categories.

items.statement: Decathlon engagement progressing, with initial supplies expected to commence in July 2026.
items.quote: We are progressing well with our Decathlon engagement, with initial supplies expected to commence in July 2026.

items.statement: Europe subsidiary in Italy to start operations mid-Q2 FY27, stocking 10,000-15,000 units initially.
items.quote: So mid of quarter 2 , the operations will start. So we have already signed the documents for incorporation of the company in Italy.

items.statement: SMK EBITDA margin is about 10% higher than STUDDS; export and domestic margins similar.
items.quote: I mean, if I'm making 17% on STUDDS EBITDA, I'll be making 27% on SMK.

items.statement: Additional 2%-2.5% price increase needed if current raw material hike sustains for full year.
items.quote: So another about 2% to 2.5%. If we take another price increase and this current price hike sustains for the full year, we should be good.

items.statement: Inventory days expected to remain at 85-90 days going forward, up from 68 days previously.
items.quote: But I would say that anywhere between 85 to 90 days of inventory is where a comfortable position is and that’s what you will see going forward as well.

items.statement: Management targets 30-35% revenue growth for FY27, consistent with historical trajectory
items.quote: If you will see about the growth, then growth will be as per previous years. If you see the historical, in historical last four, five years, it is between 30 to 35% of growth. So, we are looking at similar growth in this year also.

items.statement: Order book stands at over INR 3,000 crores as of May 25, 2026, including multi-year Weatherford order over INR 900 crores
items.quote: The order book, as on 25th May 2026, more than INR 3,000 crores of order book has been indicated, and a strong order book flow is going on.

items.statement: Three concurrent initiatives in FY27: commissioning Hyderabad facility, expanding Chhapara facility, implementing solar roofing at Chhapara plant
items.quote: In FY27, three concurrent initiatives will underpin the forward strategy. This is of: 1. Commissioning a new manufacturing facility in Hyderabad. 2. Expanding operation at a proposed new facility at Chhapara. 3. Implementing a solar roofing at the existing Chhapara plant.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to remain in historical 30-35% range; Q4 margin compression due to pre-investment in growth capabilities
items.quote: On average, we are in the range of 30 % to 35% of the EBITDAs and like that. So, that is the overall guidance presently.

items.statement: Raw material cost increases are passed through to customers; most business is ex-works basis with price escalation clauses
items.quote: When we talk about passing of raw materials, that is a very given in our line of business. So, usually it is considered that whatever there is an increase or impact on any situation that we passed on, particularly if we even talk about the logistic side of it, most of the business, what we do is all ex works.

items.statement: Strong demand visibility from energy sector (74% of order book); North America contributes 64% of order book geography
items.quote: The order book mix is currently led by Energy at 74%, followed by Motion and Automation at 14%, and Industrial Equipment is standing at around 12%. If we look at the geography-wise mix, North America is contributing around 64%, Asia is around 34%.

items.statement: Aerospace and defense entering engagement stage with 4 FA development orders received; AS9100 certified, NADCAP certification initiated
items.quote: Omnitech’s existing plants at Metoda and Chhapara have been certified for Aerospace AS9100, and we have also initiated NADCAP Certification process for surface treatment, NDT, and welding, marking another important milesto ne to get into the aerospace sector. There are already four FA development orders being received, marking a key step forward in defense and aerospace segments

items.statement: Weatherford INR 900 crore order ramps over 5 years (~70% year 1, 85% year 2); another INR 1000 crore order starts FY27 with some product lines in early FY28
items.quote: You can say, just an example, roughly INR 900 crores and 5 years is a program. So, maybe 70% on first year, second year, 85% and similarly, it will go like that.

items.statement: Existing capacity covers FY27 and early FY28; new Chhapara facility ramps from Q1 FY27; Ahmedabad land acquired for post-FY28 growth
items.quote: overall, we have to plan at least in the year ahead of our execution. So, we are overall covered with FY27 and near to FY28 only for Q1 and Q2. And by that time, we are also b uilding up the new capacity

items.statement: Targets FY27 revenue of INR750 crores with 17% EBITDA margin, H2-heavy.
items.quote: Based on these drivers, we are targeting a revenue of INR750 crores for the financial year 27 with an EBITDA margin in the range of 17% mFY27.

items.statement: India capex: INR111 crores for capacity expansion and EU-GMP upgrades, funded by IPO proceeds.
items.quote: Out of this, about INR111 crores is being deployed towards capacity expansion and EU-GMP upgrades at our manufacturing facilitics in India. This funding is being done entircly through the IPO proceeds.

items.statement: INR15 crores for dedicated R&D center in India, funded through IPO proceeds.
items.quote: In addition, there is an INRIS crores being invested towards cstablishing a dedicated R&D center in India. This investment is also being funded through the IPO proceeds.

items.statement: Australia Adelaide facility capex AUD53 million (INR311 crores), AUD20 million grant, AUD40 million invested.
items.quote: As part of the acquisition, we took ownership of the Adelaide manufacturing facility cxpansion project in Australia, which involves the total planned capex investment of about AUD 53 million or INR311 crores.

items.statement: Noumed vertical integration to improve margins by internalizing manufacturing from CMOs.
items.quote: So the backward integration starts the last quarter and then thereon in '28 it will be the full integration. So the additional business whichis going to come from the manufacturing will create additional revenue and also the integration between Sai and Noumed is also going to give an extra margin in terms of the other

items.statement: 67 dossiers under development to commercialize in FY27 and FY28, providing growth visibility.
items.quote: In addition, 67 dossiers are currently under development at Sai in various stages, and they are expected to be commercialized during financial year 27 and financial year 128, providing strong visibility for future growth.

items.statement: Over 50% consolidated revenue from long-term supply contracts in regulated markets.
items.quote: Today, more than 50% consolidated reveme comes from long-term supply contracts in regulated markets.

items.statement: FY27 peak debt year; debt to decline from FY28 onwards.
items.quote: FY '27 s expected to be the peak year of debt for the group as we complete our ongoing capex programs. However, these assets will begin contributing to carnings and cash flows in FY28. Therefore, we expect debt levels to decline from FY 128 onwards.

items.statement: Working capital requirement expected at 25-30% of incremental revenue.
items.quote: Generally, as a pharma business, we would look at about 25% of additional revenues as the working capital requirement. So as we scale up businesses, we would look at working capital requirement of about 25% to 30% range.

items.statement: Australian facility TGA license expected by March 31 next year; commissioning starts Oct-Nov.
items.quote: TGA license is expected to be commissioned and up and flowing no later than the 31t of March next year.

items.statement: Noumed provides access to 451 IP dossiers, accelerating product launches to 6-9 months.
items.quote: Additionally, through Noumed Pharmaceuticals, we gainedaccess not only to Australia and New Zealand markets but also to a growing base of 451 IP dossicrs that can be leveraged across multiple export markets, accelerating product launch timelines from 18 to 24 months to six to nine months.

items.statement: 88 dossiers approved in FY26 across regulated and emerging markets; Noumed added 5 in Q4.
items.quote: During the financial year 126, we got approvals for 88 dossiers acoss regulated and emerging markets, while Noumed added a further five dossicrs in Australia in Q4 FY '26.
